This is what the LORD had commanded: "Gather of it, each of you, as much as he can eat. You shall each take an omer, according to the number of persons each of you has in his tent."
The Israelites did so; they gathered, some more and some less.
But when they measured it by the omer, the one who had gathered much had no surplus, and the one who had gathered little had no deficit. Each gathered exactly as much as he could eat.
Moses said to them, "Let no one keep any of it until morning."
But they did not listen to Moses; some kept part of it until morning, and it bred worms and reeked. Moses was angry with them.
Morning by morning they gathered it, each as much as he could eat; but when the sun grew hot, it melted.
On the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread—two omers per person. All the leaders of the congregation came and reported it to Moses.

He said to them, "This is what the LORD has commanded: 'Tomorrow is a day of solemn rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. Bake what you will bake and boil what you will boil, and put aside all that is left over to be kept until morning.'"
So they set it aside until morning, as Moses had commanded; and it did not become putrid, nor were there any worms in it.
Moses said, "Eat it today, for today is a Sabbath to the LORD; today you will not find it in the field.
Six days you shall gather it, but on the seventh day, which is a Sabbath, there will be none."
On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather, but they found none.
The LORD said to Moses, "How long will you refuse to keep My commandments and My laws?
See, the LORD has given you the Sabbath; therefore on the sixth day He gives you bread for two days. Let each of you remain in his place; let no one go out of his place on the seventh day."
So the people rested on the seventh day.
The house of Israel called its name manna. It was like coriander seed, white, and its taste was like wafers made with honey.

Moses said, "This is what the LORD has commanded: 'Let an omer of it be kept throughout your generations, so that they may see the bread with which I fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you out of Egypt.'"
Moses said to Aaron, "Take a jar, and put an omer of manna in it, and place it before the LORD to be kept throughout your generations."
As the LORD had commanded Moses, Aaron placed it before the testimony, to be kept.
The Israelites ate the manna for forty years, until they came to the border of the land of Canaan.
An omer is a tenth of an ephah.

Then the whole congregation of the Israelites journeyed from the Wilderness of Sin, moving from place to place as the the LORD had commanded. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.
So the people quarreled with Moses, saying, "Give us water to drink." Moses replied, "Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test the the LORD?"
The people were thirsty for water there, and they grumbled against Moses, saying, "Why have you brought us up out of Egypt, only to kill us and our children and our livestock with thirst?"
Then Moses cried out to the the LORD, saying, "What am I to do with these people? They are almost ready to stone me!"
And the the LORD said to Moses, "Go on ahead of the people and take some of the elders of Israel with you. Take the staff in your hand, the one with which you struck the Nile, and go.
Behold, I will stand there before you by the rock at Horeb. When you strike the rock, water will come out of it for the people to drink." So Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.
He named the place Massah and Meribah, because the Israelites quarreled and tested the the LORD, saying, "Is the the LORD among us or not?"
Then the Amalekites came and attacked the Israelites at Rephidim.
So Moses said to Joshua, "Choose some of our men and go out to fight the Amalekites. Tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill, with the staff of God in my hand."
Joshua did as Moses had instructed and fought the Amalekites, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
As long as Moses held up his hands, Israel prevailed; but when he lowered them, Amalek prevailed.

When Moses' hands grew heavy, they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Then Aaron and Hur held his hands up, one on each side, so that his hands remained steady until the sun went down.
So Joshua overcame the Amalekite army with the sword.
Then the the LORD said to Moses, "Write this on a scroll as a reminder and recite it to Joshua, because I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven."
And Moses built an altar and named it The LORD Is My Banner.
For he said, "Because the the LORD has sworn by His throne: the the LORD will be at war with Amalek from generation to generation."
Now Jethro, the priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law, heard of all that God had done for Moses and for His people Israel, and how the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
After Moses had sent his wife Zipporah away, Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, took her back,
along with her two sons. One son was named Gershom, because Moses had said, "I have been a sojourner in a foreign land."
The other was named Eliezer, for Moses had said, "The God of my father was my help, and He delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh."
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came with Moses' wife and sons to Moses in the wilderness, where he was encamped at the mountain of God.
He said to Moses, "I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you, with your wife and her two sons."
So Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, bowed down, and kissed him; and they greeted one another and entered the tent.
Moses told his father-in-law all that the LORD had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel's sake, all the hardship that had befallen them on the way, and how the LORD had delivered them.
Jethro rejoiced over all the goodness that the LORD had done for Israel, whom He had delivered from the hand of the Egyptians.
Jethro said, "Blessed be the LORD, who has delivered you from the hand of the Egyptians and from the hand of Pharaoh, and who has delivered the people from under the hand of the Egyptians.
Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods, for in the very matter in which they dealt arrogantly against them, He proved Himself superior."
Then Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God, and Aaron came with all the elders of Israel to eat bread with Moses' father-in-law before God.
The next day Moses sat to judge the people, and the people stood about Moses from morning until evening.

When Moses' father-in-law saw all that he was doing for the people, he said, "What is this thing that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone, while all the people stand about you from morning until evening?"
Moses said to his father-in-law, "Because the people come to me to inquire of God.
When they have a dispute, they come to me, and I judge between a man and his neighbor, and I make known the statutes of God and His laws."
Moses' father-in-law said to him, "The thing that you are doing is not good.
You will surely wear yourself out—you and the people with you—for the thing is too heavy for you; you cannot do it alone.
Now listen to my voice: I will give you counsel, and God will be with you. You shall be for the people before God, and bring their matters to God.
And you shall teach them the statutes and the laws, and show them the way in which they must walk and the work they must do.
Moreover, choose able men from all the people—men who fear God, trustworthy men who hate dishonest gain—and appoint them over the people as chiefs of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.

Let them judge the people at all times. Every great matter they shall bring to you, but every small matter they shall judge themselves. So it will be easier for you, and they will bear the burden with you.
If you do this, and God so commands you, then you will be able to endure, and all this people will go to their place in peace."
So Moses listened to the voice of his father-in-law and did all that he had said.
Moses chose able men from all Israel and made them heads over the people—chiefs of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
They judged the people at all times; the hard cases they brought to Moses, but every small matter they judged themselves.
Then Moses let his father-in-law depart, and he went away to his own country.
In the third month after the Israelites had departed from the land of Egypt, on that very day, they entered the wilderness of Sinai.
Having set out from Rephidim, they came to the wilderness of Sinai and encamped there in the wilderness, opposite the mountain.
Moses ascended to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain, saying, "Thus you shall say to the house of Jacob and declare to the children of Israel:"
"You have seen what I did to Egypt, and how I bore you on eagles' wings and brought you to Myself.
Now, therefore, if you will indeed obey My voice and keep My covenant, you shall be My treasured possession among all peoples, for all the earth is Mine.
You shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. These are the words you shall speak to the children of Israel."
So Moses came and summoned the elders of the people, and he set before them all these words that the LORD had commanded him.
All the people answered together, saying, "All that the LORD has spoken we will do." Then Moses brought the people's words back to the LORD.

The LORD said to Moses, "Behold, I am coming to you in a thick cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you and may also believe in you forever." Then Moses reported the people's words to the LORD.
The LORD said to Moses, "Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow; let them wash their garments.
Be ready by the third day, for on the third day the LORD will descend upon Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.
Set bounds around the people on every side and say, 'Take heed that you do not ascend the mountain or touch its border; whoever touches the mountain shall surely be put to death.
No hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned or shot with arrows; whether man or beast, he shall not live. When the trumpet sounds a long blast, they may ascend the mountain.'"
Moses descended from the mountain to the people and consecrated them, and they washed their garments.
He said to the people, "Be ready for three days; do not have sexual relations with a woman."
On the third day, when morning came, there were thunder and lightning and a thick cloud upon the mountain, and a very loud trumpet blast, so that all the people in the camp trembled.
Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet God, and they took their stand at the foot of the mountain.
Mount Sinai was entirely wrapped in smoke because the LORD had descended upon it in fire; its smoke ascended like the smoke of a kiln, and the whole mountain quaked violently.
As the sound of the trumpet grew louder and louder, Moses spoke, and God answered him with a voice.
The LORD descended upon Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain; and the LORD called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.
The LORD said to Moses, "Go down and warn the people, lest they break through to gaze upon the LORD and many of them perish.
Also let the priests who approach the LORD consecrate themselves, lest the LORD break out against them."
Moses said to the LORD, "The people cannot ascend Mount Sinai, for You warned us, saying, 'Set bounds around the mountain and consecrate it.'"
The LORD said to him, "Go down, and come back up, you and Aaron with you; but do not let the priests and the people break through to come up to the LORD, lest He break out against them."
So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.
And God spoke all these words, saying:
“I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
You shall have no other gods before Me.
You shall not make for yourself a carved image, or any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth.

You shall not bow down to them or serve them, for I the LORD your God am a jealous God, punishing the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generation of those who hate Me,
but showing steadfast love to thousands of those who love Me and keep My commandments.
You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain, for the LORD will not hold him guiltless who takes His name in vain.
“Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.
Six days you shall labor, and do all your work,

but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. On it you shall not do any work, you, or your son, or your daughter, your male servant, or your female servant, or your livestock, or the sojourner who is within your gates.
For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested on the seventh day. Therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.
“Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
You shall not covet your neighbor's house; you shall not covet your neighbor's wife, or his male servant, or his female servant, or his ox, or his donkey, or anything that is your neighbor's.”
Now when all the people saw the thunder and the flashes of lightning and the sound of the trumpet and the mountain smoking, the people were afraid and trembled, and they stood at a distance.
And they said to Moses, “You speak to us, and we will listen; but do not let God speak to us, lest we die.”
And Moses said to the people, “Do not be afraid, for God has come to test you, that the fear of Him may be before you, that you may not sin.”
The people stood at a distance, while Moses drew near to the thick darkness where God was.
And the LORD said to Moses, “Thus you shall say to the Israelites: ‘You have seen for yourselves that I have spoken with you from heaven.
You shall not make gods of silver to be with Me, nor shall you make for yourselves gods of gold.

You shall make for Me an altar of earth, and sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your sheep and your oxen. In every place where I cause My name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
If you make Me an altar of stone, you shall not build it of hewn stones, for if you use a tool on it, you profane it.
And you shall not go up by steps to My altar, that your nakedness may not be exposed on it.’”
These are the ordinances that you shall set before them.
When you purchase a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years, and in the seventh he shall go free without payment.
If he enters alone, he shall leave alone; if he has a wife, his wife shall leave with him.
If his master provides a wife for him and she bears sons or daughters, the wife and children shall belong to the master, and he shall leave alone.
But if the servant says plainly, “I love my master, my wife, and my children; I do not wish to go free,”
then his master shall bring him before God and to the door or doorpost, and shall pierce his ear with an awl; thereafter he shall serve him permanently.
If a man sells his daughter as a maidservant, she shall not be released under the same terms as male servants.
If she fails to please the master who designated her, he must allow her redemption; he may not sell her to a foreign people, because he has broken faith with her.
If he designates her for his son, he shall grant her the rights of a daughter.
If he takes another wife, he must not reduce the first wife's food, clothing, or marital rights.
If he fails to provide these three things, she shall go free without payment.
Whoever strikes a person so that he dies shall certainly be put to death.
But if he did not lie in wait, and God delivered him into his power, I will designate a place for you to which he may flee.
But if a person acts with premeditation against his neighbor in order to kill him treacherously, you shall take him even from My altar, so that he may die.
Anyone who strikes his father or mother shall certainly be put to death.
Whoever kidnaps a person and sells him, or is found holding him in possession, shall certainly be put to death.
Anyone who curses his father or mother shall certainly be put to death.
If men quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone or his fist, and the victim does not die but is confined to bed,
and if the injured man later rises and walks about with a staff, the one who struck him shall be acquitted, provided he pays for the lost time and covers the cost of healing.
If a man strikes his male or female servant with a rod so that the servant dies under his hand, he shall be punished.
But if the servant survives a day or two, the master shall not be punished, because the servant is his property.

If men are fighting and strike a pregnant woman so that she gives birth prematurely, but no further injury occurs, the offender shall be fined as the woman's husband imposes, subject to the judges' approval.
But if further injury occurs, you shall give life for life.
An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, a hand for a hand, a foot for a foot.
A burn for a burn, a wound for a wound, a bruise for a bruise.
If a man strikes the eye of his male or female servant and destroys it, he shall release the servant in compensation for the eye.
If he knocks out a servant's tooth, he shall release that servant in compensation for the tooth.
If an ox gores a man or a woman to death, the ox shall be stoned and its flesh shall not be eaten, but the owner shall be acquitted.
But if the ox has been in the habit of goring and its owner has been warned yet fails to confine it, and it kills a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned and its owner shall also be put to death.
If a ransom is imposed on him, he shall pay whatever is required to redeem his life.
The same judgment applies whether the ox gores a son or a daughter.
If the ox gores a male or female servant, the owner shall pay the master thirty shekels of silver, and the ox shall be stoned.
If a man opens or digs a pit and fails to cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
the owner of the pit shall make restitution, paying money to the animal's owner, and the dead animal shall belong to him.
If one man's ox injures another's so that it dies, they shall sell the living ox and divide the proceeds, and they shall also divide the carcass.
But if it is known that the ox was previously in the habit of goring and its owner did not confine it, he shall pay ox for ox, and the dead animal shall be his.
If a man steals an ox or a sheep and kills it or sells it, he shall repay five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep.
If a thief is found breaking in and is struck so that he dies, there is no bloodguilt for him.
But if the sun has risen on him, there is bloodguilt for him. He shall surely make restitution; if he has nothing, he shall be sold for his theft.
If the stolen animal is found alive in his hand—whether ox, donkey, or sheep—he shall repay double.
If a man causes a field or vineyard to be grazed over, or lets his livestock loose so that they feed in another man's field, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field and vineyard.
If fire breaks out and catches thorns, so that stacked grain, standing grain, or a field is consumed, the one who started the fire shall surely make restitution.
If a man gives his neighbor silver or goods to keep, and they are stolen from the man's house, then if the thief is found, he shall pay double.
If the thief is not found, the owner of the house shall be brought before God, to determine whether he has laid hands on his neighbor's property.

In every case of breach of trust—whether concerning an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any lost thing of which one says, "This is it"—the case of both parties shall come before God, and the one whom God condemns shall pay double to his neighbor.
If a man gives his neighbor a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any beast to keep, and it dies, is injured, or is carried off, with no one seeing it,
an oath by the LORD shall be between the two of them, to determine whether he has taken his neighbor's property; the owner shall accept the oath, and the keeper need not make restitution.
But if it was stolen from him, he shall make restitution to its owner.
If it was torn by beasts, he shall bring it as evidence; he need not make restitution for what was torn.
If a man borrows anything from his neighbor, and it is injured or dies while its owner is not with it, he shall surely make restitution.
If its owner was with it, he need not make restitution; if it was hired, the hire covers the loss.
If a man seduces a virgin who is not betrothed and lies with her, he shall pay the bride-price and take her as his wife.
If her father refuses to give her to him, he shall pay money equal to the bride-price of virgins.
You shall not permit a sorceress to live.
Whoever lies with an animal shall be put to death.
Whoever sacrifices to any god other than the LORD alone must be completely destroyed.
Do not mistreat or oppress a foreigner, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
Do not afflict any widow or orphan.
If you do afflict them, and they cry out to Me, I will surely hear their cry.
My anger will burn, and I will kill you with the sword; then your wives will become widows and your children fatherless.
If you lend money to any of My people who is poor, you must not be like a creditor to him, and do not charge him interest.
If you ever take your neighbor's cloak in pledge, you shall return it to him before the sun goes down,
for it is his only covering; it is his cloak for his body. In what else shall he sleep? If he cries out to Me, I will hear, for I am gracious.
You shall not revile God, nor curse a ruler of your people.
Do not delay to offer the firstfruits of your harvest and the outflow of your presses. You shall give Me the firstborn of your sons.
You shall do the same with your oxen and your sheep: it shall remain with its mother seven days, and on the eighth day you shall give it to Me.
You shall be holy people to Me. You shall not eat flesh torn by beasts in the field; throw it to the dogs.
“You must not spread a false report, nor join your hand with the wicked to be a malicious witness.
You must not follow the multitude in doing evil, nor shall you testify in a dispute so as to turn aside after the multitude and pervert justice.
Nor shall you show partiality to a poor man in his dispute.
“If you meet your enemy’s ox or his donkey wandering astray, you shall surely return it to him.
If you see the donkey of one who hates you lying beneath its burden, and you would refrain from helping it, you shall surely help him with it.
You must not pervert the judgment due to your poor in his dispute.
“Keep far from a false charge, and do not kill the innocent and the righteous, for I will not justify the wicked.
You must take no bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and perverts the words of the righteous.
You must not oppress a sojourner, for you know the heart of a sojourner, since you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.”
“For six years you shall sow your land and gather its yield.

But in the seventh year you shall let it rest and release it, so that the poor of your people may eat; and whatever remains the beasts of the field shall eat. You shall do the same with your vineyard and your olive grove.
Six days you shall do your work, but on the seventh day you shall rest, so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the son of your maidservant and the sojourner may be refreshed.
Heed all that I have spoken to you, and do not invoke the names of other gods, nor let them be heard on your lips.
“Three times in the year you shall celebrate a feast to Me.

You shall keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread. As I commanded you, you shall eat unleavened bread for seven days at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in it you came out of Egypt. And no one shall appear before Me empty-handed.
You shall observe the Feast of Harvest, the firstfruits of your labor, which you sow in the field; and the Feast of Ingathering at the end of the year, when you gather in your produce from the field.
Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the Lord, the LORD.
You shall not offer the blood of My sacrifice with leavened bread, nor shall the fat of My feast remain until morning.
The best of the firstfruits of your ground you shall bring into the house of the LORD your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.”
“Behold, I am sending an angel before you to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared.
Beware of him and obey his voice; do not rebel against him, for he will not pardon your transgression, for My name is in him.
But if you truly obey his voice and do all that I speak, then I will be an enemy to your enemies and an adversary to your adversaries.
For My angel will go before you and bring you in to the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Canaanite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, and I will annihilate them.
You must not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor do as they do, but you shall utterly overthrow them and break their pillars.
“And you shall serve the LORD your God, and He will bless your bread and your water, and I will remove sickness from your midst.
No one in your land shall miscarry or be barren; I will fulfill the number of your days.
I will send My terror before you, and I will throw into confusion all the people among whom you come, and I will make all your enemies turn their backs to you.
And I will send the hornet before you, and it shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite from before you.
I will not drive them out from before you in one year, lest the land become desolate and the beasts of the field multiply against you.
Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you have increased and inherit the land.

And I will set your border from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River, for I will give the inhabitants of the land into your hand, and you shall drive them out before you.
“You must make no covenant with them or with their gods.
They shall not dwell in your land, lest they make you sin against Me; for if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare to you.”
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Come up to the LORD, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel, and you shall worship from afar.
Moses alone shall come near to the LORD, but they shall not come near, and the people shall not come up with him."
Moses came and told the people all the words of the LORD and all the ordinances, and all the people answered with one voice, "All the words that the LORD has spoken we will do."
Moses wrote down all the words of the LORD. He rose early in the morning and built an altar at the foot of the mountain, and twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
He sent the young men of Israel, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed peace offerings of oxen to the LORD.
Moses took half the blood and put it in basins, and the other half he sprinkled on the altar.
Then he took the Book of the Covenant and read it in the hearing of the people, and they said, "All that the LORD has spoken we will do, and we will be obedient."
Moses took the blood and sprinkled it on the people and said, "Behold, the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you in accordance with all these words."
Then Moses went up with Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel.
They saw the God of Israel, and under His feet was something like a pavement of sapphire, as clear as the sky itself.
He did not lay His hand on the nobles of the Israelites; they saw God, and they ate and drank.
The LORD said to Moses, "Come up to Me on the mountain and remain there, so that I may give you the tablets of stone, the law, and the commandment that I have written for their instruction."
So Moses arose with his assistant Joshua, and Moses went up the mountain of God.
He said to the elders, "Wait here for us until we return to you. Behold, Aaron and Hur are with you. Whoever has a dispute, let him go to them."
Then Moses went up the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
The glory of the LORD settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day He called to Moses from within the cloud.
The appearance of the glory of the LORD was like a consuming fire on the mountaintop in the sight of the Israelites.
Moses entered the cloud and went up the mountain, and he was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them to bring Me an offering. You are to receive My offering from everyone whose heart moves him to give.
This is the offering you are to receive from them: gold, silver, and bronze;
blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen and goat hair;
ram skins dyed red; fine leather; and acacia wood;
olive oil for the lamp; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
and onyx stones and other stones to be set in the ephod and breastpiece.
Then have them make a sanctuary for Me, and I will dwell among them.
You must make the tabernacle and all its furnishings according to the pattern I will show you.
"They are to make an ark of acacia wood—two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
Overlay it with pure gold, inside and out, and make a gold molding around it.
Cast four gold rings for it and attach them to its four feet, two rings on one side and two on the other.
Make poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
Insert the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark so that it may be carried.
The poles are to remain in the rings of the ark and must not be removed.
Place in the ark the Testimony that I will give you.
"Make an atonement cover of pure gold—two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
Make two cherubim of hammered gold at the two ends of the cover.
Make one cherub on one end and the second cherub on the other end; make the cherubim of one piece with the cover.
The cherubim are to spread their wings upward, overshadowing the cover with their wings, and they are to face one another, with their faces toward the cover.
Place the cover on top of the ark, and put in the ark the Testimony that I will give you.

There I will meet with you, and from above the atonement cover, from between the two cherubim that are over the ark of the Testimony, I will speak with you about all that I command you for the Israelites.
"Make a table of acacia wood—two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
Overlay it with pure gold and make a gold molding around it.
Make a rim for it a handbreadth wide all around, and make a gold molding for the rim.
Make four gold rings for it and fasten them to the four corners at its four legs.
The rings are to be placed near the rim to hold the poles for carrying the table.
Make the poles of acacia wood, overlay them with gold, and carry the table with them.
Make its plates, dishes, pitchers, and bowls for pouring drink offerings; make them of pure gold.
Place the Bread of the Presence on the table before Me at all times.
"Make a lampstand of pure gold. Hammer out its base and shaft; its cups, buds, and blossoms are to be of one piece with it.
Six branches are to extend from its sides—three on one side and three on the other.
On one branch there are to be three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with bud and flower, and the same on the next branch. The six branches extending from the lampstand are to be alike.
On the lampstand itself there are to be four cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with bud and flower.
A bud is to be under the first pair of branches coming from the lampstand, a bud under the second pair, and a bud under the third pair—the six branches extending from the lampstand.
Their buds and branches are to be one piece with the lampstand, all of it a single piece of hammered pure gold.
"Make seven lamps for it and set them up so that they light the area in front of it.
Its wick trimmers and trays are to be of pure gold.
The lampstand and all its utensils are to be made from a talent of pure gold.
See that you make them according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain."
Construct the tabernacle with ten curtains of finely spun linen, woven with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and embroidered with cherubim.
Each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide, with every curtain of identical dimensions.
Join five of the curtains to one another, and join the remaining five to one another.
Make loops of blue yarn along the edge of the last curtain in the first set, and make the same along the edge of the last curtain in the second set.
Make fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain in the second set, so that the loops align opposite one another.
Make fifty gold clasps and fasten the curtains together with them, so that the tabernacle becomes a single unit.
Make curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle—eleven curtains in all.
Each of the eleven curtains is to be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide, all of the same size.
Join five of the curtains into one set and the other six into another; then fold the sixth curtain double at the front of the tent.
Make fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the first set and fifty loops along the edge of the corresponding curtain in the second set.
Make fifty bronze clasps and insert them into the loops to join the tent into one unit.
The remaining half curtain shall hang over the back of the tabernacle.
The tent curtains will be a cubit longer on either side, and the excess length shall hang down along the sides of the tabernacle to cover it.
Make a covering for the tent from ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.
Make upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
Each frame is to be ten cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
Form two tenons on each frame, fitted to one another; make every frame of the tabernacle in this way.
Construct twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle,
with forty silver bases beneath them—two bases under each frame, one for each tenon.
For the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, make twenty frames
with forty silver bases—two bases under each frame.
Make six frames for the rear of the tabernacle, on the west side,
and make two frames for the two corners at the rear of the tabernacle,
coupled together from bottom to top and fitted into a single ring; both corner frames must be made in this way.
Thus there are to be eight frames and sixteen silver bases—two bases under each frame.
Also make five crossbars of acacia wood for the frames on one side of the tabernacle,
five for the frames on the other side, and five for the frames on the rear side, to the west.
The central crossbar in the middle of the frames shall run from one end to the other.
Overlay the frames with gold, make gold rings to hold the crossbars, and overlay the crossbars with gold.
Set up the tabernacle according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain.
Make a veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely spun linen, with cherubim skillfully worked into it.
Hang it with gold hooks on four acacia posts overlaid with gold, standing on four silver bases.
Hang the veil from the clasps and place the ark of the Testimony behind the veil, so that the veil separates the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.
Put the mercy seat on the ark of the Testimony in the Most Holy Place.
Place the table outside the veil, and put the lampstand opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle.
For the entrance to the tent, make a curtain of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely spun linen, the work of an embroiderer.
Make five acacia posts for the curtain, overlay them with gold, and make their hooks of gold; cast five bronze bases for them.
Construct an altar of acacia wood, square in plan: five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high.
Make horns on its four corners, forming them as one piece with the altar, and overlay the whole altar with bronze.
Make all its utensils of bronze—its pots for removing ashes, its shovels, its basins, its forks, and its firepans.
Make a bronze grating for it, a network of bronze, and attach four bronze rings to the four corners of the net.
Set the grating beneath the altar's ledge so that the mesh rises halfway up the altar.
Make poles of acacia wood and overlay them with bronze.
Insert the poles through the rings so that they project from the two sides of the altar whenever it is carried.
Construct the altar as a hollow framework of boards, exactly as He showed you on the mountain.
Construct the court of the tabernacle. On the south side, toward the south, the curtains of fine twisted linen shall be one hundred cubits long for that side.
It shall have twenty pillars with twenty bronze bases, and the hooks and bands of the pillars shall be silver.
The north side shall be the same in length: curtains one hundred cubits long, with twenty pillars and twenty bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands for the pillars.
The width of the court on the west side shall be fifty cubits, with ten pillars and ten bases.
The width of the court on the east side, toward the east, shall be fifty cubits.
The curtains for one side of the entrance shall be fifteen cubits, with three pillars and three bases.
The curtains for the other side shall likewise be fifteen cubits, with three pillars and three bases.

For the gate of the court there shall be a screen twenty cubits long, embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer, with four pillars and four bases.
All the pillars around the court shall be banded with silver; their hooks shall be bronze, and their bases bronze.
The court shall be one hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide, with curtains of fine twisted linen five cubits high and bronze bases.
All the utensils used in the service of the tabernacle, together with all the pegs of the court, shall be bronze.
You are to command the Israelites to bring you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, so that the lamps may burn continually.

In the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil that is before the Testimony, Aaron and his sons shall keep the lamps burning before the LORD from evening until morning. This is to be a perpetual statute for the Israelites throughout their generations.
The LORD said to Moses, “Bring near to yourself Aaron your brother, along with his sons—Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar—from among the Israelites, that he may serve Me as priest.
Make holy garments for your brother Aaron, for glory and for beauty.
Speak to all who are wise in heart, whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom, and let them make Aaron’s garments to consecrate him for his priesthood to Me.

These are the garments they shall make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, an embroidered tunic, a turban, and a sash. They shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother and for his sons, that he may serve Me as priest.
They shall take the gold, the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and the fine linen. “
You shall make the ephod of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and of finely twisted linen, the work of a skilled craftsman.
It shall have two shoulder pieces attached at its two ends, so that it is joined.
The skillfully woven waistband that is on it shall be of one piece with it—of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen.
You shall take two onyx stones.
Engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel—six of the names on one stone and the remaining six on the other stone—in the order of their birth.
You shall engrave the two stones like a signet ring with the names of the sons of Israel, and mount them in gold filigree settings.
Fasten both stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel. Aaron shall bear their names before the the LORD on his two shoulders for a memorial.
You shall make gold filigree settings.
You shall make two chains of pure gold, twisted like cords, and attach them to the settings. “
You shall make the breastpiece of judgment, skillfully worked like the ephod; you shall make it of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen.
It shall be square and doubled, a span in length and a span in width.
You shall set in it four rows of stones:
a first row of ruby, topaz, and emerald;
a second row of turquoise, sapphire, and diamond;
a third row of jacinth, agate, and amethyst; and a fourth row of beryl, onyx, and jasper. They shall be mounted in gold filigree settings.
The stones shall bear the names of the sons of Israel, twelve according to their names, engraved like signets, one for each of the twelve tribes.
You shall make for the breastpiece chains of pure gold, twisted like cords.
You shall make two gold rings for the breastpiece and attach them to its two ends.
You shall fasten the two gold chains to the two rings at the ends of the breastpiece.
you shall fasten the other ends of the chains to the two settings, attaching them to the front shoulder pieces of the ephod.
You shall make two gold rings and put them on the two ends of the breastpiece on the edge that is toward the ephod.
You shall make two gold rings and attach them to the bottom of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod on its front, near its seam, above the waistband.
They shall bind the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that it rests on the waistband and does not swing loose from the ephod.
Aaron shall bear the names of the Israelites on the breastpiece of judgment over his heart when he enters the Holy Place, as a continual memorial before the the LORD.

You shall put the Urim and the Thummim in the breastpiece of judgment, and they shall be over Aaron’s heart when he goes before the the LORD. Thus Aaron shall bear the judgment of the Israelites over his heart before the the LORD continually. “
You shall make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue.
Its opening for the head shall be in the middle; it shall have a woven binding around the opening, like the opening of a coat of mail, so that it will not tear.
You shall make pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn around its hem, with gold bells between them.
A gold bell and a pomegranate shall alternate all around the hem of the robe.
It shall be on Aaron when he ministers, and its sound shall be heard when he enters the Holy Place before the the LORD and when he comes out, so that he will not die. “
You shall make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it, like the engraving of a signet, ‘Holy to the the LORD.’
You shall fasten it on a blue cord and put it on the turban; it shall be on the front of the turban.

It shall be on Aaron’s forehead, and Aaron shall bear the iniquity of the holy things that the Israelites consecrate, all their holy gifts. It shall be on his forehead continually, to make them acceptable before the the LORD.
You shall weave the tunic of fine linen, make the turban of fine linen, and make the sash with embroidered work. “
You shall make tunics, sashes, and caps for Aaron’s sons, for glory and for beauty.
You shall dress Aaron your brother and his sons with them; you shall anoint them, ordain them, and consecrate them, that they may serve Me as priests.
You shall make linen undergarments to cover their nakedness; they shall extend from the waist to the thighs.

Aaron and his sons shall wear them when they enter the tent of meeting or when they approach the altar to minister in the Holy Place, so that they do not incur guilt and die. It shall be a perpetual statute for him and for his offspring after him.”
Now this is what you are to do to consecrate them to serve Me as priests: Take a young bull and two rams without blemish,
along with unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil. Make them out of fine wheat flour,
put them in a basket, and present them in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.
Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water.
Take the garments and dress Aaron with the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod itself, and the breastpiece. Fasten the ephod on him with its woven waistband.
Put the turban on his head and attach the holy crown to the turban.
Then take the anointing oil, pour it on his head, and anoint him.
Bring his sons and dress them in tunics.
Wrap the sashes around them and put headbands on them. The priesthood shall be theirs by a permanent statute. In this way you are to ordain Aaron and his sons.
Bring the bull to the front of the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on the bull's head.
And you shall slaughter the bull before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
Take some of the bull's blood and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger; pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
Take all the fat that covers the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and both kidneys with the fat on them, and burn them on the altar.
But burn the bull's flesh, hide, and dung outside the camp; it is a sin offering.
Take one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.
Slaughter the ram and take its blood and sprinkle it on all sides of the altar.
Cut the ram into pieces, wash the entrails and legs, and place them with its head and other pieces.
Then burn the entire ram on the altar; it is a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
Take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head.

Slaughter the ram, take some of its blood, and put it on the right earlobes of Aaron and his sons, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Then sprinkle the blood on all sides of the altar.

And take some of the blood on the altar and some of the anointing oil and sprinkle them on Aaron and his garments, as well as on his sons and their garments. Then he and his garments will be consecrated, along with his sons and their garments.
Take the fat from the ram, the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver, both kidneys with the fat on them, and the right thigh (for it is a ram of ordination),
along with one loaf of bread, one cake of bread made with oil, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the LORD.
Put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons and wave them before the LORD as a wave offering.
Then take them from their hands and burn them on the altar atop the burnt offering as a pleasing aroma before the LORD; it is an offering made by fire to the LORD.
Take the breast of the ram of Aaron's ordination and wave it before the LORD as a wave offering, and it will be your portion.
Consecrate for Aaron and his sons the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the heave offering that is waved and presented from the ram of ordination.
This will belong to Aaron and his sons as a permanent portion from the Israelites, for it is the heave offering the Israelites are to make to the LORD from their peace offerings.
The holy garments that belong to Aaron will belong to his sons after him, so they can be anointed and ordained in them.
The son who succeeds him as priest and enters the Tent of Meeting to minister in the Holy Place must wear them for seven days.
Take the ram of ordination and boil its flesh in a holy place.
At the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, Aaron and his sons are to eat the meat of the ram and the bread that is in the basket.
They must eat those things by which atonement was made for their ordination and consecration. But no outsider may eat them, because they are holy.
If any of the meat of ordination or any of the bread is left until morning, you are to burn up the remainder. It must not be eaten, because it is holy.
Do for Aaron and his sons everything I have commanded you; ordain them for seven days.
Sacrifice a bull as a sin offering each day for atonement. Purify the altar by making atonement for it, and anoint it to consecrate it.
For seven days you are to make atonement for the altar and consecrate it. Then the altar will be most holy; whatever touches the altar will be holy.
This is what you are to offer regularly on the altar: two lambs that are a year old, each day, continually.
Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight.
With the first lamb offer a tenth of an ephah of fine flour, mixed with a quarter hin of oil from pressed olives, and a drink offering of a quarter hin of wine.
And offer the second lamb at twilight with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, as a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
For the generations to come, this burnt offering is to be made regularly at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting before the LORD, where I will meet with you to speak with you.
There I will meet with the Israelites, and the place will be consecrated by My glory.
So I will consecrate the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and I will consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests.
Then I will dwell among the Israelites and be their God.
And they will know that I am the LORD their God who brought them out of the land of Egypt, so that I might dwell among them. I am the LORD their God.
You shall make an altar for burning incense; make it of acacia wood.
It shall be square—one cubit long, one cubit wide, and two cubits high—with horns of one piece with it.
Overlay it with pure gold: its top, its sides all around, and its horns; and make a gold molding around it.
Make two gold rings for it beneath the molding on its two sides; place them on opposite sides to hold the poles for carrying it.
Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
Put the altar in front of the veil that covers the ark of the testimony, in front of the atonement cover over the testimony, where I will meet with you.
Aaron shall burn fragrant incense on it. Each morning, when he tends the lamps, he shall burn it;
and when he lights the lamps at twilight, he shall burn incense on it—a perpetual incense before the the LORD throughout your generations.
You shall not offer unauthorized incense on it, nor a burnt offering, nor a grain offering; and you shall not pour a drink offering on it.

Once a year Aaron shall make atonement on its horns; with the blood of the sin offering of atonement he shall make atonement for it once a year throughout your generations. It is most holy to the the LORD.
The The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

“When you take the census of the Israelites according to their number, each man shall give a ransom for his life to the the LORD when you number them, so that no plague may come upon them when you number them.
This is what everyone who is counted shall give: half a shekel by the sanctuary shekel—twenty gerahs to the shekel—half a shekel as an offering to the the LORD.
“Everyone who is counted, from twenty years old and upward, shall give the the LORD’s offering.
The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less, than the half shekel, when giving the the LORD’s offering to make atonement for your souls.

You shall take the atonement money from the Israelites and devote it to the service of the tent of meeting, so that it may be a memorial for the Israelites before the the LORD, to make atonement for your souls.”
The The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“You shall make a bronze basin with a bronze stand for washing. Put it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and feet from it.
When they enter the tent of meeting, or approach the altar to minister by burning an offering to the the LORD, they shall wash with water, so that they do not die.
They shall wash their hands and feet, so that they do not die. This shall be a perpetual statute for them and their descendants throughout their generations.”
The The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“You also take the finest spices: five hundred shekels of free-flowing myrrh, half as much—two hundred fifty shekels—of fragrant cinnamon, and two hundred fifty shekels of aromatic cane,
and five hundred shekels of cassia, by the sanctuary shekel, and a hin of olive oil.
Make from these a holy anointing oil, a fragrant blend, the work of a perfumer; it shall be a holy anointing oil.
With it anoint the tent of meeting and the ark of the testimony,
the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, and the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the basin with its stand.
Consecrate them, and they shall be most holy; whatever touches them shall become holy.
Anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them, that they may serve Me as priests.
Speak to the Israelites and say, ‘This shall be a holy anointing oil to Me throughout your generations.’
It shall not be poured on ordinary human flesh, and you shall not make any like it in composition; it is holy, and it shall be holy to you.
Whoever compounds any like it, or puts any of it on an unauthorized person, shall be cut off from his people.”
The The LORD said to Moses, “Take spices: stacte, onycha, and galbanum—spices—and pure frankincense; let there be an equal part of each.
Make it into incense, a perfume blended by the perfumer's art, salted, pure and holy.
Grind some of it to a very fine powder and put some of it before the testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you; it shall be most holy to you.
The incense that you make must not be made for your own use according to this formula; it is to be holy to you for the the LORD.
Anyone who makes anything like it to enjoy its fragrance shall be cut off from his people.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“See, I have called by name Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.
I have filled him with the Spirit of God—with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge—and with skill in every kind of craftsmanship,
to devise artistic designs, to work in gold, silver, and bronze,
to cut stones for settings and to carve wood, so that he may carry out every kind of work.

Moreover, I have appointed Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, to work with him, and I have placed skill in the hearts of all the skilled craftsmen, so that they may make everything I have commanded you:
the tent of meeting, the ark of the Testimony, the mercy seat that is on it, and all the furnishings of the tent;
the table and its utensils, the pure lampstand and all its utensils, and the altar of incense;
the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the basin with its stand;
the woven garments, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons for their priestly service;
and the anointing oil and the fragrant incense for the Holy Place. They shall make them according to all that I have commanded you.”
And the LORD said to Moses,

“You are to speak to the sons of Israel and say, ‘You must keep My Sabbaths, for they are a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, so that you may know that I am the LORD, who sanctifies you.
You must keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you; everyone who profanes it must surely be put to death, and whoever does any work on it shall be cut off from among his people.
Six days work may be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to the LORD; whoever does any work on the Sabbath day must surely be put to death.
So the sons of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, observing it throughout their generations as a perpetual covenant.
It is a sign between Me and the sons of Israel forever, because in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed.’”
When He had finished speaking with him on Mount Sinai, He gave Moses the two tablets of the Testimony—tablets of stone written with the finger of God.

When the people saw that Moses was delayed in coming down from the mountain, they gathered around Aaron and said, “Get up, make us gods who will go before us. As for this Moses, the man who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has become of him.”
Aaron said to them, “Take off the gold earrings that are in the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me.”
So all the people took off the gold earrings from their ears and brought them to Aaron.
He took the gold from their hands, fashioned it with an engraving tool, and made it into a molded calf. Then they said, “These are your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.”
When Aaron saw this, he built an altar before it and proclaimed, “Tomorrow is a festival to the LORD.”
They rose early the next day and offered burnt offerings and brought peace offerings. The people sat down to eat and drink, and then rose up to engage in reckless revelry.
The LORD said to Moses, “Go down, for your people, whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt, have acted corruptly.

They have turned aside quickly from the way I commanded them. They have made for themselves a molded calf, and have worshiped it and sacrificed to it, and said, ‘These are your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.’
I have seen this people, and indeed, they are an obstinate people.
Now leave Me alone, so that My anger may blaze against them and destroy them, and I will make you into a great nation.”
Moses implored the LORD his God, and said, “O the LORD, why does Your anger burn against Your people, whom You brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and a mighty hand?

Why should the Egyptians say, ‘He brought them out to do evil to them, to kill them in the mountains and to consume them from the face of the earth’? Turn from Your fierce anger, and relent concerning this disaster against Your people.

Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, Your servants, to whom You swore by Yourself, and said to them, ‘I will multiply your offspring as the stars of heaven, and I will give all this land that I have spoken of to your offspring, and they shall inherit it forever.’”
So the LORD relented from the disaster that He had threatened to bring on His people.
Moses turned and went down from the mountain, with the two tablets of the testimony in his hand, tablets that were written on both sides; they were written on one side and on the other.
The tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.
When Joshua heard the noise of the people shouting, he said to Moses, “There is a sound of war in the camp.”
Moses said, “It is not the sound of victory, nor the sound of defeat; I hear the sound of singing.”
As he came near the camp, he saw the calf and the dancing, and Moses’ anger burned, and he threw the tablets from his hands and broke them at the foot of the mountain.
He took the calf that they had made, burned it in the fire, ground it to powder, scattered it on the water, and made the Israelites drink it.
Moses said to Aaron, “What did this people do to you, that you have brought a great sin upon them?”
Aaron said, “Let not my lord’s anger burn; you know the people, that they are prone to evil.
For they said to me, ‘Make us gods who will go before us; as for this Moses, the man who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has become of him.’
I said to them, ‘Whoever has gold, let him take it off.’ So they gave it to me, and I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf.”
Moses saw that the people were running unrestrained, for Aaron had let them get out of control and become a laughingstock to their enemies.
Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, “Whoever is on the LORD’s side, come to me.” And all the sons of Levi gathered around him.

He said to them, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: ‘Let each man put his sword on his thigh; go back and forth through the camp from gate to gate, and kill his brother, his friend, and his neighbor.’”
The sons of Levi did as Moses had said, and about three thousand men of the people fell that day.
Moses said, “Today you have consecrated yourselves to the LORD, because each of you has been against his son and his brother, and He has bestowed a blessing on you today.”
The next day Moses said to the people, “You have committed a great sin. Now I will go up to the LORD; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin.”
Moses returned to the LORD and said, “Alas, this people has sinned a great sin and has made for themselves gods of gold.
But now, if You will forgive their sin—but if not, please blot me out of Your book that You have written.”
The LORD said to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against Me, I will blot out of My book.
But now go, lead the people to the place about which I have spoken to you. Indeed, My angel will go before you. But on the day I punish, I will punish them for their sin.”
The LORD struck the people with a plague, because of what they did with the calf that Aaron had made.

Then the LORD spoke to Moses: “Go up from here, you and the people whom you brought up from the land of Egypt, to the land that I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, ‘I will give it to your descendants.’
I will send an angel before you, and I will drive out the Canaanites, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
A land flowing with milk and honey; for I will not go up among you, because you are a stubborn people, lest I destroy you on the way.”
When the people heard this harsh message, they mourned, and no one wore his ornaments.

The LORD said to Moses, “Say to the sons of Israel, ‘You are a stubborn people; should I go up among you for even a moment, I would destroy you. So now take off your ornaments, that I may know what I will do to you.’”
So the sons of Israel stripped off their ornaments from Mount Horeb onward.

Now Moses took the tent and pitched it outside the camp, far from the camp, and called it the tent of meeting. Everyone who sought the LORD would go out to the tent of meeting, which was outside the camp.
Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would rise and stand, each at the entrance of his tent, and watch Moses until he entered the tent.
Whenever Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would descend and stand at the entrance of the tent, and the LORD would speak with Moses.
When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, they would rise and worship, each at the entrance of his tent.
Thus the LORD used to speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his assistant Joshua son of Nun, a young man, would not leave the tent.

Then Moses said to the LORD, “See, You say to me, ‘Bring up this people,’ but You have not let me know whom You will send with me. Yet You have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have also found favor in My sight.’
Now, if I have found favor in Your sight, please teach me Your ways, so that I may know You and find favor in Your sight. Consider too that this nation is Your people.”
He said, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”
Then Moses said to Him, “If Your Presence does not go with us, do not bring us up from here.

For how then will it be known that I have found favor in Your sight—I and Your people? Is it not by Your going with us, so that we are distinguished from all the other people on the face of the earth?”
The LORD said to Moses, “I will do this thing that you have spoken, for you have found favor in My sight, and I know you by name.”
Then Moses said, “Please show me Your glory!”

He said, “I Myself will make all My goodness pass before you, and I will proclaim the name of the LORD before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will show compassion to whom I will show compassion.”
He said, “You cannot see My face, for no one can see Me and live.”
Then the LORD said, “Look, there is a place beside Me, and you are to stand on the rock.
While My glory passes by, I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with My hand until I have passed by.
Then I will take away My hand, and you shall see My back, but My face shall not be seen.”
The LORD said to Moses, “Chisel out two stone tablets like the first ones, and I will write on them the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.
Be ready by morning, and come up in the morning to Mount Sinai; present yourself to Me on the summit.
No one may come up with you, and no one may be seen anywhere on the mountain; not even flocks or herds may graze in front of that mountain.”
So Moses chiseled out two stone tablets like the first ones. He rose early in the morning and ascended Mount Sinai, as the the LORD had commanded him, carrying the two tablets in his hand.
Then the the LORD descended in the cloud, stood with him there, and proclaimed the name of the the LORD.
As the the LORD passed before him, He proclaimed, “The the LORD, the the LORD, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness,

maintaining steadfast love for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin, yet He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished, visiting the iniquity of fathers upon children and grandchildren, to the third and fourth generation.”
Moses quickly bowed his head to the ground and worshiped.
Then Moses said, “If I have found favor in your sight, O Lord, please let the Lord go among us. Although this is a stubborn people, pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us as your inheritance.”

He said, “Behold, I am making a covenant. Before all your people I will do marvels, such as have not been created in all the earth or in any nation. All the people among whom you are shall see the work of the the LORD, for it is an awe-inspiring thing that I am doing with you.
Observe what I command you this day. Behold, I will drive out before you the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
Take care, lest you make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land to which you go, lest it become a snare in your midst.“
You shall tear down their altars, break their pillars, and cut down their Asherah poles.
For you shall worship no other god, for the the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.

Lest you make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, and when they turn away in unfaithfulness to their gods and sacrifice to their gods, and one of them invites you, you eat from his sacrifice.
And lest you take their daughters for your sons, and their daughters turn away in unfaithfulness to their gods and lead your sons into the same unfaithfulness.
You shall not make for yourself any gods of cast metal.“

You shall keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in the month of Abib you came out of Egypt.
All that first opens the womb is Mine—all your male livestock, the firstborn of ox and sheep.

You shall redeem the firstborn of a donkey with a lamb, or if you do not redeem it, you shall break its neck. You shall redeem all the firstborn of your sons. No one shall appear before Me empty-handed.
Six days you shall work, but on the seventh day you shall rest; even in plowing time and harvest you shall rest.“
You shall observe the Feast of Weeks with the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the Feast of Ingathering at the year's end.
Three times a year all your males shall appear before the Lord, the the LORD, the God of Israel.
For I will drive out nations before you and enlarge your borders, and no one shall covet your land when you go up to appear before the the LORD your God three times in the year.
You shall not offer the blood of My sacrifice with anything leavened, nor shall the Passover sacrifice remain until morning.
You shall bring the best of the firstfruits of your ground to the house of the the LORD your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.”
Then the the LORD said to Moses, “Write these words down, for according to them I have made a covenant with you and with Israel.”
So Moses was there with the the LORD forty days and forty nights. He ate no bread and drank no water, and he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments.
When Moses came down from Mount Sinai, with the two tablets of the testimony in his hand as he descended, he did not know that the skin of his face shone because he had been speaking with God.
When Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, the skin of his face shone, and they were afraid to approach him.
But Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the leaders of the congregation returned to him, and Moses spoke with them.
Afterward all the Israelites came near, and he commanded them everything the the LORD had spoken with him on Mount Sinai.
When Moses had finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face.
But whenever Moses went in before the the LORD to speak with Him, he removed the veil until he came out. Then, upon coming out, he would tell the Israelites what he had been commanded.
The Israelites would see that the skin of Moses' face shone, and Moses would put the veil back over his face until he went in to speak with the the LORD.
Moses assembled the whole congregation of the Israelites and said to them, “These are the words that the LORD has commanded to be done.
For six days, work may be done, but the seventh day shall be holy to you—a Sabbath of complete rest to the LORD. Anyone who does work on it must be put to death.
Do not kindle a fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day.
Moses said to the whole congregation of the Israelites, “This is what the LORD has commanded:
Take from among you an offering to the LORD. Everyone whose heart is willing shall bring an offering to the LORD—gold, silver, and bronze;
blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen and goats’ hair;
rams’ skins dyed red and fine leather; acacia wood;
oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
and onyx stones and other gems to be set in the ephod and the breastpiece. “
Let every skilled person among you come and make all that the LORD has commanded:
the tabernacle, its tent and its covering, its clasps, its frames, its bars, its pillars, and its bases;
the ark with its poles, the mercy seat, and the veil that screens it;
the table with its poles and all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
the lampstand for the light, with its utensils and its lamps, and the oil for the light;
the altar of incense with its poles, the anointing oil and the fragrant incense, and the screen for the entrance of the tabernacle;
the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grating, its poles, and all its utensils; the basin and its stand;
the hangings of the court, its pillars and bases, and the screen for the gate of the court;
the pegs of the tabernacle and the court, and their cords;
and the woven garments for ministering in the Holy Place—the garments of Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons for their priestly service.”
Then the whole congregation of the Israelites withdrew from Moses’ presence.
Everyone whose heart stirred him and everyone whose spirit moved him came and brought an offering to the LORD for the work of the tent of meeting, for all its service, and for the holy garments.
Men and women alike came, bringing brooches, earrings, signet rings, and bracelets—every gold article—and everyone who could presented an offering of gold to the LORD.
Everyone who had blue, purple, or scarlet yarn, fine linen, goats’ hair, rams’ skins dyed red, or fine leather brought them.
Everyone who could contribute silver or bronze brought an offering to the LORD, and everyone who had acacia wood for any work brought it.
Every woman who was skilled spun with her hands and brought what she had spun—blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
All the women whose hearts were stirred by skill spun the goats’ hair.
The leaders brought onyx stones and other gems for setting in the ephod and the breastpiece,
as well as spices and oil for the light, for the anointing oil, and for the fragrant incense.
Thus all the Israelite men and women whose hearts were moved brought a freewill offering to the LORD for all the work that the LORD had commanded through Moses to be done.
Moses said to the Israelites, “See, the LORD has called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
He has filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge, and with every kind of craftsmanship,
to devise artistic designs and to work in gold, silver, and bronze;
to cut and set stones, to carve wood, and to execute every kind of artistic work.
He has also given him and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, the ability to teach others.
He has filled them with skill to perform every kind of work—engraving, designing, embroidering in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen, and weaving—and to execute every design.”

Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled person in whom the LORD had placed skill and understanding to know how to do all the work for the service of the sanctuary were to carry out everything the LORD had commanded.
Moses summoned Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled person whose heart the LORD had stirred—everyone whose heart moved him to come and do the work.
They received from Moses all the contributions the Israelites had brought for constructing the sanctuary. Moreover, the people continued to bring freewill offerings to him morning after morning.
All the skilled workers engaged in the sanctuary work came, each leaving his own task,
and said to Moses, “The people are bringing far more than enough for the work the LORD commanded us to perform.”

So Moses issued a command, and a proclamation was circulated throughout the camp: “Let no man or woman do any further work for the sanctuary offering.” Thus the people were restrained from bringing more.
For the materials they had were sufficient for all the work, and more than enough.
All the skilled workers among those doing the work made the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twisted linen, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, with cherubim skillfully worked into them.
Each curtain was twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide; all the curtains were the same size.
He joined five curtains to one another, and the other five curtains he joined to one another.
He made loops of blue yarn on the edge of the outermost curtain in the first set, and he made the same on the edge of the outermost curtain in the second set.
He made fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain in the second set, with the loops opposite one another.
He made fifty gold clasps and joined the curtains to one another with them, so that the tabernacle became a single unit.
He made curtains of goats’ hair for a tent over the tabernacle; he made eleven of them.
Each curtain was thirty cubits long and four cubits wide; the eleven curtains were all the same size.
He joined five curtains by themselves and the remaining six by themselves.
He made fifty loops on the edge of the outermost curtain in the first set and fifty loops on the edge of the corresponding curtain in the second set.
He made fifty bronze clasps to join the tent together, so that it would be one piece.
He made a covering for the tent of rams’ skins dyed red, and a covering of fine leather above it.
He made upright boards of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
Each board was ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
Each board had two tenons, fitted to one another; he made them this way for all the boards of the tabernacle.
He made twenty boards for the south side of the tabernacle.
He made forty silver sockets under the twenty boards—two sockets under one board for its two tenons, and two sockets under the next board for its two tenons.
For the second side of the tabernacle, on the north, he made twenty boards.
He also made their forty silver sockets, two under one board and two under the next.
For the rear of the tabernacle, on the west, he made six boards.
He made two boards for the corners of the tabernacle at the rear.
They were doubled beneath and joined together at the top into a single ring; he made both corners this way.
There were eight boards with sixteen silver sockets, two sockets under each board.
He made five bars of acacia wood for the boards on one side of the tabernacle.
He made five bars for the other side and five for the boards at the rear on the west.
He made the middle bar to run through the boards from end to end.
He overlaid the boards with gold and made gold rings to hold the bars, and he overlaid the bars with gold.
He made the veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, with cherubim skillfully worked into it.
He made four pillars of acacia wood for it and overlaid them with gold; their hooks were gold, and he cast four silver bases for them.
He made a screen for the entrance to the tent of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer.
He made its five pillars with their hooks, overlaid their tops and their bands with gold, and made their five bases of bronze.
Bezalel fashioned the ark from acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
He overlaid it with pure gold, both inside and outside, and he fashioned a gold molding around it.
He cast four gold rings for it—two on one side and two on the other.
He made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
Then he inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark so that it could be carried.
He fashioned the atonement cover of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
He made two cherubim of hammered gold at the ends of the atonement cover.
One cherub stood at one end and the other at the opposite end, all hammered from the same piece as the atonement cover.
The cherubim spread their wings upward, overshadowing the atonement cover; their faces were turned toward each other and toward the atonement cover.
He made the table of acacia wood, two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
He overlaid it with pure gold and fashioned a gold molding around it.
He made a rim around it a handbreadth wide and put a gold molding on the rim.
He cast four gold rings for it and attached them to the four corners at its four legs.
The rings were placed close to the rim to serve as holders for the poles used to carry the table.
He made the poles of acacia wood for carrying the table and overlaid them with gold.
He also made the utensils for the table—its plates, dishes, bowls, and pitchers for pouring drink offerings—out of pure gold.
Then he made the lampstand of pure gold, hammered out of one piece. Its base, shaft, branches, bowls, buds, and petals were all one piece.
Six branches extended from its sides, three on one side and three on the other.
Three cups shaped like almond blossoms, with buds and petals, were on one branch, three on the next, and so on for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
On the lampstand itself were four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with buds and petals.
A bud was under the first pair of branches extending from the lampstand, a bud under the second pair, and a bud under the third pair.
The buds and branches were all one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.
