He also made its seven lamps, wick trimmers, and trays of pure gold.
He made the lampstand and all its utensils from a talent of pure gold.
He made the altar of incense out of acacia wood. It was square, a cubit long and a cubit wide, and two cubits high, and its horns were of one piece with it.
He overlaid it with pure gold—its top, all around its sides, and its horns—and he made a gold molding around it.
He made two gold rings beneath the molding on opposite sides to hold the poles for carrying it.
He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
He also made the holy anointing oil and the pure, fragrant incense, the work of a perfumer.
Bezalel constructed the altar of burnt offering from acacia wood, fashioning it square—five cubits in length, five cubits in width, and three cubits in height.
He fashioned a horn at each of its four corners, integrating the horns with the altar itself, and he overlaid the whole with bronze.
He made all the altar’s utensils—the pots, shovels, sprinkling bowls, meat forks, and firepans—and he made all of them from bronze.
He fashioned a bronze grating for the altar, a network of bronze, to be situated beneath its ledge and to extend halfway up the altar.
He cast four rings for the four corners of the bronze grating, to receive the poles.
He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze.
He then inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar, so that it could be carried, and he made the altar hollow, constructing it from boards.
He made the bronze basin and its bronze stand from the mirrors of the women who ministered at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
Then he constructed the courtyard. The south side measured a hundred cubits in length and was furnished with curtains of finely twisted linen.
It had twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, with silver hooks and bands upon the posts.
The north side was likewise a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and with silver hooks and bands upon the posts.
The west side measured fifty cubits and had ten posts and ten bases, with silver hooks and bands upon the posts.
The east side, toward the sunrise, measured fifty cubits.
On one side of the entrance were curtains fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases,
and on the other side were curtains fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases.
All the curtains surrounding the courtyard were of finely twisted linen.
The bases for the posts were bronze; the hooks and bands of the posts were silver; and the overlay of the tops of the posts was silver, so that all the posts of the courtyard were banded with silver.

The curtain for the entrance to the courtyard was embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and with finely twisted linen; it was twenty cubits long and, like the curtains of the courtyard, five cubits high.
It had four posts and four bronze bases; their hooks were silver, as were the bands and the overlay of their tops.
All the tent pegs for the tabernacle and the surrounding courtyard were bronze.
This is the inventory of the tabernacle—the tabernacle of the Testimony—as recorded at Moses’ command by the Levites under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made everything that the LORD had commanded Moses.
With him was Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, a craftsman, designer, and embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and in fine linen.
All the gold that was employed in the work—in all the work of the sanctuary, the gold of the wave offering—amounted to twenty-nine talents and 730 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
The silver from those numbered in the congregation was 100 talents and 1,775 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel—
a beka per person, that is, half a shekel, according to the sanctuary shekel, from every man twenty years of age or older who was enrolled in the census: 603,550 men.
The hundred talents of silver were cast into the bases of the sanctuary and the bases of the veil: a hundred bases from the hundred talents, one talent for each base.
From the 1,775 shekels he made hooks for the posts, overlaid their tops, and made bands for them.
The bronze from the wave offering was 70 talents and 2,400 shekels.
With it he made the bases for the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, the bronze altar and its bronze grating, and all the utensils for the altar,
as well as the bases for the surrounding courtyard, the bases for the courtyard entrance, and all the tent pegs for the tabernacle and the surrounding courtyard.

From the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, the artisans fashioned woven garments for ministering in the sanctuary, and they also fashioned the holy garments for Aaron, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He fashioned the ephod from gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and from finely spun linen.
They hammered the gold into thin sheets and cut threads from them, weaving those threads into the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and the fine linen—a work of consummate craftsmanship.
They fashioned shoulder pieces for the ephod, joined at its two ends, so that it could be fastened.

The skillfully woven waistband of the ephod was of one piece with it, fashioned from the same materials—gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen—just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They mounted the onyx stones in gold filigree settings, engraved like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel.
Then they fastened them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He fashioned the breastpiece with the same craftsmanship as the ephod—of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen.
It was square when folded, a span in length and a span in width.
They mounted four rows of gemstones upon it: the first row held carnelian, chrysolite, and emerald;
the second row, turquoise, sapphire, and diamond;
the third row, jacinth, agate, and amethyst;
and the fourth row, beryl, onyx, and jasper. They set each stone in gold filigree.
The stones corresponded to the names of the sons of Israel—twelve in all—each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
For the breastpiece they fashioned braided chains of pure gold, like cords.
They also made two gold settings and two gold rings, fastening the rings to the two corners of the breastpiece.
Then they attached the two gold chains to the rings at the corners of the breastpiece,
and they secured the other ends of the chains to the two settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
They made two additional gold rings and attached them to the two lower corners of the breastpiece, on the inner edge adjacent to the ephod.
They fashioned two more gold rings and attached them to the bottom of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, on the front, near the seam just above the woven band of the ephod.

Then they laced the rings of the breastpiece to the rings of the ephod with a cord of blue yarn, so that the breastpiece rested above the waistband of the ephod and would not swing away from it, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They fashioned the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth, the work of a weaver,
with an opening in its center like the opening of a garment, and a collar around the opening so that it would not tear.
They fashioned pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely spun linen around the lower hem of the robe.
They also made bells of pure gold and attached them around the lower hem of the robe, between the pomegranates,
alternating a bell and a pomegranate all around the lower hem of the robe to be worn for ministry, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They fashioned tunics of fine linen, woven work, for Aaron and his sons,
the turban of fine linen, the ornate headbands of fine linen, and the undergarments of finely spun linen.
And the sash of finely spun linen, embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, was of woven work, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They fashioned the plate of the holy crown from pure gold and engraved upon it, like an inscription on a seal: HOLY TO the LORD.
Then they fastened to it a blue cord to mount it on the turban above, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Thus all the work on the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, was completed. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then they brought the tabernacle to Moses: the tent with all its furnishings, its clasps, its frames, its crossbars, its posts, and its bases;
the covering of ram skins dyed red, the covering of fine leather, and the veil;
the ark of the Testimony with its poles and the mercy seat;
the table with all its utensils and the Bread of the Presence;
the pure gold lampstand with its lamps, its wick trimmers, and all its utensils, as well as the oil for the light;
the gold altar, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the curtain for the entrance to the tent;
the bronze altar with its bronze grating, its poles, and all its utensils; the basin with its stand;

the curtains of the courtyard with its posts and bases; the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard; its ropes and tent pegs; and all the equipment for the service of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting;
the woven garments for ministering in the sanctuary; the holy garments for Aaron the priest; and the garments for his sons to serve as priests.
The Israelites had done all the work just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
And Moses inspected all the work and saw that they had done it just as the LORD had commanded. So Moses blessed them.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"On the first day of the first month, you are to set up the tabernacle, the tent of meeting.
Put the ark of the Testimony there, and screen it with the curtain.
Bring in the table and arrange its setting; bring in the lampstand and mount its lamps.
Place the gold altar of incense before the ark of the Testimony, and put the entrance curtain on the tabernacle.
Place the altar of burnt offering before the entrance of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.
Place the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
Set up the courtyard all around, and put the screen at the gate of the courtyard.
Take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it; consecrate it and all its vessels, so that it may be holy.
Anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its vessels, and consecrate the altar, so that it becomes most holy.
Anoint the basin and its stand, and consecrate it.
Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water.
Clothe Aaron with the holy garments, anoint him, and consecrate him, so that he may serve Me as priest.
Bring his sons near and clothe them with tunics.
Anoint them as you anointed their father, so that they may serve Me as priests; their anointing will confer on them a perpetual priesthood throughout their generations."
Moses did exactly as the LORD had commanded him.
In the first month of the second year, on the first day of the month, the tabernacle was set up.
Moses erected the tabernacle: he laid its bases, set up its frames, inserted its bars, and raised its pillars.
He spread the tent over the tabernacle and placed the covering of the tent over it from above, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He took the Testimony and placed it in the ark; he set the poles on the ark and put the atonement cover on top of the ark.
He brought the ark into the tabernacle, set up the veil of the covering, and screened the ark of the Testimony, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put the table in the tent of meeting on the north side of the tabernacle, outside the veil.
He arranged the bread on it in its proper order before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put the lampstand in the tent of meeting, opposite the table, on the south side of the tabernacle.
He set up the lamps before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put the gold altar in the tent of meeting before the veil.
He burned fragrant incense on it, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put the curtain at the entrance of the tabernacle.
He set the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting and offered on it the burnt offering and the grain offering, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He set the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar and put water in it for washing.
Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and feet from it.
Whenever they entered the tent of meeting or approached the altar, they washed, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He set up the courtyard all around the tabernacle and the altar and put the screen at the gate of the courtyard. So Moses completed the work.
Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
Moses could not enter the tent of meeting, because the cloud had settled on it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
Whenever the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the Israelites set out on all their journeys.
But if the cloud was not taken up, they did not set out until the day it was taken up.
For the cloud of the LORD was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in it by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys.
The LORD summoned Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and say to them: ‘When any of you brings an offering to the the LORD, you may bring your offering of livestock from the herd or the flock.
“‘If his offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he must present an unblemished male. He shall bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting, so that he may be accepted before the the LORD.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it will be accepted on his behalf to make atonement for him.
“‘He shall slaughter the young bull before the the LORD, and Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall present the blood and sprinkle it all around the altar at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
He shall skin the burnt offering and cut it into pieces.
The sons of Aaron the priest shall kindle a fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.
Then Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall arrange the pieces—including the head and the fat—on the burning wood that is on the altar.
He shall wash the entrails and the legs with water, and the priest shall burn all of it on the altar as a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the the LORD.
“‘If, however, his offering is a burnt offering from the flock—whether from the sheep or the goats—he must present an unblemished male.
He shall slaughter it on the north side of the altar before the the LORD, and Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall sprinkle its blood on all sides of the altar.
He shall cut it into pieces, and the priest shall arrange them—including the head and the fat—on the burning wood that is on the altar.
He shall wash the entrails and the legs with water, and the priest shall bring all of it and burn it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the the LORD.
“‘If his offering to the the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, he must present either a turtledove or a young pigeon.
The priest shall bring it to the altar, wring off its head, and burn it on the altar; its blood shall be drained out on the side of the altar.
He shall remove its crop with its feathers and throw it to the east side of the altar, to the place for ashes.

He shall tear it open by its wings without severing it completely, and the priest shall burn it on the altar, on the wood that is on the fire. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the the LORD.’”
When anyone brings a grain offering to the LORD, the offering must consist of fine flour; he is to pour oil upon it and put frankincense upon it.

He shall bring it to Aaron's sons, the priests, and the priest shall take a handful of the fine flour and oil, together with all the frankincense, and burn this memorial portion on the altar as an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
What remains of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy portion of the offerings made by fire to the LORD.
If you bring a grain offering baked in an oven, it shall be unleavened cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers spread with oil.
If your offering is a grain offering on a griddle, it shall be fine flour, unleavened and mixed with oil.
You shall break it into pieces and pour oil on it; it is a grain offering.
If your offering is a grain offering cooked in a pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
You shall bring the grain offering made of these to the LORD, and it shall be presented to the priest, who shall bring it to the altar.
The priest shall take from the grain offering its memorial portion and burn it on the altar as an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
What remains of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy portion of the offerings made by fire to the LORD.
No grain offering that you bring to the LORD shall be made with leaven, for you shall burn no leaven nor any honey as an offering by fire to the LORD.
As an offering of firstfruits you may bring them to the LORD, but they shall not be offered on the altar for a pleasing aroma.
You shall season all your grain offerings with salt; you shall not let the salt of the covenant of your God be missing from your grain offering; with all your offerings you shall offer salt.
If you offer a grain offering of firstfruits to the LORD, you shall offer for the grain offering of your firstfruits crushed heads of new grain roasted in the fire.
You shall put oil on it and lay frankincense on it; it is a grain offering.
The priest shall burn as its memorial portion some of the crushed grain and some of the oil, with all its frankincense, as an offering made by fire to the LORD.
If his offering is a sacrifice of peace offerings, and he brings an animal from the herd—whether male or female—he must present it without blemish before the LORD.
He shall lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting; then Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall sprinkle the blood all around the altar.
From the sacrifice of peace offerings he shall present an offering made by fire to the LORD: the fat that covers the entrails, together with all the fat that is on the entrails.
He shall also remove the two kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the fatty lobe attached to the liver, removing it together with the kidneys.
Aaron’s sons shall burn these on the altar on top of the burnt offering that lies on the wood over the fire, as an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
If his offering for a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD is from the flock, he must present a male or female without blemish.
If he presents a lamb as his offering, he must bring it before the LORD.
He shall lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it in front of the Tent of Meeting; then Aaron’s sons shall sprinkle its blood all around the altar.

From the peace offering he shall present an offering made by fire to the LORD: its fat, the entire fat tail cut off close to the backbone, the fat that covers the entrails, and all the fat that is on the entrails.
He shall also remove the two kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, removing it together with the kidneys.
The priest shall burn them on the altar as food, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
If his offering is a goat, he must present it before the LORD.
He must lay his hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the Tent of Meeting; then Aaron’s sons shall sprinkle its blood all around the altar.
From his offering he shall present an offering made by fire to the LORD: the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
the two kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he shall remove with the kidneys.
The priest shall burn them on the altar as food, an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma. All the fat belongs to the LORD.
This is a permanent statute for your generations, in all your dwellings: You must not eat any fat or any blood.
Then the LORD said to Moses,
“Speak to the Israelites and say, ‘When anyone sins unintentionally and does what is forbidden in any of the the LORD’s commands—’”
If the anointed priest sins, bringing guilt upon the people, he must bring to the the LORD a young bull without blemish as a sin offering for the sin he has committed.
He is to bring the bull to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting before the the LORD, lay his hand on its head, and slaughter it before the the LORD.
Then the anointed priest shall take some of the bull’s blood and bring it into the Tent of Meeting.
The priest is to dip his finger into the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the the LORD, in front of the veil of the sanctuary.

The priest shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense before the the LORD in the Tent of Meeting, and he shall pour out the rest of the bull’s blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
Then he shall remove all the fat from the bull of the sin offering—the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on them—
both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he shall remove with the kidneys.
Just as the fat is removed from the ox of the peace offering, the priest shall burn them on the altar of burnt offering.
But the hide of the bull and all its flesh, along with its head and legs, its entrails and dung—

all the rest of the bull—he must carry outside the camp to a ceremonially clean place where the ashes are poured out, and there he must burn it on a wood fire; it is to be burned where the ashes are poured out.

If the whole congregation of Israel strays unintentionally and the matter escapes the notice of the assembly so that they violate any of the the LORD’s commandments and incur guilt by doing what is forbidden,
then the assembly must bring a young bull as a sin offering. They are to bring it before the Tent of Meeting.
The elders of the congregation are to lay their hands on the bull’s head before the the LORD, and it shall be slaughtered before the the LORD.
Then the anointed priest shall bring some of the bull’s blood into the Tent of Meeting.
The priest is to dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the the LORD in front of the veil.

He is to put some of the blood on the horns of the altar before the the LORD in the Tent of Meeting, and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
Then he shall remove all the fat from it and burn it on the altar.
He shall do with this bull just as he did with the bull of the sin offering; in this way the priest will make atonement for them, and they will be forgiven.
Then he must carry the bull outside the camp and burn it, just as he burned the first bull. It is a sin offering for the assembly.
When a leader sins unintentionally and does what is forbidden in any of the commandments of the the LORD his God, he incurs guilt.
When he becomes aware of the sin he has committed, he must bring an unblemished male goat as his offering.
He is to lay his hand on the goat’s head and slaughter it at the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered before the the LORD. It is a sin offering.
Then the priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
He shall burn all the fat on the altar, like the fat of the peace offering. Thus the priest will make atonement for the man’s sin, and he will be forgiven.
If one of the common people sins unintentionally and does what is forbidden in any of the the LORD’s commands, he incurs guilt.
When he becomes aware of the sin he has committed, he must bring an unblemished female goat as his offering for the sin he has committed.
He is to lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it at the place of the burnt offering.
Then the priest is to take some of its blood with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.

He shall remove all the fat, just as the fat is removed from the peace offering, and the priest shall burn it on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the the LORD. In this way the priest will make atonement for him, and he will be forgiven.
If he brings a lamb as his sin offering, he must bring an unblemished female.
He is to lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it for a sin offering at the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
Then the priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.

He shall remove all the fat, just as the fat of the lamb is removed from the peace offering, and he shall burn it on the altar along with the offerings made by fire to the the LORD. Thus the priest will make atonement for him concerning the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven.
When a person sins by failing to testify after hearing a sworn summons, though he is a witness who saw or knew something, he shall bear his guilt.

Or if a person touches anything ceremonially unclean—whether the carcass of an unclean wild animal, an unclean domestic animal, or an unclean creeping thing—and is unaware of it, he is unclean and guilty.
Or if he touches human uncleanness of any kind by which a person becomes unclean, and is unaware of it, he is guilty once he realizes it.
Or if a person swears thoughtlessly with his lips to do good or evil—whatever a man may utter in an oath—and is unaware of it, he is guilty in any of these matters once he realizes it.
When he is guilty in any of these matters, he must confess the sin he has committed.
He must bring his guilt offering to the LORD for the sin he has committed: a female lamb or goat from the flock as a sin offering. Then the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin.
If he cannot afford a lamb, he shall bring to the LORD two turtledoves or two young pigeons—one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering.
He shall bring them to the priest, who shall first present the one for the sin offering; he shall wring its head at the front of its neck without severing it.
Then he shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering against the side of the altar, and the rest of the blood shall be drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.
The second bird he shall prepare as a burnt offering according to the ordinance. Thus the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he shall be forgiven.

But if he cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he shall bring as his offering for the sin he has committed a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. He shall not put oil on it or place frankincense on it, because it is a sin offering.
He shall bring it to the priest, and the priest shall take a handful of it as a memorial portion and burn it on the altar on top of the offerings made by fire to the LORD. It is a sin offering.
In this way the priest shall make atonement for him for any of these sins he has committed, and he shall be forgiven. The remainder shall belong to the priest, as with the grain offering.
Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying, “

If a person acts unfaithfully and sins unintentionally against the LORD’s holy things, he shall bring his guilt offering to the LORD: an unblemished ram from the flock, valued in silver shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, as a guilt offering.

He must make restitution for the holy thing in which he sinned, adding a fifth to its value, and give it to the priest. Then the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and he shall be forgiven.”
If a person sins and does any of the things the LORD has commanded not to be done, though he does not know it, he is guilty and bears his guilt.

He shall bring to the priest a ram without blemish from the flock, of proper value, as a guilt offering. Then the priest shall make atonement for him for the error he committed unintentionally, and he shall be forgiven.
It is a guilt offering; he has indeed been guilty before the LORD.
“If a person sins and acts unfaithfully against the LORD by deceiving a neighbor about a deposit, a pledge, stolen property, or by defrauding him;
or if he finds something lost and lies about it, swearing falsely in any matter of this kind by which a person sins—
then, once he has sinned and incurred guilt, he must restore what he stole or extorted, the deposit entrusted to him, or the lost property he found.
He must make full restitution, add a fifth of its value, and deliver it to the rightful owner on the day he presents his guilt offering.
He must also bring his guilt offering to the LORD: a ram without blemish from the flock, valued according to your estimate, as a guilt offering.
In this way the priest will make atonement for him before the LORD, and he will be forgiven for whatever he did that made him guilty.”

“Command Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the burnt offering. The burnt offering itself is to remain on the hearth of the altar all night until morning, and the fire on the altar must be kept burning.
The priest is to put on his linen robe and linen undergarments, remove the ashes to which the fire has reduced the burnt offering on the altar, and place them beside the altar.
Then he must remove those garments, put on others, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a ceremonially clean place.

The fire on the altar must be kept burning and never allowed to go out; each morning the priest must burn wood on it, arrange the burnt offering upon it, and burn on it the fat of the peace offerings.
The fire must be kept burning on the altar continually; it must not go out.
These are the regulations for the grain offering: Aaron's sons are to present it before the LORD in front of the altar.

One of them shall take a handful of the fine flour and oil of the grain offering, together with all the frankincense on it, and burn this memorial portion on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
Aaron and his sons are to eat the remainder; it must be eaten as unleavened bread in a holy place, in the court of the tent of meeting.
It must not be baked with leaven. I have given it as their portion of My food offerings; it is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
Every male among Aaron's descendants may eat it. It is a permanent statute throughout your generations from the LORD's food offerings. Whatever touches them will become holy.”

“This is the offering Aaron and his sons must present to the LORD on the day he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a perpetual grain offering, half in the morning and half in the evening.
It is to be prepared with oil on a griddle; you are to bring it well mixed and present the grain offering as baked pieces, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
The priest anointed to succeed him from among his sons shall prepare it. It is a permanent statute to the LORD; it must be entirely burned.
Every grain offering of a priest must be entirely burned; it must not be eaten.”
“Speak to Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the sin offering. The sin offering is to be slaughtered before the LORD in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered; it is most holy.
The priest who offers it for sin shall eat it; it is to be eaten as something holy in the court of the tent of meeting.
Anything that touches its flesh will become holy, and if any of its blood is sprinkled on a garment, you must wash that garment in a holy place.
The earthen vessel in which it is boiled must be broken, and if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, that vessel must be scoured and rinsed with water.
Every male among the priests may eat it; it is most holy.
But no sin offering whose blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the holy place may be eaten; it must be burned with fire.”
Now this is the law of the guilt offering, which is most holy:
the guilt offering must be slaughtered in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, and its blood must be sprinkled on all sides of the altar.
All its fat is to be offered—the fat tail and the fat that covers the entrails—
along with both kidneys and the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys.
The priest shall burn them on the altar as an offering made by fire to the the LORD; it is a guilt offering.
Every male among the priests may eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place; it is most holy.
The guilt offering is like the sin offering; one law applies to both. The priest who makes atonement with it shall have it.
As for the priest who presents a man's burnt offering, the hide of that burnt offering belongs to him.
Likewise, every grain offering baked in an oven or prepared in a pan or on a griddle belongs to the priest who presents it.
And every grain offering, whether dry or mixed with oil, belongs equally to all the sons of Aaron.
Now this is the law of the peace offering that one may present to the the LORD:

If he offers it in thanksgiving, then along with the sacrifice of thanksgiving he shall offer unleavened cakes mixed with oil, unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and well-kneaded cakes of fine flour mixed with oil.
Along with his peace offering of thanksgiving, he is to present an offering with cakes of leavened bread.
From the cakes he shall present one portion of each offering as a contribution to the the LORD. It belongs to the priest who sprinkles the blood of the peace offerings.
The meat of the sacrifice of his peace offering of thanksgiving must be eaten on the day he offers it; none of it may be left until morning.
If, however, the sacrifice he offers is a vow or a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day he presents his sacrifice, but what is left over may be eaten on the next day.
But any meat of the sacrifice remaining until the third day must be burned up.

If any of the meat of his peace offering is eaten on the third day, it will not be accepted. It will not be credited to the one who presented it; it shall be an abomination, and the one who eats it shall bear the guilt of his sin.
Meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten; it must be burned up. As for the meat, anyone who is clean may eat it,
but if anyone who is unclean eats meat from the peace offering that belongs to the the LORD, that person must be cut off from his people.

If anyone touches anything unclean—whether human uncleanness, an unclean animal, or any unclean, detestable thing—and then eats meat from the peace offering that belongs to the the LORD, that person must be cut off from his people.
Then the the LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the Israelites and say: 'You must not eat any fat of an ox, a sheep, or a goat.
The fat of an animal found dead or torn by wild beasts may be used for any other purpose, but you must not eat it.
If anyone eats the fat of an animal from which an offering made by fire is presented to the the LORD, the one who eats it must be cut off from his people.
You must not eat the blood of any bird or animal in any of your dwellings.
If anyone eats blood, that person must be cut off from his people.'"
Then the the LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the Israelites and say: 'Anyone who presents a peace offering to the the LORD must bring to the the LORD his offering from it.
With his own hands he is to bring the offerings made by fire to the the LORD; he shall bring the fat with the breast, to wave the breast as a wave offering before the the LORD.
The priest is to burn the fat on the altar, but the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.
And you are to give the right thigh to the priest as a contribution from your peace offerings.
The son of Aaron who presents the blood and fat of the peace offering shall have the right thigh as his portion.

For I have taken from the Israelites the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as a perpetual portion from the Israelites.'"
This is the portion of the offerings made by fire to the the LORD for Aaron and his sons on the day they were presented to serve as priests to the the LORD.
On the day they were anointed, the the LORD commanded that this be given them by the Israelites. It is a permanent statute for the generations to come.
This is the law of the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering, and the peace offering,
which the the LORD commanded Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day He commanded the Israelites to present their offerings to the the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai.
Then the LORD said to Moses,
“Take Aaron and his sons, along with their garments, the anointing oil, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread,
and assemble the whole congregation at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.”
So Moses did as the LORD commanded him, and the congregation assembled at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
And Moses said to the congregation, “This is what the LORD has commanded to be done.”
Then Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
He put the tunic on Aaron, tied the sash around him, clothed him with the robe, and put the ephod on him. He tied the woven band of the ephod around him and fastened it to him.
Then he put the breastpiece on him and placed the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece.
He also set the turban on Aaron’s head and attached the gold plate, the holy crown, to the front of the turban, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the tabernacle and everything in it; and so he consecrated them.
He sprinkled some of the oil on the altar seven times, anointing the altar and all its utensils, as well as the basin and its stand, to consecrate them.
He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head and anointed him to consecrate him.
Then Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, put tunics on them, tied sashes around them, and fastened headbands on them, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He then brought the bull for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.

Moses slaughtered the bull, took some of the blood, and applied it with his finger to all four horns of the altar, purifying the altar. He poured out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar and consecrated it so that atonement could be made for it.
Moses then took all the fat that was on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and both kidneys with their fat, and burned them on the altar.
But the bull—its hide, flesh, and dung—he burned outside the camp, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then he presented the ram for the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
Moses slaughtered the ram and sprinkled the blood on all sides of the altar.
He cut the ram into pieces and burned the head, the pieces, and the fat.

He washed the entrails and legs with water and burned the whole ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then he presented the second ram, the ram of ordination, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
Moses slaughtered it and took some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron’s right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

Moses also brought Aaron’s sons forward and put some of the blood on the lobes of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Then he sprinkled the rest of the blood on all sides of the altar.
He took the fat—the fat tail, all the fat on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, both kidneys with their fat—and the right thigh.

From the basket of unleavened bread that was before the LORD, he took one cake of unleavened bread, one cake of bread made with oil, and one wafer, and he placed them on the fat portions and on the right thigh.
He put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons and waved them as a wave offering before the LORD.
Then Moses took them from their hands and burned them on the altar with the burnt offering. They were an ordination offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
He also took the breast of the ram of ordination and waved it as a wave offering before the LORD, and it was Moses’ portion, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

Then Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood from the altar and sprinkled them on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments. So he consecrated Aaron and his garments, along with his sons and their garments.

Then Moses said to Aaron and his sons, “Cook the meat at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and eat it there, along with the bread in the basket of ordination offerings, as I commanded: ‘Aaron and his sons are to eat it.’
And you shall burn up the remainder of the meat and bread.
You must not go outside the entrance to the Tent of Meeting for seven days, until the days of your ordination are completed, because it will take seven days to ordain you.
What has been done today is as the LORD commanded, to make atonement for you.
You must remain at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting day and night for seven days and keep the LORD’s charge so that you will not die, for this is what I have been commanded.”
So Aaron and his sons did everything the LORD had commanded through Moses.
On the eighth day, Moses summoned Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel.
He said to Aaron, "Take for yourself an unblemished bull calf for a sin offering and an unblemished ram for a burnt offering, and present them before the LORD.
Speak to the Israelites and say, 'Take a male goat for a sin offering, and an unblemished calf and an unblemished lamb, each a year old, for a burnt offering.
Take also a bull and a ram for peace offerings, to sacrifice before the LORD, and a grain offering mixed with oil, because today the LORD will appear to you.'"
They brought what Moses commanded to the front of the tent of meeting, and the whole congregation drew near and stood before the LORD.
Moses said, "This is what the LORD has commanded you to do, so that the glory of the LORD may appear to you."

He also said to Aaron, "Approach the altar and offer your sin offering and your burnt offering; make atonement for yourself and for the people. Then present the people's offering and make atonement for them, as the LORD has commanded."
Aaron approached the altar and slaughtered the calf of the sin offering that was for himself.
Aaron's sons brought the blood to him; he dipped his finger in it and applied it to the horns of the altar, then poured the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
He burned the fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver from the sin offering on the altar, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The flesh and the skin he burned with fire outside the camp.
He slaughtered the burnt offering; Aaron's sons handed him the blood, and he sprinkled it around the altar.
Aaron's sons handed him the burnt offering, cut into pieces, along with the head, and he burned them on the altar.
He washed the entrails and the legs and burned them on the altar on top of the burnt offering.
Then he presented the people's offering. He took the goat for the people's sin offering, slaughtered it, and offered it for sin, just as he had done with the first.
He presented the burnt offering and offered it according to the ordinance.
He presented the grain offering, filled his hand with some of it, and burned it on the altar, in addition to the morning burnt offering.
He slaughtered the bull and the ram for the people's sacrifice of peace offerings. Aaron's sons handed him the blood, and he sprinkled it around the altar.
They also brought him the fat portions from the bull and the ram—the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver.
They placed the fat portions on the breasts, and he burned the fat portions on the altar.
Aaron waved the breasts and the right thigh as a wave offering before the LORD, as Moses had commanded.
Then Aaron lifted his hands toward the people and blessed them. Having completed the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offering, he stepped down.
Moses and Aaron entered the tent of meeting; when they came out, they blessed the people, and the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people.
Fire went out from before the LORD and consumed the burnt offering and the fat portions on the altar. When all the people saw it, they shouted and fell on their faces.
Now Aaron's sons, Nadab and Abihu, each took his censer, placed fire in it, added incense, and offered unauthorized fire before the LORD, contrary to His command.
So fire came out from the presence of the LORD and consumed them, and they died before the LORD.
Moses then said to Aaron, "This is what the LORD spoke of when He said, 'Among those who approach Me I will be proved holy; in the sight of all the people I will be honored.'" Aaron remained silent.
Moses summoned Mishael and Elzaphan, sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel, and said to them, "Come here; carry your cousins outside the camp, away from the front of the sanctuary."
So they came and carried them, still in their tunics, outside the camp, as Moses had directed.

Then Moses said to Aaron and to his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, "Do not dishevel your hair or tear your clothes, or you will die and the LORD will be angry with the whole community. But all the Israelites are to mourn for those the LORD has consumed by fire.
You must not leave the entrance to the tent of meeting, or you will die, because the LORD's anointing oil is on you." So they did as Moses said.
Then the LORD said to Aaron,
"You and your sons must not drink wine or strong drink when you go into the tent of meeting, or you will die. This is a lasting statute for your generations,
so that you can distinguish between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean,
and so that you can teach the Israelites all the statutes the LORD has spoken to them through Moses."

Moses said to Aaron and to his remaining sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, "Take the grain offering left from the food offerings presented to the LORD and eat it without leaven beside the altar, for it is most holy.
You are to eat it in a holy place, because it is your due and your sons' due from the food offerings presented to the LORD; for so I have been commanded.

You and your sons and your daughters may eat the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution in a clean place, because they have been given to you and your children as your share of the Israelites' fellowship offerings.

The thigh of the contribution and the breast of the wave offering must be brought with the fat portions of the food offerings to be waved as a wave offering before the LORD; it will be yours and your sons' with you, a statute forever, as the LORD has commanded."
When Moses inquired about the goat of the sin offering and found that it had been burned up, he was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's remaining sons, and asked,
"Why have you not eaten the sin offering in the holy place? It is most holy, and the LORD has given it to you to bear the iniquity of the congregation, to make atonement for them before the LORD.
Since its blood was not brought inside the holy place, you should have eaten it in the sanctuary, as I commanded."

Aaron replied to Moses, "Look, today they have offered their sin offering and their burnt offering before the LORD, and such things have happened to me. If I had eaten the sin offering today, would it have been acceptable in the LORD's sight?"
When Moses heard this, he was satisfied.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying to them,
"Speak to the Israelites: These are the living creatures among all the beasts on the earth that you may eat.
Among the beasts, you may eat any that has a divided hoof—cloven-footed and chewing the cud.
"But among those that chew the cud or have a divided hoof, you must not eat these: the camel, because it chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.
The rock badger, because it chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.
The hare, because it chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.
And the pig, because it has a divided hoof and is cloven-footed but does not chew the cud; it is unclean for you.
You must not eat their flesh or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.
"These you may eat of all that are in the waters: whatever has fins and scales in the seas and in the rivers—you may eat them.
But all that do not have fins and scales in the seas and rivers, among all the swarming creatures in the waters and all living creatures in the waters, are detestable to you.
They shall be detestable to you; you must not eat their flesh, and you must detest their carcasses.
Whatever in the waters does not have fins and scales is detestable to you.
"These you must detest among the birds—they must not be eaten, because they are detestable: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
the kite, any kind of falcon,
the ostrich, the screech owl, the gull, any kind of hawk,
the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,
the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
"All winged insects that go on all fours are detestable to you.
Yet you may eat these among all the winged insects that go on all fours: those that have jointed legs above their feet for hopping on the ground.
Of these you may eat: the locust of any kind, the bald locust of any kind, the cricket of any kind, and the grasshopper of any kind.
But all other winged insects that have four feet are detestable to you.
"By these you will become unclean; whoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening,
and whoever carries any part of their carcasses shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening.
Every animal that has a divided hoof but is not cloven-footed or does not chew the cud is unclean for you; everyone who touches them shall be unclean.
All that go on their paws among the four-footed animals are unclean for you; whoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
And whoever carries their carcasses shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening; they are unclean for you.
"These are unclean for you among the swarming creatures that swarm on the ground: the mole, the mouse, and any kind of great lizard,
the gecko, the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
These are unclean for you among all the swarming creatures; whoever touches them when they are dead shall be unclean until evening.

And anything on which one of them falls when dead—whether wood, cloth, hide, or sackcloth, or any article used for work—must be rinsed with water and will be unclean until evening; then it will be clean.
"If any of them falls into a clay pot, everything in it shall be unclean, and you must break the pot.
Any food that may be eaten, on which water has come, and any drink that may be drunk from such a vessel, shall be unclean.
And everything on which a carcass falls shall be unclean: an oven or stove shall be broken up; they are unclean and shall be unclean for you.
Nevertheless, a spring or a cistern holding water shall be clean, but whoever touches a carcass in them shall be unclean.
If a carcass falls on any seed that is to be sown, it is clean;
but if water has been put on the seed and a carcass falls on it, it is unclean for you.
"If an animal that you may eat dies, whoever touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.
And whoever eats of its carcass shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening, and whoever carries its carcass shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening.
"Every swarming creature that swarms on the ground is detestable; it must not be eaten.
You must not eat any creature that moves along the ground, whether it goes on its belly, or on all fours, or on many feet; all such are detestable.
Do not make yourselves detestable by any swarming creature that swarms; do not defile yourselves with them, or you will become unclean by them.
"For I am the LORD your God. Consecrate yourselves therefore, and be holy, for I am holy. You must not defile yourselves with any swarming creature that moves along the ground.
For I am the LORD who brought you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God; you shall be holy, for I am holy.
"This is the law concerning the animals, birds, every living thing that moves in the waters, and every creature that swarms on the ground,
to make a distinction between the unclean and the clean, and between the living creature that may be eaten and the living creature that may not be eaten."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the Israelites and say: When a woman conceives and bears a male child, she shall be unclean for seven days, just as during the days of her menstrual impurity, she shall be unclean.
On the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.
Then she shall continue thirty-three days in the blood of her purification; she shall not touch anything holy, nor enter the sanctuary, until the days of her purification are completed.
If she bears a female child, she shall be unclean for two weeks, as during her menstruation, and she shall continue sixty-six days in the blood of her purification.

"When the days of her purification are completed, whether for a son or a daughter, she shall bring to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting a year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a pigeon or a turtledove for a sin offering.
He shall offer it before the LORD and make atonement for her, and she shall be cleansed from the flow of her blood. This is the law for the woman who bears a male or a female child.

If she cannot afford a lamb, she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering, and the priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean."
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:

"When a person develops on the skin of his body a raised swelling, a scab, or a bright spot, and it becomes a leprous disease in the skin of his body, he shall be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons the priests. "

The priest shall examine the disease in the skin of the body; and if the hair in the diseased area has turned white and the disease appears deeper than the skin of his body, it is a leprous disease. When the priest sees it, he shall pronounce him unclean.

But if the bright spot is white in the skin of his body and does not appear deeper than the skin, and the hair in it has not turned white, the priest shall isolate the person who has the disease for seven days. "
The priest shall examine him on the seventh day, and if in his eyes the disease is unchanged and the disease has not spread in the skin, then the priest shall isolate him for another seven days.

The priest shall examine him again on the seventh day, and if the disease has faded and has not spread in the skin, the priest shall pronounce him clean; it is only a scab. He shall wash his clothes and be clean.
But if the scab spreads in the skin after he has shown himself to the priest for his cleansing, he shall show himself to the priest again.
The priest shall examine him, and if the scab has spread in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean; it is leprosy. "
When a leprous disease is in a person, he shall be brought to the priest.
The priest shall examine him, and if there is a white swelling in the skin that has turned the hair white, and there is raw flesh in the swelling,
it is a chronic leprosy in the skin of his body, and the priest shall pronounce him unclean. He shall not isolate him, for he is unclean. "
But if the leprosy breaks out all over the skin, so that the leprosy covers all the skin of the person from his head to his feet, as far as the priest can see,
then the priest shall examine him, and if the leprosy has covered all his flesh, he shall pronounce the person clean; it has all turned white, and he is clean.
But whenever raw flesh appears on him, he shall be unclean.
The priest shall examine the raw flesh and pronounce him unclean; the raw flesh is unclean; it is leprosy.
Or if the raw flesh turns again and is changed to white, then he shall come to the priest;
and the priest shall examine him, and if the disease has turned white, then the priest shall pronounce the diseased person clean; he is clean. "
When the flesh has a boil on the skin and it is healed,
and in the place of the boil there comes a white swelling or a reddish-white bright spot, then it shall be shown to the priest.
If the priest sees that its appearance is lower than the skin and its hair has turned white, the priest shall pronounce him unclean; it is a leprous disease, it has broken out in the boil.
But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in it and it is not lower than the skin but has faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
If it spreads in the skin, the priest shall pronounce him unclean; it is a leprous infection.
But if the bright spot stays in its place and does not spread, it is the scar of the boil, and the priest shall pronounce him clean. "
Or when the body has a burn from fire on the skin, and the raw flesh of the burn becomes a bright spot, reddish-white or white,

the priest shall examine it, and if the hair in the bright spot has turned white and its appearance is deeper than the skin, it is leprosy; it has broken out in the burn. The priest shall pronounce him unclean; it is a leprous disease.
But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in the bright spot and it is not lower than the skin but has faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
The priest shall examine him on the seventh day, and if it has spread in the skin, the priest shall pronounce him unclean; it is a leprous disease.
But if the bright spot stays in its place and has not spread in the skin but has faded, it is a swelling from the burn, and the priest shall pronounce him clean; for it is the scar of the burn. "
When a man or woman has a disease on the head or in the beard,

the priest shall examine the disease, and if its appearance is deeper than the skin and there is in it thin yellow hair, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean; it is a scall, it is leprosy of the head or the beard.
But if the priest examines the scall and its appearance is not deeper than the skin and there is no black hair in it, then the priest shall isolate the person with the scall for seven days. "
On the seventh day the priest shall examine the disease, and if the scall has not spread and there is no yellow hair in it and the scall is not deeper than the skin,
then he shall shave himself, but the scall he shall not shave; and the priest shall isolate the person with the scall another seven days.

On the seventh day the priest shall examine the scall, and if the scall has not spread in the skin and its appearance is not deeper than the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him clean. He shall wash his clothes and be clean. "
But if the scall spreads in the skin after his cleansing,
then the priest shall examine him, and if the scall has spread in the skin, the priest need not seek for the yellow hair; he is unclean.
But if in his eyes the scall is unchanged and black hair has grown in it, the scall is healed; he is clean, and the priest shall pronounce him clean. "
When a man or a woman has bright spots on the skin of the body, white bright spots,
the priest shall examine them, and if the bright spots on the skin of the body are dull white, it is a rash that has broken out on the skin; he is clean.
If a man's hair has fallen out from his head, he is bald; he is clean.
And if his hair has fallen out from the front of his head, he has a bald forehead; he is clean.
But if there is on the bald head or the bald forehead a reddish-white sore, it is leprosy breaking out on his bald head or his bald forehead.
Then the priest shall examine him, and if the swelling of the sore is reddish-white on his bald head or on his bald forehead, like the appearance of leprosy in the skin of the body,
he is a leprous man; he is unclean. The priest shall pronounce him utterly unclean; his disease is on his head. "
The leper who has the disease shall wear torn clothes and let the hair of his head hang loose, and he shall cover his upper lip and cry, 'Unclean, unclean.'
All the days during which the disease is on him he shall be unclean; he is unclean. He shall dwell alone; his dwelling shall be outside the camp. "
When a garment has a leprous disease in it, whether a woolen garment or a linen garment,
whether in warp or woof of linen or wool, or in a skin or in anything made of skin,
if the disease is greenish or reddish in the garment, in the skin, in the warp or the woof, or in any article made of skin, it is a leprous disease, and it shall be shown to the priest.
The priest shall examine the disease and isolate the article that has the disease for seven days. "

He shall examine the disease on the seventh day. If the disease has spread in the garment, in the warp or the woof, in the skin, or in any work made of skin, the disease is a malignant leprosy; it is unclean.
He shall burn the garment, whether in the warp or the woof, in wool or in linen, or any article of skin in which the disease is, for it is a malignant leprosy; it shall be burned in the fire. "
But if the priest examines it and the disease has not spread in the garment, in the warp or the woof, or in any article of skin,
then the priest shall command that they wash the thing in which the disease is, and he shall isolate it for seven days more.

The priest shall examine the diseased article after it is washed, and if the disease has not changed its color, though the disease has not spread, it is unclean. It must be burned in the fire; it is a raw spot, whether on the front or on the back. "
But if the priest examines it and the disease has faded after it is washed, then he shall tear it out of the garment, out of the skin, out of the warp or the woof.
But if it appears again in the garment, in the warp or the woof, or in any article of skin, it is spreading; the article in which the disease is must be burned in the fire.
But the garment, or the warp or the woof, or any article of skin that is washed and from which the disease departs, shall be washed a second time, and then it is clean.
This is the law for a leprous disease in a garment of wool or linen, either in the warp or the woof, or in any article of skin, for pronouncing it clean or unclean."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“This is the law for the leper on the day of his cleansing: he shall be brought to the priest.
The priest shall go outside the camp and examine him; and if the leprous disease has been healed in the leper,
the priest shall command that two clean living birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop be taken for the one who is to be cleansed.
“The priest shall command that one bird be killed in a clay vessel over fresh water.

As for the living bird, he shall take it together with the cedar wood, the scarlet yarn, and the hyssop, and dip them and the living bird in the blood of the bird that was killed over the fresh water.
He shall sprinkle the one to be cleansed from the leprosy seven times, pronounce him clean, and release the living bird into the open field.

“The one to be cleansed shall wash his clothes, shave off all his hair, and bathe in water, so that he may be clean; afterward he shall enter the camp, yet he shall remain outside his tent for seven days.

On the seventh day he shall shave all the hair from his head, his beard, and his eyebrows—indeed, all his hair he shall shave off; he shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he shall be clean.
“On the eighth day he shall take two unblemished male lambs, one unblemished ewe lamb a year old, three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and one log of oil.
The priest who cleanses him shall present the man to be cleansed, together with these offerings, before the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
The priest shall take one male lamb and offer it as a guilt offering, along with the log of oil, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.

He shall slaughter the lamb in the place where the sin offering and the burnt offering are slaughtered, in the holy place; for, like the sin offering, the guilt offering belongs to the priest and is most holy.

“The priest shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the tip of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the great toe of his right foot.
The priest shall take some of the log of oil and pour it into the palm of his own left hand.
The priest shall dip his right finger into the oil in his left hand and sprinkle some of the oil with his finger seven times before the LORD.

From the remaining oil in his palm, the priest shall put some on the tip of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the great toe of his right foot, over the blood of the guilt offering.
The priest shall pour the rest of the oil in his hand upon the head of the one to be cleansed, and the priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD.
“The priest shall offer the sin offering and make atonement for the one to be cleansed from his uncleanness; afterward he shall slaughter the burnt offering.
The priest shall offer the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar, and the priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be clean.

“If he is poor and cannot afford these, he shall take one male lamb for a guilt offering to be waved, to make atonement for him, one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and a log of oil.
He shall also take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whichever he can afford, one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.
“On the eighth day he shall bring them to the priest for his cleansing, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the LORD.
The priest shall take the lamb of the guilt offering and the log of oil, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.

“He shall slaughter the lamb of the guilt offering, and the priest shall take some of its blood and put it on the tip of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the great toe of his right foot.
The priest shall pour some of the oil into the palm of his own left hand.
With his right finger the priest shall sprinkle some of the oil in his left hand seven times before the LORD.

The priest shall put some of the oil in his hand on the tip of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the great toe of his right foot, on the place of the blood of the guilt offering.
The rest of the oil in the priest’s hand he shall put on the head of the one to be cleansed, to make atonement for him before the LORD.
“He shall offer one of the turtledoves or young pigeons, whichever he can afford—

whichever he is able to obtain—one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering, together with the grain offering; and the priest shall make atonement for the one to be cleansed before the LORD.
This is the law for the one who has a leprous disease, when he cannot afford the means of his cleansing.”
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
“When you enter the land of Canaan, which I am giving you as a possession, and I inflict a leprous disease on a house in the land of your possession,
“The owner of the house shall come and tell the priest that he has seen something resembling a plague in the house.

The priest shall command that the house be emptied before he enters to examine the plague, so that all that is in the house may not be made unclean; afterward the priest shall enter to examine the house.
“He shall examine the plague, and if the plague is in the walls of the house with greenish or reddish depressions that appear deeper than the wall,
the priest shall go out of the house to its doorway and quarantine the house for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest shall return and examine it; and if the plague has spread in the walls of the house,
“the priest shall command that the stones in which the plague is found be removed and cast into an unclean place outside the city.
He shall have the house scraped inside all around, and the plaster that is scraped off shall be poured out into an unclean place outside the city.
They shall take other stones and put them in the place of the removed stones, and he shall take other mortar and plaster the house.
“If the plague returns and breaks out in the house after the stones have been removed and the house has been scraped and plastered,
the priest shall come and examine it; and if the plague has spread in the house, it is a malignant leprous disease in the house; it is unclean.
He shall tear down the house—its stones, its timber, and all its plaster—and carry them out of the city to an unclean place.
“Moreover, whoever enters the house during all the days it is quarantined shall be unclean until evening.
The one who lies down in the house shall wash his clothes, and the one who eats in the house shall wash his clothes.
If the priest comes in and examines it and finds that the plague has not spread in the house after it was plastered, the priest shall pronounce the house clean, because the plague is healed.
“He shall take two birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop to cleanse the house.
He shall kill one bird in a clay vessel over fresh water.
He shall take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the scarlet yarn, and the living bird, dip them in the blood of the slain bird and in the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times.
He shall cleanse the house with the blood of the bird, the fresh water, the living bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the scarlet yarn.
He shall release the living bird outside the city into the open field; thus he shall make atonement for the house, and it shall be clean.
“This is the law for every kind of leprous disease and scall,
for leprosy in a garment or in a house,
and for a swelling, a rash, or a bright spot,
to teach when it is unclean and when it is clean. This is the law of leprosy.”
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
" 'Speak to the Israelites and say to them: Whenever a man has a bodily discharge, that discharge renders him ceremonially unclean.
This is the nature of his uncleanness with respect to the discharge: whether his body secretes it or retains it, he is unclean.
Every bed on which the man with the discharge lies shall be unclean, and every article on which he sits shall be unclean.
" 'Anyone who touches his bed must launder his garments, bathe in water, and remain ceremonially unclean until evening.
Whoever sits on any object on which the man with the discharge has sat must launder his garments, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.
Whoever touches the flesh of the man with the discharge must launder his garments, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.
If the man with the discharge spits upon a person who is clean, that person must launder his garments, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.
" 'Every saddle on which the man with the discharge rides shall be unclean.
Anyone who touches anything beneath him shall be unclean until evening, and whoever carries such articles must launder his garments, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.
If the man with the discharge touches another person without first having rinsed his hands in water, the person touched must launder his garments, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.
Any clay vessel touched by the man with the discharge must be broken, and any wooden article must be rinsed with water.
" 'When the man with the discharge has been cleansed of his discharge, he must count seven days for his purification, launder his garments, and bathe his body in fresh water; then he shall be clean.
On the eighth day he must take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, come before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, and give them to the priest.
The priest shall sacrifice one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and in this way he shall make atonement for him before the LORD because of his discharge.
" 'When a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his entire body in water and remain unclean until evening.
Any garment or leather on which there is an emission of semen must be washed with water and shall remain unclean until evening.
If a man lies with a woman and an emission of semen occurs, both must bathe in water and remain unclean until evening.
" 'Whenever a woman has a discharge of blood from her body, she shall be ceremonially unclean for seven days, and anyone who touches her shall remain unclean until evening.
Anything on which she lies during her menstrual impurity shall be unclean, and anything on which she sits shall be unclean.
Anyone who touches her bed must launder his garments, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches anything on which she has sat must launder his garments, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.
Whether the contact occurs with the bed or with an object on which she was sitting, the person who touches it shall be unclean until evening.
If a man lies with her and her menstrual flow touches him, he shall be unclean for seven days, and every bed on which he lies shall be unclean.

" 'If a woman has a discharge of blood for many days outside her menstrual period, or if it continues beyond her regular period, she shall be unclean throughout all the days of her unclean discharge, just as she is during her menstrual period.
Any bed on which she lies during the days of her discharge shall be unclean, as shall everything on which she sits.
Anyone who touches these things shall be unclean; he must launder his garments, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.
When she is cleansed of her discharge, she must count seven days, and afterward she shall be clean.
On the eighth day she must take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
The priest shall sacrifice one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and in this way he shall make atonement for her before the LORD for her unclean discharge.
" ' You must keep the Israelites separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die by defiling My tabernacle that is among them.
This is the law for a man with a discharge, for one who has an emission of semen and becomes unclean.
for a woman in her menstrual period, for anyone with a discharge, whether male or female, and for a man who lies with an unclean woman.' "
The LORD spoke to Moses after Aaron's two sons died because they approached the LORD.

The LORD said to Moses, "Tell your brother Aaron that he must not enter the Holy Place behind the veil at any time, in front of the mercy seat that is on the ark, or he will die; for I will appear in the cloud over the mercy seat."
Aaron shall enter the Holy Place with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.
He must bathe his body with water and then put on the holy linen tunic, the linen undergarments, the linen sash, and the linen turban; these are holy garments.
From the congregation of the Israelites he shall take two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
Aaron shall present the bull of the sin offering, which is for himself, and make atonement for himself and for his household.
He shall take the two goats and present them before the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
Aaron shall cast lots for the two goats—one lot for the LORD and the other for Azazel.
Aaron shall present the goat on which the lot fell for the LORD and make it a sin offering.
But the goat on which the lot fell for Azazel shall be presented alive before the LORD, to make atonement for it by sending it away into the wilderness as a scapegoat.
Aaron shall present the bull of the sin offering that is for himself and make atonement for himself and his household; then he shall slaughter the bull.
He shall take a censer full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD, and two handfuls of finely ground sweet incense, and bring them inside the veil.
He shall put the incense on the fire before the LORD, so that the cloud of incense covers the mercy seat over the testimony, and he will not die.
He shall take some of the blood of the bull and sprinkle it with his finger on the east side of the mercy seat; he shall sprinkle the blood with his finger seven times in front of the mercy seat.

Then he shall slaughter the goat of the sin offering that is for the people and bring its blood inside the veil. He shall do with its blood as he did with the blood of the bull: he shall sprinkle it on the mercy seat and in front of the mercy seat.

In this way he shall make atonement for the Holy Place because of the uncleannesses of the Israelites and because of their transgressions, all their sins. He shall do the same for the tent of meeting, which dwells among them in the midst of their uncleannesses.

No person shall be in the tent of meeting when he enters to make atonement in the Holy Place until he comes out. He shall make atonement for himself, for his household, and for the whole assembly of Israel.

Then he shall go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it. He shall take some of the blood of the bull and some of the blood of the goat and put it on the horns of the altar all around.
He shall sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, and so cleanse it and consecrate it from the uncleannesses of the Israelites.
When he has finished making atonement for the Holy Place, the tent of meeting, and the altar, he shall present the live goat.

Aaron shall lay both his hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the iniquities of the Israelites, all their transgressions, and all their sins. He shall put them on the head of the goat and send it away into the wilderness by the hand of a man appointed for the task.
The goat shall carry all their iniquities to a remote, uninhabited land, and the man shall release the goat in the wilderness.
Then Aaron shall come into the tent of meeting, remove the linen garments that he put on when he entered the Holy Place, and leave them there.

He shall bathe his body with water in a holy place, put on his own garments, and come out. Then he shall offer his burnt offering and the burnt offering of the people, and make atonement for himself and for the people.
He shall also burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
