The man who released the goat for Azazel shall wash his clothes and bathe his body with water; after that he may return to the camp.

The bull of the sin offering and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought into the Holy Place to make atonement, shall be carried outside the camp. Their hides, flesh, and dung shall be burned with fire.
The one who burns them shall wash his clothes and bathe his body with water; after that he may return to the camp.
This shall be a permanent statute for you: on the tenth day of the seventh month, you shall deny yourselves and do no work—neither the native nor the foreigner who lives among you.
For on this day atonement shall be made for you, to cleanse you; you shall be clean from all your sins before the LORD.
It is a Sabbath of solemn rest for you, and you shall deny yourselves; it is a permanent statute.
The priest who is anointed and consecrated to serve as priest in his father's place shall make atonement. He shall put on the holy linen garments.
He shall make atonement for the Most Holy Place, for the tent of meeting and the altar, and for the priests and all the people of the assembly.
This shall be a permanent statute for you, to make atonement for the Israelites once a year for all their sins. And Aaron did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
"Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites and tell them that this is what the LORD has commanded: "
Any man from the house of Israel who slaughters an ox, a lamb, or a goat—whether in the camp or outside it—

and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to offer it as a sacrifice to the LORD before the tabernacle of the LORD shall be regarded as having shed blood. He has shed blood and shall be cut off from among his people. "

This is so that the Israelites will bring to the LORD the sacrifices they are now offering in the open field, bringing them to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting and sacrificing them there as peace offerings to the LORD.
The priest shall sprinkle the blood on the altar of the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting and burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to the LORD. "
They must no longer sacrifice their offerings to the goat demons, after whom they prostitute themselves. This shall be a permanent statute for them throughout their generations. "
Tell them: Any man from the house of Israel or any foreigner residing among them who offers a burnt offering or sacrifice
and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to offer it to the LORD, that man shall be cut off from his people. "
If anyone from the house of Israel or from the foreigners residing among them eats any blood, I will set My face against that person who eats the blood and will cut him off from among his people.
For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your souls; for it is the blood that makes atonement for the soul. "
Therefore I have said to the Israelites: No person among you may eat blood, nor may the foreigner residing among you eat blood. "
If any Israelite or foreigner residing among them hunts and kills a wild animal or bird that may be eaten, he must pour out its blood and cover it with dust.

For the life of all flesh is its blood. Therefore I have said to the Israelites: You must not eat the blood of any flesh, because the life of all flesh is its blood; anyone who eats it shall be cut off. "

Anyone, whether native-born or foreigner, who eats an animal that died naturally or was torn by beasts must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening; then he will be clean.
But if he does not wash his clothes or bathe his body, he will bear his iniquity."
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: 'I am the LORD your God.
You must not adopt the practices of Egypt, where you formerly dwelt, nor those of Canaan, to which I am bringing you. Do not follow their ways.
You shall observe My ordinances and carefully follow My statutes, for I am the LORD your God.
Keep My statutes and My ordinances, for the individual who obeys them shall live by them. I am the LORD.
"'No one among you shall approach a close relative to have sexual relations with them. I am the LORD.
You shall not dishonor your father by having sexual relations with your mother; she is your mother, and you must not have sexual relations with her.
You shall not have sexual relations with your father's wife, for doing so would dishonor your father.
You shall not have sexual relations with your sister—whether she is your father's daughter or your mother's daughter—born within the household or elsewhere.
You shall not have sexual relations with your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, for that would dishonor you.
You shall not have sexual relations with the daughter of your father's wife who was born to your father, for she is your sister.
"'You shall not have sexual relations with your father's sister, because she is your father's near kinswoman.
You shall not have sexual relations with your mother's sister, for she is your mother's near kinswoman.
You shall not dishonor your father's brother by having sexual relations with his wife; she is your aunt.
You shall not have sexual relations with your daughter-in-law; she is your son's wife, and you must not have sexual relations with her.
You shall not have sexual relations with your brother's wife, for that would dishonor your brother.
You shall not have sexual relations with a woman and her daughter, nor with her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter, for they are her near relatives; such conduct is wickedness.
You shall not marry your wife's sister as a rival wife and have sexual relations with her while your wife is still living.
"'You shall not approach a woman to have sexual relations with her during her menstrual impurity.
You shall not have sexual relations with your neighbor's wife, thereby defiling yourself with her.
You shall not give any of your children to be sacrificed to Molech, for that would profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
You shall not have sexual relations with a man as with a woman; that is detestable.
You shall not have sexual relations with an animal, thereby defiling yourself with it; nor shall a woman offer herself to an animal for sexual relations, for that is perversion.
"'You shall not defile yourselves by any of these practices, for by them the nations that I am driving out before you have become defiled.
The land itself was defiled, so I punished it for its iniquity, and the land vomited out its inhabitants.
You shall keep My statutes and My ordinances, and you shall not practice any of these abominations, whether you are native-born or a sojourner dwelling among you.
For the people who inhabited the land before you committed all these abominations, and the land became defiled.
If you defile the land, it will vomit you out just as it vomited out the nations that preceded you.
Everyone who commits any of these abominations shall be cut off from among his people.
Keep My charge, and do not practice any of the abominable customs that were observed before you, lest you become defiled by them. I am the LORD your God.'"
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the entire congregation of Israel and tell them: You shall be holy, for I, the LORD, your God, am holy.
Every one of you shall revere his mother and his father, and you shall keep My Sabbaths; I am the LORD your God.
You shall not turn to idols, nor shall you make for yourselves molten gods; I am the LORD your God.
When you offer a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD, you shall offer it so that you may be accepted.
It shall be eaten on the day of your sacrifice, and on the next day; but what remains until the third day shall be burned with fire.
If it is eaten at all on the third day, it is an abomination; it shall not be accepted.
Whoever eats it shall bear his iniquity, because he has profaned what is holy to the LORD; and that person shall be cut off from his people.
“When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not reap to the very edges of your field, nor shall you gather the gleanings of your harvest.
You shall not glean your vineyard, nor shall you gather the fallen grapes of your vineyard; you shall leave them for the poor and the sojourner; I am the LORD your God.
You shall not steal, nor shall you deal falsely, nor shall you lie to one another.
You shall not swear falsely by My name, nor shall you profane the name of your God; I am the LORD.
You shall not oppress your neighbor, nor shall you rob him; the wages of a hired worker shall not remain with you overnight until morning.
You shall not curse the deaf, nor shall you put a stumbling block before the blind; but you shall fear your God; I am the LORD.
You shall do no injustice in judgment; you shall not show partiality to the poor, nor shall you honor the mighty; but in righteousness you shall judge your neighbor.
You shall not go about as a slanderer among your people, nor shall you stand against the blood of your neighbor; I am the LORD.
You shall not hate your brother in your heart; you shall surely rebuke your neighbor, and you shall not bear sin because of him.
You shall not take vengeance, nor shall you bear a grudge against the children of your people; but you shall love your neighbor as yourself; I am the LORD.

“You shall keep My statutes: you shall not let your cattle breed with a different kind; you shall not sow your field with two kinds of seed; and you shall not wear a garment made of two kinds of material.
If a man lies with a woman who is a slave, betrothed to a husband, and not yet ransomed or given her freedom, there shall be an inquiry; they shall not be put to death, because she was not free.
He shall bring his guilt offering to the LORD, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, a ram for a guilt offering.
And the priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD with the ram of the guilt offering for his sin which he has committed; and he shall be forgiven for the sin which he has committed.
When you come into the land and plant any kind of tree for food, you shall regard its fruit as forbidden; for three years it shall be forbidden to you, and it shall not be eaten.
In the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, a praise offering to the LORD.
In the fifth year you may eat its fruit, that it may yield its increase to you; I am the LORD your God.
You shall not eat anything with the blood, nor shall you practice divination or soothsaying.
You shall not round off the hair of your head, nor shall you mar the edges of your beard.
You shall not make any cuttings in your flesh for the dead, nor shall you tattoo any marks upon you; I am the LORD.
You shall not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, lest the land fall into prostitution and become full of wickedness.
“You shall keep My Sabbaths and reverence My sanctuary; I am the LORD.
You shall not turn to mediums or wizards; you shall not seek them out to be defiled by them; I am the LORD your God.
You shall rise before the gray-headed and honor the face of an old man; and you shall fear your God; I am the LORD.
When a sojourner sojourns with you in your land, you shall not mistreat him.
The sojourner who sojourns with you shall be to you as the native among you, and you shall love him as yourself; for you were strangers in the land of Egypt; I am the LORD your God.
You shall do no wrong in judgment, in measures of length or weight or quantity.
You shall have just balances, just weights, a just ephah, and a just hin; I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
You shall observe all My statutes and all My ordinances, and do them; I am the LORD.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Say to the Israelites: Any Israelite or any foreigner residing in Israel who gives any of his children to Molech must be put to death. The people of the land are to stone him.
I will oppose that man and remove him from his people, because he has given his children to Molech, defiling My sanctuary and profaning My holy name.
If the people of the land deliberately overlook that man when he gives his children to Molech and do not put him to death,
then I will oppose that man and his family. I will remove him from his people, along with all who follow him in prostituting themselves to Molech.
I will also oppose anyone who turns to mediums or spiritists and prostitutes himself after them, and I will remove him from his people.”
“Consecrate yourselves and be holy, for I am the LORD your God.
Keep My statutes and practice them; I am the LORD, who sanctifies you.”
“If anyone curses his father or mother, he must be put to death. He has cursed his father or mother; he is responsible for his own death.
If a man commits adultery with another man's wife—with his neighbor's wife—both the adulterer and the adulteress must be put to death.
If a man has sexual relations with his father's wife, he has dishonored his father. Both of them must be put to death; they are responsible for their own deaths.
If a man has sexual relations with his daughter-in-law, both of them must be put to death. They have committed a perversion; they are responsible for their own deaths.
If a man has sexual relations with another man as with a woman, both of them have committed an abomination. They must be put to death; they are responsible for their own deaths.”
“If a man marries a woman and her mother, it is depravity. He and both women must be burned with fire, so that no depravity will exist among you.
If a man has sexual relations with an animal, he must be put to death, and you must kill the animal.
If a woman approaches an animal to mate with it, you must kill the woman and the animal. They must be put to death; they are responsible for their own deaths.

If a man marries his sister, whether his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and has sexual relations with her, it is a disgrace. They must be publicly removed from their people. He has violated his sister; he will bear his guilt.
If a man has sexual relations with a woman during her menstrual period, he has exposed her flow and she has exposed the source of her blood. Both of them must be removed from their people.”
“You must not have sexual relations with your mother's sister or your father's sister, for that exposes the nakedness of a close relative. They will bear their guilt.
If a man has sexual relations with his aunt, he has dishonored his uncle. They will bear their sin; they will die childless.
If a man marries his brother's wife, it is impurity. He has dishonored his brother; they will be childless.”
“You must therefore keep all My statutes and all My judgments and do them, so that the land I am bringing you into will not expel you.
You must not follow the customs of the nation I am driving out before you, because they did all these things, and I abhorred them.
I have told you, ‘You will inherit their land, and I will give it to you to possess—a land flowing with milk and honey.’ I am the LORD your God, who has set you apart from the nations.

You must therefore distinguish between clean and unclean animals and between unclean and clean birds. Do not defile yourselves by any animal or bird or by anything that creeps on the ground, which I have set apart as unclean for you.
You must be holy to Me, for I, the LORD, am holy, and I have separated you from the nations to be My own.
Any man or woman who is a medium or spiritist must be put to death. They must be stoned; they are responsible for their own deaths.”
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them: 'No one shall defile himself for a dead person among his people,
except for his close relative—his mother, father, son, daughter, or brother—
or his unmarried sister who is near to him, since she has had no husband; for her he may defile himself.
He must not defile himself for a leader among his people, thereby profaning himself.
They must not shave their heads or trim the edges of their beards or make cuts in their flesh.

They must be holy to their God and not profane the name of their God. For they present the offerings made by fire to the LORD, the food of their God. So they must be holy. "'They must not marry a woman defiled by prostitution, nor a woman divorced from her husband, for the priest is holy to his God.
You shall consecrate him, for he presents the food of your God. He shall be holy to you, because I the LORD am holy who sanctifies you.

If a priest's daughter defiles herself by prostituting herself, she defiles her father; she must be burned in the fire. "'The high priest, the one among his brothers on whose head the anointing oil has been poured and who has been consecrated to wear the garments, must not let his hair hang loose or tear his garments.
He must not go near any dead body or defile himself, even for his father or mother.
He must not leave the sanctuary or desecrate the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is on him. I am the LORD. "'He must marry a virgin.
He must not marry a widow, a divorced woman, or a woman defiled by prostitution. He must marry a virgin from his own people,
so that he does not defile his offspring among his people. For I am the LORD who sanctifies him.'"
Then the LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to Aaron and tell him: 'No man among your descendants for all generations who has a physical defect may approach to offer the food of his God.
No man who has a defect may approach—no blind man, no lame man, no man with a disfigured face, and no man with a deformed limb. "'
No man with a broken foot or hand,
no hunchback, no dwarf, no man with an eye defect, no man with a scab or rash, and no man with crushed testicles.
No descendant of Aaron the priest who has a defect may approach to present the offerings made by fire to the LORD. He has a defect; he must not approach to offer the food of his God. "'
He may eat the food of his God, both the most holy and the holy.
But he must not go near the curtain or approach the altar, because he has a defect, so that he does not desecrate My sanctuary. For I am the LORD who sanctifies them.'
So Moses spoke to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying, "
Speak to Aaron and his sons, instructing them to keep away from the sacred offerings that the Israelites consecrate to Me, so that they do not profane My holy name. I am the LORD.

Say to them, 'Throughout your generations, any man among all your descendants who approaches the sacred offerings that the Israelites consecrate to the LORD while uncleanness rests upon him shall be cut off from My presence. I am the LORD.'

No descendant of Aaron who suffers from a skin disease or a bodily discharge may eat of the sacred offerings until he is cleansed. And whoever touches anything defiled by a corpse, or a man from whom semen has issued,
or whoever touches any swarming creature that can render him unclean, or any person whose condition renders him unclean—in accordance with every form of his uncleanness—
that person shall remain unclean until evening and may not eat of the sacred offerings unless he has bathed his body in water.
When the sun sets, he shall be clean, and afterward he may eat of the sacred offerings, for they constitute his food.
He shall not eat anything that dies of itself or is torn by beasts, lest he defile himself thereby. I am the LORD.
They shall guard My charge, lest they bear sin on account of it and die within it, because they have profaned it. I am the LORD who sanctifies them.
No outsider may eat a sacred offering; neither a priest's guest nor a hired worker may eat a sacred offering.
But if a priest purchases a person with his own money, that person may eat of it, as may one born in his house; they may eat his food.
If a priest's daughter marries a layman, she may not eat of the sacred contribution.
But if a priest's daughter is widowed or divorced, has no child, and returns to her father's house as in her youth, she may eat of her father's food; yet no layman may eat of it.
If a man eats a sacred offering unintentionally, he shall add a fifth to its value and give the sacred offering to the priest.
They shall not profane the sacred offerings of the Israelites, which they present to the LORD,
and thus cause them to bear the guilt of their iniquity when they eat their sacred offerings, for I am the LORD who sanctifies them."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying, "

Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites, and say to them, 'Any man of the house of Israel or of the sojourners residing in Israel who presents an offering for any of their vows or freewill offerings that they present to the LORD as a burnt offering—
it shall be accepted on your behalf: a male without blemish from the herd, from the sheep, or from the goats.
Whatever has a blemish you shall not offer, for it will not be accepted on your behalf.
And if a man offers a peace offering to the LORD to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering, from the herd or from the flock, it must be without defect to be accepted; no blemish shall be in it.
Blind, injured, maimed, or afflicted with a running sore, eczema, or scabs—these you shall not offer to the LORD, nor present them as a food offering to the LORD upon the altar.
A bull or lamb with disproportionately long or short limbs you may offer as a freewill offering, but for a vow it shall not be accepted.
You shall not offer to the LORD an animal with bruised, crushed, torn, or severed testicles; nor shall you do so in your land.
Nor shall you offer, from the hand of a foreigner, any of these as the bread of your God, because corruption is in them and a blemish is in them; they shall not be accepted on your behalf.'"
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying, "
When a bull, sheep, or goat is born, it shall remain seven days with its mother; from the eighth day onward it shall be accepted as a food offering to the LORD.
You shall not slaughter a cow or sheep and its young on the same day.
When you sacrifice a thanksgiving offering to the LORD, you shall sacrifice it so that you may be accepted.
It shall be eaten on that day; you shall not leave any of it until morning. I am the LORD.
You shall keep My commandments and do them. I am the LORD.
You shall not profane My holy name, but I will be sanctified among the Israelites. I am the LORD who sanctifies you,
who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: These are My appointed festivals—the appointed festivals of the LORD—which you are to proclaim as holy convocations.
For six days labor may be performed, but the seventh day shall be a Sabbath of solemn rest, a holy convocation; you shall do no work on it. It is a Sabbath to the LORD in all your dwellings.
These are the appointed festivals of the LORD, the holy convocations that you are to proclaim at their appointed times. “
On the fourteenth day of the first month, at twilight, is the LORD's Passover.
On the fifteenth day of the same month is the Feast of Unleavened Bread to the LORD; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
On the first day you shall have a holy convocation; you shall do no laborious work.
For seven days you shall present an offering by fire to the LORD. On the seventh day there shall be a holy convocation; you shall do no laborious work.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land that I am giving you, and you reap its harvest, you shall bring the sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest to the priest.
He shall wave the sheaf before the LORD, that you may be accepted. On the day after the Sabbath the priest shall wave it.
On the day when you wave the sheaf, you shall offer a male lamb a year old without blemish as a burnt offering to the LORD.
Its grain offering shall be two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering by fire to the LORD, a pleasing aroma, and its drink offering shall be a quarter of a hin of wine.

You shall eat neither bread nor roasted grain nor fresh ears until this same day, until you have brought the offering of your God. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings. “
You shall count for yourselves from the day after the Sabbath, from the day you brought the sheaf of the wave offering, seven full weeks.
You shall count fifty days to the day after the seventh Sabbath; then you shall present a new grain offering to the LORD.
From your dwellings you shall bring two loaves of bread as a wave offering; they shall be of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour, baked with leaven, as firstfruits to the LORD.

Along with the bread, you shall present seven lambs a year old without blemish, one young bull, and two rams. They shall be a burnt offering to the LORD, with their grain offering and drink offerings, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
You shall also offer one male goat for a sin offering and two male lambs a year old for a peace offering.
The priest shall wave them with the bread of the firstfruits as a wave offering before the LORD, together with the two lambs; they shall be holy to the LORD for the priest.
On this same day you shall proclaim a holy convocation; you shall do no laborious work. It is a perpetual statute in all your dwellings throughout your generations.

When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not reap to the very edge of your field, nor shall you gather the gleanings of your harvest. You shall leave them for the poor and for the sojourner. I am the LORD your God.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites, saying: In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have a Sabbath rest, a memorial proclaimed with blasts of the trumpet, a holy convocation.
You shall do no laborious work, and you shall present an offering by fire to the LORD.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“On the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. It shall be a holy convocation for you; you shall deny yourselves and present an offering by fire to the LORD.
You shall do no work on this very day, for it is a Day of Atonement, to make atonement for you before the LORD your God.
For whoever does not deny himself on this very day shall be cut off from his people.
And whoever does any work on this very day, I will destroy that person from among his people.
You shall do no work at all. It is a perpetual statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
It shall be a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you shall deny yourselves. On the ninth day of the month at evening, from evening to evening, you shall keep your Sabbath.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites, saying: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Feast of Tabernacles to the LORD for seven days.
On the first day there shall be a holy convocation; you shall do no laborious work.

For seven days you shall present an offering by fire to the LORD. On the eighth day you shall have a holy convocation and present an offering by fire to the LORD. It is a solemn assembly; you shall do no laborious work. “

These are the appointed festivals of the LORD, which you shall proclaim as holy convocations, to present to the LORD offerings by fire—burnt offerings, grain offerings, sacrifices, and drink offerings—each on its proper day—
besides the LORD's Sabbaths and besides your gifts and besides all your vows and besides all your freewill offerings that you give to the LORD.

On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in the produce of the land, you shall keep the feast of the LORD seven days. On the first day shall be a Sabbath rest, and on the eighth day a Sabbath rest.

On the first day you shall take for yourselves the fruit of majestic trees, branches of palm trees, boughs of leafy trees, and willows of the brook, and you shall rejoice before the LORD your God seven days.
You shall keep it as a feast to the LORD seven days in the year. It is a perpetual statute throughout your generations; you shall keep it in the seventh month.
You shall dwell in booths seven days; all the native-born in Israel shall dwell in booths,
so that your generations may know that I made the Israelites dwell in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.”
Moses declared to the Israelites the appointed festivals of the LORD.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Command the Israelites to bring to you clear oil of beaten olives for the light, so that a lamp may burn continually.
Outside the veil of the Testimony, in the Tent of Meeting, Aaron shall arrange it continually from evening until morning before the LORD, a perpetual statute throughout your generations.
He shall arrange the lamps on the pure lampstand before the LORD continually.”
“You shall take fine flour and bake it into twelve loaves; two-tenths of an ephah shall be in each loaf.
You shall set them in two rows, six in a row, on the pure table before the LORD.
You shall put pure frankincense on each row, so that it may be a memorial portion for the bread, an offering by fire to the LORD.
Every Sabbath day he shall arrange it before the LORD continually, from the Israelites as an everlasting covenant.
It shall be for Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat it in a holy place, for it is most holy to him from the offerings by fire to the LORD, a perpetual statute.”
Now the son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the Israelites; and the son of the Israelite woman and an Israelite man fought in the camp.
The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name and cursed, so they brought him to Moses. His mother was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
They put him in custody until it was declared to them according to the mouth of the LORD.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Bring the blasphemer outside the camp, and let all who heard him lay their hands on his head, and let all the congregation stone him.
You shall speak to the Israelites, saying, ‘Any man who curses his God shall bear his sin.
Whoever blasphemes the Name of the LORD shall surely be put to death; all the congregation shall stone him. The foreigner and the native alike, when he blasphemes the Name, shall be put to death.’
Whoever strikes any person mortally shall surely be put to death.
Whoever strikes an animal shall make restitution for it, life for life.
If a man causes a defect in his neighbor, as he has done, so shall it be done to him:
fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; as he has caused a defect in a man, so shall it be done to him.
Whoever strikes an animal shall make restitution for it, and whoever strikes a man shall be put to death.
You shall have one judgment for the foreigner and for the native, for I am the LORD your God.”
Moses spoke to the Israelites, and they brought the blasphemer outside the camp and stoned him with stones. The Israelites did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying,
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them:
For six years you may sow your field, prune your vineyard, and gather its produce.
But in the seventh year the land is to have a complete Sabbath rest, a Sabbath to the LORD: you must not sow your field or prune your vineyard.
You must not reap the aftergrowth of your harvest or gather the grapes of your unpruned vine; it is to be a year of complete rest for the land.
The Sabbath produce of the land will be food for you—for you, your male and female servants, your hired worker, and the temporary resident living among you—
and for your livestock and the wild animals in your land. All its yield is to be eaten." "
You are to count off seven Sabbath years—seven times seven years—so the seven Sabbath years amount to forty-nine years.
Then you must sound a ram's horn with a loud blast on the tenth day of the seventh month, on the Day of Atonement; you must sound the horn throughout your land.

You must consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It will be a Jubilee for you: each of you is to return to his own property, and each is to return to his clan.
The fiftieth year will be a Jubilee for you: you must not sow or reap the aftergrowth or gather grapes from the unpruned vines.
Because it is a Jubilee, it is to be holy to you; you may eat its produce from the field.
In this Year of Jubilee, you are to return, each to his own property." "
If you sell property to your neighbor or buy from your neighbor, you must not wrong one another.
You are to buy from your neighbor according to the number of years after the Jubilee, and he is to sell to you according to the number of years of crops.
If the years are many, you must increase the price; if they are few, you must decrease it, because he is selling you a number of harvests.
You must not wrong one another, but fear your God, for I am the LORD your God.
You must keep My statutes and observe My ordinances, and then you will dwell securely in the land.
The land will yield its fruit, you will eat your fill, and you will dwell securely in it.
If you ask, ‘What will we eat in the seventh year if we do not sow or gather our produce?’
I will command My blessing to you in the sixth year, and it will produce a crop sufficient for three years.
You will sow in the eighth year, but you will eat from the old crop until the ninth year; until its crop comes in, you will eat the old.” "
The land must not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is Mine; you are strangers and sojourners with Me.
In all the land you possess, you must allow redemption of the land.
If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his property, his nearest redeemer must come and redeem what his brother sold.
If a man has no one to redeem it, but he himself prospers and finds enough to redeem it,
then he must calculate the years since its sale and refund the excess to the man to whom he sold it, and then return to his property.
But if he cannot secure enough to refund him, what he sold remains in the buyer's hand until the Year of Jubilee; in the Jubilee it is released, and he returns to his property.
If a man sells a house in a walled city, his right of redemption lasts until the end of the year of its sale; for a full year he has the right of redemption.
If it is not redeemed within a full year, the house in the walled city belongs permanently to the buyer and his descendants; it is not released in the Jubilee.
But houses in villages without walls around them are to be counted as fields of the land; they have redemption and are released in the Jubilee.
As for the cities of the Levites, the houses in their possessed cities, the Levites have a permanent right of redemption.

If one of the Levites redeems it, the house that was sold and the city of his possession are released in the Jubilee, because the houses of the Levites' cities are their possession among the Israelites.
But the fields of pastureland around their cities may not be sold, for that is their permanent possession." "
If your brother becomes poor and cannot maintain himself with you, you must support him as a stranger and a sojourner, and he will live with you.
You must not take interest or profit from him, but you must fear your God, so that your brother may live with you.
You must not lend him your money at interest or give him your food for profit.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God." "
If your brother becomes poor beside you and sells himself to you, you must not make him serve as a slave.
He shall be with you as a hired worker and as a sojourner; he shall serve with you until the Year of Jubilee.
Then he and his children with him shall go out from you and return to his clan and to the property of his fathers.
For they are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt; they shall not be sold as slaves.
You must not rule over him ruthlessly, but you must fear your God.
As for your male and female slaves whom you may have—from the nations around you, from them you may buy male and female slaves.
You may also buy from the children of the strangers who sojourn among you, and from their clans that are with you, which they have begotten in your land; they may become your property.

You may leave them as an inheritance to your children after you, to inherit as property; you may make them serve forever. But as for your brothers, the children of Israel, no man shall rule over his brother ruthlessly.
If a stranger or sojourner with you becomes rich, and your brother beside him becomes poor and sells himself to the stranger or sojourner with you, or to a member of the stranger's clan,
after he is sold, he retains the right of redemption; one of his brothers may redeem him,
or his uncle or his cousin may redeem him, or any close relative from his clan may redeem him; or if he prospers, he may redeem himself.

He and his buyer shall count the time from the year he sold himself to him until the Year of Jubilee, and the price of his redemption shall be based on the number of years, with his time treated as that of a hired worker.
If there are still many years, he shall refund his redemption money in proportion to them.
If few years remain until the Year of Jubilee, he shall calculate and refund accordingly.
He shall be with him as a hired worker year by year; he shall not rule ruthlessly over him in your sight.
And if he is not redeemed by these means, then he and his children with him shall go out in the Year of Jubilee.
For the children of Israel are servants to Me; they are My servants whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God."
"Do not make worthless idols for yourselves, nor set up a carved image or a sacred pillar, and do not place a sculptured stone in your land to bow down to it, for I am the LORD your God.
You shall keep My Sabbaths and reverence My sanctuary: I am the LORD."
"If you walk in My statutes and keep My commandments and do them,
then I will give you your rains in their season, and the land shall yield its increase, and the trees of the field shall yield their fruit.
Your threshing shall last to the time of the grape harvest, and the grape harvest shall last to the time of sowing. You shall eat your bread to the full and dwell in your land securely."
"And I will give peace in the land, and you shall lie down, and none shall make you afraid. And I will remove harmful beasts from the land, and the sword shall not go through your land.
You shall chase your enemies, and they shall fall before you by the sword.
Five of you shall chase a hundred, and a hundred of you shall chase ten thousand, and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword."
"I will turn to you and make you fruitful and multiply you and will establish My covenant with you.
You shall eat provisions long stored, and you shall clear out the old to make room for the new."
"I will make My dwelling among you, and My soul shall not abhor you.
And I will walk among you and will be your God, and you shall be My people.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, that you should not be their slaves. And I have broken the bars of your yoke and made you walk upright."
"But if you will not listen to Me and will not do all these commandments,
if you spurn My statutes, and if your soul abhors My rules, so that you will not do all My commandments, but break My covenant,
then I will do this to you: I will visit you with panic, with wasting disease and fever that dim the eyes and drain the life. And you shall sow your seed in vain, for your enemies shall eat it.
I will set My face against you, and you shall be struck down before your enemies. Those who hate you shall rule over you, and you shall flee when none pursues."
"And if in spite of this you will not listen to Me, then I will discipline you sevenfold for your sins.
And I will break your proud strength, and I will make your heavens like iron and your earth like bronze.
And your strength shall be spent in vain, for your land shall not yield its increase, and the trees of the land shall not yield their fruit."
"Then if you remain hostile to Me and will not listen to Me, I will continue striking you, sevenfold, for your sins.
And I will let loose the wild beasts against you, which shall bereave you of your children and destroy your livestock and make you few in number, so that your roads shall be deserted."
"And if by this discipline you are not turned to Me but remain hostile to Me,
then I also will remain hostile to you, and I Myself will strike you sevenfold for your sins.

And I will bring a sword upon you, that shall execute vengeance for the covenant. And if you gather within your cities, I will send pestilence among you, and you shall be delivered into the hand of the enemy.
When I break your supply of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in a single oven and shall dole out your bread by weight, and you shall eat and not be satisfied."
"But if in spite of this you will not listen to Me, but remain hostile to Me,
then I will walk in fury against you, and I Myself will discipline you sevenfold for your sins.
You shall eat the flesh of your sons, and you shall eat the flesh of your daughters."
"And I will destroy your high places and cut down your incense altars and cast your dead bodies upon the dead bodies of your worthless idols, and My soul will abhor you.
And I will lay your cities waste and will make your sanctuaries desolate, and I will not accept your soothing aromas.
And I Myself will devastate the land, so that your enemies who dwell in it shall be appalled.
And I will scatter you among the nations, and I will unsheathe the sword after you, and your land shall be a desolation, and your cities shall be a waste."
"Then the land shall enjoy its Sabbaths as long as it lies desolate, while you are in your enemies' land; then the land shall rest, and enjoy its Sabbaths.
As long as it lies desolate it shall have rest, the rest that it did not have on your Sabbaths when you dwelt on it.

And as for those of you who are left, I will send faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a driven leaf shall put them to flight, and they shall flee as one flees from the sword, and they shall fall when none pursues.
They shall stumble over one another, as if to escape a sword, though none pursues. And you shall have no power to stand before your enemies.
And you shall perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies shall eat you up.
And those of you who are left shall rot away in your enemies' lands because of their iniquity, and also because of the iniquities of their fathers they shall rot away like them."
"But if they confess their iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers in their treachery that they committed against Me, and also in remaining hostile to Me,
so that I opposed them and brought them into the land of their enemies—if then their hardened heart is humbled and they make amends for their iniquity,
then I will remember My covenant with Jacob, and I will remember My covenant with Isaac and My covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land.

But the land shall be abandoned by them and enjoy its Sabbaths while it lies desolate without them, and they shall make amends for their iniquity, because they spurned My rules and their soul abhorred My statutes."

"Yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not spurn them, neither will I abhor them so as to destroy them utterly, and break My covenant with them, for I am the LORD their God.
But I will for their sake remember the covenant with their forefathers, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, that I might be their God: I am the LORD."
These are the statutes and rules and laws that the LORD made between Him and the people of Israel through Moses on Mount Sinai.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When a person makes a special vow to the LORD, the value of the person vowed shall be set according to your valuation.
For a male between twenty and sixty years of age, your valuation shall be fifty shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel.
For a female, your valuation shall be thirty shekels.
If the person is from five to twenty years old, your valuation for a male shall be twenty shekels, and for a female ten shekels.
If the person is from one month to five years old, your valuation for a male shall be five shekels of silver, and for a female three shekels of silver.
If the person is sixty years old or older, your valuation for a male shall be fifteen shekels, and for a female ten shekels.
If he is too poor to pay your valuation, he shall be brought before the priest, and the priest shall value him; according to what the one who vowed can afford, the priest shall value him.
"If it is an animal of the kind that may be offered as an offering to the LORD, all that is given to the LORD shall be holy.
He shall not exchange it or substitute another for it, whether good for bad or bad for good; and if he does substitute animal for animal, then both it and its substitute shall be holy.
If it is any unclean animal that is not offered as an offering to the LORD, he shall bring the animal before the priest.
The priest shall value it, whether good or bad; as the priest values it, so it shall be.
But if he indeed redeems it, he shall add a fifth of its value to your valuation.
When a man dedicates his house as holy to the LORD, the priest shall value it, whether good or bad; as the priest values it, so it shall stand.
If the one who dedicated redeems his house, he shall add a fifth of the money of your valuation to it, and it shall be his.
"If a man dedicates to the LORD a field from his inherited land, the valuation shall be according to the amount of seed required for it: fifty shekels of silver for each homer of barley seed.
If he dedicates his field from the year of Jubilee, it shall stand according to your valuation.

But if he dedicates his field after the Jubilee, the priest shall calculate the money for him according to the years remaining until the year of Jubilee, and a deduction shall be made from your valuation.
If the one who dedicated redeems the field, he shall add a fifth of the money of your valuation to it, and it shall be confirmed to him.
If he does not redeem the field, or if he sells the field to another man, it shall no longer be redeemed.
When the field is released in the Jubilee, it shall be holy to the LORD, like a field devoted to the LORD; the priest shall take possession of it.
If he dedicates to the LORD a field that he has bought, which is not part of his inherited land,
then the priest shall calculate for him the amount of your valuation up to the year of Jubilee, and he shall give your valuation on that day as a holy thing to the LORD.
In the year of Jubilee the field shall return to the one from whom he bought it, to whom the land's possession belongs.
All of your valuations shall be according to the sanctuary shekel: twenty gerahs to the shekel.
"However, no one may dedicate a firstborn among animals, since it is firstborn to the LORD; whether ox or sheep, it belongs to the LORD.
If it is an unclean animal, he shall redeem it according to your valuation and add a fifth to it; if it is not redeemed, it shall be sold according to your valuation.
Nevertheless, anything that a man devotes to the LORD of all that he has, whether person, animal, or inherited field, shall not be sold or redeemed; every devoted thing is most holy to the LORD.
No person devoted to destruction from among mankind shall be redeemed; he shall surely be put to death.
All the tithe of the land, whether from the seed of the land or from the fruit of the trees, belongs to the LORD; it is holy to the LORD.
If a man redeems any of his tithe, he shall add a fifth to it.
All the tithe of the herd or the flock, every tenth animal that passes under the rod, shall be holy to the LORD.
He shall not examine whether it is good or bad, nor shall he substitute for it; and if he does substitute for it, then both it and its substitute shall be holy, and it shall not be redeemed."
These are the commandments that the LORD commanded Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai.
On the first day of the second month in the second year after the Israelites had departed from Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses in the Tent of Meeting in the Wilderness of Sinai, saying:
"Enroll the entire Israelite community according to their clans and ancestral houses, recording every male individually by name.
You and Aaron shall register all men twenty years old and upward who are fit for military service in Israel, each according to his division.
One man from each tribe—each the patriarchal head of his ancestral house—shall assist you.
These are the names of the men who shall serve alongside you: from Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur;
from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab;
from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar;
from Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon;
from the sons of Joseph—from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud, and from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;
from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni;
from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
from Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran;
from Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel;
and from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan."
These men were chosen from the congregation; they were the leaders of their ancestral tribes and the heads of the clans of Israel.
Moses and Aaron took these men, who had been designated by name,

and on the first day of the second month they assembled the whole congregation. The people registered their lineage by clans and ancestral houses, and every male twenty years old and upward was recorded individually by name,
just as the LORD had commanded Moses. Thus he counted them in the Wilderness of Sinai.

From the descendants of Reuben, Israel's firstborn, their lineages were recorded by clans and ancestral houses; every male twenty years of age or older who was fit for military service was listed individually by name.
The number recorded for the tribe of Reuben was 46,500.
From the descendants of Simeon, their lineages were recorded by clans and ancestral houses; every male twenty years of age or older who was fit for military service was listed individually by name.
The number recorded for the tribe of Simeon was 59,300.
From the descendants of Gad, their lineages were recorded by clans and ancestral houses; every male twenty years of age or older who was fit for military service was listed individually by name.
The number recorded for the tribe of Gad was 45,650.
From the descendants of Judah, their lineages were recorded by clans and ancestral houses; every male twenty years of age or older who was fit for military service was listed individually by name.
The number recorded for the tribe of Judah was 74,600.
From the descendants of Issachar, their lineages were recorded by clans and ancestral houses; every male twenty years of age or older who was fit for military service was listed individually by name.
The number recorded for the tribe of Issachar was 54,400.
From the descendants of Zebulun, their lineages were recorded by clans and ancestral houses; every male twenty years of age or older who was fit for military service was listed individually by name.
The number recorded for the tribe of Zebulun was 57,400.

From the descendants of Ephraim, son of Joseph, their lineages were recorded by clans and ancestral houses; every male twenty years of age or older who was fit for military service was listed individually by name.
The number recorded for the tribe of Ephraim was 40,500.
From the descendants of Manasseh, their lineages were recorded by clans and ancestral houses; every male twenty years of age or older who was fit for military service was listed individually by name.
The number recorded for the tribe of Manasseh was 32,200.
From the descendants of Benjamin, their lineages were recorded by clans and ancestral houses; every male twenty years of age or older who was fit for military service was listed individually by name.
The number recorded for the tribe of Benjamin was 35,400.
From the descendants of Dan, their lineages were recorded by clans and ancestral houses; every male twenty years of age or older who was fit for military service was listed individually by name.
The number recorded for the tribe of Dan was 62,700.
From the descendants of Asher, their lineages were recorded by clans and ancestral houses; every male twenty years of age or older who was fit for military service was listed individually by name.
The number recorded for the tribe of Asher was 41,500.
From the descendants of Naphtali, their lineages were recorded by clans and ancestral houses; every male twenty years of age or older who was fit for military service was listed individually by name.
The number recorded for the tribe of Naphtali was 53,400.
These were the men counted by Moses and Aaron, together with the twelve leaders of Israel, each one representing his ancestral house.
Thus all the Israelites twenty years old and upward who were able to serve in Israel's army were counted according to their ancestral houses.
The aggregate of all those enrolled was 603,550.
The Levites, however, were excluded from this enumeration according to their ancestral tribe.
The LORD had said to Moses:
"You must not enumerate the tribe of Levi or register it alongside the other Israelites.

Instead, assign the Levites to the tabernacle of the Testimony and to all its furnishings and everything belonging to it. They shall transport the tabernacle and all its furnishings; they shall attend to it and encamp around it.
Whenever the tabernacle is to be moved, the Levites shall take it down, and whenever it is pitched, they shall set it up. Any unauthorized person who approaches it shall be executed.
The Israelites shall encamp by their divisions, each man in his own camp under his own standard.
The Levites shall encamp around the tabernacle of the Testimony, lest wrath befall the Israelite community; the Levites shall maintain custody of the tabernacle of the Testimony."
The Israelites did all of this just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
“The Israelites shall camp on every side of the Tent of Meeting, each man by his standard, with the banners of his ancestral house.”
On the east side, toward the sunrise, the standard of the camp of Judah shall be pitched by its armies, and the leader of the children of Judah shall be Nahshon son of Amminadab.
His army, whose mustered number was seventy-four thousand six hundred,
shall be joined by the tribe of Issachar, whose leader shall be Nethanel son of Zuar.
His army, whose mustered number was fifty-four thousand four hundred,
shall be joined by the tribe of Zebulun, whose leader shall be Eliab son of Helon.
His army, whose mustered number was fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
All who were numbered for the camp of Judah were one hundred eighty-six thousand four hundred, and they shall set out first.
On the south side shall be the standard of the camp of Reuben by its armies, and the leader of the children of Reuben shall be Elizur son of Shedeur.
His army, whose mustered number was forty-six thousand five hundred,
shall be joined by the tribe of Simeon, whose leader shall be Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
His army, whose mustered number was fifty-nine thousand three hundred,
shall be joined by the tribe of Gad, whose leader shall be Eliasaph son of Reuel.
His army, whose mustered number was forty-five thousand six hundred fifty.
All who were numbered for the camp of Reuben were one hundred fifty-one thousand four hundred fifty, and they shall set out second.
Then the Tent of Meeting shall set out, with the camp of the Levites in the midst of the camps; as they camp, so shall they set out, each man in his place, by his standard.
On the west side shall be the standard of the camp of Ephraim by its armies, and the leader of the children of Ephraim shall be Elishama son of Ammihud.
His army, whose mustered number was forty thousand five hundred,
shall be joined by the tribe of Manasseh, whose leader shall be Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
His army, whose mustered number was thirty-two thousand two hundred,
shall be joined by the tribe of Benjamin, whose leader shall be Abidan son of Gideoni.
His army, whose mustered number was thirty-five thousand four hundred.
All who were numbered for the camp of Ephraim were one hundred eight thousand one hundred, and they shall set out third.
On the north side shall be the standard of the camp of Dan by its armies, and the leader of the children of Dan shall be Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
His army, whose mustered number was sixty-two thousand seven hundred,
shall be joined by the tribe of Asher, whose leader shall be Pagiel son of Ocran.
His army, whose mustered number was forty-one thousand five hundred,
shall be joined by the tribe of Naphtali, whose leader shall be Ahira son of Enan.
His army, whose mustered number was fifty-three thousand four hundred.
All who were numbered for the camp of Dan were one hundred fifty-seven thousand six hundred, and they shall set out last, by their standards.
These are the Israelites who were numbered according to their ancestral houses. All who were numbered of the camps by their armies were six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty.
But the Levites were not numbered among the Israelites, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
So the Israelites did everything the LORD commanded Moses: they camped by their standards, and then set out, each man by his family and by his ancestral house.
These are the genealogical records of Aaron and Moses from the day the LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai.
The names of Aaron's sons were Nadab the firstborn, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
These are the names of Aaron's sons, the anointed priests, whom he ordained to serve as priests.

Nadab and Abihu, however, died in the presence of the LORD when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no sons. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests in the presence of Aaron their father.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
“Bring the tribe of Levi and present them before Aaron the priest to assist him.
They are to guard his duties and the duties of the whole community before the Tent of Meeting, performing the work of the tabernacle.
They are to take charge of all the furnishings of the Tent of Meeting and to perform the duties of the Israelites in carrying out the work of the tabernacle.
Give the Levites to Aaron and his sons; they are wholly given to him from among the Israelites.
Appoint Aaron and his sons to carry out the duties of the priesthood, but any outsider who approaches the sanctuary must be put to death.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
“I have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of every firstborn Israelite who opens the womb. The Levites belong to Me,
for all the firstborn are Mine. On the day I struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, I consecrated to Myself every firstborn in Israel, both human and animal. They are Mine; I am the LORD.”
The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying:
“Count the Levites by their ancestral houses and clans. Count every male a month old or more.”
So Moses counted them according to the word of the LORD, as he had been commanded.
These were the sons of Levi by name: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The sons of Gershon by clans were Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath by clans were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari by clans were Mahli and Mushi. These were the Levite clans according to their ancestral houses.
To Gershon belonged the clans of the Libnites and Shimeites; these were the Gershonite clans.
The number of all males a month old or more was 7,500.
The Gershonite clans were to camp behind the tabernacle on the west.
The leader of the families of the Gershonites was Eliasaph son of Lael.
The duties of the Gershonites at the Tent of Meeting were the tabernacle and tent, its covering, the curtain at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting,
the curtains of the courtyard, the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard surrounding the tabernacle and altar, and the ropes—all the service pertaining to these.
To Kohath belonged the clans of the Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites, and Uzzielites; these were the Kohathite clans.
The number of all males a month old or more was 8,600, and they were responsible for the duties of the sanctuary.
The Kohathite clans were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle.
The leader of the families of the Kohathites was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
Their duties were the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the articles of the sanctuary used in ministering, the curtain, and all the service pertaining to them.
The chief leader of the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron the priest; he oversaw those responsible for the duties of the sanctuary.
To Merari belonged the clans of the Mahlites and Mushites; these were the Merarite clans.
The number of all males a month old or more was 6,200.
The leader of the families of the Merarites was Zuriel son of Abihail; they were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle.
The duties assigned to the sons of Merari were the tabernacle's frames, crossbars, posts, bases, and all its equipment—all the service pertaining to these,
along with the posts of the surrounding courtyard, their bases, tent pegs, and ropes.

Moses, Aaron, and his sons were to camp to the east of the tabernacle, in front of the Tent of Meeting, keeping charge of the sanctuary on behalf of the Israelites; any outsider who approached was to be put to death.
The total number of Levites counted by Moses and Aaron at the command of the LORD, all males a month old or more, was 22,000.
The LORD said to Moses, “Count all the firstborn males of the Israelites a month old or more and list their names.

You are to take the Levites for Me in place of all the firstborn among the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the livestock of the Israelites. I am the LORD.”
So Moses counted all the firstborn males among the Israelites, as the LORD had commanded him,
and the total number of firstborn males a month old or more, listed by name, was 22,273.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
“Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites belong to Me; I am the LORD.
For the redemption of the 273 firstborn Israelites who exceed the number of Levites,
collect five shekels for each one, according to the sanctuary shekel of twenty gerahs.
Give the money to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for the excess.”
So Moses collected the redemption money from those in excess of the number redeemed by the Levites.
He collected 1,365 shekels from the firstborn of the Israelites, according to the sanctuary shekel.
Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons, according to the word of the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.
Then the the LORD addressed Moses and Aaron, saying,
“Conduct a census of the Kohathites among the Levites, by their clans and ancestral families—
men from thirty to fifty years of age, all those eligible to serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
This is the service of the Kohathites at the Tent of Meeting: the most holy things.
“Whenever the camp sets out, Aaron and his sons shall enter, take down the veil of the screen, and cover the ark of the Testimony with it.
Then they shall place over it a covering of fine leather, spread a cloth of solid blue over it, and insert its carrying poles.
Over the table of the Presence they shall spread a blue cloth and place on it the plates, dishes, bowls, and pitchers for the drink offering, together with the continual bread offering.
And they shall spread a scarlet cloth over them, cover them with fine leather, and insert the poles.
They shall take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand that gives light, along with its lamps, wick trimmers, trays, and all the oil vessels used in its service.
Then they shall place it, with all its utensils, inside a covering of fine leather and set it upon the transport frame.
Over the golden altar they shall spread a blue cloth, cover it with fine leather, and insert its poles.
They shall take all the utensils employed in sanctuary service, place them in a blue cloth, cover them with fine leather, and set them upon a transport frame.
They shall remove the ashes from the bronze altar and spread a purple cloth over it.

And they shall place on it all the vessels used for service—the firepans, meat forks, shovels, and sprinkling bowls, every utensil of the altar. Over it they shall spread a covering of fine leather and insert its poles.

“When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the holy objects and all their utensils, as the camp sets out the Kohathites shall come and bear them; yet they must not touch the holy objects, lest they die. These are the bearing responsibilities of the Kohathites concerning the Tent of Meeting.

Eleazar son of Aaron the priest shall have charge of the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering, and the anointing oil. He shall have oversight of the entire tabernacle and everything within it, including the holy objects and their utensils.”
Then the the LORD addressed Moses and Aaron, saying,
“Do not permit the Kohathite clans to be severed from among the Levites.
So that they may live and not die when they approach the most holy things, do this for them: Aaron and his sons shall enter and assign each man his task and what he is to carry.
But the Kohathites shall not enter to look upon the holy objects, even for a moment, or they will die.”
Then the the LORD addressed Moses, saying,
“Likewise, register the Gershonites by their families and clans,
men from thirty to fifty years of age, all those eligible to perform service in the Tent of Meeting.
This is the service of the Gershonite clans pertaining to labor and transport:
They shall carry the curtains of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting with its covering and the covering of fine leather above it, and the screen for the entrance to the Tent of Meeting,

the curtains of the courtyard, the screen for the entrance to the courtyard surrounding the tabernacle and altar, and their ropes, together with all the equipment for their service and everything related to them. They shall perform every aspect of this work.
“All the service of the Gershonites—their loads and their labor—shall be executed under the directive of Aaron and his sons. You shall designate for them every article they are charged to bear.
This is the service of the Gershonite clans at the Tent of Meeting, and their duties shall be under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
“Regarding the Merarites, you shall enumerate them by their clans and families,
men from thirty to fifty years of age, all those eligible to perform service in the Tent of Meeting.
This is the obligation encompassing their entire service at the Tent of Meeting: to carry the frames of the tabernacle, its crossbars, posts, and bases,

as well as the posts of the surrounding courtyard with their bases, tent pegs, and ropes, including all their equipment and all the work related to them. You shall designate by name the articles each individual must transport.
This is the service of the Merarite clans according to all their work at the Tent of Meeting, under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.”
So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of the congregation enumerated the Kohathites by their clans and families,
men from thirty to fifty years of age, all those able to serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
And the number of those registered by their clans was 2,750.
These were the enumerated men of the Kohathite clans, all who could serve at the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron numbered them according to the command of the the LORD through Moses.
Then the Gershonites were enumerated by their clans and families,
men from thirty to fifty years of age, all those able to serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
And the number of those registered by their clans and families was 2,630.
These were the enumerated men of the Gershonite clans, all who could serve at the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron numbered them according to the command of the the LORD.
And the Merarites were enumerated by their clans and families,
men from thirty to fifty years of age, all those able to serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
The number of those registered was 3,200.
These were the enumerated men of the Merarite clans, all who could serve at the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron numbered them according to the command of the the LORD through Moses.
So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel enumerated all the Levites by their clans and families,
men from thirty to fifty years of age, all those able to serve in the labor at the Tent of Meeting and in its transport.
And the number of those registered was 8,580.
At the the LORD’s command, they were numbered by Moses, each man according to his service and his responsibility, as the the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Command the Israelites to expel from the camp every leper, every person afflicted with a discharge, and everyone defiled by contact with a corpse.
You shall remove both men and women; you shall send them outside the camp so that they do not defile the dwelling place where I reside among them.”
And the Israelites complied, sending them outside the camp exactly as the LORD had spoken to Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites: whenever a man or woman commits any transgression common to humanity, thereby acting treacherously against the LORD, that individual stands guilty.
The offender must confess the sin committed, render full restitution for the guilt, augment it by one-fifth, and deliver the total to the person wronged.
Yet if the wronged man has no redeemer to receive restitution, the amount owed to the LORD shall be given to the priest, along with the ram of atonement that procures atonement for him.
Furthermore, every contribution of holy things that the Israelites present to the priest shall belong to him.
Each person’s sacred gifts shall remain his own; whatever anyone offers to the priest shall belong to him.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and declare to them: If a man’s wife strays and proves unfaithful to him,

and another man lies with her, and the affair is concealed from her husband’s eyes so that she is defiled without detection—no witness appearing against her and she not having been apprehended in the act—
and if a spirit of jealousy overcomes him so that he is jealous of his wife, whether she has defiled herself or not,

then the man shall bring his wife to the priest and bring her offering for her: one-tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He shall pour no oil upon it and place no frankincense upon it, because it is a grain offering of jealousy, a memorial offering that summons iniquity to remembrance. “
The priest shall bring her near and station her before the LORD;
he shall take holy water in an earthen vessel, take some dust from the floor of the tabernacle, and put it into the water.

Then the priest shall stand the woman before the LORD, loosen the hair of her head, and place in her hands the memorial grain offering, which is the grain offering of jealousy; in the priest’s hand shall be the water of bitterness that brings a curse. “

The priest shall administer an oath to her and say to the woman, ‘If no man has lain with you and you have not strayed into uncleanness while under your husband, you shall be immune to these waters of bitterness that bring a curse;
but if you have strayed while under your husband and have defiled yourself, and a man other than your husband has lain with you’—

then the priest shall bind the woman under the oath of the curse and say to her, ‘May the LORD make you a curse and an oath among your people when the LORD makes your thigh waste away and your belly swell;
may these waters of bitterness that bring a curse enter your stomach and make your belly swell and your thigh waste away.’ And the woman shall say, ‘Amen, Amen.’ “
The priest shall write these curses in a book and wash them into the water of bitterness.
He shall make the woman drink the water of bitterness that brings a curse, so that it may enter her.
The priest shall take the grain offering of jealousy from the woman’s hand, wave the grain offering before the LORD, and bring it to the altar. “
The priest shall take a handful of the grain offering, its memorial portion, and burn it on the altar; afterward he shall make the woman drink the water.

When she has drunk it, if she has defiled herself and been unfaithful to her husband, the waters of bitterness that bring a curse shall enter her and produce bitterness, her belly shall swell and her thigh shall waste away, and the woman shall become a curse among her people.
But if the woman has not defiled herself and is clean, she shall be free and shall bear children. “
This is the law of jealousy when a wife, while under her husband, goes astray and defiles herself,
or when a spirit of jealousy comes over a man and he is jealous of his wife; then he shall make the woman stand before the LORD, and the priest shall carry out for her all this law.
The man shall be free from guilt, but the woman shall bear her guilt.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the people of Israel and say to them, When a man or woman undertakes a distinctive vow—the vow of a Nazirite—to dedicate himself to the the LORD,
he must abstain from wine and strong drink; he shall drink no vinegar derived from wine or strong drink, and he shall neither drink grape juice nor eat grapes, whether fresh or dried.
Throughout the days of his separation, he shall eat nothing produced by the grapevine, not even its seeds or skins.

Throughout the days of his vow of separation, no razor shall pass over his head; until the period he has consecrated to the the LORD is complete, he shall remain holy, and he shall allow the hair of his head to grow untrimmed.
Throughout the entire period of his dedication to the the LORD, he shall not approach a corpse.
He shall not defile himself even for his father or mother, or for his brother or sister, should they die, because the consecration to God rests upon his head.
Throughout all the days of his separation, he is holy to the the LORD.
"If someone dies suddenly in his presence and thereby defiles his consecrated head, he shall shave his head on the day of his purification; on the seventh day he shall shave it.
On the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting,

and the priest shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, making atonement for him because he incurred guilt through contact with the dead; and he shall reconsecrate his head on that same day.

He shall then dedicate to the the LORD the remaining days of his separation and bring a one-year-old male lamb as a guilt offering; yet the former days shall be forfeited, because his consecration was defiled.
"This is the law governing the Nazirite: when the days of his separation are fulfilled, he shall be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting,

and he shall present his offering to the the LORD: one unblemished male lamb a year old for a burnt offering, one unblemished ewe lamb a year old for a sin offering, and one unblemished ram for a peace offering,
together with a basket of unleavened bread—cakes of fine flour mixed with oil and unleavened wafers spread with oil—along with their grain offering and drink offerings.
The priest shall bring them before the the LORD and present his sin offering and burnt offering,
and he shall offer the ram as a peace offering to the the LORD, along with the basket of unleavened bread; the priest shall also present its grain offering and drink offering.
The Nazirite shall then shave his consecrated head at the entrance to the tent of meeting, take the hair from his head, and place it upon the fire beneath the peace offering.

The priest shall take the shoulder of the ram once it has been boiled, together with one unleavened loaf from the basket and one unleavened wafer, and place them upon the hands of the Nazirite after he has shaved off his hair.

The priest shall wave them as a wave offering before the the LORD; this portion is holy for the priest, together with the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution. Thereafter the Nazirite may drink wine.

This is the law of the Nazirite. If he vows an offering to the the LORD in accordance with his separation, beyond what his means allow, he shall fulfill the vow he has made, in addition to the requirements of his separation."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to Aaron and his sons and tell them: Thus you shall bless the people of Israel: you shall say to them,
The LORD bless you and keep you;
the LORD make His face shine upon you and be gracious to you;
the LORD lift up His countenance upon you and give you peace.
In this way they shall put My name upon the people of Israel, and I will bless them."
On the day Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed and consecrated it, along with all its furnishings, the altar, and all the altar's furnishings.
The leaders of Israel—the heads of their ancestral houses, the tribal leaders who had overseen the census—brought offerings.
They brought their offering before the LORD: six covered wagons and twelve oxen—one wagon for every two leaders and one ox for each leader—and they presented them before the tabernacle.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Receive these from them, that they may be used for the service of the tent of meeting, and give them to the Levites, each man according to his service.”
So Moses took the wagons and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.
He gave two wagons and four oxen to the sons of Gershon, according to their service,
and four wagons and eight oxen to the sons of Merari, according to their service, under Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
But to the sons of Kohath he gave none, because the service of the holy things was their responsibility; they carried them on their shoulders.
The leaders brought the dedication offering for the altar on the day it was anointed, and they presented their offering before the altar.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying, “Each day one leader shall bring his offering for the dedication of the altar.”
On the first day, Nahshon son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah, brought his offering.
His offering was one silver dish weighing 130 shekels, one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
On the second day, Nethanel son of Zuar, leader of the tribe of Issachar, brought his offering.
