His offering was one silver dish weighing 130 shekels, one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Nethanel son of Zuar.
On the third day, Eliab son of Helon, leader of the tribe of Zebulun, brought his offering.
His offering was one silver dish weighing 130 shekels, one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Eliab son of Helon.
On the fourth day, Elizur son of Shedeur, leader of the tribe of Reuben, brought his offering.
His offering was one silver dish weighing 130 shekels, one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Elizur son of Shedeur.
On the fifth day, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai, leader of the tribe of Simeon, brought his offering.
His offering was one silver dish weighing 130 shekels, one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
On the sixth day, Eliasaph son of Deuel, leader of the tribe of Gad, brought his offering.
His offering was one silver dish weighing 130 shekels, one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Eliasaph son of Deuel.
On the seventh day, Elishama son of Ammihud, leader of the tribe of Ephraim, brought his offering.
His offering was one silver dish weighing 130 shekels, one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Elishama son of Ammihud.
On the eighth day, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur, leader of the tribe of Manasseh, brought his offering.
His offering was one silver dish weighing 130 shekels, one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
On the ninth day, Abidan son of Gideoni, leader of the tribe of Benjamin, brought his offering.
His offering was one silver dish weighing 130 shekels, one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Abidan son of Gideoni.
On the tenth day, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai, leader of the tribe of Dan, brought his offering.
His offering was one silver dish weighing 130 shekels, one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
On the eleventh day, Pagiel son of Ochran, leader of the tribe of Asher, brought his offering.
His offering was one silver dish weighing 130 shekels, one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Pagiel son of Ochran.
On the twelfth day, Ahira son of Enan, leader of the tribe of Naphtali, brought his offering.
His offering was one silver dish weighing 130 shekels, one silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Ahira son of Enan.
This was the dedication offering for the altar from the leaders of Israel when it was anointed: twelve silver dishes, twelve silver bowls, and twelve gold dishes.
Each silver dish weighed 130 shekels and each bowl 70 shekels, so all the silver of the vessels was 2,400 shekels by the sanctuary shekel.
The twelve gold dishes, full of incense, weighed 10 shekels each by the sanctuary shekel, so all the gold of the dishes was 120 shekels.
All the cattle for the burnt offering were twelve bulls, twelve rams, and twelve male lambs a year old, with their grain offering; and there were twelve male goats for a sin offering.
All the cattle for the peace offering were twenty-four bulls, sixty rams, sixty male goats, and sixty male lambs a year old. This was the dedication of the altar after it had been anointed.

When Moses went into the tent of meeting to speak with Him, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat that was on the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim; and the LORD spoke to him.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to Aaron and tell him, 'When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps shall shine toward the front of the lampstand.'"
Aaron did so: he set up its lamps so that they shone toward the front of the lampstand, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The lampstand itself was hammered gold, from its base to its blossoms; it was hammered work, fashioned according to the pattern the LORD had shown Moses.
"Take the Levites from among the Israelites and purify them.
This is how you shall purify them: sprinkle on them the water of purification; have them shave their entire bodies and wash their clothes, and they shall be purified.
Then let them take a young bull with its grain offering—fine flour mixed with oil—and you shall take a second young bull for a sin offering.
You shall bring the Levites before the tent of meeting and assemble the whole congregation of the Israelites.
You shall bring the Levites before the LORD, and the Israelites shall lay their hands on the Levites.
Aaron shall present the Levites before the LORD as an offering on behalf of the Israelites, so that they may perform the service of the LORD.
The Levites shall lay their hands on the heads of the bulls; then you shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the LORD, to make atonement for the Levites.
You shall set the Levites before Aaron and his sons, and present them before the LORD as an offering.
Thus you shall separate the Levites from among the Israelites, and the Levites shall be Mine.
After that the Levites shall come to serve in the tent of meeting; you shall purify them and present them as an offering.
For they are wholly given to Me from among the Israelites; in place of every firstborn who opens the womb—every firstborn of the Israelites—I have taken them for Myself.
For all the firstborn among the Israelites are Mine, both human and animal; on the day I struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated them to Myself.
I have taken the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the Israelites.

I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons from among the Israelites, to perform the service of the Israelites in the tent of meeting and to make atonement for the Israelites, so that no plague may strike the Israelites when they approach the sanctuary."
Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation of the Israelites did for the Levites everything the LORD had commanded Moses concerning them; the Israelites did so for them.
The Levites purified themselves and washed their clothes; Aaron presented them as an offering before the LORD, and Aaron made atonement for them to purify them.
After that the Levites came to perform their service in the tent of meeting before Aaron and his sons, just as the LORD had commanded Moses concerning the Levites.
"This is what applies to the Levites: from twenty-five years old and upward they shall enter to perform service in the work of the tent of meeting.
But from the age of fifty years they shall withdraw from the service of the work and shall work no more.
They may, however, assist their brothers in the tent of meeting by keeping guard, but they shall perform no service. Thus you shall deal with the Levites in regard to their duties."
In the first month of the second year after the Israelites had departed from the land of Egypt, the the LORD spoke to Moses in the Wilderness of Sinai, saying,
“Command the Israelites to observe the Passover at its appointed time.
You are to celebrate it at that appointed time—at twilight on the fourteenth day of this month—in full accordance with all its statutes and ordinances.”
Accordingly, Moses instructed the Israelites to observe the Passover,
and they did so in the Wilderness of Sinai at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month. The Israelites carried out everything precisely as the the LORD had commanded Moses.
Yet certain men had become ceremonially unclean through contact with a human corpse, so they could not observe the Passover on that day. They approached Moses and Aaron that same day,
and said to Moses, “Although we are unclean because of a corpse, why should we be deprived of presenting the the LORD’s offering alongside the rest of the Israelites at the appointed time?”
Moses answered them, “Wait here while I ascertain what the the LORD commands concerning you.”
Then the the LORD said to Moses,
“Tell the Israelites that if any one of you or your descendants is unclean because of a corpse, or is away on a distant journey, he may nevertheless observe the Passover to the the LORD.
They are to observe it on the fourteenth day of the second month at twilight, eating it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
They must not leave any of it until morning, nor may they break any of its bones. They are to observe the Passover in accordance with all its statutes.

“But the man who is ceremonially clean and is not on a journey, yet fails to observe the Passover, must be excluded from his people, because he did not present the the LORD’s offering at its appointed time; that man shall bear the guilt of his sin.

If a foreigner residing among you wishes to observe the Passover to the the LORD, he must do so according to the Passover’s statutes and ordinances. You are to have the same statute for the foreigner and for the native of the land.”
On the day the tabernacle was erected, the cloud covered the tabernacle of the Testimony; from evening until morning it had the appearance of fire above the tabernacle.
So it was continually: the cloud covered the tabernacle by day, and by night it appeared like fire.
Whenever the cloud was lifted from over the tabernacle, the Israelites would set out; and wherever the cloud settled, there the Israelites would encamp.
At the command of the the LORD the Israelites set out, and at the command of the the LORD they encamped. As long as the cloud remained over the tabernacle, they remained in camp.
Even when the cloud lingered over the tabernacle for many days, the Israelites kept the the LORD’s charge and did not set out.
At times the cloud remained over the tabernacle for only a few days; at the command of the the LORD they would encamp, and at the command of the the LORD they would set out.
At times the cloud remained only from evening until morning, and when it lifted in the morning, they set out. Whether by day or by night, whenever the cloud was taken up, they set out.
Whether the cloud remained over the tabernacle for two days, a month, or a full year, the Israelites would encamp and not set out; but when it was taken up, they would set out.
They encamped at the command of the the LORD, and they set out at the command of the the LORD. They kept the the LORD’s charge, in accordance with the the LORD’s command through Moses.
Then the LORD said to Moses,
"Make two trumpets of hammered silver for yourself, and use them to summon the congregation and to signal when the camps are to move.
When both are sounded, the whole congregation must assemble before you at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
If only one is sounded, then the leaders—the heads of Israel's clans—must gather before you.
When you sound short blasts, the camps on the east side must set out.
When you sound a second short blast, the camps on the south side must set out; the blasts will signal their movements.
To assemble the congregation, you must sound long blasts, not short ones.
The sons of Aaron, the priests, are to sound the trumpets; this will be a permanent statute for you and your descendants.
When you go to war in your land against an enemy who attacks you, sound short blasts on the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the LORD your God and delivered from your enemies.

On your days of rejoicing, your appointed feasts, and the first day of each month, you are to blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and peace offerings, and they will serve as a reminder for you before your God. I am the LORD your God."
On the twentieth day of the second month of the second year, the cloud lifted from above the tabernacle of the Testimony,
and the Israelites set out from the Desert of Sinai, traveling from place to place until the cloud settled in the Desert of Paran.
They set out for the first time at the LORD's command through Moses.
First, the divisions of the camp of Judah set out under their standard, with Nahshon son of Amminadab in command.
Nethanel son of Zuar was over the division of the tribe of Issachar,
and Eliab son of Helon was over the division of the tribe of Zebulun.
Then the tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonites and Merarites, who carried it, set out.
Next, the divisions of the camp of Reuben set out under their standard, with Elizur son of Shedeur in command.
Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was over the division of the tribe of Simeon,
and Eliasaph son of Deuel was over the division of the tribe of Gad.
Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things; the tabernacle was to be set up before they arrived.
Next, the divisions of the camp of Ephraim set out under their standard, with Elishama son of Ammihud in command.
Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was over the division of the tribe of Manasseh,
and Abidan son of Gideoni was over the division of the tribe of Benjamin.
Finally, the divisions of the camp of Dan set out under their standard, serving as the rear guard for all the camps, with Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai in command.
Pagiel son of Ocran was over the division of the tribe of Asher,
and Ahira son of Enan was over the division of the tribe of Naphtali.
This was the order of march for the Israelite divisions as they set out.

Then Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses' father-in-law, "We are setting out for the place of which the LORD said, 'I will give it to you.' Come with us, and we will treat you well, for the LORD has promised good things to Israel."
"I will not go," he replied. "I am returning to my own country and my own people."
"Please do not leave us," Moses said, "since you know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you can be our eyes.
If you come with us, whatever good the LORD does for us we will share with you."
So they set out from the mountain of the LORD and traveled for three days, and the ark of the covenant of the LORD went before them to seek out a resting place for them.
The cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp.
Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say, "Arise, O the LORD, and let Your enemies be scattered! Let those who hate You flee before You!"
And whenever it came to rest, he would say, "Return, O the LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel."

Now the people complained about their hardships in the hearing of the LORD, and when He heard them, His anger was aroused. Then fire from the LORD burned among them and consumed some of the outskirts of the camp.
When the people cried out to Moses, he prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down.
So that place was called Taberah, because fire from the LORD had burned among them.
The rabble among them began to crave other food, and the Israelites also began to weep again and said, "If only we had meat to eat!"
We remember the fish we ate in Egypt at no cost—the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic.
But now we have lost our appetite; we see nothing but this manna."
The manna resembled coriander seed and looked like resin.
The people went about and gathered it, then ground it in hand mills or crushed it in mortars. They cooked it in pots or made it into cakes, and it tasted like cakes baked with olive oil.
When the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna came down with it.
Moses heard the people weeping, family by family, each at the entrance to his tent. The LORD was very angry, and Moses was distressed.
So he asked the LORD, "Why have You treated Your servant so badly? Why have I not found favor in Your sight, that You lay the burden of all these people on me?
Did I conceive all these people? Did I give birth to them? Why do You tell me to carry them in my arms, as a nurse carries an infant, to the land You swore to their fathers?
Where can I get meat for all these people? They keep weeping to me, 'Give us meat to eat!'
I cannot carry all these people by myself; the burden is too heavy for me.
If You are going to treat me this way, please kill me now—if I have found favor in Your sight—so that I do not have to see my own ruin."
The LORD said to Moses, "Bring Me seventy men from the elders of Israel, men you know to be elders and officers of the people. Bring them to the tent of meeting, and have them stand there with you.

I will come down and speak with you there, and I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put it on them. They will share the people's burden with you, so that you will not have to carry it alone.

Tell the people, 'Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, when you will eat meat. The LORD heard you when you wailed, "If only we had meat to eat! We were better off in Egypt!" Now the LORD will give you meat, and you will eat it.
You will not eat it for just one day, or two days, or five, ten, or twenty days,
but for a whole month—until it makes you sick and you loathe it—because you have rejected the LORD, who is among you, and have wailed before Him, saying, "Why did we ever leave Egypt?"'
But Moses said, "Here I am among six hundred thousand men on foot, and You say, 'I will give them meat to eat for a whole month!'
Would they have enough if flocks and herds were slaughtered for them? Would they have enough if all the fish in the sea were gathered for them?"
The LORD answered Moses, "Is the LORD's power too limited? Now you will see whether what I have said will happen to you."
So Moses went out and told the people what the LORD had said. He gathered seventy men from the elders of the people and stationed them around the tent.

Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke with him, and He took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and put it on the seventy elders. When the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied, but they did not continue.
Two men, however, had remained in the camp. One was named Eldad and the other Medad. The Spirit rested on them as well, though they had not gone out to the tent, and they prophesied in the camp.
A young man ran and told Moses, "Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp."
Joshua son of Nun, who had been Moses' assistant since his youth, spoke up and said, "Moses, my lord, stop them!"
But Moses replied, "Are you jealous for my sake? I wish that all the LORD's people were prophets and that the LORD would put His Spirit on them!"
Then Moses and the elders of Israel returned to the camp.
Now a wind from the LORD drove quail in from the sea and dropped them over the camp, about two cubits above the ground, for about a day's journey in every direction.
All that day and night and all the next day the people went out and gathered quail. No one gathered less than ten homers, and they spread them out all around the camp.
But while the meat was still between their teeth, before it could be consumed, the LORD's anger burned against the people, and He struck them with a severe plague.
So that place was named Kibroth Hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had craved other food.
From Kibroth Hattaavah the people moved on to Hazeroth and stayed there.
Miriam and Aaron began to speak against Moses because of the Cushite woman he had married, for he had married a Cushite woman.
They said, “Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Hasn’t He also spoken through us?” And the LORD heard this.
Now Moses was a very humble man, more humble than anyone else on the face of the earth.
Suddenly the LORD said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, “All three of you, come out to the tent of meeting.” So the three of them went out.
Then the LORD came down in a pillar of cloud, stood at the entrance to the tent, and called Aaron and Miriam. The two of them came forward.
The LORD said, “Listen to My words: If there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, reveal Myself to him in visions; I speak to him in dreams.
Not so with My servant Moses; he is faithful in all My house.
With him I speak face to face—clearly, not in riddles—and he sees the form of the LORD. Why then were you not afraid to speak against My servant Moses?”
The anger of the LORD burned against them, and He departed.
When the cloud lifted from above the tent, Miriam was leprous, white as snow. Aaron turned toward her and saw that she was leprous.
Aaron said to Moses, “Please, my lord, do not hold against us the sin we have so foolishly committed.
Please do not let her be like a stillborn infant whose flesh is half consumed when it comes out of its mother’s womb.”
Moses cried out to the LORD, “O God, please heal her!”
The LORD replied to Moses, “If her father had publicly shamed her, would she not be disgraced for seven days? Let her be confined outside the camp for seven days; after that she may be brought back.”
So Miriam was confined outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not move on until she was brought back.
Afterward the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the Wilderness of Paran.
"Send some men to explore the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites. From each ancestral tribe send one of its leaders."
So at the LORD's command Moses sent them out from the wilderness of Paran. All of them were leaders among the Israelites.
These are their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;
from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori;
from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;
from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;
from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;
from the tribe of Manasseh, a tribe of Joseph, Gaddi son of Susi;
from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;
from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;
from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;
and from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.
These are the names of the men Moses sent to explore the land. Moses gave Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua.
When Moses sent them to explore Canaan, he said, "Go up through the Negev and on into the hill country.
See what the land is like and whether the people who live there are strong or weak, few or many.
What kind of land do they live in? Is it good or bad? What kind of towns do they live in? Are they unwalled or fortified?
How is the soil? Is it fertile or poor? Are there trees in it or not? Do your best to bring back some of the fruit of the land." (It was the season for the first ripe grapes.)
So they went up and explored the land from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, toward Lebo Hamath.
They went up through the Negev and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the descendants of Anak, lived. (Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.)
When they reached the Valley of Eshkol, they cut off a branch bearing a single cluster of grapes. Two of them carried it on a pole between them, along with some pomegranates and figs.
That place was called the Valley of Eshkol because of the cluster the Israelites cut off there.
At the end of forty days they returned from exploring the land.
They came back to Moses and Aaron and the whole Israelite community at Kadesh in the wilderness of Paran. There they reported to them and to the whole assembly and showed them the fruit of the land.
They gave Moses this account: "We went into the land to which you sent us, and it is indeed a land of abundant fertility. Here is its fruit.
But the people who live there are powerful, and the cities are fortified and very large. We even saw descendants of Anak there.
The Amalekites live in the Negev; the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the hill country; and the Canaanites live near the sea and along the Jordan."
Then Caleb silenced the people before Moses and said, "We should go up and take possession of the land, for we can certainly do it."
But the men who had gone up with him said, "We cannot attack those people; they are stronger than we are."
And they spread among the Israelites a bad report about the land they had explored. They said, "The land we explored destroys those who live in it. All the people we saw there are of great size.
We saw the Nephilim there (the descendants of Anak come from the Nephilim). We seemed like grasshoppers in our own eyes, and we looked the same to them."
That night the entire assembly raised a loud cry and wept.
All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole assembly said to them, “If only we had died in Egypt—or even in this wilderness!
Why is the LORD bringing us into this land only to have us fall by the sword? Our wives and children will be taken as plunder. Wouldn’t it be better for us to go back to Egypt?”
And they said to one another, “Let us appoint a leader and go back to Egypt.”
Then Moses and Aaron fell facedown before the whole assembly of the Israelites.
Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had explored the land, tore their clothes.
They said to the whole assembly of the Israelites, “The land we passed through and explored is exceedingly good.
If the LORD is pleased with us, He will bring us into that land and give it to us—a land flowing with milk and honey.

Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not be afraid of the people of the land, for they are helpless before us. Their protection has been removed, and the LORD is with us; do not be afraid of them.”
But the whole assembly threatened to stone them. Then the glory of the LORD appeared at the tent of meeting to all the Israelites.
The LORD said to Moses, “How long will these people treat Me with contempt? How long will they refuse to believe in Me, despite all the signs I have performed among them?
I will strike them with a plague and destroy them, but I will make you into a nation greater and stronger than they.”
Moses said to the LORD, “Then the Egyptians will hear of it! By Your power You brought these people up from among them.

And they will tell the inhabitants of this land. They have heard that You, the LORD, are among these people, for You, the LORD, are seen face to face, and Your cloud stands over them. You go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
Now if You put this entire people to death at once, the nations that have heard of Your fame will say,
‘The LORD was not able to bring these people into the land He promised them on oath, so He slaughtered them in the wilderness.’
Now may the power of the Lord be great, just as You have declared:

‘The LORD is slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, forgiving iniquity and transgression. Yet He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished; He punishes the children for the fathers’ iniquity to the third and fourth generation.’
In accordance with Your great love, forgive the sin of these people, just as You have pardoned them from Egypt until now.”
The LORD replied, “I have forgiven them, as you asked.
Nevertheless, as surely as I live and as surely as the glory of the LORD fills the whole earth,
not one of those who saw My glory and the signs I performed in Egypt and in the wilderness but who disobeyed Me and tested Me ten times—
not one of them will ever see the land I promised on oath to their ancestors. No one who has treated Me with contempt will ever see it.
But because My servant Caleb has a different spirit and follows Me wholeheartedly, I will bring him into the land he went to, and his descendants will inherit it.
Since the Amalekites and Canaanites are living in the valleys, turn back tomorrow and set out toward the wilderness along the route to the Red Sea.”
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
“How long must I endure this wicked community that grumbles against Me? I have heard the complaints the Israelites are making against Me.
Say to them, ‘As surely as I live, declares the LORD, I will do to you exactly what you said in My hearing:
Your corpses will fall in this wilderness—all of you who were counted in the census, twenty years old or more, because you grumbled against Me.
Not one of you will enter the land I swore with uplifted hand to make your home, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
As for your children you said would be taken as plunder, I will bring them in to enjoy the land you have rejected.
But as for you, your bodies will fall in this wilderness.
Your children will wander in the wilderness for forty years and bear the consequences of your unfaithfulness until your bodies perish in the wilderness.
For forty years—one year for each of the forty days you explored the land—you will suffer for your sins and know what it is like to have Me against you.
I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will surely do these things to this whole wicked community, which has banded together against Me. They will perish in this wilderness; here they will die.’”
The men Moses sent to explore the land, who returned and made the whole assembly grumble against him by spreading a bad report about the land—
those very men who were responsible for spreading the bad report about the land were struck down and died of a plague before the LORD.
Of the men who went to explore the land, only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh survived.
When Moses reported this to all the Israelites, they mourned bitterly.
Early the next morning they set out for the hill country, saying, “Here we are; we will go up to the place the LORD promised, for we have sinned.”
But Moses said, “Why are you now disobeying the LORD’s command? It will not succeed.
Do not go up, for the LORD is not with you, and you will be struck down before your enemies.
For the Amalekites and Canaanites are there before you, and you will fall by the sword, because you have turned away from the LORD; therefore the LORD will not be with you.”
Nevertheless, in their presumption they went up toward the top of the mountain, although neither Moses nor the ark of the covenant of the LORD had left the camp.
Then the Amalekites and Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down and attacked them and beat them down all the way to Hormah.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land I am giving you to inhabit,

and you present to the LORD a fire offering from the herd or the flock—an aroma pleasing to the LORD—whether a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering, or at your appointed festivals,
then the one who presents the offering shall bring to the LORD his offering: a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil;
and for the drink offering you shall add a quarter of a hin of wine for each lamb, with the burnt offering or the sacrifice.
For a ram, you shall prepare a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of oil,
and for the drink offering you shall offer a third of a hin of wine, an aroma pleasing to the LORD.
When you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or sacrifice, to fulfill a vow or as a fellowship offering to the LORD,
then with the bull you shall present a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil,
and you shall offer half a hin of wine for the drink offering, a fire offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD.
Thus it shall be done for each bull, ram, lamb, or young goat.
According to the number you prepare, so you shall do for each one.
Every native-born Israelite shall do these things in this way when presenting a fire offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD.
And throughout your generations, if a foreigner residing among you or among your people makes a fire offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD, he shall do just as you do.

For the assembly, there shall be one statute for you and for the foreigner residing among you; it shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations. Before the LORD, you and the foreigner shall be the same.
One law and one ordinance shall apply to you and to the foreigner residing among you."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you come into the land to which I am bringing you,
and you eat of the bread of the land, you shall set apart a contribution to the LORD.
From the first of your dough you shall set apart a cake as a contribution; like the contribution from the threshing floor, so you shall set it apart.
Throughout your generations you shall give to the LORD a contribution from the first of your dough."
"If you unintentionally fail to observe all these commandments that the LORD has spoken to Moses—
everything that the LORD has commanded you through Moses, from the day the LORD gave the command and onward throughout your generations—

and if it was done unintentionally without the knowledge of the community, then the whole community shall offer one young bull as a burnt offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD, with its grain offering and drink offering according to the ordinance, and one male goat for a sin offering.

The priest shall make atonement for the whole community of Israelites, and they shall be forgiven, because it was unintentional, and they have brought their offering, a fire offering to the LORD, and their sin offering before the LORD for their unintentional sin.
The whole community of Israelites shall be forgiven, and the foreigner residing among them, because all the people acted unintentionally.
"If one person sins unintentionally, he shall offer a female goat a year old for a sin offering.
The priest shall make atonement before the LORD for the person who erred through unintentional sin, to make atonement for him, and he shall be forgiven.
You shall have one law for the native-born among the Israelites and for the foreigner residing among them, for anyone who acts unintentionally.
"But the person who acts defiantly, whether native-born or foreigner, reviles the LORD; that person shall be removed from among his people.
Because he has despised the word of the LORD and has broken His commandment, his guilt shall remain on him."
While the Israelites were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
Those who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses, Aaron, and the whole community.
They put him in custody, because it had not been declared what should be done to him.
The LORD said to Moses, "The man shall surely be put to death; the whole community shall stone him with stones outside the camp."
So the whole community brought him outside the camp and stoned him with stones, and he died, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: Throughout your generations you shall make tassels on the corners of your garments, and you shall put a blue cord on the tassel of each corner.

The tassels shall be for you a reminder, so that you will remember all the commandments of the LORD and do them, and so that you will not follow after your own hearts and your own eyes, by which you are led into unfaithfulness.
Thus you shall remember and do all My commandments and be holy to your God.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God."
Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, together with Dathan and Abiram sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, descendants of Reuben, took 250 men of Israel—
leaders of the congregation, chosen from the assembly, men of renown—and confronted Moses.

They assembled against Moses and Aaron and said to them, “You have gone too far! For all the congregation is holy, every one of them, and the LORD is among them. Why then do you exalt yourselves above the assembly of the LORD?”
When Moses heard this, he fell facedown.

Then he said to Korah and all his followers, “In the morning the LORD will show who belongs to Him and who is holy, and He will bring that person near to Himself. The one He chooses, He will bring near to Himself.”
“Do this: take censers for yourselves, Korah and all his company,
and tomorrow put fire and incense on them before the LORD. The man whom the LORD chooses will be the holy one. You Levites have gone too far!”
Moses also said to Korah, “Listen now, you sons of Levi:

is it too small a thing for you that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel, to bring you near to Himself, to perform the service of the LORD’s tabernacle, and to stand before the congregation to minister to them?
“He has brought you near, along with all your fellow Levites, and now you seek the priesthood as well?
Therefore you and all your company are gathered together against the LORD. And who is Aaron, that you grumble against him?”
Moses sent to summon Dathan and Abiram sons of Eliab, but they said, “We will not come up.”
“Was it not enough that you brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey to die in the wilderness? Must you also make yourself a prince over us?
Moreover, you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey or given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards. Will you gouge out the eyes of these men? We will not come up.”
Moses was very angry and said to the LORD, “Do not regard their grain offering. I have not taken one donkey from them, nor have I wronged any of them.”
Moses said to Korah, “You and all your congregation are to be present before the LORD tomorrow—you and they, along with Aaron.
Let each man take his censer, put incense on it, and bring it before the LORD—250 censers in all. You as well, and Aaron, each with his censer.”
So each man took his censer, put fire in it, laid incense on it, and stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting with Moses and Aaron.
Korah assembled the whole congregation against them at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD appeared to the entire congregation.
Then the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
“Separate yourselves from this congregation, so that I may consume them in a moment.”
They fell facedown and said, “O God, God of the spirits of all flesh, if one man sins, will You be angry with the whole congregation?”
“Speak to the congregation and say, ‘Move away from the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.’”
Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel followed him.
He said to the congregation, “Please move away from the tents of these wicked men and touch nothing that belongs to them, lest you be swept away in all their sins.”
So they moved away from the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrance of their tents with their wives, sons, and little ones.
Moses said, “By this you shall know that the LORD has sent me to do all these works, for they are not from my own mind.
If these men die the death of all men, or if they suffer the common fate of all mankind, then the LORD has not sent me.

But if the LORD creates something new, and the ground opens its mouth and swallows them and all that belongs to them, and they go down alive into Sheol, then you shall know that these men have despised the LORD.”
As soon as he finished speaking all these words, the ground beneath them split apart.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households, all Korah’s men and all their possessions.
They went down alive into Sheol, and the earth closed over them; they vanished from the midst of the assembly.
All Israel around them fled at their cry, for they said, “Lest the earth swallow us too!”
Fire came out from the LORD and consumed the 250 men who were offering the incense.
“Tell Eleazar son of Aaron the priest to remove the censers from the burning and scatter the fire some distance away, for they are holy.

As for the censers of these men who sinned at the cost of their lives, let them be hammered into sheets as a covering for the altar, because they were presented before the LORD and became holy. They shall be a sign to the Israelites.”
So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers that had been presented by the men who were burned, and they were hammered into a covering for the altar,

as a reminder to the Israelites that no outsider who is not a descendant of Aaron should come near to burn incense before the LORD, lest he become like Korah and his company, just as the LORD had told Moses.
The next day the whole congregation of the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, saying, “You have killed the people of the LORD.”
When the congregation had assembled against Moses and Aaron, they turned toward the tent of meeting, and behold, the cloud covered it, and the glory of the LORD appeared.
Moses and Aaron came to the front of the tent of meeting,
and the LORD spoke to Moses:
“Withdraw from this congregation, so that I may consume them in a moment.” Then they fell facedown.

Moses said to Aaron, “Take the censer, put fire on it from the altar, lay incense on it, and hurry to the congregation to make atonement for them, for wrath has gone out from the LORD; the plague has begun.”
Aaron took it as Moses had said, ran into the midst of the assembly, and saw that the plague had already begun among the people. He put on the incense and made atonement for the people.
He stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stopped.
Those who died by the plague numbered 14,700, besides those who died on account of Korah.
Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and the plague was stopped.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and obtain from them twelve staffs, one from the leader of each ancestral house; write each man’s name on his staff.
Write Aaron’s name on the staff of Levi, for there is one staff for the head of each ancestral house.
Place them in the Tent of Meeting before the Testimony, where I meet with you.
The staff of the man I choose will sprout, and I will rid Myself of the Israelites’ complaints that they are making against you.”
So Moses spoke to the Israelites, and each of their leaders gave him a staff—one for each leader of their ancestral houses—twelve staffs in all. Aaron’s staff was among them.
Moses placed the staffs before the LORD in the Tent of the Testimony.
The next day Moses entered the Tent of the Testimony and saw that Aaron’s staff for the house of Levi had sprouted, putting forth buds, blossoming, and bearing ripe almonds.
Then Moses brought all the staffs out from before the LORD to all the Israelites. They looked at them, and each man took his own staff.
The LORD said to Moses, “Put Aaron’s staff back before the Testimony, to be kept as a sign for the rebellious, so that their complaints against Me may cease and they will not die.”
Moses did just as the LORD had commanded him.
Then the Israelites said to Moses, “Behold, we are perishing! We are lost; we are all lost!
Anyone who approaches the tabernacle of the LORD will die. Are we all going to perish?”
The LORD said to Aaron, “You and your sons and your father’s house with you shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary, and you and your sons with you shall bear the iniquity of your priesthood.
Bring near to you your brothers, the tribe of Levi, your father’s tribe, and let them be joined to you and minister to you, while you and your sons with you stand before the tent of the testimony.
They shall keep your charge and the charge of the whole tent, but they must not come near the holy vessels or the altar, lest they die—and you with them.
They shall be joined to you and keep the charge of the tent of meeting for all its service, and no stranger shall approach you. “
You shall keep the charge of the sanctuary and the charge of the altar, so that wrath does not fall on the Israelites.
Behold, I have taken your brothers the Levites from among the Israelites; they are a gift to you, given to the LORD, to do the service of the tent of meeting.

You and your sons with you shall keep your priesthood for everything concerning the altar and for what is within the veil, and you shall serve. I give your priesthood as a gift, and any stranger who approaches shall be put to death.”
The LORD spoke to Aaron: “Behold, I have given you charge of My contributions; I have given you all the holy things of the Israelites as your portion and your sons’ portion, as an anointing forever.

This shall be yours from the most holy things, from the offerings made by fire: every offering of theirs, every grain offering, every sin offering, and every guilt offering that they render to Me shall be most holy for you and your sons.
You shall eat it in the most holy place; every male shall eat it. It shall be holy to you.

This also is yours: the contribution from their gifts, all the wave offerings of the Israelites. I have given them to you, your sons, and your daughters with you, as a perpetual statute. Everyone who is clean in your house may eat it. “
All the best of the fresh oil, all the best of the new wine and grain, their firstfruits that they give to the LORD, I have given to you.
The firstfruits of all that is in their land, which they bring to the LORD, shall be yours; everyone who is clean in your house may eat it.
Every devoted thing in Israel shall be yours.

Everything that opens the womb of all flesh, whether man or beast, which they offer to the LORD, shall be yours; nevertheless, the firstborn of man you shall redeem, and the firstborn of an unclean animal you shall redeem.
Their redemption price, from one month old, you shall redeem according to your valuation: five shekels of silver, by the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs.

But the firstborn of an ox, a sheep, or a goat you shall not redeem; they are holy. You shall sprinkle their blood on the altar and burn their fat as an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
Their meat shall be yours, as the breast of the wave offering and the right thigh are yours.

All the holy contributions that the Israelites raise to the LORD I have given to you, your sons, and your daughters with you, as a perpetual statute. It is a perpetual covenant before the LORD for you and your offspring with you.”
The LORD said to Aaron, “You shall have no inheritance in their land, nor shall you have any portion among them. I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites.” “
Behold, I have given the Levites all the tithe in Israel as an inheritance, in return for the service they perform, the service of the tent of meeting.
The Israelites must no longer approach the tent of meeting, lest they incur guilt and die.

The Levites shall perform the service of the tent of meeting, and they shall bear their own iniquity. It shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations, and they shall have no inheritance among the Israelites.

For the tithe that the Israelites raise to the LORD as a contribution I have given to the Levites as their inheritance. That is why I have said of them, ‘They shall have no inheritance among the Israelites.’”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

“Speak to the Levites and say to them, ‘When you receive from the Israelites the tithe that I have given you from them as your inheritance, you shall present from it a contribution to the LORD—a tithe of the tithe.
Your contribution shall be reckoned to you as grain from the threshing floor and as the full produce of the winepress.
Thus you shall also present a contribution to the LORD from all your tithes that you receive from the Israelites, and from it you shall give the LORD’s contribution to Aaron the priest.
From all the gifts you receive, you shall present every contribution to the LORD, all its best part, its holy portion.’
Say to them, ‘When you have presented its best part, it shall be reckoned to the Levites as the produce of the threshing floor and of the winepress.
You may eat it anywhere, you and your households, for it is your reward in return for your service in the tent of meeting.
You shall bear no sin because of it when you have presented its best part, and you shall not profane the holy things of the Israelites, lest you die.’”
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
“This is the statute of the law that the the LORD has commanded: Tell the Israelites to bring you a red heifer without blemish, without defect, and upon which no yoke has ever been laid.
“Give it to Eleazar the priest, and he shall take it outside the camp and slaughter it in his presence.
Then Eleazar the priest is to take some of its blood on his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the Tent of Meeting.
Then the heifer shall be burned in his sight; its hide, flesh, and blood, along with its dung, shall be burned.
The priest is to take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet yarn and cast them into the fire consuming the heifer.
“Then the priest must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water; afterward he may enter the camp, though he remains unclean until evening.
The one who burned the heifer must likewise wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he too remains unclean until evening.

“Then a man who is ceremonially clean shall gather the ashes of the heifer and deposit them in a clean place outside the camp. They are to be kept for the congregation of Israel for use in the water of purification; it is for purification from sin.
The man who gathers the ashes of the heifer must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening. This is a permanent statute for the Israelites and for the foreigner residing among them.”
“Whoever touches any dead body shall be unclean for seven days.
He must purify himself with the water on the third day and on the seventh day; then he will be clean. But if he does not purify himself on the third and seventh days, he will not be clean.

Anyone who touches a corpse—the body of a person who has died—and does not purify himself defiles the tabernacle of the the LORD; that person must be cut off from Israel. He remains unclean because the water of purification has not been sprinkled upon him, and his uncleanness still rests upon him.
“This is the law when a man dies in a tent: everyone who enters the tent and everyone already in the tent shall be unclean for seven days.
Any open vessel that has no lid fastened upon it is unclean.
Anyone in the open field who touches one slain by the sword, or a dead person, or a human bone, or a grave, shall be unclean for seven days.”
“For the unclean person, they shall take some of the ashes of the burnt sin offering and place them in a vessel of fresh water.

Then a ceremonially clean person is to take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it upon the tent, upon all the furnishings, upon the people who were there, and upon anyone who touched a bone, a slain person, or a grave.

The clean person shall sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day; after he has purified himself on the seventh day, he must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be clean by evening.

“But if a person who is unclean does not purify himself, he will be cut off from the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the the LORD. The water of purification has not been sprinkled upon him; he is unclean.
This is a permanent statute for them. The one who sprinkles the water of purification must wash his clothes, and whoever touches the water of purification will be unclean until evening.
Anything the unclean person touches will become unclean, and anyone who touches it will be unclean until evening.”
In the first month, the whole congregation of the Israelites came into the Wilderness of Zin, and the people settled at Kadesh. There Miriam died and was buried.
Because there was no water for the congregation, they gathered against Moses and Aaron.
The people quarreled with Moses and said, "If only we had died when our brothers died before the LORD!
Why have you brought the LORD's assembly into this wilderness, so that we and our livestock should die here?
Why did you bring us up out of Egypt to this wretched place—a place with no grain, figs, vines, or pomegranates, and no water to drink?"
Moses and Aaron went from the presence of the assembly to the entrance of the tent of meeting and prostrated themselves. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to them.
And the LORD spoke to Moses:

"Take the staff and assemble the congregation—you and your brother Aaron. Speak to the rock before their eyes, and it will yield its water. You shall bring water out of the rock for them and give drink to the congregation and their livestock."
So Moses took the staff from before the LORD, just as He had commanded him.
Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly before the rock, and Moses said to them, "Listen now, you rebels! Shall we bring water out of this rock for you?"
Then Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff, and abundant water gushed out, so that the congregation and their livestock drank.
But the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "Because you did not believe in Me, to honor Me as holy in the sight of the Israelites, you shall not bring this assembly into the land I have given them."
These are the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites quarreled with the LORD, and He proved Himself holy among them.
From Kadesh, Moses sent messengers to the king of Edom: "Thus says your brother Israel: 'You know all the hardship that has befallen us—
how our fathers went down to Egypt and we lived there many years, and the Egyptians mistreated us and our fathers.
We cried out to the LORD, and He heard our voice and sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now here we are at Kadesh, a city on the edge of your border.

Please let us pass through your land. We will not pass through any field or vineyard, nor drink water from any well. We will travel along the king's highway and will not deviate to the right or to the left until we have crossed your territory.'"
But Edom said to him, "You shall not pass through me, or I will attack you with the sword."
The Israelites replied, "We will go up by the highway, and if we or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. Only let us pass through on foot; we ask for nothing more."
But Edom insisted, "You shall not pass through." Then Edom marched out against them with a large and powerful army.
So Edom refused to allow Israel to pass through his territory, and Israel turned away from him.
They set out from Kadesh, and the whole congregation of the Israelites came to Mount Hor.
At Mount Hor, on the border of Edom, the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Aaron will die and be gathered to his ancestors, for he shall not enter the land I have given to the Israelites, because you rebelled against My command at the waters of Meribah.
Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up to Mount Hor.
Remove Aaron's garments and put them on Eleazar his son; Aaron will die there."
Moses did as the LORD commanded. They went up Mount Hor in the sight of the whole congregation.
Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son. Aaron died there on the top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
When the whole congregation saw that Aaron had died, all the house of Israel wept for Aaron thirty days.
When the Canaanite king of Arad, who dwelt in the Negev, learned that Israel was advancing along the route of Atharim, he attacked Israel and carried off some of its people as captives.
Then Israel made a vow to the LORD and said, "If You will indeed give this people into my hand, then I will utterly destroy their cities."
The LORD heeded Israel's plea and delivered the Canaanites into their power; Israel then devoted them and their cities to destruction, and the place was named Hormah.
The people then journeyed from Mount Hor along the route to the Red Sea in order to skirt Edom, but they grew impatient along the way.
The people spoke against God and Moses, saying, "Why did You bring us up from Egypt only to die in this wilderness? There is no bread and no water, and we have come to loathe this wretched bread."
Therefore The LORD sent fiery serpents among the people; they bit the people, and many Israelites died.

Then the people came to Moses and said, "We have sinned, for we have spoken against the LORD and against you; pray to the LORD that He may remove the serpents from us." So Moses interceded for the people.
The LORD said to Moses, "Make a fiery serpent and set it on a pole; everyone who is bitten, when he looks at it, shall live."
So Moses made a bronze serpent and set it on a pole; and if a serpent bit anyone, he would look at the bronze serpent and live.
The Israelites set out and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim in the wilderness opposite Moab, to the east.
From there they set out and camped in the Valley of Zered.
From there they set out and camped beyond the Arnon, which lies in the wilderness extending from the territory of the Amorites; for the Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
Therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of the LORD, "Waheb in Suphah, and the valleys of the Arnon,
and the ravines of the streams that slope toward the settlement at Ar and lean against the border of Moab."
From there they went to Beer; that is the well of which the LORD said to Moses, "Gather the people together, and I will give them water."
Then Israel sang this song: "Spring up, O well—sing to it!
The well that the princes dug, that the nobles of the people sank, with their scepters and staffs." From the wilderness they went to Mattanah,
and from Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth,
and from Bamoth to the valley that is in the field of Moab, to the top of Pisgah, which looks down on the wasteland.
Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,
"Let me pass through your land. We will not turn aside into field or vineyard; we will not drink water from wells. We will go by the King's Highway until we have passed through your territory."
But Sihon would not allow Israel to pass through his territory. So Sihon gathered all his people and went out against Israel in the wilderness, and came to Jahaz, and fought against Israel.
Israel struck him down by the sword and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the Ammonites, for the border of the Ammonites was strong.
Israel took all these cities, and Israel dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon and in all its surrounding towns.
For Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab and taken all his land from him as far as the Arnon.
Therefore those who speak in proverbs say, "Come to Heshbon; let it be rebuilt; let the city of Sihon be established.
For fire went out from Heshbon, a flame from the city of Sihon. It consumed Ar of Moab, and the lords of the heights of the Arnon.
Woe to you, Moab! You are undone, O people of Chemosh! He has given his sons as fugitives, and his daughters into captivity, to Sihon king of the Amorites.
We have overthrown them; Heshbon has perished as far as Dibon; we have laid waste as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba."
Thus Israel dwelt in the land of the Amorites.
Moses sent men to spy out Jazer, and they captured its towns and dispossessed the Amorites who were there.
Then they turned and went up by the way of Bashan. Og the king of Bashan came out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.

But the LORD said to Moses, "Do not be afraid of him, for I have given him into your hand, and all his people, and his land; and you shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt at Heshbon."
So they struck him and his sons and all his people, until no survivor remained, and they took possession of his land.
The Israelites set out and camped in the plains of Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho.
Balak son of Zippor saw everything Israel had done to the Amorites.
Moab was terrified of the people, because they were numerous, and Moab dreaded the Israelites.
So Moab said to the elders of Midian, “Now this horde will consume everything around us, as an ox grazes the grass of the field.” Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.

He sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor at Pethor, near the River, in the land of his people, to summon him, saying, “Look, a people has come out of Egypt. They cover the surface of the earth and are dwelling opposite me.

Come now and curse this people for me, because they are too mighty for me. Perhaps I can defeat them and drive them from the land, for I know that whomever you bless is blessed, and whomever you curse is cursed.”
The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian departed with divination fees in their hands. They came to Balaam and relayed Balak’s words.
He said to them, “Stay here tonight, and I will bring you word as the LORD speaks to me.” So the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam.
Then God came to Balaam and asked, “Who are these men with you?”
Balaam said to God, “Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, has sent to me and says
that a people has come out of Egypt and covers the surface of the earth; he asks me to curse them for him, so he can fight them and drive them out.”
God said to Balaam, “You must not go with them, and you must not curse the people, for it is blessed.”
In the morning Balaam rose and said to Balak’s princes, “Go back to your land, for the LORD refuses to let me go with you.”
The princes of Moab rose, went to Balak, and said, “Balaam refuses to come with us.”
Then Balak sent more princes, more numerous and more distinguished than the first.
They came to Balaam and said, “Balak son of Zippor asks you not to refuse to come to him.
He promises to honor you richly and to do whatever you say to him, and he asks you to curse this people for him.”
Balaam answered Balak’s servants, “Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not transgress the word of the LORD my God, to do anything small or great.
Now please stay here tonight as well, so I may learn what more the LORD will say to me.”
That night God came to Balaam and said, “If the men have come to call you, rise and go with them; but do only the word I speak to you.”
In the morning Balaam rose, saddled his donkey, and went with the princes of Moab.
Then God’s anger was kindled because he was going, and the angel of the LORD stood in the road as an adversary against him. He was riding on his donkey, and his two servants were with him.

The donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand. The donkey turned aside from the road and went into the field, and Balaam struck the donkey to turn her back onto the road.
Then the angel of the LORD stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, with a wall on either side.
When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she pressed against the wall and crushed Balaam’s foot against it, so he struck her again.
The angel of the LORD went farther and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn to the right or to the left.
When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she lay down under Balaam. Balaam’s anger was kindled, and he struck the donkey with his staff.
Then the LORD opened the donkey’s mouth, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?”
Balaam said to the donkey, “Because you mocked me. If I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you now.”
The donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not your donkey, which you have ridden all your life until today? Have I ever been accustomed to do this to you?” He said, “No.”
Then the LORD opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand. He bowed down and fell on his face.
The angel of the LORD said to him, “Why have you struck your donkey these three times? Look, I have come out to oppose you, because your way is perverse before me.
The donkey saw me and turned aside before me these three times. If she had not turned aside from me, I would surely have killed you and spared her.”
Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, “I have sinned, for I did not know you were standing in the road against me. Now if it is evil in your sight, I will turn back.”
The angel of the LORD said to Balaam, “Go with the men, but speak only the word I tell you.” So Balaam went with the princes of Balak.
When Balak heard that Balaam had come, he went out to meet him at the city of Moab, on the border of the Arnon, at the farthest boundary.
Balak said to Balaam, “Did I not earnestly send to you to call you? Why did you not come to me? Am I not able to honor you?”
Balaam said to Balak, “Look, I have come to you. Now, do I have any power at all to speak anything? The word that God puts in my mouth, that I will speak.”
Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.
Balak sacrificed oxen and sheep and sent some to Balaam and to the princes who were with him.
In the morning Balak took Balaam and brought him up to the high places of Baal, and from there he saw the edge of the people.
Balaam said to Balak, “Construct seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me.”
Balak did exactly as Balaam requested, and the two of them offered a bull and a ram on each altar.

“Remain here beside your burnt offering,” Balaam told Balak, “while I step aside. Perhaps the the LORD will meet me, and whatever He reveals, I will report to you.” So Balaam went off to a barren height.
God met Balaam, and Balaam said to Him, “I have arranged seven altars, and I have offered a bull and a ram on each.”
Then the the LORD put a word in Balaam's mouth and said, “Return to Balak and speak as I command.”
So Balaam returned to Balak, who was standing beside his burnt offering with all the princes of Moab.
Then Balaam lifted up his oracle and said, “Balak, king of Moab, has brought me from Aram, from the mountains of the east, saying, ‘Come, curse Jacob for me; come, denounce Israel.’
How can I curse those whom God has not cursed? How can I denounce those whom the the LORD has not denounced?
For I see them from the summit of the rocks, and from the heights I behold them. Behold, a people dwelling apart, not counted among the nations.
Who can number Jacob's countless descendants, or count even a quarter of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous, and may my end be like theirs!”
Then Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I brought you to curse my enemies, yet you have blessed them thoroughly!”
Balaam answered, “Must I not speak exactly what the the LORD puts in my mouth?”
Balak said to him, “Please come with me to another place, from which you can see them. You will see only a portion of them, not all of them; and from there curse them for me.”
So Balak took him to the field of Zophim, on the summit of Pisgah, and built seven altars there, offering a bull and a ram on each.
“Remain here beside your burnt offering,” Balaam said to Balak, “while I meet the the LORD over there.”
The The LORD met Balaam and put a word in his mouth, saying, “Return to Balak and speak as I command.”
So Balaam returned to Balak, who was standing beside his burnt offering with the princes of Moab. “What did the the LORD say?” Balak asked.
Then Balaam lifted up his oracle and said, “Arise, Balak, and listen; give ear to me, son of Zippor.
God is not a man, that He should lie, nor a son of man, that He should change His mind. Does He speak and not act? Does He promise and not fulfill?
Behold, I have received a command to bless; He has blessed, and I cannot revoke it.
He has seen no iniquity in Jacob, and no trouble in Israel. The The LORD their God is with them, and the shout of a king is among them.
God brought them out of Egypt; they have the strength of a wild ox.
For there is no sorcery against Jacob and no divination against Israel. It will now be said of Jacob and Israel, ‘What has God wrought!’
Behold, the people rise like a lioness; they rouse themselves like a lion. They will not lie down until they devour the prey and drink the blood of the slain.”
Then Balak said to Balaam, “Do not curse them at all, and do not bless them at all!”
Balaam answered, “Did I not tell you, ‘All that the the LORD speaks, I must do’?”
Balak said to Balaam, “Please come; I will take you to another place. Perhaps it will please God to let you curse them for me from there.”
So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, overlooking the wasteland.
Balaam said to Balak, “Construct seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me.”
Balak did as Balaam said and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
When Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not resort to sorcery as he had on previous occasions, but turned his face toward the wilderness.
Balaam lifted his eyes and saw Israel encamped tribe by tribe, and the Spirit of God came upon him.
He lifted up an oracle and said: “This is the oracle of Balaam son of Beor, the oracle of the man whose eyes are open—
the oracle of one who hears the words of God, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who falls prostrate with eyes uncovered:
How beautiful are your tents, O Jacob, your tabernacles, O Israel!
They spread out like valleys, like gardens beside a river, like aloes the LORD has planted, like cedars beside the waters.
Water will flow from their buckets, and their seed will have abundant water. Their king will be greater than Agag, and their kingdom will be exalted.
God brought them out of Egypt; they have the strength of a wild ox. They devour hostile nations and crush their bones; they pierce them with arrows.
They crouch and lie down like a lion, like a lioness—who dares to rouse them? Blessed are those who bless you, and cursed are those who curse you!”
Then Balak’s anger burned against Balaam, and he struck his hands together. Balak said to Balaam, “I summoned you to curse my enemies, but you have persisted in blessing them these three times!
Now get up and go home! I said I would richly reward you, but the LORD has withheld your reward.”
Balaam answered Balak, “Did I not tell the messengers you sent me:
‘Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the command of the LORD to do good or evil of my own accord; I must speak only what the LORD says’?
Now I am returning to my people, but come, let me warn you what this people will do to your people in the days to come.”
Then he lifted up an oracle and said: “This is the oracle of Balaam son of Beor, the oracle of the man whose eyes are open—
the oracle of one who hears the words of God and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who falls prostrate with eyes uncovered:
I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star will come forth from Jacob, and a scepter will arise from Israel. He will crush the foreheads of Moab and destroy all the sons of Sheth.
Edom will become a possession; Seir, his enemies, will also become a possession; but Israel will perform valiantly.
One from Jacob will rule and destroy the survivors of the city.”
Then he looked at Amalek and lifted up an oracle, saying: “Amalek was first among the nations, but his end will be destruction.”
Then he looked at the Kenites and lifted up an oracle, saying: “Your dwelling place is secure, and your nest is set in a cliff.
Yet Kain will be destroyed when Asshur takes you captive.”
Then he lifted up an oracle and said: “Alas, who can live when God does this?
Ships will come from the coast of Kittim; they will subdue Asshur and Eber, but they too will perish.”
Then Balaam arose and departed, returning to his home, and Balak also went his own way.
While Israel was encamped at Shittim, the people began to engage in promiscuity with the Moabite women.
These women invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate and bowed down to those gods.
Thus Israel yoked itself to Baal of Peor, and the LORD's anger burned against Israel.
The LORD said to Moses, "Take all the leaders of the people and hang them in the sun before the LORD, so that the fierce anger of the LORD may turn away from Israel."
So Moses said to the judges of Israel, "Each of you must kill those men of his who have yoked themselves to Baal of Peor."
Then an Israelite man brought a Midianite woman to his relatives in the sight of Moses and of the whole congregation of the Israelites while they were weeping at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
When Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw this, he rose from the midst of the congregation, took a spear in his hand,
and followed the Israelite man into the tent, where he pierced both of them—the Israelite man and the woman—through her belly. Thus the plague was stopped among the Israelites.
Those who died by the plague numbered twenty-four thousand.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

"Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned My wrath away from the Israelites, because he was jealous with My jealousy among them, so that I did not consume the Israelites in My zeal.
Therefore say, 'Behold, I give him My covenant of peace.
It shall be to him and to his descendants after him a covenant of perpetual priesthood, because he was jealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites.'"
The name of the Israelite who was slain, he who was slain with the Midianite woman, was Zimri son of Salu, a leader of a Simeonite family.
The name of the Midianite woman who was slain was Cozbi daughter of Zur, who was head of a clan among the Midianites.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

for they have harassed you with their schemes, by which they deceived you in the matter of Peor and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite leader, their sister who was slain on the day of the plague because of Peor."
After the plague, the LORD said to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron, the priest,
“Take a census of the whole congregation of the Israelites, from twenty years old and upward, by their ancestral houses—all in Israel who are able to go to war.”
So Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,
“Take a census of the people from twenty years old and upward, as the LORD commanded Moses.” And these were the Israelites who came out of the land of Egypt:
Reuben, the firstborn of Israel. The sons of Reuben: of Hanoch, the clan of the Hanochites; of Pallu, the clan of the Palluites;
of Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; of Carmi, the clan of the Carmites.
These are the clans of the Reubenites, and those numbered were 43,730.

The sons of Eliab: Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the Dathan and Abiram who were chosen from the congregation and contended against Moses and Aaron in the company of Korah when they contended against the LORD.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them together with Korah when that company died, when fire devoured 250 men, and they became a warning.
But the sons of Korah did not die.
The sons of Simeon according to their clans: of Nemuel, the clan of the Nemuelites; of Jamin, the clan of the Jaminites; of Jachin, the clan of the Jachinites;
of Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites; of Shaul, the clan of the Shaulites.
These are the clans of the Simeonites, 22,200.
The sons of Gad according to their clans: of Zephon, the clan of the Zephonites; of Haggi, the clan of the Haggites; of Shuni, the clan of the Shunites;
of Ozni, the clan of the Oznites; of Eri, the clan of the Erites;
of Arod, the clan of the Arodites; of Areli, the clan of the Arelites.
These are the clans of the sons of Gad as they were numbered, 40,500.
The sons of Judah were Er and Onan, and Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
The sons of Judah according to their clans: of Shelah, the clan of the Shelanites; of Perez, the clan of the Perezites; of Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites.
The sons of Perez: of Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; of Hamul, the clan of the Hamulites.
These are the clans of Judah as they were numbered, 76,500.
The sons of Issachar according to their clans: of Tola, the clan of the Tolaites; of Puvah, the clan of the Punites;
of Jashub, the clan of the Jashubites; of Shimron, the clan of the Shimronites.
These are the clans of Issachar as they were numbered, 64,300.
