The sons of Zebulun according to their clans: of Sered, the clan of the Seredites; of Elon, the clan of the Elonites; of Jahleel, the clan of the Jahleelites.
These are the clans of the Zebulunites as they were numbered, 60,500.
The sons of Joseph according to their clans: Manasseh and Ephraim.
The sons of Manasseh: of Machir, the clan of the Machirites—and Machir was the father of Gilead—of Gilead, the clan of the Gileadites.
These are the sons of Gilead: of Iezer, the clan of the Iezerites; of Helek, the clan of the Helekites;
of Asriel, the clan of the Asrielites; of Shechem, the clan of the Shechemites;
of Shemida, the clan of the Shemidaites; of Hepher, the clan of the Hepherites.
Now Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, only daughters, and the names of the daughters of Zelophehad were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
These are the clans of Manasseh, and those numbered were 52,700.
These are the sons of Ephraim according to their clans: of Shuthelah, the clan of the Shuthelahites; of Becher, the clan of the Becherites; of Tahan, the clan of the Tahanites.
These are the sons of Shuthelah: of Eran, the clan of the Eranites.
These are the clans of the sons of Ephraim as they were numbered, 32,500. These are the sons of Joseph according to their clans.
The sons of Benjamin according to their clans: of Bela, the clan of the Belaites; of Ashbel, the clan of the Ashbelites; of Ahiram, the clan of the Ahiramites;
of Shephupham, the clan of the Shephuphamites; of Hupham, the clan of the Huphamites.
The sons of Bela: Ard and Naaman—of Ard, the clan of the Ardites; of Naaman, the clan of the Naamites.
These are the sons of Benjamin according to their clans, and those numbered were 45,600.
These are the sons of Dan according to their clans: of Shuham, the clan of the Shuhamites. These are the clans of Dan according to their clans.
All the clans of the Shuhamites, as they were numbered, were 64,400.
The sons of Asher according to their clans: of Imnah, the clan of the Imnites; of Ishvi, the clan of the Ishvites; of Beriah, the clan of the Beriites.
Of the sons of Beriah: of Heber, the clan of the Heberites; of Malchiel, the clan of the Malchielites.
The name of the daughter of Asher was Serah.
These are the clans of the sons of Asher as they were numbered, 53,400.
The sons of Naphtali according to their clans: of Jahzeel, the clan of the Jahzeelites; of Guni, the clan of the Gunites;
of Jezer, the clan of the Jezerites; of Shillem, the clan of the Shillemites.
These are the clans of Naphtali as they were numbered, 45,400.
This was the list of the Israelites: 601,730.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Among these the land shall be divided as an inheritance according to the number of names.
To a large tribe you shall give a large inheritance, and to a small tribe a small inheritance; each one’s inheritance shall be given according to the number of those listed.
But the land shall be divided by lot. According to the names of the tribes of their fathers they shall inherit.
Their inheritance shall be divided by lot between the larger and the smaller.”
This is the list of the Levites according to their clans: of Gershon, the clan of the Gershonites; of Kohath, the clan of the Kohathites; of Merari, the clan of the Merarites.
These are the clans of Levi: the Libnites, the Hebronites, the Mahlites, the Mushites, and the Korahites. And Kohath was the father of Amram.
The name of Amram’s wife was Jochebed, daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Egypt; and she bore to Amram Aaron, Moses, and Miriam their sister.
To Aaron were born Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
But Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD.
Those numbered were 23,000, every male from a month old and upward. For they were not numbered among the Israelites, because no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites.
These are those numbered by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who numbered the Israelites in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
But among these there was not one of those numbered by Moses and Aaron the priest when they numbered the Israelites in the wilderness of Sinai.
For the LORD had said of them, “They shall die in the wilderness.” Not one of them was left, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

The daughters of Zelophehad—son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh—belonged to the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph. These were the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
They approached the entrance of the tent of meeting and stood before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, before the leaders, and before the whole congregation, saying,
“Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the company of those who banded together against the LORD in Korah’s rebellion; rather, he died for his own sin, and he had no sons.
Why should our father’s name disappear from his clan simply because he had no son? Give us a possession among our father’s brothers.”
Moses brought their case before the LORD.
The LORD said to Moses, “The daughters of Zelophehad speak rightly.
You must give them a possession of inheritance among their father’s brothers, and you shall transfer their father’s inheritance to them.
And you shall say to the children of Israel, ‘If a man dies and has no son, then you shall transfer his inheritance to his daughter.’
If he has no daughter, then you shall give his inheritance to his brothers.
If he has no brothers, then you shall give his inheritance to his father’s brothers.

If his father has no brothers, then you shall give his inheritance to his nearest kinsman from his clan, who shall possess it. This shall be a statute of justice for the Israelites, as the LORD commanded Moses.”
Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go up to this mountain of Abarim and see the land that I have given to the children of Israel.
When you have seen it, you too will die, just as your brother Aaron died.

because you rebelled against My command in the Wilderness of Zin when the congregation contended, failing to honor Me as holy before their eyes at the waters—these are the waters of Meribah Kadesh in the Wilderness of Zin.”
Moses spoke to the LORD, saying,
“O LORD, God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation
who will go out before them and come in before them, who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the congregation of the LORD will not be like sheep without a shepherd.”
The LORD said to Moses, “Take Joshua son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay your hand on him.
Set him before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation, and commission him in their sight.
You shall put some of your authority on him, so that all the congregation of the children of Israel will obey him.

He is to stand before Eleazar the priest, who will inquire of the LORD for him by the judgment of the Urim. At his command they will go out, and at his command they will come in—he and all the children of Israel with him, together with the whole congregation.”
So Moses did as the LORD commanded him. He took Joshua and set him before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation.
He laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Command the children of Israel, and say to them, 'My offering, My food for My offerings made by fire, My soothing aroma, you shall be careful to offer to Me at the appointed time.'
And say to them, 'This is the fire offering that you shall offer to the the LORD:'
Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight,
with a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a grain offering, mixed with a quarter of a hin of pressed oil.
It is the continual burnt offering instituted at Mount Sinai, a pleasing aroma, a fire offering to the the LORD.
Its drink offering shall be a quarter of a hin for each lamb; in the holy place pour out a drink offering of strong drink to the the LORD.
Offer the second lamb at twilight, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to the the LORD.
"On the Sabbath day, two male lambs a year old without blemish, with two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and its drink offering.
This is the burnt offering for every Sabbath, in addition to the continual burnt offering with its drink offering.
At the beginnings of your months, you shall present a burnt offering to the the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old without blemish,
with three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering for each bull, and two-tenths for the ram,
and one-tenth of an ephah for each lamb, a grain offering mixed with oil. This is a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, a fire offering to the the LORD.

Their drink offerings shall be half a hin of wine for a bull, a third of a hin for a ram, and a quarter of a hin for a lamb. This is the burnt offering for each month throughout the months of the year.
Also one male goat shall be offered to the the LORD as a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering with its drink offering.
"On the fourteenth day of the first month is the LORD's Passover.
On the fifteenth day of this month is a feast; unleavened bread shall be eaten for seven days.
On the first day there shall be a holy convocation; you shall not do any ordinary work.
And you shall present a fire offering as a burnt offering to the the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, and seven lambs a year old; they shall be without blemish for you.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: you shall offer three-tenths of an ephah for a bull, and two-tenths for a ram,
and one-tenth of an ephah for each of the seven lambs.
Also one goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
You shall offer these besides the continual burnt offering of the morning.
In this manner you shall offer the food of the fire offering daily for seven days, a pleasing aroma to the the LORD; it shall be offered besides the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.
And on the seventh day you shall have a holy convocation; you shall not do any ordinary work.
"Also on the day of the firstfruits, when you offer a new grain offering to the the LORD at your Feast of Weeks, you shall have a holy convocation; you shall not do any ordinary work.
You shall present a burnt offering as a pleasing aroma to the the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, and seven lambs a year old.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for each bull, two-tenths for the ram,
and one-tenth of an ephah for each of the seven lambs.
Also one male goat to make atonement for you.
You shall offer them, with their drink offerings, besides the continual burnt offering and its grain offering; they shall be without blemish for you."
On the first day of the seventh month, you shall have a sacred assembly. You shall not do any regular work. It is a day for you to sound the trumpets.
As a pleasing aroma to the the LORD, you shall offer one burnt offering: one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, without blemish.
Its grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for the bull, two-tenths for the ram,
and one-tenth for each of the seven lambs.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.

In addition to the monthly burnt offering and its grain offering, and the daily burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offerings, according to their ordinance, these shall be offered as a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the the LORD.
On the tenth day of this seventh month, you shall have a sacred assembly. You must deny yourselves; you shall do no work.
You shall offer as a pleasing aroma to the the LORD one burnt offering: one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, without blemish.
Its grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for the bull, two-tenths for the ram,
and one-tenth for each of the seven lambs.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering, besides the sin offering of atonement, the continual burnt offering, and its grain offering and drink offerings.
On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, you shall have a sacred assembly; you shall not do any regular work. You shall celebrate a feast to the the LORD for seven days.
You shall offer as an offering made by fire, a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the the LORD: thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without blemish.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for each of the thirteen bulls, two-tenths for each of the two rams,
and one-tenth for each of the fourteen lambs.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
On the second day, you shall offer twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without blemish,
with the grain offering and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to their number, as prescribed.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offerings.
On the third day, you shall offer eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without blemish,
with the grain offering and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to their number, as prescribed.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
On the fourth day, you shall offer ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without blemish,
with the grain offering and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to their number, as prescribed.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
On the fifth day, you shall offer nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without blemish,
with the grain offering and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to their number, as prescribed.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
On the sixth day, you shall offer eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without blemish,
with the grain offering and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to their number, as prescribed.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offerings.
On the seventh day, you shall offer seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without blemish,
with the grain offering and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to their number, as prescribed.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
On the eighth day, you shall hold a solemn assembly; you shall do no regular work.
You shall offer as an offering made by fire, a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the the LORD: one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, without blemish.
Their grain offering and drink offerings shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering, besides the continual burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
These you shall offer to the the LORD at your appointed feasts, in addition to your vows and freewill offerings, for your burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, and peace offerings.
Moses told the Israelites everything the the LORD had commanded him.
Moses said to the heads of the tribes of Israel, “This is what the the LORD has commanded:
When a man makes a vow to the the LORD or swears an oath to obligate himself by a pledge, he must not break his word; he must do everything he has promised. “
If a woman makes a vow to the the LORD and obligates herself by a pledge while she is young and living in her father’s house,
and her father hears her vow and the pledge by which she has bound herself yet says nothing to her, then all her vows and every pledge by which she has bound herself will stand.

But if her father overrules her on the day he hears of it, none of her vows or pledges by which she has bound herself will stand; the the LORD will forgive her, because her father has overruled her. “
If a woman marries while bound by a vow or by a spoken pledge by which she has obligated herself,
and her husband hears of it but says nothing to her on the day he hears, then her vows will stand, and the pledges by which she has bound herself will stand.
But if her husband overrules her when he hears of it, he nullifies the vow upon her or the spoken pledge by which she has bound herself, and the the LORD will forgive her.
Every vow or obligation pledged by a widow or a divorced woman will be binding upon her.
If a woman in her husband’s house has made a vow or put herself under an oath,
and her husband hears of it but says nothing to her and does not overrule her, then all her vows will stand, and every pledge by which she has bound herself will stand.

But if her husband nullifies them on the day he hears them, then nothing that came from her lips—whether her vows or her pledges—will stand. Her husband has nullified them, and the the LORD will forgive her.
Her husband may confirm or nullify any vow or any sworn obligation by which she denies herself.
But if her husband says nothing to her from day to day, then he confirms all the vows and pledges that are upon her; he confirms them by saying nothing to her on the day he hears of them.
But if he nullifies them after he hears of them, then he will bear her guilt.”
These are the statutes that the the LORD commanded Moses concerning the relationship between a man and his wife, and between a father and a daughter still in her youth in her father’s house.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Avenge the Israelites on the Midianites. Afterward you will die and be gathered to your ancestors.”
So Moses spoke to the people, saying, “Arm some of your men for war, that they may go against Midian to execute the LORD’s vengeance on Midian.
You shall send a thousand from each tribe of Israel to the war.”
So from the thousands of Israel, twelve thousand armed for war were delivered, a thousand from each tribe.
Moses sent them to the war, a thousand from each tribe, with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to the war, with the holy vessels and the trumpets for the alarm in his hand.
They fought against Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses, and killed every male.
They killed the kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
The Israelites took captive the women of Midian and their little ones, and plundered all their livestock, all their herds, and all their wealth.
They burned all their cities where they dwelt and all their encampments with fire.
They took all the spoil and all the plunder, both man and beast.
They brought the captives, the plunder, and the spoil to Moses and Eleazar the priest and to the congregation of the Israelites, to the camp on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.
Moses and Eleazar the priest and all the leaders of the congregation went out to meet them outside the camp.
Moses was angry with the officers of the army, the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds who returned from the war.
Moses said to them, “Have you spared all the women?
Behold, these were the ones who, on Balaam’s advice, caused the Israelites to act treacherously against the LORD in the matter of Peor, so that the plague came upon the congregation of the LORD.
Now therefore kill every male among the little ones, and kill every woman who has known a man by lying with him.
But all the young girls who have not known a man by lying with him, keep alive for yourselves.

And you, camp outside the camp seven days; everyone who has killed a person and everyone who has touched a slain person shall purify themselves on the third day and on the seventh day, both you and your captives.
And every garment, every leather thing, everything made of goats’ hair, and every article of wood, you shall purify.”
Eleazar the priest said to the men of war who had gone into battle, “This is the statute of the law that the LORD commanded Moses:
Only the gold, the silver, the bronze, the iron, the tin, and the lead—

everything that can go into fire, you shall pass through the fire, and it shall be clean; nevertheless it shall be purified with the water of purification; and everything that cannot go into fire you shall pass through water.
You shall wash your clothes on the seventh day, and you shall be clean; and afterward you may come into the camp.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Take a count of the plunder that was taken, both of man and of beast, you and Eleazar the priest and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the congregation;
and divide the plunder between the warriors who went out to battle and all the congregation.
And levy a tribute for the LORD from the men of war who went out to battle: one soul out of five hundred, both of man and of cattle, of donkeys and of sheep.
Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as the LORD’s offering.

And from the half of the Israelites take one portion out of fifty, of man, of cattle, of donkeys, and of sheep, of all the livestock, and give them to the Levites who keep guard over the tabernacle of the LORD.”
So Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD commanded Moses.
The rest of the plunder that the people of the army had plundered was 675,000 sheep,
and 32,000 persons in all, women who had not known a man by lying with him.
The half, the portion of those who went out to war, was 337,500 sheep,
and the tribute to the LORD from the sheep was 675;
the cattle were 36,000, of which the tribute to the LORD was 72;
the donkeys were 30,500, of which the tribute to the LORD was 61;
the persons were 16,000, of which the tribute to the LORD was 32 persons.
Moses gave the tribute, the LORD’s offering, to Eleazar the priest, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
From the half of the Israelites, which Moses had divided from the men who had gone to war—
Moses took from the half of the Israelites one portion out of fifty, of man and of beast, and gave them to the Levites who kept guard over the tabernacle of the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The officers of the army, the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, came near to Moses
and said to Moses, “Your servants have taken a count of the men of war who are under our command, and not one of us is missing.
We have brought as an offering to the LORD the gold articles that each man found: armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and pendants, to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from them, all the articles of worked gold.
The gold of the offering that the commanders of thousands and of hundreds raised for the LORD was 16,750 shekels.
(Each man of the army had plundered for himself.)
Moses and Eleazar the priest brought the gold into the tent of meeting as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD.
The Reubenites and Gadites owned an exceptionally large number of livestock, and when they saw that the territory of Jazer and Gilead was ideally suited to pastoral use,
they came to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the congregation and said,
“Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon—
the land that the LORD subdued before the congregation of Israel—is pastoral country, and your servants possess livestock.
If we have found favor in your sight, let this land be granted to your servants as a possession; do not require us to cross the Jordan.”
Moses said to the Gadites and Reubenites, “Shall your brothers march to war while you remain here?
Why would you sap the courage of the Israelites and deter them from crossing into the land the LORD has given them?
This is precisely what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to inspect the land.
They ascended to the Valley of Eshcol, surveyed the land, and discouraged the Israelites from entering the land the LORD had given them.

So the LORD’s anger was kindled that day, and He swore that not one of the men twenty years old or more who came up from Egypt would see the land He had sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because they had not followed Him wholeheartedly—
except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, for they followed the LORD wholeheartedly.

Thus the LORD’s anger burned against Israel, and He made them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until the whole generation of those who had committed evil in the sight of the LORD had perished.
And now you, a brood of sinful men, have arisen in your fathers’ stead to intensify still further the LORD’s fierce anger against Israel.
If you turn away from following Him, He will once again abandon this people in the wilderness, and you will bring ruin upon all of them.”
They came closer and said, “We will build sheepfolds here for our livestock and cities for our children.

But we will arm ourselves and march as the vanguard before the Israelites until we have brought them to their place. Our children will dwell in fortified cities because of the inhabitants of the land.
We will not return to our homes until every Israelite has received his inheritance.
We will not claim an inheritance with them beyond the Jordan, because our inheritance has fallen to us on this side, east of the Jordan.”
Moses said to them, “If you do this—if you arm yourselves before the LORD for battle,
and every armed man among you crosses the Jordan before the LORD until He has driven out His enemies before Him,
and the land is subdued before the LORD—then afterward you may return, and you will be absolved of obligation to the LORD and to Israel, and this land will be your possession before the LORD.
But if you do not do this, you will have sinned against the LORD, and be assured that your sin will overtake you.
Build cities for your little ones and pens for your flocks, but do what you have promised.”
The Gadites and Reubenites said to Moses, “Your servants will do as my lord commands.
Our children, wives, livestock, and all our animals will remain here in the cities of Gilead,
while your servants, all armed for war, cross over before the LORD to battle, as my lord says.”
Moses commanded them—to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the Israelites—saying,
“If the Gadites and Reubenites cross the Jordan with you, every man armed for battle before the LORD, and the land is subdued before you, then you shall give them the land of Gilead as a possession.
But if they do not cross over with you armed, they shall receive their inheritance among you in the land of Canaan.”
The Gadites and Reubenites answered, “We will do what the LORD has spoken.
We will cross over into Canaan armed before the LORD, and our inheritance will remain with us east of the Jordan.”

So Moses gave to the Gadites, the Reubenites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan—the land with its cities and the territories surrounding them.
The Gadites built Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
Beth-nimrah, and Beth-haran as fortified cities, and they built sheepfolds.
The Reubenites built Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
Nebo, Baal-meon (whose name they changed), and Sibmah, and they renamed the cities they built.
The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, captured it, and drove out the Amorites who were there.
So Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled there.
Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their villages and called them Havvoth-jair.
Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages and called it Nobah after his own name.
These are the stages of the Israelites' journey after they left Egypt in battle formation, under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
At the the LORD's command, Moses recorded their departures and encampments in the order they occurred.
They left Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month—the day after the Passover—with unmistakable boldness, in full view of all the Egyptians,
while the Egyptians were burying all the firstborn whom the the LORD had struck down among them; the the LORD had also executed judgment against their gods.
The Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.
They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.
They set out from Etham, turned back toward Pi-hahiroth, east of Baal-zephon, and camped before Migdol.
They set out from Pi-hahiroth, crossed through the sea into the wilderness, traveled three days in the Wilderness of Etham, and camped at Marah.
They set out from Marah and came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees; there they camped.
They set out from Elim and camped beside the Red Sea.
They set out from the Red Sea and camped in the Wilderness of Sin.
They set out from the Wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush.
They set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
They set out from Rephidim and camped in the Wilderness of Sinai.
They set out from the Wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
They set out from Libnah and camped at Rissah.
They set out from Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
They set out from Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
They set out from Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
They set out from Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
They set out from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
They set out from Tahath and camped at Terah.
They set out from Terah and camped at Mithkah.
They set out from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
They set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.
They set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad.
They set out from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
They set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.
They set out from Ezion-geber and camped in the Wilderness of Zin—that is, Kadesh.
They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the border of Edom.
At the the LORD's command, Aaron the priest ascended Mount Hor and died there on the first day of the fifth month, in the fortieth year after the Israelites had left Egypt.
Aaron was one hundred twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev of Canaan, heard that the Israelites were approaching.
They set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
They set out from Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab.
They set out from Iyim and camped at Dibon-gad.
They set out from Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
They set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim, before Nebo.
They set out from the mountains of Abarim and camped in the plains of Moab beside the Jordan opposite Jericho.
They camped by the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim in the plains of Moab.
The The LORD spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab beside the Jordan at Jericho, saying, "Speak to the Israelites and tell them:
'When you cross the Jordan into Canaan,
you must drive out all the inhabitants of the land before you. You must destroy all their carved images and cast idols, and you must demolish all their high places.
You must take possession of the land and live in it, for I have given it to you to possess.

You are to divide the land by lot among your families: increase the inheritance for the larger group and decrease it for the smaller; wherever the lot falls for a family, that shall be its inheritance. You shall receive your allotments according to the tribes of your ancestors.
But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land before you, then those you leave behind will become relentless irritants and adversaries, harassing you in the land you occupy.
Then I will do to you what I intended to do to them.'"
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Command the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land of Canaan—this is the land that will be allotted to you as an inheritance, the land of Canaan with its borders— “
your southern boundary shall be from the wilderness of Zin along the border of Edom; on the east, your southern boundary shall begin at the end of the Salt Sea.
your boundary shall turn south of the ascent of Akrabbim, pass through Zin, and end south of Kadesh-barnea; then it shall go to Hazar-addar and pass on to Azmon.
The boundary shall turn from Azmon to the Brook of Egypt, and its end shall be at the Sea.
For the western boundary, you shall have the Great Sea and its coast; this shall be your western boundary. “
This shall be your northern boundary: from the Great Sea you shall mark out your line to Mount Hor.
From Mount Hor you shall mark out your line to Lebo-hamath, and the end of the boundary shall be at Zedad.
Then the boundary shall go to Ziphron, and its end shall be at Hazar-enan; this shall be your northern boundary.
you shall draw your eastern boundary from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
The boundary shall go down from Shepham to Riblah on the east side of Ain, and the boundary shall descend and reach the eastern slope of the Sea of Chinnereth.
The boundary shall descend to the Jordan, and its end shall be at the Salt Sea. This shall be your land with its boundaries all around.”
Moses commanded the Israelites, saying, “This is the land that you shall inherit by lot, which the LORD has commanded to be given to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
For the tribe of the Reubenites by their ancestral houses, the tribe of the Gadites by their ancestral houses, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance.
The two tribes and the half-tribe have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan at Jericho, eastward, toward the sunrise.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“These are the names of the men who shall apportion the land to you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
You shall take one leader from every tribe to apportion the land for inheritance. “
These are the names of the men: For the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh.
For the tribe of the Simeonites, Shemuel son of Ammihud.
For the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon.
For the tribe of the Danites, a leader, Bukki son of Jogli.
For the Josephites: for the tribe of the Manassites, a leader, Hanniel son of Ephod,
and for the tribe of the Ephraimites, a leader, Kemuel son of Shiphtan.
For the tribe of the Zebulunites, a leader, Elizaphan son of Parnach.
For the tribe of the Issacharites, a leader, Paltiel son of Azzan.
For the tribe of the Asherites, a leader, Ahihud son of Shelomi.
For the tribe of the Naphtalites, a leader, Pedahel son of Ammihud.”
These are those whom the LORD commanded to apportion the inheritance for the Israelites in the land of Canaan.
While Israel was encamped in the plains of Moab beside the Jordan opposite Jericho, the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Command the Israelites to give the Levites cities to live in from the inheritance they possess, and you shall also give the Levites pasturelands around those cities.
The cities shall be theirs for residence, and their pasturelands shall be for their cattle, their property, and all their animals.
The pasturelands of the cities that you give the Levites shall extend a thousand cubits from the city wall in every direction.

You shall measure outside the city two thousand cubits on the east, two thousand on the south, two thousand on the west, and two thousand on the north, with the city in the center; these shall be the pasturelands of the cities.
Among the cities you give the Levites shall be six cities of refuge, which you shall designate so that a manslayer may flee there; besides these, you shall give them forty-two cities.
The total number of cities you give the Levites shall be forty-eight, with their pasturelands.

The cities you give from the Israelites' possession shall be given according to the size of each tribe's inheritance: from the larger inheritance you shall take more, and from the smaller you shall take less."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them that when you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
you shall designate cities to be cities of refuge for you, so that a manslayer who kills a person unintentionally may flee there.
These cities shall be a refuge for you from the blood avenger, so that the manslayer does not die until he stands before the assembly for judgment.
The six cities you give shall be your cities of refuge.
You shall give three cities beyond the Jordan and three cities in the land of Canaan; they shall be cities of refuge.
These six cities shall be a refuge for the Israelites, for the foreigner, and for the sojourner among them, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there.
"If anyone strikes a person with an iron object and that person dies, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
If anyone strikes a person with a stone that can cause death and that person dies, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
If anyone strikes a person with a wooden object that can cause death and that person dies, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
The blood avenger shall put the murderer to death; when he meets him, he shall kill him.
If anyone pushes another out of hatred, or throws something at him with intent, and he dies,
or if he strikes him in enmity with his hand and he dies, the one who struck him shall surely be put to death; he is a murderer. The blood avenger shall put the murderer to death when he finds him.
But if he pushes him suddenly without enmity, or throws any object at him without intent,
or drops a stone on him without seeing him, and it causes death, though he was not his enemy and did not seek his harm,
then the assembly shall judge between the one who struck and the blood avenger according to these ordinances.

The assembly shall rescue the manslayer from the hand of the blood avenger and return him to the city of refuge to which he fled, and he shall live there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
But if the manslayer goes at all beyond the boundary of his city of refuge to which he fled,
and the blood avenger finds him outside the boundary of his city of refuge and kills the manslayer, the avenger shall not be guilty of blood.
For the manslayer must remain in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest; after the death of the high priest, the manslayer may return to the land of his possession.
These things shall be a statute of judgment for you throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
If anyone kills a person, the murderer shall be put to death on the testimony of witnesses; but no one may be put to death on the testimony of a single witness.
You shall take no ransom for the life of a murderer who is guilty of death; he shall surely be put to death.
You shall take no ransom to allow a manslayer to leave his city of refuge and dwell in the land before the death of the high priest.
So you shall not pollute the land in which you are; for blood pollutes the land, and no atonement can be made for the land for the blood that is shed in it except by the blood of the one who shed it.
You shall not defile the land in which you dwell, where I dwell among you; for I am the LORD, dwelling among the Israelites."
The heads of the families of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh—one of the clans of Joseph—approached Moses and the leaders, who were the heads of the Israelite families.

They said, “The LORD commanded my lord to give the land as an inheritance to the Israelites by lot, and my lord was commanded by the LORD to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.

But if they marry any of the men from the other tribes of Israel, their inheritance will be withdrawn from the inheritance of our fathers and added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry; thus a portion of our allotted inheritance would be taken away.

And when the Jubilee for the Israelites comes, their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they marry, and their inheritance will be removed from the inheritance of the tribe of our fathers.”
So at the the LORD’s command, Moses gave this order to the Israelites: “The tribe of the sons of Joseph has spoken correctly.
This is what the the LORD has commanded concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: They may marry anyone they please, provided they marry within the clan of their father’s tribe.
No inheritance in Israel may be transferred from tribe to tribe, because each Israelite is to retain the inheritance of his fathers’ tribe.
Every daughter who inherits property in any Israelite tribe must marry within the clan of her father’s tribe, so that every Israelite will retain the inheritance of his fathers.
No inheritance may be transferred from one tribe to another, for each Israelite tribe must retain its inheritance.”
So the daughters of Zelophehad did as the the LORD had commanded Moses.
Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, married their cousins,
and they married within the clans of the sons of Manasseh son of Joseph; thus their inheritance remained within their father’s tribe and clan.
These are the commandments and ordinances that the the LORD gave the Israelites through Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.
These are the words Moses spoke to all Israel in the wilderness east of the Jordan, in the Arabah opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
It is an eleven-day journey from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea by way of Mount Seir.
In the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month, Moses spoke to the Israelites according to all that the LORD had commanded him concerning them,
after he had defeated Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth in Edrei.
East of the Jordan in the land of Moab, Moses began to explain this law, saying:
The LORD our God said to us at Horeb, “You have stayed at this mountain long enough.

Turn now and set out for the hill country of the Amorites and all their neighbors in the Arabah, in the hill country, in the foothills, in the Negev, along the coast of the Great Sea, and in Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates.
See, I have set the land before you. Go in and possess the land that the LORD swore to give to your fathers—to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—and to their descendants after them.”
At that time I said to you, “I cannot carry you alone.
The LORD your God has multiplied you, and today you are as numerous as the stars of heaven.
May the LORD, the God of your fathers, increase you a thousand times over and bless you as He has promised.
How can I bear your troubles, burdens, and disputes by myself?”
Choose wise, discerning, and respected men from your tribes, and I will appoint them as your leaders.
You answered me, “What you propose is good.”
So I took the leaders of your tribes, wise and respected men, and appointed them as officials over you—commanders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, and officers for your tribes.
And I charged your judges at that time, “Hear the disputes between your brothers and judge fairly between a man and his brother or a foreign resident.

Do not show partiality in judgment; hear both small and great alike. Do not be intimidated by anyone, for judgment belongs to God. Bring me any case that is too difficult for you, and I will hear it.”
And at that time I commanded you all the things you were to do.
Then we set out from Horeb and went through that vast and terrifying wilderness you saw, on our way to the hill country of the Amorites, and we came to Kadesh-barnea.
And I said to you, “You have reached the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving us.
See, the LORD your God has placed the land before you. Go up and possess it, as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has told you. Do not be afraid or discouraged.”
Then all of you came to me and said, “Let us send men ahead to spy out the land and bring back a report about the route we should take and the cities we will encounter.”
The plan pleased me, so I selected twelve men from among you, one from each tribe.
They left and went up into the hill country and came to the Valley of Eshcol and scouted it out.
They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands, brought it down to us, and reported, “The land the LORD our God is giving us is good.”
But you were unwilling to go up; you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God.
You grumbled in your tents and said, “The LORD hates us; that is why He brought us out of Egypt, to deliver us into the hands of the Amorites to destroy us.

Where can we go? Our brothers have made our hearts melt by saying, ‘The people are greater and taller than we are; the cities are large, with walls up to the sky; and we have even seen the Anakim there.’”
Then I said to you, “Do not be terrified or afraid of them.
The LORD your God, who goes before you, will fight for you, just as He did for you in Egypt before your very eyes.
And in the wilderness you saw how the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, all the way you traveled until you reached this place.
Yet in spite of all this, you did not trust in the LORD your God,
who went before you on the journey, in fire by night and in a cloud by day, to seek out a place for you to camp and to show you the way you should go.”
When the LORD heard your words, He was angry and swore an oath:
“Not one of the men of this evil generation shall see the good land I swore to give your fathers,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He will see it, and I will give him and his descendants the land he has walked on, because he followed the LORD wholeheartedly.”
The LORD was angry with me as well because of you, and He said, “You shall not enter there either.”
Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you, will enter it. Encourage him, for he will enable Israel to inherit it.
And your little ones, whom you said would become plunder, and your children who today do not know good from evil, will enter there. I will give it to them, and they will possess it.
But as for you, turn back and set out toward the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea.

Then you answered me, “We have sinned against the LORD. We will go up and fight, just as the LORD our God commanded us.” And each of you strapped on his weapons of war, thinking it would be easy to go up into the hill country.
But the LORD said to me, “Tell them not to go up and not to fight, for I am not among you; otherwise you will be defeated by your enemies.”
So I told you, but you would not listen; you rebelled against the LORD's command and presumptuously went up into the hill country.
Then the Amorites who lived in that hill country came out against you and chased you like a swarm of bees. They beat you down in Seir all the way to Hormah.
You returned and wept before the LORD, but the LORD would not listen to your voice or give ear to you.
So you stayed in Kadesh many days—the same number of days you had already spent there.
Then we reversed course and set out toward the wilderness along the route to the Red Sea, as the LORD had directed me, and for many days we roamed about Mount Seir.
Then the LORD said to me,
"You have circled this hill country long enough; turn northward.
Command the people that they shall pass through the territory of your brothers, the descendants of Esau, who inhabit Seir. They will be exceedingly afraid of you, so exercise utmost caution.
Do not antagonize them, for I will not grant you any of their land—not even a foothold—because I have assigned Mount Seir to Esau as his possession.
You are to purchase food from them with silver so that you may eat, and you are to purchase water from them with silver so that you may drink.

For the LORD your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He has watched over your journey through this vast wilderness. The LORD your God has accompanied you these forty years, and you have not been deprived of anything."

So we passed by our brothers, the descendants of Esau, who inhabit Seir. We turned away from the Arabah road, which comes up from Elath and Ezion-geber, and traveled along the road of the wilderness of Moab.
Then the LORD said to me, "Do not afflict Moab or incite them to war, for I will not give you any of their land, because I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as their possession."
The Emim formerly inhabited that region—a people great, numerous, and tall, like the Anakim.
Like the Anakim, they too are classified as Rephaim, although the Moabites designate them Emim.
The Horites once dwelt in Seir, but the descendants of Esau expelled and exterminated them and occupied their territory, just as Israel did in the land that the LORD granted them as their possession.
"Now rise up and cross the Zered Valley." So we crossed the Zered Valley.

The interval we spent traveling from Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the Zered Valley amounted to thirty-eight years, until the entire generation of warriors had perished from the camp, as the LORD had sworn to them.
Indeed, the LORD's hand was against them, to eradicate them from the camp, until they were eliminated.
Now when all the fighting men among the people had died,
"Today you are to cross the border of Moab at Ar.

When you approach the Ammonites, do not afflict them or incite them to war, for I will not give you any of the land of the Ammonites, because I have given it to the descendants of Lot as their possession."
That land too was considered the domain of the Rephaim, who once inhabited it, but the Ammonites call them Zamzummim.
They were a people great, numerous, and tall, like the Anakim. Yet the LORD annihilated them before the Ammonites, who expelled them and occupied their territory.
This is what He did for the descendants of Esau who reside in Seir, when He destroyed the Horites before them. They expelled them and occupied their territory, and they remain there to this day.
Moreover, the Avvim, who inhabited villages as far as Gaza—the Caphtorites originated in Caphtor and destroyed them and occupied their territory.
"Arise, set out, and cross the Arnon Valley. Observe, I have delivered Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his domain into your hand. Begin to take possession of it, and engage him in battle.
This day I will commence instilling the dread and fear of you among all the nations beneath heaven, who will hear the report concerning you and tremble and be distressed because of you."
So I dispatched messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon with overtures of peace, saying,
"Permit me to pass through your land; I will remain on the main road. I will not deviate to the right or to the left.
You may sell me food for money so that I may eat, and provide me water for money so that I may drink. Just let me pass through on foot,
as the descendants of Esau who dwell in Seir and the Moabites who dwell in Ar did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD our God is bestowing upon us."

But Sihon king of Heshbon refused to allow us passage, for the LORD your God had hardened his spirit and rendered his heart obstinate, so that He might deliver him into your hand, as is the case this very day.
Then the LORD said to me, "Behold, I have begun to deliver Sihon and his land over to you. Begin to take possession of his land."
Then Sihon and all his people advanced to meet us in battle at Jahaz.
And the LORD our God delivered him over to us, and we struck him down, together with his sons and all his people.
At that time we captured all his cities and devoted every city to destruction, along with its men, women, and children. We left no survivors.
We carried off for ourselves only the livestock and the spoil of the cities we had captured.
From Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley, as far as Gilead, no city proved too fortified for us. The LORD our God gave us all of them.
But we did not approach the land of the Ammonites, or the land along the Jabbok River, or the cities of the hill country, or any place that the LORD our God had forbidden us.
Then we turned and ascended the road to Bashan, and Og, king of Bashan, marched out with his whole army to meet us in battle at Edrei.

But the LORD said to me, "Do not be afraid of him, for I have delivered him into your hand, along with his whole army and his land. Do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon."
So the LORD our God also delivered Og king of Bashan and his whole army into our hands. We struck them down until no survivor remained.
At that time we captured all his cities. There was not a city that we did not take—the sixty cities of the whole region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
All these cities were fortified with high walls and gates and bars, besides a great many unwalled villages.
We devoted them to destruction, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, destroying every city, including women and children.
But all the livestock and plunder of the cities we carried off for ourselves.
At that time we took from the two kings of the Amorites the land east of the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon
(the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir),
all the cities of the plateau, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as the cities of Salecah and Edrei in the kingdom of Og.
(For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of the Rephaim. His bed was made of iron and was more than thirteen feet long and six feet wide, according to the standard cubit.)
So at that time we took possession of this land. To the Reubenites and Gadites I gave the land east of the Arnon Valley, along with half the hill country of Gilead and its cities.
To the half-tribe of Manasseh I gave the rest of Gilead and all of Bashan, the kingdom of Og. (The whole region of Argob in Bashan used to be called the land of the Rephaim.
Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and he named Bashan after himself, Havvoth-jair, as it is to this day.)
And to the Reubenites and Gadites I gave the land from Gilead to the Arnon Valley (the middle of the valley was the border) and up to the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites.
The Jordan River in the Arabah bordered it on the west, from Chinnereth to the Sea of the Arabah (the Salt Sea) below the slopes of Pisgah to the east.
At that time I commanded you: "The LORD your God has given you this land to possess. All your men of valor are to cross over, armed, before your brothers, the Israelites.
But your wives, your children, and your livestock—I know that you have much livestock—may remain in the cities I have given you,

until the LORD gives rest to your brothers as He has to you, and they too have taken possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving them across the Jordan. Then each of you may return to the possession I have given you."
At that time I also charged Joshua: "Your eyes have seen all that the LORD your God has done to these two kings. The LORD will do the same to all the kingdoms you are about to enter.
Do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God Himself will fight for you."
At that time I also pleaded with the LORD:
"O Lord the LORD, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your strong hand. For what god is there in heaven or on earth who can do the deeds and mighty works You do?
Please let me cross over and see the good land beyond the Jordan—that good hill country and Lebanon."
But the LORD was angry with me on account of you, and He would not listen to me. "Enough!" the LORD said to me. "Do not speak to Me about this matter again.
Go up to the top of Pisgah and look to the west, north, south, and east. See it with your own eyes, but you will not cross this Jordan.
But commission Joshua and encourage and strengthen him, for he will cross over ahead of this people and enable them to inherit the land you will see."
So we stayed in the valley opposite Beth-peor.
Now, O Israel, listen to the statutes and judgments I am teaching you to perform, so that you may live and go in and possess the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, is giving you.
You must not add to the word I command you, nor take away from it, so that you may keep the commandments of the LORD your God, which I am commanding you.
Your eyes have seen what the LORD did at Baal Peor, how the LORD your God destroyed from among you everyone who followed Baal Peor.
But you who held fast to the LORD your God are alive today, every one of you.
See, I have taught you statutes and judgments, just as the LORD my God commanded me, so that you may follow them in the land you are entering to possess.

Keep them and do them, for this will be your wisdom and understanding in the sight of the peoples, who will hear all these statutes and say, “Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.”
For what great nation has a god so near to it as the LORD our God is to us whenever we call on Him?
And what great nation has statutes and judgments as righteous as all this law that I am setting before you today?

Only be very careful and watch yourself closely, lest you forget the things your eyes have seen, and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life. Teach them to your sons and to your grandsons.

On the day you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb, when the LORD said to me, “Assemble the people before Me, that I may let them hear My words, so that they may learn to fear Me all the days they live on the earth, and so that they may teach them to their children.”
You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain, while the mountain burned with fire to the heart of heaven, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.
Then the LORD spoke to you out of the fire. You heard the sound of words but saw no form; there was only a voice.
He declared to you His covenant, which He commanded you to follow—the Ten Commandments—and He wrote them on two tablets of stone.
At that time the LORD commanded me to teach you the statutes and ordinances, so that you may follow them in the land you are crossing over to possess.
So since you saw no form of any kind on the day the LORD spoke to you out of the fire at Horeb, be very careful to guard your lives.
That you do not act corruptly and make for yourselves an idol in the form of any figure—male or female—
the form of any beast on the earth, the form of any winged bird that flies in the sky,
the form of anything that creeps on the ground, or the form of any fish in the waters below the earth.

And when you look to the heavens and see the sun and moon and stars—all the host of heaven—do not be led astray to bow down to them and serve them. The LORD your God has allotted them to all the nations under heaven.
But the LORD has taken you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be a people for His inheritance, as you are this day.
Now the LORD was angry with me on account of your words, and He swore that I would not cross the Jordan or enter the good land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
For I am going to die in this land; I will not cross the Jordan. But you are going to cross over and possess that good land.
Be careful not to forget the covenant of the LORD your God that He made with you, and do not make for yourselves an idol in the form of anything the LORD your God has forbidden you.
For the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.

When you have children and grandchildren and have grown old in the land, if you act corruptly and make an idol in the form of anything, and do evil in the sight of the LORD your God, provoking Him to anger,
I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today that you will quickly perish from the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess. You will not live there long, but will be utterly destroyed.
Then the LORD will scatter you among the peoples, and you will be left few in number among the nations where the LORD will drive you.
There you will worship man-made gods of wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or eat or smell.
But from there you will seek the LORD your God, and you will find Him if you seek Him with all your heart and with all your soul.
When you are in distress and all these things have happened to you, then in the latter days you will return to the LORD your God and obey His voice.
For the LORD your God is a merciful God; He will not abandon you or destroy you or forget the covenant with your fathers, which He swore to them.

For ask now about the former days that were before you, since the day God created man on the earth, and ask from one end of heaven to the other whether anything as great as this has ever happened or been heard of.
Has any people ever heard the voice of God speaking out of the fire, as you have heard, and survived?

Or has any god tried to take for himself a nation out of another nation, by trials, signs, wonders, war, a mighty hand, an outstretched arm, and great terrors, as the LORD your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?
You were shown these things so that you might know that the LORD is God; there is no other besides Him.
He let you hear His voice from heaven to discipline you, and on earth He showed you His great fire, and you heard His words out of the fire.
Because He loved your fathers and chose their descendants after them, He brought you out of Egypt by His great power,
to drive out before you nations greater and stronger than you, to bring you into their land and give it to you as an inheritance, as it is today.
Know therefore today, and take it to heart, that the LORD is God in heaven above and on earth below; there is no other.

Keep His statutes and commandments, which I am giving you today, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you, and that you may live long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you for all time.
Then Moses set apart three cities east of the Jordan, toward the sunrise,
to which a manslayer could flee if he kills his neighbor unintentionally, without having been his enemy or intending to harm him in the past, and by fleeing to one of these cities he may live:
Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
This is the law Moses set before the Israelites.
These are the decrees, statutes, and ordinances Moses proclaimed to the Israelites when they came out of Egypt,
in the valley beyond the Jordan, opposite Beth Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, whom Moses and the Israelites defeated when they came out of Egypt.
They took possession of his land and of the land of Og king of Bashan, the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan,
from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley to Mount Sirion, that is, Hermon,
together with all the Arabah east of the Jordan, as far as the Sea of the Arabah, below the slopes of Pisgah.
Then Moses summoned all Israel and said to them: “Hear, O Israel, the statutes and ordinances that I am declaring in your hearing today. Learn them and be careful to follow them.
The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
He did not make this covenant with our fathers, but with all of us who are alive here today.
The LORD spoke to you directly out of the fire on the mountain.
At that time I stood between the LORD and you to declare His word to you, because you were afraid of the fire and did not go up the mountain. And He said:
‘I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of slavery.
You shall have no other gods before Me.
You shall not make for yourself a carved image or any likeness of what is in heaven above, or on the earth beneath, or in the waters below.

You shall not bow down to them or serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, punishing the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me,
but showing steadfast love to thousands of those who love Me and keep My commandments.
‘You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain, for the LORD will not leave unpunished anyone who takes His name in vain.
Observe the Sabbath day by keeping it holy, as the LORD your God has commanded you.
Six days you shall labor and do all your work,

but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. On it you shall not do any work—neither you, nor your son or daughter, nor your male or female servant, nor your ox or donkey, nor any of your livestock, nor the foreigner within your gates—so that your male and female servants may rest as you do.
Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out of there by His mighty power. Therefore the LORD your God has commanded you to observe the Sabbath day.
‘Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God has commanded you, so that your days may be prolonged and that it may go well with you in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, and you shall not desire your neighbor’s house, his field, his male or female servant, his ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.’

“These are the words the LORD spoke with a loud voice to your whole assembly on the mountain, out of the fire, the cloud, and the thick darkness; and He added nothing more. He wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
“When you heard the voice out of the darkness while the mountain was burning with fire, all the leaders of your tribes and your elders approached me,

and you said: ‘Look, the LORD our God has shown us His glory and greatness, and we have heard His voice out of the fire. Today we have seen that a man can live even if God speaks with him. But now, why should we die? For this great fire will consume us, and we will die if we hear the voice of the LORD our God any longer. For what mortal man has ever heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the fire, as we have, and survived? You go near and listen to all that the LORD our God says. Then you can tell us everything the LORD our God tells you; we will listen and obey.’
“And the LORD heard the voice of your words when you spoke to me, and the LORD said to me: ‘I have heard the words that this people have spoken to you. They have done well in all that they have said.
If only they had such a heart to fear Me and keep all My commandments always, so that it might go well with them and their children forever!
Go and tell them: “Return to your tents.”
But you, stand here by Me, and I will speak to you all the commandments, statutes, and ordinances you are to teach them, so that they may follow them in the land I am giving them to possess.’
“So be careful to do as the LORD your God has commanded you; do not turn aside to the right or to the left.
Walk in all the ways that the LORD your God has commanded you, so that you may live and prosper and prolong your days in the land that you will possess.”
Now this is the commandment—the statutes and the ordinances—that the LORD your God commanded me to teach you, so that you may do them in the land that you are crossing over to possess.
so that you may fear the LORD your God—you and your son and your grandson—all the days of your life, and so that your days may be prolonged.

Hear therefore, Israel, and be careful to do them, that it may go well with you, and that you may multiply greatly, as the LORD, the God of your fathers, promised you, in a land flowing with milk and honey.
Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one.
You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might.
And these words that I command you today shall be on your heart.
You shall teach them diligently to your children, and you shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise.
You shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes.
You shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
And when the LORD your God brings you into the land that He swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give you—with great and good cities that you did not build—
and houses full of all good things that you did not fill, and cisterns that you did not dig, and vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant—and when you eat and are full—
then take care lest you forget the LORD, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
It is the LORD your God whom you shall fear. Him you shall serve, and by His name you shall swear.
You shall not go after other gods, the gods of the peoples who are around you—
for the LORD your God in your midst is a jealous God—lest the anger of the LORD your God be kindled against you, and He destroy you from off the face of the earth.
You shall not put the LORD your God to the test, as you tested Him at Massah.
You shall diligently keep the commandments of the LORD your God, and His testimonies and His statutes, which He has commanded you.
And you shall do what is right and good in the sight of the LORD, that it may go well with you, and that you may go in and take possession of the good land that the LORD swore to give your fathers,
by thrusting out all your enemies from before you, as the LORD has spoken.
When your son asks you in time to come, “What is the meaning of the testimonies and the statutes and the rules that the LORD our God has commanded you?”
then you shall say to your son, “We were Pharaoh’s slaves in Egypt, and the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
And before our eyes the LORD did great and grievous signs and wonders in Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his house.
And He brought us out from there, that He might bring us in and give us the land that He swore to our fathers. “
And the LORD commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the LORD our God, for our good always, that He might preserve us alive, as we are this day.
And it will be righteousness for us, if we are careful to do all this commandment before the LORD our God, as He has commanded us.”

When the LORD your God brings you into the land you are entering to possess, He will clear away many nations before you—the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites—seven nations more numerous and mightier than you.
When the LORD your God delivers them over to you, you shall defeat them and devote them to complete destruction. You shall make no covenant with them and show them no mercy.
You shall not intermarry with them, neither giving your daughter to one of their sons nor taking one of their daughters for your son.
For he would turn your son away from following Me to serve other gods. Then the anger of the LORD would burn against you, and He would swiftly destroy you.
Instead, this is what you shall do to them: tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their carved images in the fire.
For you are a holy people to the LORD your God; the LORD your God has chosen you to be a people for His treasured possession out of all the peoples on the face of the earth.
It was not because you were more numerous than any other people that the LORD set His love on you and chose you, for you were the fewest of all peoples.

Rather, it is because the LORD loves you and keeps the oath He swore to your fathers that the LORD brought you out with a mighty hand and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
Know therefore that the LORD your God is God, the faithful God who keeps covenant and steadfast love with those who love Him and keep His commandments, to the thousandth generation,
but who repays those who hate Him to their face by destroying them. He will not delay in repaying the one who hates Him; He will repay him to his face.
You shall therefore be careful to do the commandment, the statutes, and the judgments that I am commanding you today.
And because you listen to these judgments and keep and do them, the LORD your God will keep with you the covenant and the steadfast love that He swore to your fathers.

He will love you, bless you, and multiply you; He will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground—your grain, your wine, and your oil—the increase of your herds and the young of your flock, in the land He swore to your fathers to give you.
You shall be blessed above all peoples; there shall be no barren man or woman among you, nor among your livestock.
The LORD will remove from you all sickness and will not put upon you any of the evil diseases of Egypt that you knew; instead, He will give them to all who hate you.
You shall consume all the peoples that the LORD your God gives you; your eye shall not pity them, nor shall you serve their gods, for that would be a snare to you.
If you say in your heart, “These nations are greater than I; how can I dispossess them?”
You shall not be afraid of them, but you shall remember what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt—

the great trials your eyes saw, the signs and wonders, the mighty hand and outstretched arm by which the LORD your God brought you out. So will the LORD your God do to all the peoples of whom you are afraid.
Moreover, the LORD your God will send the hornet among them until those left and hiding from you are destroyed.
You shall not be in dread of them, for the LORD your God is in your midst, a great and awesome God.
The LORD your God will clear away these nations before you little by little; you cannot destroy them all at once, lest the wild animals of the field multiply against you.
But the LORD your God will give them over to you and throw them into great confusion until they are destroyed.
He will give their kings into your hand, and you shall destroy their name from under heaven; no one will be able to stand against you until you have destroyed them.

You shall burn the carved images of their gods in the fire; you shall not covet the silver or gold on them or take it for yourself, lest you be ensnared by it, for it is an abomination to the LORD your God.
You shall not bring an abomination into your house, or you will become devoted to destruction like it. You shall utterly detest and abhor it, for it is devoted to destruction.
You shall be careful to do all the commandment that I command you today, so that you may live and multiply and go in and possess the land that the the LORD swore to your fathers.

And you shall remember the whole way that the the LORD your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, to humble you and test you, to know what was in your heart, whether you would keep His commandments or not.

He humbled you and let you hunger, and fed you with manna, which neither you nor your fathers had known, that He might make you know that man does not live by bread alone, but man lives by every word that comes from the mouth of the the LORD “
Your clothing did not wear out from you, and your foot did not swell these forty years.
Know then in your heart that, as a man disciplines his son, so the the LORD your God disciplines you.
You shall keep the commandments of the the LORD your God, walking in His ways and fearing Him “
For the the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, a land of brooks of water, of springs and deep waters gushing out in valleys and hills,
a land of wheat and barley, of vines and fig trees and pomegranates, a land of olive trees and honey,
a land where you will eat bread without scarcity and lack nothing, a land whose stones are iron and out of whose hills you can dig copper.
And you shall eat and be full, and you shall bless the the LORD your God for the good land He has given you “
Take care lest you forget the the LORD your God by not keeping His commandments, His ordinances, and His statutes, which I command you today,
lest, when you have eaten and are full and have built good houses and live in them,
and when your herds and flocks multiply and your silver and gold increase and all that you have increases— “
then your heart be lifted up, and you forget the the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery,
who led you through the great and terrifying wilderness, with its fiery serpents and scorpions and thirsty ground where there was no water, who brought water for you out of the flinty rock,
who fed you in the wilderness with manna that your fathers did not know, that He might humble you and test you, to do you good in the end “
Beware lest you say in your heart, ‘My power and the might of my hand have gotten me this wealth.’
You shall remember the the LORD your God, for it is He who gives you power to get wealth, that He may confirm His covenant that He swore to your fathers, as it is this day “
And if you forget the the LORD your God and go after other gods and serve them and bow down to them, I testify against you today that you shall surely perish.
Like the nations that the the LORD makes perish before you, so you shall perish, because you would not obey the voice of the the LORD your God.”
Hear, O Israel: today you are crossing the Jordan to enter and dispossess nations greater and mightier than you, cities great and fortified up to heaven.
A people great and tall, the descendants of the Anakim, whom you know, and concerning whom you have heard the saying, “Who can stand before the descendants of Anak?”

Know, therefore, today that the LORD your God is the One who goes before you as a consuming fire. He will destroy them and subdue them before you, so that you may drive them out and annihilate them quickly, just as the LORD has promised you.

When the LORD your God has driven them out before you, do not say in your heart, “It is because of my righteousness that the LORD has brought me in to possess this land,” whereas it is because of the wickedness of these nations that the LORD is driving them out before you.

It is not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart that you are going in to possess their land; rather, it is because of the wickedness of these nations that the LORD your God is driving them out before you, and so that He may keep the word that the LORD swore to your fathers—to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Know, therefore, that the LORD your God is not giving you this good land to possess because of your righteousness, for you are a stiff-necked people.
