Remember, and do not forget, how you provoked the LORD your God to wrath in the wilderness. From the day you came out of the land of Egypt until you arrived at this place, you have been rebellious against the LORD.
Even at Horeb you provoked the LORD to wrath, so that the LORD was angry with you and would have destroyed you.

When I ascended the mountain to receive the tablets of stone—the tablets of the covenant that the LORD made with you—I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights, eating no bread and drinking no water.
And the LORD gave me the two tablets of stone, written with the finger of God; on them were all the words that the LORD had spoken to you from the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly.
At the end of forty days and forty nights, the LORD gave me the two tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant.

Then the LORD said to me, “Arise, go down quickly from here, for your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have corrupted themselves. They have turned aside quickly from the way I commanded them; they have made for themselves a molded image.”
The LORD also said to me, “I have seen this people, and indeed they are a stiff-necked people.”
“Let Me alone, that I may destroy them and blot out their name from under heaven; and I will make of you a nation mightier and greater than they.”
So I turned and came down from the mountain while it burned with fire, the two tablets of the covenant in my two hands.
And I looked, and behold, you had sinned against the LORD your God and had made for yourselves a molded calf; you had turned aside quickly from the way that the LORD had commanded you.
Then I took the two tablets and threw them from my two hands, breaking them before your eyes.

And I fell down before the LORD, as before, for forty days and forty nights; I ate no bread and drank no water, because of all your sins that you had committed, doing what was evil in the sight of the LORD, so as to provoke Him to anger.
For I was afraid of the anger and fierce wrath with which the LORD was angry with you, to destroy you. But the LORD listened to me at that time also.
The LORD was also very angry with Aaron, to destroy him; so I prayed for Aaron at that time as well.

Then I took your sin, the calf that you had made, burned it with fire, crushed it and ground it thoroughly until it was as fine as dust, and I threw its dust into the brook descending from the mountain.
At Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth Hattaavah, you also provoked the LORD.
When the LORD sent you from Kadesh Barnea, saying, “Go up and possess the land that I have given you,” you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God and did not believe Him or obey His voice.
You have been rebellious against the LORD from the day I knew you.
So I fell down before the LORD for forty days and forty nights, as at the first, because the LORD had said He would destroy you.
I prayed to the LORD and said, “O Lord the LORD, do not destroy Your people and Your inheritance, which You have redeemed through Your greatness, which You brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
Remember Your servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; do not look on the stubbornness of this people, or on their wickedness and sin,

lest the land from which You brought us say, ‘Because the LORD was not able to bring them into the land which He promised them, and because He hated them, He has brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.’
Yet they are Your people and Your inheritance, whom You brought out by Your mighty power and by Your outstretched arm.”
At that time, the LORD said to me, “Carve out two stone tablets for yourself, like the first ones, and come up to Me on the mountain. Make an ark of wood for yourself.
I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets—the ones you broke—and you are to put them in the ark.”
So I made an ark of acacia wood and carved two stone tablets like the first ones. Then I went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hand.
He wrote on the tablets what had been written before—the Ten Commandments that the LORD had spoken to you on the mountain out of the fire on the day of the assembly—and the LORD gave them to me.
I turned and came down from the mountain and put the tablets in the ark I had made, and there they remain, just as the LORD commanded me.
The Israelites set out from Beeroth Bene-jaakan for Moserah. There Aaron died and was buried, and his son Eleazar succeeded him as priest.
From there they traveled to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of flowing streams.
At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the LORD’s covenant, to stand before the LORD and minister to Him, and to bless in His name, as they do to this day.
That is why Levi has no portion or inheritance among his brothers: the LORD is his inheritance, just as the LORD your God promised him.
I remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights, as I had the first time, and the LORD listened to me then as well. The LORD was unwilling to destroy you.
Then the LORD said to me, “Get up and go on ahead of the people, so that they may enter and possess the land I swore to give their fathers.”
And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you? He asks that you fear the LORD your God, walk in all His ways, love Him, and serve the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul.
He asks that you keep the LORD’s commands and statutes, which I am giving you today, for your good.
Look, to the LORD your God belong the heavens, even the highest heavens, and the earth with everything in it.
Yet the LORD set His affection on your fathers and loved them; He chose their descendants after them—yes, you—above all peoples, as it is today.
Purify your hearts, then, and do not be stubborn any longer.
For the LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, mighty, and awesome God, who shows no partiality and accepts no bribe.
He executes justice for the fatherless and the widow, and loves the foreigner, giving him food and clothing.
So you must love the foreigner, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
You shall fear the LORD your God. You shall serve Him and cling to Him, and you shall swear by His name.
He is your praise and your God, who has done for you these great and awesome things your eyes have seen.
Your fathers went down to Egypt with seventy persons, and now the LORD your God has made you as numerous as the stars of heaven.
Love the the LORD your God all your days, and keep His charge, His statutes, His ordinances, and His commandments.
Today you know that it was not your children—who have not known and have not seen the discipline of the the LORD your God, His greatness, His mighty hand, and His outstretched arm—
nor His signs and His works that He did in the midst of Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to all his land.
And what He did to the army of Egypt, to its horses and chariots, when He made the waters of the Red Sea flood over them as they pursued you, and the the LORD destroyed them to this day.
And what He did for you in the wilderness until you came to this place.

And what He did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, son of Reuben, when the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their households, their tents, and every living thing that followed them, in the midst of all Israel.
But your own eyes have seen all the great work that the the LORD has done.
Therefore keep the whole commandment that I am commanding you today, so that you may be strong and go in and possess the land that you are crossing over to possess,
and so that you may prolong your days on the land that the the LORD swore to your fathers to give to them and to their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey.
For the land that you are entering to possess is not like the land of Egypt, from which you came out, where you sowed your seed and watered it by foot, like a vegetable garden.
But the land that you are crossing over to possess is a land of hills and valleys; it drinks water from the rain of heaven,
a land that the the LORD your God cares for; the eyes of the the LORD your God are always upon it, from the beginning of the year to its end.
And it shall be that if you listen carefully to the commandments that I am commanding you today, to love the the LORD your God and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul,
then I will give the rain of your land in its season, the early rain and the late rain, and you shall gather in your grain, your new wine, and your oil.
And I will give grass in your field for your livestock, and you shall eat and be satisfied.
Take care lest your heart be deceived, and you turn aside and serve other gods and worship them.

Then the anger of the the LORD will be kindled against you, and He will shut up the heavens so that there will be no rain, and the land will not yield its fruit, and you will perish quickly from the good land that the the LORD is giving you.
Therefore lay up these words of mine in your heart and in your soul, and bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes.
And you shall teach them to your children, speaking of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise.
And you shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,
so that your days and the days of your children may be multiplied on the land that the the LORD swore to your fathers to give them, as long as the heavens are above the earth.
For if you carefully keep all this commandment that I am commanding you to do, to love the the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, and to cling to Him,
then the the LORD will drive out all these nations before you, and you will dispossess nations greater and mightier than you.
Every place on which the sole of your foot treads shall be yours; your border shall be from the wilderness and Lebanon, from the River, the river Euphrates, to the western sea.
No man shall be able to stand against you; the the LORD your God will put the fear and dread of you on all the land that you tread, just as He has spoken to you.
See, I am setting before you today blessing and curse:
the blessing, if you obey the commandments of the the LORD your God that I am commanding you today;
and the curse, if you do not obey the commandments of the the LORD your God, but turn aside from the way that I am commanding you today, to go after other gods that you have not known.
And it shall be, when the the LORD your God brings you into the land that you are going in to possess, that you shall put the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
Are they not beyond the Jordan, toward the west, in the land of the Canaanites who dwell in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, beside the oaks of Moreh?
For you are crossing the Jordan to go in to possess the land that the the LORD your God is giving you, and you shall possess it and dwell in it.
And you shall keep and do all the statutes and the ordinances that I am setting before you today.
These are the statutes and ordinances you must keep and perform all the days you live on the earth—in the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, gives you to possess.
You must utterly destroy all the places where the nations you are dispossessing served their gods—on the high mountains, on the hills, and under every leafy tree.
You must tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, burn their Asherah poles with fire, and cut down the carved images of their gods; you must also wipe out their names from that place.
You shall not do this to the LORD your God.
Instead, you must seek the place that the LORD your God chooses from among all your tribes to establish His name as His dwelling, and you must go there.
There you must bring your burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your tithes, the heave offering of your hand, your vows, your freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your herd and flock.
There you shall eat before the LORD your God, and you shall rejoice in all your undertakings—you and your households—as the LORD your God has blessed you.
You must not do as we are doing here today, each person doing whatever is right in his own eyes.
For you have not yet come to the rest and to the inheritance that the LORD your God is giving you.
But when you cross the Jordan and dwell in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to inherit, and He gives you rest from all your enemies around you, so that you dwell securely,

then to the place that the LORD your God chooses to make His name dwell, you shall bring all that I command you: your burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your tithes, the heave offering of your hand, and all your choice vows that you vow to the LORD.

And you shall rejoice before the LORD your God—you, your sons, your daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levite who is within your gates—because he has no portion or inheritance with you.
Take heed to yourself that you do not offer your burnt offerings in every place you see.
But in the place that the LORD chooses in one of your tribes, there you shall do all that I command you.

However, you may slaughter and eat meat in all your towns, according to the blessing of the LORD your God that He has given you; the unclean and the clean alike may eat it, as the gazelle and the deer.
You shall not eat the blood; you must pour it on the earth like water.

You may not eat within your towns the tithe of your grain, your new wine, or your oil, nor the firstborn of your herd or flock, nor any vow you make, nor your freewill offerings, nor the heave offering of your hand.

Instead, you must eat them before the LORD your God in the place that the LORD your God chooses—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, and the Levite who is within your towns—and you shall rejoice before the LORD your God in all your undertakings.
Take heed to yourself that you do not forsake the Levite as long as you live in your land.
When the LORD your God enlarges your territory, as He has promised you, and you say, “I want to eat meat,” because your soul craves meat, you may eat meat whenever you desire.

If the place that the LORD your God chooses to put His name is too far from you, then you may slaughter from your herd and flock that the LORD has given you, as I have commanded you, and you may eat within your towns whenever you desire.
Just as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so you may eat them; the unclean and the clean alike may eat them.
Only be sure that you do not eat the blood, for the blood is the life, and you shall not eat the life with the flesh.
You shall not eat it; you must pour it on the earth like water.
You shall not eat it, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you, because you do what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
But your holy things that are yours, and your vows, you shall take and go to the place that the LORD chooses.

And you shall offer your burnt offerings—the flesh and the blood—on the altar of the LORD your God; and the blood of your sacrifices shall be poured out on the altar of the LORD your God, and you shall eat the flesh.
Observe and obey all these words that I command you, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you forever, because you do what is good and right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
When the LORD your God cuts off before you the nations that you are going in to dispossess, and you dispossess them and dwell in their land,

take care that you are not ensnared after them, after they are destroyed from before you, and that you do not inquire about their gods, saying, “How did these nations serve their gods? I will do the same.”

You shall not do so to the LORD your God, for everything that is an abomination to the LORD, which He hates, they have done for their gods; for they even burn their sons and their daughters in the fire to their gods.
You shall keep everything that I command you to do; you shall not add to it, nor shall you take away from it.
If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises among you and proclaims a sign or wonder to you,
and the sign or wonder he spoke to you comes to pass, and he says, “Let us follow other gods, whom you have not known, and let us serve them,”
you must not heed the words of that prophet or dreamer. For the the LORD your God is testing you to discover whether you love the the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul.
You are to follow the the LORD your God and fear Him. Keep His commandments and obey His voice, and you shall serve Him and cling to Him.

But that prophet or dreamer must be put to death, because he has spoken rebellion against the the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery, to turn you from the way the the LORD your God commanded you to walk in. So you shall purge the evil from your midst.

If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son or daughter, or the wife you embrace, or your closest friend secretly entices you, saying, “Let us go and serve other gods”—whom neither you nor your fathers have known—
the gods of the peoples around you, whether near to you or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other—
you must not yield to him or listen to him. Show him no pity, and do not spare him or shield him.
Instead, you must surely put him to death. Your hand must be first against him to put him to death, and then the hands of all the people.
Stone him to death, because he has tried to turn you away from the the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
Then all Israel will hear and fear, and they will never again do such an evil thing among you.
If you hear it said about one of the cities the the LORD your God is giving you to live in,
that wicked men have gone out from among you and led the inhabitants of their city astray, saying, “Let us go and serve other gods”—whom you have not known—
then you must investigate, probe, and inquire thoroughly. If it is true and confirmed that such an abomination has been committed among you,
you must surely put to the sword all who live in that city. Devote it and everything in it, including its livestock, to complete destruction.

And you are to gather all its plunder into the middle of its square and burn the city and all its plunder as a whole burnt offering to the the LORD your God. It must remain a heap of ruins forever; it must never be rebuilt.
Nothing devoted to destruction may cling to your hand, so that the the LORD will turn from His fierce anger, give you mercy, and show you compassion, and multiply you as He swore to your fathers.
because you obey the voice of the the LORD your God by keeping all His commandments that I am giving you today, and by doing what is right in the eyes of the the LORD your God.
You are children of the LORD your God; you must not lacerate yourselves nor shave a bald patch between your eyes for the dead.
For you are a holy people to the LORD your God, and the LORD has chosen you to be a people for Himself, a treasured possession above all the peoples on the face of the earth.
You shall not eat any abominable thing.
These are the beasts you may eat: the ox, the sheep, the goat,
the deer, the gazelle, the roe deer, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope, and the mountain sheep.
You may eat every beast that has a divided hoof and is cloven-footed and chews the cud.
Yet of those that chew the cud or have a divided hoof, you shall not eat these: the camel, the hare, and the rock badger, because they chew the cud but do not part the hoof; they are unclean to you.
And the pig, because it parts the hoof but does not chew the cud, is unclean to you; you shall not eat their flesh, nor shall you touch their carcass.
Of all that is in the waters, you may eat these: everything that has fins and scales you may eat.
But you shall not eat whatever lacks fins and scales; it is unclean to you.
You may eat any clean bird.
But these you shall not eat: the eagle, the vulture, the black vulture,
the kite, the falcon, and the buzzard of any kind;
the ostrich, the short-eared owl, the gull, and the hawk of any kind;
the little owl, the great owl, the white owl,
the pelican, the carrion vulture, the cormorant,
the stork, the heron of any kind, the hoopoe, and the bat.
And every swarming winged creature is unclean to you; it shall not be eaten.
You may eat any clean bird.

You shall not eat any carcass; you may give it to the sojourner within your gates, and he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner, for you are a holy people to the LORD your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
You shall surely tithe all the produce of your seed that comes from the field year by year.

And you shall eat before the LORD your God, in the place He chooses to make His name dwell, the tithe of your grain, your new wine, and your oil, and the firstborn of your herd and flock, so that you may learn to fear the LORD your God all your days.
And if the way is too long for you, so that you are not able to carry it, because the LORD your God has blessed you, and the place the LORD your God chooses to set His name is too far from you,
then you shall convert it into money, bind the money in your hand, and go to the place the LORD your God chooses.

And you shall spend the money on whatever your soul desires—on oxen, sheep, wine, strong drink, or whatever your soul asks of you—and you shall eat there before the LORD your God and rejoice, you and your household.
And you shall not forsake the Levite within your gates, for he has no portion or inheritance with you.
At the end of every third year you shall bring out all the tithe of your produce for that year and store it within your gates.

And the Levite, because he has no portion or inheritance with you, and the sojourner, the fatherless, and the widow who are within your gates, shall come and eat and be satisfied, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hand that you do.
At the conclusion of every seventh year, you must declare a remission of debts.

This is the statute of the release: every creditor who has lent anything to his neighbor shall cancel it; he shall not demand payment from his neighbor or his brother, because the LORD has proclaimed a release.
You may collect from a foreigner, but you must relinquish your claim against your brother.
Nevertheless, there should be no poor among you, for the LORD will surely bless you in the land that the LORD your God gives you to possess as an inheritance,
provided you diligently obey the voice of the LORD your God, observing to do all this commandment that I command you today.
For the LORD your God will bless you, as He has spoken to you, and you shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow; you shall rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over you.
If a poor man is found among you—one of your brothers—within any of your towns in the land that the LORD your God gives you, you must not become callous or withhold assistance from your poor brother.
Rather, you must open your hand generously to him and lend him enough to cover whatever he lacks.

Beware, lest a wicked thought arise in your heart, saying, “The seventh year, the year of release, is near,” so that you look resentfully on your poor brother and give him nothing; then he will cry out to the LORD against you, and guilt will rest on you.
You shall surely give to him, and your heart must not resent giving to him, because for this the the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in all to which you put your hand.
For the poor will never cease from the midst of the land; therefore I command you, saying, “You shall surely open your hand to your brother, to your poor and needy in your land.”
If your brother, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, is sold to you and serves you six years, then in the seventh year you shall let him go free from you.
And when you let him go free from you, you shall not send him away empty-handed.
You shall furnish him generously from your flock, from your threshing floor, and from your winepress; from that with which the LORD your God has blessed you, you shall give to him.
You shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you; therefore I command you this thing today.
And it shall be, if he says to you, “I will not leave you,” because he loves you and your household, because it is good for him with you,
then you shall take an awl and thrust it through his ear into the door, and he shall be your servant for life. And to your female servant you shall do likewise.

It shall not seem a hardship to you when you let him go free from you, for in serving six years he has been worth twice as much as a hired worker to you; and the LORD your God will bless you in all that you do.
You shall set apart to the LORD your God every firstborn male that is born of your herd and of your flock. You shall do no work with the firstborn of your ox, nor shear the firstborn of your sheep.
You shall eat it before the LORD your God each year in the place that the LORD will choose, you and your household.
But if there is any blemish in it—if it is lame or blind, or has any serious defect—you shall not sacrifice it to the LORD your God.
You shall eat it within your towns; both the unclean and the clean may eat it, as the gazelle and the deer.
Only you shall not eat its blood; you shall pour it out on the earth as water.
Observe the month of Aviv and celebrate the Passover to the LORD your God, because in the month of Aviv the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
You shall sacrifice the Passover to the LORD your God from the flock and the herd at the place the LORD chooses to establish His name.

You must not eat leavened bread with it; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, the bread of hardship, because you left Egypt in haste, so that you may remember for the rest of your life the day you departed from Egypt.
No leaven shall be seen anywhere within your territory for seven days, and none of the meat you sacrifice on the evening of the first day shall remain until morning.
You may not sacrifice the Passover in just any town the LORD your God gives you;
rather, you shall sacrifice it at the place the LORD your God chooses for His name to dwell, in the evening at sunset, at the appointed time of your departure from Egypt.
You shall cook it and eat it at the place the LORD your God chooses, and in the morning you may turn and return to your tents.
For six days you shall eat unleavened bread, but on the seventh day there shall be a sacred assembly to the LORD your God, and you shall do no work.
You shall count seven weeks for yourself; begin counting the seven weeks from the time you first begin harvesting the standing grain.
Then you shall celebrate the Feast of Weeks to the LORD your God with a freewill offering from your hand, in proportion to the blessing the LORD your God has given you.

You shall rejoice before the LORD your God at the place He chooses—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, the Levite within your towns, and the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow among you.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and carefully keep and obey these statutes.
You shall celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days when you gather in the produce from your threshing floor and your winepress.
You shall rejoice in your feast—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow within your towns.

For seven days you shall celebrate the feast to the LORD your God at the place He chooses, because the LORD your God will bless you in all your produce and in every work of your hands, and you shall be altogether joyful.

Three times a year all your males shall appear before the LORD your God at the place He chooses: at the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Tabernacles. They shall not appear before the LORD without an offering,
but each shall give as he is able, according to the blessing the LORD your God has given him.
You shall appoint judges and officers for your tribes in all the towns the LORD your God gives you, and they shall judge the people with righteousness.
You shall not pervert justice, show partiality, or accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.
You must pursue justice, and only justice, so that you may live and possess the land the LORD your God is giving you.
You shall not plant for yourself an Asherah of any kind of tree beside the altar of the LORD your God that you build,
and you shall not set up for yourself a sacred pillar, which the LORD your God hates.
Do not sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or a sheep that has any blemish or defect, for such an offering is detestable to Him.
If a man or a woman among you in one of the towns that the LORD your God gives you is found doing evil in the sight of the LORD your God by breaking His covenant,
and, contrary to My command, has worshiped other gods—bowing down to them, or to the sun, the moon, or any of the heavenly bodies—
and this is reported to you, then you must investigate it meticulously. If the report proves true and the matter is established—that this detestable thing has been done in Israel—
you must bring that man or woman who has committed this wickedness to the gates of your city and stone them to death.
On the testimony of two or three witnesses the accused must be put to death, but no one may be executed on the testimony of a single witness.
The witnesses must be the first to put the person to death, and then all the people must take part. You must remove the evil from among you.

If a case comes before your courts that is too difficult for you to judge—whether it concerns bloodshed, legal disputes, or bodily injury—then you must go up to the place that the LORD your God will choose.
You must go to the Levitical priests and to the judge in office at that time, inquire of them, and they will declare to you the verdict in the case.
You must act according to the decision they give you at the place the LORD will choose, and you must be careful to do everything they instruct you to do.
You must act according to the law they teach you and according to the judgment they pronounce; do not deviate from what they tell you in any way.
The man who acts arrogantly, refusing to listen either to the priest who stands there to minister before the LORD your God or to the judge, must be put to death. You must purge the evil from Israel.
Then all the people will hear and be afraid, and they will not act so arrogantly again.

When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, and you take possession of it, and you settle in it, and then you say, "Let us appoint a king over us, as all the nations around us have,"
be sure to set over you a king whom the LORD your God chooses. He must be one of your own people; do not set a foreigner over you, one who is not an Israelite.
The king must not acquire many horses for himself, and he must not make the people return to Egypt to obtain more horses, for the LORD has said to you, "You are not to go back that way again."
He must not take many wives, lest he be drawn into moral compromise, nor may he accumulate excessive silver and gold.
When he sits on the throne of his kingdom, he must write for himself a copy of this law on a scroll, taken from the one kept before the Levitical priests.
It must remain with him, and he must read it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to revere the LORD his God and to observe faithfully all the words of this law and these statutes.
Then he will not regard himself as superior to his fellow Israelites, and he will not deviate from the commandment in any respect, so that he and his sons may reign long over his kingdom in Israel.
The Levitical priests—that is, the whole tribe of Levi—shall have no land allotment or inheritance among the Israelites. They shall eat the offerings made by fire to the the LORD and His inheritance.
They shall have no inheritance among their brothers; the the LORD is their inheritance, just as He promised them.
This shall be the priests’ prescribed share from the people, from those who offer a sacrifice, whether an ox or a sheep: they shall give to the priest the shoulder, the cheeks, and the stomach.
The firstfruits of your grain, your new wine, and your oil, and the first wool sheared from your flock, you shall give to him.
For the the LORD your God has chosen him and his sons from among all your tribes to stand and serve the the LORD all their days.
If a Levite comes from one of your towns, from anywhere in Israel where he has been sojourning, and comes with all his heart’s desire to the place that the the LORD will choose,
then he shall minister in the name of the the LORD his God, like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the the LORD.
They shall eat equal portions, apart from what comes from the sale of his ancestral property.
When you enter the land that the the LORD your God is giving you, you must not learn to imitate the abominations of those nations.
No one among you shall be found who sacrifices his son or daughter in the fire, or who practices divination, soothsaying, enchantment, or witchcraft,
or who casts spells, or consults a medium or spiritist, or seeks guidance from the dead.
For everyone who does these things is an abomination to the the LORD, and because of these abominations the the LORD your God is driving them out before you.
You shall be blameless before the the LORD your God.
For these nations that you are dispossessing listen to soothsayers and diviners, but as for you, the the LORD your God has not permitted you to do so.
The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers; you shall listen to him.

This is in accordance with all that you asked of the the LORD your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, saying, “Let me not hear again the voice of the the LORD my God, nor see this great fire any longer, lest I die.”
And the the LORD said to me, “They have spoken well.”
I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their brothers, and I will put My words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I command him.
And whoever does not listen to My words that he speaks in My name, I Myself will require it of him.
But the prophet who presumes to speak a word in My name that I have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods—that prophet shall die.
And if you say in your heart, “How shall we know the word that the the LORD has not spoken?”

When a prophet speaks in the name of the the LORD, if the thing does not happen or come to pass, that is the word that the the LORD has not spoken; the prophet has spoken it presumptuously. You shall not be afraid of him.
When the LORD your God annihilates the nations whose land the LORD your God is giving you, and you dispossess them and dwell in their cities and houses,
you shall set apart three cities for yourself within the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
You shall prepare the road for yourself and divide into three parts the territory of your land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, so that every manslayer may flee there.
Now this is the case of the manslayer who flees there and lives: whoever strikes his neighbor without knowledge, not having hated him previously.

For example, when a man goes into the forest with his neighbor to cut wood, and his hand swings the axe to fell a tree, and the iron head slips from the handle and strikes his neighbor so that he dies, that man may flee to one of these cities and live.

Otherwise the avenger of blood may pursue the manslayer while his anger is hot, overtake him because the way is long, and strike him dead, although he does not deserve death, since he had not hated his neighbor before.
Therefore I command you: set apart three cities for yourself.
If the LORD your God enlarges your territory, as He swore to your fathers, and gives you all the land He promised to your fathers,
provided you carefully keep all this commandment that I am commanding you today—to love the LORD your God and to walk in His ways all your days—then you shall add three more cities to these three.
Thus innocent blood will not be shed in the midst of the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and bloodguilt will not be upon you.
But if a man hates his neighbor, lies in wait for him, rises against him, strikes him dead, and then flees to one of these cities,
the elders of his city shall send for him, bring him back from there, and deliver him into the hand of the avenger of blood, that he may die.
Your eye shall not pity him, but you shall purge the guilt of innocent blood from Israel, so that it may go well with you.
You shall not move your neighbor’s landmark, which the ancestors set in the inheritance you will inherit in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
A single witness shall not rise against a man for any iniquity or sin; at the testimony of two or three witnesses a matter shall be established.
If a malicious witness rises against a man to accuse him of wrongdoing,
then both men in the dispute shall stand before the LORD, before the priests and the judges who are in office in those days.
The judges shall investigate thoroughly, and if the witness is a false witness who has testified falsely against his brother,
then you shall do to him as he intended to do to his brother. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst.
Those who remain shall hear and fear, and they shall never again do such an evil thing among you.
Your eye shall not pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

When you go out to war against your enemies and see horses and chariots and an army greater than yours, do not be afraid of them, because the LORD your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt, is with you.
When you draw near to the battle, the priest shall come forward and speak to the people.
“Hear, O Israel: Today you are drawing near to battle against your enemies. Do not let your hearts grow faint; do not be afraid, do not panic, and do not be terrified by them.
For the LORD your God is He who goes with you to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.”
Then the officers shall address the people: “Who is the man who has built a new house but has not dedicated it? Let him return home, lest he die in battle and another man dedicate it.
And who is the man who has planted a vineyard but has not yet enjoyed its fruit? Let him return home, lest he die in battle and another man enjoy its fruit.
And who is the man who has betrothed a wife but has not married her? Let him return home, lest he die in battle and another man marry her.”
The officers shall speak further to the people and say, “Who is the man who is fearful and fainthearted? Let him return home, so that his brothers’ hearts do not melt as his own has.”
When the officers have finished speaking to the people, they shall appoint commanders over the troops at the head of the people.
When you approach a city to fight against it, first offer it terms of peace.
If it responds peacefully and opens its gates to you, then all the people found in it shall be subject to forced labor and shall serve you.
But if it refuses to make peace with you and makes war against you, then you shall besiege it.
When the LORD your God delivers it into your hand, you shall put all its men to the sword.

But the women, the children, the livestock, and everything else in the city—all its spoil—you shall take as plunder for yourself, and you shall enjoy the spoil of your enemies, which the LORD your God has given you.
This is how you shall treat all the cities that are very far from you and do not belong to these nations.
But in the cities of these peoples that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, you shall not spare anything that breathes.
Rather, you shall devote them to complete destruction—the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites—just as the LORD your God has commanded you.
Do this so that they do not teach you to follow all the abominations they practice for their gods and cause you to sin against the LORD your God.

When you lay siege to a city for a long time, fighting against it to capture it, do not destroy its trees by swinging an axe against them, for you may eat from them. Do not cut them down. Are the trees of the field human beings, that you should besiege them as well?
You may, however, destroy and cut down trees that you know are not fruit trees, so that you may build siege works against the city that is waging war against you, until it falls.
If a homicide victim is discovered fallen in a field within the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess, and the perpetrator remains unknown,
then your elders and judges shall go out and measure the distance from the victim to the surrounding cities.
The city nearest the victim shall have its elders take a heifer from the herd—one that has never been worked and has never drawn a yoke.
The elders of that city shall bring the heifer down to a valley with a perennial stream, land that has neither been plowed nor sown, and there they shall break the heifer's neck in the valley.

Then the priests, the sons of Levi, shall approach, because the LORD your God has chosen them to minister to Him and to bless in the name of the LORD, and every dispute and every assault shall be settled by their verdict.
All the elders of the city nearest the victim shall wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley.
They shall declare, "Our hands did not shed this blood, nor did our eyes witness the deed.
Atone, O the LORD, for Your people Israel, whom You have redeemed, and do not let innocent blood remain among Your people Israel." Then the bloodguilt shall be atoned for them.
So you shall purge the innocent blood from your midst, for you must do what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
When you march out to war against your enemies, and the LORD your God delivers them into your hand, and you take captives,
and you see among the captives a woman of striking beauty and desire her, you may take her as your wife.
Then you shall bring her into your house, and she shall shave her head and trim her nails.

She shall remove the garments of her captivity, remain in your house, and mourn her father and mother for a full month; after that you may consummate the marriage with her, and she shall be your wife.

But if you no longer take pleasure in her, you shall release her to go wherever she wishes; you shall not sell her for money, and you shall not reduce her to servitude, because you have dishonored her.
If a man has two wives, one beloved and the other despised, and both bear him sons, and the firstborn son is the child of the despised wife,
then on the day he distributes his inheritance among his sons, he may not grant the son of the beloved wife the status of firstborn in preference to the firstborn son of the despised wife.

Rather, he shall acknowledge the firstborn, the son of the despised wife, by allotting him a double share of all that he possesses, for he is the first yield of his vigor; the right of the firstborn belongs to him.
If a man has a stubborn and intractable son who will not obey his father or mother, and even when they chastise him he still refuses to heed them,
then his father and mother shall seize him and bring him before the elders of his city and to the gate of his hometown.
They shall say to the elders, "This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious; he will not obey us; he is a glutton and a drunkard."
Then all the men of his city shall stone him to death. So you shall purge the evil from your midst, and all Israel shall hear and fear.
If a man is guilty of a capital offense and is put to death, and you hang him on a tree,

his corpse shall not remain on the tree overnight; you shall certainly bury him that same day, because a hanged man is accursed of God. You shall not defile the land that the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance.
If you see your brother's ox or sheep going astray, do not ignore them; return them to your brother.
If your brother is not nearby and you do not know him, bring the animal home and keep it with you until he comes looking for it; then restore it to him.
Do the same with his donkey, his cloak, or anything else your brother loses that you find; you must not ignore it.
If you see your brother's donkey or ox fallen on the road, do not ignore it; help him lift it up.
A woman must not wear a man's clothing, and a man must not put on a woman's garment, for everyone who does these things is detestable to the LORD your God.
If you come across a bird's nest along the road, in any tree or on the ground, with chicks or eggs, and the mother is sitting on the chicks or on the eggs, do not take the mother with the young.
You may take the young for yourself, but you must let the mother go, so that it may go well with you and you may live long.
When you build a new house, make a parapet around your roof, so that you do not bring bloodguilt on your house if anyone falls from it.
Do not sow your vineyard with two kinds of seed, or the whole harvest will be defiled—both the seed you sow and the vineyard's fruit.
Do not plow with an ox and a donkey together.
Do not wear clothing made of wool and linen woven together.
Make tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wear.
If a man marries a woman and, after sleeping with her, comes to hate her,
and he accuses her of shameful conduct and gives her a bad name by saying, “I married this woman, and when I approached her, I did not find evidence of her virginity,”
then the girl's father and mother must take the evidence of her virginity and bring it to the elders at the city gate.
The girl's father must say to the elders, “I gave my daughter to this man as a wife, and he has come to hate her.

Now he has accused her of shameful conduct, saying, ‘I did not find your daughter a virgin.’ But here is the evidence of my daughter's virginity.” Then they must spread the cloth before the elders of the city.
The elders of that city must take the man and punish him.
They must fine him a hundred shekels of silver and give them to the girl's father, because he has given a bad name to a virgin in Israel. She must remain his wife, and he may never divorce her.
But if the charge is true and no evidence of virginity is found for the girl,

they must bring her to the door of her father's house, and the men of her city must stone her to death, because she committed a disgraceful act in Israel by prostituting herself in her father's house. So you must purge the evil from your midst.
If a man is found lying with a woman who is married to another man, both of them must die—the man who lay with the woman and the woman. So you must purge the evil from Israel.
If a virgin is betrothed to a man and another man meets her in the city and sleeps with her,

you must bring both of them to the gate of that city and stone them to death—the girl because she did not cry out for help though she was in the city, and the man because he violated his neighbor's wife. So you must purge the evil from your midst.
But if a man finds the betrothed girl in the open country and seizes her and sleeps with her, only the man who lay with her must die.
Do nothing to the girl; she has committed no sin deserving death, for this case is like that of a man who attacks his neighbor and murders him.
For the man found her in the open country, and although the betrothed girl cried out, there was no one to save her.
If a man finds a virgin who is not betrothed and seizes her and sleeps with her, and they are discovered,
the man who lay with her must give the girl's father fifty shekels of silver, and she must become his wife, because he has humiliated her. He may never divorce her.
A man must not take his father's wife or uncover his father's nakedness.
No man whose genitals have been crushed or cut off may enter the assembly of the LORD.
No person born of a forbidden union may enter the assembly of the LORD; even to the tenth generation, none of his descendants may enter the assembly of the LORD.
No Ammonite or Moabite may enter the assembly of the LORD; even to the tenth generation, none of them may ever enter the assembly of the LORD,
because they did not meet you with bread and water on the way when you came out of Egypt, and because they hired Balaam son of Beor from Pethor in Mesopotamia to curse you.
But the LORD your God would not listen to Balaam; instead the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the LORD your God loved you.
You shall never seek their peace or prosperity throughout your entire life.
You shall not despise an Edomite, for he is your brother. You shall not despise an Egyptian, because you were a stranger in his land.
The children born to them in the third generation may enter the assembly of the LORD.
When you march out against your enemies, you must guard against every evil thing.
If any man among you becomes unclean because of a nocturnal emission, he must go outside the camp and not enter its midst.
Toward evening he shall bathe in water, and when the sun has set, he may return to the camp.
You shall have a designated place outside the camp, and you shall go out to it.
You shall carry a trowel among your equipment; when you relieve yourself outside, you shall dig with it and then cover your excrement.

For the LORD your God walks in the midst of your camp to deliver you and to defeat your enemies before you; therefore your camp must be holy, so that He sees no indecent thing among you and turns away from you.
You shall not hand over to his master a slave who has escaped from his master to you.
He shall live with you, in your midst, in whatever place he chooses among one of your towns, wherever it suits him; you shall not oppress him.
No daughter of Israel shall be a cult prostitute, and no son of Israel shall be a cult prostitute.
You shall not bring the fee of a prostitute or the price of a dog into the house of the LORD your God to pay any vow, for both are an abomination to the LORD your God.
You shall not charge interest to your brother—interest on money, interest on food, or interest on anything that is lent.
You may charge a foreigner interest, but you may not charge your brother interest, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all that you undertake in the land you are entering to possess.
If you make a vow to the LORD your God, you shall not delay to fulfill it, for the LORD your God will surely require it of you, and you will incur guilt.
But if you refrain from vowing, you will not be guilty.
You must be careful to perform what you have promised, for you have voluntarily vowed to the LORD your God what you spoke with your mouth.
If you enter your neighbor's vineyard, you may eat grapes to your satisfaction, as many as you wish, but you shall not put any into your container.
If you enter your neighbor's standing grain, you may pluck heads of grain with your hand, but you shall not put a sickle to your neighbor's standing grain.

When a man takes a wife and marries her, and she does not find favor in his eyes because he has found some indecency in her, he may write her a certificate of divorce, place it in her hand, and send her away from his house.
If she leaves his house and becomes the wife of another man,
and the latter husband hates her and writes her a certificate of divorce, places it in her hand, and sends her away from his house—or if the latter husband dies, who took her as his wife—

then her former husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife after she has been defiled; for that is an abomination before the LORD, and you must not bring sin upon the land that the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance.
When a man takes a new wife, he shall not go out with the army, nor shall any duty be laid upon him; he shall be free at home for one year and cheer his wife whom he has taken.
No one shall take a handmill or an upper millstone as security for a debt, since that would be taking a man's livelihood as security.
If a man is found kidnapping one of his fellow Israelites and treating him as a slave or selling him, that kidnapper shall die; so you shall purge the evil from among you.
Take care in the case of leprous disease to observe and do according to all that the Levitical priests teach you; as I have commanded them, so you shall be careful to do.
Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the way as you came out of Egypt.
When you lend your neighbor anything, you shall not go into his house to take his pledge.
You shall stand outside, and the man to whom you lend shall bring the pledge out to you.
And if the man is poor, you shall not sleep with his pledge.
You shall surely return the pledge to him when the sun goes down, that he may sleep in his garment and bless you; and it shall be righteousness for you before the LORD your God.
You shall not oppress a hired servant who is poor and needy, whether he is one of your brothers or a foreigner in your land within your gates.
You must pay his wages on the same day, before the sun goes down, because he is poor and depends on them for his life; otherwise he may cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
Fathers shall not be put to death for their children, nor shall children be put to death for their fathers; each shall be put to death for his own sin.
You shall not pervert justice for the foreigner or the fatherless, nor take a widow's garment as security.
But you shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you from there; therefore I command you to do this thing.

When you reap your harvest in your field and forget a sheaf in the field, you shall not go back to take it; it shall be for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
When you beat your olive trees, you shall not go over the branches again; it shall be for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you shall not glean it afterward; it shall be for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt; therefore I command you to do this thing.
When a dispute arises between men, they are to go to court, and the judges shall decide the case, acquitting the innocent and condemning the guilty.
If the guilty man deserves a beating, the judge must have him lie down and be flogged in his presence with the number of lashes his crime deserves.
Do not give him more than forty lashes, so that your brother is not degraded in your sight.
Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.

If brothers live together and one of them dies without a son, the widow must not marry outside the family; her husband's brother shall take her as his wife and perform the duty of a brother-in-law for her.
The first son she bears will carry on the name of the dead brother, so that his name will not be blotted out from Israel.

If the man does not want to marry his brother's widow, she shall go to the elders at the city gate and say, "My husband's brother refuses to carry on his brother's name in Israel. He will not fulfill the duty of a brother-in-law to me."
Then the elders of his city shall summon him and speak with him. If he persists and says, "I do not want to marry her,"

then his brother's widow shall go up to him in the presence of the elders, remove his sandal from his foot, spit in his face, and declare, "This is what is done to the man who will not build up his brother's family line."
And in Israel he will be called "The Family of the Unsandaled."
If two men are fighting and the wife of one comes to rescue her husband from his assailant, and she reaches out and seizes the man by his private parts,
You are to cut off her hand. Show her no pity.
You shall not have two differing weights in your bag, one heavy and one light.
You shall not have two differing measures in your house, one large and one small.
You must have accurate and honest weights and measures, so that you may live long in the land the the LORD your God is giving you.
For everyone who does these things and acts unjustly is an abomination to the the LORD your God.
Remember what the Amalekites did to you on the way when you came out of Egypt.
How they attacked you on the way when you were faint and weary, striking down those who lagged behind; they did not fear God.

When the the LORD your God gives you rest from all your enemies around you in the land that He is giving you as an inheritance to possess, you must blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget.
When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and you take possession of it and dwell in it,

you shall take some of the first of all the fruit of the ground that you harvest from your land, which the LORD your God is giving you, place it in a basket, and go to the place the LORD your God will choose for His name to dwell.
You shall go to the priest who is in office in those days and say to him, “I declare today to the LORD your God that I have come into the land the LORD swore to our fathers to give us.”
Then the priest shall take the basket from your hand and set it before the altar of the LORD your God.

You shall respond before the LORD your God, “My father was a wandering Aramean. He went down into Egypt and sojourned there with only a few people, and there he became a nation—great, mighty, and numerous.
But the Egyptians treated us harshly and afflicted us, and they laid heavy labor upon us.
Then we cried out to the LORD, the God of our fathers, and the LORD heard our voice and saw our affliction, our toil, and our oppression.
“The LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, and with signs and wonders.
He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And now, behold, I have brought the firstfruits of the ground that You, the LORD, have given me.” Then you shall set it before the LORD your God and worship before the LORD your God.
And you shall rejoice—you, the Levite, and the sojourner who is among you—in all the good that the LORD your God has given to you and to your house.

When you have finished tithing all the tithe of your produce in the third year, the year of tithing, and have given it to the Levite, the sojourner, the fatherless, and the widow, so that they may eat within your towns and be filled,

you shall say before the LORD your God, “I have removed the sacred portion from my house, and moreover I have given it to the Levite, the sojourner, the fatherless, and the widow, according to all Your commandment that You have commanded me. I have not transgressed any of Your commandments, nor have I forgotten them.

I have not eaten of it while mourning, or removed any of it while unclean, or given any of it for the dead. I have obeyed the voice of the LORD my God. I have done according to all that You have commanded me.
“Look down from Your holy habitation, from heaven, and bless Your people Israel and the ground that You have given us, as You swore to our fathers—a land flowing with milk and honey.”
This day the LORD your God commands you to do these statutes and rules. You shall therefore be careful to do them with all your heart and with all your soul.
You have declared today that the LORD is your God, and that you will walk in His ways and keep His statutes and His commandments and His rules, and will obey His voice.
And the LORD has declared today that you are a people for His treasured possession, as He said to you, and that you are to keep all His commandments,
and that He will set you in praise and in fame and in honor above all the nations that He has made, and that you shall be a people holy to the LORD your God, as He has spoken.
Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people, “Keep every commandment that I am giving you today.”
On the day you cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD your God is giving you, you shall erect large stones and coat them with plaster.

You shall write on them all the words of this law as you cross over, so that you may enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the LORD, the God of your fathers, promised you.
When you cross the Jordan, you shall set up these stones on Mount Ebal, as I command you today, and you shall coat them with plaster.
You shall build an altar there to the LORD your God, an altar of stones that no iron tool has touched.
You shall build the altar of the LORD your God of unhewn stones, and you shall offer burnt offerings on it to the LORD your God.
You shall sacrifice peace offerings there, eat them, and rejoice before the LORD your God.
You shall write clearly on the stones all the words of this law.
Moses and the Levitical priests spoke to all Israel, saying, “Be quiet and listen, O Israel: today you have become the people of the LORD your God.”
You shall therefore obey the voice of the LORD your God and carry out His commandments and statutes, which I am commanding you today.
Moses also charged the people on that day,
“When you cross the Jordan, these shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
And these shall stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.”
Then the Levites shall declare in a loud voice to all the men of Israel:
“Cursed is anyone who makes a carved or molten image, an abomination to the LORD, the work of a craftsman’s hands, and sets it up in secret.
Cursed is anyone who dishonors his father or his mother.
Cursed is anyone who moves his neighbor’s boundary marker.

Cursed is anyone who leads a blind person astray on the road.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.”
“Cursed is anyone who perverts justice for the foreigner, the fatherless, or the widow.
Cursed is anyone who has sexual relations with his father’s wife, because he has violated his father’s bed.
Cursed is anyone who has sexual relations with an animal.

Cursed is anyone who has sexual relations with his sister, whether she is his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.”
“Cursed is anyone who has sexual relations with his mother-in-law.
Cursed is anyone who strikes down his neighbor in secret.
Cursed is anyone who accepts a bribe to kill an innocent person.

Cursed is anyone who does not uphold the words of this law by carrying them out.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.” And all the people shall answer, “Amen.”

If you diligently obey the voice of the LORD your God, being careful to observe all His commands that I am giving you today, then the LORD your God will set you high above all the nations of the earth.
All these blessings will come upon you and overtake you, if you obey the voice of the LORD your God.
You will be blessed in the city and blessed in the country.
Blessed will be the fruit of your womb, the produce of your ground, and the young of your livestock—the calves of your herds and the lambs of your flocks.
Blessed will be your basket and your kneading bowl.
You will be blessed when you come in and blessed when you go out.
The LORD will cause the enemies who rise against you to be defeated before you. They will march out against you by one road but flee before you by seven.
The LORD will command the blessing to be with you in your barns and in everything you put your hand to, and He will bless you in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
The LORD will establish you as His holy people, as He swore to you, if you keep the commands of the LORD your God and walk in His ways.
All the peoples of the earth will see that you are called by the name of the LORD, and they will stand in awe of you.
The LORD will grant you abundant prosperity—in the fruit of your womb, the offspring of your livestock, and the produce of your ground—in the land the LORD swore to your fathers to give you.
The LORD will open for you the heavens, His good treasury, to send rain on your land in its season and to bless all the work of your hands. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow.
The LORD will grant you preeminence, not subordination; you will be only above and never beneath, if you obey the commands of the LORD your God that I am giving you today.
Do not turn aside from any of the words I am commanding you today, either to the right or to the left, by following other gods to serve them.
But if you do not obey the voice of the LORD your God, to keep all His commands and statutes that I am giving you today, then all these curses will come upon you and overtake you.
You will be cursed in the city and cursed in the country.
Cursed will be your basket and your kneading bowl.
Cursed will be the fruit of your womb, the produce of your ground, the calves of your herds, and the lambs of your flocks.
You will be cursed when you come in and cursed when you go out.

The LORD will send against you curses, confusion, and rebuke in every undertaking you pursue, until you are destroyed and quickly perish, because of the evil of your deeds, by which you have forsaken Me.
The LORD will make pestilence cling to you until He has consumed you from the land you are entering to possess.
The LORD will strike you with wasting disease, fever, inflammation, fiery heat, the sword, blight, and mildew; and they will pursue you until you perish.
The sky above your head will be bronze, and the earth beneath you will be iron.
The LORD will make the rain of your land dust and powder; it will come down on you from the sky until you are destroyed.
The LORD will cause you to be defeated before your enemies. You will march out against them by one road but flee before them by seven, and you will become a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
Your carcasses will be food for every bird of the sky and for the beasts of the earth, with no one to frighten them away.
The LORD will strike you with the boils of Egypt, with tumors, scabs, and itch, from which you cannot be healed.
The LORD will strike you with madness, blindness, and confusion of heart.
You will grope at noon as the blind grope in darkness, and you will not prosper in your ways. You will be only oppressed and robbed continually, and there will be no one to save you.
You will betroth a wife, but another man will sleep with her. You will build a house, but not live in it. You will plant a vineyard, but not enjoy its fruit.

Your ox will be slaughtered before your eyes, but you will not eat any of it. Your donkey will be seized from before you and will not be returned to you. Your sheep will be given to your enemies, and there will be no one to rescue you.
Your sons and daughters will be given to another people, while your eyes look on and waste away with longing for them all day long; but you will be powerless to help.
A people you do not know will eat the fruit of your ground and all your labor, and you will be only oppressed and crushed continually.
You will be driven mad by the sights your eyes see.
The LORD will strike you with severe boils on your knees and legs, from the sole of your foot to the top of your head, an affliction from which you cannot recover.
The LORD will bring you and your king, whom you set over you, to a nation neither you nor your fathers have known, and there you will serve other gods—wood and stone.
You will become an object of horror, a proverb, and a byword among all the peoples where the LORD drives you.
You will sow much seed in the field, but gather little, because locusts will consume it.
You will plant vineyards and tend them, but you will not drink the wine or gather the grapes, because worms will eat them.
You will have olive trees throughout your territory, but you will not anoint yourself with oil, because your olives will drop off.
You will father sons and daughters, but they will not remain yours, because they will go into captivity.
Locusts will take possession of all your trees and the produce of your ground.
The foreigner residing among you will rise higher and higher above you, while you sink lower and lower.
He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him; he will be your superior, and you will be his subordinate.
All these curses will come upon you and pursue and overtake you until you are destroyed, because you did not obey the voice of the LORD your God or keep His commands and statutes that He gave you.
They will be a sign and a wonder against you and your descendants forever.
Because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy and gladness of heart in the midst of all abundance,
You will serve your enemies, whom the LORD will send against you, in hunger, thirst, nakedness, and lack of everything. He will put an iron yoke on your neck until He has destroyed you.
The LORD will bring against you a nation from far away, from the end of the earth, swooping down like an eagle—a nation whose language you do not understand,
a grim-faced nation that will show no respect to the elderly and no mercy to the young.
It will devour the offspring of your livestock and the produce of your soil until you are destroyed; it will leave you no grain, new wine, or oil, no calves or lambs, until it has annihilated you.

It will besiege you in all your towns throughout your land until your high and fortified walls, in which you trust, come down; it will besiege you in every town throughout the land the LORD your God has given you.
In the siege and distress that your enemy will inflict upon you, you will eat the fruit of your womb—the flesh of your sons and daughters whom the LORD your God has given you.
The most tender and delicate man among you will begrudge his brother, the wife of his bosom, and the children he has left,
refusing to give any of them the flesh of his children that he is eating, because he has nothing else left in the siege and distress your enemy will inflict upon you in all your cities.
The most tender and delicate woman among you—so delicate that she would not venture to set the sole of her foot on the ground—will begrudge the husband of her bosom, her son, and her daughter,

as well as the afterbirth that comes from between her feet and the children she bears, because she will eat them in secret for lack of everything, in the siege and distress your enemy will inflict upon you in your cities.
If you do not carefully observe all the words of this law that are written in this book, to fear this glorious and awesome name—the LORD your God—
then the LORD will bring upon you and your descendants extraordinary plagues—great and lasting plagues—and severe and lasting illnesses.
He will bring back upon you all the diseases of Egypt that you dreaded, and they will cling to you.
The LORD will also bring upon you every sickness and plague not recorded in this Book of the Law, until you are destroyed.
You were as numerous as the stars of heaven, but you will be left few in number, because you did not obey the voice of the LORD your God.

Just as the LORD rejoiced over you to do you good and multiply you, so the LORD will now rejoice over you to destroy you and annihilate you; and you will be uprooted from the land you are entering to possess.
The LORD will scatter you among all the nations, from one end of the earth to the other, and there you will serve other gods—wood and stone—that neither you nor your fathers have known.
Among those nations you will find no rest, nor will the sole of your foot find a resting place; there the LORD will give you a trembling heart, failing eyes, and a despairing soul.
Your life will hang in doubt before you; you will be in dread night and day, never sure of your life.
In the morning you will say, 'If only it were evening!' and in the evening, 'If only it were morning!'—because of the terror in your heart and the sights your eyes will see.

The LORD will send you back to Egypt in ships, by the route I said you would never see again. There you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as male and female slaves, but no one will buy you.
These are the terms of the covenant that the LORD commanded Moses to ratify with the Israelites in the land of Moab, supplementing the covenant He established with them at Horeb.

Moses summoned all Israel and declared to them, “You have witnessed everything the LORD accomplished before your eyes in the land of Egypt—against Pharaoh, against all his servants, and against all his territory.
Your eyes have beheld the great trials, the signs, and the great wonders.
Yet to this day the LORD has not granted you a heart to comprehend, eyes to perceive, or ears to apprehend. “
I guided you through the wilderness for forty years; your garments did not deteriorate upon you, nor did your sandals wear out beneath your feet.
You consumed no bread and drank no wine or intoxicating drink, so that you might recognize that I am the LORD your God. “
When you arrived at this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan advanced to meet us in battle, and we defeated them.
We seized their land and apportioned it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
Therefore observe the stipulations of this covenant and execute them, so that you may prosper in all your undertakings. “
All of you stand today before the LORD your God—your leaders, your tribes, your elders, and your officers, every Israelite—
your children, your wives, and the resident alien in your camp, from the woodcutter to the water drawer—
so that you may enter the covenant of the LORD your God and the oath He is making with you today,
that He may constitute you today as His people and be your God, exactly as He promised you and swore to your fathers—to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. “
I am not ratifying this covenant and this oath with you alone,
but with those standing here with us today before the LORD our God, and with those absent from us today. “
You are aware how we resided in the land of Egypt and how we traversed the nations through which you passed.
You witnessed their abominations and their idols of wood and stone, silver and gold, that were among them.

Ensure that no man or woman, family or tribe among you today possesses a heart turning away from the LORD our God to serve the gods of those nations, and that no root among you matures into a toxic, bitter weed. “

When anyone hears the words of this oath and congratulates himself in his heart, saying, ‘I shall enjoy peace, though I persist in the stubbornness of my heart,’ he thereby brings calamity upon both the watered and the dry. “

The LORD will not deign to forgive him; rather, His anger and jealousy will smolder against that man, and every curse inscribed in this book will descend upon him, and the LORD will expunge his name from under heaven.
The LORD will set him apart for calamity from all the tribes of Israel, in accordance with all the curses of the covenant recorded in this Book of the Law. “

A later generation—your descendants who arise after you—and the foreigner who arrives from a distant land will declare, when they behold the afflictions of that land and the maladies the LORD has imposed upon it:

all its terrain scorched with sulfur and salt, unsown and unproductive, with no vegetation sprouting in it—resembling the cataclysm of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the LORD overturned in His fierce anger and wrath. “
All the nations will inquire, ‘Why has the LORD perpetrated such a thing against this land? What explains this great conflagration of His anger?’ “
And they will respond, ‘Because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD, the God of their fathers, which He established with them when He liberated them from the land of Egypt.
They proceeded to serve other gods and prostrated themselves before them—gods they had not known and that He had not apportioned to them.’ “
Therefore the LORD’s anger ignited against that land, bringing upon it all the curses recorded in this book.
In fierce anger and great wrath the LORD uprooted them from their soil and hurled them into another land, as is evident to this day. “
The concealed things belong to the the LORD our God, but the revealed things belong to us and to our children in perpetuity, so that we may execute all the words of this law.”
When the blessings and curses that I have set before you come upon you, and you take them to heart among all the nations where the the LORD your God has driven you,
you and your children will return to the the LORD your God and obey His voice in all that I command you today, with all your heart and with all your soul.
Then the the LORD your God will restore you from captivity, have compassion on you, and gather you again from all the peoples among whom He has scattered you.
Even if you have been banished to the farthest horizon, the the LORD your God will gather you from there and take you back.
He will bring you into the land your fathers possessed, so that you may possess it; He will prosper you and multiply you beyond your fathers.
The the LORD your God will also circumcise your heart and the hearts of your descendants, so that you love the the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul, and so that you may live.
The the LORD your God will place all these curses on your enemies and on those who hate and persecute you.
You, for your part, will return and obey the voice of the the LORD, keeping all the commandments I am giving you today.

The the LORD your God will make you abundantly prosperous in all your undertakings—in the fruit of your womb, your livestock, and your land—to your good, for the the LORD will once again delight in prospering you, as He delighted in your fathers.

This will happen when you obey the voice of the the LORD your God and keep His commandments and statutes recorded in this Book of the Law, and when you return to the the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
For this commandment that I am giving you today is not too difficult for you, nor is it beyond your reach.
It is not in heaven, that you should say, “Who will ascend to heaven for us and retrieve it, so that we may hear it and obey it?”
Nor is it beyond the sea, that you should say, “Who will cross the sea for us and retrieve it, so that we may hear it and obey it?”
On the contrary, the word is very near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart, so that you can do it.
See, I have set before you today life and prosperity, as well as death and disaster.

If you love the the LORD your God, walk in His ways, and keep His commandments, statutes, and ordinances, you will live and multiply, and the the LORD your God will bless you in the land you are entering to possess.
But if your heart turns away and you refuse to listen, if you are lured into bowing down to other gods and serving them,
