I declare to you today that you will certainly perish; you will not live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess.
I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that I have set before you life and death, blessing and curse. Therefore choose life, so that you and your offspring may live—

loving the the LORD your God, obeying His voice, and holding fast to Him—for He is your life and the length of your days, and He will let you dwell in the land the the LORD swore to give your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.
He said to them, "I am now a hundred and twenty years old, and I am no longer able to lead you. The LORD has said to me, 'You shall not cross this Jordan.'"
"The LORD your God Himself will cross over ahead of you. He will destroy these nations before you, and you will dispossess them. Joshua also will cross over ahead of you, as the LORD has promised.
The LORD will do to them as He did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land, which He destroyed.
The LORD will deliver them over to you, and you must deal with them according to all the commandments I have given you.
Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or terrified of them, for the LORD your God goes with you; He will never leave you nor forsake you."

Then Moses summoned Joshua and said to him in the sight of all Israel, "Be strong and courageous, for you will go with this people into the land that the LORD swore to their fathers to give them, and you will give it to them as an inheritance.
The LORD Himself goes before you and will be with you. He will never leave you nor forsake you. Do not be afraid or discouraged."
So Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and to all the elders of Israel.
Then Moses commanded them, "At the end of every seven years, in the appointed time of the year of release, during the Feast of Tabernacles,
when all Israel comes to appear before the LORD your God in the place He will choose, you are to read this law aloud in the hearing of all Israel.
Assemble the people—men, women, children, and the foreigners residing within your gates—so that they may listen and learn to fear the LORD your God and to carefully follow all the words of this law.
Then their children, who do not know, will hear and learn to fear the LORD your God as long as you live in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess."

The LORD said to Moses, "Your days are drawing near for you to die. Summon Joshua and present yourselves at the Tent of Meeting, so that I may commission him." So Moses and Joshua went and presented themselves at the Tent of Meeting.
And the LORD appeared at the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the cloud stood over the entrance to the tent.

The LORD said to Moses, "You are about to die and join your ancestors. Then these people will rise up and chase after the foreign gods of the land they are entering. They will forsake Me and break the covenant I made with them.

On that day My anger will burn against them, and I will forsake them and hide My face from them, so that they will be consumed. Many troubles and afflictions will confront them, and on that day they will say, 'Have not these disasters come upon us because our God is not among us?'
And on that day I will surely hide My face because of all the evil they have done by turning to other gods."
"Now therefore, write down for yourselves this song and teach it to the Israelites; have them sing it, so that it may be a witness for Me against them.

For when I have brought them into the land I swore to their fathers—a land flowing with milk and honey—they will eat and be satisfied and grow fat. Then they will turn to other gods and worship them, and they will reject Me and break My covenant.

When many troubles and afflictions have come upon them, this song will stand as a witness against them, because it will not be forgotten from the mouths of their descendants. For I know their inclination, even before I bring them into the land I have sworn to give them."
So that day Moses wrote down this song and taught it to the Israelites.
Then the LORD commissioned Joshua son of Nun and said, "Be strong and courageous, for you will bring the Israelites into the land I swore to give them, and I will be with you."
When Moses had finished writing in a book the words of this law from beginning to end,
he commanded the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD,
"Take this Book of the Law and place it beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, so that it may remain there as a witness against you.
For I know your rebellion and your stubbornness. Even while I am alive among you today, you have been rebellious against the LORD; how much more after my death!
Assemble before me all the elders of your tribes and all your officers, so that I may speak these words in their hearing and call heaven and earth to witness against them.

For I know that after my death you will become utterly corrupt and turn from the path I have commanded you, and disaster will befall you in the latter days when you do evil in the sight of the LORD and provoke Him to anger by the work of your hands."
Then Moses recited the words of this song in the hearing of the whole assembly of Israel, to the very end.
“Listen, O heavens, and I will speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
Let my teaching fall like rain and my words settle like dew, like showers on fresh grass and gentle rain on tender shoots.
For I will proclaim the name of the LORD; give greatness to our God.
The Rock—His work is perfect, for all His ways are justice. God is faithful and without injustice; righteous and upright is He.
They have dealt corruptly with Him; their defect is not that of His children—they are a crooked and perverse generation.
Do you thus repay the LORD, O foolish and unwise people? Is He not your Father, your Creator, who made you and established you?
Remember the days of old; consider the years of many generations. Ask your father, and he will show you; your elders, and they will tell you.
When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when He separated the sons of man, He set the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the sons of Israel.
For the LORD’s portion is His people, Jacob His allotted inheritance.
He found him in a desert land, in the howling waste of the wilderness; He encircled him, He cared for him, He kept him as something infinitely precious.
Like an eagle that stirs up its nest and hovers over its young, that spreads its wings and takes them up and carries them on its pinions,
the LORD alone guided him, and no foreign god was with him.
He made him ride on the high places of the earth, and he ate the produce of the fields; He nourished him with honey from the rock and oil from the flinty crag.
He fed him curds from cattle and milk from sheep, with fat of lambs and rams of Bashan and goats, with the finest wheat, and you drank the blood of the grape, the wine.
But Jeshurun grew fat and turned rebellious; you grew fat, thick, and sleek. Then he forsook God who made him and scorned the Rock of his salvation.
They made Him jealous with strange gods; with abominations they provoked Him.
They sacrificed to demons that are not God, to gods they had not known, new gods that had come recently, whom your fathers had not feared.
You neglected the Rock who begot you, and you forgot the God who gave you birth.
The LORD saw it and spurned them, because of the provocation of His sons and daughters.
And He said, “I will hide My face from them; I will see what their end will be, for they are a perverse generation, children in whom there is no faithfulness.

They have made Me jealous with what is no god; they have provoked Me to anger with their idols. So I will make them jealous with those who are no people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.”
For a fire is kindled in My anger, and it burns to the depths of Sheol; it devours the earth and its produce and sets ablaze the foundations of the mountains.
I will heap disasters upon them; I will spend My arrows on them.
They shall be wasted with hunger and devoured by plague and bitter destruction; I will send the teeth of beasts against them, with the venom of things that crawl in the dust.
Outdoors the sword shall bereave, and indoors terror, for young man and virgin, infant and gray-haired man alike.
I would have said, “I will scatter them to distant places; I will make the memory of them cease from mankind”—
had I not feared the provocation by the enemy, lest their adversaries misunderstand and say, “Our hand is exalted, and the LORD has not done all this.”
For they are a nation void of counsel, and there is no understanding in them.
If they were wise, they would understand this; they would discern their latter end.
How could one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, unless their Rock had sold them and the LORD had given them up?
For their rock is not like our Rock; our enemies are judges.
For their vine is of the vine of Sodom and of the fields of Gomorrah; their grapes are grapes of poison, and their clusters are bitter.
Their wine is the venom of serpents and the cruel poison of asps.
“Is not this laid up in store with Me, sealed up in My treasuries?
Vengeance is Mine, and recompense, for the time when they stumble; for the day of their calamity is at hand, and their doom comes swiftly.”
For the LORD will judge His people and have compassion on His servants, when He sees that their power is gone and there is none remaining, bond or free.
Then He will say, “Where are their gods, the rock in which they took refuge,
who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their drink offering? Let them rise up and help you; let them be your shelter.
See now that I, even I, am He, and there is no god besides Me; I kill and I make alive; I wound and I heal; and there is none who can deliver from My hand.
For I lift up My hand to heaven and swear, As I live forever,
if I sharpen My flashing sword and My hand takes hold on judgment, I will render vengeance to My adversaries and repay those who hate Me.
I will make My arrows drunk with blood, and My sword shall devour flesh, with the blood of the slain and the captives, from the leaders of the enemy.”
Rejoice, O nations, with His people, for He avenges the blood of His servants and renders vengeance to His adversaries, and makes atonement for His land, for His people.
Moses came with Joshua son of Nun and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people.
When Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel,
he said to them, “Take to heart all the words by which I am warning you today, that you may command your sons to be careful to do all the words of this law.
For it is no empty word for you, but it is your life, and by this word you shall live long in the land that you are going over the Jordan to possess.”
That very day the LORD spoke to Moses:
“Go up this mountain of the Abarim, Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab, opposite Jericho, and view the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the people of Israel for a possession.
And die on the mountain which you are going up, and be gathered to your ancestors, as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his ancestors.

Because you broke faith with Me in the midst of the people of Israel at the waters of Meribah Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin, and because you did not treat Me as holy in the midst of the people of Israel.
For you shall see the land before you, but you shall not go there, into the land that I am giving to the people of Israel.”
This is the blessing that Moses, the man of God, pronounced over the Israelites before his death.
He said: “The LORD came from Sinai and dawned upon us from Seir; He shone forth from Mount Paran and came with myriads of holy ones, with flaming fire at His right hand.
Surely You love the peoples; all Your holy ones are in Your hand, and they sit at Your feet, receiving Your words.
Moses gave us the law as a possession for the assembly of Jacob.
So He became King in Jeshurun when the leaders of the people assembled, when the tribes of Israel came together.”
“Let Reuben live and not die, nor his men be few.”
And this he said of Judah: “Hear, O the LORD, the voice of Judah, and bring him to his people. With his hands he contends for them, and You shall be a help against his foes.”
And of Levi he said: “Your Thummim and Urim belong to Your godly one, whom You tested at Massah and contended with at the waters of Meribah,
who said of his father and mother,”“I do not consider them.”“He disregarded his brothers and did not acknowledge his own children. For they obeyed Your word and kept Your covenant.
They will teach Your ordinances to Jacob and Your law to Israel. They will set incense before You and whole burnt offerings on Your altar.
Bless, O the LORD, his substance, and accept the work of his hands. Strike the loins of those who rise against him and of his foes, so they rise no more.”
Of Benjamin he said: “The beloved of the LORD rests secure in Him; He shields him all day long, and he rests between His shoulders.”
And of Joseph he said: “May his land be blessed by the LORD with the precious dew from heaven and the deep waters beneath,
with the bountiful harvest of the sun and the rich yield of the months,
with the best of the ancient mountains and the bounty of the everlasting hills,
with the choice gifts of the earth and its fullness, and the favor of Him who dwelt in the burning bush. May these rest on the head of Joseph, on the brow of the prince among his brothers.

In majesty he is like a firstborn bull; his horns are the horns of a wild ox; with them he will gore the nations, even to the ends of the earth. Such are the myriads of Ephraim, and such are the thousands of Manasseh.”
And of Zebulun he said: “Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tents.
They will summon peoples to the mountain; there they will offer sacrifices of righteousness, for they will feast on the abundance of the seas and the hidden treasures of the sand.”
And of Gad he said: “Blessed is He who enlarges Gad! He dwells as a lion and tears off arm and scalp.
He chose the best land for himself, for there a commander's portion was reserved. He came with the leaders of the people; he carried out the LORD's justice and His ordinances for Israel.”
And of Dan he said: “Dan is a lion's cub, leaping out of Bashan.”
And of Naphtali he said: “Naphtali is abounding with favor, full of the blessing of the LORD; he will take possession of the sea and the south.”
And of Asher he said: “Most blessed of sons is Asher; let him be favored by his brothers, and let him dip his foot in oil.
Your bars shall be iron and bronze, and your strength shall match your days.”
“There is no one like the God of Jeshurun, who rides through the heavens to your help, and in His majesty through the skies.
The eternal God is your dwelling place, and underneath are the everlasting arms. He will drive out the enemy before you, saying,”“Destroy them!”
“So Israel will dwell in safety; Jacob will dwell secure in a land of grain and new wine, where the heavens drop down dew.

Blessed are you, O Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD? He is the shield that protects you, the sword that exalts you. Your enemies will cower before you, and you will trample their high places.”
Moses ascended from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the summit of Pisgah opposite Jericho, and the the LORD showed him the entire land—Gilead as far as Dan,
all of Naphtali, the lands of Ephraim and Manasseh, all of Judah as far as the western sea,
the Negev, the plain of the Jericho Valley, the City of Palms, and as far as Zoar.

The The LORD said to him, "This is the land I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, 'I will give it to your descendants.' I have granted you a view of it with your own eyes, but you shall not cross over into it."
So Moses, the servant of the the LORD, died there in the land of Moab at the the LORD's command.
He was buried in a valley in Moab, opposite Beth-peor, and no one knows his grave to this day.
Moses was one hundred twenty years old when he died; his eyesight had not failed, nor had his strength diminished.
The Israelites mourned Moses in the plains of Moab for thirty days, until the period of mourning had ended.
Joshua son of Nun was filled with the Spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid hands on him; the Israelites obeyed him and carried out everything the the LORD had commanded Moses.
No prophet has since arisen in Israel like Moses, with whom the the LORD spoke directly.
He performed all the signs and wonders the the LORD had sent him to do in Egypt against Pharaoh, his officials, and his whole land;
and he displayed all the mighty power and great terror that Moses manifested before all Israel.
After the death of Moses, the servant of the LORD, the LORD spoke to Joshua son of Nun, Moses' assistant, saying,
"Moses My servant is dead. Now rise—you and all this people—and cross this Jordan into the land that I am giving to them, to the children of Israel.
Every place where you set foot, I have given to you, just as I promised Moses.
Your territory will extend from the wilderness and this Lebanon to the great river, the Euphrates—all the land of the Hittites—and as far as the Great Sea to the west.
No one will be able to stand against you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you; I will not leave you or forsake you."
"Be strong and courageous, because you will give this people possession of the land I swore to their fathers that I would give them.
Only be strong and very courageous, so that you carefully obey all the law that Moses My servant commanded you. Do not deviate from it in any way, so that you may prosper wherever you go.

This Book of the Law must not depart from your mouth; meditate on it day and night, so that you may be careful to do everything written in it. Then you will prosper in your way and enjoy good success.
Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or discouraged, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go."
Then Joshua commanded the officers of the people, saying,

"Pass through the camp and command the people, 'Prepare provisions for yourselves, for within three days you will cross this Jordan to go in and possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.'"
To the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh Joshua said,
"Remember the word that Moses, the servant of the LORD, commanded you, saying, 'The LORD your God is giving you rest and giving you this land.'

Your wives, your little ones, and your livestock shall remain in the land that Moses gave you on the east side of the Jordan. But you shall cross over before your brothers armed, all your valiant warriors, and help them,

until the LORD has given your brothers rest, as He gave you, and they too have taken possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving them. Then you shall return to the land of your possession and take possession of it, which Moses, the servant of the LORD, gave you on the east side of the Jordan."
They answered Joshua, "All that you command us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go.
Just as we obeyed Moses in all things, so we will obey you. Only may the LORD your God be with you, as He was with Moses.
Whoever rebels against your command and does not obey your words in all that you command him shall be put to death. Only be strong and courageous."
Then Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two spies from Shittim and told them, "Go and scout the land, especially Jericho." They went and entered the house of a prostitute named Rahab, where they lodged.
The king of Jericho was told, "Tonight men from Israel have come here to spy out the land."
So the king of Jericho sent word to Rahab: "Bring out the men who came to you and entered your house, for they have come to spy out the whole land."
But the woman had already taken the two men and hidden them. She said, "Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they were from.
They left near dusk, just as the gate was about to close, and I do not know where they went. Pursue them quickly, and you may catch them."
She had, however, brought them up to the roof and hidden them under stalks of flax that she had arranged on the roof.
The pursuers chased them along the road toward the fords of the Jordan, and as soon as the pursuers had gone out, the gate was shut.
Before the spies had lain down for the night, she went up to them on the roof.
She said to the men, "I know that the LORD has given you this land and that a deep dread of you has fallen on us, so that everyone living in the land is overcome with fear of you.

For we have heard how the LORD dried up the water of the Red Sea before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to Sihon and Og, the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan, whom you devoted to destruction.
When we heard these things, our courage failed, and everyone lost heart before you, because the LORD your God is God in heaven above and on the earth below.
Now please swear to me by the LORD that, because I have shown kindness to you, you will also show kindness to my father's household. Give me a reliable sign
that you will spare my father, mother, brothers, sisters, and all who belong to them, and that you will rescue us from death."
The men answered her, "We pledge our lives for your lives! If you do not reveal our mission, we will show you kindness and faithfulness when the LORD gives us the land."
Then she let them down by a rope through the window, for her house was built into the city wall; she lived in the wall.
She said to them, "Go to the hill country so the pursuers do not find you. Hide there for three days until the pursuers return, and then go on your way."
The men said to her, "We will be released from this oath you made us swear
unless, when we enter the land, you have tied this scarlet cord in the window through which you lowered us, and have gathered into your house your father, mother, brothers, and all your family.
Anyone who goes out the door of your house will bear responsibility for his own death, and we will be innocent. But if anyone with you in the house is harmed, his death will be our responsibility.
If you report our mission, however, we will be released from the oath you made us swear."
"Agreed," she replied. "Let it be as you say." So she sent them away, and they departed; and she tied the scarlet cord in the window.
So they went up into the hills and stayed there three days, until the pursuers had searched all along the road and returned without finding them.
Then the two men came down from the hills, crossed over, and returned to Joshua son of Nun. They reported to him everything that had happened to them.
They said to Joshua, "Surely the LORD has given the whole land into our hands; indeed, everyone living in the land is overcome with fear of us."
Early in the morning Joshua and all the Israelites set out from Shittim and went to the Jordan, where they camped before crossing over.
After three days the officers went through the camp.
They commanded the people, "When you see the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God being carried by the Levitical priests, you must break camp and follow it.
But keep a distance of about two thousand cubits between yourselves and the ark; do not approach it, so that you may know the way you are to go, since you have never traveled this road before."
Joshua said to the people, "Consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you."
Then Joshua said to the priests, "Take up the ark of the covenant and go on ahead of the people." So they took up the ark of the covenant and went ahead of the people.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Today I will begin to exalt you in the sight of all Israel, so that they may know that, just as I was with Moses, so I will be with you."
You are to command the priests who carry the ark of the covenant, 'When you reach the edge of the Jordan's waters, you must stand still in the Jordan.'"
Then Joshua said to the Israelites, "Come closer and listen to the words of the LORD your God.
By this you will know that the living God is among you and that He will surely drive out before you the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites.
Behold, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is crossing over ahead of you into the Jordan.
Now choose twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one from each tribe.

When the soles of the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the LORD—the Lord of all the earth—touch the waters of the Jordan, the waters flowing down from above will be cut off and stand up in a heap."
So when the people set out from their tents to cross the Jordan, with the priests carrying the ark of the covenant ahead of them,
the Jordan was overflowing all its banks throughout the harvest season. But as soon as the priests carrying the ark reached the Jordan and their feet touched the water's edge,

the waters flowing down from above stood still and rose up in a heap a great distance away at Adam, the city beside Zarethan, while the waters flowing into the Sea of the Arabah—the Salt Sea—were completely cut off. So the people crossed over opposite Jericho.

The priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD stood firmly on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, and all Israel passed over on dry ground until the entire nation had finished crossing the Jordan.
When the entire nation had completed its passage across the Jordan, the LORD addressed Joshua, saying,
“Select twelve men from the people—one from each tribe—for yourselves, and command them,
‘Take twelve stones from this place, from the midst of the Jordan, from the very spot where the priests’ feet stood firm; carry them with you and deposit them in the camp where you lodge tonight.’”
Accordingly, Joshua summoned the twelve men whom he had designated from among the Israelites, one from each tribe,
and said to them, “Cross before the ark of the LORD your God into the middle of the Jordan, and each of you shall lift one stone onto his shoulder, corresponding to the tribes of the Israelites,
so that this may serve as a sign among you. When your children ask tomorrow, ‘What do these stones mean to you?’

you shall tell them, ‘The waters of the Jordan were severed before the ark of the covenant of the LORD. When it crossed the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were severed. These stones shall remain a memorial for the Israelites forever.’”

The Israelites acted precisely as Joshua had commanded. They lifted twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, one for each tribe of the Israelites, just as the LORD had instructed Joshua, and they carried them to the camp and set them down there.
Joshua also erected twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, at the place where the priests who bore the ark of the covenant had stood; and they remain there to this day.

The priests who bore the ark stood in the middle of the Jordan until the LORD had completed through Joshua everything He had commanded him to speak to the people, in accordance with all that Moses had commanded Joshua. Then the people hastened across.
As soon as all the people had finished crossing, the ark of the LORD and the priests crossed over before them.
The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed over before the Israelites, armed for battle, just as Moses had spoken to them—
about forty thousand equipped for war passed before the LORD toward the plains of Jericho.
On that day the LORD exalted Joshua in the sight of all Israel, and they revered him as they had revered Moses throughout all the days of his life.
Then the LORD said to Joshua,
“Command the priests who carry the ark of the testimony to come up from the Jordan.”
So Joshua commanded the priests, “Come up from the Jordan.”

When the priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD came up from the middle of the Jordan, and the soles of their feet touched dry ground, the waters of the Jordan returned to their course and overflowed all its banks, as they had before.
The people came up from the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and they encamped at Gilgal on the eastern border of Jericho.
Joshua set up at Gilgal the twelve stones that had been taken from the Jordan.
He said to the Israelites, “When your children ask their fathers in the future, ‘What do these stones mean?’
you shall make known to your children, ‘Israel crossed the Jordan on dry ground.’
For the LORD your God dried up the waters of the Jordan before you until you had crossed, just as the LORD your God did to the Red Sea, which He dried up before us until we had crossed.
This was so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the hand of the LORD is mighty, and so that you may fear the LORD your God forever.”

When all the Amorite kings west of the Jordan and all the Canaanite kings along the coast learned that the LORD had dried up the Jordan’s waters before the Israelites until they had crossed, their courage failed and their resolve dissolved before the Israelites.
At that time the LORD said to Joshua, “Make flint knives for yourself and circumcise the Israelites a second time.”
So Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the Israelites at Gibeath-haaraloth.
This is why Joshua performed the circumcision: every male among the people who had left Egypt—all the men of war—had died in the wilderness on the journey after leaving Egypt.
Although everyone who had departed had been circumcised, none of those born in the wilderness during the journey after leaving Egypt had been circumcised.

For the Israelites had wandered in the wilderness forty years, until the entire nation of men of war who had left Egypt had perished, because they had disobeyed the LORD. Indeed, the LORD had sworn to them that He would never let them see the land He had promised their fathers—a land of abundant prosperity.
Consequently, He raised up their sons in their place, and Joshua circumcised them, for they were uncircumcised, having never been circumcised during the journey.
When the whole nation had been circumcised, they remained in camp until they had recovered.
Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Today I have rolled away the disgrace of Egypt from you.” Therefore that place has been called Gilgal to this day.
On the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, while camped at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho, the Israelites observed the Passover.
The very next day after the Passover, they ate unleavened bread and roasted grain from the produce of the land.
The day after they had eaten the produce of the land, the manna ceased, and the Israelites had no more manna; from then on they ate the yield of the land of Canaan.
Now as Joshua neared Jericho, he lifted his eyes and saw a man standing before him with a drawn sword in his hand. Joshua approached him and asked, “Are you for us or for our enemies?”
“Neither,” he replied. “I have come now as commander of the army of the LORD.” Then Joshua fell facedown to the ground and worshiped, and he asked, “What does my Lord say to His servant?”
The commander of the army of the LORD said to Joshua, “Remove your sandals from your feet, for the place where you are standing is holy.” And Joshua did so.
Now Jericho was shut tight because of the Israelites; no one went out, and no one came in.
Then the LORD said to Joshua, “See, I have delivered Jericho into your hands, along with its king and its elite warriors.
March around the city once with all the men of war; do this for six days.
Have seven priests carry seven rams' horns before the ark, and on the seventh day march around the city seven times while the priests blow the horns.
When you hear them sound a long blast on the horns, have all the people raise a great shout; then the city wall will collapse, and every man will charge straight in.”
So Joshua son of Nun summoned the priests and said to them, “Take up the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and have seven priests carry seven trumpets ahead of it.”
And he commanded the people, “Move out! March around the city, with an armed vanguard going ahead of the ark of the LORD.”
When Joshua had spoken to the people, the seven priests carrying the seven trumpets before the LORD advanced and blew their trumpets, while the ark of the covenant of the LORD followed them.
The armed guard marched ahead of the priests who were blowing the trumpets, and the rearguard followed the ark, with the trumpets sounding continually.
But Joshua had commanded the people, “Do not raise a war cry, do not lift your voices, and do not let a word escape your lips until the day I tell you to shout; then shout!”
So he had the ark of the LORD carried around the city, circling it once; then they returned to camp and spent the night there.
Joshua rose early the next morning, and the priests took up the ark of the LORD.

The seven priests carrying the seven trumpets advanced, marching before the ark of the LORD and blowing the trumpets; the armed men went ahead of them, and the rearguard followed the ark of the LORD, while the trumpets kept sounding.
On the second day they marched around the city once and returned to camp. They did this for six days.
On the seventh day they rose at dawn and marched around the city seven times in the same manner; on that day alone they circled it seven times.
The seventh time around, when the priests sounded the trumpet blast, Joshua commanded the people, “Shout! For the LORD has given you the city!
The city and everything in it are to be devoted to the LORD. Only Rahab the prostitute and all who are with her in her house will be spared, because she hid the messengers we sent.

But keep away from the devoted things, so that you will not bring about your own destruction by taking any of them. Otherwise you will make the camp of Israel liable to destruction and bring trouble on it.
All the silver and gold and the articles of bronze and iron are sacred to the LORD and must go into His treasury.”
When the trumpets sounded, the people shouted; at the sound of the trumpet the people raised a great shout, and the wall collapsed. Then everyone charged straight in, and they captured the city.
They devoted the city to the LORD and destroyed with the sword everything in it—men and women, young and old, cattle, sheep, and donkeys.
Joshua said to the two men who had spied out the land, “Go into the prostitute's house and bring out the woman and all who belong to her, as you swore to her.”

So the young men who had been spies went in and brought out Rahab, her father and mother, her brothers and sisters, and all who belonged to her. They brought out her whole family and settled them outside the camp of Israel.
Then they burned the entire city and everything in it, but the silver and gold and the articles of bronze and iron they put into the treasury of the LORD's house.
But Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute, along with her family and all who belonged to her, because she hid the men Joshua had sent to spy on Jericho—and she lives among the Israelites to this day.

At that time Joshua pronounced this curse: “Cursed before the LORD is the one who undertakes to rebuild this city, Jericho. At the cost of his firstborn he will lay its foundations, and at the cost of his youngest he will set up its gates.”
So the LORD was with Joshua, and his renown spread throughout the land.
But the Israelites were unfaithful with the devoted things. Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of them, and the LORD's anger burned against Israel.
Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is near Beth Aven, east of Bethel, and said to them, "Go up and spy out the land." So the men went up and spied out Ai.
When they returned to Joshua, they said, "Not all the people need go up. About two or three thousand men are enough to attack Ai. Do not weary all the people, for the enemy is few."
So about three thousand men went up there, but they fled before the men of Ai.
The men of Ai struck down about thirty-six of them. They pursued them from the city gate as far as Shebarim and struck them on the slopes, so the hearts of the people melted and became like water.
Then Joshua tore his clothes and fell facedown to the ground before the ark of the LORD until evening, as did the elders of Israel. They sprinkled dust on their heads.

Joshua said, "Ah, Lord, the LORD, why did You ever bring this people across the Jordan to deliver us into the hands of the Amorites to destroy us? If only we had been content to stay on the other side of the Jordan!
O Lord, what can I say, now that Israel has turned its back before its enemies?
The Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear of this and surround us and wipe out our name from the earth. What then will You do for Your great name?"
The LORD said to Joshua, "Stand up! Why are you lying on your face?

Israel has sinned; they have violated My covenant, which I commanded them to keep. They have taken some of the devoted things; they have stolen, they have lied, and they have put them among their own possessions.

That is why the Israelites cannot stand against their enemies; they turn their backs and run before their enemies, because they have become liable to destruction. I will no longer be with you unless you remove the devoted things from among you.

Go, consecrate the people. Tell them, 'Consecrate yourselves in preparation for tomorrow; for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: There is a devoted thing among you, Israel. You cannot stand against your enemies until you remove it.

In the morning, present yourselves tribe by tribe. The tribe the LORD chooses shall come forward clan by clan; the clan the LORD chooses shall come forward family by family; and the family the LORD chooses shall come forward man by man.
Whoever is caught with the devoted things shall be destroyed by fire, along with all that belongs to him. He has violated the covenant of the LORD and has done an outrageous thing in Israel.'"
Early the next morning Joshua had Israel come forward by tribes, and Judah was chosen.
Joshua brought forward the clans of Judah, and the Zerahite clan was chosen. Then he brought forward the Zerahite clan family by family, and Zabdi's family was chosen.
He brought Zabdi's household forward man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was chosen.
Then Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and give Him praise. Tell me what you have done; do not hide it from me."
Achan replied, "It is true! I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel. This is what I have done:

When I saw among the plunder a beautiful robe from Babylonia, two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels, I coveted them and took them. They are hidden in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath."
So Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent. There it was, hidden in his tent, with the silver underneath.
They took the things from the tent, brought them to Joshua and all the Israelites, and spread them out before the LORD.

Then Joshua, together with all Israel, took Achan son of Zerah, the silver, the robe, the gold bar, his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys, and sheep, his tent, and all that he had, to the Valley of Achor.
Joshua said, "Why have you brought this trouble on us? The LORD will bring trouble on you today." Then all Israel stoned him and burned them with fire after stoning them with stones.
Over Achan they heaped up a large pile of rocks, which remains to this day. Then the LORD turned from His fierce anger. Therefore that place has been called the Valley of Achor ever since.

Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid or discouraged. Take the whole army with you and go up and attack Ai, for I have delivered into your hand the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land.
Do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king, except that you may carry off their plunder and livestock for yourselves. Set an ambush behind the city.”
So Joshua and the whole army set out to attack Ai. Joshua chose thirty thousand mighty warriors and sent them out by night.
with these orders: “See, you are to lie in ambush behind the city, not too far from it. All of you be ready.
Then I and all the people who are with me will approach the city, and when they come out to meet us as before, we will flee from them.
They will pursue us until we have drawn them away from the city, for they will say, ‘They are running away from us as they did before.’ So we will flee from them.
Then you shall rise up from the ambush and seize the city, for the LORD your God will deliver it into your hand.
When you have taken the city, set it on fire. Do as the LORD has commanded. See, I have given you orders.”
So Joshua sent them out, and they went to the place of ambush and lay in wait between Bethel and Ai, to the west of Ai. But Joshua spent that night among the people.
Early the next morning Joshua mustered his men and went up to Ai with the elders of Israel in front of the army.
Then all the troops who were with him marched up and approached the city. They camped to the north of Ai, with the valley between them and the city.
Now Joshua had taken about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, to the west of the city.
So the forces were stationed with the main camp to the north of the city and the rear guard to the west. And that night Joshua went into the valley.

When the king of Ai saw this, he and all his men hurried out early in the morning to meet Israel in battle at an appointed place overlooking the Arabah. But he did not know there was an ambush waiting behind the city.
Joshua and all Israel let themselves be beaten back before them and fled toward the wilderness.
Then all the men of Ai were summoned to pursue them, and they pursued Joshua and were drawn away from the city.
Not a man remained in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel. They left the city open and pursued Israel.
Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Hold out your javelin toward Ai, for I will hand the city over to you.” So Joshua held out his javelin toward Ai.
As soon as he did so, the men in ambush rose quickly from their position and rushed into the city. They captured it and set it on fire.
When the men of Ai turned and looked back, they saw the smoke rising into the sky. They had nowhere to run; the Israelites who had been fleeing toward the wilderness turned around and attacked them.
When Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had taken the city and that smoke was rising from it, they turned around and struck down the men of Ai.
Meanwhile, the men from the city came out against them, so they were caught in the middle, with Israelites on both sides. And Israel struck them down, leaving no survivors or fugitives.
But they took the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

When Israel had finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the fields and in the wilderness where they had chased them, and when every last one of them had fallen by the sword, all the Israelites returned to Ai and put it to the sword.
All those who fell that day, both men and women, were twelve thousand—the entire population of Ai.
Joshua did not draw back the hand that held his javelin until he had devoted to destruction all who lived in Ai.
Israel took for themselves only the livestock and plunder of that city, as the LORD had commanded Joshua.
So Joshua burned Ai and made it a permanent heap of ruins, a desolate place to this day.

He hung the king of Ai on a tree until evening, and at sunset Joshua commanded that his body be taken down from the tree and thrown at the entrance of the city gate. And they raised over it a large heap of stones, which remains to this day.
At that time Joshua built an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,

as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites. He built it with uncut stones on which no iron tool had been used, and on it they offered burnt offerings to the LORD and sacrificed peace offerings.
And there, in the presence of the Israelites, Joshua inscribed on the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he had written.

All Israel, foreigners and citizens alike, with their elders, officers, and judges, stood on both sides of the ark of the covenant of the LORD, facing the Levitical priests who carried the ark. Half of the people stood in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded for the blessing of the people of Israel.
Afterward, Joshua read aloud all the words of the law—the blessings and the curses—according to all that is written in the Book of the Law.
There was not a word of all that Moses had commanded that Joshua did not read before the whole assembly of Israel, including the women and children and the foreigners who lived among them.

When all the kings beyond the Jordan—in the hill country, in the lowlands, and along the whole coast of the Great Sea toward Lebanon—heard what had happened, namely the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites,
they gathered together with one accord to make war against Joshua and Israel.
But when the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai,
they acted with shrewd cunning. They went and made themselves look like travelers from afar: they took worn-out sacks for their donkeys, wineskins that were old, torn, and patched,
worn and patched sandals on their feet, worn garments, and bread that was dry and moldy for all their provisions.
They came to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal and said to him and to the men of Israel, “We have come from a distant country; therefore make a covenant with us.”
The men of Israel said to the Hivites, “Perhaps you dwell among us. How then could we make a covenant with you?”
They answered Joshua, “We are your servants.” Joshua said to them, “Who are you, and from where have you come?”
They said to him, “Your servants have come from a very distant country because of the name of the LORD your God. For we have heard the report of Him and all that He did in Egypt,
and all that He did to the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan—to Sihon king of Heshbon and to Og king of Bashan, who was at Ashtaroth.
So our elders and all the inhabitants of our country said to us, ‘Take provisions for the journey and go to meet them, and say to them, “We are your servants; now make a covenant with us.”’
This bread of ours was hot when we packed it in our houses on the day we set out to come to you, but now, behold, it is dry and moldy.
These wineskins were new when we filled them, and behold, they have burst. These garments and sandals of ours have worn out from the very long journey.”
The men took some of their provisions, but they did not seek the counsel of the LORD.
Joshua made peace with them and made a covenant with them to let them live, and the leaders of the congregation swore an oath to them.
At the end of three days, after they had made the covenant with them, they heard that they were near and that they dwelt among them.
The children of Israel set out and came to their cities on the third day; their cities were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.
But the children of Israel did not strike them, because the leaders of the congregation had sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel; and the whole congregation grumbled against the leaders.
All the leaders said to the whole congregation, “We have sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel, and now we cannot touch them.
This is what we will do to them: we will let them live, lest wrath come upon us because of the oath that we swore to them.”
The leaders said to them, “Let them live.” So they became woodcutters and water carriers for the whole congregation, as the leaders had spoken to them.
Joshua called them and said to them, “Why have you deceived us, saying, ‘We are very far from you,’ when you dwell among us?
Now therefore you are cursed, and none of you shall ever be freed from being servants—woodcutters and water carriers—for the house of my God.”

They answered Joshua, “Because it was surely told your servants that the LORD your God commanded His servant Moses to give you all the land and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land from before you. Therefore we were very much afraid for our lives because of you, and we did this thing.
And now, behold, we are in your hand. Do to us as seems good and right in your eyes to do.”
So he did to them and delivered them out of the hand of the children of Israel, and they did not kill them.
That day Joshua made them woodcutters and water carriers for the congregation and for the altar of the LORD, in the place which He would choose, to this day.

When Adoni-zedek, king of Jerusalem, heard that Joshua had captured Ai and devoted it to destruction, treating Ai and its king as he had treated Jericho and its king, and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were living among them,
he was greatly alarmed. Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities, larger than Ai, and all its men were mighty warriors.
So Adoni-zedek, king of Jerusalem, sent word to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon, saying,
“Come up to me and help me, so that we may strike Gibeon, because it has made peace with Joshua and with the Israelites.”
So these five Amorite kings—the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon—gathered their forces, marched up with all their armies, encamped against Gibeon, and attacked it.

The men of Gibeon sent word to Joshua at the camp in Gilgal: “Do not abandon your servants. Come up to us quickly and save us and help us, for all the kings of the Amorites who live in the hill country have gathered against us.”
So Joshua marched up from Gilgal with all his troops, including all the mighty warriors.
The LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, for I have given them into your hand. Not one of them will be able to stand against you.”
Joshua therefore came upon them suddenly, having marched all night from Gilgal.

The LORD threw them into confusion before Israel, and Israel struck them with a great slaughter at Gibeon. Israel pursued them along the road up to Beth Horon and struck them as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

While they fled before Israel down the descent from Beth Horon, the LORD hurled large hailstones from heaven upon them as far as Azekah, and they died. More died from the hailstones than the Israelites killed with the sword.
On the day the LORD delivered the Amorites to the Israelites, Joshua spoke to the LORD in the sight of Israel: “Sun, stand still over Gibeon, and moon, over the Valley of Aijalon.”

So the sun stood still and the moon stopped, until the nation avenged itself on its enemies. Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? The sun stood still in the middle of the sky and did not hurry to set for about a whole day.
There has never been a day like it before or since, when the LORD listened to the voice of a man, for the LORD fought for Israel.
Then Joshua returned, with all Israel, to the camp at Gilgal.
Those five kings fled and hid in the cave at Makkedah.
Joshua was told, “The five kings have been found; they are hiding in the cave at Makkedah.”
Joshua said, “Roll large stones against the mouth of the cave and station men there to guard them.”
“But do not stay there yourselves. Pursue your enemies and attack them from the rear. Do not let them reach their cities, for the LORD your God has given them into your hand.”
When Joshua and the Israelites had finished striking them down with a very great slaughter, until they were wiped out, the survivors entered the fortified cities.
Then all the people returned safely to Joshua at the camp at Makkedah, and no one spoke against the Israelites.
Joshua said, “Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out to me.”
They did so and brought out the five kings—the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.

When they brought them out to Joshua, he summoned all the Israelites and said to the commanders of the soldiers who had marched with him, “Come near and put your feet on the necks of these kings.” They came near and put their feet on their necks.
Joshua said to them, “Do not be afraid or discouraged. Be strong and courageous, for the LORD will do this to all your enemies against whom you fight.”
Then Joshua struck them down and killed them, and he hanged them on five trees, where they hung until evening.

At sunset Joshua gave the command, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden. They placed large stones at the mouth of the cave, and they remain there to this day.

That same day Joshua captured Makkedah. He struck it and its king with the sword, devoting every inhabitant to destruction and leaving no survivor. He treated the king of Makkedah as he had treated the king of Jericho.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Makkedah to Libnah and fought against it.
The LORD also gave it and its king into Israel’s hand. Joshua struck it and every person in it with the sword, leaving no survivor, and he treated its king as he had treated the king of Jericho.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Libnah to Lachish, besieged it, and fought against it.
The LORD gave Lachish into Israel’s hand, and Joshua captured it on the second day. He struck it and every person in it with the sword, just as he had done to Libnah.
Then Horam, king of Gezer, came up to help Lachish, but Joshua struck him and his people until no survivor remained.
From Lachish, Joshua and all Israel with him moved on to Eglon. They besieged it and fought against it.
They captured it that day and struck it with the sword, devoting every inhabitant to destruction, just as they had done to Lachish.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him went up from Eglon to Hebron and fought against it.

They captured it and struck it with the sword—its king, all its towns, and every inhabitant—leaving no survivor, just as they had done to Eglon. Joshua devoted the city and every inhabitant to destruction.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him turned back to Debir and fought against it.

He captured it, along with its king and all its towns. They struck them with the sword and devoted every inhabitant to destruction, leaving no survivor. Just as he had done to Hebron, to Libnah, and to their kings, so he did to Debir and to its king.

Thus Joshua struck the entire land—the hill country, the Negev, the lowlands, and the slopes—along with all their kings. He left no survivor, but devoted to destruction everything that breathed, just as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded.
Joshua struck them from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, and all the land of Goshen as far as Gibeon.
Joshua captured all these kings and their land at one time, because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.
Then Joshua returned, with all Israel, to the camp at Gilgal.

When Jabin, king of Hazor, learned of Israel’s triumphs, he dispatched envoys to Jobab, king of Madon, to the kings of Shimron and Achshaph, and to the kings of the north—those in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Chinnereth, in the lowland, and in the heights of Dor toward the sea.
He also summoned the Canaanites from east and west, the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, and Jebusites from the highlands, and the Hivites dwelling beneath Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
They sallied forth with all their armies—a host as innumerable as the sand upon the seashore—accompanied by an overwhelming multitude of horses and chariots.
All these kings converged, advanced, and encamped in unison at the waters of Merom to make war upon Israel.

The LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, for by this time tomorrow I will deliver all of them, slain, before Israel. You shall hamstring their horses and incinerate their chariots with fire.”
Joshua, together with all his men of war, came upon them suddenly at the waters of Merom and struck them.

The LORD delivered them into Israel’s hand; Israel struck them down and pursued them to Great Sidon, to Misrephoth-maim, and eastward to the Valley of Mizpeh, striking them until no survivor remained.
Joshua did precisely as the LORD had commanded him: he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
At that juncture Joshua turned back, captured Hazor, and struck down its king with the sword, for Hazor had formerly been the paramount power among all those kingdoms.
He struck every inhabitant with the edge of the sword, devoting them to utter destruction; no breath survived, and Hazor itself he burned with fire.
Joshua captured all these cities and all their kings, striking them with the edge of the sword and devoting them to destruction, exactly as Moses, the servant of the LORD, had commanded.
Nevertheless, Israel did not burn any of the cities that stood upon their mounds, save Hazor alone, which Joshua burned.
Israel seized as plunder all the spoil and livestock of these cities, yet every human being they struck with the edge of the sword until they were annihilated; they left no one breathing.
As the LORD had commanded Moses His servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and Joshua executed it without omission; he left undone nothing of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
Joshua took all this land—the hill country, the Negev, all the land of Goshen, the lowland, the Arabah, and the hill country of Israel together with its lowland.
From Mount Halak, which ascends toward Seir, to Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon beneath Mount Hermon, he captured all their kings, struck them down, and put them to death.
Joshua waged war against all these kings for many days.
No city sought terms of peace with the Israelites except the Hivites dwelling in Gibeon; Israel took everything by force of arms.

For it was the LORD who hardened their hearts to confront Israel in battle, in order that they might be devoted to destruction and receive no mercy, but rather be destroyed, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

At that time Joshua came and extirpated the Anakim from the hill country—from Hebron, Debir, and Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah and all the hill country of Israel—and he devoted them, along with their cities, to destruction.
No Anakim remained in the land of the Israelites except in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod, where some survived.
Joshua took the whole land, in accordance with everything the LORD had spoken to Moses, and he gave it to Israel as an inheritance, according to their tribal divisions; then the land rested from war.
These are the kings of the land whom the Israelites defeated, seizing their territory east of the Jordan—from the Arnon River as far as Mount Hermon, including all the Arabah eastward.

Sihon, king of the Amorites, who resided in Heshbon, exercised dominion from Aroer on the bank of the Arnon River, through the middle of that valley, as far as the Jabbok River—the frontier of the Ammonites—together with half of Gilead.

He likewise ruled the eastern Arabah as far as the Sea of Chinnereth and as far as the Sea of the Arabah—the Salt Sea—eastward, along the route to Beth-jeshimoth, and southward beneath the slopes of Pisgah.
The domain of Og, king of Bashan—one who belonged to the remnant of the Rephaim—encompassed Ashtaroth and Edrei.
He governed Mount Hermon, Salecah, all Bashan to the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and half of Gilead, the border of Sihon, king of Heshbon.
Moses, servant of the LORD, and the Israelites struck them down, and Moses, servant of the LORD, allotted their land as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the Israelites defeated on the western side of the Jordan—from Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon to Mount Halak, which ascends toward Seir—distributed according to their tribal allotments.

Joshua conferred that territory as an inheritance upon the tribes of Israel: the hill country, the lowland, the Arabah, the slopes, the wilderness, and the Negev, along with the lands of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
the king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;
the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;
the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;
the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one.
the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lasharon, one;
the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
the king of Shimron-meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;
the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;
the king of Dor in Naphath-dor, one; the king of Goiim in Gilgal, one;
the king of Tirzah, one—thirty-one kings altogether.
Now Joshua was very old, and the LORD said to him, “You are very old, and much land remains to be possessed.
This is the land that remains: all the regions of the Philistines and all the Geshurites,

from the Shihor, which lies east of Egypt, northward to the border of Ekron—it is reckoned as Canaanite territory—the five Philistine rulers of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron, together with the Avvites;
in the south, all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah, which belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek, to the border of the Amorites;
and the land of the Gebalites and all Lebanon eastward, from Baal-gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo-hamath;
all the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim—all the Sidonians—I will drive out before the Israelites. Only allot it to Israel as an inheritance, as I have commanded you.
Now therefore divide this land as an inheritance for the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.”
The Reubenites and Gadites, together with the half-tribe of Manasseh, had already received their inheritance, which Moses, the servant of the LORD, gave them east of the Jordan.
It ran from Aroer on the bank of the Arnon Valley, including the city in the middle of the valley, and all the plateau of Medeba as far as Dibon;
and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the border of the Ammonites;
and Gilead, and the territory of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah;
all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei—he was one of the last of the Rephaim—and Moses struck them down and dispossessed them.
Yet the Israelites did not dispossess the Geshurites or the Maacathites, and Geshur and Maacah still live among Israel to this day.
Only the tribe of Levi received no inheritance; the fire offerings of the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, as He had spoken to them.
Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of Reuben according to its clans.
Their territory ran from Aroer on the bank of the Arnon Valley, including the city in the middle of the valley, and all the plateau near Medeba;
with Heshbon and all its cities on the plateau—Dibon, Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon,
Kiriathaim, Sibmah, and Zereth-shahar on the hill of the valley,
Beth-peor, the slopes of Pisgah, and Beth-jeshimoth—

all the cities of the plateau and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses defeated together with the Midianite leaders Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the princes of Sihon who lived in the land.
The Israelites also put Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, to the sword among those they struck down.
The border of the Reubenites was the Jordan. This was the inheritance of the Reubenites, according to their clans, with its cities and villages.
Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of Gad, to the Gadites, according to their clans.
Their territory was Jazer and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites as far as Aroer, which is east of Rabbah;
from Heshbon to Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir;
and in the valley, Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon—the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon—with the Jordan as its border, eastward to the end of the Sea of Chinnereth.
This was the inheritance of the Gadites, according to their clans, with its cities and villages.
Moses gave an inheritance to the half-tribe of Manasseh; it was for the half-tribe of Manasseh according to its clans.
Their territory ran from Mahanaim through all Bashan—all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan—and all the settlements of Jair in Bashan, sixty cities;

and half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan. These were given to the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh, to half of the descendants of Machir, according to their families.
These are the inheritances that Moses gave in the plains of Moab, east of the Jordan, across from Jericho.
But to the tribe of Levi Moses gave no inheritance; the LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as He had spoken to them.
These are the allotments the Israelites received in the land of Canaan, distributed by Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of Israel's ancestral tribes.
Their inheritance was assigned by lot to the nine and a half tribes, as the LORD had commanded through Moses,
because Moses had granted the inheritance of the two and a half tribes east of the Jordan, but he gave no inheritance among them to the Levites.

For the descendants of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim; and the Levites received no territorial share, except cities in which to dwell, together with pasturelands for their livestock and possessions.
Thus the Israelites carried out what the LORD had commanded Moses, and they divided the land.

Then the sons of Judah approached Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, “You know what the LORD said to Moses, the man of God, at Kadesh-barnea concerning you and me.
I was forty years old when Moses, the servant of the LORD, sent me from Kadesh-barnea to reconnoiter the land, and I returned with a report faithful to what was in my heart.
Nevertheless, my brothers who ascended with me discouraged the people, but I followed the LORD my God wholeheartedly.
On that day Moses swore, saying, ‘Surely the land your foot has trodden shall be an inheritance to you and your descendants forever, because you have followed the LORD my God wholeheartedly.’
Now the LORD has preserved my life, just as He said, these forty-five years since the LORD spoke this word to Moses while Israel wandered in the wilderness; and now I am eighty-five years old today.
I am still as strong today as I was when Moses sent me; my strength now is what it was then, for battle and for daily life.

Now give me this hill country about which the LORD spoke that day, for you heard that day how the Anakim were there, with great fortified cities; perhaps the LORD will be with me, and I will drive them out, just as the LORD said.’”
Then Joshua blessed him and gave Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh as an inheritance.
Therefore Hebron became the inheritance of Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite to this day, because he wholly followed the LORD, the God of Israel.
Now Hebron was formerly called Kiriath-arba; Arba was the greatest man among the Anakim. And the land had rest from war.
The allotment for the clans of the tribe of Judah extended southward to the border of Edom, to the wilderness of Zin at the farthest south.
Their southern boundary began at the end of the Salt Sea, at the bay that faces southward.
It went out southward of the ascent of Akrabbim, crossed Zin, ascended south of Kadesh-barnea, passed Hezron, rose to Addar, and turned toward Karka.
Then it passed Azmon, went out by the Brook of Egypt, and ended at the sea. This shall be your southern boundary.
The eastern boundary was the Salt Sea as far as the mouth of the Jordan, and the northern boundary ran from the bay of the sea at the mouth of the Jordan.
It went up to Beth-hoglah and passed north of Beth-arabah. Then it ascended to the stone of Bohan son of Reuben.

From there it went up to Debir from the Valley of Achor, turning northward toward Gilgal, opposite the ascent of Adummim on the south side of the valley. It crossed to the waters of En-shemesh and ended at En-rogel.

Then it went up by the Valley of the Son of Hinnom at the southern shoulder of the Jebusite city, that is, Jerusalem, and ascended to the top of the mountain that lies west of the Valley of Hinnom, at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim.
From the top of the mountain the boundary extended to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah and reached the cities of Mount Ephron. Then it bent around to Baalah, that is, Kiriath-jearim.
From there it went westward to Mount Seir, passed along the northern shoulder of Mount Jearim, that is, Chesalon, descended to Beth-shemesh, and passed Timnah.
It went out northward to the shoulder of Ekron, bent around to Shikkeron, passed Mount Baalah, went out to Jabneel, and ended at the sea.
The western boundary was the Great Sea with its coastline. This is the boundary surrounding the clans of the people of Judah.
According to the command of the LORD to Joshua, Caleb son of Jephunneh received a portion among the people of Judah: Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron. Arba was the father of Anak.
Caleb drove out from there the three sons of Anak—Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, the descendants of Anak.
He then went up against the inhabitants of Debir, whose former name was Kiriath-sepher.
Caleb said, "Whoever attacks Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give him my daughter Achsah as wife."
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, captured it, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as wife.
When she arrived, she urged him to ask her father for a field. She dismounted from her donkey, and Caleb said to her, "What do you want?"
She said, "Give me a blessing. Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me also springs of water." And he gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the people of Judah according to their clans.

The cities belonging to the tribe of the people of Judah in the extreme south, toward the border of Edom, were Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur, Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah, Kedesh, Hazor, Ithnan, Ziph, Telem, Bealoth, Hazor-hadattah, Kerioth-hezron (that is, Hazor), Amam, Shema, Moladah, Hazar-gaddah, Heshmon, Beth-pelet, Hazar-shual, Beersheba, Bizjothjah, Baalah, Iim, Azem, Eltolad, Chesil, Hormah, Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah, Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon—twenty-nine cities with their villages.
In the lowland: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, Zanoah, En-gannim, Tappuah, Enam, Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah, Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gedera, and Gederothaim—fourteen cities with their villages.
Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal-gad, Dilean, Mizpeh, Joktheel, Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, Cabbon, Lahmas, Kithlish, Gederoth, Beth-dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah—sixteen cities with their villages.
Libnah, Ether, Ashan, Iphthah, Ashnah, Nezib, Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah—nine cities with their villages.
Ekron, with its towns and villages;
from Ekron to the sea, all that lies beside Ashdod, with its villages;
Ashdod, with its towns and villages; Gaza, with its towns and villages; to the Brook of Egypt and the Great Sea with its boundary.
In the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, Socoh, Dannah, Kiriath-sannah (that is, Debir), Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim, Goshen, Holon, and Giloh—eleven cities with their villages.
Arab, Dumah, Eshan, Janim, Beth-tappuah, Aphekah, Humtah, Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), and Zior—nine cities with their villages.
Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah, Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah, Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah—ten cities with their villages.
Maarath, Beth-anoth, and Eltekon—six cities with their villages.
Kiriath-baal (that is, Kiriath-jearim) and Rabbah—two cities with their villages.
In the wilderness: Beth-arabah, Middin, Secacah, Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En-gedi—six cities with their villages.
But the people of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so the Jebusites live among the people of Judah in Jerusalem to this day.

The lot apportioned to the descendants of Joseph extended from the Jordan at Jericho to the waters of Jericho on the east, traversing the wilderness that ascends from Jericho into the hill country of Bethel.
It proceeded from Bethel to Luz, crossed over to the border of the Archites at Ataroth,
and descended westward to the border of the Japhletites, as far as the border of Lower Beth-horon and onward to Gezer, terminating at the sea.
Thus Ephraim and Manasseh, the sons of Joseph, received their inheritance.
The territory of the Ephraimites, according to their clans, extended eastward from Ataroth-addar to Upper Beth-horon.
From there the border issued westward: from Michmethath on the north it turned eastward toward Taanath-shiloh, passed by it, and reached Janoah on the east.
From Janoah it descended to Ataroth and Naarah, touched Jericho, and emerged at the Jordan.
From Tappuah the border ran westward to the Brook of Kanah and ended at the sea. This constituted the inheritance of the tribe of Ephraim by its clans,
together with all the cities and villages allotted to the Ephraimites within the inheritance of the Manassites.
Yet they did not dispossess the Canaanites dwelling in Gezer, so the Canaanites remain among the Ephraimites to this day, though they are subjected to forced labor.

This was the allotment for the tribe of Manasseh, since he was Joseph's firstborn, and it also belonged to Machir, Manasseh's firstborn and the father of Gilead, because he was a man of war; therefore he received Gilead and Bashan.

The rest of Manasseh's descendants received their allotments by families: the sons of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, listed by family.
Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons—only daughters—and their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

They came before Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders, and said, "The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers." So they gave them an inheritance among their father's brothers, in keeping with the LORD's command.
Thus ten portions fell to Manasseh, in addition to the land of Gilead and Bashan beyond the Jordan.
Manasseh's daughters inherited among his sons, while the land of Gilead went to the rest of Manasseh's sons.
Manasseh's border ran from Asher to Michmethath, east of Shechem, and then turned south toward the inhabitants of En-tappuah.
The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah itself, on Manasseh's border, belonged to the sons of Ephraim.

The border descended southward to the Brook of Kanah; these cities belonged to Ephraim, though they lay among Manasseh's cities. Manasseh's border ran along the north side of the brook and ended at the sea.
South of it was Ephraim's territory, and north of it was Manasseh's, with the sea as its boundary; they reached Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.

In Issachar and Asher, Manasseh held Beth-shean and its villages, Ibleam and its villages, Dor and its villages, En-dor and its villages, Taanach and its villages, and Megiddo and its villages—the three regions.
Yet the sons of Manasseh could not drive out the inhabitants of these cities, because the Canaanites were determined to remain in that land.
When the Israelites grew strong, they subjected the Canaanites to forced labor, but they never completely drove them out.
The sons of Joseph spoke to Joshua and said, "Why have you given me only one lot and one portion as an inheritance, when I am such a numerous people and the LORD has blessed me this far?"

Joshua replied, "If you are a numerous people, go up into the forest and clear a place for yourselves there in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, because the hill country of Ephraim is too narrow for you."

The sons of Joseph said, "The hill country is not enough for us, and all the Canaanites who live in the valley have iron chariots—those in Beth-shean and its villages and those in the Valley of Jezreel."
Joshua spoke to the house of Joseph—to Ephraim and Manasseh—and said, "You are a numerous people with great strength; you will not have only one lot.
The hill country will be yours; though it is forest, you will clear it, and its borders will be yours. You will drive out the Canaanites, even though they have iron chariots and are strong."
Then the whole congregation of the Israelites assembled at Shiloh and established the Tent of Meeting there, and the land had been subdued before them.
Seven tribes among the Israelites still remained without an allotted inheritance.
Joshua said to the Israelites, "How long will you be slack in going to possess the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given to you?
Appoint for yourselves three men from each tribe, and I will send them; they shall arise and traverse the land, writing it down according to their inheritance, and then they shall return to me.
They shall divide it into seven portions: Judah shall remain in its territory in the south, and the house of Joseph shall remain in their territory in the north.
And you shall record the seven portions of the land and bring them to me here, and I will cast lots for you here before the LORD our God.

For the Levites have no portion among you, since the priesthood of the LORD is their inheritance; and Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already received the inheritance that Moses, the servant of the LORD, gave them beyond the Jordan to the east."

The men rose and went, and Joshua commanded those going to write the land, saying, "Go and walk through the land and write it down, and return to me; I will cast lots for you here before the LORD in Shiloh."
So the men went and passed through the land and recorded it by cities into seven portions in a book, and they came to Joshua at the camp in Shiloh.
Then Joshua cast lots for them in Shiloh before the LORD, and there Joshua divided the land among the Israelites according to their divisions.
The lot of the tribe of Benjamin came up according to their families, and the border of their lot fell between the descendants of Judah and the descendants of Joseph.
Their northern border began at the Jordan and went up to the slope north of Jericho; then it went westward into the hill country, and its end was at the wilderness of Beth-aven.
From there the border passed southward to Luz—that is, Bethel—then descended to Ataroth-addar on the hill south of Lower Beth-horon.
On the west it curved southward from the hill facing Beth-horon on the south, and its end was at Kiriath-baal (that is, Kiriath-jearim), a city of the sons of Judah. This was the western side.
The southern side began at the edge of Kiriath-jearim and extended westward to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.
