Then the border descended to the foot of the hill facing the Valley of Hinnom on the north, at the Valley of Rephaim, and continued down the Valley of Hinnom along the southern slope of the Jebusite city—that is, Jerusalem—and went down to En-rogel.
From there it turned northward, went to En-shemesh, and continued to Geliloth, which faces the Ascent of Adummim; then it descended to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
It continued north of the Arabah and descended into the Arabah.
Then the border passed north of Beth-hoglah and ended at the northern bay of the Salt Sea, at the southern end of the Jordan. This was the southern border.
The Jordan bounded it on the east. This was the inheritance of the sons of Benjamin, with its boundaries all around.
Now the cities of the tribe of Benjamin according to their families were Jericho, Beth-hoglah, Emek-keziz,
Chephar-ammoni, Ophni, and Geba—twelve cities with their villages;
Zelah, Eleph, the Jebusite city (that is, Jerusalem), Gibeah, and Kiriath—fourteen cities with their villages. This was the inheritance of the sons of Benjamin according to their families.
The second lot fell to the clans of the tribe of Simeon, and their inheritance lay within the territory of Judah.
Their inheritance included Beersheba (or Sheba), Moladah,
Beth-lebaoth, and Sharuhen—thirteen cities with their villages.
They also received Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan—four cities with their villages—
along with all the villages surrounding these cities as far as Baalath-beer and Ramah of the Negev. This was the inheritance of the tribe of Simeon according to its clans.
The inheritance of Simeon was taken from Judah's portion, because Judah's allotment was too large for them; therefore Simeon received an inheritance within Judah's inheritance.
The third lot fell to the clans of Zebulun, and the boundary of their inheritance reached as far as Sarid.
Their boundary ascended westward to Maralah and touched Dabbasheth, then reached the brook east of Jokneam.
From Sarid it turned eastward toward the sunrise to the border of Chisloth-tabor, proceeded to Daberath, and ascended to Japhia.
From there it passed eastward to Gath-hepher and Eth-kazin, went out to Rimmon, and turned toward Neah.
The northern boundary turned at Hannathon and ended at the Valley of Iphtah-el.
The inheritance included Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem—twelve cities with their villages.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of Zebulun according to its clans—these cities and their villages.
The fourth lot fell to the clans of Issachar.
Their territory included Jezreel, Chesulloth, and Shunem,
The boundary touched Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth-shemesh, and ended at the Jordan—sixteen cities with their villages.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of Issachar according to its clans—these cities and their villages.
The fifth lot fell to the clans of Asher.
Their territory included Helkath, Hali, Beten, and Achshaph,
Allammelech, Amad, and Mishal; westward it touched Carmel and Shihor-libnath.
It turned eastward to Beth-dagon, touched Zebulun and the Valley of Iphtah-el on the north, then Beth-emek and Neiel, and went out to Cabul on the left.
It included Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Great Sidon.
The boundary turned to Ramah and the fortified city of Tyre, then turned to Hosah and ended at the sea in the region of Achzib.
The inheritance also included Ummah, Aphek, and Rehob—twenty-two cities with their villages.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of Asher according to its clans—these cities and their villages.
The sixth lot fell to the clans of Naphtali.
Their boundary ran from Heleph, from the oak at Zaanannim, through Adami-nekeb and Jabneel, as far as Lakkum, and ended at the Jordan.
The boundary turned westward to Aznoth-tabor, went out to Hukkok, touched Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan on the east.
The fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, and Chinnereth.
It also included Adamah, Ramah, and Hazor,
Iron, Migdal-el, Horem, Beth-anath, and Beth-shemesh—nineteen cities with their villages.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of Naphtali according to its clans—these cities and their villages.
The seventh lot fell to the clans of Dan.
Their territory included Zorah, Eshtaol, and Ir-shemesh,
Me-jarkon, Rakkon, and the territory opposite Joppa.

The territory allotted to Dan was too small for them, so the Danites went up and fought against Leshem, captured it, struck it with the sword, took possession of it, settled in it, and renamed Leshem Dan after their ancestor Dan.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of Dan according to its clans—these cities and their villages.
When Israel finished allotting the land by its boundaries, they gave Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them.
At the LORD's command they gave him the city he requested—Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim—and he rebuilt the city and settled in it.

These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of Israel distributed by lot at Shiloh before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting. So they finished dividing the land.
"Speak to the Israelites and say, ‘Designate for yourselves the cities of refuge that I promised you through Moses,
so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally and without knowing what he has done may flee there, and they will be your refuge from the avenger of blood.’"

He shall flee to one of these cities, station himself at the city gate, and present his case to the elders of that city; whereupon they shall admit him into the city and allot him a residence among them.
If the avenger of blood pursues him, they shall not surrender the manslayer into his power, because he struck his neighbor unintentionally and had harbored no prior hatred toward him.

He shall dwell in that city until he has stood trial before the congregation and until the death of the high priest then in office; only thereafter may the manslayer return to his own home, to the city from which he fled.
They consecrated Kedesh in Galilee, in the hill country of Naphtali; Shechem, in the hill country of Ephraim; and Kiriath-arba—that is, Hebron—in the hill country of Judah.

East of the Jordan, beyond Jericho, they assigned Bezer in the wilderness on the tableland, from the tribe of Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Manasseh.

These cities were appointed for all the Israelites and for the resident alien living among them, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there and not perish by the hand of the avenger of blood before he has stood trial before the congregation.
Then the heads of the Levite families approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the Israelite tribal families,
while Israel was at Shiloh in Canaan, and said to them, “The The LORD commanded through Moses that you give us towns in which to live, together with pasturelands for our livestock.”
So, at the the LORD’s command, the Israelites gave the Levites these towns and their pasturelands from their own inheritance:
The first lot fell to the Kohathite clans. The priestly descendants of Aaron received thirteen towns from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.
The remaining Kohathites received ten towns from the clans of Ephraim, Dan, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
The descendants of Gershon received thirteen towns from the clans of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
The descendants of Merari, by their clans, received twelve towns from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
Thus the Israelites gave the Levites these towns and their pasturelands, just as the the LORD had commanded through Moses, by casting lots.
From the tribes of Judah and Simeon they gave these towns, which are named:
to the descendants of Aaron, who belonged to the Kohathite clans of the Levites, because the first lot fell to them:
Kiriath Arba—that is, Hebron—with its surrounding pastureland in the hill country of Judah. Arba was the father of Anak.
But the fields and villages around the city had been given to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his possession.
To the priestly descendants of Aaron they gave Hebron, a city of refuge for the manslayer, together with its pastureland; Libnah and its pastureland;
Jattir and its pastureland; Eshtemoa and its pastureland;
Holon and its pastureland; Debir and its pastureland;
Ain and its pastureland; Juttah and its pastureland; and Beth Shemesh and its pastureland—nine towns from these two tribes.
From the tribe of Benjamin they gave Gibeon and its pastureland, Geba and its pastureland,
Anathoth and its pastureland, and Almon and its pastureland—four towns.
In all, the priests, the descendants of Aaron, received thirteen towns, together with their pasturelands.
The rest of the Kohathite clans among the Levites received towns from the tribe of Ephraim by lot:
Shechem, a city of refuge in the hill country of Ephraim, with its pastureland; Gezer and its pastureland;
Kibzaim and its pastureland; and Beth Horon and its pastureland—four towns.
From the tribe of Dan they received Eltekeh and its pastureland, Gibbethon and its pastureland,
Aijalon and its pastureland, and Gath Rimmon and its pastureland—four towns.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh they received Taanach and its pastureland and Gath Rimmon and its pastureland—two towns.
These ten towns, with their pasturelands, were given to the remaining Kohathite clans.
The Gershonite clans among the Levites received from the half-tribe of Manasseh Golan in Bashan, a city of refuge, with its pastureland, and Beeshterah with its pastureland—two towns.
From the tribe of Issachar they received Kishion and its pastureland, Daberath and its pastureland,
Jarmuth and its pastureland, and En Gannim and its pastureland—four towns.
From the tribe of Asher they received Mishal and its pastureland, Abdon and its pastureland,
Helkath and its pastureland, and Rehob and its pastureland—four towns.
From the tribe of Naphtali they received Kedesh in Galilee, a city of refuge, with its pastureland; Hammoth Dor and its pastureland; and Kartan and its pastureland—three towns.
In all, the Gershonite clans received thirteen towns, together with their pasturelands.
The Merarite clans, the rest of the Levites, received from the tribe of Zebulun Jokneam and its pastureland, Kartah and its pastureland,
Dimnah and its pastureland, and Nahalal and its pastureland—four towns.
From the tribe of Reuben they received Bezer and its pastureland, Jahzah and its pastureland,
Kedemoth and its pastureland, and Mephaath and its pastureland—four towns.
From the tribe of Gad they received Ramoth in Gilead, a city of refuge, with its pastureland; Mahanaim and its pastureland;
Heshbon and its pastureland; and Jazer and its pastureland—four towns.
In all, twelve towns were allotted to the Merarite clans, the rest of the Levites, together with their pasturelands.
The Levites’ cities within the Israelites’ inheritance totaled forty-eight cities, together with their pasturelands.
Each of these cities had pasturelands all around it; so it was with all these cities.
Thus the the LORD gave Israel all the land He had sworn to give to their fathers, and they took possession of it and settled in it.

The the LORD gave them rest on every side, according to all that He had sworn to their fathers, and none of their enemies could stand against them; the the LORD delivered all their enemies into their hand.
Not one of all the good promises the the LORD had made to the house of Israel failed; everything came to pass.
Then Joshua summoned the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
He said to them, “You have kept all that Moses, the servant of the the LORD, commanded you, and you have obeyed my voice in everything I commanded you.
For many days you have not abandoned your brothers until this day, and you have kept the charge of the commandment of the the LORD your God.

And now the the LORD your God has given rest to your brothers, as He promised them. Therefore turn and go to your tents, to the land of your possession, which Moses, the servant of the the LORD, gave you beyond the Jordan.

Only be very careful to observe the commandment and the law that Moses, the servant of the the LORD, commanded you: to love the the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, to keep His commandments, to cling to Him, and to serve Him with all your heart and all your soul.”
Then Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their tents.

Now to the half-tribe of Manasseh Moses had given an inheritance in Bashan, but to the other half Joshua gave land west of the Jordan, along with their brothers. When Joshua sent them home, he blessed them.

He said to them, “Return to your homes with your great wealth—with very large herds, with silver, gold, bronze, and iron, and with a great quantity of clothing. Divide with your brothers the spoil of your enemies.”

So the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh returned and left the Israelites at Shiloh in Canaan to go to Gilead, the land of their possession, which they had acquired according to the word of the the LORD through Moses.
When they reached the districts of the Jordan in Canaan, the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar there by the Jordan, an altar impressive in size.
The Israelites heard that the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had built an altar on the frontier of Canaan, in the districts of the Jordan, on the Israelite side.
When the whole congregation of Israelites heard this, they assembled at Shiloh to march against them.
The Israelites sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to Gilead, to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
With him went ten leaders, one from each ancestral house of the tribes of Israel; each was the head of his ancestral house among the thousands of Israel.
They came to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead and spoke to them:

“Thus says the whole congregation of the the LORD: What is this treachery you have committed today against the God of Israel by turning away from following the the LORD, by building an altar for yourselves, so that you might rebel today against the the LORD?
Is the iniquity of Peor not enough for us, from which we have not cleansed ourselves to this day, although a plague came upon the congregation of the the LORD?
Yet today you turn away from following the the LORD. If you rebel today against the the LORD, tomorrow He will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel.

If the land of your possession is unclean, then cross over to the land of the possession of the the LORD, where the the LORD’s tabernacle dwells, and take possession among us. But do not rebel against the the LORD, and do not rebel against us by building an altar for yourselves apart from the altar of the the LORD our God.
Did not Achan son of Zerah commit a trespass in the devoted thing, and wrath fell on the whole congregation of Israel? He did not perish alone for his iniquity.”
Then the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered the heads of the clans of Israel:
“The the LORD God of gods—the the LORD God of gods—He knows, and Israel will know: if it was in rebellion or in trespass against the the LORD, do not save us today.
If we have built this altar to turn away from following the the LORD, or to offer burnt offerings, grain offerings, or peace offerings on it, may the the LORD Himself require it.
No, we did this out of concern, from fear that in time to come your children might say to our children, ‘What have you to do with the the LORD, the God of Israel?’

For the the LORD has made the Jordan a border between us and you, Reubenites and Gadites. You have no portion in the the LORD, so your children might make our children cease from fearing the the LORD.
Therefore we said, ‘Let us now build an altar, not for burnt offering or sacrifice.’

But it shall be a witness between us and you and our generations after us, that we may perform the service of the the LORD before Him with our burnt offerings, our sacrifices, and our peace offerings, so that your children will not say to our children in time to come, ‘You have no portion in the the LORD.’

Therefore we said that, when in time to come they say this to us or to our generations, we will answer, ‘Look at the pattern of the altar of the the LORD that our fathers made—not for burnt offering or sacrifice, but as a witness between us and you.’

Far be it from us to rebel against the the LORD and turn away today from following the the LORD by building an altar for burnt offering, grain offering, or sacrifice, besides the altar of the the LORD our God that stands before His tabernacle.”
Phinehas the priest, the leaders of the congregation, and the heads of Israel with him heard the words that the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the Manassites had spoken, and it pleased them.

Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the Manassites, “Today we know that the the LORD is among us, because you have not committed this trespass against the the LORD. Now you have delivered the Israelites from the hand of the the LORD.”
Then Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders returned from the Reubenites and Gadites in Gilead to Canaan, to the Israelites, and brought back a report.
The matter pleased the Israelites, and they blessed God and spoke no more of going up against them in war to destroy the land where the Reubenites and Gadites lived.
The Reubenites and Gadites called the altar Witness, for they said, “It is a witness between us that the the LORD is God.”
Following a lengthy interval after the LORD had granted Israel respite from all surrounding enemies, Joshua had become elderly and advanced in years.
Joshua convened all Israel—its elders, chieftains, judges, and officers—and addressed them, “I have become elderly and advanced in years. “
You have witnessed everything the LORD your God accomplished among these nations on your behalf, for the LORD your God Himself waged war for you.
Observe that I have assigned to your tribes, as their inheritance, the nations that remain, together with every nation I annihilated from the Jordan to the Great Sea in the west.
The LORD your God will expel them before you and dispossess them, enabling you to occupy their land, precisely as the LORD your God promised you.“
Therefore, be exceedingly resolute in observing and executing everything inscribed in the Book of the Law of Moses, without deviating from it to the right or to the left.
Do not assimilate with these remaining nations; do not invoke their gods, swear by them, serve them, or bow down to them.
Rather, remain devoted to the LORD your God, as you have done to this day.“
For the LORD has driven out before you great and formidable nations, and to this day no one has been able to withstand you.
A single one of you can put a thousand to flight, because the LORD your God fights for you, just as He promised.
Therefore, be exceedingly vigilant in loving the LORD your God. “
If you turn back and ally yourselves with the remnant of these nations still among you, intermarrying with them until you are thoroughly entangled with them and they with you,

then know with certainty that the LORD your God will no longer drive these nations out before you; instead, they will become a snare and a trap for you, a scourge at your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this good land that the LORD your God has given you. “

Now I am about to die, as all mortals do, and you know with all your heart and soul that not one of the good promises the LORD your God made concerning you has failed; every one has been fulfilled, and not a single word has fallen short.

But just as every good promise the LORD your God made to you has come to pass, so the LORD will bring upon you every calamity until He has destroyed you from this good land that the LORD your God has given you,

if you violate the covenant of the LORD your God that He commanded you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them. Then the LORD’s anger will burn against you, and you will quickly perish from the good land He has given you.”
Joshua assembled all the tribes of Israel at Shechem and summoned the elders, heads, judges, and officers of Israel, and they presented themselves before God.
Joshua said to all the people, “Thus says the the LORD, the God of Israel: Long ago your fathers dwelt beyond the River—Terah, the father of Abraham and of Nahor—and they served other gods.
I took your father Abraham from beyond the River and led him through all the land of Canaan; I multiplied his descendants and gave him Isaac.
To Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau; to Esau I gave Mount Seir as his possession, while Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
“I sent Moses and Aaron, and I struck Egypt with the plagues I inflicted there; afterward I brought you out.
I brought your fathers out of Egypt, and you came to the sea; the Egyptians pursued your fathers with chariots and horsemen to the Red Sea.

When they cried out to the the LORD, He placed darkness between you and the Egyptians and brought the sea over them and covered them; your eyes saw what I did in Egypt. You then lived in the wilderness for many days.
“I brought you into the land of the Amorites, who lived beyond the Jordan; they fought against you, but I gave them into your hand, and you took possession of their land; I destroyed them before you.
Then Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and fought against Israel; he sent for Balaam son of Beor to curse you.
Yet I would not listen to Balaam, so he blessed you instead, and I delivered you from his hand.

“You crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho; the men of Jericho fought against you, as did the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites; but I gave them into your hand.
I sent hornets ahead of you, and they drove out before you the two kings of the Amorites—not by your sword or your bow.
I gave you a land on which you did not toil and cities you did not build; you dwell in them and eat from vineyards and olive groves you did not plant.
“Now therefore fear the the LORD and serve Him in sincerity and truth; remove the gods your fathers served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the the LORD.

If it seems displeasing in your eyes to serve the the LORD, choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve—whether the gods your fathers served beyond the River or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you dwell. But as for me and my household, we will serve the the LORD.”
The people answered, “Far be it from us that we should forsake the the LORD to serve other gods!

For the the LORD our God, He brought us and our fathers up from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery, and performed those great signs before our eyes; He preserved us throughout the journey and among all the peoples through whom we passed.
The the LORD drove out before us all the peoples, including the Amorites who inhabited the land. Therefore we too will serve the the LORD, for He is our God.”
Joshua said to the people, “You cannot serve the the LORD, for He is a holy God; He is a jealous God. He will not forgive your transgressions and your sins.
If you forsake the the LORD and serve foreign gods, He will turn and bring harm upon you and consume you, after having done good to you.”
The people said to Joshua, “No; rather, we will serve the the LORD.”
Joshua said to the people, “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the the LORD, to serve Him.” They said, “We are witnesses.”
Joshua then said, “Now then, put away the foreign gods that are among you, and incline your hearts to the the LORD, the God of Israel.”
The people said to Joshua, “We will serve the the LORD our God and obey His voice.”
On that day Joshua made a covenant for the people at Shechem and established for them a statute and an ordinance.
Joshua wrote these words in the Book of the Law of God; he took a great stone and set it up there under the oak that was by the sanctuary of the the LORD.

Joshua said to all the people, “Behold, this stone shall be a witness against us, for it has heard all the words of the the LORD that He spoke to us; it shall be a witness against you, lest you deny your God.”
Then Joshua sent the people away, each to his own inheritance.
After these things Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the the LORD, died at the age of one hundred and ten years.
They buried him within the border of his inheritance at Timnath-serah, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
Israel served the the LORD all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua and who had known all the work that the the LORD had done for Israel.

The bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel had brought up from Egypt, were buried at Shechem in the parcel of ground that Jacob had bought from the sons of Hamor, Shechem's father, for one hundred pieces of silver; it became the inheritance of the descendants of Joseph.
Eleazar son of Aaron died, and they buried him at Gibeah of Phinehas his son, which had been given him in the hill country of Ephraim.
After Joshua’s death, the Israelites inquired of the LORD, “Who among us shall go up first against the Canaanites to fight them?”
The LORD said, “Judah shall go up; behold, I have given the land into his hand.”
Judah said to Simeon his brother, “Come up with me into my allotment, and let us fight against the Canaanites; I will also go with you into your allotment.” So Simeon went with him.
Judah went up, and the LORD delivered the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand; they struck ten thousand men at Bezek.
They found Adoni-bezek in Bezek and fought against him, and they struck the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
Adoni-bezek fled, but they pursued him, seized him, and cut off his thumbs and his big toes.
Adoni-bezek said, “Seventy kings with thumbs and big toes cut off used to gather scraps under my table. As I have done, so God has repaid me.” Then they brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
The men of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it; they struck it with the sword and set the city on fire.
Afterward the men of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Negev, and the lowland.
Judah went against the Canaanites who lived in Hebron, formerly Kiriath-arba, and they struck Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
From there Judah went against the inhabitants of Debir, formerly Kiriath-sepher.
Caleb said, “Whoever strikes Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give him my daughter Achsah as a wife.”
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, captured it, so Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as a wife.
When she arrived, she urged him to ask her father for a field. She got down from her donkey, and Caleb asked her, “What do you want?”
She said to him, “Give me a blessing. Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me also springs of water.” So Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
The descendants of Moses’ father-in-law the Kenite went up with the men of Judah from the City of Palms into the wilderness of Judah in the Negev near Arad; they went and settled among the people.
Judah went with his brother Simeon and struck the Canaanites living in Zephath and devoted it to destruction; so the city was called Hormah.
Judah also captured Gaza with its territory, Ashkelon with its territory, and Ekron with its territory.
The LORD was with Judah, and they took possession of the hill country, but they could not drive out the inhabitants of the plain because they had chariots of iron.
Hebron was given to Caleb, as Moses had said, and he drove out from there the three sons of Anak.
But the Benjamites did not drive out the Jebusites who inhabited Jerusalem; so the Jebusites have lived with the Benjamites in Jerusalem to this day.
The house of Joseph also went up against Bethel, and the LORD was with them.
The house of Joseph scouted Bethel, formerly called Luz.
The scouts saw a man coming out of the city and said to him, “Show us the entrance to the city, and we will treat you kindly.”
So he showed them the entrance to the city, and they struck the city with the sword, but they let the man and all his family go.
The man went to the land of the Hittites and built a city and called it Luz, which is its name to this day.

Manasseh did not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shean and its villages, or Taanach and its villages, or the inhabitants of Dor and its villages, or the inhabitants of Ibleam and its villages, or the inhabitants of Megiddo and its villages; for the Canaanites were determined to remain in that land.
When Israel grew strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, but they did not drive them out completely.
Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer, so the Canaanites continued to live among them in Gezer.
Zebulun did not drive out the inhabitants of Kitron or the inhabitants of Nahalol, so the Canaanites lived among them and became subject to forced labor.
Asher did not drive out the inhabitants of Acco, or of Sidon, or of Ahlab, or of Achzib, or of Helbah, or of Aphek, or of Rehob.
So the Asherites lived among the Canaanites who inhabited the land, because they did not drive them out.

Naphtali did not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh or the inhabitants of Beth-anath, so they lived among the Canaanites who inhabited the land; nevertheless, the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath became subject to forced labor.
The Amorites forced the Danites into the hill country, for they did not allow them to come down to the plain.
The Amorites were determined to remain in Har-heres, in Aijalon, and in Shaalbim; but when the house of Joseph grew strong, they became subject to forced labor.
The border of the Amorites ran from the Ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela upward.

The angel of the LORD ascended from Gilgal to Bochim and declared, “I brought you out of Egypt and led you into the land I swore to give your ancestors. I said, ‘I will never break My covenant with you,
and you must not make a covenant with the inhabitants of this land; you must dismantle their altars.’ But you have not obeyed Me. What is this you have done?
Therefore I now say to you, I will not drive them out before you; they will be a constant source of distress to you, and their gods will ensnare you.”
When the angel of the LORD had spoken these words to all the Israelites, the people raised their voices and wept.
So they called that place Bochim, and there they sacrificed to the LORD.
After Joshua had dismissed the Israelites, they went to take possession of the land, each to his own inheritance.
The people served the LORD throughout the days of Joshua and throughout the days of the elders who outlived him, those who had seen all the great works the LORD had done for Israel.
Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of one hundred ten.
They buried him in the territory of his inheritance at Timnath-heres in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
After that entire generation had passed away, another generation arose who did not know the LORD or the works He had done for Israel.
Then the Israelites did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and served the Baals.
They abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors, who had brought them out of Egypt. They followed and worshiped the gods of the peoples around them, and they provoked the LORD to anger.
They abandoned the LORD and served Baal and the Ashtoreths.
Then the anger of the LORD flared against Israel, and He handed them over to raiders who plundered them. He delivered them to their enemies all around, and they could no longer withstand their foes.
Wherever Israel went, the power of the LORD was against them to bring disaster, just as the LORD had said and as He had sworn to them. So they were in great distress.
Then the LORD appointed judges, who rescued them from those who plundered them.

Yet they would not listen to their judges, but prostituted themselves to other gods and worshiped them. They quickly turned from the way their ancestors had lived in obedience to the commands of the LORD; they did not do as their ancestors had done.

Whenever the LORD appointed a judge for them, He was with the judge and rescued them from their enemies as long as the judge lived, for the LORD was moved to pity by their groaning under those who oppressed and afflicted them.

But when the judge died, they relapsed and behaved even more corruptly than their ancestors, following other gods to serve and worship them. They refused to give up their evil practices and stubborn ways.
So the anger of the LORD flared against Israel, and He said, “Because this nation has transgressed the covenant I commanded their ancestors and has not obeyed My commands,
I will no longer drive out before them any of the nations Joshua left when he died.
I will use them to test Israel, to see whether they will keep the way of the LORD and walk in it as their ancestors did.”
So the LORD left those nations alone, not driving them out at once, and did not deliver them to Joshua.
These are the nations that the LORD left in place to test Israel—all those who had not known the wars of Canaan—
only so that later generations of Israelites, especially those who had never experienced such warfare, might learn it.
The five Philistine rulers, all the Canaanites, Sidonians, and Hivites who lived in the hill country of Lebanon from Mount Baal Hermon to the entrance of Hamath,
remained to test Israel and to reveal whether the people would obey the commands that the LORD had given their ancestors through Moses.
So the Israelites lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
They took the daughters of those nations as wives for themselves and gave their own daughters to their sons, and they served their gods.
The Israelites did what was evil in the sight of the LORD: they forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asherahs.
Therefore the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim, king of Aram-naharaim, and the Israelites served him for eight years.
But when the Israelites cried out to the LORD, the LORD raised up Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, as a deliverer for them, and he saved them.
The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel. He went out to war, and the LORD delivered Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram into his hand, so that his hand prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim.
Then the land had rest for forty years, until Othniel son of Kenaz died.
Again the Israelites did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, so the LORD strengthened Eglon king of Moab against Israel, because they had done what was evil in the sight of the LORD.
He gathered the Ammonites and Amalekites to himself, marched against Israel, defeated them, and took possession of the City of Palms.
The Israelites served Eglon king of Moab for eighteen years.
But when the Israelites cried out to the LORD, the LORD raised up Ehud son of Gera, a Benjamite who was left-handed, and through him the Israelites sent tribute to Eglon king of Moab.
Ehud made for himself a double-edged sword about a cubit long and strapped it to his right thigh beneath his clothing.
He brought the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man.
When Ehud had finished presenting the tribute, he sent away the men who had carried it.
Yet he himself turned back at the idols near Gilgal and said, "I have a secret message for you, O king." The king said, "Silence!" and all who stood around him withdrew.
Ehud then approached him as he sat alone in the cool upper chamber and said, "I have a word from God for you." The king rose from his throne.
Ehud reached with his left hand, drew the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into Eglon's belly.
The hilt followed the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, because he did not withdraw the sword from the belly; and dung came out.
Then Ehud went out through the vestibule, shutting and locking the doors of the upper room behind him.
After he had gone, Eglon's servants came and saw that the doors of the upper room were locked, and they said, "He must be relieving himself in the cool chamber."
They waited until they were embarrassed, but when he still did not open the doors, they took the key and unlocked them. There they found their lord fallen dead on the floor.
While they delayed, Ehud escaped; he passed beyond the idols and fled to Seirah.
When he arrived, he sounded the trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites went down with him from the hills, with him leading the way.
He said to them, "Follow me, for the LORD has delivered your enemies, the Moabites, into your hand." They went down after him, seized the fords of the Jordan against Moab, and let no one cross.
At that time they struck down about ten thousand Moabites, all robust and valiant men; not one escaped.
So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel, and the land had rest for eighty years.
After him came Shamgar son of Anath, who struck down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad; he too saved Israel.
After Ehud died, the Israelites once again committed what was evil in the sight of the the LORD.
So the the LORD delivered them into the power of Jabin, king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor. The commander of his army was Sisera, who resided in Harosheth-hagoyim.
Then the Israelites cried out to the the LORD, because Jabin possessed nine hundred iron chariots and had ruthlessly oppressed them for twenty years.
Now Deborah, a prophetess and the wife of Lappidoth, was administering justice in Israel at that time.
She used to sit beneath the palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites came up to her for adjudication.

She summoned Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali and said to him, “Has not the the LORD, the God of Israel, commanded, ‘Go, advance toward Mount Tabor and take with you ten thousand men from the sons of Naphtali and from the sons of Zebulun’?
I will lure Sisera, the commander of Jabin’s army, with his chariots and his multitude, to you at the Kishon River, and I will deliver him into your power.”
Barak said to her, “If you go with me, I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go.”

She said, “I will surely go with you; nevertheless, the glory will not be yours on the expedition you are taking, for the the LORD will deliver Sisera into the power of a woman.” Then Deborah arose and went with Barak to Kedesh.
Barak called Zebulun and Naphtali together to Kedesh, and ten thousand men went up after him; Deborah also went up with him.
Now Heber the Kenite had separated himself from the Kenites, from the sons of Hobab, Moses’ father-in-law, and had pitched his tent as far as the oak in Zaanannim, which is near Kedesh.
They told Sisera that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor.
So Sisera called together all his chariots, nine hundred iron chariots, and all the people who were with him, from Harosheth-hagoyim to the Kishon River.

Then Deborah said to Barak, “Arise, for this is the day on which the the LORD has delivered Sisera into your power. Has not the the LORD gone before you?” So Barak went down from Mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.
And the the LORD routed Sisera and all his chariots and all his army before Barak by the sword. Sisera got down from his chariot and fled on foot.
But Barak pursued the chariots and the army to Harosheth-hagoyim, and all the army of Sisera fell to the sword; not a single man survived.
But Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin, king of Hazor, and the house of Heber the Kenite.
Jael went out to meet Sisera and said to him, “Come in, my lord; come in to me; do not be afraid.” So he entered her tent, and she covered him with a blanket.
He said to her, “Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty.” So she opened a skin of milk and gave him a drink and covered him.
He said to her, “Stand at the entrance of the tent, and if anyone comes and asks you, ‘Is there a man here?’ you shall say, ‘No.’”
But Jael, Heber’s wife, took a tent peg and took a hammer in her hand, and approached him stealthily, and drove the peg into his temple until it sank into the ground; and he died.

Now Barak was pursuing Sisera, and Jael came out to meet him and said to him, “Come, and I will show you the man you are seeking.” So he came to her, and there lay Sisera dead with the peg in his temple.
So on that day God subdued Jabin, king of Canaan, before the Israelites.
The Israelites pressed Jabin, king of Canaan, with ever-increasing severity until they destroyed him.
On that day Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang, saying,
“When the princes in Israel take the lead, when the people willingly offer themselves—praise the LORD!
Hear, O kings; give ear, O rulers! I, even I, will sing to the LORD; I will make music to the LORD, the God of Israel.”
The LORD, when You went out from Seir, when You marched from the field of Edom, the earth trembled, the heavens poured, indeed, the clouds poured water.
The mountains quaked before the LORD, even Sinai before the LORD, the God of Israel.
In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were deserted, and travelers walked the byways.
Villages in Israel ceased; they ceased until I, Deborah, arose—a mother in Israel.
When they chose new gods, war came to the gates; not a shield or spear was seen among forty thousand in Israel.
My heart goes out to the leaders of Israel, who offered themselves willingly among the people. Bless the LORD!
You who ride on white donkeys, you who sit on saddle blankets, and you who walk along the road, consider.

At the sound of those who divide flocks at the watering places, there they recount the righteous acts of the LORD, the righteous acts of His villagers in Israel. Then the people of the LORD went down to the gates.
Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake, sing a song! Arise, Barak, and lead away your captives, son of Abinoam.
Then the survivors came down to the nobles; the people of the LORD came down to me against the mighty.
From Ephraim those whose root is in Amalek came down, following you, Benjamin, with your peoples; from Machir commanders came down, and from Zebulun those who wield the staff of office.
The princes of Issachar were with Deborah; indeed, Issachar was with Barak, sent into the valley under his command. Among the clans of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.
Why did you sit among the sheepfolds, to hear the whistling for the flocks? Among the clans of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.
Gilead stayed beyond the Jordan; and Dan, why did he dwell in ships? Asher sat on the seashore and stayed by his coves.
Zebulun is a people who risked their lives to the death; Naphtali also, on the heights of the field.
The kings came and fought; then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo; they took no spoil of silver.
From heaven the stars fought; from their courses they fought against Sisera.
The torrent Kishon swept them away, the ancient torrent, the torrent Kishon. March on, my soul, with might!
Then the hooves of the horses pounded—the galloping, galloping of his stallions.
“Curse Meroz,” says the angel of the LORD; “curse bitterly its inhabitants, because they did not come to the help of the LORD, to the help of the LORD against the mighty.”
Most blessed among women is Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite; most blessed is she among women in the tent.
He asked for water, she gave him milk; in a noble's bowl she brought him curds.
She reached for the tent peg, and her right hand for the workman's hammer; she struck Sisera, she crushed his head, she shattered and pierced his temple.
Between her feet he sank, he fell, he lay; between her feet he sank, he fell; where he sank, there he fell—dead.
Sisera's mother looked through the window and cried out through the lattice: “Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why do the hoofbeats of his chariots delay?”
Her wise women answer her, and she repeats to herself,
“Are they not finding and dividing the spoil—a girl or two for each warrior, a plunder of dyed garments for Sisera, the spoil of embroidered garments for the neck of the looter?”
So may all Your enemies perish, the LORD! But may those who love You be like the sun when it rises in its strength. And the land had rest forty years.
The Israelites did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD gave them into the hand of Midian for seven years.
The hand of Midian prevailed over Israel, and because of Midian the Israelites made for themselves hiding places in the mountains—caves and strongholds.
Whenever Israel had sown its crops, the Midianites, the Amalekites, and the peoples of the east would come up against them.
They would encamp against them and destroy the produce of the land as far as Gaza, leaving no sustenance in Israel—neither sheep, nor ox, nor donkey.
For they came up with their livestock and their tents like a swarm of locusts in number; both they and their camels were without number, and they entered the land to ravage it.
So Israel was brought very low because of Midian, and the Israelites cried out to the LORD.
When the Israelites cried out to the LORD because of Midian,
the LORD sent a prophet to the Israelites. He said to them, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I brought you up from Egypt and brought you out of the house of slavery.
I delivered you from the hand of the Egyptians and from the hand of all your oppressors. I drove them out before you and gave you their land.
I said to you, 'I am the LORD your God. Do not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell.' But you have not obeyed My voice."
Now the angel of the LORD came and sat under the terebinth at Ophrah that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite, while his son Gideon was threshing wheat in the winepress to hide it from the Midianites.
The angel of the LORD appeared to him and said to him, "The LORD is with you, O mighty man of valor."

Gideon said to him, "Please, my lord, if the LORD is with us, why has all this happened to us? Where are all His wonders that our fathers told us about, saying, 'Did not the LORD bring us up from Egypt?' But now the LORD has forsaken us and given us into the hand of Midian."
The LORD turned to him and said, "Go in this strength of yours and deliver Israel from the hand of Midian. Have I not sent you?"
He said to Him, "Please, Lord, how can I deliver Israel? Behold, my clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house."
The LORD said to him, "Surely I will be with you, and you shall strike Midian as one man."
He said, "If now I have found favor in Your sight, then show me a sign that it is You who speak with me.
Please do not depart from here until I come to You and bring my offering and set it before You." "I will stay until you return," He said.

So Gideon went in and prepared a young goat and unleavened cakes from an ephah of flour. He put the meat in a basket and the broth in a pot, and he brought them out to him under the terebinth and presented them.
The angel of God said to him, "Take the meat and the unleavened cakes and lay them on this rock, and pour out the broth." And he did so.

Then the angel of the LORD stretched out the tip of the staff that was in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened cakes. Fire sprang up from the rock and consumed the meat and the cakes, and the angel of the LORD vanished from his sight.
When Gideon realized that it was the angel of the LORD, he said, "Alas, Lord the LORD! For I have seen the angel of the LORD face to face."
The LORD said to him, "Peace be to you. Do not be afraid; you shall not die."
So Gideon built an altar there to the LORD and called it "The LORD Is Peace." To this day it still stands at Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
That night the LORD said to him, "Take your father's bull, the second bull seven years old, and tear down the altar of Baal that belongs to your father, and cut down the Asherah that is beside it.
Then build an altar to the LORD your God on top of this stronghold, using the wood of the Asherah that you cut down, and take the second bull and offer it as a burnt offering."
So Gideon took ten men from his servants and did as the LORD had told him. But because he was afraid of his father's household and the men of the city, he did it by night.
When the men of the city rose early in the morning, behold, the altar of Baal was thrown down, the Asherah beside it was cut down, and the second bull was offered on the newly built altar.
They said to one another, "Who has done this thing?" And after they had inquired and searched, they said, "Gideon the son of Joash has done this thing."
Then the men of the city said to Joash, "Bring out your son, that he may die, because he has broken down the altar of Baal and because he has cut down the Asherah that was beside it."

But Joash said to all who stood against him, "Will you contend for Baal? Or will you save him? Whoever contends for him shall be put to death by morning. If he is a god, let him contend for himself, because his altar has been broken down."
Therefore on that day he was called Jerubbaal, that is to say, "Let Baal contend against him," because he had broken down his altar.
Now all the Midianites and the Amalekites and the peoples of the east gathered together, and they crossed over and encamped in the Valley of Jezreel.
But the Spirit of the LORD clothed Gideon, and he blew the trumpet, and the Abiezrites rallied after him.
He sent messengers throughout all Manasseh, and they also were gathered to him; he also sent messengers to Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they came up to meet them.
Then Gideon said to God, "If You will deliver Israel by my hand, as You have spoken,

behold, I am laying a fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If there is dew on the fleece alone, and all the ground is dry, then I shall know that You will deliver Israel by my hand, as You have spoken."
And so it was. When he rose early the next morning and squeezed the fleece, he wrung out a bowlful of water from the fleece.

Then Gideon said to God, "Do not let Your anger burn against me, but let me speak once more. Please let me test once more with the fleece: let the fleece alone be dry, and let there be dew on all the ground."
And God did so that night: it was dry on the fleece alone, and there was dew on all the ground.
Jerubbaal—that is, Gideon—and all the people with him rose early and encamped beside the spring of Harod, while the Midianite camp lay north of them in the valley near the hill of Moreh.
Then the LORD said to Gideon, "The people with you are too many for Me to give Midian into their hand, lest Israel boast against Me, claiming that its own hand had saved it.

Now therefore proclaim in the hearing of the people, 'Whoever is afraid and trembling, let him return and depart from Mount Gilead.'" So twenty-two thousand of the people returned, and ten thousand remained.

The LORD said to Gideon, "The people are still too many. Bring them down to the water, and there I will test them for you. Everyone of whom I say, 'This one shall go with you,' shall go with you, and everyone of whom I say, 'This one shall not go with you,' shall not go."

So Gideon brought the people down to the water, and the LORD said to him, "Everyone who laps the water with his tongue, as a dog laps, you shall set by himself, and likewise everyone who kneels down to drink."
The number of those who lapped, putting their hands to their mouths, was three hundred men; all the rest of the people knelt down to drink water.
Then the LORD said to Gideon, "With the three hundred men who lapped I will save you and give Midian into your hand. Let all the other people go, each to his own place."

So the people took provisions in their hands and their trumpets, and he sent all the rest of Israel away to their tents, but retained the three hundred men. Now the camp of Midian lay below him in the valley.
That same night the LORD said to him, "Arise, go down against the camp, for I have given it into your hand."
"But if you are afraid to go down, go down to the camp with Purah your servant,

and you shall hear what they say; then afterward your hands shall be strengthened, and you shall go down against the camp." So he went down with Purah his servant to the outposts of the armed men who were in the camp.
Now Midian, Amalek, and all the sons of the East lay spread throughout the valley like locusts in multitude; their camels were without number, as countless as the sand on the seashore.

When Gideon came, a man was telling a dream to his companion, and he said, "I had a dream: a loaf of barley bread rolled into the Midianite camp, came to the tent, struck it so that it fell, turned it upside down, and the tent collapsed."
His companion answered, "This is nothing else but the sword of Gideon the son of Joash, a man of Israel. God has given Midian and all the camp into his hand."

As soon as Gideon heard the telling of the dream and its interpretation, he worshiped. Then he returned to the camp of Israel and said, "Arise, for the LORD has given the Midianite camp into your hand."
He divided the three hundred men into three companies and put a trumpet into every man's hand, with empty pitchers and torches inside the pitchers.
He said to them, "Watch me and do as I do. When I come to the edge of the camp, do just as I do.
When I blow the trumpet, I and all who are with me, then you also blow the trumpets all around the camp and shout, 'For the LORD and for Gideon!'"

So Gideon and the hundred men with him came to the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, just as the guards had been posted. They blew the trumpets and smashed the pitchers that were in their hands.

The three companies blew their trumpets and broke their pitchers; they held the torches in their left hands and the trumpets in their right hands for blowing, and they cried out, "A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!"
Each man stood in his place around the camp, and the whole camp ran, cried out, and fled.

When the three hundred blew the trumpets, the LORD set every man's sword against his companion throughout the camp, and the army fled as far as Beth-shittah toward Zererah, as far as the border of Abel-meholah by Tabbath.
Then the men of Israel were called out from Naphtali, Asher, and Manasseh, and they pursued Midian.

Gideon sent messengers throughout the hill country of Ephraim, saying, "Come down against Midian and seize the waters of the Jordan before them, as far as Beth-barah." So every man of Ephraim was called out, and they seized the waters of the Jordan as far as Beth-barah.

They captured the two Midianite princes, Oreb and Zeeb. They killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb; they pursued Midian and brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon beyond the Jordan.
Then the men of Ephraim said to him, “What is this that you have done to us? Why did you not summon us when you went to fight against Midian?” And they argued with him vehemently.
Gideon answered, “What have I accomplished now in comparison with you? Are not the gleanings of Ephraim superior to the vintage of Abiezer?
God has delivered the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb, into your hands. What could I have done in comparison with you?” Then their anger toward him subsided when he said this.
Gideon and the three hundred men who accompanied him came to the Jordan, weary yet in pursuit.
He said to the men of Succoth, “Please provide loaves of bread for the people who are with me, for they are weary, and I am pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.”
The officials of Succoth replied, “Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your power, that we should give bread to your troops?”
Gideon answered, “When the the LORD has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will tear your flesh with thorns of the wilderness and briers.”
From there he ascended to Penuel and addressed them in the same manner, and the men of Penuel answered him as the men of Succoth had answered.
He said to the men of Penuel, “When I return in peace, I will demolish this tower.”
Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with their camp, about fifteen thousand men—all that remained of the entire host of the people of the East, for one hundred twenty thousand swordsmen had fallen.
Gideon ascended by the route of those who dwelt in tents east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and he struck the camp while it was unsuspecting.
Zebah and Zalmunna fled, and he pursued them; he seized the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and threw the whole army into confusion.
Gideon son of Joash returned from the battle by the ascent of Heres.
He captured a young man of Succoth and interrogated him, and the young man wrote down for him the officials and elders of Succoth—seventy-seven men.

He came to the men of Succoth and said, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, ‘Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your power, that we should give bread to your weary men?’”
He took the elders of the city, together with thorns and briers from the wilderness, and with them he scourged the men of Succoth.
He demolished the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.
Then he said to Zebah and Zalmunna, “Where are the men you killed at Tabor?” They answered, “As you are, so were they; each one resembled a son of a king.”
He said, “They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As the the LORD lives, if you had spared them, I would not kill you.”
He said to Jether his firstborn, “Rise and kill them.” But the boy did not draw his sword, for he was afraid, because he was still young.

Zebah and Zalmunna said, “Rise and strike us down yourself, for as a man is, so is his strength.” So Gideon rose and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and he took the crescent ornaments from their camels’ necks.
The men of Israel said to Gideon, “Rule over us—you and your son and your grandson as well—for you have delivered us from the hand of Midian.”
Gideon replied, “I will not rule over you, nor shall my son rule over you; the the LORD will rule over you.”
Gideon said to them, “Let me make a request of you: each of you give me an earring from his plunder.” (They had golden earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.)
They answered, “We will gladly give them.” They spread out a garment, and each man threw an earring from his plunder onto it.

The weight of the gold earrings that he requested was one thousand seven hundred shekels of gold, besides the crescents, the pendants, the purple garments of the kings of Midian, and besides the chains on their camels’ necks.
Gideon made an ephod from it and placed it in his city, Ophrah, and all Israel turned to it in idolatry there, so that it became a snare to Gideon and his household.
Thus Midian was subdued before the Israelites, and they did not lift their heads again; the land had rest for forty years in the days of Gideon.
Jerubbaal son of Joash went and lived in his own house.
Gideon had seventy sons, his own offspring, for he had many wives.
His concubine who was in Shechem also bore him a son, and he named him Abimelech.
Gideon son of Joash died at a good old age and was buried in the tomb of Joash his father at Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
As soon as Gideon died, the Israelites turned again and gave themselves to the Baals in idolatry, and they made Baal-berith their god.
The Israelites did not remember the the LORD their God, who had saved them from the hand of all their enemies on every side.
Nor did they show steadfast love to the house of Jerubbaal—that is, Gideon—in keeping with all the good he had done for Israel.
Abimelech son of Jerubbaal went to his mother's brothers at Shechem and spoke to them and to all the clan of his mother's father, saying,

"Please speak in the hearing of all the leaders of Shechem: Which is better for you—that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you, or one man rule over you? Remember also that I am your bone and your flesh."
His mother's brothers spoke all these words about him to all the leaders of Shechem, and their hearts inclined toward Abimelech, for they said, "He is our brother."
They gave him seventy shekels of silver from the temple of Baal-berith, and with it Abimelech hired worthless and reckless men, who followed him.
He went to his father's house at Ophrah and killed his brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal—seventy men—on one stone. Only Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, was left, because he hid himself.
Then all the leaders of Shechem and all the house of Millo assembled beside the oak of the pillar in Shechem and went and made Abimelech king.
When Jotham was told about this, he went and stood on the top of Mount Gerizim, lifted up his voice, and cried out, "Hear me, leaders of Shechem, that God may hear you.
"The trees went to anoint a king over them, and they said to the olive tree, 'Reign over us.'
"The olive tree answered, 'Should I give up my rich oil, which honors God and people, just to sway over the trees?'
"Then the trees said to the fig tree, 'You come and reign over us.'
"The fig tree answered, 'Should I give up my sweetness and my good fruit just to sway over the trees?'
"Then the trees said to the vine, 'You come and reign over us.'
"The vine answered, 'Should I give up my new wine, which cheers God and people, just to sway over the trees?'
"Finally all the trees said to the thornbush, 'You come and reign over us.'
"The thornbush said to the trees, 'If you truly anoint me king over you, come and take refuge in my shade. But if you will not, let fire come out of the thornbush and devour the cedars of Lebanon.'
"Now therefore, if you have acted in truth and integrity in making Abimelech king, and if you have dealt well with Jerubbaal and his house, and if you have treated him as his deeds deserved—
for my father fought for you, risked his life, and delivered you from the hand of Midian—

yet you have risen up against my father's house today and killed his seventy sons on one stone, and you have made Abimelech, the son of his maidservant, king over the leaders of Shechem, because he is your brother—
if, then, you have acted in truth and integrity with Jerubbaal and his house today, rejoice in Abimelech, and let him rejoice in you.
But if not, let fire come out from Abimelech and devour the leaders of Shechem and the house of Millo, and let fire come out from the leaders of Shechem and the house of Millo and devour Abimelech."
Then Jotham fled and escaped and went to Beer, where he remained because of Abimelech his brother.
Abimelech ruled over Israel three years.
God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem, and the leaders of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech,

so that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might be avenged and their blood laid upon Abimelech their brother, who killed them, and upon the leaders of Shechem, who strengthened his hand to kill his brothers.
The leaders of Shechem set men in ambush against him on the mountaintops, and they robbed everyone who passed by them on the road; and this was reported to Abimelech.
Gaal son of Ebed came with his brothers and passed through Shechem, and the leaders of Shechem put their confidence in him.
They went out into the fields, gathered their vineyards, trod the grapes, and held a celebration. Then they went into the temple of their god, ate and drank, and cursed Abimelech.

Gaal son of Ebed said, "Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerubbaal, and is Zebul not his officer? Serve the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem! Why should we serve Abimelech?
If only this people were under my hand, then I would remove Abimelech." And he said to Abimelech, "Increase your army and come out."
When Zebul, the governor of the city, heard the words of Gaal son of Ebed, his anger burned.
He sent messengers to Abimelech deceitfully, saying, "Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem, and they are fortifying the city against you.
"Now therefore, arise by night, you and the people with you, and lie in wait in the field.
"In the morning, as soon as the sun rises, get up early and rush upon the city. When he and the people with him come out against you, do to him as you find opportunity."
So Abimelech and all the people with him rose by night and lay in ambush against Shechem in four companies.
Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood at the entrance of the city gate, and Abimelech and the people with him rose from the ambush.
When Gaal saw the people, he said to Zebul, "Look, people are coming down from the mountaintops." Zebul said to him, "You are seeing the shadow of the mountains and mistaking it for men."
Gaal spoke again and said, "Look, people are coming down from the center of the land, and one company is coming by way of the diviners' oak."
Then Zebul said to him, "Where is your mouth now, you who said, 'Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him?' Are not these the people you despised? Go out now and fight with them."
So Gaal went out before the leaders of Shechem and fought with Abimelech.
Abimelech pursued him, and he fled before him; and many fell wounded all the way to the entrance of the gate.
Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul drove Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem so that they could not live there.
The next day the people went out into the field, and this was reported to Abimelech.
He took his people, divided them into three companies, and lay in ambush in the field. When he saw the people coming out of the city, he rose against them and struck them.
Abimelech and the companies with him rushed forward and stood at the entrance of the city gate, while the other two companies rushed upon everyone in the field and struck them.
Abimelech fought against the city all that day. He captured the city, killed the people in it, razed the city, and sowed it with salt.
When all the leaders of the tower of Shechem heard of this, they entered the stronghold of the temple of El-berith.
It was reported to Abimelech that all the leaders of the tower of Shechem had gathered there.

Abimelech and all the people with him went up Mount Zalmon. Abimelech took an axe in his hand, cut off a branch from a tree, lifted it, and put it on his shoulder. He said to the people with him, "What you have seen me do, hurry and do likewise."

So every one of the people also cut off a branch and followed Abimelech. They put the branches against the stronghold and set the stronghold on fire over them. Thus all the people of the tower of Shechem died, about a thousand men and women.
Then Abimelech went to Thebez, encamped against Thebez, and captured it.
There was a strong tower in the middle of the city, and all the men and women and all the leaders of the city fled to it, shut themselves in, and went up to the roof of the tower.
Abimelech came to the tower, fought against it, and approached the entrance of the tower to burn it with fire.
But a certain woman threw an upper millstone down on Abimelech's head and crushed his skull.
He quickly called to his armor-bearer and said to him, "Draw your sword and kill me, lest they say, 'A woman killed him.'" So his young man thrust him through, and he died.
When the Israelites saw that Abimelech was dead, each man went to his own place.
Thus God repaid the evil of Abimelech, which he had committed against his father by killing his seventy brothers.
God also made all the evil of the men of Shechem return on their own heads, and the curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came upon them.
After Abimelech, Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, arose to save Israel. He lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
He judged Israel twenty-three years; then he died and was buried in Shamir.
After him, Jair the Gileadite arose and judged Israel twenty-two years.
He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys, and they owned thirty towns in the land of Gilead, called Havvoth-jair to this day.
Jair died and was buried in Kamon.

The Israelites again did evil in the sight of the LORD. They served the Baals and the Ashtoreths, the gods of Aram, Sidon, Moab, the Ammonites, and the Philistines. They forsook the LORD and did not serve Him.
The LORD’s anger burned against Israel, and He sold them into the hands of the Philistines and the Ammonites.
That year they shattered and crushed the Israelites. For eighteen years they oppressed all the Israelites beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead.
The Ammonites also crossed the Jordan to fight Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim, and Israel was in great distress.
Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, saying, “We have sinned against You; we have forsaken our God and served the Baals.”
The LORD said to the Israelites, “Did I not deliver you from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites, and the Philistines?
The Sidonians, the Amalekites, and the Maonites oppressed you, and you cried out to Me, and I saved you from their hands.
Yet you have forsaken Me and served other gods. Therefore I will no longer save you.
Go and cry out to the gods you have chosen; let them save you in your time of distress.”
The Israelites said to the LORD, “We have sinned. Do to us whatever seems good to You; only please deliver us this day.”
So they put away the foreign gods from among them and served the LORD, and He could bear Israel’s misery no longer.
Then the Ammonites were summoned and camped in Gilead, while the Israelites assembled and camped at Mizpah.
The people, the leaders of Gilead, said to one another, “Who is the man who will begin the fight against the Ammonites? He shall be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”
Jephthah the Gileadite was a formidable warrior, yet he was born to a prostitute, and Gilead was his father.
Gilead's wife bore him sons, and when they grew up, they drove Jephthah away, saying, You shall have no inheritance in our father's house, because you are the son of another woman.
So Jephthah fled from his brothers and settled in the land of Tob, where worthless men gathered around him and went out with him.
After some time, the Ammonites waged war against Israel.
When the Ammonites made war against Israel, the elders of Gilead went to bring Jephthah back from the land of Tob.
"Come," they said to Jephthah, "be our commander, so that we may fight against the Ammonites."
But Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "Did you not hate me and drive me from my father's house? Why do you come to me now, when you are in distress?"
The elders of Gilead replied to Jephthah, "That is why we now turn to you, that you may go with us, fight against the Ammonites, and become head over all who live in Gilead."
Jephthah answered them, "If you bring me back to fight against the Ammonites, and the the LORD gives them into my hand, will I be your head?"
The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "The the LORD is witness between us; we will certainly do as you say."
So Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him their leader and commander. Then Jephthah repeated all his words before the the LORD at Mizpah.
Then Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites, saying, "What do you have against me, that you have come to fight against my land?"

The king of the Ammonites answered Jephthah's messengers, "Because Israel, when coming up from Egypt, took my land from the Arnon to the Jabbok and to the Jordan. Now, therefore, restore it in peace."
Jephthah again sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites.
Jephthah said to him, "This is what Jephthah declares: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the Ammonites.
For when Israel came up from Egypt, they traveled through the wilderness to the Red Sea and came to Kadesh.

Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, 'Please let us pass through your land.' But the king of Edom would not listen. They also sent to the king of Moab, but he refused. So Israel remained at Kadesh.

Then they journeyed through the wilderness, skirted the lands of Edom and Moab, came to the eastern side of Moab, and camped beyond the Arnon. They did not enter Moab's territory, for the Arnon was Moab's border.
Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon, king of the Amorites, king of Heshbon, saying, 'Please let us pass through your land to our own territory.'
But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory; instead, he gathered all his people, encamped at Jahaz, and fought against Israel.

And the the LORD, the God of Israel, delivered Sihon and all his people into Israel's hand, and they defeated them. So Israel took possession of all the land of the Amorites who inhabited that region.
They took possession of all the Amorite territory from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the wilderness to the Jordan.
So now the the LORD, the God of Israel, has driven out the Amorites before His people Israel; and should you possess their land?
Do you not possess what Chemosh your god gives you to possess? So whatever the the LORD our God has driven out before us, we will possess.
Are you now better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever contend with Israel, or did he ever go to war against them?
For three hundred years Israel has lived in Heshbon and its villages, in Aroer and its villages, and in all the cities along the Arnon. Why did you not recover them during that time?
Therefore I have not sinned against you, but you are doing me wrong by waging war against me. May the the LORD, the Judge, decide today between the Israelites and the Ammonites."
But the king of the Ammonites would not listen to the message Jephthah sent him.
Then the Spirit of the the LORD came upon Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh, and through Mizpah of Gilead; from there he advanced against the Ammonites.
And Jephthah made a vow to the the LORD, saying, "If You will indeed deliver the Ammonites into my hand,
then whatever comes out of the door of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the Ammonites shall belong to the the LORD, and I will offer it as a burnt offering."
So Jephthah crossed over to the Ammonites to fight against them, and the the LORD delivered them into his hand.
He struck them down from Aroer to the entrance of Minnith—twenty cities—and as far as Abel-keramim. Thus the Ammonites were subdued before the Israelites.
When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, his daughter came out to meet him with tambourines and dancing. She was his only child; he had no son or daughter besides her.

As soon as he saw her, he tore his clothes and said, "Alas, my daughter! You have brought me to ruin; you have brought disaster upon me. For I have opened my mouth to the the LORD and cannot retract it."
"My father," she replied, "you have given your word to the the LORD. Do to me as you have said, since the the LORD has avenged you of your enemies, the Ammonites."
She also said to her father, "Let this be done for me: allow me two months to wander in the mountains with my friends and mourn my virginity."
"Go," he said, and he sent her away for two months. So she and her friends went into the mountains and wept over her virginity.
At the end of two months she returned to her father, and he did to her as he had vowed; she had never known a man. And it became a custom in Israel
that the daughters of Israel would go each year to commemorate the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite for four days.

The men of Ephraim mustered their forces, crossed to the north, and challenged Jephthah: “Why did you march to fight the Ammonites without calling us to go with you? We will burn your house down over you.”
Jephthah answered them, “My people and I were in a severe conflict with the Ammonites, and when I cried out to you, you did not rescue me from their power.

When I saw that you would not save me, I risked my own life and crossed against the Ammonites, and the LORD delivered them into my hand. Why, then, have you come up against me today to make war on me?”

Then Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead and fought against Ephraim. The Gileadites struck them down because the Ephraimites had taunted, “You are fugitives of Ephraim—Gileadites living among Ephraim and Manasseh.”
The Gileadites seized the fords of the Jordan leading to Ephraim. Whenever an Ephraimite fugitive asked to cross, the Gileadites challenged him, “Are you an Ephraimite?”

If he denied it, they told him, “Then say ‘Shibboleth.’” When he could produce only “Sibboleth,” because he could not pronounce the word correctly, they seized him and slaughtered him at the fords. At that time forty-two thousand Ephraimites fell.
Jephthah judged Israel for six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in the cities of Gilead.
After him, Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel.
He had thirty sons and thirty daughters. He sent his daughters away in marriage and brought in thirty young women from outside for his sons. He judged Israel for seven years.
Then Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.
After him, Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel for ten years.
Then Elon the Zebulunite died and was buried at Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
After him, Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel.
He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy donkeys. He judged Israel for eight years.
Then Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite died and was buried at Pirathon in the hill country of Ephraim, in the territory of the Amalekites.
Once again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD, so the LORD delivered them into the hands of the Philistines for forty years.
Now there was a certain man from Zorah, of the clan of the Danites, whose name was Manoah; his wife was barren and had no children.
The Angel of the LORD appeared to the woman and said to her, “Behold, you are barren and have borne no children, but you will conceive and give birth to a son.
Now then, be careful not to drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean.

For behold, you will conceive and bear a son. No razor shall touch his head, for the boy will be a Nazirite to God from the womb, and he will begin to deliver Israel from the hand of the Philistines.”

Then the woman came and told her husband, “A man of God came to me, and his appearance was like the appearance of the Angel of God—most awe-inspiring. I did not ask him where he came from, and he did not tell me his name.

But he said to me, ‘Behold, you will conceive and give birth to a son. Now then, do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean, for the boy will be a Nazirite to God from the womb until the day of his death.’”
Then Manoah prayed to the LORD and said, “O Lord, please let the man of God whom You sent come to us again and teach us what we should do for the child who will be born.”
And God listened to the voice of Manoah, and the Angel of God came again to the woman as she sat in the field; but Manoah her husband was not with her.
So the woman ran quickly and told her husband, “Behold, the man who came to me the other day has appeared to me.”
Then Manoah arose and followed his wife, and when he came to the man, he said to him, “Are you the man who spoke to the woman?” “I am,” he replied.
