God also raised up another adversary against Solomon—Rezon son of Eliada, who had fled from his master Hadadezer king of Zobah.
He gathered men around him and became captain of a marauding band when David struck them down; they went to Damascus, settled there, and reigned in Damascus.
Rezon was an adversary to Israel throughout Solomon’s reign, adding to the trouble caused by Hadad; he ruled over Aram and despised Israel.
Then Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephraimite from Zeredah, Solomon’s servant—whose mother was Zeruah, a widow—also rebelled against the king.
This was the reason he rebelled: Solomon built the Millo and repaired the gap in the wall of his father David’s city.
Now Jeroboam was a valiant warrior, and when Solomon saw that the young man was industrious, he appointed him over all the forced labor of the house of Joseph.
At that time, when Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him on the road. Ahijah was wearing a new cloak, and the two of them were alone in the field.
Then Ahijah took hold of the new cloak that was on him and tore it into twelve pieces.
He said to Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces for yourself, for thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: ‘Behold, I will tear the kingdom from Solomon’s hand and give you ten tribes.
But he shall have one tribe, for the sake of My servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel,

because they have forsaken Me and have worshiped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites, and because they have not walked in My ways, doing what is right in My eyes and keeping My statutes and My ordinances, as his father David did.

Nevertheless, I will not take the whole kingdom from his hand, but I will make him ruler all the days of his life, for the sake of David My servant, whom I chose, who kept My commandments and My statutes.
I will take the kingdom from his son’s hand and give it to you—ten tribes.
To his son I will give one tribe, so that My servant David may always have a successor before Me in Jerusalem, the city I have chosen for My name.
I will take you, and you shall reign over whatever your soul desires, and you shall be king over Israel.

Then it shall be, if you listen to all that I command you and walk in My ways, and do what is right in My sight by observing My statutes and My commandments, as My servant David did, then I will be with you and build you an enduring house, as I built for David, and I will give you Israel.
I will afflict the descendants of David for this, but not always.’”
Solomon sought therefore to put Jeroboam to death, but Jeroboam arose and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and remained in Egypt until Solomon’s death.
Now the rest of Solomon’s deeds, all that he accomplished, and his wisdom—are they not recorded in the book of the acts of Solomon?
The duration of Solomon’s reign in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.
Solomon died and was buried in the city of his father David, and his son Rehoboam reigned in his place.
Rehoboam went to Shechem, because all Israel had come there to crown him king.
Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of this while he was still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon, and he remained there.
So they sent for Jeroboam, and he and all Israel came to Rehoboam and said,
"Your father made our yoke heavy. Now lighten the harsh servitude your father imposed on us, and we will serve you."
He replied, "Go away for three days, then return to me." So the people departed.
King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime and asked, "How do you advise me to answer this people?"
They answered, "If today you will be a servant to this people and serve them, and if you speak kindly to them, they will be your servants forever."
But he rejected the advice the elders gave him and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and now stood before him.
He asked them, "What advice do you give? How should we answer these people who have said, 'Lighten the yoke your father put on us'?"
The young men who had grown up with him replied,
"I will be far harsher than my father: he burdened you heavily, and I will increase your burden; he punished you with whips, and I will punish you far more severely."
On the third day, Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam, just as the king had said, "Return to me on the third day."
The king answered the people harshly, rejecting the advice of the elders.
He spoke to them as the young men had advised: "My father made your yoke heavy, but I will make it heavier. My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you far more severely."
So the king did not listen to the people, because this turn of events was from the the LORD, so that He might fulfill the word He had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.

When all Israel saw that the king would not listen to them, they answered, "What share do we have in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. To your tents, Israel! Look after your own house, David!" Then Israel went to their tents.
However, Rehoboam continued to reign over the Israelites who lived in the cities of Judah.
King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, but all Israel stoned him to death. King Rehoboam then hurriedly mounted his chariot and fled to Jerusalem.
Thus Israel has rebelled against the house of David to this day.
When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, they summoned him to the assembly and made him king over all Israel. Only the tribe of Judah remained loyal to the house of David.

Rehoboam went to Jerusalem and mustered all the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin—180,000 chosen warriors—to fight against the house of Israel and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
But the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God:
"Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people:"

"Thus says the the LORD: 'You shall not go up or fight against your brothers, the sons of Israel. Return, every man, to his home, for this thing is from Me.' " They listened to the word of the the LORD and turned back, going home as the the LORD had said.
Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. From there he went out and built Penuel.
Jeroboam said to himself, "The kingdom is likely to return to the house of David."

"If these people go up to offer sacrifices in the house of the the LORD at Jerusalem, their hearts will turn to their lord, Rehoboam king of Judah. They will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah."

So the king took counsel and made two calves of gold. Then he said to the people, "It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem. Here are your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt."
He set one in Bethel and the other in Dan.
This became a sin, for the people went to worship before one of the calves even as far as Dan.
He also built shrines on the high places and appointed priests from every class of people, not just from the sons of Levi.

Jeroboam instituted a feast on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, like the feast in Judah, and he went up to the altar in Bethel to sacrifice to the calves he had made. He also stationed in Bethel the priests of the high places he had made.

On the fifteenth day of the eighth month—the month he had chosen of his own accord—he offered sacrifices on the altar he had made in Bethel. He instituted a feast for the Israelites and went up to the altar to burn incense.
By the word of the LORD, a man of God came from Judah to Bethel while Jeroboam was standing by the altar to burn incense.

By the word of the LORD he cried out against the altar: “Altar, altar! This is what the LORD says: ‘A son named Josiah will be born to the house of David. On you he will sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn incense on you, and human bones will be burned on you.’”
That same day the man of God gave a sign and said, “This is the sign the LORD has declared: The altar will be split apart, and the ashes on it will be poured out.”

When King Jeroboam heard what the man of God cried out against the altar at Bethel, he stretched out his hand from the altar and said, “Seize him!” But the hand he stretched out toward the man shriveled up, so that he could not pull it back.
The altar was split apart, and its ashes poured out, according to the sign the man of God had given by the word of the LORD.

Then the king said to the man of God, “Intercede with the LORD your God and pray for me, that my hand may be restored.” So the man of God interceded with the LORD, and the king’s hand was restored and became as it was before.
The king said to the man of God, “Come home with me for a meal, and I will give you a gift.”
But the man of God answered the king, “Even if you gave me half your house, I would not go with you, nor would I eat bread or drink water here.
For I was commanded by the word of the LORD: ‘You must not eat bread or drink water or return by the way you came.’”
So he took another road and did not return by the way he had come to Bethel.
Now an old prophet was living in Bethel, and his sons came and told him all that the man of God had done there that day. They also told their father what he had said to the king.
Their father asked them, “Which way did he go?” And his sons showed him the road the man of God from Judah had taken.
So he said to his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.” And when they had saddled the donkey for him, he mounted it
and rode after the man of God. He found him sitting under an oak tree and asked, “Are you the man of God who came from Judah?” “I am,” he replied.
So the prophet said to him, “Come home with me and eat.”
The man of God said, “I cannot turn back and go with you, nor can I eat bread or drink water with you in this place.
I have been told by the word of the LORD: ‘You must not eat bread or drink water there or return by the way you came.’”

The old prophet answered, “I too am a prophet, as you are. And an angel said to me by the word of the LORD: ‘Bring him back with you to your house so that he may eat bread and drink water.’” (But he was lying to him.)
So the man of God returned with him and ate and drank in his house.
While they were sitting at the table, the word of the LORD came to the old prophet who had brought him back.
He cried out to the man of God who had come from Judah: “This is what the LORD says: ‘You have defied the LORD’s word and have not kept the command the LORD your God gave you.
You came back and ate bread and drank water in the place where he told you not to eat or drink. Therefore your body will not be buried in the tomb of your ancestors.’”
When the man of God had finished eating and drinking, the prophet who had brought him back saddled his donkey for him.
As he went on his way, a lion met him on the road and killed him, and his body was left lying on the road, with both the donkey and the lion standing beside it.
Some people who passed by saw the body lying there, with the lion standing beside the body; and they went and reported this in the city where the old prophet lived.

When the prophet who had brought him back heard this, he said, “He is the man of God who defied the LORD’s word. The LORD has given him to the lion, which has mauled him and killed him, as the LORD’s word declared.”
The prophet said to his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me,” and they did so.
Then he went out and found the body lying on the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside it. The lion had neither eaten the body nor mauled the donkey.
So the prophet picked up the body of the man of God, laid it on the donkey, and brought it back to his own city to mourn for him and bury him.
Then he laid the body in his own tomb, and they mourned over him and said, “Alas, my brother!”
After burying him, he said to his sons, “When I die, bury me in the same tomb where the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his bones.
For the message he proclaimed by the word of the LORD against the altar in Bethel and against all the shrines on the high places in the towns of Samaria will certainly come true.”
Even after this, Jeroboam did not turn from his evil way, but once more appointed priests for the high places from all sorts of people. Anyone who wanted to become a priest he consecrated.
This was the sin of the house of Jeroboam that led to its ruin and complete destruction from the face of the earth.
At that time, Abijah, the son of Jeroboam, fell gravely ill.

Jeroboam said to his wife, "Go and disguise yourself so that no one will recognize you as Jeroboam's wife. Then travel to Shiloh, where the prophet Ahijah resides—the man who declared that I would reign over this people.
Take with you ten loaves of bread, some cakes, and a jar of honey, and go to him; he will tell you what will become of the boy."
Jeroboam's wife did as he instructed: she arose, traveled to Shiloh, and came to Ahijah's house. Now Ahijah could not see, for his eyes had grown dim with age.
Yet the LORD had said to Ahijah, "Behold, the wife of Jeroboam is coming to inquire of you concerning her son, for he is ill. Speak to her thus and so, and when she arrives, she will be disguised."
When Ahijah heard the sound of her footsteps at the door, he said, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why do you disguise yourself? For I have been sent to you with a severe message.
"Go and tell Jeroboam that this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Because I exalted you from among the people and appointed you ruler over My people Israel,

and because I tore the kingdom from the house of David and gave it to you—yet you have not been like My servant David, who kept My commandments and followed Me with all his heart, doing only what was right in My eyes—
but you have done more evil than all who preceded you. You have gone and made for yourself other gods and molten images to provoke Me to anger, and you have cast Me behind your back—

therefore, behold, I am bringing disaster upon the house of Jeroboam. I will cut off from Jeroboam every male, whether slave or free, in Israel, and I will sweep away the house of Jeroboam as completely as dung is swept away.
Anyone belonging to Jeroboam who dies in the city will be eaten by dogs, and anyone who dies in the field will be eaten by the birds of the sky, for the LORD has spoken.' "
Now arise and go to your house. When your feet enter the city, the child will die.

All Israel will mourn for him and bury him, for he alone among Jeroboam's household will receive a burial, because in him something good was found toward the LORD, the God of Israel, within the house of Jeroboam.
Moreover, the LORD will raise up for Himself a king over Israel who will cut off the house of Jeroboam that very day. What then—even now?

The LORD will strike Israel as a reed is shaken in water; He will uproot Israel from this good land that He gave to their fathers, and He will scatter them beyond the Euphrates River, because they have made their Asherah poles, provoking the LORD.
He will give up Israel because of the sins of Jeroboam, which he committed and by which he made Israel sin."
Then Jeroboam's wife arose, departed, and came to Tirzah. As she reached the threshold of the house, the child died.
All Israel buried him and mourned for him, in accordance with the word that the LORD had spoken through His servant Ahijah the prophet.
The rest of the acts of Jeroboam—how he waged war and how he reigned—are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Jeroboam reigned twenty-two years; then he died and was buried with his ancestors, and his son Nadab reigned in his place.

Meanwhile, Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned over Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that the LORD had chosen from all the tribes of Israel to put His name there. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
Judah did evil in the sight of the LORD, and they provoked Him to jealousy with their sins, which they committed beyond all that their fathers had done.
For they also built high places, pillars, and Asherah poles for themselves on every high hill and under every green tree.
There were even male cult prostitutes in the land; they did according to all the abominations of the nations that the LORD had driven out before the sons of Israel.
In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem.
He took away the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house; he took everything, including all the gold shields that Solomon had made.
King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place and entrusted them to the captains of the guard who kept the door of the king's house.
Whenever the king went into the house of the LORD, the guards would carry them and then return them to the guardroom.
The rest of the acts of Rehoboam and all that he did—are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam throughout their days.
Rehoboam died and was buried with his fathers in the City of David. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite. And his son Abijam reigned in his place.
In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam son of Nebat’s reign, Abijam assumed the throne over Judah.
He reigned in Jerusalem for three years. His mother was Maacah, the daughter of Abishalom.
He followed all the sins his father had committed before him, and his heart was not wholly devoted to the LORD his God, as the heart of David his father had been.
Yet, for David’s sake, the LORD his God preserved a royal line for him in Jerusalem, raising up his son after him and strengthening the city.
For David had done what was right in the eyes of the LORD and had not turned aside from anything the LORD commanded throughout his life, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
War persisted between Rehoboam and Jeroboam throughout Abijam’s lifetime.
The remaining acts of Abijam, and all that he did, are recorded in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah. War also continued between Abijam and Jeroboam.
Abijam died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David, and his son Asa succeeded him.
In the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa became king of Judah.
He reigned in Jerusalem for forty-one years. His mother was Maacah, the daughter of Abishalom.
Asa did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as his father David had done.
He banished the male shrine prostitutes from the land and removed all the idols his ancestors had made.
He also deposed his mother Maacah from her position as queen mother, because she had made an abhorrent image for Asherah. Asa cut down her image and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
The high places were not removed, yet Asa’s heart was fully devoted to the LORD throughout his life.
He brought into the house of the LORD the silver, gold, and vessels that his father had consecrated, along with his own consecrated gifts.
War continued between Asa and Baasha king of Israel throughout their reigns.
Baasha king of Israel advanced against Judah and fortified Ramah, intending to block all movement into and out of the territory of Asa king of Judah.

Then Asa took all the silver and gold that remained in the treasuries of the LORD’s house and the royal palace, and he entrusted them to his servants. King Asa sent them to Ben-Hadad son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion, king of Aram, who resided in Damascus, with this message:

“Let there be a treaty between you and me, as there was between my father and your father. I am sending you a gift of silver and gold. Go and break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me.”
Ben-Hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel. He struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah, and all Chinnereth, together with the whole land of Naphtali.
When Baasha heard of it, he ceased fortifying Ramah and withdrew to Tirzah.

Then King Asa issued a proclamation throughout Judah—no one was exempt—and the people carried away the stones and timber of Ramah that Baasha had used. With them King Asa built Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.

The rest of Asa’s acts, his might, all he accomplished, and the cities he built are recorded in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah. In his old age, however, he became diseased in his feet.
Asa died and was buried with his fathers in the city of his father David, and his son Jehoshaphat reigned in his place.
Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel for two years.
He did evil in the sight of the LORD and followed his father’s example and the sin he had caused Israel to commit.
Baasha son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him and struck him down at Gibbethon, a Philistine city, while Nadab and all Israel were besieging it.
Baasha killed Nadab in the third year of Asa king of Judah and reigned in his place.

As soon as he became king, Baasha struck down the entire house of Jeroboam. He did not leave Jeroboam a single survivor, but destroyed them all, according to the word the LORD had spoken through His servant Ahijah the Shilonite.
This happened because of the sins Jeroboam had committed and had caused Israel to commit, and because he had provoked the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger.
The rest of Nadab’s acts and all he did are recorded in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
War continued between Asa and Baasha king of Israel throughout their days.
In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king over all Israel in Tirzah, and he reigned for twenty-four years.
He did evil in the sight of the LORD and followed Jeroboam’s example and the sin he had caused Israel to commit.
The word of the the LORD came to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, saying,
“Because I exalted you from the dust and made you ruler over My people Israel, yet you walked in the way of Jeroboam and caused My people Israel to sin, provoking Me to anger with their sins,
behold, I will sweep Baasha and his house away, and I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
Whoever of Baasha’s line dies in the city will be devoured by dogs, and whoever dies in the open country will be devoured by the birds of the heavens.”
Now the rest of the acts of Baasha, together with what he did and the might he displayed, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Baasha died and was buried with his ancestors in Tirzah, and his son Elah reigned in his place.

Moreover, the word of the the LORD came through the prophet Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha and his house, because of all the evil he had done in the sight of the the LORD, provoking Him to anger by the work of his hands and becoming like the house of Jeroboam, and also because he had struck down the house of Jeroboam.
In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king over Israel in Tirzah, and he reigned two years.
His servant Zimri, commander of half the chariots, conspired against him. Now Elah was in Tirzah, drinking himself into a stupor in the house of Arza, who was in charge of the palace in Tirzah.
Zimri went in, struck him down, and killed him—in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah—and reigned in his place.
As soon as Zimri began to reign and sat on his throne, he struck down the entire house of Baasha; he left no male, neither kinsmen nor friends.
Thus Zimri destroyed the whole house of Baasha, in accordance with the word of the the LORD that He had spoken against Baasha through Jehu the prophet,
because of all the sins of Baasha and of his son Elah—sins by which they sinned and caused Israel to sin, provoking the the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless idols.
Now the rest of the acts of Elah, and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigned in Tirzah seven days. Now the army was encamped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.
When the troops in camp heard, “Zimri has conspired and has also killed the king,” all Israel that day proclaimed Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel.
Omri went up from Gibbethon, and all Israel with him, and they besieged Tirzah.
When Zimri saw that the city had been taken, he entered the citadel of the royal palace and burned the king’s house down around him, and he died.
This happened because of the sins he had committed, doing evil in the sight of the the LORD by walking in the way of Jeroboam and by the sin he committed, causing Israel to sin.
Now the rest of the acts of Zimri, and the conspiracy he formed, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Then the people of Israel were divided into two factions: half the people followed Tibni son of Ginath, to make him king, and half followed Omri.
But the faction that followed Omri prevailed over the faction that followed Tibni son of Ginath. So Tibni died, and Omri reigned.
In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri began to reign over Israel; he reigned twelve years, six of them in Tirzah.
He purchased the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, built upon the hill, and named the city he built Samaria, after Shemer, the owner of the hill.
Omri did evil in the sight of the the LORD, and he acted more wickedly than all who had preceded him.
For he walked in all the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and in the sins by which he caused Israel to sin, provoking the the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless idols.
Now the rest of the acts of Omri, which he did, and the might he displayed, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Omri died and was buried with his ancestors in Samaria, and his son Ahab reigned in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah, Ahab son of Omri became king over Israel; Ahab son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.
Ahab son of Omri did evil in the sight of the the LORD more than all who had preceded him.
As though walking in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat had been a trivial matter, he married Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and went and served Baal and worshiped him.
He erected an altar for Baal in the temple of Baal that he built in Samaria.
Ahab also made the Asherah, and Ahab did more to provoke the the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel who had preceded him.

In his days Hiel the Bethelite rebuilt Jericho: he laid its foundation at the cost of Abiram, his firstborn, and set up its gates at the cost of Segub, his youngest, according to the word of the the LORD that He had spoken through Joshua son of Nun.

Elijah the Tishbite, one of the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, “As surely as the the LORD—the God of Israel—lives, before whom I stand, there will be no dew or rain in these years except at my word.”
Then the word of the the LORD came to him:
“Leave here, turn eastward, and hide in the Brook Cherith, which lies east of the Jordan.
You will drink from the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to provide for you there.”
So he did what the the LORD had said. He went and stayed by the Brook Cherith, east of the Jordan.
The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning and bread and meat in the evening, and he drank from the brook.
After some time the brook dried up, because there was no rain in the land.
Then the word of the the LORD came to him:
“Get up, go to Zarephath in Sidon, and stay there. I have commanded a widow there to provide for you.”
So he got up and went to Zarephath. When he arrived at the town gate, a widow was there gathering sticks. He called to her and said, “Please bring me a little water in a jar so I may drink.”
As she was going to get it, he called, “Please bring me a piece of bread as well.”

But she said, “As surely as the the LORD your God lives, I have no bread—only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. I am gathering a couple of sticks to go in and bake it for myself and my son, so that we may eat it and then die.”
Elijah said to her, “Do not be afraid. Go and do as you have said. But first make me a small cake of bread from what you have and bring it to me; afterward make some for yourself and your son.
For this is what the the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘The jar of flour will not be used up and the jug of oil will not run dry until the day the the LORD sends rain on the face of the earth.’”
So she went and did as Elijah had said, and there was food for Elijah, the woman, and her household for many days.
The jar of flour was not used up and the jug of oil did not run dry, in keeping with the word of the the LORD spoken by Elijah.
Some time later the son of the woman who owned the house became ill. His illness grew so severe that he stopped breathing.
She said to Elijah, “What do you have against me, man of God? Have you come to me to call my sin to mind and to kill my son?”
Elijah replied, “Give me your son.” He took the boy from her arms, carried him to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his bed.
Then he cried out to the the LORD, “The LORD my God, have You brought calamity upon this widow with whom I am staying by killing her son?”
Then he stretched himself out over the child three times and cried out to the the LORD, “The LORD my God, please let this child’s life return to him!”
The LORD heard Elijah’s cry, and the child’s life returned to him, and he lived.
Elijah took the child and brought him down from the upper room into the house. He gave him to his mother and said, “Look, your son is alive!”
Then the woman said to Elijah, “Now I know that you are a man of God and that the word of the the LORD from your mouth is true.”
After many days, the word of the the LORD came to Elijah in the third year, saying, "Go and present yourself before Ahab, and I will send rain upon the face of the earth."
So Elijah went to present himself to Ahab. Now the famine was severe in Samaria.
Ahab summoned Obadiah, who was in charge of the palace. (Now Obadiah feared the the LORD greatly,
for when Jezebel was killing the prophets of the the LORD, Obadiah had taken a hundred prophets and hidden them—fifty in a cave—and had provided them with bread and water.)

Then Ahab said to Obadiah, "Go through the land to all the springs of water and to all the brooks. Perhaps we may find grass and keep the horses and mules alive, so that we do not have to destroy any of the livestock."
So they divided the land between them to pass through it: Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went another way by himself.
As Obadiah was on the way, behold, Elijah met him. Obadiah recognized him and fell on his face and said, "Is it you, my lord Elijah?"
He answered, "It is I. Go, tell your lord, 'Behold, Elijah is here.'"
But Obadiah said, "How have I sinned, that you are giving your servant into the hand of Ahab to be killed?

As the the LORD your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom to which my lord has not sent to search for you. And when they said, 'He is not here,' he made the kingdom or nation swear that they could not find you.
And now you say, 'Go, tell your lord, "Behold, Elijah is here."'

And it will come to pass, as soon as I have gone from you, that the Spirit of the the LORD will carry me away—I know not where—and when I come and tell Ahab and he cannot find you, he will kill me. Yet I, your servant, have feared the the LORD from my youth.
Has it not been told to my lord what I did when Jezebel killed the prophets of the the LORD, how I hid a hundred men of the the LORD's prophets, fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water?
And now you say, 'Go, tell your lord, "Behold, Elijah is here,"' and he will kill me."
Elijah said, "As the the LORD of Hosts lives, before whom I stand, I will surely show myself to him today."
So Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him. And Ahab went to meet Elijah.
When Ahab saw Elijah, Ahab said to him, "Is it you, you troubler of Israel?"
He answered, "I have not troubled Israel, but you and your father's house have, because you have forsaken the commandments of the the LORD and followed the Baals."
"Now therefore send and gather all Israel to me at Mount Carmel, and the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah who eat at Jezebel's table."
So Ahab sent to all the children of Israel and gathered the prophets together at Mount Carmel.
Elijah came near to all the people and said, "How long will you vacillate between two opinions? If the the LORD is God, follow Him; but if Baal, follow him." But the people did not answer him a word.
Then Elijah said to the people, "I alone am left a prophet of the the LORD, but Baal's prophets are four hundred and fifty men."

"Let them give us two bulls, and let them choose one bull for themselves and cut it in pieces and lay it on the wood, but put no fire under it. And I will prepare the other bull and lay it on the wood and put no fire under it."
"Then you call on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of the the LORD. The God who answers by fire—He is God." And all the people answered, "It is good."
Then Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, "Choose for yourselves one bull and prepare it first, for you are many; and call on the name of your god, but put no fire under it."

So they took the bull that was given to them and prepared it, and called on the name of Baal from morning until noon, saying, "O Baal, answer us!" But there was no voice; no one answered. And they leaped about the altar that they had made.

At noon Elijah mocked them and said, "Cry aloud, for he is a god! Either he is deep in thought, or he has stepped away to relieve himself, or he is on a journey, or perhaps he is asleep and must be awakened."
So they cried aloud and cut themselves after their custom with swords and lances, until the blood gushed out upon them.
And as midday passed, they raved on until the time of the offering of the evening sacrifice; but there was no voice, no one answered, and no one paid attention.
Then Elijah said to all the people, "Come near to me." So all the people came near to him. And he repaired the altar of the the LORD that had been torn down.
Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of the the LORD had come, saying, "Israel shall be your name."
And with the stones he built an altar in the name of the the LORD, and he made a trench around the altar, large enough to hold two seahs of seed.
And he arranged the wood, and cut the bull in pieces and laid it on the wood.

And he said, "Fill four jars with water and pour it on the burnt offering and on the wood." Then he said, "Do it a second time." And they did it a second time. And he said, "Do it a third time." And they did it a third time.
And the water ran around the altar, and he also filled the trench with water.

At the time of the offering of the evening sacrifice, Elijah the prophet came near and said, "The the LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let it be known today that You are God in Israel, and that I am Your servant, and that I have done all these things at Your word.
Answer me, the the LORD, answer me, that this people may know that You are the the LORD, their God, and that You have turned their hearts back again."
Then the fire of the the LORD fell and consumed the burnt offering and the wood and the stones and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the trench.
When all the people saw it, they fell on their faces and said, "The the LORD—He is God! The the LORD—He is God!"
Then Elijah said to them, "Seize the prophets of Baal! Let not one of them escape." So they seized them; and Elijah brought them down to the brook Kishon and slaughtered them there.
Then Elijah said to Ahab, "Go up, eat and drink; for there is the sound of the abundance of rain."
So Ahab went up to eat and drink. And Elijah went up to the top of Carmel, and he bowed himself to the earth and put his face between his knees.
And he said to his servant, "Go up now, look toward the sea." So he went up and looked and said, "There is nothing." And he said, "Go back seven times."
And at the seventh time he said, "Behold, a small cloud, like a man's hand, is rising from the sea." And he said, "Go up, say to Ahab, 'Prepare your chariot and go down, lest the rain stop you.'"
And in a little while the heavens grew black with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain. And Ahab rode and went to Jezreel.
And the hand of the the LORD was on Elijah, and he girded up his loins and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.
Ahab told Jezebel everything Elijah had done, including how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.
Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, threatening, "May the gods strike me down and worse if, by this time tomorrow, I have not put you to death like one of them."
When Elijah saw this, he fled for his life and came to Beersheba in Judah, where he left his servant.
He went a day's journey into the wilderness and sat down under a broom tree. Then he asked that he might die, saying, "I have had enough, the LORD; take my life, for I am no better than my fathers."
He lay down and slept under the broom tree, and suddenly an angel touched him and said, "Get up and eat."
He looked, and there at his head was a loaf baked on hot stones and a jar of water. He ate and drank, and then lay down again.
The angel of the LORD came back a second time, touched him, and said, "Get up and eat, for the journey is too much for you."
He got up, ate and drank, and strengthened by that food he traveled forty days and forty nights until he reached Horeb, the mountain of God.
There he came to a cave and spent the night in it. Then the word of the LORD came to him, and He said, "What are you doing here, Elijah?"

Elijah replied, "I have been intensely zealous for the LORD, the God of Hosts, because the Israelites have forsaken Your covenant, torn down Your altars, and killed Your prophets with the sword. I alone am left, and they are seeking my life to take it."

The LORD said, "Go out and stand on the mountain before the LORD." Then the LORD passed by. A great and mighty wind tore through the mountains and shattered the rocks before the LORD, but the LORD was not in the wind. After the wind came an earthquake, but the LORD was not in the earthquake.
After the earthquake came a fire, but the LORD was not in the fire; and after the fire came a soft, hushed whisper.
When Elijah heard it, he wrapped his face in his cloak, went out, and stood at the entrance of the cave. Then a voice came to him and said, "What are you doing here, Elijah?"

He answered, "I have been intensely zealous for the LORD, the God of Hosts, because the Israelites have forsaken Your covenant, torn down Your altars, and killed Your prophets with the sword. I alone am left, and they are seeking my life to take it."
The LORD said to him, "Go back the way you came toward the wilderness of Damascus. When you arrive, anoint Hazael king over Aram.
Also anoint Jehu son of Nimshi king over Israel, and anoint Elisha son of Shaphat from Abel-meholah to be prophet in your place.
Jehu will put to death whoever escapes the sword of Hazael, and Elisha will put to death whoever escapes the sword of Jehu.
Yet I will spare seven thousand in Israel—all whose knees have not bowed to Baal and every mouth that has not kissed him."
So Elijah left there and found Elisha son of Shaphat, who was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen ahead of him, while he himself drove the twelfth. Elijah passed by him and threw his cloak over him.
Elisha left the oxen and ran after Elijah, saying, "Please let me kiss my father and mother goodbye, and then I will follow you." Elijah replied, "Go back; I have not compelled you."

So Elisha returned, took the yoke of oxen, and sacrificed them. He boiled their meat using the oxen's yokes as fuel and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he got up and followed Elijah and served him.
Ben-Hadad, king of Aram, gathered his entire army, and thirty-two kings marched with him, along with horses and chariots. He advanced, besieged Samaria, and attacked it.
He sent messengers into the city to Ahab, king of Israel.
They said to him, "This is what Ben-Hadad says: 'Your silver and gold are mine, and your best wives and children are mine as well.'"
The king of Israel answered, "As you say, my lord the king, I am yours, and all that I have is yours."
The messengers returned and said, "This is what Ben-Hadad says: 'I already sent to you, saying, "Give me your silver and gold, your wives and children."'"
"But tomorrow at this time I will send my servants to you. They will search your house and your servants' houses and take everything you value most."

Then the king of Israel summoned all the elders of the land and said, "Please take note and see that this man is seeking trouble, for he has demanded my wives, my children, my silver, and my gold, and I did not refuse him."
All the elders and the people said to him, "Do not listen to him or consent."

So he said to Ben-Hadad's messengers, "Tell my lord the king, 'All that you first demanded of your servant I will do, but this I cannot do.'" The messengers departed and brought this reply back to him.
Then Ben-Hadad sent word to him and said, "May the gods do so to me, and even more, if the dust of Samaria is enough to provide a handful for each of the people who follow me."
The king of Israel answered, "The man who is just buckling on his armor should not boast like the man who is taking it off."
When Ben-Hadad received this message, he and the kings who were helping him were drinking in temporary shelters. He said to his servants, "Prepare for battle," and they advanced against the city.

Then a prophet approached Ahab, king of Israel, and said, "This is what the LORD says: 'Have you seen all this great multitude? Behold, I will give it into your hand today, and you will know that I am the LORD.'"
Ahab asked, "By whom?" The prophet replied, "This is what the LORD says: 'By the young officers of the provincial governors.'" Ahab asked, "Who will begin the battle?" The prophet answered, "You."
So he mustered the young officers of the provincial governors, and they numbered two hundred thirty-two. After them he mustered all the people of Israel, seven thousand men.
They marched out at noon, while Ben-Hadad was drinking himself drunk in the shelters, along with the thirty-two kings who were helping him.
The young officers of the provincial governors led the advance. Ben-Hadad sent out scouts, and they reported, "Men are coming out of Samaria."
He said, "If they have come out for peace, capture them alive; if they have come out for war, capture them alive."
So those young officers led the advance, and the army followed them.
Each man struck down his opponent. The Arameans fled, and Israel pursued them. Ben-Hadad, king of Aram, escaped on horseback with the cavalry.
Then the king of Israel went out and struck the horses and chariots, inflicting a severe defeat on Aram.

Afterward the prophet approached the king of Israel and said to him, "Go, strengthen yourself, and carefully consider what you must do, for at the turn of the year the king of Aram will march against you."
Meanwhile the servants of the king of Aram said to him, "Their gods are gods of the hills, which is why they overpowered us. But if we fight them on the plain, we will surely overpower them."
"Do this: remove the kings from their commands and appoint governors in their place.
Then muster an army like the force you lost—horse for horse and chariot for chariot—and we will fight them on the plain. Surely we will overpower them." So he listened to their advice and did so.
At the turn of the year, Ben-Hadad mustered the Arameans and went up to Aphek to fight against Israel.
The Israelites were also mustered and provisioned, and they went to meet them. The Israelites camped opposite them like two small flocks of goats, while the Arameans filled the land.

Then the man of God approached the king of Israel and said, "This is what the LORD says: 'Because the Arameans said, "The LORD is a god of the hills, but He is not a god of the valleys," I will give all this great multitude into your hand, and you will know that I am the LORD.'"
For seven days they camped opposite each other. On the seventh day the battle was joined, and the Israelites struck down one hundred thousand Aramean foot soldiers in a single day.
The rest fled into the city of Aphek, but the wall collapsed on twenty-seven thousand of the survivors. Ben-Hadad also fled and hid in an inner room of the city.

His servants said to him, "Look, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful. Let us put sackcloth around our waists and ropes around our heads and go out to the king of Israel. Perhaps he will spare your life."

So they put sackcloth around their waists and ropes around their heads, went to the king of Israel, and said, "Your servant Ben-Hadad says, 'Please let me live.'" He asked, "Is he still alive? He is my brother."
The men seized on this as a good omen and quickly said, "Your brother Ben-Hadad!" Ahab said, "Go and bring him." So Ben-Hadad came out to him, and Ahab had him ride in the chariot.

Ben-Hadad said to him, "I will restore the cities my father took from your father, and you may establish marketplaces for yourself in Damascus, as my father did in Samaria." Ahab replied, "On these terms I will release you," and he made a covenant with him and sent him away.
By the word of the LORD, one of the sons of the prophets said to his companion, "Strike me, please." But the man refused to strike him.
Then he said to him, "Because you did not obey the voice of the LORD, as soon as you leave me a lion will strike you down." And as soon as he left him, a lion found him and struck him down.
Then he found another man and said, "Strike me, please." The man struck him and wounded him.
So the prophet went and waited for the king by the road, disguising himself with a bandage over his eyes.

As the king passed by, he cried out to him, "Your servant went out into the thick of the battle, and someone turned aside and brought a man to me and said, 'Guard this man. If he is missing, your life will be for his life, or you must pay a talent of silver.' But while your servant was busy here and there, the man disappeared."
The king of Israel said to him, "So your judgment stands; you yourself have decided it."
Then he quickly removed the bandage from his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized him as one of the prophets.
He said to him, "This is what the LORD says: 'Because you let slip from your hand the man I had devoted to destruction, your life will be for his life, and your people for his people.'"
So the king of Israel went to his house sullen and angry, and he came to Samaria.
After these events, Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard in Jezreel, beside the palace of Ahab, king of Samaria.

Ahab said to Naboth, “Give me your vineyard, that I may make it a vegetable garden, for it is near my house; and I will give you a better vineyard in its place. Or, if it seems good to you, I will give you its price in silver.”
Naboth said to Ahab, “The LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my ancestors.”

Ahab went into his house sullen and angry because Naboth the Jezreelite had said to him, “I will not give you the inheritance of my ancestors.” He lay down on his bed, turned his face away, and refused to eat.
Jezebel his wife came to him and said, “Why is your spirit so sullen that you are not eating?”

He said to her, “I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said to him, ‘Give me your vineyard for silver, or, if you wish, I will give you another vineyard in its place.’ But he said, ‘I will not give you my vineyard.’”
Jezebel his wife said to him, “Do you now rule Israel? Arise, eat, and let your heart be cheerful. I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.”
So she wrote letters in Ahab's name, sealed them with his seal, and sent them to the elders and nobles who lived in Naboth's city.
In the letters she wrote, “Proclaim a fast and seat Naboth at the head of the people.
Set two worthless men opposite him, and let them testify against him, saying, ‘You have cursed God and the king.’ Then take him out and stone him to death.”
The men of his city—the elders and nobles who lived there—did as Jezebel had instructed them, just as it was written in the letters she had sent.
They proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth at the head of the people.

Then two worthless men came in and sat opposite him, and these worthless men testified against Naboth before the people, saying, “Naboth cursed God and the king.” So they carried him outside the city and stoned him to death with stones.
Then they sent word to Jezebel: “Naboth has been stoned and is dead.”

When Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and was dead, she said to Ahab, “Arise, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give you for money; for Naboth is no longer alive, but dead.”
When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he arose and went down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite to take possession of it.
Then the word of the the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite:
“Arise, go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria. Behold, he is in the vineyard of Naboth, where he has gone down to take possession of it.

You shall speak to him, saying, ‘Thus says the the LORD: Have you killed and also taken possession?’ And you shall speak to him, saying, ‘Thus says the the LORD: In the place where the dogs licked the blood of Naboth, the dogs shall lick your blood—even yours.’”
Ahab said to Elijah, “Have you found me, my enemy?” Elijah answered, “I have found you, because you have sold yourself to do evil in the sight of the the LORD.
Behold, I am bringing calamity upon you. I will consume your descendants and cut off from Ahab every male in Israel, slave or free.

I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of the provocation with which you have provoked Me to anger, and because you have caused Israel to sin.
And concerning Jezebel the the LORD has declared: ‘The dogs will devour Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.’
Anyone of Ahab's who dies in the city will be eaten by dogs, and anyone who dies in the field will be eaten by the birds of the air.”
Surely there was no one like Ahab, who sold himself to do evil in the sight of the the LORD, because Jezebel his wife incited him.
He acted most abominably by going after idols, as the Amorites had done, whom the the LORD drove out before the Israelites.
When Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes, put sackcloth on his body, fasted, lay in sackcloth, and walked about dejectedly.
Then the word of the the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite:

“Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before Me? Because he has humbled himself before Me, I will not bring the disaster in his days; but in the days of his son I will bring the disaster upon his house.”
For three years, Aram and Israel remained at peace.
In the third year, Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to the king of Israel.
The king of Israel said to his servants, "Do you know that Ramoth-gilead is rightfully ours, yet we have done nothing to recover it from the king of Aram?"
Then he said to Jehoshaphat, "Will you march with me against Ramoth-gilead?" Jehoshaphat replied to the king of Israel, "I am as you are; my people are as your people; my horses are as your horses."
Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Please seek a word from the LORD today."

So the king of Israel assembled about four hundred prophets and asked them, "Shall I go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or shall I hold back?" They replied, "March up, and the Lord will deliver it into the king's hand."
Jehoshaphat asked, "Is there no other prophet of the LORD here, that we may consult him?"

The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man through whom we may inquire of the LORD—Micaiah son of Imlah—but I despise him, because he never prophesies prosperity for me, only calamity." Jehoshaphat said, "Let the king not speak so."
Then the king of Israel summoned one of his court officials and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imlah immediately."

Meanwhile, the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were seated on their thrones, arrayed in their robes, at the threshing floor beside the gate of Samaria, while all the prophets prophesied before them.
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah had fashioned horns of iron for himself and declared, "Thus says the LORD: 'With these you shall gore the Arameans until they are annihilated.'"
All the prophets prophesied similarly, saying, "Advance against Ramoth-gilead and succeed, for the LORD will deliver it into the hand of the king."
The messenger who had gone to summon Micaiah said to him, "See, the prophets are unanimous in promising success to the king. Please let your word accord with theirs, and speak favorably."
Micaiah replied, "As the LORD lives, I will speak only what the LORD says to me."

When he arrived before the king, the king asked him, "Micaiah, shall we go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or shall we desist?" He answered, "Go up and triumph, for the LORD will deliver it into the hand of the king."
The king said to him, "How many times must I adjure you to speak to me nothing but the truth in the name of the LORD?"
Micaiah said, "I saw all Israel scattered upon the mountains, like sheep without a shepherd. And the LORD said, 'These have no master; let each return to his home in peace.'"
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?"
Micaiah said, "Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on His throne, and all the host of heaven standing beside Him, on His right hand and on His left.
And the LORD said, 'Who will entice Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?' And one said this, and another said that.
Then a spirit came forward and stood before the LORD and said, 'I will entice him.' And the LORD said to him, 'By what means?'
And he said, 'I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' And He said, 'You are to entice him, and you shall succeed; go out and do so.'
Now therefore behold, the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these your prophets, and the LORD has spoken evil concerning you."
Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came near and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said, "Which way did the Spirit of the LORD go from me to speak to you?"
Micaiah said, "Behold, you will see on that day when you go into an inner room to hide."
The king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and carry him back to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king's son,
and say, 'Thus says the king, "Put this fellow in prison and feed him with bread and water of affliction until I come in peace."'"
Micaiah said, "If you return in peace, the LORD has not spoken by me." Then he said, "Hear, all you peoples!"
So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah advanced against Ramoth-gilead.
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself and enter the battle, but you wear your royal robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself and entered the battle.
Meanwhile, the king of Aram had ordered his thirty-two chariot commanders, "Do not engage either the small or the great, but single out the king of Israel."
When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they concluded, "That must be the king of Israel." They turned to attack him, and Jehoshaphat cried out.
But when the commanders realized he was not the king of Israel, they broke off their pursuit.

Yet a random archer drew his bow and struck the king of Israel between the joints of his armor and his breastplate. The king told his charioteer, "Wheel about and take me out of the ranks, for I am wounded."
The battle intensified that day, and the king remained propped up in his chariot facing the Arameans while the blood from his wound pooled in the bottom of the chariot; by evening he was dead.
At sunset a cry swept through the army: "Every man to his own city, and every man to his own land!"
The king died and was conveyed to Samaria, where they buried him.
They washed the chariot at the pool of Samaria, and the dogs licked up his blood while the prostitutes bathed there, fulfilling the word of the LORD that He had spoken.

The remaining acts of Ahab—everything he accomplished, including the ivory palace he constructed and all the cities he built—are they not recorded in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Ahab rested with his fathers, and his son Ahaziah succeeded him.
Jehoshaphat son of Asa began his reign over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.
He was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.

He followed the example of his father Asa in every respect, never deviating from it, and he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD. Even so, the high places were not abolished; the people continued to sacrifice and burn incense on them.
Jehoshaphat also maintained peace with the king of Israel.
As for the rest of Jehoshaphat's acts—his valor and the wars he waged—are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
He expelled from the land the remaining male shrine prostitutes who had survived from the days of his father Asa.
At that time there was no king in Edom; a deputy served as king.
Jehoshaphat built a fleet of Tarshish ships to sail to Ophir for gold, but the voyage never took place because the ships were wrecked at Ezion-geber.
Ahaziah son of Ahab then proposed to Jehoshaphat, "Let my servants sail with your servants," but Jehoshaphat refused.
Jehoshaphat died and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father, and his son Jehoram succeeded him.
Ahaziah son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned two years over Israel.
He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, walking in the ways of his father and mother and in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had induced Israel to sin.
He served Baal and worshiped him, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger, just as his father had done.
After Ahab died, Moab rebelled against Israel.

Now Ahaziah had fallen through the lattice of his upper room in Samaria and injured himself, so he sent messengers with this command: “Go and inquire of Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron, whether I will recover from this injury.”

But the angel of the LORD said to Elijah the Tishbite, “Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and say to them, ‘Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to consult Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron?’
Therefore this is what the LORD says: ‘You will not rise from the bed on which you lie; you will certainly die.’” So Elijah went.
When the messengers returned to the king, he asked them, “Why have you come back?”

They replied, “A man came up to meet us and said, ‘Go back to the king who sent you and tell him, “This is what the LORD says: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are sending to consult Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore you will not rise from the bed on which you lie; you will certainly die.”’”
The king asked them, “What sort of man was it who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?”
They answered, “He was a hairy man wearing a leather belt around his waist.” The king said, “That is Elijah the Tishbite.”
Then Ahaziah sent a captain of fifty with his fifty men to Elijah. The captain went up to him while Elijah was sitting on the summit of the hill and said, “Man of God, the king says, ‘Come down.’”
Elijah answered the captain of fifty, “If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men.” Then fire fell from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.
So the king sent another captain of fifty with his fifty men. The captain approached and said to Elijah, “Man of God, the king says, ‘Come down immediately.’”
Elijah answered, “If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men.” Then the fire of God fell from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.

So the king sent a third captain of fifty with his fifty men. The third captain went up, fell on his knees before Elijah, and pleaded with him, “Man of God, please value my life and the lives of these fifty servants of yours.
See, fire has come down from heaven and consumed the first two captains with their men. But now please value my life.”
The angel of the LORD said to Elijah, “Go down with him; do not be afraid of him.” So Elijah arose and went down with him to the king.

Then Elijah said to the king, “This is what the LORD says: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are sending to consult Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore you will not rise from the bed on which you lie; you will certainly die.”

So Ahaziah died in accordance with the word of the LORD that Elijah had spoken. Because Ahaziah had no son, Joram became king in his place during the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah.
As for the remaining acts of Ahaziah, are they not recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
When the the LORD was about to take Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha were traveling from Gilgal.

Elijah said to Elisha, “Please remain here, for the the LORD has sent me as far as Bethel.” But Elisha said, “As surely as the the LORD lives and as you live, I will not leave you.” So they went down to Bethel.
The company of prophets at Bethel came out to Elisha and said to him, “Do you know that the the LORD will take your master away from you today?” He said, “Yes, I know it too; be silent.”

Elijah said to him, “Elisha, please remain here, for the the LORD has sent me to Jericho.” But he said, “As surely as the the LORD lives and as you live, I will not leave you.” So they came to Jericho.
The company of prophets at Jericho came to Elisha and said to him, “Do you know that the the LORD will take your master away from you today?” He said, “Yes, I know it too; be silent.”
Elijah said to him, “Please remain here, for the the LORD has sent me to the Jordan.” But he said, “As surely as the the LORD lives and as you live, I will not leave you.” So the two of them went on.
Fifty men from the company of prophets went and stood at a distance, facing them, while the two of them stood by the Jordan.
Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up, and struck the water; it divided to the right and to the left, and the two of them crossed on dry ground.
When they had crossed, Elijah said to Elisha, “Ask what I shall do for you before I am taken from you.” Elisha said, “Please let a double portion of your spirit be upon me.”
He said, “You have asked for something difficult; yet if you see me as I am being taken from you, it shall be so for you, but if not, it shall not be.”
As they walked along and conversed, suddenly a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated them, and Elijah ascended to heaven in the whirlwind.
Elisha saw it and cried out, “My father, my father, the chariots and horsemen of Israel!” And he saw him no more. He took hold of his own clothes and tore them into two pieces.
He picked up the cloak that had fallen from Elijah and went back and stood by the bank of the Jordan.

He took Elijah's cloak that had fallen from him and struck the water, saying, “Where is the the LORD, the God of Elijah?” When he had struck the water, it divided to the right and to the left, and Elisha crossed over.
When the company of prophets at Jericho saw him from afar, they said, “The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha.” They came to meet him and bowed to the ground before him.

They said to him, “Look, your servants have fifty strong men. Please let them go and search for your master, lest the Spirit of the the LORD has carried him away and cast him upon some mountain or into some valley.” But he said, “You shall not send.”
They pressed him until he could no longer refuse, and he said, “Send them.” So they sent fifty men, and they searched for three days but did not find him.
When they returned to him while he was staying in Jericho, he said to them, “Did I not tell you, ‘Do not go’?”
The men of the city said to Elisha, “Look, my lord, the city is pleasantly situated, as my lord sees, but the water is bad and the land is barren.”
He said, “Bring me a new bowl, and put salt in it.” So they brought it to him.

He went out to the spring of water and threw the salt into it, and said, “This is what the the LORD says: ‘I have healed these waters; from now on neither death nor miscarriage shall come from them.’”
So the waters have been healed to this day, according to the word that Elisha spoke.
He went up from there to Bethel, and as he was going up on the way, young boys came out of the city and mocked him, saying, “Go up, you bald head! Go up, you bald head!”
He turned around, looked at them, and cursed them in the name of the the LORD. Then two she-bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of the boys.
From there he went to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.
In the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, Jehoram son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned twelve years.
He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, though not like his father and mother, for he removed the pillar of Baal that his father had made.
Nevertheless, he clung to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he had made Israel sin, and he did not turn away from them.
Now Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he paid the king of Israel one hundred thousand lambs and the wool of one hundred thousand rams.
But when Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
At that time King Jehoram went out from Samaria and mustered all Israel.

He also sent word to Jehoshaphat king of Judah: “The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to war against Moab?” Jehoshaphat answered, “I will go. I am as you are, my people are as your people, and my horses are as your horses.”
Then Jehoshaphat asked, “Which way shall we go up?” The reply came, “By the way of the wilderness of Edom.”
So the king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom set out, and they took a circuitous route for seven days; but there was no water for the camp or for the animals that followed them.
Then the king of Israel said, “Alas! The The LORD has called these three kings together only to deliver them into the hand of Moab.”

But Jehoshaphat asked, “Is there no prophet of the LORD here, through whom we may inquire of the LORD?” One of the servants of the king of Israel answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here, who served as Elijah’s attendant.”
Jehoshaphat said, “The word of the LORD is with him.” So the king of Israel, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom went down to him.

Elisha said to the king of Israel, “Why do you involve me? Go to the prophets of your father and to the prophets of your mother.” The king of Israel replied, “No, for the LORD has called these three kings together to deliver them into the hand of Moab.”
Elisha answered, “As the LORD of Hosts lives, before Whom I stand, if I did not respect the presence of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not even look your way.”
“But now bring me a musician.” When the musician played, the hand of the LORD came upon Elisha.
Then he said, “Thus says the LORD: ‘Make this valley full of ditches.’
For thus says the LORD: ‘You shall not see wind, nor shall you see rain, yet this valley shall be filled with water, so that you, your cattle, and your livestock may drink.
This is a small matter in the sight of the LORD; He will also give Moab into your hand.
You shall strike every fortified city and every choice city, fell every good tree, stop up all springs of water, and ruin every good piece of land with stones.’”
In the morning, when the morning offering was being presented, suddenly water came by the way of Edom, and the land was filled with water.
When all Moab heard that the kings had come up to fight against them, all who could bear arms, from the youngest to the oldest, were called out and stood on the border.
They rose early in the morning, and the sun shone on the water; and Moab saw the water red as blood on the other side.
They said, “This is blood! The kings have surely destroyed one another. Now, Moab, to the plunder!”
But when they came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and struck Moab, so that the Moabites fled before them. Israel pursued them into the land and continued striking Moab.

They destroyed the cities, and each man threw a stone on every good field until it was filled. They stopped up all the springs of water and felled all the good trees, until only Kir-hareseth was left with its stones; but the slingers surrounded it and struck it.
When the king of Moab saw that the battle was too strong for him, he took seven hundred swordsmen to break through to the king of Edom, but he could not.

Then he took his firstborn son, who was to reign in his place, and offered him as a burnt offering on the wall. And there came a great wrath against Israel, so they withdrew from him and returned to their own land.

Now a certain woman from the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, saying, “Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that your servant feared the the LORD. Now the creditor has come to take my two sons to be his slaves.”
Elisha said to her, “What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?” She said, “Your servant has nothing in the house except a jar of oil.”
He said, “Go, borrow vessels from outside, from all your neighbors; do not borrow just a few.
Then go in and shut the door behind you and your sons, and pour into all these vessels; when one is full, set it aside.”
So she went from him and shut the door behind her and her sons. They brought the vessels to her, and she poured.
When the vessels were full, she said to her son, “Bring me another vessel.” He said to her, “There is no other vessel.” Then the oil stopped flowing.
Then she came and told the man of God. He said, “Go, sell the oil and pay your debts, and you and your sons can live on the rest.”
One day Elisha went to Shunem, where there was a prominent woman, and she urged him to eat. So whenever he passed by, he would turn in there to eat.
She said to her husband, “Look, I know that this is a holy man of God who keeps passing by us.
Please let us make a small upper room on the wall, and let us put a bed, a table, a chair, and a lampstand there for him, so that whenever he comes to us he can turn in there.”
One day he came there, turned into the upper room, and lay down.
He said to Gehazi his servant, “Call this Shunammite.” So he called her, and she stood before him.

He said to him, “Now say to her, ‘See, you have shown all this concern for us. What can be done for you? Shall I speak a word for you to the king or to the commander of the army?’” She answered, “I live among my own people.”
He said, “What then can be done for her?” Gehazi answered, “Well, she has no son, and her husband is old.”
He said, “Call her.” So he called her, and she stood in the doorway.
He said, “At this season, about this time next year, you will hold a son in your arms.” She said, “No, my lord, O man of God, do not deceive your servant.”
The woman conceived and bore a son at that season, about that time the next year, as Elisha had said to her.
When the child grew, one day he went out to his father among the reapers.
He said to his father, “My head, my head!” His father said to his servant, “Carry him to his mother.”
He carried him and brought him to his mother, and he sat on her knees until noon, and then he died.
She went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, and shut the door behind him, and went out.
She called to her husband and said, “Please send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, that I may run to the man of God and come back.”
He said, “Why will you go to him today? It is neither new moon nor Sabbath.” She said, “All is well.”
Then she saddled the donkey and said to her servant, “Drive on; do not slow the pace for me unless I tell you.”
So she went and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her from a distance, he said to his servant Gehazi, “Look, there is the Shunammite.
Please run now to meet her and say to her, ‘Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with the child?’” She answered, “It is well.”

When she came to the man of God on the mountain, she caught hold of his feet. Gehazi came near to push her away, but the man of God said, “Let her alone, for her soul is bitter within her; and the the LORD has hidden it from me and has not told me.”
Then she said, “Did I ask my lord for a son? Did I not say, ‘Do not deceive me’?”
He said to Gehazi, “Get ready, take my staff in your hand and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet him; and if anyone greets you, do not answer him. And lay my staff on the face of the child.”
The mother of the child said, “As the the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you.” And he arose and followed her.
Gehazi went on ahead of them and laid the staff on the face of the child, but there was no sound or response. So he returned to meet him and told him, “The child has not awakened.”
When Elisha came into the house, there was the child, lying dead on his bed.
He went in and shut the door behind the two of them and prayed to the the LORD.
He went up and lay on the child, and put his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands. He stretched himself upon him, and the flesh of the child became warm.
Then he returned and walked once back and forth in the house, and went up and stretched himself upon him. The child sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
He called Gehazi and said, “Call this Shunammite.” So he called her. When she came to him, he said, “Take up your son.”
She came in and fell at his feet and bowed to the ground. Then she took up her son and went out.

Elisha returned to Gilgal, and there was a famine in the land. The sons of the prophets were sitting before him. He said to his servant, “Put on the large pot and boil stew for the sons of the prophets.”

One of them went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine and gathered from it wild gourds until his garment was full. He came and cut them up into the pot of stew, for they did not know what they were.
They poured out for the men to eat. As they were eating the stew, they cried out and said, “O man of God, there is poison in the pot!” And they could not eat it.
He said, “Bring flour.” He threw it into the pot and said, “Pour it out for the people, that they may eat.” Then there was no harm in the pot.
A man came from Baal-shalishah and brought the man of God bread of the firstfruits—twenty loaves of barley and fresh ears of grain in his sack. He said, “Give it to the people, that they may eat.”
His servant said, “How can I set this before a hundred men?” But he said, “Give it to the people, that they may eat, for thus says the the LORD, ‘They shall eat and have some left over.’”
So he set it before them, and they ate and had some left over, according to the word of the the LORD.

Now Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man in the sight of his master and highly esteemed, because through him the the LORD had given victory to Aram. He was a mighty warrior, but he was a leper.
The Arameans had gone out in raiding parties and brought back a young girl from the land of Israel, and she served Naaman's wife.
She said to her mistress, "If only my master were with the prophet in Samaria! Then he would cure him of his leprosy."
Naaman went in and told his master, "The girl from the land of Israel said such and such."
The king of Aram said, "Go now, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel." So Naaman departed, taking with him ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold, and ten sets of clothing.
He brought the letter to the king of Israel, which read, "With this letter I am sending my servant Naaman to you, so that you may cure him of his leprosy."

When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, "Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man sends to me to cure a man of his leprosy? Just consider and see how he is seeking a quarrel with me!"

When Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent to the king, saying, "Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel."
So Naaman came with his horses and chariots and stood at the door of Elisha's house.
Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, "Go and wash in the Jordan seven times, and your flesh shall be restored to you, and you shall be clean."

Naaman was angry and went away, saying, "Look, I thought that he would surely come out to me and stand and call on the name of the the LORD his God, and wave his hand over the spot and cure the leprosy."
"Are not the Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and be cleansed?" So he turned and went away in a rage.

His servants came near and spoke to him and said, "My father, if the prophet had told you to do some great thing, would you not have done it? How much more, then, when he says to you, 'Wash and be cleansed'!"
So Naaman went down and dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the word of the man of God, and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.

Then he returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and came and stood before him. And he said, "Look, now I know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel. So please accept a gift from your servant."
But he said, "As the the LORD lives, before whom I stand, I will receive nothing." And though Naaman urged him, he refused.

Then Naaman said, "If not, please let your servant be given as much earth as a pair of mules can carry, for your servant will no longer offer burnt offerings or sacrifices to any god except the the LORD.

Yet may the the LORD forgive your servant this one thing: when my master goes into the temple of Rimmon to worship there, and he leans on my arm, and I bow down in the temple of Rimmon, may the the LORD forgive your servant in this matter."
He said to him, "Go in peace." So Naaman went a short distance.

Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said, "Look, my master has spared this Aramean, Naaman, by not accepting what he brought. As surely as the the LORD lives, I will run after him and get something from him."
So Gehazi pursued Naaman. When Naaman saw him running toward him, he got down from the chariot to meet him and asked, "Is everything all right?"

He replied, "Everything is all right. My master has sent me to say, 'Just now two young men from the sons of the prophets have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent of silver and two sets of clothing.'"
