David said to Gad, “I am in great distress. Let me fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are very great; but do not let me fall into the hand of man.”
So the LORD sent a pestilence upon Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell.

God sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem, but as he was destroying, the LORD looked and relented from the calamity and said to the destroying angel, “Enough! Withdraw your hand.” The angel of the LORD was standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

David lifted his eyes and saw the angel of the LORD standing between heaven and earth, with his drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem. Then David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell on their faces.

David said to God, “Was it not I who commanded the people to be numbered? I am the one who has sinned and done evil indeed; but these sheep, what have they done? The LORD my God, let Your hand, I pray, be against me and my father’s house, but not against Your people, that they should be plagued.”
The angel of the LORD commanded Gad to say to David that David should go up and raise an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
So David went up at the word of Gad, which he had spoken in the name of the LORD.
Now Ornan was threshing wheat, and when he turned and saw the angel, he and his four sons hid themselves.
As David came to Ornan, Ornan looked and saw David, went out from the threshing floor, and bowed himself to David with his face to the ground.
David said to Ornan, “Give me the site of this threshing floor, that I may build an altar to the LORD on it. Give it to me at full price, so that the plague may be restrained from the people.”

Ornan said to David, “Take it, my lord the king, and do what seems good to you. See, I give the oxen for burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for wood, and the wheat for the grain offering. I give it all.”
King David said to Ornan, “No, but I will surely buy it for the full price, for I will not take what is yours for the LORD, nor offer a burnt offering that costs me nothing.”
So David gave to Ornan six hundred shekels of gold by weight for the place.
David built there an altar to the LORD and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and he called upon the LORD; and He answered him from heaven by fire upon the altar of burnt offering.
Then the LORD commanded the angel, and he put his sword back into its sheath.
At that time, when David saw that the LORD had answered him at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, he sacrificed there.
Now the tabernacle of the LORD, which Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offering were at that time at the high place in Gibeon.
But David could not go before it to inquire of God, because he was afraid of the sword of the angel of the LORD.
Then David said, “This is the house of the LORD God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel.”
So David gave orders to gather the foreigners residing in the land of Israel, and he appointed stonecutters to cut dressed stone for building the house of God.
David also provided a great quantity of iron for nails for the doors of the gates and for the clamps, and bronze without weight,
along with cedar logs without number, for the Sidonians and Tyrians had brought a great quantity of cedar logs to David.

David said, “My son Solomon is young and inexperienced, and the house to be built for the LORD must be exceedingly magnificent, famous and glorious throughout all lands. Therefore I will make preparations for it.” So David made extensive preparations before his death.
Then he called for his son Solomon and charged him to build a house for the LORD, the God of Israel.
David said to Solomon, “My son, I had it in my heart to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God.
“But the word of the LORD came to me, saying, ‘You have shed much blood and waged great wars. You shall not build a house for My Name, because you have shed so much blood on the earth in My sight.

But behold, a son will be born to you. He will be a man of rest, and I will give him rest from all his enemies on every side. For his name will be Solomon, and I will grant peace and quiet to Israel in his days.
He will build a house for My Name. He will be My son, and I will be his Father. And I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.’
“Now, my son, may the LORD be with you, and may you succeed and build the house of the LORD your God, as He has spoken concerning you.
May the LORD give you insight and understanding when He appoints you over Israel, so that you may keep the law of the LORD your God.
Then you will prosper, if you are careful to observe the statutes and ordinances that the LORD commanded Moses for Israel. Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or discouraged.”

“Now behold, in my affliction I have provided for the house of the LORD 100,000 talents of gold, 1,000,000 talents of silver, and bronze and iron without weight, for there is an abundance. I have also provided timber and stone, and you may add to them.
You also have many workers: stonecutters, masons, carpenters, and men skilled in every kind of work—
in gold and silver, bronze and iron—beyond number. Now rise up and build, and may the LORD be with you.”
Then David ordered all the leaders of Israel to help his son Solomon:

“Is not the LORD your God with you? Has He not given you rest on every side? For He has delivered the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land is subdued before the LORD and before His people.

Now set your hearts and souls to seek the LORD your God. Rise up and build the sanctuary of the LORD God, so that you may bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the holy articles of God into the house built for the Name of the LORD.”
When David had grown old and lived out a full span of years, he established his son Solomon as king over Israel.
He then convened all Israel's leaders, together with the priests and Levites.
The Levites thirty years of age and older were enumerated, and their total by individual head count came to thirty-eight thousand men.
Of these, twenty-four thousand were charged with supervising the work of the LORD's house, while six thousand served as officials and judges.
Four thousand were gatekeepers, and four thousand praised the LORD with the instruments David had fashioned for praise.
David divided them into divisions according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The Gershonites were Laadan and Shimei.
The sons of Laadan were Jehiel the chief, Zetham, and Joel—three in all.
The sons of Shimei were Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran—three in all. These were the heads of the fathers' houses of Laadan.
The sons of Shimei were Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah—four in all.
Jahath was the chief and Zizah the second; Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they were counted as one father's house.
The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel—four in all.
The sons of Amram were Aaron and Moses. Aaron was set apart to consecrate the most holy things, to offer incense before the LORD, to minister to Him, and to bless in His name in perpetuity.
Moses, the man of God, had his sons counted among the tribe of Levi.
The sons of Moses were Gershom and Eliezer.
The son of Gershom was Shebuel the chief.
The sons of Eliezer were Rehabiah the chief; Eliezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah were very many.
The son of Izhar was Shelomith the chief.
The sons of Hebron were Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel were Micah the chief and Isshiah the second.
The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli were Eleazar and Kish.
Eleazar died without sons, having only daughters; their kinsmen, the sons of Kish, married them.
The sons of Mushi were Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth—three in all.

These were the sons of Levi according to their fathers' houses, the heads of the fathers' houses, enumerated by number of names, twenty years old and upward, who performed the work for the service of the LORD's house.
For David had declared, "The LORD, the God of Israel, has granted rest to His people, and He will dwell in Jerusalem forever."
Consequently, the Levites no longer needed to transport the tabernacle and all its vessels for service.
By David's final instructions, the Levites were numbered from twenty years old and upward.
Their post was beside the sons of Aaron for the service of the LORD's house, over the courts and chambers, over the cleansing of all holy things, and over the work of the service of the house of God.
They were responsible for the showbread, the fine flour for the grain offering, the unleavened wafers, the pan, the mixed flour, and every measure and quantity.
They also stood morning by morning to thank and praise the LORD, and likewise in the evening.
They provided for all the burnt offerings offered to the LORD on Sabbaths, new moons, and appointed feasts, according to the required number, continually before the LORD.
Thus they kept charge of the tent of meeting, charge of the sanctuary, and charge of their brothers the sons of Aaron, for the service of the LORD's house.
The priestly divisions of Aaron’s sons were as follows: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu, however, died before their father and left no sons, so Eleazar and Ithamar carried out the priestly office.
With Zadok, a descendant of Eleazar, and Ahimelech, a descendant of Abiathar, assisting him, David apportioned them according to their duties in the sacred service.
Because Eleazar’s lineage produced more leading men than Ithamar’s, the apportionment comprised sixteen patriarchal heads from Eleazar and eight from Ithamar.
They were assigned by lot, since both lineages produced officials of the sanctuary and officials of God.

Shemaiah son of Nethanel, a Levite and scribe, recorded their names before the king, his officers, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and the patriarchal heads of the priestly and Levitical houses—one household drawn from Eleazar and one from Ithamar.
The first lot fell to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah,
the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim,
the fifth to Malchijah, the sixth to Mijamin,
the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah,
the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah,
the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim,
the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab,
the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer,
the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Happizzez,
the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezkel,
the twenty-first to Jachin, the twenty-second to Gamul,
the twenty-third to Delaiah, and the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.

This was their appointed order of ministry for entering the house of the LORD, in accordance with the ordinance established for them by Aaron their father, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded him.
Among the remaining Levites, the sons of Amram included Shubael, and Shubael’s sons included Jehdeiah.
Of Rehabiah, among his sons, Isshiah was the chief.
Of the Izharites, Shelomoth’s sons included Jahath.
The sons of Hebron were Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel included Micah, and among Micah’s sons was Shamir.
Micah’s brother was Isshiah, and among Isshiah’s sons was Zechariah.
The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi, and the sons of Jaaziah were Beno.
Through Jaaziah his son, the Merarite line included Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
Mahli’s son was Eleazar, who had no sons.
The sons of Kish included Jerahmeel.
The sons of Mushi were Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These constituted the Levitical families according to their ancestral houses.

These likewise cast lots, just as their brothers the sons of Aaron had done, before King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the priestly and Levitical families—the principal households alongside the junior ones.

David and the commanders of the army set apart for service the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, who prophesied with harps, lyres, and cymbals. The number of those assigned to this work was as follows:
From the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asharelah. The sons of Asaph served under Asaph's direction; he prophesied under the king's authority.

From the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah—six in all—under the direction of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with the harp, giving thanks and praise to the LORD.
From the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.
All these were sons of Heman, the king's seer in the words of God, to exalt his strength; and God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.
All these served under their father's direction in the house of the LORD, with cymbals, harps, and lyres, for the service of the house of God, under the king's authority—Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman.
Together with their relatives, all of them trained and skilled in singing to the LORD, their number was two hundred eighty-eight.
They cast lots for their assignments, treating the lesser and the greater alike, teacher and student together.
The first lot fell to Asaph and was assigned to Joseph; the second to Gedaliah, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The third to Zaccur, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The fourth to Izri, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The fifth to Nethaniah, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The sixth to Bukkiah, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The seventh to Jesharelah, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The eighth to Jeshaiah, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The ninth to Mattaniah, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The tenth to Shimei, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The eleventh to Azarel, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The twelfth to Hashabiah, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The thirteenth to Shubael, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The fourteenth to Mattithiah, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The fifteenth to Jerimoth, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The sixteenth to Hananiah, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The seventeenth to Joshbekashah, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The eighteenth to Hanani, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The nineteenth to Mallothi, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The twentieth to Eliathah, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The twenty-first to Hothir, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The twenty-second to Giddalti, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The twenty-third to Mahazioth, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
The twenty-fourth to Romamti-ezer, with his sons and brothers—twelve.
As for the divisions of the gatekeepers: from the Korahites, Meshelemiah son of Kore, one of the sons of Asaph.
Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, and Elioenai the seventh.
Obed-edom had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sacar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,
Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, and Peullethai the eighth. For God had blessed Obed-edom.
Also to his son Shemaiah were born sons who ruled over their father's house, because they were men of conspicuous strength and valor.
The sons of Shemaiah were Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad; his brothers Elihu and Semachiah were likewise men of strength and valor.
All these were descendants of Obed-edom; they and their sons and their brothers were capable men of strength for the service—sixty-two in all belonging to Obed-edom.
Meshelemiah had eighteen sons and brothers, all men of strength.
Hosah, one of the descendants of Merari, also had sons: Shimri the first, although he was not the firstborn, his father had designated him chief;
Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, and Zechariah the fourth. The sons and brothers of Hosah numbered thirteen in all.
These divisions of the gatekeepers, through their chief men, had duties for ministering in the house of the LORD, just as their brothers did.
They cast lots for each gate, according to their families, young and old alike.
The lot for the East Gate fell to Shelemiah. Then lots were cast for his son Zechariah, a wise counselor, and the lot for the North Gate fell to him.
The lot for the South Gate fell to Obed-edom, and the lot for the storehouses fell to his sons.
The lot for the West Gate fell to Shuppim and Hosah. There was a gate at Shallecheth on the ascending road, and each watch stood opposite its corresponding watch.
There were six Levites on the east, four on the north, four on the south, and two pairs at the storehouse.
At the Parbar on the west, there were four at the road and two at the Parbar.
These were the divisions of the gatekeepers who were descendants of Korah and of Merari.
Now their fellow Levites were in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the dedicated things.
Among the descendants of Ladan—the Gershonites through Ladan, heads of the fathers' houses of Ladan the Gershonite—was Jehieli.
His sons Zetham and Joel were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
Of the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites,
Shebuel, a descendant of Gershom son of Moses, was the officer in charge of the treasuries.
His relatives through Eliezer included Rehabiah his son, Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, Zichri his son, and Shelomoth his son.

This Shelomoth and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries of the dedicated things that King David, the heads of families, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the army commanders had dedicated.
They had dedicated some of the plunder and war spoils to the repair and upkeep of the house of the LORD.

Everything that had been dedicated by Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah, together with everything else that had been dedicated, was under the care of Shelomith and his brothers.
From the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were assigned to the outside work as officers and judges over Israel.
From the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers—1,700 able men—had charge of Israel west of the Jordan for all the work of the LORD and for the service of the king.

As for the Hebronites, Jerijah was the chief according to the genealogical records of his ancestors. In the fortieth year of David's reign, a search was conducted, and capable men of valor were found among them at Jazer in Gilead.

Along with 2,700 of his relatives, all capable men and heads of families, Jerijah was appointed by King David over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh for every matter pertaining to God and to the king.

Now the Israelites were counted according to their number: the heads of the ancestral houses, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and their officers who served the king in all the affairs of the divisions that rotated in and out month by month throughout the year, each division numbering twenty-four thousand men.
Jashobeam son of Zabdiel was over the first division for the first month, and his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
He was one of the sons of Perez and was chief of all the commanders of the army for the first month.
Dodai the Ahohite commanded the second division for the second month, and Mikloth was his chief officer; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest was chief of the third division for the third month; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
This Benaiah was a mighty man among the Thirty and their commander, and his son Ammizabad was over his division.
Joab, brother of Asahel, commanded the fourth division for the fourth month, and after him Zebadiah his son; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Shamhuth the Izrahite commanded the fifth division for the fifth month; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite commanded the sixth division for the sixth month; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Helez the Pelonite, one of the sons of Ephraim, commanded the seventh division for the seventh month; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites, commanded the eighth division for the eighth month; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Abiezer the Anathothite, of the Benjamites, commanded the ninth division for the ninth month; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zerahites, commanded the tenth division for the tenth month; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Benaiah the Pirathonite, one of the sons of Ephraim, commanded the eleventh division for the eleventh month; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel, commanded the twelfth division for the twelfth month; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
These were the leaders over the tribes of Israel: for Reuben, Eliezer son of Zichri was leader; for Simeon, Shephatiah son of Maacah.
For Levi, Hashabiah son of Kemuel; for Aaron, Zadok.
For Judah, Elihu, one of David's brothers; for Issachar, Omri son of Michael.
For Zebulun, Ishmaiah son of Obadiah; for Naphtali, Jerimoth son of Azriel.
For the sons of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Azaziah; for the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel son of Pedaiah.
For the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo son of Zechariah; for Benjamin, Jaasiel son of Abner.
For Dan, Azarel son of Jeroham. These were the leaders of the tribes of Israel.
David did not number those who were under twenty years of age, because the LORD had said that He would make Israel as numerous as the stars of heaven.
Joab son of Zeruiah began to count, but he did not finish, and wrath came upon Israel because of this; and the number was not recorded in the chronicles of King David.
Azmaveth son of Adiel was over the king's treasuries; Jonathan son of Uzziah was over the treasuries in the fields, in the cities, in the villages, and in the towers.
Ezri son of Chelub was over those who worked the fields for tilling the ground.
Shimei the Ramathite was over the vineyards; Zabdi the Shiphmite was over the wine in the storehouses.
Baal-hanan the Gederite was over the olive and sycamore trees in the Shephelah; Joash was over the oil stores.
Shitrai the Sharonite was over the cattle that grazed in Sharon; Shaphat son of Adlai was over the cattle in the valleys.
Obil the Ishmaelite was over the camels; Jehdeiah the Meronothite was over the donkeys.
Jaziz the Hagrite was over the flocks. All these were stewards of King David's property.
Jonathan, David's uncle, was a counselor, a man of understanding and a scribe; Jehiel son of Hachmoni was with the king's sons.
Ahithophel was counselor to the king; Hushai the Archite was the king's friend.
After Ahithophel came Jehoiada son of Benaiah and Abiathar; Joab was commander of the king's army.

David assembled all the officials of Israel in Jerusalem: the leaders of the tribes, the leaders of the divisions in royal service, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officials in charge of all the property and livestock of the king and his sons, together with the court officials, the mighty men, and all the valiant warriors.

King David rose to his feet and said, "Listen to me, my brothers and my people. I had set my heart on building a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and for the footstool of our God, and I made preparations for the building.
But God said to me, 'You are not to build a house for My Name, because you are a man of war and have shed blood.'

Yet the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me from all my father's house to be king over Israel forever. For He chose Judah as leader, and from the house of Judah, my father's house, and among my father's sons He was pleased to make me king over all Israel.
And of all my sons—for the LORD has given me many sons—He has chosen Solomon my son to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel.
He said to me, 'Solomon your son is the one who will build My house and My courts, for I have chosen him to be My son, and I will be his Father.'
I will establish his kingdom forever, if he is steadfast to keep My commandments and My ordinances, as he is today.

Now therefore, in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of the LORD, and in the hearing of our God, keep and seek out all the commandments of the LORD your God, so that you may possess this good land and leave it as an inheritance to your children after you forever.

And you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father, and serve Him with a whole heart and a willing mind; for the LORD searches all hearts and understands every intent of the thoughts. If you seek Him, He will be found by you; but if you forsake Him, He will reject you forever.
Consider now, for the LORD has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong and do it."
Then David gave his son Solomon the plans for the portico of the temple, its buildings, its storerooms, its upper rooms, its inner rooms, and the room for the mercy seat,

and the plans for all that he had by the Spirit: for the courts of the house of the LORD, for all the surrounding chambers, for the treasuries of the house of God, and for the treasuries of the dedicated things.
and for the divisions of the priests and Levites, and for all the work of the service of the house of the LORD, and for all the articles of service in the house of the LORD.
for the gold by weight for all the articles of gold for every kind of service, and for all the silver articles by weight for every kind of service.

and the weight of gold for the golden lampstands and their lamps, with the weight for each lampstand and its lamps; and the weight of silver for the silver lampstands, with the weight for each lampstand and its lamps, according to the service of each lampstand.
and the weight of gold for the tables of the showbread, and of silver for the tables of silver.
and the weight of pure gold for the forks, basins, and cups; and the weight of gold for the golden bowls, and the weight of silver for the silver bowls, by weight for each bowl.
and for the altar of incense, the weight of refined gold; and for the pattern of the chariot, the gold cherubim that spread their wings and cover the ark of the covenant of the LORD.
"All this," David said, "the LORD made me understand in writing by His hand upon me, all the details of the pattern."

And David said to Solomon his son, "Be strong and courageous, and do it. Do not be afraid or dismayed, for the LORD God, my God, is with you. He will not fail you or forsake you until all the work for the service of the house of the LORD is finished.

And behold, the divisions of the priests and Levites are ready for all the service of the house of God, and every willing man skilled in any craft will be with you in all the work; for all the officials and all the people are at your command."
King David said to the whole assembly, "My son Solomon, whom God has chosen, is young and tender, and the work is great; for the temple is not for man but for the the LORD God.

With all my strength I have prepared for the house of my God gold for gold, silver for silver, bronze for bronze, iron for iron, and wood for wood, together with onyx stones, stones for settings, turquoise and colored stones, every kind of precious stone, and marble stones in abundance.
Moreover, because I delight in the house of my God, I have a personal treasure of gold and silver that I have given to the house of my God, over and above all that I have prepared for the holy house.
Three thousand talents of gold, of the gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of refined silver, to overlay the walls of the houses.
Gold for gold and silver for silver, and for all the work to be done by the craftsmen. Who then is willing to consecrate himself to the the LORD today?"
Then the leaders of the ancestral houses, the leaders of the tribes of Israel, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the officials in charge of the king's work volunteered.

For the service of the house of God they gave five thousand talents and ten thousand darics of gold, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and one hundred thousand talents of iron.
Those who had precious stones gave them to the treasury of the house of the the LORD, under the care of Jehiel the Gershonite.
The people rejoiced because they had given willingly, with a whole heart; and King David also rejoiced with great joy.
David blessed the the LORD before the eyes of the whole assembly and said, "Blessed are You, the LORD God of our father Israel, from everlasting to everlasting.

Yours, O the LORD, are greatness and power and glory and victory and majesty, for all that is in heaven and on earth is Yours. Yours, O the LORD, is the kingdom, and You are exalted above all as head.
Riches and honor come from You, and You rule over all. In Your hand are power and might; in Your hand it is to make great and to give strength to all.
"And now, our God, we thank You and praise Your glorious name.
But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to offer willingly like this? For all things come from You, and of Your own we have given You.
For we are strangers and sojourners before You, as all our fathers were. Our days on earth are like a shadow, and there is no hope.
"O the LORD our God, all this abundance that we have prepared to build You a house for Your holy name comes from Your hand and is all Yours.

I know, my God, that You test the heart and take pleasure in uprightness. In the uprightness of my heart I have freely offered all these things; and now I have seen with joy Your people who are present here offering freely to You.
O the LORD, God of our fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, keep this forever in the thoughts of the hearts of Your people, and direct their hearts toward You.
And give to my son Solomon a whole heart to keep Your commandments, Your testimonies, and Your statutes, and to carry out all these things, and to build the temple that I have prepared."
Then David said to the whole assembly, "Bless the the LORD your God." And the whole assembly blessed the the LORD, the God of their fathers, and bowed down and worshiped the the LORD and the king.

The next day they offered sacrifices and burnt offerings to the the LORD—a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs, with their drink offerings—and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.

They ate and drank before the the LORD with great gladness on that day. Then they made Solomon the son of David king a second time, and they anointed him before the the LORD as leader, and Zadok as priest.
So Solomon sat on the throne of the the LORD as king in place of his father David; he prospered, and all Israel obeyed him.
All the leaders and mighty men, and also all the sons of King David, pledged their allegiance to King Solomon.
The LORD exalted Solomon greatly in the sight of all Israel and bestowed on him royal splendor such as no king over Israel had before him.
Thus David the son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.
The length of his reign over Israel was forty years: he reigned seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
He died at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor; and his son Solomon reigned in his place.
Now the acts of King David, from first to last, are written in the records of Samuel the seer, Nathan the prophet, and Gad the seer,
together with all his reign and his might, and the times that passed over him and over Israel and over all the kingdoms of the lands.
Solomon son of David consolidated his authority over the kingdom, and the the LORD his God was with him and elevated him to unparalleled greatness.
Then Solomon addressed all Israel—to the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges, and to every leader throughout Israel, the heads of the ancestral houses.
Solomon and the entire assembly went to the high place at Gibeon, because God’s Tent of Meeting was there, the one Moses, the servant of the the LORD, had constructed in the wilderness.
David had already brought the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim to the place he had prepared for it, having pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.
The bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, had made stood in Gibeon before the tabernacle of the the LORD; there Solomon and the assembly sought Him.
Solomon ascended to the bronze altar before the the LORD at the Tent of Meeting and offered a thousand burnt offerings upon it.
That night God appeared to Solomon and said, “Ask what you would have Me give you.”
Solomon answered God, “You have shown my father David great and faithful love, and You have established me as king in his place.
Now, the LORD my God, let Your promise to my father David be fulfilled, for You have made me king over a people as innumerable as the dust of the earth.
Grant me wisdom and knowledge, so that I may lead this people, for who can govern this great people of Yours?”

God said to Solomon, “Because this desire arose from your heart, and you did not ask for riches, wealth, honor, or the death of your enemies, nor did you ask for a long life, but you asked for wisdom and knowledge to govern My people over whom I have made you king—
therefore I will give you wisdom and knowledge. I will also give you riches, wealth, and honor, such as no king before you or after you has possessed.”
So Solomon returned to Jerusalem from the high place at Gibeon, from before the Tent of Meeting, and he reigned over Israel.
Solomon amassed chariots and horsemen; he had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, which he stationed in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stone, and cedar as plentiful as sycamore in the foothills.
Solomon’s horses were imported from Egypt and from Kue; the king’s merchants acquired them from Kue at the prevailing price.
They imported a chariot from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for one hundred fifty. They also exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Aram.
Solomon determined to build a temple for the Name of the LORD and a royal palace for himself.
He numbered seventy thousand men to carry loads, eighty thousand to quarry stone in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred to supervise them.
Solomon sent this message to Huram king of Tyre: "Just as you dealt with my father David, sending him cedar to build a house in which to live, please do the same now.

I am building a temple for the Name of the LORD my God, to dedicate it to Him, to burn incense before Him, to maintain the continual bread offering, and to present burnt offerings morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, at the new moons, and on the festivals of the LORD our God. This is a perpetual ordinance for Israel.
"The temple I am building will be great, because our God is greater than every other god.
Yet who can truly build a house for Him, when even the heavens—and the highest heavens—cannot contain Him? And who am I, that I should build a house for Him, except to burn incense before Him?

"Therefore send me a skilled craftsman who can work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, purple, crimson, and blue yarn, and who knows how to execute engraved designs. He will work with the skilled artisans already with me in Judah and Jerusalem, whom my father David appointed.
Also send me cedar, cypress, and algum timber from Lebanon, for I know your servants are skilled in cutting Lebanese timber. My servants will work alongside yours.
They will prepare timber in abundance for me, because the temple I am building will be great and extraordinary.
I will give your servants, the woodcutters, twenty thousand cors of ground wheat, twenty thousand cors of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil."
Huram king of Tyre replied in writing and sent it to Solomon: "Because The LORD has loved His people, He has made you king over them.

Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, and who has given King David a wise son endowed with discretion and understanding, to build a house for the LORD and a royal palace for himself.
"So now I am sending you Huram-abi, a skilled man endowed with understanding.

He is the son of a Danite woman and a Tyrian father, and he is skilled in working gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, wood, purple, blue, fine linen, and crimson. He can execute any engraved design and devise whatever plan is assigned to him. He will work with your skilled artisans and with those of my lord David, your father.
Now let my lord send his servants the wheat, barley, oil, and wine he mentioned.
We will cut as much timber from Lebanon as you need, float it by sea to Joppa, and you can transport it up to Jerusalem."
Solomon also took a census of all the foreigners residing in Israel, following the census his father David had taken, and found 153,600.
He assigned 70,000 as carriers, 80,000 as stonecutters in the mountains, and 3,600 as supervisors to direct the people's labor.

Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to his father David. This was the place David had prepared on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
He began building on the second day of the second month in the fourth year of his reign.
The foundation Solomon laid for building the house of God was sixty cubits long and twenty cubits wide, according to the old standard.
The portico at the front of the temple was twenty cubits long across the width of the building and one hundred twenty cubits high. He overlaid the inside with pure gold.
He paneled the main hall with cypress and covered it with fine gold, and adorned it with palm trees and chains.
He adorned the temple with precious stones for beauty, and its gold was gold of Parvaim.
He overlaid its beams, thresholds, walls, and doors with gold, and carved cherubim on the walls.
He built the Most Holy Place; its length corresponded to the width of the temple, twenty cubits, and its width was also twenty cubits. He overlaid it with six hundred talents of fine gold.
The weight of the gold nails was fifty shekels. He also overlaid the upper rooms with gold.
In the Most Holy Place he made two cherubim of sculptured work, and he overlaid them with gold.

The wingspan of the cherubim was twenty cubits. One wing of one cherub was five cubits long and touched the wall of the temple, and the other wing was five cubits long and touched the wing of the other cherub.
The wing of the other cherub was five cubits long and touched the wall of the temple, and its other wing was five cubits long and touched the wing of the first cherub.
The wings of these cherubim extended twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, and their faces were turned toward the main hall.
He made the veil of blue, purple, crimson, and fine linen, with cherubim woven into it.
In front of the temple he made two pillars, thirty-five cubits high, with a capital of five cubits on top of each.
He made interlocking chains and put them on top of the pillars. He made a hundred pomegranates and fastened them to the chains.
He set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right and one on the left. He named the pillar on the right Jachin and the pillar on the left Boaz.
Solomon made a bronze altar twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high.
He also made the Sea of cast metal, round, ten cubits from rim to rim, five cubits high, with a circumference of thirty cubits; a measuring line of thirty cubits encircled it.
Beneath it were figures of oxen all around, ten per cubit, completely surrounding the Sea; the oxen were cast in two rows when the Sea itself was cast.
The Sea stood on twelve oxen: three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east, with the Sea resting on them and all their hindquarters turned inward.
It was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was shaped like the rim of a cup, like a lily blossom; it could hold three thousand baths.
He made ten basins for washing and set five on the right and five on the left. In them they washed the articles used for the burnt offering, but the Sea was for the priests to wash in.
He made ten golden lampstands according to their prescribed pattern and placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left.
He made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left, and he made one hundred golden bowls.
He made the priests' courtyard, the great court, and doors for the court, and he overlaid their doors with bronze.
He set the Sea at the southeast corner, east of the south side.
Huram made the pots, shovels, and basins. Huram finished all the work he had done for King Solomon in the house of God.
He made the two pillars, the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars, and the two lattice networks covering the two bowls of the capitals on the pillars.
He also made four hundred pomegranates for the two networks—two rows of pomegranates on each network—to cover the two bowls of the capitals on the pillars.
He made the stands and the basins on the stands.
He made one Sea with the twelve oxen beneath it.
The pots, shovels, meat forks, and all their articles that Huram-abi made for King Solomon for the house of the the LORD were of polished bronze.
The king cast them in the plain of the Jordan, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.
Solomon made all these articles in such great abundance that the weight of the bronze could not be determined.
Solomon also made all the furnishings for the house of God: the golden altar; the tables for the bread of the Presence;
the lampstands with their lamps to burn before the inner sanctuary, according to the ordinance, of pure gold;
the flowers, the lamps, and the tongs, all of pure gold, and of the finest gold;
the snuffers, basins, spoons, and censers, of pure gold; and the entrance of the house, with its inner doors to the Most Holy Place, and the doors of the temple, were of gold.

Thus all the labor Solomon performed for the house of the LORD reached completion; moreover, Solomon brought in the sacred treasures of David his father—the silver, the gold, and all the vessels—and placed them in the treasuries of the house of God.

Then Solomon convened the elders of Israel, along with all the heads of the tribes and the leaders of the ancestral houses of the Israelites, in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the City of David, which is Zion.
All the men of Israel assembled before the king at the festival held in the seventh month.
When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the Levites lifted the ark.
They carried up the ark, the tent of meeting, and all the holy utensils that were in the tent; the Levitical priests brought them up.
King Solomon and the entire assembly of Israel, gathered before him at the ark, sacrificed sheep and oxen in such abundance that they could not be counted or numbered.
Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house—to the Most Holy Place—beneath the wings of the cherubim.
The cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark, and they covered the ark and its poles from above.
The poles were so long that their ends were visible from the front of the inner sanctuary, yet they could not be seen from outside; and they remain there to this day.
There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses had placed there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites when they came out of Egypt.
Now when the priests came out of the Holy Place—for all the priests who were present had consecrated themselves, without regard to their divisions—

and all the Levitical singers—Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and relatives—stood east of the altar, clothed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps, and lyres, together with one hundred twenty priests sounding trumpets,

in unison, as the trumpeters and singers made themselves heard with one voice in praising and thanking the LORD. When they lifted up their voice, accompanied by trumpets, cymbals, and other musical instruments, and when they praised the LORD, saying, “He indeed is good, for His lovingkindness endures forever,” then the house of the LORD was filled with a cloud.
Consequently, the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.
Then Solomon said, “The LORD has said that He would dwell in thick darkness.
But I have built You an exalted house, a place for You to dwell forever.”
Then the king turned around and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, while all the assembly of Israel was standing.
And he said, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who has fulfilled with His hands what He spoke with His mouth to my father David, saying,

‘Since the day I brought My people out of the land of Egypt, I have not chosen a city from any tribe of Israel in which to build a house for My Name to dwell, nor have I chosen any man to be ruler over My people Israel.
But now I have chosen Jerusalem for My Name to be there, and I have chosen David to be over My people Israel.’
Now it was in the heart of my father David to build a house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
But the LORD said to my father David, ‘Since it was in your heart to build a house for My Name, you did well to have this in your heart.
Nevertheless, you are not the one to build the house, but your son, your own offspring, will build the house for My Name.’

Now the LORD has fulfilled the word that He spoke. I have succeeded my father David and sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised. I have built the house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
There I have placed the ark, in which is the covenant of the LORD that He made with the sons of Israel.”
Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in front of the whole assembly of Israel and spread out his hands.

(Now Solomon had made a bronze platform five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high, and had placed it in the middle of the courtyard. He stood on it, then knelt down before the whole assembly of Israel, spread out his hands toward heaven,)
and said, “O the LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like You in heaven or on earth, keeping covenant and loving devotion to Your servants who walk before You with all their heart.
You have kept what You promised to Your servant David my father. You spoke with Your mouth and fulfilled with Your hand this day.

Now therefore, O the LORD, God of Israel, keep for Your servant David my father what You promised him when You said, ‘You will never fail to have a man to sit before Me on the throne of Israel, if only your sons guard their way to walk in My law as you have walked before Me.’
And now, O the LORD, God of Israel, let Your word be confirmed, which You spoke to Your servant David.
But will God indeed dwell with man on the earth? Behold, heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain You, how much less this house that I have built!
Yet regard the prayer of Your servant and his plea, O the LORD my God, to listen to the cry and the prayer that Your servant prays before You.
May Your eyes be open toward this house day and night, toward the place where You said You would put Your Name, to listen to the prayer that Your servant prays toward this place.
Hear the plea of Your servant and of Your people Israel when they pray toward this place. May You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, and when You hear, may You forgive.
“If a man sins against his neighbor and is required to take an oath, and he comes to take an oath before Your altar in this house,

then may You hear from heaven and act; may You judge Your servants, repaying the wicked by bringing his own conduct upon his head, and vindicating the righteous by rewarding him according to his righteousness.
If Your people Israel are defeated before an enemy because they have sinned against You, and they return to You and confess Your Name, praying and pleading before You in this house,
then may You hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your people Israel, and bring them back to the land You gave to them and to their fathers.
When the heavens are shut up and there is no rain because they have sinned against You, and they pray toward this place and confess Your Name, turning from their sin when You afflict them,

then may You hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your servants and Your people Israel, teaching them the good way in which they should walk, and send rain on Your land that You have given to Your people as an inheritance.
If there is famine in the land, or pestilence, blight, mildew, locusts, or grasshoppers; if their enemies besiege them in their cities; whatever plague or sickness may come—
then whatever prayer or plea is made by any man or by all Your people Israel, each knowing his own affliction and pain, and spreading out his hands toward this house—
may You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, and forgive and repay each man according to all his ways, since You know his heart (for You alone know the hearts of the sons of men),
so that they may fear You and walk in Your ways all the days they live in the land You gave to our fathers.

“And as for the foreigner who is not of Your people Israel but has come from a distant land because of Your great Name and Your mighty hand and Your outstretched arm—when he comes and prays toward this house,

may You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, and do according to all that the foreigner asks of You, so that all the peoples of the earth may know Your Name and fear You as Your people Israel do, and may know that this house I have built is called by Your Name.
When Your people go to war against their enemies, wherever You send them, and they pray to You toward this city You have chosen and toward this house I have built for Your Name,
then may You hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and may You uphold their cause.
If they sin against You—for there is no one who does not sin—and You become angry with them and deliver them to an enemy who takes them captive to a land far or near,

and if they come to their senses in the land where they are held captive, and they repent and plead with You in the land of their captivity, saying, ‘We have sinned; we have done wrong and acted wickedly,’

and if they return to You with all their heart and soul in the land of their captivity where they were taken, and if they pray toward the land You gave to their fathers, toward the city You have chosen, and toward the house I have built for Your Name,
then may You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, their prayer and their plea, and may You uphold their cause and forgive Your people who have sinned against You.
“Now, my God, may Your eyes be open and Your ears attentive to the prayer offered in this place.
Now arise, O the LORD God, and enter Your resting place, You and the ark of Your strength. May Your priests, O the LORD God, be clothed with salvation, and may Your godly ones rejoice in goodness.
O the LORD God, do not reject Your anointed. Remember Your loving devotion to Your servant David.”
When Solomon had finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple.
The priests could not enter the temple of the LORD, because the glory of the LORD had filled it.

When all the Israelites saw the fire coming down and the glory of the LORD above the temple, they knelt on the pavement with their faces to the ground, and they worshiped and gave thanks to the LORD, saying, "For He is good; His loving devotion endures forever."
Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the LORD.
King Solomon offered a sacrifice of 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep, so the king and all the people dedicated the temple of God.

The priests stood at their posts, and the Levites with the musical instruments of the LORD—which King David had made for giving thanks to the LORD and with which David had offered praise, saying, "His loving devotion endures forever"—stood opposite them. The priests sounded trumpets, and all Israel stood.

Then Solomon consecrated the middle of the courtyard in front of the temple of the LORD, for there he offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar he had made could not hold all these offerings.
So Solomon observed the feast at that time for seven days, along with all Israel—a very great assembly—people from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt.
On the eighth day they held a solemn assembly, for the dedication of the altar had lasted seven days, and the feast seven days.

On the twenty-third day of the seventh month, Solomon sent the people away to their homes, joyful and glad of heart for the good things the LORD had done for David, for Solomon, and for His people Israel.
When Solomon had finished the temple of the LORD and the royal palace, and had succeeded in all that he had planned to do,
The LORD appeared to him at night and said: "I have heard your prayer and have chosen this place for Myself as a house of sacrifice.
If I shut up the heavens so that there is no rain, or if I command the locust to devour the land, or if I send a plague among My people,
and if My people who are called by My name humble themselves and pray and seek My face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven and forgive their sin and heal their land.
Now My eyes will be open and My ears attentive to the prayer offered in this place.
For I have now chosen and consecrated this temple, so that My Name may be there forever. My eyes and My heart will be there for all time. "
And as for you, if you walk before Me as your father David walked, doing all I have commanded you, and if you keep My statutes and ordinances,
then I will establish your royal throne, as I covenanted with your father David when I said, 'You will never fail to have a man on the throne of Israel.' "
But if you turn away and forsake My statutes and commandments that I have set before you, and if you go and serve and worship other gods,
then I will uproot them from My land that I have given them, and I will reject this temple that I have consecrated for My Name. I will make it an object of scorn and ridicule among all the nations.
And though this temple is now exalted, all who pass by it will be appalled and will say, 'Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?'

And they will answer, 'Because they have forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and have embraced other gods, worshiping and serving them—that is why He has brought all this disaster upon them.'"
At the conclusion of twenty years—during which Solomon had constructed the house of the LORD and his own palace—
Solomon rebuilt the cities that Huram had given him and settled the Israelites in them.
He then campaigned against Hamath-zobah and subdued it.
He built Tadmor in the wilderness, together with all the store cities he had established in Hamath.
He fortified Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon, equipping them with walls, gates, and bars.

He also rebuilt Baalath and all the store cities belonging to Solomon, along with the chariot cities, the cavalry cities, and every other city he desired to build in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and throughout his dominion.
As for all the people who remained of the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—peoples not of Israelite descent—
namely, their descendants who remained in the land after them, whom the Israelites had not wholly destroyed—Solomon conscripted them into forced labor, and they remain so to this day.
Yet Solomon did not reduce any Israelite to slave labor for his projects, because they were warriors, officers of his elite guard, and commanders of his chariots and cavalry.
These were the two hundred fifty chief officers who supervised the people under King Solomon.

Solomon brought Pharaoh’s daughter up from the City of David to the house he had built for her, for he said, “My wife shall not live in the house of David, king of Israel, because the places to which the ark of the LORD has come are holy.”
Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of the LORD that he had built before the portico.

He offered them according to the daily requirement, as Moses had commanded, for the Sabbaths, the New Moons, and the three annual feasts—the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Tabernacles.

In accordance with the ordinance of his father David, he appointed the divisions of the priests for their service, the Levites for their duties of praise and ministry before the priests according to each day’s requirement, and the gatekeepers by their divisions at each gate; for this was the command of David, the man of God.
They did not depart from the king’s command in any matter concerning the priests and Levites, including the treasuries.
Thus all of Solomon’s work was accomplished, from the day the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid until it was completed. So the house of the LORD was finished.
Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and to Eloth on the seacoast in the land of Edom.

Huram sent him ships by the hand of his servants, along with servants who knew the sea; they sailed with Solomon’s servants to Ophir and brought back four hundred fifty talents of gold, which they delivered to King Solomon.

Upon hearing reports of Solomon’s renown, the queen of Sheba came to Jerusalem to test him with difficult questions. She arrived with an exceedingly large caravan—camels bearing spices, gold in abundance, and precious stones. She came to Solomon and discoursed with him concerning everything that occupied her mind.
Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was too difficult for him to explain to her.
When the queen of Sheba saw Solomon’s wisdom and the house that he had built,

together with the food of his table, the seating of his servants, the attendance of his ministers and their apparel, his cupbearers and their apparel, and his ascent by which he went up to the house of the the LORD, she had no more spirit in her.
She said to the king, “The report that I heard in my own country concerning your words and your wisdom was true.
I did not believe their reports until I came and saw with my own eyes; and behold, not even half of the greatness of your wisdom had been told to me. You have exceeded the report that I heard.
Happy are your men, and happy are these your servants, who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom.

Blessed be the the LORD your God, who has delighted in you and set you on His throne as king for the the LORD your God. Because of the love of your God for Israel, to establish them forever, He has made you king over them, to do justice and righteousness.”
She gave the king 120 talents of gold, a very great quantity of spices, and precious stones; never again were there such spices as those the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
Moreover, the servants of Hiram and the servants of Solomon, who brought gold from Ophir, also brought algum wood and precious stones.
The king made of the algum wood supports for the house of the the LORD and for the king’s house, and lyres and harps for the singers; such had never been seen before in the land of Judah.
King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all that she desired and requested, besides what she had brought to the king. Then she turned and went to her own country, she and her servants.
The weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was 666 talents,
besides that which came from the traders and merchants and all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land, who brought gold and silver to Solomon.
King Solomon made 200 large shields of beaten gold; 600 shekels of beaten gold went into each shield.
He also made 300 small shields of beaten gold; 300 shekels of gold went into each shield. The king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
The king made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with pure gold.
The throne had six steps, and a footstool of gold attached to the throne, with arms on each side by the seat, and two lions standing beside the arms.
Twelve lions stood there on the six steps, six on each side. Nothing like this was made for any other kingdom.
All King Solomon’s drinking vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were of pure gold; silver was considered as nothing in the days of Solomon.
For the king’s ships went to Tarshish with the servants of Hiram; once every three years the ships of Tarshish came, bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
So King Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom.
All the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon to hear his wisdom, which God had put into his heart.
Each brought his tribute: articles of silver and gold, garments, weapons, spices, horses, and mules, year by year.
Solomon had 4,000 stalls for horses and chariots, and 12,000 horsemen, and he stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
He ruled over all the kings from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt.
The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as plentiful as sycamore in the lowland.
Horses were imported for Solomon from Egypt and from all lands.

Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, from first to last, are they not written in the records of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam the son of Nebat?
Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.
Then Solomon slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David his father; and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.
Rehoboam traveled to Shechem, because all Israel had assembled there to install him as king.
When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of it—he was still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon—he returned from Egypt.
Then the people sent for Jeroboam and brought him before Rehoboam, and Jeroboam and all Israel spoke to Rehoboam, saying:
“Your father imposed an oppressive yoke upon us. Now lighten the severe labor and the heavy burden that he placed on us, and we will serve you.”
Rehoboam replied, “Return to me in three days.” So the people departed.
King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had attended his father Solomon during his lifetime and asked, “How do you advise me to answer this people?”
They replied, “If today you become a servant to this people and serve them, speaking kindly to them, they will remain your servants forever.”
But Rehoboam rejected the elders’ counsel and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and now served him.
He asked them, “What counsel do you offer? How should we answer these people who say to me, ‘Lighten the yoke your father placed on us’?”
The young men who had grown up with him replied, “Tell this people who said to you, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you should lighten it for us,’ this: ‘I am far more severe than my father.
My father burdened you with a heavy yoke, yet I will increase your burden. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with far harsher blows.’”
Three days later, Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam, just as the king had said, “Come back to me in three days.”
The king answered them harshly, for he had rejected the elders’ counsel.

Instead, he spoke to them according to the young men’s advice: “My father made your yoke heavy, but I will make it heavier. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with far harsher blows.”
So the king did not heed the people, because this turn of events was from God, to fulfill the word that the LORD had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.

When all Israel saw that the king refused to listen to them, they answered him: “What share do we have in David? What inheritance in the son of Jesse? Go to your homes, Israel! Look after your own house, David!” Then all the people of Israel returned to their homes.
Yet Rehoboam continued to reign over the Israelites who lived in the towns of Judah.
King Rehoboam sent out Hadoram, who was in charge of forced labor, but all Israel stoned him to death. King Rehoboam, however, managed to mount his chariot and flee to Jerusalem.
So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.
When Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he assembled the house of Judah and Benjamin—one hundred eighty thousand chosen warriors—to fight against Israel and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam.
Then the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God:
"Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin,

'Thus says the LORD: You shall not go up or fight against your brothers. Let every man return to his house, for this matter is from Me.'" So they listened to the words of the LORD and turned back from marching against Jeroboam.
Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem and built cities for defense in Judah.
Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron—the fortified cities of Judah and Benjamin.
He strengthened the fortresses, placed commanders in them, and stored food, oil, and wine there.
He also put shields and spears in every city and strengthened them greatly. Thus Judah and Benjamin remained under his rule.
Meanwhile, the priests and Levites throughout Israel stood with Rehoboam, coming to him from all their districts.
For the Levites had left their pasturelands and holdings and gone to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons had rejected them from serving as priests to the LORD.
Jeroboam had appointed his own priests for the high places, for the goat idols, and for the calves he had made.
People from every tribe of Israel who set their hearts to seek the LORD, the God of Israel, followed them to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
They strengthened the kingdom of Judah and supported Rehoboam son of Solomon for three years, because during those three years they walked in the way of David and Solomon.
Rehoboam married Mahalath, daughter of Jerimoth son of David, and Abihail, daughter of Eliab son of Jesse.
She bore him sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
After her, he took Maacah daughter of Absalom, who bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
Rehoboam loved Maacah daughter of Absalom more than all his other wives and concubines; in all he had eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and he fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
He appointed Abijah son of Maacah as chief prince among his brothers, intending to make him king.
Acting wisely, he dispersed some of his sons throughout the territories of Judah and Benjamin, to every fortified city, providing them with abundant supplies and seeking wives for them.
When Rehoboam had established his kingdom and strengthened himself, with all Israel standing beside him, he abandoned the Law of the the LORD.
In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, because they had been unfaithful to the the LORD, Shishak king of Egypt marched against Jerusalem—
with twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen, and an innumerable host of Libyans, Sukkiites, and Cushites who had come with him from Egypt.
He captured the fortified cities of Judah and advanced as far as Jerusalem.

Then Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and to the leaders of Judah who had assembled at Jerusalem because of Shishak, and he said to them, "This is what the the LORD says: 'You have abandoned Me, so I have abandoned you to Shishak.'"
The leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, "The LORD is righteous."

When the the LORD saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of the the LORD came to Shemaiah: "They have humbled themselves; I will not destroy them, but I will grant them a little deliverance, and My wrath will not be poured out upon Jerusalem by Shishak.
Nevertheless, they will become his servants, so that they may learn the difference between serving Me and serving the kingdoms of other lands."

So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem and took the treasures of the house of the the LORD and the treasures of the king's house. He took everything, including the gold shields that Solomon had made.
King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place and entrusted them to the commanders of the guard who kept watch at the entrance of the king's house.
Whenever the king entered the house of the the LORD, the guard would carry the shields and then return them to the guardroom.
When he humbled himself, the wrath of the the LORD turned from him, so that he was not destroyed completely; and conditions in Judah were favorable.

King Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem and reigned. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that the the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put His name there. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonitess.
He did evil, for he did not set his heart to seek the the LORD.

Now the acts of Rehoboam, first and last, are they not written in the records of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer concerning genealogies? And there were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam throughout all his days.
Rehoboam rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David. Abijah his son reigned in his place.
In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah became king over Judah.
He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother was Micaiah, the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
Abijah went into battle with an army of four hundred thousand chosen men, valiant warriors; Jeroboam drew up in battle against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, mighty warriors.
Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim in the hill country of Ephraim and said, "Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel.
Do you not know that the LORD, the God of Israel, gave the kingdom to David and to his sons forever by an everlasting covenant?
Yet Jeroboam son of Nebat, servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his master.
Worthless scoundrels gathered to him and strengthened themselves against Rehoboam son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and tenderhearted and could not withstand them.
And now you intend to withstand the kingdom of the LORD in the hand of David's sons. You are a great multitude, and with you are the golden calves that Jeroboam made for you as gods. "

Have you not driven out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron and the Levites, and made priests for yourselves like the peoples of other lands? Whoever comes to consecrate himself with a young bull and seven rams may become a priest of things that are not gods.
But as for us, the LORD is our God, and we have not forsaken Him. The priests who minister to the LORD are the sons of Aaron and the Levites, and they are at their work.

They burn to the LORD every morning and evening burnt offerings and fragrant incense; they set the rows of bread on the pure table; and they tend the golden lampstand with its lamps every evening. For we keep the charge of the LORD our God, but you have forsaken Him.
Behold, God is with us at our head, and His priests with trumpets to sound the alarm against you. O sons of Israel, do not fight against the LORD, the God of your fathers, for you will not prosper."
Jeroboam had sent an ambush around to come behind Judah, so that the Israelites stood before Judah and the ambush behind them.
When Judah looked around, the battle was before and behind them; they cried out to the LORD, and the priests blew the trumpets.
Then the men of Judah raised a shout; and as they shouted, God struck Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.
The sons of Israel fled before Judah, and God gave them into their hand.
Abijah and his people struck them with a great blow: five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel fell slain.
Thus the sons of Israel were subdued at that time, and the sons of Judah prevailed, because they relied on the LORD, the God of their fathers.
Abijah pursued Jeroboam and captured cities from him: Bethel with its villages, Jeshanah with its villages, and Ephron with its villages.
Jeroboam did not recover strength again in the days of Abijah; the LORD struck him, and he died.
Abijah grew strong, took fourteen wives, and fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
The rest of the acts of Abijah—his ways and his words—are written in the commentary of the prophet Iddo.
Abijah died and was interred with his ancestors in the City of David; his son Asa ascended the throne in his place, and throughout his reign the land enjoyed a decade of peace.
Asa did what was good and right in the sight of the LORD his God.
He eradicated the foreign altars and the high places, shattered the sacred pillars, and hewed down the Asherah poles.
He charged Judah to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, and to observe the law and the commandment.
He removed the high places and the incense altars from every city in Judah, and the kingdom remained tranquil under his rule.
Because the land was at rest, he fortified cities throughout Judah during those years; no war threatened him, for the LORD had granted him rest.

He urged Judah, “Let us build these cities and encircle them with walls, towers, doors, and bars. The land is still ours, for we have sought the LORD our God; we have sought Him, and He has granted us rest on every side.” Thus they built and prospered.

Asa mustered an army of three hundred thousand men from Judah, equipped with shields and spears, and two hundred eighty thousand from Benjamin, equipped with shields and bows; all were valiant warriors.
Zerah the Cushite marched against them with an army of one million men and three hundred chariots, advancing as far as Mareshah.
Asa went out to confront him, and they drew up battle lines in the Valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.

Asa cried out to the LORD his God: “LORD, it is as easy for You to help the powerless as the mighty. Help us, O LORD our God, for we rely on You, and in Your name we have come against this multitude. O LORD, You are our God; do not let mortal man prevail against You.”
The LORD struck down the Cushites before Asa and Judah, and they fled.
Asa and his people pursued them to Gerar. The Cushites collapsed until none could recover, for they were crushed before the LORD and before His army. They seized an enormous quantity of plunder.
They assaulted every city surrounding Gerar, because the terror of the LORD had fallen upon them, and they plundered all the cities, for the spoil was great.
They also attacked the tents of the herdsmen, carrying off sheep and camels in abundance, and then returned to Jerusalem.
The Spirit of God came upon Azariah son of Oded.

He went out to meet Asa and said, “Listen to me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin: the LORD is with you when you are with Him; if you seek Him, He will be found by you; but if you forsake Him, He will forsake you.
“For many days Israel had been without the true God, without a teaching priest, and without the law.
But in their distress they turned to the LORD, the God of Israel, and sought Him, and He was found by them.
In those times there was no peace for anyone who went out or came in, because great turmoil was upon all the inhabitants of the lands.
Nation rose against nation, and city against city, for God troubled them with every calamity.
But as for you, be strong and do not let your hands grow weak, for your work will be rewarded.”

When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage and removed the detestable things from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim; and he renewed the altar of the LORD that was before the porch of the LORD.

He gathered all Judah and Benjamin, together with those from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who were staying with them, for many from Israel had defected to him when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
They assembled at Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa’s reign.
On that day they sacrificed to the LORD seven hundred bulls and seven thousand sheep from the plunder they had brought.
They entered into a covenant to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and all their soul.
Whoever would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel, was to be put to death, whether small or great, man or woman.
They swore to the LORD with a loud voice, with shouting, and with trumpets and horns.
All Judah rejoiced over the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart and sought Him with all their desire; and He was found by them, and the LORD gave them rest on every side.
King Asa also removed Maacah his mother from being queen mother, because she had made an abominable image for Asherah; Asa cut down her image, crushed it, and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
The high places, however, were not removed from Israel; nevertheless Asa’s heart was wholly devoted to the LORD all his days.
He brought into the house of God the things his father had dedicated and his own dedicated things—silver, gold, and vessels.
There was no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa’s reign.
In the thirty-sixth year of Asa’s reign, Baasha, king of Israel, marched up against Judah and fortified Ramah, so that no one could leave or enter the territory of Asa, king of Judah.
Asa then took silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the the LORD and from the royal palace, and he sent them to Ben-Hadad, king of Aram, who lived in Damascus, with this message:

“There is a treaty between me and you, and between my father and your father. Look, I have sent you silver and gold. Go and break your treaty with Baasha, king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me.”
Ben-Hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel. They struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and all the store cities of Naphtali.
When Baasha heard of it, he stopped building Ramah and abandoned his work.
Then King Asa gathered all Judah, and they carried away the stones and timber of Ramah that Baasha had been using. With them Asa built Geba and Mizpah.

At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa, king of Judah, and said to him, “Because you relied on the king of Aram and did not rely on the the LORD your God, the army of the king of Aram has escaped your hand.
Were not the Cushites and Libyans a vast army with very many chariots and horsemen? Yet when you relied on the the LORD, He gave them into your hand.
For the eyes of the the LORD range throughout the earth to strengthen those whose hearts are fully devoted to Him. You have acted foolishly in this; from now on you will be at war.”
Asa was enraged with the seer and imprisoned him, for he was furious with him over this matter. Asa also oppressed some of the people at that time.
The acts of Asa, from first to last, are recorded in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
In the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa became diseased in his feet, and the disease was severe. Yet even in his illness he did not seek the the LORD, but physicians.
Asa died in the forty-first year of his reign and was gathered to his fathers.
