They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah. This is the number of the men of the people of Israel:
the descendants of Pahath-moab, through the lines of Jeshua and Joab, 2,812;
the descendants of Ater, through Hezekiah, 98;
the people of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, 743;
the people of Ramah and Geba, 621;
The people of Bethel and Ai, 223;
the descendants of the other Elam, 1,254;
the people of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, 725;
The priests: the descendants of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, 973;
The Levites: the descendants of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the house of Hodaviah, 74.
The singers: the descendants of Asaph, 128.
The gatekeepers: the descendants of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai, 139 in all.
The temple servants: the descendants of Ziha, Hasupha, and Tabbaoth;
the descendants of Keros, Siaha, and Padon;
the descendants of Lebanah, Hagabah, and Akkub;
the descendants of Hagab, Shamlai, and Hanan;
the descendants of Giddel, Gahar, and Reaiah;
the descendants of Rezin, Nekoda, and Gazzam;
the descendants of Uzza, Paseah, and Besai;
the descendants of Asnah, Meunim, and Nephusim;
the descendants of Bakbuk, Hakupha, and Harhur;
the descendants of Bazluth, Mehida, and Harsha;
the descendants of Barkos, Sisera, and Temah;
the descendants of Neziah and Hatipha.
The descendants of Solomon's servants: the descendants of Sotai, Hasophereth, and Peruda;
the descendants of Jaalah, Darkon, and Giddel;
the descendants of Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth-hazzebaim, and Ami.
The temple servants and the descendants of Solomon's servants totaled 392.
These are the people who came up from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Cherub, Addan, and Immer, but could not prove their fathers' houses or their descent, whether they belonged to Israel:
the descendants of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda, 652.
And from among the priests: the descendants of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai, who had taken a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
These sought their genealogical records, but they were not found; therefore they were excluded from the priesthood as unclean.
The governor told them that they must not eat of the most holy things until a priest should stand with Urim and Thummim.
The whole assembly, taken together, numbered 42,360,
besides their 7,337 male and female servants; and they had 200 singing men and singing women.
When they reached the House of the LORD in Jerusalem, some of the heads of the fathers' houses gave freewill offerings to rebuild the house of God on its foundation.
According to their means, they gave to the treasury for the work 61,000 gold darics, 5,000 minas of silver, and 100 priestly garments.
So the priests, the Levites, some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants lived in their own towns, and all Israel in their towns.
In the seventh month, after the Israelites had settled in their towns, the people congregated in Jerusalem in unanimous accord.

Then Jeshua son of Jozadak, together with his fellow priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, together with his relatives, rose and constructed the altar of the God of Israel, so that they might present burnt offerings upon it, as prescribed in the Law of Moses, the man of God.

They established the altar upon its foundations, although they remained apprehensive of the peoples of the surrounding lands, and they offered burnt offerings upon it to the LORD—burnt offerings each morning and evening.
They also observed the Feast of Tabernacles, as it is written, presenting the daily burnt offerings in their prescribed number, according to the ordinance governing each day.

Thereafter they offered the continual burnt offering, together with the offerings for the new moons and all the LORD’s consecrated appointed feasts, as well as every freewill offering presented to the LORD.
From the first day of the seventh month they began offering burnt offerings to the LORD, although the temple of the LORD had not yet been founded.

They also disbursed money to the masons and carpenters, and furnished food, drink, and oil to the Sidonians and Tyrians, so that cedar logs might be transported from Lebanon to the sea at Joppa, in accordance with the authorization granted by Cyrus king of Persia.

In the second month of the second year after their arrival at the house of God in Jerusalem, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Jeshua son of Jozadak, and the remainder of their brothers—the priests and Levites—and all who had returned from exile to Jerusalem began the work; and they appointed the Levites, from twenty years of age and older, to supervise the work of the house of the LORD.

Jeshua, with his sons and brothers, and Kadmiel, with his sons—the descendants of Judah—together with the sons of Henadad and their sons and brothers, the Levites, stood united to direct the workmen in the house of God.

When the builders laid the foundation of the temple of the LORD, the priests stood in their vestments with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise the LORD according to the ordinance of David king of Israel.

They sang responsively, praising and giving thanks to the LORD, for He is good and His loving devotion endures forever toward Israel. All the people shouted with a great shout as they praised the LORD, because the foundation of the house of the LORD had been laid.

Yet many of the priests, Levites, and heads of ancestral houses—older men who had seen the first temple—wept aloud when this temple’s foundation was laid before their eyes, while many others shouted for joy.
The people could not distinguish the sound of the joyful shout from the sound of the weeping, for the people shouted with a great shout, and the sound was heard from afar.
Now when the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the returned exiles were building a temple to the LORD, the God of Israel,

they approached Zerubbabel and the heads of the fathers' houses and said to them, "Let us build with you, for we worship your God as you do, and we have been sacrificing to Him since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us here."

But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the rest of the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel said to them, "You have nothing to do with us in building a house to our God; but we alone will build to the LORD, the God of Israel, as King Cyrus, the king of Persia, has commanded us."
Then the people of the land discouraged the people of Judah and made them afraid to build,
and they bribed counselors against them to frustrate their purpose, all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius king of Persia.
In the beginning of the reign of Ahasuerus they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.
In the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of their associates wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia. The letter was written in Aramaic and translated.
Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king as follows:

Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates—the judges, the governors, the officials, the Persians, the men of Erech, the Babylonians, the men of Susa, that is, the Elamites—
and the rest of the nations whom the great and noble Asnappar deported and settled in the cities of Samaria and in the rest of the province Beyond the River. And now
this is a copy of the letter that they sent to him: "To Artaxerxes the king: Your servants, the men of the province Beyond the River, send greeting.

Be it known to the king that the Jews who came up from you to us have gone to Jerusalem. They are rebuilding that rebellious and wicked city. They are finishing the walls and repairing the foundations.
Now be it known to the king that if this city is rebuilt and the walls finished, they will not pay tribute, custom, or toll, and the royal revenue will be impaired.
Now because we are in the service of the palace, and it is not fitting for us to see the king's dishonor, therefore we send and inform the king.

So that a search may be made in the book of the records of your fathers; You will find in the book of the records and learn that this city is a rebellious city, hurtful to kings and provinces, and that sedition was committed in it from of old. That is why this city was laid waste.
We inform the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls finished, you will have no portion in the province Beyond the River."
The king sent an answer: "To Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe and the rest of their associates who live in Samaria and in the rest of the province Beyond the River, greeting. And now
the letter that you sent to us has been plainly read before me.
And I made a decree, and search has been made, and it has been found that this city from of old has made insurrection against kings, and that rebellion and sedition have been made in it.
And mighty kings have been over Jerusalem, who ruled over the whole province Beyond the River, to whom tribute, custom, and toll were paid.
Therefore make a decree that these men be made to cease, and that this city be not rebuilt, until a command is given by me.
And take care not to be slack in this matter. Why should damage grow to the hurt of the kings?"
Then, when the copy of King Artaxerxes' letter was read before Rehum and Shimshai the scribe and their associates, they went in haste to the Jews at Jerusalem and by force and power made them cease.
Then the work on the house of God that is in Jerusalem stopped, and it ceased until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
The prophets Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo prophesied to the Jews living in Judah and Jerusalem, speaking in the name of the God of Israel.
Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak arose and began to rebuild the house of God in Jerusalem, while the prophets of God stood with them and supported them.

At that time Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai, together with their associates, came to them and asked, “Who issued you a decree to build this house and finish this structure?”
They also asked them, “What are the names of the men who are building this building?”
Yet the eye of their God was upon the elders of the Jews, so they did not stop them until a report was sent to Darius and an answer returned concerning the matter.
This is a copy of the letter that Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and his associates—the officials in the province Beyond the River—sent to King Darius.
They sent him a report written as follows: “To King Darius: May you enjoy complete peace and prosperity.

Let it be known to the king that we went to the province of Judah, to the house of the great God. It is being built with massive stones, and timber is being fitted into the walls. The work is proceeding diligently and prospering in their hands. “
Then we asked those elders and said to them, ‘Who issued you a decree to build this house and finish this structure?’
We also asked them their names, so that we might inform you and write down the names of the men who lead them. “
And this is the answer they gave us: ‘We are servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are rebuilding the house that was built many years ago, which a great king of Israel built and completed.

But because our fathers provoked the God of heaven to anger, He gave them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean, who destroyed this house and carried the people away to Babylon.
However, in the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon, King Cyrus issued a decree to rebuild this house of God.

Moreover, the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem and brought to the temple in Babylon, King Cyrus took from the temple in Babylon and entrusted to a man named Sheshbazzar, whom he had appointed governor.
And he said to him, “Take these vessels, go and place them in the temple in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be rebuilt on its original site.”
Then this Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the house of God in Jerusalem, and from that time until now it has been under construction and is not yet finished.’ “

Now therefore, if it pleases the king, let a search be made in the royal archives in Babylon to see whether King Cyrus issued a decree to rebuild this house of God in Jerusalem. Then let the king send us his decision concerning this matter.”
Then King Darius issued a decree, and a search was made in the house of the archives, where the treasures were stored in Babylon.
A scroll was found in the fortress at Ecbatana in the province of Media, and this was written in it: a memorandum.

In the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus issued a decree concerning the house of God in Jerusalem: let the house be built, the place where sacrifices are offered, and let its foundations be firmly laid. Its height shall be sixty cubits and its width sixty cubits,
with three courses of large stones and one course of new timber. Let the cost be paid from the royal treasury.

Moreover, let the gold and silver articles of the house of God that Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon be returned and brought back to the temple in Jerusalem, to their proper places, and let them be placed in the house of God.
Now, Tattenai, governor of the province beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and your associates, the Apharsachites who are beyond the River—you must stay far away from that place.
Leave the work on this house of God alone. Let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews build this house of God on its site.

Moreover, I issue a decree concerning what you are to do for these elders of the Jews in building this house of God: the full cost is to be paid to these men from the royal revenue, from the tribute of the province beyond the River, so that the work is not interrupted.

Whatever they need—young bulls, rams, and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, together with wheat, salt, wine, and oil, according to the requirement of the priests in Jerusalem—is to be given to them day by day without fail,
so that they may offer pleasing sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons.
Furthermore, I have issued a decree that if anyone alters this edict, a beam shall be pulled from his house, and he shall be impaled on it; and his house shall be made a refuse heap because of this.

May the God who has caused His name to dwell there overthrow every king and people who lifts a hand to alter this or to destroy this house of God in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued this decree; let it be carried out with diligence.
Then Tattenai, governor of the province beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates carried out the decree of King Darius with all diligence.

The elders of the Jews built and prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo. They finished the building according to the command of the God of Israel and according to the decrees of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
This temple was completed on the third day of the month Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.
Then the people of Israel—the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the exiles—celebrated the dedication of this house of God with joy.

For the dedication of this house of God they offered one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and, as a sin offering for all Israel, twelve male goats, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
They also appointed the priests to their divisions and the Levites to their courses for the service of God in Jerusalem, as it is written in the Book of Moses.
On the fourteenth day of the first month, the exiles celebrated the Passover.
For the priests and Levites had purified themselves together; all of them were clean. They slaughtered the Passover lamb for all the exiles, for their fellow priests, and for themselves.

The Israelites who had returned from exile ate the Passover, together with all who had separated themselves from the uncleanness of the nations of the land in order to seek the LORD, the God of Israel.

For seven days they celebrated the Feast of Unleavened Bread with joy, because the LORD had made them joyful and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them, to strengthen their hands in the work on the house of God, the God of Israel.
After these events, during the reign of Artaxerxes, king of Persia, Ezra—son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,
son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,
son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,
son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the chief priest—
came up from Babylon. He was a scribe skilled in the Law of Moses, which the LORD, the God of Israel, had given; and the king granted him every request, because the LORD his God favored him.
In the seventh year of King Artaxerxes, some Israelites—priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants—also ascended to Jerusalem.
Ezra reached Jerusalem in the fifth month of the king's seventh year.
He had departed from Babylon on the first day of the first month and arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month, because his God graciously prospered his journey.
For Ezra had resolved to study the Law of the LORD, to practice it, and to teach its statutes and ordinances throughout Israel.
The following is a copy of the letter that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe, a scribe of the LORD's commandments and statutes for Israel:
"Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, scribe of the Law of the God of heaven: Greetings.
I decree that all people in my realm from Israel, including their priests and Levites, who willingly choose to go to Jerusalem may travel with you.
For you are sent by the king and his seven counselors to investigate Judah and Jerusalem according to the Law of your God, which you are authorized to administer,
and to transport the silver and gold that the king and his counselors have freely contributed to the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem,
together with all the silver and gold you may locate throughout the province of Babylon, as well as the freewill offerings of the people and priests for the house of their God in Jerusalem.
"With this money you shall diligently purchase bulls, rams, and lambs, along with their grain and drink offerings, and present them on the altar of the house of your God in Jerusalem.
You and your brothers may do whatever seems best to you with the remaining silver and gold, according to the will of your God.
Deliver to the God of Jerusalem the vessels entrusted to you for service in the house of your God.
Provide from the royal treasury whatever else the house of your God requires.
I, King Artaxerxes, decree to all treasurers in the province Beyond the River that whatever Ezra the priest, scribe of the Law of the God of heaven, requests from you, you must supply without delay,
up to one hundred talents of silver, one hundred cors of wheat, one hundred baths of wine, one hundred baths of oil, and salt without limit.
"Whatever the God of heaven commands shall be carried out diligently for the house of the God of heaven, lest wrath befall the kingdom of the king and his sons.
We also notify you that no tribute, tax, or toll may be levied on any priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, temple servants, or other servants of this house of God.

And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom your God has granted you, appoint magistrates and judges to judge all the people in the province Beyond the River—all who know the laws of your God—and instruct those who do not.
Whoever refuses to obey the Law of your God and the law of the king shall be punished promptly, whether by death, exile, confiscation of property, or imprisonment."
Blessed be the LORD, the God of our fathers, who put such a purpose into the king's heart to glorify the house of the LORD in Jerusalem,
and who extended His lovingkindness to me before the king, his counselors, and all the king's mighty men. I was strengthened and gathered the leaders of Israel to accompany me.
These are the heads of their ancestral houses and the genealogical records of those who went up with me from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes.
From the sons of Phinehas: Gershom. From the sons of Ithamar: Daniel. From the sons of David: Hattush.
From the sons of Shecaniah, namely from the sons of Parosh: Zechariah, with whom one hundred fifty men were registered.
From the sons of Pahath-moab: Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, with two hundred men.
From the sons of Shecaniah son of Jahaziel: three hundred men.
From the sons of Adin: Ebed son of Jonathan, with fifty men.
From the sons of Elam: Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, with seventy men.
From the sons of Shephatiah: Zebadiah son of Michael, with eighty men.
From the sons of Joab: Obadiah son of Jehiel, with two hundred eighteen men.
From the sons of Shelomith son of Josiphiah: one hundred sixty men.
From the sons of Bebai: Zechariah son of Bebai, with twenty-eight men.
From the sons of Azgad: Johanan son of Hakkatan, with one hundred ten men.
From the last sons of Adonikam, whose names were Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah, with sixty men.
From the sons of Bigvai: Uthai and Zabbud, with seventy men.
I assembled them at the river that flows to Ahava, and we encamped there for three days. When I examined the people and the priests, I found that no Levites were among them.
So I sent for the leaders Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam, and for Joiarib and Elnathan, men of discernment.

I dispatched them to Iddo, the chief at Casiphia, and I instructed them what to say to Iddo and his relatives, the temple servants at Casiphia, so that they might bring us ministers for the house of our God.
Because the good hand of our God was upon us, they brought us a man of understanding from the sons of Mahli son of Levi son of Israel—Sherebiah—together with his sons and brothers, eighteen in all.
They also brought Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari, along with his relatives and their sons, twenty in all.
From the temple servants, whom David and the officials had appointed to assist the Levites, came two hundred twenty, all designated by name.
There, at the river Ahava, I proclaimed a fast, that we might humble ourselves before our God and seek from Him a straight way for ourselves, our children, and all our possessions.

For I was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen to protect us from enemies on the road, because we had said to the king, "The hand of our God is for good upon all who seek Him, but His power and His wrath are against all who forsake Him."
So we fasted and petitioned our God concerning this, and He answered our plea.

Then I set apart twelve of the leading priests—Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brothers—and weighed out to them the silver, the gold, and the vessels, the offering that the king, his counselors, his officials, and all Israel present had contributed for the house of our God.
I weighed into their hands six hundred fifty talents of silver, silver articles weighing one hundred talents, and one hundred talents of gold,
along with twenty gold basins valued at a thousand darics and two vessels of fine bronze, precious as gold.
Then I said to them, "You are holy to the the LORD, and the vessels are holy, and the silver and the gold are a freewill offering to the the LORD, the God of your fathers.
Guard them carefully until you weigh them out in the storerooms of the house of the the LORD in Jerusalem, before the chief priests, the Levites, and the leaders of the fathers' houses of Israel."
So the priests and the Levites received the silver, the gold, and the vessels by weight, to bring them to Jerusalem, to the house of our God.

Then we departed from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month, to go to Jerusalem. The hand of our God was upon us, and He delivered us from the hand of the enemy and from ambush along the way.
We came to Jerusalem and remained there three days.

On the fourth day, the silver, the gold, and the vessels were weighed in the house of our God into the hands of Meremoth son of Uriah the priest; with him were Eleazar son of Phinehas, and with them Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui, the Levites.
Everything was accounted for by number and by weight, and the total weight was recorded at that time.

The exiles who had returned from captivity offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering. All of this was a burnt offering to the the LORD.
They also delivered the king's decrees to the royal satraps and to the governors of the province beyond the River, and these officials supported the people and the house of God.

Now when these things had been completed, the leaders approached me, saying, “The people of Israel, along with the priests and Levites, have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands with respect to their abominations—the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.”

For they have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and for their sons, so that the holy seed has been mixed with the peoples of the lands; indeed, the leaders and officials have been foremost in this unfaithfulness.
When I heard this report, I tore my tunic and my cloak, pulled hair from my head and my beard, and sat down, utterly appalled.
Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered to me because of the unfaithfulness of the exiles, while I sat appalled until the evening offering.
At the evening offering I arose from my fasting, with my tunic and cloak torn, fell upon my knees, and spread out my hands to the LORD my God;
and I said, “O my God, I am too ashamed and humiliated to lift up my face to You, my God, for our iniquities have risen above our heads, and our guilt has mounted up to the heavens.

“From the days of our fathers until this day we have been in great guilt; and because of our iniquities we, our kings, and our priests have been delivered into the hand of the kings of the lands—to the sword, to captivity, to plunder, and to public disgrace—as we are this day.

“But now, for a brief moment, grace has been shown by the LORD our God, leaving us a remnant and giving us a secure foothold in His holy place, so that our God may refresh us and grant us a little reviving in our bondage.

“For we are slaves; yet our God has not forsaken us in our slavery, but has extended lovingkindness to us before the kings of Persia, to give us reviving, to raise up the house of our God, to repair its ruins, and to give us a protective wall in Judah and Jerusalem.
“And now, O our God, what can we say after this? For we have forsaken Your commandments,

which You commanded through Your servants the prophets, saying, ‘The land that you are entering to possess is an unclean land because of the uncleanness of the peoples of the lands, because of their abominations with which they have filled it from one end to the other with their impurity.

And now do not give your daughters to their sons, nor take their daughters for your sons, and never seek their peace or their prosperity, so that you may be strong and eat the good of the land and leave it as an inheritance to your sons forever.’
“And after all that has come upon us for our evil deeds and our great guilt—seeing that You, our God, have punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and have given us such deliverance as this—
“should we again break Your commandments and intermarry with these abominable peoples? Would You not be angry with us until You had consumed us, so that no remnant or survivor would remain?
“O the LORD, God of Israel, You are righteous, for we are left a remnant, as we are this day. Behold, we are before You in our guilt, for no one can stand before You because of this.”
While Ezra was praying and confessing, weeping and prostrating himself before the house of God, a vast assembly of Israelites—men, women, and children—gathered to him, and the people wept bitterly.

Then Shecaniah son of Jehiel, one of the descendants of Elam, said to Ezra, "We have broken faith with our God and have married foreign women from the peoples of the land, yet now there is hope for Israel in this.

Now therefore let us make a covenant with our God to put away all these wives and their children, according to the counsel of my lord and of those who tremble at the command of our God, and let it be done according to the Law.
Arise, for this matter is your responsibility, and we are with you; be strong and act."
Then Ezra arose and made the priests, the Levites, and all Israel swear an oath to do according to this word; and they swore.

Then Ezra withdrew from before the house of God and went to the chamber of Jehohanan son of Eliashib; and there he ate no bread and drank no water, for he was mourning over the faithlessness of the exiles.
And they made a proclamation throughout Judah and Jerusalem to all the exiles to assemble at Jerusalem.
Whoever did not come within three days, all his property would be forfeited, and he himself would be excluded from the assembly of the exiles, according to the counsel of the officials and elders.

So all the men of Judah and Benjamin assembled at Jerusalem within the three days. It was the twentieth day of the ninth month, and all the people sat in the square before the house of God, trembling because of this matter and because of the rain.
Then Ezra the priest stood up and said to them, "You have broken faith and married foreign women, increasing the guilt of Israel.
Now therefore make confession to the LORD, the God of your fathers, and do His will; separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from the foreign wives."
And all the assembly answered with a loud voice, "It is so; as you have said, it is upon us to do.
But the people are many, and it is the season of heavy rains, and we have no strength to stand outside; nor is this a work for one day or two, for we have greatly transgressed in this matter.

Let our officials stand for the whole assembly, and let all those in our cities who have married foreign women come at appointed times, together with the elders and judges of each city, until the fierce anger of our God is turned away from us because of this matter."
Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah opposed this, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite supported them.

Then the exiles did so. Ezra the priest selected men, heads of fathers' houses, according to their fathers' houses, each by name; and they sat down on the tenth day of the tenth month to examine the matter.
And they finished with all the men who had married foreign women by the first day of the first month.
Among the sons of the priests who had married foreign women were found: of the sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and his brothers: Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah.
They pledged themselves to put away their wives, and each one, being guilty, offered a ram of the flock for his guilt.
Of the sons of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.
Of the sons of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
Of the sons of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
Of the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (that is, Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
Of the singers: Eliashib. Of the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
And of Israel: of the sons of Parosh: Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malchijah, and Benaiah.
Of the sons of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah.
Of the sons of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.
Of the sons of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.
Of the sons of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Jeremoth.
Of the sons of Pahath-moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh.
Of the sons of Harim: Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon, Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemariah.
Of the sons of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei.
Of the sons of Bani: Maadai, Amram, and Uel.
Of the sons of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah.
All these had married foreign women, and some of them had wives by whom they had children.
The words of Nehemiah son of Hachaliah: In the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, while I was in the citadel of Susa,
Hanani, one of my brothers, arrived with several men from Judah, and I inquired of them about the Jews who had survived the captivity and about Jerusalem.
They replied, "The remnant there in the province suffers great affliction and disgrace. The wall of Jerusalem lies in ruins, and its gates have been consumed by fire."
Upon hearing these words, I sat down and wept. I mourned for days, fasting and praying before the God of heaven.
Then I said, "I beseech the LORD, God of heaven, the great and awesome God, who keeps covenant and steadfast love with those who love Him and keep His commandments,

let Your eyes be open and Your ears attentive to hear the prayer of Your servant that I pray before You day and night for Your servants, the Israelites, confessing the sins of the Israelites, which we have committed against You. Both I and my father's house have sinned.
We have acted very corruptly toward You and have not kept the commandments, statutes, and ordinances that You commanded Your servant Moses.
"Remember, I pray, the word that You commanded Your servant Moses, saying, 'If you act unfaithfully, I will scatter you among the nations;

but if you return to Me and keep and do My commandments, then even if your exiles are at the farthest horizon, I will gather them from there and bring them to the place I have chosen to set My Name there.'
They are Your servants and Your people, whom You redeemed by Your great power and Your strong hand.

O Lord, let Your ear be attentive to the prayer of Your servant and to the prayer of Your servants who desire to fear Your Name. Grant Your servant success today, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man." For I was cupbearer to the king.
In the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, wine was set before him. I took the wine and presented it to the king, for I had never before appeared downcast in his presence.
The king said to me, "Why does your countenance appear so dejected when you are not ill? This can only be anguish of heart." I was exceedingly afraid.
I said to the king, "O king, live forever! Why should my face not be downcast when the city, the place of my fathers' graves, lies in ruins and its gates have been consumed by fire?"
The king said to me, "What is your request?" So I prayed to the God of heaven.
I said to the king, "If it pleases the king, and if your servant has found favor in your sight, send me to Judah, to the city of my fathers' tombs, that I may rebuild it."
The king, with the queen seated beside him, asked me, "How long will your journey take, and when will you return?" It pleased the king to send me, and I set him an appointed time.
I said to the king, "If it pleases the king, let letters be given to me for the governors beyond the River, that they may grant me safe passage until I reach Judah."

And a letter was given to Asaph, keeper of the king's forest, that he may give me timber to make beams for the gates of the fortress by the temple, for the city wall, and for the house into which I am to go. The king granted my request, for the gracious hand of my God was upon me.
I went to the governors beyond the River and delivered the king's letters. The king had also sent army officers and cavalry with me.
When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard of this, they were deeply displeased that someone had come to seek the welfare of the Israelites.
I arrived in Jerusalem and remained there three days.
Then I set out by night with a few men. I had told no one what my God had put into my heart to do for Jerusalem, and there was no animal with me except the beast on which I rode.

I went out by night through the Valley Gate toward the Dragon Spring and on to the Dung Gate, inspecting the walls of Jerusalem, which had been broken down, and its gates, which had been destroyed by fire.
Then I proceeded to the Fountain Gate and to the King's Pool, but there was not enough room for the animal under me to pass.
So I went up by night along the valley and inspected the wall. Then I turned back and reentered through the Valley Gate.
The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing, for I had not yet told the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the officials, or the rest of those who were doing the work.

Then I said to them, "You see the trouble we are in: Jerusalem lies in ruins, and its gates have been burned with fire. Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, so that we will no longer be an object of scorn."
I also told them about the gracious hand of my God upon me, and about what the king had said to me. They replied, "Let us start rebuilding." So they began the good work.

But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite official, and Geshem the Arab heard about it, they mocked and despised us, saying, "What is this you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?"
I answered them by saying, "The God of heaven will grant us success. We His servants will start rebuilding, but you have no share, right, or memorial in Jerusalem."

Eliashib the high priest, together with his fellow priests, rebuilt the Sheep Gate. They consecrated it and set its doors in place, dedicating the work as far as the Tower of the Hundred and the Tower of Hananel.
The men of Jericho built beside it, and Zaccur son of Imri built beside them.
The sons of Hassenaah rebuilt the Fish Gate; they laid its beams and installed its doors, bolts, and bars.
Beside them Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, made repairs; beside him Meshullam son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel, made repairs; and beside him Zadok son of Baana made repairs.
Beside him the men of Tekoa made repairs, yet their nobles refused to submit to the labor demanded by their masters.
Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah repaired the Old Gate; they laid its beams and installed its doors, bolts, and bars.
Beside them Melatiah the Gibeonite, Jadon the Meronothite, and the men of Gibeon and Mizpah repaired the section under the authority of the governor of the province beyond the River.
Beside them Uzziel son of Harhaiah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs; beside him Hananiah, one of the perfumers, made repairs. They fortified Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.
Beside them Rephaiah son of Hur, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made repairs.
Beside them Jedaiah son of Harumaph made repairs opposite his house; beside him Hattush son of Hashabneiah made repairs.
Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab repaired another section, together with the Tower of the Ovens.
Beside him Shallum son of Hallohesh, ruler of the other half of the district of Jerusalem, made repairs, he and his daughters.
Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate; they rebuilt it and installed its doors, bolts, and bars, and they repaired a thousand cubits of the wall as far as the Dung Gate.
Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth-haccerem, repaired the Dung Gate; he rebuilt it and installed its doors, bolts, and bars.

Shallun son of Col-hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate; he rebuilt it, roofed it, and installed its doors, bolts, and bars. He also repaired the wall of the Pool of Siloam by the king's garden, as far as the stairs descending from the City of David.
After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of half the district of Beth-zur, made repairs up to the point opposite the tombs of David, as far as the artificial pool and the House of the Mighty.
After him the Levites made repairs under Rehum son of Bani; beside him Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, made repairs for his district.
After him their brothers made repairs under Binnui son of Henadad, ruler of the other half of the district of Keilah.
Beside him Ezer son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section opposite the ascent to the armory at the angle.
After him Baruch son of Zabbai zealously repaired another section, from the angle to the doorway of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
After him Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired another section, from the doorway of Eliashib's house to the end of the house.
Beside him the priests from the surrounding region made repairs.
After them Benjamin and Hasshub made repairs opposite their house; beside them Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, made repairs beside his house.
After him Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from the house of Azariah to the angle and the corner.
Palal son of Uzai made repairs opposite the angle and the tower projecting from the upper palace of the king, by the courtyard of the guard. Next to him, Pedaiah son of Parosh
and the temple servants living on the Ophel made repairs up to the point opposite the Water Gate toward the east and the tower that juts out.
Next to them the men of Tekoa repaired another section, from the great tower that juts out to the wall of Ophel.
Above the Horse Gate the priests made repairs, each in front of his own house.
After them Zadok son of Immer made repairs opposite his house. After him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, the guard of the East Gate, made repairs.
After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah, along with Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another section. After them Meshullam son of Berechiah made repairs opposite his chamber.
After him Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs as far as the house of the temple servants and merchants, opposite the Inspection Gate, and as far as the upper chamber of the corner.
Between the upper chamber of the corner and the Sheep Gate, the goldsmiths and merchants made repairs.
When Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he became furious and greatly enraged, and he mocked the Jews.

In the presence of his brothers and the army of Samaria, he said, “What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they restore it for themselves? Will they sacrifice? Will they finish in a day? Will they revive the stones from the heaps of rubble—burned as they are?”
Tobiah the Ammonite was beside him and said, “Yes, what they are building—if a fox goes up on it, he will break down their stone wall.”
Hear, our God, for we are despised. Turn their reproach back on their own heads, and give them as plunder in a land of captivity.
Do not cover their iniquity, and do not let their sin be blotted out from before You, for they have provoked You to anger before the builders.
So we built the wall, and all of it was joined together to half its height, because the people were willing to work.
When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that the repair of Jerusalem’s walls had advanced and that the breaches had begun to be closed, they were very angry.
They all conspired together to come and fight against Jerusalem and to throw it into confusion.
So we prayed to our God and stationed a guard against them day and night because of them.
Then Judah said, “The strength of the burden bearers is failing, and there is much rubble, so we are not able to build the wall.”
Our enemies said, “They will not know or see until we come among them, kill them, and stop the work.”
The Jews who lived near them came and told us ten times over, “Wherever you turn, they will attack us.”
So I stationed people behind the wall at the lower sections and at the exposed places; I stationed the people by families, with their swords, their spears, and their bows.

I looked, rose up, and said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, “Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your houses.”
When our enemies heard that it was known to us and that God had frustrated their plan, we all returned to the wall, each to his work.
From that day on, half of my servants worked on the construction, while the other half held the spears, the shields, the bows, and the body armor; and the leaders stood behind all the house of Judah.
Those who carried burdens and those who loaded them did their work with one hand and held a weapon with the other.
Each of the builders had his sword strapped to his side while he built, and the trumpeter stood beside me.
I said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, “The work is great and extensive, and we are separated on the wall, far from one another.
In whatever place you hear the sound of the trumpet, rally to us there. Our God will fight for us.”
So we labored at the work, and half of them held the spears from dawn until the stars appeared.
At that time I also said to the people, “Let each man and his servant spend the night within Jerusalem, that they may be a guard for us by night and labor by day.”
Neither I nor my brothers nor my men nor the guards with me took off our clothes; each kept his weapon even when he went for water.
A great outcry arose among the people and their wives against their fellow Jews.
Some said, "We have many sons and daughters, so we must obtain grain in order to eat and survive."
Some said, "We are mortgaging our fields, vineyards, and houses to buy grain during the famine."
Some said, "We have borrowed money for the king's tax on our fields and vineyards."

"Now our very flesh is the same as our brothers' flesh, and our children are like their children; yet we are forcing our sons and daughters into slavery, and some of our daughters have already been enslaved, while we are powerless, because our fields and vineyards belong to others."
When I heard their outcry and these words, I was very angry.
After careful deliberation, I rebuked the nobles and officials, saying, "You are exacting usury from your own brothers!" Then I convened a great assembly against them.

I said to them, "We have, according to our ability, redeemed our Jewish brothers who were sold to the nations. Now would you even sell your brothers, that they might be sold back to us?" They were silent and found nothing to say.
Again I said, "What you are doing is not good. Should you not walk in the fear of our God, to avoid the reproach of the nations, our enemies?"
I, my brothers, and my servants are also lending them money and grain. Please, let us stop charging this interest.
Please restore to them this very day their fields, vineyards, olive groves, and houses, along with the hundredth part of the money, grain, new wine, and oil that you have been exacting from them.
Then they said, "We will restore it and require nothing from them; we will do exactly as you say." So I called the priests and made them swear to do according to this promise.

I also shook out the fold of my garment and said, "Thus may God shake out every man from his house and from his labor who does not fulfill this promise; even so may he be shaken out and emptied." And all the assembly said, "Amen!" And they praised the LORD. Then the people did according to this promise.

Moreover, from the day King Artaxerxes appointed me to be governor in the land of Judah—from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of his reign, twelve years—neither I nor my brothers ate the food allotted to the governor.

But the former governors who preceded me laid heavy burdens on the people and took from them bread and wine, besides forty shekels of silver; even their servants lorded it over the people. But I did not do so, because of the fear of God.
I also devoted myself to the work on this wall, and all my servants were gathered there for the work; we did not acquire any field.
Moreover, there were at my table one hundred fifty Jews and officials, besides those who came to us from the nations around us.

Now what was prepared for each day was one ox, six choice sheep, and birds; and every ten days an abundance of all kinds of wine was provided. Yet with all this I did not demand the governor's food allowance, because the service was heavy on this people.
Remember me, O my God, for good, according to all that I have done for this people.
Now when Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies heard that I had rebuilt the wall and that no gap remained in it—though at that time I had not yet set up doors in the gates—
Sanballat and Geshem sent me a message, saying, “Come, let us meet together in one of the villages on the plain of Ono.” But they were planning to harm me.
So I sent messengers to them with this reply: “I am engaged in a great work and cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it to come down to you?”
They sent me the same message four times, and each time I answered them in the same way.
Then, for the fifth time, Sanballat sent his servant to me with an open letter in his hand,

and this is what it said: “It is reported among the nations—and Gashmu agrees—that you and the Jews are plotting rebellion; therefore you are building the wall. Moreover, according to these reports, you are to become their king.
You have also appointed prophets in Jerusalem to proclaim concerning you, ‘A king is in Judah.’ Now these matters will be reported to the king. So come, let us confer together.”
I sent word back to him: “Nothing like the things you are alleging has happened; you are inventing them in your own mind.”
For they were all trying to intimidate us, saying, “Their hands will be weakened from the work, and it will not be done.” But now, strengthen my hands!

I then went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, the son of Mehetabel, who was confined to his home. He said, “Let us meet in the house of God, inside the temple. Let us shut the doors of the temple, for they are coming to kill you—by night they are coming to kill you!”
But I replied, “Should a man like me run away? Or should one like me enter the temple to save his life? I will not go in!”
Then I realized that God had not sent him, but that he had prophesied against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
He had been hired to intimidate me so that I would sin by doing this, and then they would have grounds to discredit me.
O my God, remember Tobiah and Sanballat for what they have done, and also the prophetess Noadiah and the rest of the prophets who have been trying to intimidate me.
So the wall was completed on the twenty-fifth day of Elul, in fifty-two days.
When all our enemies heard about this, all the nations around us were afraid and lost their confidence, for they realized that this work had been accomplished by our God.
Also in those days, the nobles of Judah sent many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah's letters came to them.
For many in Judah were bound to him by oath, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
Moreover, they kept speaking of his good deeds in my presence and reporting my words to him. And Tobiah sent letters to intimidate me.
After the wall had been rebuilt and I had set the doors in place, the gatekeepers, the singers, and the Levites were appointed.
I put my brother Hanani in charge of Jerusalem, along with Hananiah the commander of the citadel, because he was a faithful man who feared God more than most.

I told them, “The gates of Jerusalem must not be opened until the sun is hot; while the guards are still on duty, the doors must be shut and secured. Also appoint the residents of Jerusalem as guards, some at their posts and some near their own houses.”
Now the city was large and spacious, but the people in it were few, and the houses had not yet been rebuilt.

Then my God put it into my heart to assemble the nobles, the officials, and the people so that they could be registered by genealogy. I found the genealogical record of those who had first returned, and I found written in it:
These are the people of the province who came up from the captivity of the exiles whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away. They returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town,
accompanied by Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah. This is the number of the men of the people of Israel:
the descendants of Pahath-moab, through Jeshua and Joab, 2,818;
the descendants of Ater, through Hezekiah, 98;
the men of Bethlehem and Netophah, 188;
the men of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, 743;
the men of Ramah and Geba, 621;
the men of Bethel and Ai, 123;
the men of the other Nebo, 52;
the descendants of the other Elam, 1,254;
the descendants of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, 721;
The priests: the descendants of Jedaiah, through the house of Jeshua, 973;
The Levites: the descendants of Jeshua, through Kadmiel, through the line of Hodaviah, 74.
The singers: the descendants of Asaph, 148.
The gatekeepers: the descendants of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai, 138.
The temple servants: the descendants of Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth,
The descendants of Solomon’s servants: the descendants of Sotai, Sophereth, Perida,
The temple servants and the descendants of Solomon’s servants totaled 392.
The following came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer, but they could not prove that their families or their ancestry were Israelite:
the descendants of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda, 642;
and from the priests, the descendants of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai, who had married a daughter of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
These searched for their genealogical records but could not find them, so they were excluded from the priesthood as unclean.
The governor ordered them not to eat the most holy food until a priest could consult the Urim and Thummim.
besides their 7,337 menservants and maidservants, as well as 245 male and female singers.
Some of the heads of the families contributed to the work. The governor gave to the treasury 1,000 darics of gold, 50 bowls, and 530 priestly garments.
Some of the heads of the families gave to the treasury for the project 20,000 darics of gold and 2,200 minas of silver.
The rest of the people gave 20,000 darics of gold, 2,000 minas of silver, and 67 priestly garments.
So the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the temple servants, and all Israel settled in their own towns. By the seventh month the Israelites had settled in their towns.

All the people gathered together as a unified whole in the square before the Water Gate, and they urged Ezra the scribe to bring out the Book of the Law of Moses, which the LORD had commanded for Israel.
On the first day of the seventh month, Ezra the priest brought the Law before the assembly—men and women and everyone capable of understanding what they heard.

He read from it in the square before the Water Gate from daybreak until midday, in the presence of the men and women and those who could understand; and all the people listened attentively to the Book of the Law.

Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform erected for the occasion. Beside him, on his right, stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah; on his left stood Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people, for he was above them all; and when he opened it, all the people stood.
Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God, and all the people answered, "Amen, Amen," raising their hands. Then they bowed down and worshiped the LORD with their faces to the ground.

The Levites—Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the other Levites—instructed the people in the Law while the people remained in their places.
They read from the Book of the Law of God distinctly, and they explained its meaning, so that the people understood the reading.

Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who were instructing the people said to all the people, "This day is holy to the LORD your God. Do not mourn or weep." For all the people were weeping as they heard the words of the Law.

Then he said to them, "Go, eat rich foods and drink sweet drinks, and send portions to anyone who has nothing prepared; for this day is holy to our Lord. Do not be grieved, for the joy of the LORD is your strength."
So the Levites calmed all the people, saying, "Be still, for the day is holy; do not be grieved."
Then all the people went to eat and drink, to send portions and to celebrate with great joy, because they understood the words that had been made known to them.
On the second day of the month, the heads of all the families, along with the priests and Levites, gathered to Ezra the scribe to study the words of the Law.
They found written in the Law that the LORD had commanded through Moses that the Israelites were to live in booths during the feast of the seventh month.

So they proclaimed and circulated this message throughout their cities and in Jerusalem: "Go out to the hill country and bring back branches of olive, wild olive, myrtle, palm, and other leafy trees, to make booths, as it is written."

So the people went out and brought them and made booths for themselves—each on his own roof, in his courtyard, in the courts of the house of God, in the square at the Water Gate, and in the square at the Gate of Ephraim.

The whole assembly of those who had returned from exile made booths and lived in them. From the days of Joshua son of Nun until that day, the Israelites had not celebrated like this. And there was very great joy.

Day by day, from the first day to the last, Ezra read from the Book of the Law of God. They kept the feast for seven days, and on the eighth day there was a solemn assembly, according to the ordinance.
On the twenty-fourth day of this month, the Israelites assembled, fasting and wearing sackcloth, with dust upon their heads.
Those of Israelite descent separated themselves from all foreigners; they stood and confessed their own sins and the iniquities of their ancestors.
Standing in their places, they read from the Book of the Law of the the LORD their God for a quarter of the day, and for another quarter they confessed and worshiped the the LORD their God.
The Levites—Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani—stood on the steps and cried out with a loud voice to the the LORD their God.

Then the Levites—Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah—said, “Stand up and bless the the LORD your God from everlasting to everlasting. Blessed be Your glorious name, exalted above all blessing and praise.

You alone are the the LORD. You made the heavens, the highest heavens and all their host, the earth and everything on it, the seas and all that is in them. You give life to all things, and the heavenly host worships You.
You are the the LORD, the God who chose Abram and brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and gave him the name Abraham.

You found his heart faithful before You and made a covenant with him to give the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and Girgashites to his descendants. You have kept Your word, for You are righteous. “
You saw the affliction of our ancestors in Egypt and heard their cry at the Red Sea.

You performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, all his servants, and all the people of his land, for You knew how arrogantly they treated our ancestors. You made a name for Yourself that endures to this day.
You divided the sea before them, so they passed through the midst of the sea on dry ground; You hurled their pursuers into the depths, like a stone into mighty waters.
By a pillar of cloud You led them by day, and by a pillar of fire by night, to light for them the way they should go.
You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven. You gave them just ordinances, true laws, and good statutes and commandments.
You made known to them Your holy Sabbath, and You commanded them statutes, ordinances, and a law through Your servant Moses.
From heaven You gave them bread for their hunger, and from the rock You brought out water for their thirst. You told them to go in and take possession of the land You had sworn to give them.
But they and our ancestors acted arrogantly and were stubborn, refusing to obey Your commandments.

They refused to listen and did not remember the wonders You had performed for them. They were stubborn and chose a leader to take them back to slavery in Egypt. But You are a forgiving God, gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love; You did not abandon them. “
Even when they made a molten calf and said, ‘This is your god who brought you up out of Egypt,’ committing great blasphemies,

In Your great compassion You did not abandon them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud did not leave them by day to guide them on their way, nor did the pillar of fire by night to light the path they should take.
You gave Your good Spirit to instruct them. You did not withhold Your manna from their mouths, and You gave them water for their thirst.
For forty years You sustained them in the wilderness; they lacked nothing. Their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.
You gave them kingdoms and peoples, allotting them their territories. They took possession of the land of Sihon, king of Heshbon, and the land of Og, king of Bashan.
You multiplied their descendants like the stars of heaven and brought them into the land You had promised their ancestors they would enter and possess.

So their descendants went in and possessed the land. You subdued before them the Canaanites who inhabited the land and delivered their kings and the peoples of the land into their hands, to do with them as they pleased.

They captured fortified cities and fertile land; they took possession of houses filled with all kinds of good things, hewn cisterns, vineyards, olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance. They ate, were filled, grew fat, and delighted themselves in Your great goodness. “
Nevertheless, they were disobedient and rebelled against You. They rejected Your law and killed Your prophets, who had warned them to return to You, committing great blasphemies.

So You delivered them into the hands of their enemies, who oppressed them. But in the time of their distress they cried out to You, and You heard from heaven. According to Your abundant mercy, You gave them deliverers who saved them from the hand of their enemies.

But whenever they had rest, they would turn again to do evil before You. Then You abandoned them to the hand of their enemies, so that they ruled over them. Yet when they cried out to You again, You heard from heaven and rescued them many times, according to Your mercy.

You warned them to return to Your law, but they acted arrogantly and did not obey Your commandments. They sinned against Your ordinances, by which a person lives if he does them. They stubbornly turned away and refused to listen.
For many years You were patient with them. By Your Spirit You warned them through Your prophets, yet they would not listen. Therefore You delivered them into the hands of the peoples of the lands.
Yet in Your great mercy You did not make an end of them or abandon them, for You are a gracious and compassionate God.

Now therefore, our God, the great, mighty, and awesome God who keeps covenant and steadfast love, do not treat as slight all the hardship that has come upon us—upon our kings, our leaders, our priests, our prophets, our ancestors, and all Your people—since the days of the kings of Assyria until this day.
You are righteous in all that has come upon us, for You have acted faithfully, but we have acted wickedly.
Our kings, our leaders, our priests, and our ancestors did not keep Your law or listen to Your commandments and testimonies that You declared against them.
Even in their own kingdom, amid the great goodness You gave them and the broad, fertile land You set before them, they did not serve You or turn from their wicked deeds.
Look, we are slaves today in the land You gave our ancestors to eat its fruit and enjoy its goodness; look, we are slaves in it.
Its abundant produce goes to the kings You have set over us because of our sins; they rule over our bodies and our livestock as they please, and we are in great distress.
Because of all this, we are making a firm covenant and writing it down; our leaders, our Levites, and our priests are affixing their seals.”
Nehemiah the governor, son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah;
Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah—these are the priests.
The Levites: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, and Kadmiel;
and their brothers Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, and Hanan;
The leaders of the people: Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu, and Bani;

The rest of the people—the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the temple servants, and all who had separated themselves from the peoples of the lands to the Law of God, together with their wives, their sons, and their daughters, everyone who had knowledge and understanding—

joined with their nobles and their brothers and entered into a curse and an oath to walk in the Law of God, which was given by the hand of Moses, the servant of God, and to observe and to do all the commandments of the LORD our Lord, together with His ordinances and His statutes.
They swore that they would not give their daughters to the peoples of the land, nor take their daughters for their sons.

If the peoples of the land brought merchandise or any grain to sell on the Sabbath day, they would not buy from them on the Sabbath or on a holy day; and they would forgo the harvest of the seventh year and cancel every debt.
We also take upon ourselves the commandment to give a third of a shekel each year for the service of the house of our God:

for the showbread, for the regular grain offering, for the regular burnt offering, for the Sabbaths, the new moons, and the appointed feasts, for the holy things, for the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God.

We have cast lots among the priests, the Levites, and the people for the wood offering, to bring it into the house of our God according to our ancestral houses at appointed times year by year, to burn on the altar of the LORD our God, as it is written in the Law.
We also obligate ourselves to bring the firstfruits of our ground and the firstfruits of every fruit tree to the house of the LORD year by year.
We will bring the firstborn of our sons and of our livestock, as it is written in the Law, and the firstborn of our herds and flocks, to the house of our God, to the priests who minister there.

We will bring the first portion of our dough, our contributions, the fruit of every tree, the new wine, and the oil to the priests, to the chambers of the house of our God; and we will bring the tithe of our ground to the Levites, for the Levites are the ones who collect the tithes in all the towns where we work.
The priest, the son of Aaron, shall be with the Levites when they receive the tithe, and the Levites shall bring up a tenth of the tithe to the house of our God, to the chambers of the storehouse.

For the people of Israel and the sons of Levi shall bring the contribution of grain, new wine, and oil to the chambers where the vessels of the sanctuary are, together with the priests who minister, the gatekeepers, and the singers. We will not neglect the house of our God.

The civic leaders took up residence in Jerusalem, while the remaining populace cast lots to select one in ten to dwell in Jerusalem, the holy city; the other nine-tenths remained in their respective towns.
The people blessed every man who volunteered to reside in Jerusalem.

These are the provincial administrators who settled in Jerusalem. (Throughout Judah’s cities, each man settled on his own property within their towns—the Israelites, priests, Levites, temple servants, and descendants of Solomon’s servants—
while some descendants of Judah and Benjamin settled in Jerusalem.)
and Maaseiah son of Baruch, son of Col-hozeh, son of Hazaiah, son of Adaiah, son of Joiarib, son of Zechariah, son of the Shilonite;
the descendants of Perez who settled in Jerusalem totaled 468 men of valor.
From the descendants of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Joed, son of Pedaiah, son of Kolaiah, son of Maaseiah, son of Ithiel, son of Jeshaiah;
and after him, Gabbai and Sallai—928.
Joel son of Zichri served as chief officer over them, and Judah son of Hassenuah oversaw the city as second-in-command.
From the priests: Jedaiah son of Joiarib; Jachin;
Seraiah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, ruler of the house of God;
and their associates who performed the temple service—822. Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pelaliah, son of Amzi, son of Zechariah, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah;
and his associates, the heads of families—242. Amashsai son of Azarel, son of Ahzai, son of Meshillemoth, son of Immer;
and their associates—128 mighty men of valor. Zabdiel son of Haggedolim was their overseer.
From the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, son of Bunni;
Shabbethai and Jozabad, leaders of the Levites, who supervised the exterior work of the house of God;

Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zabdi, son of Asaph, leader of the praise who led in thanksgiving and prayer; Bakbukiah, second among his associates; and Abda son of Shammua, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun.
The Levites in the holy city totaled 284.
And the gatekeepers: Akkub, Talmon, and their associates, who kept watch at the gates—172.
The rest of the Israelites, priests, and Levites were in all the cities of Judah, each on his own inheritance.
The temple servants lived on the hill of Ophel, with Ziha and Gishpa over them.

Now the overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi son of Bani, son of Hashabiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Mica, one of Asaph’s descendants, who were the singers assigned to the service of the house of God.
For there was a command from the king concerning them, and a fixed provision for the singers, day by day.
Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, a descendant of Zerah son of Judah, was the king’s agent in every matter concerning the people.
As for the villages with their fields, some of the people of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba and its villages, Dibon and its villages, Jekabzeel and its villages,
Zanoah, Adullam and their villages, Lachish and its fields, Azekah and its villages. So they settled from Beersheba all the way to the Valley of Hinnom.
The descendants of Benjamin from Geba lived in Michmash, Aija, Bethel and its villages,
Lod, Ono, and the Valley of Craftsmen.
And some of the Levites of Judah settled in Benjamin.
These are the priests and Levites who returned with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and with Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and Jedaiah. These were the chief priests and their associates in the days of Jeshua.
The Levites were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, who, together with his brothers, led the songs of thanksgiving.
Bakbukiah and Unni, their kinsmen, stood opposite them in their appointed watches.
Jeshua was the father of Joiakim, Joiakim the father of Eliashib, and Eliashib the father of Joiada.
Joiada was the father of Jonathan, and Jonathan was the father of Jaddua.
In the days of Joiakim, the heads of the priestly families were as follows: for Seraiah, Meraiah; for Jeremiah, Hananiah;
for Ezra, Meshullam; for Amariah, Jehohanan;
for Malluchi, Jonathan; for Shebaniah, Joseph;
for Harim, Adna; for Meraioth, Helkai;
for Iddo, Zechariah; for Ginnethon, Meshullam;
for Abijah, Zichri; for Miniamin and Moadiah, Piltai;
for Bilgah, Shammua; for Shemaiah, Jehonathan;
for Joiarib, Mattenai; for Jedaiah, Uzzi;
for Sallai, Kallai; for Amok, Eber;
for Hilkiah, Hashabiah; and for Jedaiah, Nethanel.
The heads of the Levite and priestly families were recorded in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, continuing until the reign of Darius the Persian.
The Levites’ ancestral heads were inscribed in the Book of the Chronicles down to the days of Johanan son of Eliashib.

The chiefs of the Levites—Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua son of Kadmiel, and their associates—stood opposite one another to chant praise and thanksgiving, watch corresponding to watch, as David, the man of God, had commanded.
Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers who guarded the storerooms at the gates.
These served in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and scribe.

At the dedication of Jerusalem’s wall, the Levites were summoned from every place where they resided and brought to Jerusalem to celebrate the dedication with gladness, thanksgiving, and song, accompanied by cymbals, harps, and lyres.
The singers assembled from the surrounding district of Jerusalem and from the villages of the Netophathites,
and from Beth-gilgal and from the fields of Geba and Azmaveth, because the singers had built villages for themselves around Jerusalem.
The priests and Levites purified themselves, and then they purified the people, the gates, and the wall.
Then I led Judah’s leaders up onto the wall and stationed two large thanksgiving choirs, which processed along the wall to the right toward the Dung Gate.
Hoshaiah and half of Judah’s leaders followed them,
along with Azariah, Ezra, and Meshullam,
and some of the priests’ sons bearing trumpets—Zechariah son of Jonathan son of Shemaiah son of Mattaniah son of Micaiah son of Zaccur son of Asaph—
and his brothers Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani, with the musical instruments of David, the man of God. Ezra the scribe walked before them.
At the Fountain Gate they ascended straight up the steps of the City of David, along the wall’s ascent, above David’s house, to the Water Gate on the east.
The second thanksgiving choir proceeded to the left, and I followed it with half the people along the wall, above the Tower of the Ovens, to the Broad Wall.

It passed above the Gate of Ephraim, above the Old Gate, above the Fish Gate, and past the Tower of Hananel and the Tower of the Hundred, reaching the Sheep Gate; there they stopped at the Gate of the Guard.
So both thanksgiving choirs took their stand in the house of God, and I stood with half the officials,
while the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah blew trumpets,
and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer joined them. The singers sang under the direction of Jezrahiah.
On that day they offered great sacrifices and rejoiced, for God had granted them great joy; the women and children rejoiced as well, so that Jerusalem’s joy was heard from afar.

On that day men were appointed to oversee the storerooms for the contributions, firstfruits, and tithes, gathering from the fields of the cities the portions prescribed by the Law for the priests and Levites, because Judah rejoiced over the priests and Levites who served.
They kept the service of their God and the service of purification, as did the singers and gatekeepers, according to the command of David and his son Solomon.
For in former days, under David and Asaph, the chief singers had led songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.

In the days of Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, all Israel contributed the daily portions for the singers and gatekeepers; they consecrated the sacred portion for the Levites, and the Levites consecrated the sacred portion for the sons of Aaron.
On that day, the Book of Moses was read aloud in the hearing of the people, and it was discovered that the text recorded that no Ammonite or Moabite was ever to be admitted into the assembly of God.
For they had not welcomed the Israelites with provisions and water; instead, they had retained Balaam to pronounce a curse upon them, though our God transformed the curse into a blessing.
Upon hearing this law, the people separated from Israel all those of mixed descent.
Before this, Eliashib the priest, who had been appointed over the storerooms of the house of our God and was intimately allied with Tobiah,

had furnished him with a spacious chamber where they had previously housed the grain offerings, the frankincense, the vessels, the tithes of grain, the new wine, and the oil ordained for the Levites, the singers, and the gatekeepers, together with the contributions for the priests.
During these events, I was absent from Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes, king of Babylon, I had returned to the king; and after an interval I requested permission from the king.
When I returned to Jerusalem, I uncovered the wrongdoing that Eliashib had committed on Tobiah's behalf by allocating him a chamber in the courts of the house of God.
I was deeply indignant, so I expelled all of Tobiah's household effects from the chamber.
Then I commanded that the chambers be purified, and I restored to them the vessels of the house of God, together with the grain offerings and the frankincense.
I also learned that the Levites' allotments had been withheld, so that each of the Levites and singers who performed the service had withdrawn to his own estate.
So I reprimanded the leaders and asked, “Why is the house of God forsaken?” Then I assembled them and reinstated them in their offices.
And all Judah delivered a tithe of the grain, the new wine, and the oil into the storerooms.

I designated as custodians over the storerooms Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites, with Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, to assist them, because they were deemed reliable. They were charged with apportioning the supplies to their brothers.
“Remember me for this, O my God, and do not erase the acts of steadfast devotion that I have performed for the house of my God and for its ministrations.”

In those days I saw people in Judah operating winepresses on the Sabbath and transporting sheaves and loading them on donkeys, along with wine, grapes, figs, and every manner of burden. And they were bringing all this into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. So I admonished them for marketing provisions on that day.
Tyrians who dwelt there were importing fish and all kinds of merchandise and selling them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah in Jerusalem.
Then I rebuked the nobles of Judah and asked, “What is this wickedness you are perpetrating—profaning the Sabbath day?
Did not your ancestors act likewise, so that our God inflicted all this calamity upon us and upon this city? Yet you are compounding His indignation against Israel by profaning the Sabbath.”
