He stretches out the north over empty space and hangs the earth upon nothing.
He gathers the waters into His thick clouds, yet the cloud does not burst beneath them.
He obscures the face of His throne, spreading His cloud upon it.
He has drawn a circle on the face of the waters, at the boundary of light and darkness.
The pillars of heaven tremble and are astounded at His rebuke.
By His power He quieted the sea, and by His understanding He shattered Rahab.
By His Spirit the heavens were adorned, and His hand pierced the fleeing serpent.
Behold, these are but the fringes of His ways; what a faint whisper we hear of Him! Yet who can comprehend the thunder of His might?”
Job resumed his discourse and said:
"As God lives, who has deprived me of justice, and the Almighty, who has embittered my soul—
as long as my breath is within me and the spirit of God is in my nostrils,
my lips will not speak wickedness, nor will my tongue utter deceit.
I will never concede that you are right; I will not relinquish my integrity.
I cling to my righteousness and will not let it go; my heart will not reproach me as long as I live.
"Let my enemy be like the wicked, and my adversary like the unrighteous.
For what is the hope of the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him?
Will he delight in the Almighty? Will he call upon God at all times?
I will teach you about the hand of God; I will not conceal what is with the Almighty.
Behold, all of you have seen it; why then do you talk such nonsense?
"This is the wicked man's portion from God, and the inheritance that oppressors receive from the Almighty.
If his sons are many, they are for the sword, and his offspring will never have enough bread.
Those who survive him are carried off by plague, and his widows do not weep.
Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up clothing like clay,
he may prepare it, but the righteous will wear it, and the innocent will divide his silver.
He builds his house like a moth's cocoon, like a booth that a watchman sets up.
He lies down wealthy, but will not do so again; he opens his eyes, and he is gone.
Terrors overtake him like a flood; a tempest snatches him away by night.
The east wind carries him off, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place.
It hurls itself at him without pity; he flees in vain from its power.
It claps its hands at him and hisses at him from its place."
Surely silver has its source, and gold a place where it is refined.
Iron is taken from the dust, and copper is smelted from stone.
He sets a boundary to darkness and searches out the farthest limit—the stone of gloom and deep shadow.
A shaft breaks open far from where men dwell; untrodden by the foot, they hang and sway, remote from humankind.
As for the earth, food comes from it, yet beneath it is overturned as though by fire.
Its stones are a place of sapphires, and its dust contains gold.
No bird of prey knows that path, nor has the falcon's eye seen it.
The proud beasts have not trodden it, and no lion has passed over it.
He lays his hand upon the flinty rock and overturns mountains by their roots.
He cuts channels through the rock, and his eye sees every precious thing.
He dams the streams so they do not trickle, and brings what is hidden into the light.
But where can wisdom be found, and where is the place of understanding?
Man does not know its value, nor is it found in the land of the living.
The deep says, "It is not in me." And the sea says, "It is not with me."
It cannot be purchased with gold, nor can silver be weighed out as its price.
It cannot be valued in Ophir's gold, nor in precious onyx or sapphire.
Neither gold nor glass can equal it, nor can it be exchanged for vessels of fine gold.
Coral and crystal are scarcely worth mentioning; the price of wisdom is above pearls.
The topaz of Cush cannot equal it; it cannot be valued in pure gold.
From where, then, does wisdom come, and where is the place of understanding?
It is hidden from the eyes of all living and concealed from the birds of the sky.
Abaddon and Death say, "We have heard a rumor of it with our ears."
God understands its way, and He knows its place.
For He looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under heaven.
When He made a weight for the wind and measured out the waters by measure,
when He made a decree for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt,
then He saw it and declared it; He established it and searched it out.
And He said to man, "The fear of the Lord—that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding."
Job again took up his discourse and said:
“If only I were as in months gone by, in the days when God watched over me—
when His lamp shone above my head, and by His light I walked through darkness;
when I was in my prime, and God’s intimate friendship rested upon my tent;
when the Almighty was still with me, and my children surrounded me;
when prosperity bathed my steps, and abundance poured out for me like oil from the rock.
When I went out to the city gate and took my seat in the square,
the young men saw me and stepped aside, while the aged rose to their feet.
Princes refrained from speaking and laid their hands over their mouths;
the voices of nobles fell silent, and their tongues clung to their palates.
For the ear that heard me called me blessed, and the eye that saw me bore witness to me.
Because I delivered the poor man who cried for help, and the fatherless who had no advocate;
the blessing of the perishing came upon me, and I made the widow’s heart sing for joy.
I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; my justice was my robe and my turban.
I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.
I was a father to the needy, and I investigated cases I did not know.
I broke the fangs of the wicked and snatched the prey from his teeth.
Then I thought, “I would die in my nest, with my days as numerous as the sand.
My roots reached to the waters, and dew rested upon my branches.
My glory stayed fresh within me, and my bow was renewed in my hand.”
Men listened to me and waited; they kept silent for my counsel.
After I spoke, they had nothing more to say, and my words settled upon them.
They waited for me as for rain, and opened their mouths wide as for the latter rain.
I smiled at them when they had no confidence, and they did not diminish the light of my countenance.
I chose their way and sat as chief; I dwelt like a king among his troops, like one who comforts mourners.
But now they deride me—men younger than I, whose fathers I would have deemed unworthy even to run with my sheepdogs.
What value could the strength of their hands have offered me, when their vitality had already withered?
Blighted by want and hard hunger, they gnaw the parched earth by night amid waste and desolation;
they gather saltwort among the shrubs and broom roots for sustenance. “
They are banished from human society and shouted at as though they were thieves.
They must dwell in the gullies of torrents, in holes of earth and rock.
Among the brush they bray; beneath the nettles they cluster.
A witless, nameless brood, they have been scourged from the land. “
Now I have become their song of mockery, a byword among them.
They detest me and keep their distance; they do not hesitate to spit when they see me.
Because God has loosed my cord and humbled me, they cast off all restraint before me.
On my right the rabble rise; they push away my feet and throw up causeways of ruin against me.
They tear up my path; they advance my ruin, and they need no accomplice.
They pour through a wide breach; amid the crashing ruin they roll on.
Terrors overwhelm me; my dignity is driven before the wind, and my prosperity has vanished like a cloud. “
Now my very soul is poured out within me, and days of affliction have seized me.
Night pierces my bones; the pain that gnaws at me grants no rest.
My garment is distorted by violent force; it clings to me like the collar of my tunic.
God has cast me into the mire, and I have become like dust and ashes. “
I cry out to You for help, but You do not answer; I stand before You, and You merely look at me.
You have turned cruel toward me; with the might of Your hand You persecute me.
You lift me up into the wind and make me ride upon it; You toss me about in the roar of the storm.
For I know that You will bring me down to death, to the house appointed for all the living.
Yet does not a man in ruins stretch out his hand, crying for help in his calamity? “
Did I not weep for those whose days were hard? Was my soul not grieved for the needy?
But when I hoped for good, evil came; when I waited for light, darkness came.
My inward parts churn and find no rest; days of affliction come upon me.
I walk about darkened, though not by the sun; I stand in the assembly and cry for help. “
I have become a brother to jackals and a companion of ostriches.
My skin grows black and peels from me, and my bones are scorched with heat.
My lyre is tuned to mourning, and my flute to the sound of weeping.”
"I made a solemn pledge to my eyes never to look with lust upon a young woman; how, then, could I have fixed my gaze upon a virgin?
For what portion would God allot me from above, and what inheritance would the Almighty grant me from the heights?
Is not ruin the lot of the wicked, and disaster the portion of those who practice iniquity?
Does He not see my ways and count every step I take?"
"If I have walked in falsehood, or if my foot has hurried toward deceit,
let God weigh me on honest scales and know my integrity.
If my steps have strayed from the path, if my heart has followed the craving of my eyes, or if any stain has clung to my hands,
then let me sow while another reaps, and let all that I have planted be uprooted."
"If my heart has been seduced by a woman, or if I have lurked at my neighbor's doorway in pursuit of adultery,
then let my wife grind grain for another man, and let strangers lie with her.
For that would be a heinous crime, an iniquity deserving judgment;
it would be a fire consuming down to Abaddon, devouring all my increase to the root."
"If I have dismissed the complaint of my male or female servant when they contended with me,
what could I do when God arises? When He examines me, what answer could I give Him?
Did not He who formed me in the womb form him as well? Did not one and the same God fashion us both in the womb?"
"If I have withheld from the poor what they needed, or made a widow's eyes grow dim with longing,
or eaten my bread alone while the orphan had none of it—
though from my youth the orphan grew up beside me as though I were his father, and from my mother's womb I guided the widow—
if I have seen anyone perish for lack of clothing, or the needy without a covering,
if his loins have not blessed me, or if he was not warmed by the fleece of my sheep,
if I have lifted my hand against an orphan because I knew I had allies at the gate,
then let my shoulder blade fall from my shoulder and my arm be broken from its socket.
For calamity from God was a terror to me, and because of His majesty I could not endure it."
"If I have made gold my confidence, or called fine gold my security,
if I have rejoiced because my wealth was great or because my hand had gained much,
if I have looked upon the sun in its brilliance or the moon moving in splendor
and been secretly enticed, so that my mouth kissed my hand in homage,
that too would be an iniquity deserving judgment, for I would have been false to God above."
"If I have rejoiced at the ruin of my enemy, or exulted when misfortune overtook him—
though I never let my mouth sin by demanding his life with a curse—
if the men of my household could not say, 'Who has ever gone hungry at his table?'—
for no stranger had to sleep in the street, since I opened my doors to the traveler—
if I have hidden my transgressions like other men, concealing my iniquity in my heart,
because I dreaded the multitude and the contempt of families terrified me, so that I kept silent and never stepped outside my door—"
"Oh, that someone would hear me! Here is my signature—let the Almighty answer me! Oh, that my accuser had written an indictment!
Surely I would carry it on my shoulder and bind it upon myself like a crown;
I would give Him an account of every step I have taken and approach Him like a prince."
"If my land has cried out against me, or its furrows have wept together,
if I have eaten its produce without payment and caused its owners to lose their lives,
then let thorns grow in place of wheat and foul weeds in place of barley." Thus the words of Job came to an end.
Now these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
Then Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, became very angry; he burned with anger at Job for justifying himself rather than God.
He was also angry with Job’s three friends, because they had found no answer, yet they had condemned Job.
Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job because they were older than he.
But when Elihu saw that the three men had no answer in their mouths, his anger burned.
So Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, “I am young in years, and you are old; therefore I was timid and afraid to declare what I know to you.
I thought, ‘Age should speak, and a multitude of years should teach wisdom.’
But there is a spirit in man, and the breath of the Almighty gives them understanding.
It is not only the old who are wise, or the aged who understand justice.
Therefore I say, ‘Listen to me; I too will declare what I know.’
“Behold, I waited for your words; I listened to your reasonings while you searched out what to say.
I gave you my full attention, yet not one of you has refuted Job or answered his claims.
Beware lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom; God, not man, will refute him.’
Now he has not directed his words against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.
“They are dismayed; they answer no more; words have failed them.
I have waited, because they do not speak, because they stand still and answer no more.
I too will have my say; I too will declare what I know.
For I am full of words; the spirit within my belly compels me.
Behold, my belly is like wine that has no outlet; it is ready to burst like new wineskins.
I must speak, so that I may find relief; I must open my lips and respond.
I will be partial to no one, nor will I flatter any man.
For I do not know how to flatter, or my Maker would soon take me away.”
But now, Job, hear my words, please; listen to all that I have to say.
Behold, I have opened my mouth; my tongue speaks.
My words declare the uprightness of my heart, and my lips utter pure knowledge.
The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
Answer me, if you can; arrange your arguments before me and take your stand.
Behold, I am as you are before God; I too was formed from clay.
Behold, my terror will not frighten you, nor will my burden weigh heavily on you.
Surely you spoke in my hearing, and I heard the sound of your words.
"I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, and there is no iniquity in me.
Look, He finds reasons to oppose me; He counts me as His enemy.
He puts my feet in the stocks and watches all my paths."
Look, in this you are not right; I will answer you, for God is greater than man.
Why do you contend with Him, saying that He will not answer any of your words?
For God speaks once, and even twice, yet man does not perceive it.
In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on men, while they slumber on their beds,
then He opens the ears of men and seals His discipline upon them,
to turn a man from his deed and hide pride from him.
He spares his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.
He is also chastened with pain on his bed, and with strife in his bones,
so that his life abhors bread, and his soul craves delicacies.
His flesh wastes away so that it cannot be seen, and his bones, once hidden, protrude.
His soul draws near to the pit, and his life to those who destroy.
If there is an angel for him, one mediator among a thousand, to declare to a man his uprightness,
and He is gracious to him and says, "Deliver him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom,"
his flesh is restored like a child's; he returns to the days of his youth.
He prays to God, and He accepts him; he sees His face with a shout of joy, and He restores his righteousness to man.
Then he sings before men and says, "I have sinned and perverted what is right, yet it was not repaid to me."
He has redeemed my soul from going down to the pit, and my life will see the light.
Behold, God does all these things two or three times with a man,
to bring back his soul from the pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of life.
Pay attention, Job, and listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.
If you have words, answer me; speak, for I desire to justify you.
If not, listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.
"Hear my words, you wise men; listen to me, you who have knowledge.
For the ear tests words as the palate tastes food.
Let us choose for ourselves what is right; let us determine among ourselves what is good."
For Job has declared: "I am righteous, yet God has deprived me of justice.
Should I lie about my right? My wound is incurable, though I am without transgression."
What man is like Job, who drinks up mockery like water,
who keeps company with evildoers and walks with wicked men?
For he has said: "It profits a man nothing that he should delight in God."
Therefore listen to me, you men of understanding: Far be it from God to do wickedness, and from the Almighty to do wrong.
For He repays a man according to his deeds, and makes him find according to his ways.
Indeed, God does not act wickedly, and the Almighty does not pervert justice.
Who appointed Him over the earth? Or who set Him over the whole world?
If He set His heart upon it and gathered to Himself His Spirit and His breath,
all flesh would perish together, and man would return to dust."
If you have understanding, hear this; listen to the words of my mouth.
Could one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the just and mighty One?
Is it fitting to say to a king, "You are worthless," or to nobles, "You are wicked"—
how much less to Him who is not partial to princes and does not favor the rich over the poor? For they are all the work of His hands.
They die in a moment, in the middle of the night; the people are shaken and pass away; the mighty are removed without human hand.
For His eyes are on the ways of a man, and He sees all his steps.
There is no darkness or deep shadow where evildoers can hide.
For God does not need to investigate a man further before bringing him to judgment.
He shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets up others in their place.
Therefore He recognizes their deeds, and He overthrows them in the night so that they are crushed.
He strikes them for their wickedness in a place where onlookers can see,
because they turned aside from following Him and had no regard for any of His ways.
So that they caused the cry of the poor to come before Him, and He heard the cry of the afflicted.
When He is quiet, who can condemn? When He hides His face, who can see Him? Yet He rules over both man and nation,
to keep a godless man from reigning and from ensnaring the people.
Suppose a man says to God: "I have endured my punishment; I will offend no more.
Teach me what I do not see; if I have done wrong, I will not do it again."
Should God repay you on your terms, when you refuse to repent? You must decide, not I; so tell me what you know.
Men of understanding will declare to me—and any wise man who hears me—
that Job speaks without knowledge; his words lack insight.
Oh, that Job were tested to the utmost, for he answers like a wicked man.
For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us and multiplies his words against God.
"Do you think this is just? You said, 'My righteousness is greater than God's.'
For you ask, 'What advantage will it be to you? How am I better off than if I had sinned?'
I will answer you, and your friends with you.
"Look up at the heavens and see; gaze at the clouds high above you.
If you sin, what do you accomplish against Him? And if your transgressions are many, what do you do to Him?
If you are righteous, what do you give Him? Or what does He receive from your hand?
Your wickedness affects a man like you, and your righteousness touches a son of man.
"The oppressed cry out under a heavy burden; they plead for relief from the arm of the powerful.
Yet no one asks, 'Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?'
There they cry out, but He does not answer, because of the arrogance of evildoers.
Surely God does not listen to empty pleas, and the Almighty does not regard them.
"How much less, then, when you say you do not see Him! Your case is before Him, and you must wait for Him.
And now, because His anger does not punish and He does not take much notice of transgression,
Job opens his mouth in vain and multiplies words without knowledge."
Bear with me a little longer, and I will show you; for I still have words to speak on God’s behalf.
I will carry my knowledge from afar and ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
For truly my words are not false; one perfect in knowledge is with you. “
Behold, God is mighty and does not despise anyone; He is mighty in strength of understanding.
He does not keep the wicked alive, but He gives justice to the afflicted.
He never withdraws His eyes from the righteous; He enthrones them with kings forever and exalts them. “
If they are bound in chains and caught in the cords of affliction,
then He declares to them their deeds and their transgressions, that they have acted arrogantly.
He opens their ears to instruction and commands them to turn back from iniquity.
If they obey and serve Him, they complete their days in prosperity and their years in pleasantness.
But if they do not obey, they perish by the sword and die without knowledge. “
The godless in heart harbor anger; they do not cry for help when He binds them.
They die in their youth, and their life ends among the male shrine prostitutes.
He delivers the afflicted through their affliction and opens their ears by adversity.
He is even drawing you out of distress into a broad place where there is no cramping, and the table set before you is laden with rich food. “
Yet you are filled with the judgment due the wicked; judgment and justice have seized you.
Beware lest wealth entice you, and do not let a great ransom turn you aside.
Will your riches avail you, or all your mighty strength?
Do not long for the night, when peoples are cut off in their place.
Be careful; do not turn to iniquity, for you have chosen it rather than affliction. “
Behold, God is exalted in His power; who is a teacher like Him?
Who has prescribed His way for Him, or who can say, ‘You have done wrong’?
Remember to extol His work, of which men have sung.
All mankind has looked upon it; men behold it from afar. “
Behold, God is great, and we do not know Him; the number of His years is unsearchable.
For He draws up the drops of water; they distill rain from His mist.
The clouds pour it down and drop it abundantly upon mankind.
Can anyone understand the spreading of the clouds, the thunderings of His pavilion? “
Behold, He spreads His lightning over it and covers the depths of the sea.
For by these He judges the peoples and gives food in abundance.
He covers His hands with lightning and commands it to strike its mark.
Its thunder announces Him, and even the cattle sense what is rising.”
At this my heart pounds and leaps from its place.
Listen carefully to the thunder of His voice and the rumbling that comes from His mouth.
He unleashes it beneath the whole sky, and His lightning flashes to the ends of the earth.
After it His voice roars; He thunders with His majestic voice. He does not hold back the lightning when His voice is heard.
God thunders wondrously with His voice; He does great things we cannot comprehend.
For He says to the snow, "Fall on the earth," and to the rain shower, "Be a mighty downpour."
He seals up the hand of every man, so that all men may know His work.
Then the beasts take cover in their lairs and remain in their dens.
The tempest comes from its chamber, and the cold from the driving winds.
By the breath of God ice is formed, and the broad waters are frozen solid.
He also loads the clouds with moisture and scatters His lightning through the clouds.
And they swirl about, turning round and round at His direction, accomplishing whatever He commands them over the face of the whole earth.
Whether for punishment, or for His land, or for mercy, He makes it happen.
Listen to this, Job; stand still and consider the wondrous works of God.
Do you know how God directs them, making the lightning flash in His cloud?
Do you know the balancing of the clouds, the wondrous works of Him who is perfect in knowledge—
you whose garments grow hot when the earth is still because of the south wind?
Can you, with Him, spread out the skies, hard as a mirror of bronze?
Teach us what we should say to Him; we cannot draw up our case because of darkness.
Should it be reported to Him that I would speak? If a man speaks, surely he would be swallowed up.
Now no one can look at the sun when it is bright in the skies, after the wind has swept through and cleared them.
Out of the north comes golden splendor; God is clothed with awesome majesty.
The Almighty—we cannot find Him; He is great in power and justice, and abundant righteousness He does not oppress.
Therefore men fear Him; He does not regard any who are wise in their own heart.
The LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said, “
Who is this who obscures My counsel with words devoid of knowledge?
Now prepare yourself like a man, for I will question you, and you shall make known to Me. “
Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell Me, if you have understanding.
Who determined its measurements, if you know, or who stretched the measuring line across it?
Upon what were its foundations sunk, or who laid its cornerstone,
when the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy? “
Or who enclosed the sea behind doors when it burst forth from the womb,
when I made the cloud its garment and thick darkness its swaddling band,
and fixed My boundary for it and set bars and doors,
and said, ‘Thus far shall you come, and no farther, and here shall your proud waves be stayed’? “
Have you ever in your days commanded the morning, or caused the dawn to know its place,
that it might seize the ends of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?
The earth is transformed like clay under a seal, and its forms stand out like a garment.
From the wicked their light is withheld, and the uplifted arm is broken.” “
Have you entered the springs of the sea, or walked in the recesses of the deep?
Have the gates of death been revealed to you, or have you seen the gates of deep darkness?
Have you comprehended the expanse of the earth? Declare it, if you know all this. “
Where is the way to the dwelling of light, and where is the place of darkness,
that you may take it to its territory and discern the paths to its home?
You surely know, for you were born then, and the number of your days is great!” “
Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, or have you seen the storehouses of the hail,
which I have reserved for the time of trouble, for the day of battle and war?
What is the way to the place where the light is distributed, or where the east wind is scattered over the earth? “
Who has cleft a channel for the torrents of rain and a path for the thunderbolt,
to bring rain on a land where no one lives, on a desert uninhabited by man,
to satisfy the waste and desolate land and to make the ground sprout with grass? “
Has the rain a father, or who has begotten the drops of dew?
From whose womb did the ice come forth, and who has given birth to the frost of heaven?
The waters become hard like stone, and the face of the deep is frozen.” “
Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades, or loose the cords of Orion?
Can you bring forth the constellations in their season, or guide the Bear with its cubs?
Do you know the ordinances of the heavens? Can you establish their rule on the earth? “
Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, that a flood of waters may cover you?
Can you send forth lightnings, that they may go and say to you, ‘Here we are’?
Who has put wisdom in the inward parts, or given understanding to the mind?
Who can count the clouds by wisdom, or tip over the waterskins of the heavens,
when the dust runs into a mass and the clods stick fast together? “
Can you hunt the prey for the lion, or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,
when they crouch in their dens and lie in wait in the thicket?
Who provides food for the raven when its young cry to God and wander about for lack of food?”
Do you know when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch over the does as they calve?
Can you count the months they carry to term? Do you know the time they give birth?
They crouch, they bring forth their young, and they cast off their birth pangs.
Their young grow strong in the wild; they leave and do not return to them. “
Who set the wild donkey free? Who untied the bonds of the wild ass,
to whom I have made the wilderness a home and the salt flats a dwelling?
He scorns the uproar of the town and does not hear the driver's shouts.
The mountains are his pasture, and he seeks out every green thing. “
Will the wild ox consent to serve you? Will he stay by your manger?
Can you bind the wild ox with a rope in the furrow? Or will he plow the valleys behind you?
Will you trust him because his strength is great? Or will you leave your toil to him?
Will you rely on him to bring your grain home and gather it to your threshing floor? “
The ostrich's wings flap joyously, but are they the pinions and plumage of a stork?
For she leaves her eggs on the ground and warms them in the dust,
forgetting that a foot may crush them or that a wild beast may trample them.
She treats her young harshly, as though they were not her own; her labor is in vain, and she feels no fear.
For God has deprived her of wisdom and has not imparted understanding to her.
Yet when she rears herself up, she scorns the horse and its rider. “
Do you give the horse his strength? Do you clothe his neck with a mane?
Can you make him leap like a locust? His majestic snorting is terrifying.
He paws in the valley and exults in his strength; he charges out to meet the weapons.
He mocks fear and is not dismayed; he does not turn back from the sword.
The quiver rattles against him, along with the flashing spear and javelin.
In frenzy and rage he races across the ground; he does not halt at the trumpet's sound.
At the sound of the trumpet he cries, 'Aha!' He scents the battle from afar—the thunder of commanders and the shouting. “
Does the hawk soar by your wisdom and spread her wings toward the south?
Does the eagle soar at your command and build her nest on high?
She dwells on the rock and lodges there, on the crag and the stronghold.
From there she spies out food; her eyes see it from afar.
Her young feed on blood, and where the slain are, there she is.”
Then the LORD answered Job and said,
“Shall the faultfinder contend with the Almighty? Let him who argues with God answer it.”
Then Job answered the LORD and said:
“Behold, I am unworthy—how can I reply to You? I have put my hand over my mouth.
I have spoken once, but I have no answer—twice, but I will add nothing more.”
Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:
“Brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall answer Me.
Would you indeed annul My justice? Would you condemn Me to justify yourself?
Do you have an arm like God's? Can you thunder with a voice like His?
Adorn yourself now with majesty and dignity; clothe yourself with honor and splendor.
Unleash the fury of your wrath; look on every proud man and humble him.
Look on every proud man and bring him low; trample the wicked where they stand.
Bury them all in the dust; imprison their faces in the grave.
Then I will also confess to you that your own right hand can save you.”
“Look now at the behemoth, which I made along with you. He feeds on grass like an ox.
See the strength in his loins and the power in the muscles of his belly.
His tail sways like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are tightly knit.
His bones are tubes of bronze; his limbs are like bars of iron.
He ranks first among the works of God; only his Maker can draw the sword against him.
The hills yield him their produce, and all the beasts of the field play nearby.
He lies under the lotus plants, in the shelter of the reeds and the marsh.
The lotus plants conceal him in their shade; the willows of the brook surround him.
Though the river rages, he is not alarmed; he is secure, though the Jordan should surge against his mouth.
Can anyone capture him by his eyes, or pierce his nose with a snare?”
Can you draw Leviathan with a fishhook, or bind his tongue with a rope?
Can you put a reed through his nose, or pierce his jaw with a hook?
Will he plead with you for mercy, or speak softly to you?
Will he make a covenant with you, to serve you forever?
Can you play with him as with a bird, or bind him for your maidens?
Will merchants barter for him, or divide him among the traders?
Can you fill his skin with harpoons, or his head with fishing spears?
If you lay a hand on him, you will remember the battle and never attempt it again.
Behold, the hope of subduing him is a delusion; one is overwhelmed at the mere sight of him. "
No one is so fierce as to rouse him; who then can stand before Me?
Who has first given to Me, that I should repay him? Everything under heaven is Mine.
I will not keep silent about his limbs, his mighty strength, or his graceful form.
Who can strip off his outer coat? Who can approach him with a bridle?
Who can open the doors of his face? His teeth are a terror all around. "
His back is rows of shields, shut tight as a sealed closure.
One scale draws near to another, so that no breath can pass between them.
They cleave to one another; they hold fast and cannot be separated. "
His snorting flashes forth light; his eyes are like the eyelids of dawn.
Firebrands stream from his mouth; sparks of fire shoot out.
Smoke billows from his nostrils as from a boiling pot over burning reeds.
His breath sets coals ablaze, and a flame pours from his mouth.
Strength abides in his neck, and dismay leaps before him.
The folds of his flesh are tightly joined; they are firm and immovable.
His heart is as hard as stone, even as hard as a lower millstone. "
When he rises up, the mighty are terrified; they retreat before his thrashing.
The sword that reaches him cannot avail; neither spear, nor dart, nor javelin.
He regards iron as straw, bronze as rotten wood.
The bow cannot make him flee; slingstones become like chaff to him.
A club is regarded as stubble; he laughs at the rattling of spears.
His undersides are jagged potsherds, leaving a trail in the mud like a threshing sledge.
He makes the depths churn like a cauldron; he makes the sea like a pot of ointment.
He leaves a glistening wake behind him; one would think the deep had white hair.
Nothing on earth is his equal—a creature devoid of fear.
He looks down on all that is lofty; he is king over every proud creature."
Then Job answered the LORD and said,
"I know that You can do all things, and that no purpose of Your can be thwarted.
Who is this who obscures counsel without knowledge? Therefore I have spoken of what I did not understand—things too wonderful for me, which I did not know.
Hear, I pray, and I will speak; I will question You, and You will make it known to me.
I had heard of You by report, but now my eye sees You.
Therefore I despise myself and repent in dust and ashes."
After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite,

"My anger burns against you and against your two friends, for you have not spoken of Me what is right, as My servant Job has. Now therefore take seven bulls and seven rams, go to My servant Job, and offer up a burnt offering for yourselves; and My servant Job shall pray for you, for I will accept his prayer, that I may not deal with you according to your folly, because you have not spoken of Me what is right, as My servant Job has."
So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD had told them, and the LORD accepted Job's prayer.
And the LORD restored Job's fortunes when he had prayed for his friends, and the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.

Then all his brothers and sisters and all who had known him before came to him and ate bread with him in his house; they consoled him and comforted him over all the adversity that the LORD had brought upon him, and each gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.
The LORD blessed the latter days of Job more than his beginning, and he had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys.
He had also seven sons and three daughters.
He named the first Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-happuch.
In all the land no women were found as beautiful as Job's daughters, and their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
After this Job lived one hundred forty years, and saw his sons and his sons' sons to the fourth generation.
Then Job died, old and full of days.
How blessed is the one who does not follow the advice of the wicked, adopt the ways of sinners, or join the company of mockers.
Rather, his delight is in the law of the the LORD, and he meditates on His law day and night.
He is like a tree planted beside streams of water, producing fruit in its season, whose leaves never wither; everything he does prospers.
The wicked are not like this; they are like chaff blown away by the wind.
Therefore the wicked will not be acquitted in judgment, and sinners will have no place among the righteous.
For the the LORD knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked leads to ruin.
Why do the nations rage, and why do the peoples plot in vain?
The kings of the earth take their stand, and the rulers conspire together against the LORD and against His Anointed,
saying, "Let us break their chains and cast off their cords."
He who sits in heaven laughs; the Lord holds them in derision.
Then He speaks to them in His wrath and terrifies them in His fury:
"As for Me, I have installed My King on Zion, My holy mountain."
I will proclaim the decree: "The LORD said to Me, 'You are My Son; today I have begotten You.
Ask of Me, and I will make the nations Your inheritance and the ends of the earth Your possession.
You shall break them with an iron rod and shatter them like a potter's vessel.'"
Now then, O kings, be wise; be warned, O judges of the earth.
Serve the LORD with fear and rejoice with trembling.
Pay homage to the Son, lest He be angry and you perish in the way, for His wrath can flare up in a moment. Blessed are all who take refuge in Him.
O the LORD, how numerous are my foes! Many rise up against me.
Many say of me, "God will not deliver him." Selah.
But You, O the LORD, are a shield around me, my glory, and the One who lifts my head.
I cried aloud to the LORD, and He answered me from His holy hill. Selah.
I lay down and slept; I awoke again, for the LORD sustained me.
I will not fear ten thousands of people who have set themselves against me all around.
Arise, O the LORD! Save me, O my God! For You strike all my enemies on the cheek; You break the teeth of the wicked.
Salvation belongs to the LORD; Your blessing be on Your people! Selah.
Answer me when I call, O God of my righteousness; You have brought me into a broad place amid my distress. Be gracious to me and hear my prayer.
How long, O men, will my honor be turned to shame? How long will you love vanity and pursue falsehood? Selah.
But know that the LORD has set apart the godly for Himself; the LORD hears when I call to Him.
Tremble, yet do not sin; commune with your own hearts upon your beds, and be still. Selah.
Offer sacrifices of righteousness, and trust in the LORD.
Many say, "Who will show us any good?" Let the light of Your face shine upon us, O the LORD.
You have put more joy in my heart than they have when their grain and new wine abound.
I will both lie down and sleep in peace, for You alone, O the LORD, make me dwell in safety.
Give ear to my words, O LORD; ponder my meditation.
Attend to the voice of my cry, my King and my God, for to You I pray.
In the morning, O LORD, You hear my voice; in the morning I set my prayer in order before You and wait expectantly.
For You are not a God who delights in wickedness; evil cannot dwell with You.
The arrogant cannot stand before Your eyes; You hate all who practice iniquity.
You destroy those who speak lies; the LORD abhors the bloodthirsty and deceitful.
But I, through the abundance of Your steadfast love, will enter Your house; in reverence for You I will bow toward Your holy temple.
Lead me, O LORD, in Your righteousness because of my adversaries; make Your path straight before me.
For nothing reliable dwells in their mouths; destruction fills their inmost being; their throats are open graves; their tongues deal in flattering deceit.
Declare them guilty, O God; let them fall by their own counsels; drive them out for the multitude of their transgressions, for they have rebelled against You.
But let all who take refuge in You rejoice; let them sing aloud forever. Spread Your protection over them, so that those who love Your name may exult in You.
For You, O LORD, bless the righteous; You surround him with favor as with a shield.
For the director of music, with stringed instruments, according to Sheminith—a psalm of David. The LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger, and do not discipline me in Your wrath.
Be gracious to me, the LORD, for I am languishing; heal me, the LORD, for my bones are in agony.
My soul is profoundly distressed. But You, the LORD—how long?
Return, the LORD, and deliver my soul; save me for the sake of Your steadfast love.
For in death there is no remembrance of You; in Sheol who will praise You?
I am weary with my groaning; all night I flood my bed with tears; I drench my couch with weeping.
My eye grows dim with grief; it wastes away because of all my foes.
Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity, for the LORD has heard the voice of my weeping.
The LORD has heard my supplication; the LORD accepts my prayer.
All my enemies will be ashamed and utterly dismayed; they will turn back and be put to shame in a moment.
The LORD my God, in You I seek refuge; save me from all my pursuers and deliver me,
lest my soul be torn apart as by a lion, rent with no one to rescue.
The LORD my God, if I have done this, if iniquity clings to my hands,
if I have requited my friend with evil or plundered my adversary unprovoked,
then let my enemy hunt down my life and overtake it; let him crush my life into the dust and consign my glory to the dust. Selah.
Rise up, the LORD, in Your wrath; lift Yourself against the rage of my adversaries. Awaken the justice You have ordained for me.
Let the congregation of nations assemble around You, and over them be exalted on high.
The LORD judges the peoples. Vindicate me, the LORD, according to my righteousness and integrity.
Terminate the malice of the wicked, yet establish the righteous—You who examine hearts and minds, O God.
My shield rests with God, who saves the upright in heart.
God is a righteous judge, a God who is indignant every day.
If a man will not repent, He sharpens His sword; He has bent His bow and made it ready.
He has prepared instruments of death; He makes His arrows fiery shafts.
Behold, the wicked travails in iniquity, conceives trouble, and births deception.
He excavated a pit and deepened it, only to fall into the snare he contrived.
His mischief returns upon his own head, and his violence descends upon his own crown.
I will render thanks to the LORD for His righteousness, and I will sing to the name of the LORD Most High.
The LORD, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth! You have set Your glory above the heavens.
From the mouths of children and infants You have ordained strength, to silence the enemy and the avenger.
When I behold Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and the stars, which You have set in place—
what is man that You are mindful of him, and the son of man that You care for him?
You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor.
You made him ruler over the works of Your hands; You have put all things under his feet:
all sheep and oxen, and even the beasts of the field,
the birds of the air, and the fish of the sea, all that swim the paths of the seas.
The LORD, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!
I will give thanks to the LORD with all my heart; I will recount all Your wonders.
I will be glad and exult in You; I will sing praise to Your name, O Most High.
When my enemies turn back, they stumble and perish before You.
For You have upheld my just cause; You sat enthroned, judging in righteousness.
You have rebuked the nations; You have destroyed the wicked; You have blotted out their name forever and ever.
The enemy has come to an end in everlasting ruins; You have uprooted their cities, and even their memory has perished.
But the LORD sits enthroned forever; He has established His throne for judgment.
He judges the world with righteousness and governs the peoples with equity.
The LORD is a refuge for the oppressed, a stronghold in times of trouble.
Those who know Your name trust in You, for You, the the LORD, have not forsaken those who seek You.
Sing praises to the LORD, who dwells in Zion; declare His deeds among the nations.
For the One who avenges blood remembers; He does not forget the cry of the afflicted.
Be gracious to me, O the LORD; see my affliction from those who hate me. You who lift me up from the gates of death,
that I may declare all Your praises in the gates of Daughter Zion and rejoice in Your salvation.
The nations have sunk into the pit they made; their foot is caught in the net they hid.
The LORD is known by the justice He executes; the wicked are snared by the work of their own hands. Meditation. Selah.
The wicked will return to Sheol—all the nations who forget God.
For the needy will not always be forgotten, nor will the hope of the afflicted perish forever.
Arise, O the LORD! Do not let man prevail; let the nations be judged in Your presence.
Put them in fear, O the LORD; let the nations know that they are but men. Selah.
Why do You, the LORD, stand so far off? Why do You hide Yourself in times of trouble?
In the wicked man's insolence, the poor are hunted relentlessly; may he be ensnared by the very stratagems he has conceived.
Indeed, he exults in his own cravings, commends greed, and treats the LORD with contempt.
In his overweening pride, he refuses to seek God, and every design he entertains assumes that God is absent.
His undertakings prosper at all times; Your judgments are loftier than his vision can reach; he sneers at every adversary.
He assures himself, "I shall never be shaken; age after age, I shall remain untouched by calamity."
His speech brims with curses, deception, and violence; mischief and wickedness lurk beneath his words.
He lurks in ambush near the settlements; in concealed places he murders the innocent; his eyes search furtively for the vulnerable.
He crouches in ambush like a lion in its cover; he lurks to capture the destitute, and he drags them into his snare.
The vulnerable are crushed; they sink down and fall beneath his power.
He tells himself, "God has forgotten; He has turned away His face; He will never notice."
Rise up, the LORD; lift up Your hand, O God; do not forget the afflicted.
Why does the wicked man spurn God and tell himself, "You will never call me to account"?
Yet You do see, for You observe trouble and vexation, in order to take them into Your hands; the helpless entrusts himself to You; You have been the protector of the fatherless.
Shatter the strength of the wicked and the evildoer; pursue his wickedness until You have found nothing left of it.
The LORD is King forever and ever; the nations perish from His land.
You hear, the LORD, the longing of the afflicted; You will strengthen their hearts; You will incline Your ear.
to vindicate the fatherless and the oppressed, so that earthly man may no longer inspire terror.
In the LORD I have taken refuge. How can you say to me, “Flee like a bird to your mountain”?
For indeed, the wicked bend the bow; they set their arrows on the string to shoot from the darkness at the upright in heart.
If the foundations are destroyed, what can the righteous do?
The LORD is in His holy temple; the LORD’s throne is in heaven. His eyes observe; His eyelids examine the sons of men.
The LORD tests the righteous and the wicked, and His soul hates the one who loves violence.
Upon the wicked He will rain down fiery coals and sulfur; a scorching wind will be their allotted portion.
For the LORD is righteous; He loves righteous deeds. The upright will see His face.
Deliver, O the LORD, for the godly have disappeared; the faithful have vanished from among the children of men.
They speak deception to one another, flattering with their lips while concealing duplicity in their hearts.
May the LORD cut off all flattering lips and the tongue that speaks arrogantly—
those who say, "With our tongues we will prevail; our lips are our own—who is master over us?"
"Because of the oppression of the poor and the groaning of the needy, now I will arise," says the LORD, "I will establish him in the safety for which he longs."
The words of the LORD are immaculate, like silver refined in a furnace upon the earth, purified sevenfold.
You, the LORD, will keep them; You will preserve them from this generation forever.
The wicked prowl on every side when vileness is exalted among the children of men.
How long, O LORD? Will You forget me forever? How long will You hide Your face from me?
How long must I wrestle with my own counsel, bearing grief in my heart day after day? How long will my enemy exalt himself over me?
Consider and answer me, O LORD my God; enlighten my eyes, lest I sleep in death.
Lest my enemy say, “I have prevailed over him,” and my foes exult because I falter.
But I have trusted in Your steadfast love; my heart will rejoice in Your salvation.
I will sing to the LORD, for He has dealt bountifully with me.
For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.” They have corrupted their conduct; their deeds are abominable; no one does what is good.
The LORD looks down from heaven upon the children of men to see whether any understand, whether any seek God.
They have all turned aside; together they have become corrupt. No one does good—not even one.
Do all the evildoers lack understanding? They devour my people as though eating bread, and they do not call upon the LORD.
There they are, overwhelmed with dread, for God is with the generation of the righteous.
You have frustrated the plans of the poor, but the LORD is their refuge.
Oh, that salvation for Israel would come out of Zion! When the LORD restores the fortunes of His people, let Jacob rejoice and Israel be glad.
A psalm of David. The LORD, who may sojourn in Your tent? Who may dwell upon Your holy hill?
He who walks in integrity and practices righteousness,
who does not slander with his tongue, who does no evil to his neighbor, and who does not take up a reproach against his friend;
who regards the vile as contemptible but honors those who fear the the LORD, who keeps his oath even when it proves costly;
who lends his money without usury and does not accept a bribe against the innocent. Whoever does these things shall never be shaken.
A Miktam of David. Preserve me, O God, for in You I have taken refuge.
I said to the the LORD, “You are my Lord; apart from You I have no good thing.”
As for the holy ones in the land, they are the noble ones in whom is all my delight.
The sorrows of those who run after another god will multiply; I will not pour out their drink offerings of blood, nor take their names upon my lips.
The LORD is my chosen portion and my cup; You uphold my lot.
The boundary lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; indeed, my inheritance is beautiful.
I will bless the the LORD, who counsels me; even at night my conscience instructs me.
I have set the the LORD always before me; because He is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.
Therefore my heart is glad, and my whole being rejoices; my body also will dwell in safety.
For You will not abandon my soul to Sheol, nor will You let Your Holy One see decay.
You will make known to me the path of life; in Your presence there is fullness of joy; at Your right hand are pleasures forevermore.
Hear, O the LORD, my righteous plea; attend to my cry; give ear to my prayer, which does not arise from deceitful lips.
May my vindication come forth from Your presence; may Your eyes behold what is upright.
You have tested my heart; You have visited me in the night; You have refined me, and You will find no evil design; my mouth will not transgress.
As for the deeds of men, by the word of Your lips I have kept myself from the paths of the violent.
My steps have held fast to Your paths; my feet have not slipped.
I call upon You, for You will answer me, O God; incline Your ear to me and hear my word.
Show the wonders of Your loving devotion, O Savior of those who take refuge at Your right hand against those who rise up.
Keep me as the most treasured thing in Your sight; hide me in the shadow of Your wings.
From the wicked who assail me, from my mortal enemies who surround me.
They have closed their callous hearts; with their mouths they speak arrogantly.
They have tracked me down; now they surround me; they set their eyes to cast me to the ground.
They are like a lion eager to tear, like a young lion lurking in ambush.
Arise, O the LORD; confront them, bring them down; deliver my soul from the wicked by Your sword—from men of the world whose portion is in this life.
You fill their bellies with Your treasure; their sons are satisfied, and they leave their abundance to their children.
As for me, I shall behold Your face in righteousness; when I awake, I shall be satisfied with Your likeness.

For the choirmaster. Of David, the servant of the LORD, who sang this song to the LORD on the day the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul. He said: “I love You, O the LORD, my strength.
The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer; my God is my rock, in whom I take refuge, my shield and the power of my salvation, my stronghold.
I call upon the LORD, who is worthy of praise, and I am saved from my enemies. “
The cords of death entangled me, and the torrents of destruction overwhelmed me.
The cords of Sheol coiled around me; the snares of death confronted me.
In my distress I called upon the LORD; I cried to my God for help. From His temple He heard my voice, and my cry for help reached His ears. “
Then the earth reeled and quaked, and the foundations of the mountains trembled; they were shaken because He was angry.
Smoke rose from His nostrils, and consuming fire came from His mouth; glowing coals blazed forth from Him.
He parted the heavens and came down, with thick darkness beneath His feet.
He rode upon a cherub and flew; He soared on the wings of the wind.
He made darkness His hiding place, His canopy around Him—darkness of waters and thick clouds of the skies.
From the brightness before Him, His clouds passed through, with hail and coals of fire.
The LORD thundered in heaven; the voice of the Most High resounded with hail and coals of fire.
He shot His arrows and scattered the foes, and He hurled lightning and routed them.
The channels of the sea were exposed, and the foundations of the world were laid bare at Your rebuke, O the LORD, at the blast of the breath of Your nostrils. “
He reached down from on high and took hold of me; He drew me out of deep waters.
He rescued me from my powerful enemy, from my foes who were too strong for me.
They confronted me in the day of my calamity, but the LORD was my support.
He brought me out into a spacious place; He rescued me because He delighted in me. “
The LORD has rewarded me according to my righteousness; He has repaid me according to the cleanness of my hands.
For I have kept the ways of the LORD and have not wickedly departed from my God.
For all His ordinances are before me; I have not turned away from His statutes.
I have been blameless before Him and have kept myself from iniquity.
So the LORD has repaid me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands in His sight. “
To the faithful You show Yourself faithful, to the blameless You show Yourself blameless, to the pure You show Yourself pure, but to the crooked You show Yourself shrewd.
You save an afflicted people, but You humble arrogant eyes.
For You, the LORD, light my lamp; my God illuminates my darkness. “
For You, O the LORD, light my lamp; my God illuminates my darkness.
For with You I can charge through a troop, and with my God I can scale a wall.
As for God, His way is perfect; the word of the LORD is flawless. He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him. “
For who is God besides the LORD? And who is the Rock except our God?
It is God who arms me with strength and makes my way blameless.
He makes my feet like those of a deer and sets me upon the heights.
He trains my hands for battle; my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
You have given me the shield of Your salvation; Your right hand sustains me, and Your gentleness makes me great.
You have enlarged my steps beneath me, so that my feet have not slipped. “
I pursued my enemies and overtook them; I did not turn back until they were consumed.
I crushed them so that they could not rise; they fell beneath my feet.
You have armed me with strength for the battle; You have subdued my adversaries beneath me.
You have made my enemies turn their backs to me, and I annihilated those who hated me.
They cried for help, but there was no one to save them—even to the LORD, but He did not answer.
I ground them as dust before the wind; I trampled them like mud in the streets. “
You have delivered me from the strife of the people; You have made me the head of nations; a people I did not know serve me.
As soon as they hear me, they obey me; foreigners cringe before me.
Foreigners fade away and come trembling from their strongholds. “
The LORD lives! Blessed be my Rock! Exalted be the God of my salvation!
He is the God who avenges me and subdues nations beneath me,
who delivers me from my enemies. You exalt me above my foes; You rescue me from violent men.
Therefore I will praise You among the nations, O the LORD; I will sing praises to Your name.
He gives great victories to His king; He shows steadfast love to His anointed, to David and his descendants forever.”
The heavens declare the glory of God, and the expanse proclaims the work of His hands.
Day after day they pour forth speech, and night after night they reveal knowledge.
They have no speech and no words; their voice is not heard.
Yet their message goes out through all the earth, and their words reach to the ends of the world. In the heavens He has pitched a tent for the sun—
like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, like a champion rejoicing to run his course.
It rises at one end of the heavens and travels to the other, and nothing is hidden from its heat.
The law of the LORD is perfect, restoring the soul; the testimony of the LORD is trustworthy, making wise the simple.
The precepts of the LORD are right, bringing joy to the heart; the commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes.
The fear of the LORD is clean, enduring forever; the judgments of the LORD are true and altogether righteous.
They are more desirable than gold, even much fine gold; they are sweeter than honey, even honey from the comb.
Moreover, by them Your servant is warned; in keeping them there is great reward.
Who can discern his own errors? Cleanse me from hidden faults.
Keep back Your servant also from presumptuous sins; do not let them rule over me. Then I shall be blameless and innocent of great transgression.
May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in Your sight, O the LORD, my Rock and my Redeemer.
May the LORD answer you in your day of distress; may the name of the God of Jacob set you securely on high.
May He send you help from the sanctuary and sustain you from Zion.
May He remember all your sacrifices and regard your burnt offerings with favor. Selah
May He grant you the desires of your heart and bring all your plans to fruition.
Let us shout for joy at your deliverance and raise our banners in the name of our God. May the LORD fulfill all your petitions.
Now I know that the LORD delivers His anointed; He answers him from His holy heaven with the mighty salvation of His right hand.
Some put their trust in chariots and others in horses, but we trust in the name of the LORD our God.
They collapse and fall, but we rise and stand firm.
The LORD, save the king! Answer us when we call.
The king rejoices in Your might, O LORD; how profoundly he exults in Your salvation!
You have granted him his heart’s desire and have not withheld the supplication of his lips. Selah.
For You welcomed him with abundant blessings; You set a crown of pure gold upon his head.
He petitioned You for life, and You bestowed it upon him—length of days forever and ever.
Great is his glory through Your salvation; You confer upon him splendor and majesty.
For You grant him blessings forever; You gladden him with joy in Your presence.
For the king trusts in the LORD; through the loving devotion of the Most High, he shall not be shaken.
Your hand will lay hold of all Your enemies; Your right hand will seize those who hate You.
You will make them like a fiery furnace at the time of Your appearing. In His wrath the LORD will engulf them, and fire will consume them.
You will obliterate their descendants from the earth and their offspring from among humanity.
Though they intended evil against You, the schemes they devised will not prevail.
For You will rout them when You aim Your bow at their faces.
Be exalted, O LORD, in Your might; we will sing and celebrate Your power.
My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from saving me, and so far from heeding my anguished cries?
I cry out to you by day, yet you do not answer; I call by night, but find no rest.
Yet you are enthroned as the Holy One, the praise of Israel.
In you our ancestors trusted; they trusted, and you delivered them.
They cried to you and were rescued; they trusted in you and were never put to shame.
But I am a worm, and not a man—scorned by everyone, despised by the people.
All who see me mock me; they sneer and shake their heads.
"He trusts in the the LORD," they say. "Let the the LORD rescue him. Let him deliver him, since he delights in him."
Yet you brought me forth from the womb; you made me trust in you, even at my mother's breast.
From birth I was cast upon you; from my mother's womb you have been my God.
Do not be far from me, for trouble is near and no helper is at hand.
Many bulls surround me; the strong bulls of Bashan encircle me.
They open their mouths against me like roaring lions that tear their prey.
I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint. My heart has turned to wax; it melts within me.
My strength is dried up like a shard of pottery, and my tongue cleaves to the roof of my mouth; you lay me in the dust of death.
Dogs surround me; a band of evildoers encircles me. They have pierced my hands and my feet.
I can count all my bones; people stare and gloat over me.
They divide my garments among them and cast lots for my clothing.
But you, the the LORD, do not be far from me. You are my strength; come quickly to help me.
Deliver me from the sword, my precious life from the power of the dogs.
Rescue me from the mouth of the lions; save me from the horns of the wild oxen. You have answered me.
I will proclaim your name to my brothers; in the assembly I will praise you.
You who fear the the LORD, praise Him! All you descendants of Jacob, honor Him! Revere Him, all you descendants of Israel!
For He has not despised or scorned the suffering of the afflicted one; He has not hidden His face from him but has listened to his cry for help.
From you comes the theme of my praise in the great assembly; before those who fear Him I will fulfill my vows.
The poor will eat and be satisfied; those who seek the the LORD will praise Him—may your hearts live forever!
All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the the LORD, and all the families of the nations will bow down before you,
for dominion belongs to the the LORD and He rules over the nations.
All the rich of the earth will feast and worship; all who go down to the dust will kneel before Him—those who cannot keep themselves alive.
Posterity will serve Him; future generations will be told about the Lord.
They will proclaim His righteousness, declaring to a people yet unborn: He has done it!
The LORD is my shepherd; I lack nothing.
He lets me rest in verdant meadows and leads me beside tranquil waters.
He revives my spirit and guides me along righteous paths for the sake of His name.
Even though I walk through the darkest valley, I fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff comfort me.
You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows.
Surely goodness and faithful love will follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the the LORD forever.
A psalm of David. The earth, together with everything that fills it, belongs to the LORD, as does the world and all who dwell within it.
For He laid its foundations upon the seas and secured it above the rivers.
Who may ascend the hill of the LORD, and who may stand in His holy sanctuary?
The one whose hands are clean and whose heart is pure, who has not devoted his soul to falsehood or sworn deceitfully.
He will receive a blessing from the LORD and righteousness from God his Savior.
Such is the generation of those who seek Him, who seek Your face, O God of Jacob. Selah.
Lift up your heads, O gates, and be lifted up, O everlasting doors, so that the King of Glory may enter.
Who is this King of Glory? The LORD, strong and mighty; the LORD, mighty in battle.
Lift up your heads, O gates; lift them up, O everlasting doors, so that the King of Glory may enter.
Who is this King of Glory? The LORD of Hosts—He is the King of Glory. Selah.
To You, O the LORD, I lift up my soul.
In You, my God, I trust; let me not be put to shame, and let not my enemies triumph over me.
Indeed, none who wait for You will be put to shame; but those who act treacherously without cause will be ashamed.
Make known to me Your ways, O the LORD; teach me Your paths.
Lead me in Your truth and teach me, for You are the God of my salvation; all day long I wait for You.
Remember Your compassion, O the LORD, and Your steadfast love, for they have been from of old.
Do not remember the sins of my youth or my transgressions; according to Your steadfast love remember me, for the sake of Your goodness, O the LORD.
Good and upright is the the LORD; therefore He instructs sinners in the way.
He leads the humble in justice and teaches the humble His way.
All the paths of the the LORD are steadfast love and faithfulness to those who keep His covenant and His testimonies.
For Your name's sake, O the LORD, pardon my guilt, for it is great.
Who is the man who fears the the LORD? He will instruct him in the way He chooses.
His soul will abide in prosperity, and his offspring will inherit the land.
The LORD confides in those who fear Him, and He makes known to them His covenant.
My eyes are ever toward the the LORD, for He will pluck my feet out of the net.
Turn to me and be gracious to me, for I am lonely and afflicted.
The troubles of my heart have enlarged; bring me out of my distresses.
Look upon my affliction and my trouble, and forgive all my sins.
Consider how many are my foes, and with what violent hatred they hate me.
Guard my soul and deliver me; let me not be put to shame, for I take refuge in You.
May integrity and uprightness preserve me, for I wait for You.
Redeem Israel, O God, from all his troubles.
Vindicate me, O the LORD, for I have walked in my integrity; I have trusted in the the LORD and have not wavered.
Examine me, O the LORD, and test me; refine my heart and mind.
For Your loving devotion is before my eyes, and I have walked in Your truth.
I have not sat with the worthless, nor will I consort with hypocrites.
I hate the assembly of evildoers, and I will not sit with the wicked.
I wash my hands in innocence and walk around Your altar, O the LORD, that I may proclaim thanksgiving aloud and declare all Your wondrous works.
O the LORD, I love the house where You dwell, the place where Your glory resides.
Do not sweep my soul away with sinners, nor my life with bloodthirsty men,
in whose hands are wicked schemes and whose right hands are full of bribes.
But as for me, I will walk in my integrity; redeem me and be gracious to me.
My foot stands on level ground; in the great assembly I will bless the the LORD.
The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the fortress of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
When evildoers advance to devour my flesh, my adversaries and my foes stumble and fall.
Though an army encamp against me, my heart will not fear; though war erupt against me, in this I trust.
One thing I have asked of the LORD, and this I seek: to dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD and to seek Him in His sanctuary.
For in the day of adversity He will conceal me in His shelter; He will hide me in the secret place of His tent; He will set me high upon a rock.
Then my head will be exalted above my enemies on every side. In His tent I will offer sacrifices with joyful shouts; I will sing and make music to the LORD.
Hear my voice when I call, the LORD; be gracious to me and answer me.
My heart says of You, "Seek His face." Your face, the LORD, I will seek.
Do not avert Your face from me; do not reject Your servant in anger; You have been my help. Do not abandon or forsake me, O God my Savior.
Though my father and mother forsake me, the LORD will receive me.
Teach me Your way, the LORD, and lead me on level ground because of my adversaries.
Do not surrender me to the desire of my foes, for false witnesses have risen against me, uttering violent threats.
I am confident that I will see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living.
Wait for the LORD; be strong, and let your heart take courage; wait for the LORD.
To You, O the LORD, I call; my Rock, do not be deaf to me. For if You remain silent, I shall become like those who descend into the pit.
Hear the voice of my supplications when I cry to You for help, when I lift my hands toward Your holy sanctuary.
Do not drag me away with the wicked, with those who practice iniquity, who speak peace to their neighbors while malice fills their hearts.
Repay them according to their deeds and the wickedness of their actions; repay them according to the work of their hands, and render to them their due.
Because they do not comprehend the works of the the LORD or the work of His hands, He will tear them down and never rebuild them.
Blessed be the the LORD, for He has heard the voice of my supplications.
The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart has trusted in Him, and I was helped. Therefore my heart exults, and with my song I will praise Him.
The LORD is strength to His people and a stronghold of salvation for His Anointed.
Save Your people and bless Your inheritance; shepherd them and carry them forever.
A psalm of David. Ascribe to the LORD glory and strength, O sons of God; ascribe to the LORD the glory due His name.
Worship the LORD in the splendor of His holiness.
The voice of the LORD resounds over the waters; the God of Glory thunders; the LORD presides over the many waters.
The voice of the LORD is powerful; the voice of the LORD is majestic.
The voice of the LORD breaks the cedars; indeed, the LORD shatters the cedars of Lebanon.
He makes Lebanon skip like a calf, and Sirion like a young wild ox.
The voice of the LORD hews forth flames of fire.
The voice of the LORD shakes the wilderness; the LORD shakes the wilderness of Kadesh.
The voice of the LORD twists the oaks and strips the forests bare; and in His temple all cry, “Glory!”
The LORD sat enthroned over the deluge; the LORD is enthroned as King forever.
The LORD gives strength to His people; the LORD blesses His people with peace.
I will extol You, O the LORD, for You have lifted me up and have not allowed my enemies to gloat over me.
O the LORD my God, I cried to You, and You healed me.
O the LORD, You brought my soul up from Sheol; You preserved my life from among those going down to the pit.
Sing to the LORD, you His faithful ones, and give thanks to His holy name.
For His anger lasts but a moment, while His favor lasts a lifetime; weeping may lodge for the night, but joy comes with the morning.
In my prosperity I said, “I shall never be shaken.”
O the LORD, by Your favor You made my mountain stand firm; You hid Your face, and I was dismayed.
I cried to You, O the LORD; I sought mercy from my Lord:
“What profit is there in my death if I go down to the pit? Will the dust praise You? Will it declare Your faithfulness?”
Hear, O the LORD, and be gracious to me; O the LORD, be my helper.
You have turned my mourning into dancing; You have removed my sackcloth and clothed me with gladness,
so that my whole being may sing Your praise and never be silent. O the LORD my God, I will give thanks to You forever.
For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. In You, O the LORD, I have taken refuge; let me never be put to shame; deliver me in Your righteousness.
Turn Your ear to me and rescue me quickly; be my rock of refuge, a strong fortress that saves me.
For You are my rock and my fortress; lead me and guide me for Your name's sake.
Free me from the net they have hidden for me, for You are my stronghold.
Into Your hand I commit my spirit; You have redeemed me, O the LORD, God of truth.
I hate those who devote themselves to worthless idols, but as for me, I trust in the LORD.
I will be glad and rejoice in Your steadfast love, for You have seen my affliction; You have known the anguish of my soul.
You have not handed me over to the enemy; You have set my feet in a safe, open place.
Be gracious to me, O the LORD, for I am in distress; my eyes grow weak with sorrow, as do my soul and body.
For my life is consumed with grief and my years with groaning; my iniquity has sapped my strength, and my bones waste away.
Because of all my adversaries I have become a reproach, especially to my neighbors; I am dreaded by my friends, and those who see me on the street flee from me.
I am forgotten as though I were dead, out of mind; I am like a broken vessel.
For I hear the slander of many; terror is on every side. They conspire together against me and plot to take my life.
But I trust in You, O the LORD; I say, "You are my God."
My times are in Your hands; deliver me from my enemies and from those who pursue me.
Look upon Your servant with favor; save me by Your steadfast love.
O the LORD, let me not be put to shame, for I call upon You. Let the wicked be put to shame; let them be silenced in the grave.
Let lying lips be silenced—those that speak arrogantly against the righteous with pride and contempt.
How great is Your goodness, which You have stored up for those who fear You and shown openly before all people for those who take refuge in You!
You hide them in the shelter of Your presence from human plots; You conceal them in Your pavilion from contentious tongues.
Blessed be the LORD, for He has shown me His wonderful steadfast love in a besieged city.
In my alarm I said, "I am cut off from Your sight!" Yet You heard my cry for mercy when I called to You.
Love the LORD, all His godly ones! The LORD preserves the faithful, but He fully repays the arrogant.
Be strong and let your heart take courage, all you who hope in the LORD.
Blessed is the one whose transgressions are forgiven, whose sins are covered.
Blessed is the man whose iniquity the LORD does not count against him and in whose spirit there is no deceit.
When I kept silent, my bones became brittle through my groaning all day long.
For day and night Your hand was heavy upon me; my strength was drained as in the summer heat. Selah
Then I acknowledged my sin to You and did not cover up my iniquity. I said, “I will confess my transgressions to the LORD,” and You forgave the guilt of my sin. Selah
Therefore let every godly man pray to You while You may be found; surely when great waters rise, they will not reach him.
You are my hiding place; You will protect me from trouble and surround me with songs of deliverance. Selah
“I will instruct you and teach you the way you should go; I will counsel you with My eye upon you.
Do not be like the horse or the mule, which lack understanding and must be controlled by bit and bridle, or they will not come near you.”
Many are the sorrows of the wicked, but loving devotion surrounds the one who trusts in the LORD.
Be glad in the LORD and rejoice, you righteous; shout for joy, all you upright in heart.
Rejoice in the LORD, O righteous ones; praise is fitting for the upright.
Praise the LORD with the harp; make music to Him on the ten-stringed lyre.
Sing to Him a new song; play skillfully with a shout of joy.
For the word of the LORD is upright, and all His work is done in faithfulness.
He loves righteousness and justice; the earth is full of the LORD's steadfast love.
By the word of the LORD the heavens were made, and by the breath of His mouth all their host.
He gathers the waters of the sea into a heap; He stores the ocean depths in His storehouses.
Let all the earth fear the LORD; let all the inhabitants of the world stand in awe of Him.
For He spoke, and it came to be; He commanded, and it stood firm.
The LORD nullifies the counsel of the nations and frustrates the plans of the peoples.
The counsel of the LORD stands forever, the plans of His heart to all generations.
Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD, the people He has chosen as His inheritance.
The LORD looks down from heaven; He sees all the sons of men.
From His dwelling place He gazes on all the inhabitants of the earth.
He who fashions their hearts considers all their works.
The king is not saved by a great army; a warrior is not delivered by great strength.
The horse is a false hope for salvation, and its great strength cannot deliver.
Behold, the eye of the LORD is on those who fear Him, on those who hope in His steadfast love,
to deliver their lives from death and to sustain them in famine.
Our soul waits for the LORD; He is our help and our shield.
For our heart rejoices in Him, because we have trusted in His holy name.
Let Your steadfast love, O LORD, be upon us, according as we have hoped in You.
I will bless the LORD at all times; His praise shall be continually in my mouth.
My soul boasts in the LORD; let the humble hear and rejoice.
