Oh, magnify the LORD with me, and let us exalt His name together.
I sought the LORD, and He answered me; He delivered me from all my fears.
Those who look to Him are radiant, and their faces shall never be put to shame.
This poor man cried out, and the LORD heard him and saved him from all his troubles.
The angel of the LORD encamps around those who fear Him, and He delivers them.
Oh, taste and see that the LORD is good! Blessed is the man who takes refuge in Him.
Fear the LORD, you His saints, for those who fear Him have no lack.
The young lions suffer want and hunger, but those who seek the LORD lack no good thing.
Come, O children, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the LORD.
What man is there who desires life and loves many days, that he may see good?
Keep your tongue from evil and your lips from deceit.
Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.
The eyes of the LORD are toward the righteous, and His ears are toward their cry.
The face of the LORD is against those who do evil, to cut off their memory from the earth.
When the righteous cry for help, the LORD hears and delivers them from all their troubles.
The LORD is near to the brokenhearted and saves the crushed in spirit.
Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but the LORD delivers him from them all.
He keeps all his bones; not one of them is broken.
Evil shall slay the wicked, and those who hate the righteous will be condemned.
The LORD redeems the life of His servants; none of those who take refuge in Him will be condemned.
Strive, O the LORD, with my adversaries; wage war against those who war against me.
Take hold of shield and buckler, and rise to my aid.
Brandish spear and javelin against my pursuers; say to my soul, “I am your salvation.”
Let those who seek my life be dishonored and disgraced; let those who devise evil against me be turned back and confounded.
Let them be like chaff before the wind, with the angel of the LORD driving them away.
Let their path be dark and slippery, with the angel of the LORD pursuing them.
For without cause they hid their net for me; without cause they dug a pit for my soul.
Let ruin come upon them unawares; let the net they hid ensnare them; let them fall into it, to their ruin.
Then my soul will rejoice in the LORD and exult in His salvation.
All my bones will say, “the LORD, who is like You, delivering the poor from those too strong for them, the poor and needy from those who rob them?”
Malicious witnesses rise up; they ask me of things I do not know.
They repay me evil for good, to the bereavement of my soul.
Yet when they were sick, I wore sackcloth; I humbled my soul with fasting, and I prayed with my head bowed upon my chest.
I went about as though he were my friend or my brother; I bowed down in mourning, as one grieving for his mother.
But when I stumbled, they rejoiced and gathered together; attackers gathered against me without my knowledge; they slandered me without ceasing.
Like godless mockers at a feast, they gnashed their teeth at me.
O Lord, how long will You look on? Rescue my soul from their ravages, my precious life from the lions.
Then I will give You thanks in the great assembly; I will praise You among many people.
Let not my enemies gloat over me without cause, nor those who hate me without reason wink maliciously.
For they do not speak peace, but devise deceitful schemes against those who live quietly in the land.
They gape at me and say, “Aha, aha! Our eyes have seen!”
O the LORD, You have seen; be not silent. O Lord, be not far from me.
Awake and rise to my defense, to my cause, my God and my Lord.
Vindicate me by Your righteousness, O the LORD my God, and do not let them gloat over me.
Let them not say in their hearts, “Aha! We have swallowed him up!” Let them not say, “We have devoured him!”
May all who gloat over my distress be ashamed and confounded; may those who exalt themselves over me be clothed with shame and disgrace.
May those who favor my righteous cause shout for joy and be glad; may they ever say, “The LORD be magnified, who delights in the prosperity of His servant.”
Then my tongue will proclaim Your righteousness and Your praises all day long.
An oracle stirs within my heart concerning the transgression of the wicked: no fear of God stands before his eyes.
For in his own sight he flatters himself beyond measure, so that he cannot discern or abhor his sin.
The words of his mouth are iniquity and deceit; he has ceased to act wisely and do good.
Even upon his bed he devises wickedness; he places himself on a path that is not good; he does not reject evil.
Your loving devotion, O the LORD, reaches to the heavens; Your faithfulness extends to the clouds.
Your righteousness is like the mountains of God; Your judgments are like the great deep. O the LORD, You preserve both man and beast.
How precious is Your loving devotion, O God! Both men and the sons of men take refuge in the shadow of Your wings.
They feast on the abundance of Your house, and You give them drink from Your river of delights.
For with You is the fountain of life; in Your light we see light.
Extend Your loving devotion to those who know You, and Your righteousness to the upright in heart.
Let not the foot of the proud come against me, nor the hand of the wicked drive me away.
There the evildoers have fallen; they are thrown down and cannot rise.
Do not be vexed by evildoers, nor envy those who practice iniquity.
For they will soon be mown down like grass and wither like tender herbs.
Trust in the LORD and do good; dwell in the land and rest secure in His faithfulness.
Take delight in the LORD, and He will grant the desires of your heart.
Commit your course to the LORD; rely upon Him, and He will accomplish it.
He will bring forth your vindication like the dawn and your justice like the noonday sun.
Be still before the LORD and wait patiently for Him; do not be vexed by the prosperous wrongdoer, by the man who executes wicked schemes.
Desist from anger and forsake wrath; do not be vexed, for it leads only to evil.
For evildoers will be cut off, but those who hope in the LORD will inherit the land.
In a little while the wicked will be no more; though you search for them, they will not be found.
But the meek will inherit the land and delight in abundant peace.
The wicked plot against the righteous and gnash their teeth at them;
but the Lord laughs at them, for He sees that their day is approaching.
The wicked have drawn the sword and bent the bow to cast down the poor and needy, to slaughter those whose conduct is upright.
Yet their sword will pierce their own hearts, and their bows will be shattered.
Better is the little that the righteous possess than the abundance of many wicked;
for the arms of the wicked will be broken, but the LORD sustains the righteous.
The LORD knows the days of the blameless, and their inheritance will endure forever.
In times of calamity they will not be put to shame, and in days of famine they will be satisfied.
But the wicked will perish, and the LORD's enemies, like the splendor of the pastures, will vanish; like smoke they will vanish away.
The wicked borrow and do not repay, but the righteous are gracious and generous.
Surely those blessed by Him will inherit the land, but those cursed by Him will be cut off.
The steps of a man are established by the LORD, and He delights in his way.
Though he stumble, he will not be cast down, for the LORD upholds him with His hand.
I have been young and now am old, yet I have never seen the righteous forsaken, nor their children begging for bread.
They are ever generous and lend freely, and their children are blessed.
Turn from evil and do good, and you will dwell in the land forever.
For the LORD loves justice and will not forsake His saints; they are preserved forever, but the offspring of the wicked will be cut off.
The righteous will inherit the land and dwell in it forever.
The mouth of the righteous utters wisdom, and his tongue speaks justice.
The law of his God is in his heart; his feet do not slip.
The wicked lie in wait for the righteous and seek to slay them;
but the LORD will not abandon them to the power of the wicked, nor condemn them when they are brought to judgment.
Wait for the LORD and keep His way, and He will exalt you to inherit the land; you will witness the destruction of the wicked.
I have seen a ruthless wicked man flourishing like a luxuriant tree in its native soil;
yet he passed away and was no more; though I sought him, he could not be found.
Consider the blameless and observe the upright, for a future awaits the man of peace.
But transgressors will be utterly destroyed; the future of the wicked will be cut off.
The salvation of the righteous comes from the LORD; He is their stronghold in time of trouble.
The LORD helps them and delivers them; He rescues them from the wicked and saves them, because they take refuge in Him.
A Psalm of David, to bring to remembrance. The LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger, nor discipline me in Your wrath.
For Your arrows have sunk deep into me, and Your hand has fallen heavily upon me.
There is no health in my body because of Your indignation; there is no wholeness in my bones because of my sin.
For my iniquities have risen above my head; like a heavy burden, they weigh me down more than I can bear.
My wounds reek and fester because of my folly.
I am bent over and brought low; all day long I go about in mourning.
For my sides are filled with searing pain, and there is no health in my flesh.
I am feeble and utterly crushed; I groan because of the anguish of my heart.
O Lord, all my longing is before You, and my sighing is not hidden from You.
My heart pounds, my strength has left me, and even the light of my eyes has failed me.
My friends and companions keep their distance from my affliction, and my relatives stand far off.
Those who seek my life set traps for me; those who seek my ruin speak of destruction and plot deceit all day long.
But I am like a deaf man who does not hear, like a mute man who cannot open his mouth.
I have become like one who cannot hear, and in whose mouth there is no defense.
But I put my hope in You, the LORD; You will answer, O Lord my God.
For I said, "Do not let them gloat over me, those who boast against me when my foot slips."
For I am about to collapse, and my pain is always before me.
I confess my guilt; I am distressed over my sin.
My enemies are strong and active, and those who hate me without cause have multiplied.
Those who repay good with evil oppose me because I pursue what is good.
The LORD, do not forsake me; O my God, do not be far from me.
Come quickly to my aid, O Lord, my salvation.
I said, "I will guard my ways, lest I sin with my tongue; I will muzzle my mouth while the wicked stand before me."
I was struck dumb with silence; I refrained from speaking even what was good, and my grief was aggravated.
My heart grew hot within me; as I mused, fire burned, and I spoke with my tongue.
Make known to me, O the LORD, my end and the measure of my days, that I may know how fleeting I am.
Behold, You have made my days a few handbreadths, and my lifetime is as nothing before You; surely every man stands as a mere breath. Selah.
Surely a man goes about as a mere shadow; surely they bustle in vain; he amasses wealth without knowing who will collect it.
And now, O Lord, what do I wait for? My hope is in You.
Deliver me from all my transgressions; do not make me the reproach of a fool.
I am mute; I do not open my mouth, for You have done it.
Remove Your plague from me; I am consumed by the blow of Your hand.
You discipline a man with rebukes for iniquity, consuming his treasure like a moth; surely every man is but a breath. Selah.
Hear my prayer, O the LORD, and attend to my cry; do not be deaf to my tears, for I am a sojourner with You, a temporary resident like all my fathers.
Turn Your gaze away from me, that I may smile again, before I depart and am no more.
I waited patiently for the LORD, and He inclined to me and heard my cry.
He drew me up from the pit of destruction, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, steadying my steps.
He placed a new song in my mouth—a hymn of praise to our God. Many will see and stand in awe, and they will trust in the LORD.
Blessed is the man who makes the LORD his trust and does not turn to the arrogant or to those who stray after falsehood.
Many are the wonders You have performed, O the LORD my God, and the plans You have devised for us are beyond reckoning; if I tried to proclaim and recount them, they would exceed all number.
Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but You have opened my ears to hear Your will; burnt offering and sin offering You did not require.
Then I said, "Here I am; I have come, as it is written of me in the scroll of the book."
I delight to do Your will, O my God; Your law is written within my heart.
I have proclaimed righteousness in the great assembly; I have not held back my lips, as You know, O the LORD.
I have not hidden Your righteousness in my heart; I have spoken of Your faithfulness and Your salvation; I have not concealed Your steadfast love and Your truth from the great assembly.
You, O the LORD, will not withhold Your compassion from me; Your steadfast love and truth will continually guard me.
For evils beyond number have surrounded me; my iniquities have overtaken me, until I cannot see; they outnumber the hairs of my head, and my heart has failed me.
Be pleased, O the LORD, to deliver me; hurry, O the LORD, to help me.
May those who seek my life be ashamed and dismayed together; may those who desire my ruin be turned back and disgraced.
May they be appalled because of their shame—those who say to me, "Aha! Aha!"
May all who seek You rejoice and be glad in You; may those who love Your salvation say continually, "The LORD be magnified!"
But I am poor and needy; may the Lord consider me. You are my help and my deliverer; do not delay, O my God.
For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. Blessed is the one who considers the poor! In the day of trouble, the LORD delivers him.
The LORD protects him and keeps him alive; he is counted blessed in the land, and You do not surrender him to the desire of his enemies.
The LORD sustains him upon his sickbed; You restore him from every illness.
As for me, I said, "O the LORD, be gracious to me; heal my soul, for I have sinned against You!"
My enemies speak evil concerning me: "When will he die, and his name perish?"
If one comes to see me, he speaks falsehood; he gathers iniquity within his heart, and when he departs, he proclaims it abroad.
All who hate me whisper together against me; they devise harm for me.
"A deadly thing is poured out upon him," they say; "he will not rise again from where he lies."
Even my close friend, in whom I trusted, who ate my bread, has lifted his heel against me.
But You, the LORD, be gracious to me and raise me up, that I may repay them.
By this I know that You delight in me: my enemy does not triumph over me.
As for me, You uphold me in my integrity and set me in Your presence forever.
Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting! Amen and Amen.
As a deer longs for flowing streams, so my soul longs for You, my God.
My soul thirsts for God—for the living God. When may I come and behold God's face?
My tears have served as my sustenance day and night, while people deride me continually, asking, “Where is your God?”
These things I remember as I pour out my soul: how I once journeyed with the throng, leading them to the house of God with shouts of joy and thanksgiving, among the festive crowd.
Why are you downcast, O my soul, and why are you disquieted within me? Put your hope in God, for I shall yet praise Him—my Savior and my God.
My soul is downcast within me; therefore I remember You from the land of the Jordan, from the heights of Hermon, from Mount Mizar.
Deep calls to deep at the thunder of Your waterfalls; all Your breakers and waves have swept over me.
By day the LORD bestows His steadfast love, and at night His song is with me—a prayer to the God of my life.
I say to God, my Rock, “Why have You forgotten me? Why must I walk in mourning, oppressed by the foe?”
My foes taunt me with a wound that pierces my bones, saying to me all day long, “Where is your God?”
Why are you downcast, O my soul, and why are you disquieted within me? Put your hope in God, for I shall yet praise Him—my Savior and my God.
Vindicate me, O God, and plead my case against an ungodly nation; deliver me from the deceitful and unjust man.
For You are the God of my strength; why have You rejected me? Why must I go about in mourning because of the enemy’s oppression?
Send forth Your light and Your truth; let them lead me and bring me to Your holy mountain and to Your dwelling places.
Then I will approach the altar of God—to God, my supreme delight—and I will praise You with the harp, O God, my God.
Why are you downcast, O my soul? And why are you disquieted within me? Hope in God, for I will yet praise Him—my Savior and my God.
O God, our ears have heard what our fathers recounted to us—the mighty deeds You performed in their days, in those ancient times.
With Your own hand You drove out the nations and planted our ancestors; You crushed the peoples and made our forebears flourish.

For they did not conquer the land by their own sword, nor did their own arm save them; rather, Your right hand and Your arm, together with the light of Your face, secured their triumph, because You favored them.
You are my King, O God; ordain salvation for Jacob!
Through You we push down our foes; through Your name we trample those who rise against us.
For I do not trust in my bow, and my sword cannot save me.
But You have saved us from our foes and shamed those who hate us.
In God we boast all day long, and we will give thanks to Your name forever. Selah
Yet You have rejected us and brought us to shame, and You no longer go out with our armies.
You turn us back before the foe, and those who hate us plunder us.
You hand us over like sheep to be slaughtered and scatter us among the nations.
You sell Your people for a pittance, demanding no great price for them.
You make us a reproach to our neighbors, a scorn and a derision to those around us.
You make us a byword among the nations, a laughingstock among the peoples.
All day long my disgrace is before me, and shame has covered my face,
at the taunt and reproach of the scoffer, before the enemy and the avenger.
All this has befallen us, yet we have not forgotten You, and we have not dealt falsely with Your covenant.
Our heart has not turned back, nor have our steps strayed from Your path;
yet You have shattered us in the haunt of jackals and covered us with the shadow of death.
If we had forgotten the name of our God or stretched out our hands to a foreign god,
would not God have discovered it? For He knows the secrets of the heart.
Yet for Your sake we are killed all day long; we are reckoned as sheep for the slaughter.
Awake! Why do You sleep, O Lord? Rouse Yourself! Do not reject us forever!
Why do You hide Your face? Why do You forget our affliction and our oppression?
For our soul is bowed down to the dust; our body clings to the ground.
Rise up and help us! Redeem us for the sake of Your steadfast love!
My heart overflows with a noble theme; I recite my verses to the king, and my tongue is the pen of a skillful writer.
You are the most handsome of men; grace is poured out upon Your lips; therefore God has blessed You forever.
Strap Your sword upon Your thigh, O mighty one, in Your splendor and majesty.
In Your majesty ride forth in victory on behalf of truth, humility, and righteousness; let Your right hand perform awesome deeds.
Your arrows pierce the hearts of the king’s enemies; the nations fall beneath You.
Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom.
You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, Your God, has anointed You above Your companions with the oil of joy.
All Your garments are fragrant with myrrh and aloes and cassia; from palaces of ivory the music of strings makes You glad.
The daughters of kings are among Your honored women; the queen stands at Your right hand in gold of Ophir.
Listen, O daughter! Consider and incline your ear: Forget your people and your father’s house,
and the king will desire your beauty. Bow to Him, for He is your Lord.
The daughter of Tyre will come with a gift, and the wealthy among the people will seek your favor.
All glorious is the princess in her chamber, with gold embroidery.
In colorful garments she is led to the king; her virgin companions are brought to You.
They are led in with joy and gladness; they enter the palace of the king.
Your sons will take the place of your fathers; You will make them princes throughout the land.
I will perpetuate Your name through all generations; therefore the nations will praise You forever and ever.
God is our refuge and our strength, a help exceedingly present in every affliction.
Therefore we shall not fear though the earth be rent asunder and the mountains be cast into the depths of the sea,
though its waters roar and foam and the mountains quake before its swelling surge. Selah.
There is a river whose streams gladden the city of God, the holy dwelling of the Most High.
God is in her midst; she shall not be shaken; God will help her at the break of dawn.
The nations rage and the kingdoms totter; He lifts His voice, and the earth dissolves.
The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold. Selah.
Come, behold the works of the LORD, the desolations He has wrought upon the earth.
He causes wars to cease to the very ends of the earth; He shatters the bow and breaks the spear; He burns the chariots with fire.
“Cease your striving and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted in the earth.”
The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold. Selah.
Clap your hands, all peoples; shout to God with a voice of jubilation.
For the LORD Most High is awesome, a great King over all the earth.
He subdues peoples beneath us and nations under our feet.
He chooses our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob, whom He loves. Selah.
God has ascended amid shouting, the LORD amid the sound of a trumpet.
Sing praises to God, sing praises; sing praises to our King, sing praises.
For God is King of all the earth; sing praises with understanding.
God reigns over the nations; God sits on His holy throne.
The nobles of the peoples gather as the people of the God of Abraham, for the shields of the earth belong to God; He is highly exalted.
Great is the LORD, and highly to be praised in the city of our God, upon His holy mountain.
Beautiful in its lofty situation, the joy of all the earth, Mount Zion stands on the northern slopes—the city of the great King.
God is known in her citadels as a stronghold.
For behold, the kings assembled and advanced together.
They looked, and they were thunderstruck; seized by panic, they fled.
Trembling seized them on the spot, anguish like that of a woman in labor.
By an east wind You shatter the ships of Tarshish.
As we have heard, so have we seen in the city of the LORD of Hosts, in the city of our God: God will establish it forever. Selah
Within Your temple, O God, we meditate on Your loving devotion.
As Your name, O God, so Your praise extends to the ends of the earth; Your right hand is full of righteousness.
Mount Zion rejoices, and the daughters of Judah exult because of Your judgments.
Walk about Zion, encircle her, and count her towers.
Consider her ramparts; pass through her citadels, that you may recount them to the next generation—
that this God is our God forever and ever; He will guide us even to death.
For the choir director: a psalm of the sons of Korah. Hear this, all peoples; give ear, all inhabitants of the world.
Both the lowborn and the highborn, the rich and the poor together—
my mouth speaks wisdom, and the meditation of my heart is understanding.
I will incline my ear to a proverb and unfold my riddle to the music of the harp.
Why should I fear in days of adversity, when deceitful adversaries close in around me?
Those who trust in their wealth and boast in the abundance of their riches.
Yet no one can redeem a brother or pay God his ransom—
for the price of a life is too costly to be paid forever—
so that he might live on endlessly and never see the grave.
For he sees that the wise die; the fool and the brute perish together and leave their wealth to others.
Their inward thought is that their houses will last forever and their dwellings endure for all generations; they call their lands by their own names.
Yet man, though honored, does not remain; he is like the beasts that perish.
Such is the path of the foolish, and of those after them who approve their words. Selah.
Like sheep they are destined for Sheol; death will be their shepherd, and the upright will rule over them in the morning. Their forms will waste away in Sheol, far from their dwellings.
But God will redeem my soul from the hand of Sheol, for He will receive me. Selah.
Do not fear when a man becomes rich, when the glory of his house increases.
For when he dies he carries nothing away; his glory does not descend after him.
For in his lifetime he congratulates himself, and people praise you when you prosper—
yet he must go to the generation of his fathers, and they will never see the light.
Man, though honored and without understanding, is like the beasts that perish.
The Mighty One, God, the LORD, speaks and summons the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting.
From Zion, perfect in beauty, God shines forth.
Our God comes and will not be silent; fire devours before Him, and a tempest rages around Him.
He calls to the heavens above and to the earth, that He may judge His people.
"Gather to Me My faithful ones, who made a covenant with Me by sacrifice."
The heavens declare His righteousness, for God Himself is judge. Selah
"Hear, O My people, and I will speak; O Israel, I will testify against you: I am God, your God.
I do not rebuke you for your sacrifices and burnt offerings, which are ever before Me.
I have no need of a bull from your stall or goats from your pens,
for every beast of the forest is Mine, and the cattle on a thousand hills.
I know every bird of the mountains, and the creatures of the field are Mine.
If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world is Mine and all that is in it.
Do I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats?
Sacrifice a thank offering to God, and fulfill your vows to the Most High.
Call upon Me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you will honor Me."
But to the wicked God says: "What right have you to recite My statutes or to take My covenant on your lips?
For you hate My instruction and turn your back on My words.
When you see a thief, you side with him, and you make common cause with adulterers.
You give your mouth free rein for evil and devote your tongue to deceit.
You sit and speak ill of your brother; you slander your mother's son.
These things you have done, and I kept silent; you thought I was just like you. But now I rebuke you and accuse you to your face.
Consider this, you who forget God, lest I tear you to pieces, with no one to rescue you.
He who sacrifices a thank offering honors Me, and to him who orders his way aright, I will show the salvation of God."
Be gracious to me, O God, according to Your steadfast love; according to Your abundant compassion, blot out my transgressions.
Cleanse me thoroughly from my iniquity, and purify me from my sin.
For I acknowledge my transgressions, and my sin is always before me.
Against You—You alone—I have sinned and done evil in Your sight, so that You may be vindicated in Your words and blameless in Your judgment.
Indeed, I was born in iniquity, and in sin my mother conceived me.
Indeed, You delight in truth in the innermost being, and in the secret place You make wisdom known to me.
Purify me with hyssop, and I shall be clean; wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.
Let me hear joy and gladness; let the bones You have crushed rejoice.
Turn Your face away from my sins, and erase all my iniquities.
Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me.
Do not banish me from Your presence, and do not take Your Holy Spirit from me.
Restore to me the joy of Your salvation, and uphold me with a willing spirit.
Then I will teach transgressors Your ways, and sinners will return to You.
Deliver me from bloodguilt, O God, the God of my salvation, and my tongue will sing of Your righteousness.
O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare Your praise.
For You do not delight in sacrifice, or I would offer it; You are not pleased with burnt offerings.
The sacrifices acceptable to God are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.
In Your favor, do good to Zion; build up the walls of Jerusalem.
Then You will delight in righteous sacrifices, in burnt offerings and whole burnt offerings; then bulls will be offered on Your altar.
Why do you boast of wickedness, O mighty man? God’s loving devotion endures all day long.
Your tongue plots ruin, sharp as a razor, O worker of deceit.
You love evil rather than good, and falsehood rather than speaking what is right. Selah.
You love every word that devours, O treacherous tongue.
But God will bring you down forever; He will snatch you up and tear you from your tent; He will uproot you from the land of the living. Selah.
The righteous will see and fear, and they will laugh at him.
Behold, the man who did not make God his refuge, but trusted in the abundance of his riches and strengthened himself in his wickedness.
But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God; I trust in the loving devotion of God forever and ever.
I will praise You forever, because You have done it. I will wait on Your name, for it is good, in the presence of Your saints.
The fool declares in his heart, "There is no God." They are thoroughly corrupt; they have committed abominable deeds; no one does good.
God gazes down from heaven upon humankind to see whether anyone understands, whether anyone seeks God.
All have turned aside; together they have become corrupt; no one does good, not even one.
Will the evildoers never comprehend? They consume my people as though eating bread; they do not call upon God.
There they are, overwhelmed with dread where no dread existed. God has scattered the bones of those who besieged you; You have put them to shame, for God has rejected them.
If only salvation for Israel would come from Zion! When God restores the fortunes of His captive people, let Jacob rejoice; let Israel be glad.
Deliver me, O God, by Your name; vindicate me by Your might.
Hear my prayer, O God; attend to the words of my mouth.
For strangers have risen against me, and ruthless men seek my life, giving no thought to God. Selah.
Surely God is my helper; the Lord is the sustainer of my soul.
He will requite my foes with evil; in Your faithfulness, annihilate them.
With a willing heart I will sacrifice to You; I will give thanks to Your name, the LORD, for it is good.
For He has delivered me from all trouble, and my eyes have looked upon my foes.
Attend to my prayer, O God, and do not conceal Yourself from my supplication.
Hear me and answer me, for I am restless in my complaint, and I groan aloud.
I am distraught because of the enemy's voice and the oppression of the wicked, for they cast iniquity upon me and persecute me with fury.
My heart is in anguish within me, and the terrors of death have fallen upon me.
Fear and trembling have seized me, and horror has overwhelmed me.
I said, "If only I had the wings of a dove, I would fly away and find rest."
See how far I would flee; I would take refuge in the wilderness.
I would hasten to my refuge, away from the sweeping wind and storm.
O Lord, confound their speech, for I see violence and strife in the city.
Day and night they encircle its walls; iniquity and turmoil are within it.
Desolation is within it; oppression and deceit never leave its streets.
For it is not an enemy who taunts me—otherwise I could bear it; it is not a foe who exalts himself against me—otherwise I could conceal myself from him.
But you are a man like me—my companion, my close friend.
We shared intimate counsel; together we walked among the throng in the house of God.
Let death seize them; let them descend alive into Sheol, for iniquity dwells within them.
I call upon God, and the LORD delivers me.
Morning, noon, and evening I lament and cry out, and He hears my voice.
He redeems my soul in peace from the battle waged against me, for many contend against me.
God will hear and afflict them—He who sits enthroned from eternity—because they have no intention of changing and do not fear God.
He has stretched out his hand against those at peace with him; he has profaned his covenant.
His speech is smooth as butter, yet war is in his heart; his words are softer than oil, but they are drawn swords.
Cast your burden upon the LORD, and He will sustain you; He will never permit the righteous to be shaken.
But You, O God, will cast them into the pit of destruction; bloodthirsty and deceitful men will not live out half their days. But I will trust in You.

For the choirmaster, to the melody “A Dove on Distant Oaks,” a Miktam of David, composed when the Philistines seized him in Gath: Be gracious to me, O God, because mortal men hound me without respite, pressing their attack from dawn until dusk;
my adversaries pursue me relentlessly, for many haughtily oppose me.
Whenever fear assails me, I will place my trust in You;
in God, whose word I praise, I have trusted, and therefore I will not be afraid—what can mere mortal flesh accomplish against me?
All day long they distort my words, and every thought they entertain is bent upon my harm;
they conspire together, lurk in ambush, and watch my steps, just as they have waited to seize my life.
In spite of such wickedness, shall they escape? In Your anger, O God, cast down the nations.
You have tallied my wanderings; place my tears in Your bottle—are they not inscribed in Your book?
Then my enemies will retreat on the day I call, for this I know with certainty: God is on my side.
In God, whose word I praise, and in the the LORD, whose word I praise,
I have trusted; I will not be afraid—what can mortal man do to me?
Your vows rest upon me, O God; I will render thank offerings to You,
for You have delivered my soul from death and my feet from stumbling, so that I may walk before God in the light of life.
Be gracious to me, O God, be gracious to me, for in You my soul takes refuge; in the shadow of Your wings I take refuge, until the calamities pass by.
I cry out to God Most High, to God who brings His purpose to completion for me.
He will send from heaven and save me; He will rebuke those who trample on me. Selah. God will send forth His steadfast love and His faithfulness.
My soul is among lions; I lie down among ravenous beasts—sons of men whose teeth are spears and arrows, and whose tongues are sharp swords.
Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; let Your glory be over all the earth.
They have prepared a net for my steps; my soul is bowed down. They have dug a pit before me, yet they have fallen into it themselves. Selah.
My heart is steadfast, O God, my heart is steadfast. I will sing and make music.
Awake, my glory! Awake, O harp and lyre! I will awaken the dawn.
I will give thanks to You, O Lord, among the peoples; I will sing praises to You among the nations.
For Your loving devotion is great to the heavens, and Your faithfulness reaches to the clouds.
Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; let Your glory be over all the earth.
Do you indeed speak justice, O rulers? Do you judge fairly, O sons of men?
No, in your hearts you devise injustice; your hands mete out violence in the land.
The wicked are estranged from the womb; those who speak lies go astray from birth.
Their venom is like a serpent's venom, like a deaf adder that stops its ear,
so that it cannot hear the voice of charmers or of the skillful enchanter.
O God, shatter their teeth in their mouths; O the LORD, tear out the fangs of the young lions.
May they vanish like water that runs off; when He bends His bow, may His arrows be blunted.
Like a slug that melts as it crawls, like a stillborn child that never sees the sun.
Before your pots can feel the heat of the thorns—whether green or dry—He will sweep them away in a whirlwind.
The righteous will rejoice when they see vengeance; they will bathe their feet in the blood of the wicked.
Then men will say, "Surely the righteous have a reward; surely there is a God who judges on the earth."

For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A miktam of David, when Saul sent men to watch his house in order to kill him. Deliver me from my enemies, O my God; protect me from those who rise up against me.
Deliver me from workers of iniquity, and save me from bloodthirsty men.
For behold, they lie in wait for my life; fierce men conspire against me for no transgression or sin of mine, O the LORD.
Without fault, they run and prepare themselves. Arise to meet me, and see!
And You, O the LORD God of Hosts, the God of Israel, rouse Yourself to punish all the nations; show no mercy to any wicked traitors. Selah.
They return in the evening, snarling like dogs and prowling around the city.
See what they belch from their mouths—swords from their lips—for who can hear?
But You, O the LORD, laugh at them; You scoff at all the nations.
O my Strength, I watch for You, for You, O God, are my fortress.
My God of loving devotion will come to meet me; God will let me see triumph over my enemies.
Do not kill them, lest my people forget; scatter them by Your power, and bring them down, O Lord our shield.
For the sin of their mouths and the words of their lips, let them be ensnared in their pride. For the curses and lies they utter,
consume them in Your wrath; consume them until they are no more, so that it may be known to the ends of the earth that God rules over Jacob. Selah.
They return in the evening, snarling like dogs and prowling around the city.
They scavenge for food and growl if they are not satisfied.
But I will sing of Your strength and proclaim Your loving devotion in the morning. For You are my fortress, my refuge in times of trouble.
O my Strength, I will sing praise to You, for You, O God, are my fortress, my God of loving devotion.

For the choir director. To the tune of “Lily of the Covenant.” A Miktam of David for instruction. When he fought Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab returned and struck down twelve thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt. O God, You have rejected us; You have shattered us; You have been incensed; restore us!
You have shaken the earth and torn it open; heal its breaches, for it is tottering.
You have made Your people experience affliction; You have given us a wine that makes us reel.
You have given a banner to those who fear You, to be raised for the sake of truth. Selah
Save us by Your right hand and answer us, that those You love may be rescued.
God has spoken in His sanctuary: “I will triumph! I will parcel out Shechem and apportion the Valley of Succoth.
“Gilead is Mine, and Manasseh is Mine; Ephraim is My helmet, Judah is My scepter.
“Moab is My washbasin; I claim Edom as My possession; over Philistia I shout in triumph.”
Who will bring me into the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?
Have You not rejected us, O God? Will You not march forth with our armies?
Grant us help in our distress, for human help is futile.
With God we will act valiantly, and He will trample our enemies.
Hear my cry, O God; attend to my prayer.
From the remotest ends of the earth I call to You when my heart is overwhelmed; lead me to the rock that rises higher than I.
For You have been my refuge, a fortified tower against the enemy.
I will abide in Your tabernacle forever; I will seek shelter in the shelter of Your wings. Selah.
For You, O God, have heard my vows; You have granted me the inheritance reserved for those who revere Your name.
Prolong the king's days; may his years span generation after generation.
May he sit enthroned before God forever; ordain Your steadfast love and faithfulness to guard him.
Then I will sing Your praises forever, fulfilling my vows day by day.
Truly my soul waits in silence for God; my salvation comes from Him.
He alone is my rock and my salvation; He is my fortress; I will not be greatly shaken.
How long will you assail a man? All of you will be slain, like a leaning wall, like a tottering fence.
They conspire only to bring him down from his lofty place; they delight in lies. With their mouths they bless, but inwardly they curse. Selah.
Rest in God alone, O my soul, for my hope comes from Him.
He alone is my rock and my salvation; He is my fortress; I will not be shaken.
My salvation and my honor rest on God; my strong rock and my refuge are in God.
Trust in Him at all times, O people; pour out your hearts before Him. God is our refuge. Selah.
Surely the lowborn are but a breath, and the highborn are but a lie; weighed on the scales, they are lighter than a breath.
Do not trust in extortion, or put vain hope in robbery; if riches increase, do not set your hearts on them.
One thing God has spoken; two things I have heard: that power belongs to God,
and that loving devotion belongs to You, O Lord—for You repay each man according to his work.
O God, You are my God; with ardent devotion I seek You. My soul thirsts for You, and my flesh languishes for You in a parched and weary land devoid of water.
Thus I have beheld You in the sanctuary, to gaze upon Your power and glory.
Because Your loving devotion surpasses life itself, my lips will extol You.
Therefore I will bless You throughout my days; in Your name I will lift up my hands.
My soul shall be sated as with the richest fare, and my mouth shall praise You with exultant lips.
When I remember You upon my bed, I meditate upon You through the night watches.
For You have been my help, and in the shadow of Your wings I will sing for joy.
My soul clings to You; Your right hand sustains me.
Yet those who seek my life to destroy it shall descend into the depths of the earth.
They will be delivered to the power of the sword; they will become sustenance for jackals.
But the king will rejoice in God; all who swear by Him will glory, for the mouths of liars will be silenced.
Hear my voice, O God, in my lamentation; preserve my life from the dread inspired by my enemy.
Conceal me from the clandestine counsel of evildoers, from the tumult of those who perpetrate iniquity.
They have whetted their tongues like swords; they have aimed bitter words as though they were arrows.
From ambush they shoot at the blameless; suddenly they loose their shafts, and they entertain no fear.
They fortify one another in wickedness; they conspire to conceal snares, saying, “Who will see us?”
They scrutinize iniquities and complete a meticulous search; the inward thought of each man is profound, and his heart is unfathomable.
But God will shoot at them with an arrow; suddenly they will be wounded.
Their own tongues will precipitate their ruin; all who behold them will recoil.
Then all humanity will fear and proclaim the work of God, for they will discern His deed.
The righteous will rejoice in the LORD and trust in Him; all the upright in heart will glory.
Praise awaits You, O God, in Zion, and to You our vows shall be fulfilled.
You who hear prayer, to You all flesh will come.
My iniquities have overwhelmed me, yet You atone for our transgressions.
Blessed is the one You choose and bring near to dwell in Your courts. We shall be satisfied with the goodness of Your house, the holiness of Your temple.
You answer us with awesome deeds in righteousness, O God of our salvation, You who are the hope of all the ends of the earth and of the farthest seas.
You formed the mountains by Your power, girded with strength.
You stilled the roaring of the seas, the roaring of their waves, and the tumult of the nations.
Thus the inhabitants of the ends of the earth fear Your signs; You make the dawn and the sunset shout for joy.
You visit the earth and water it; You greatly enrich it. The river of God is full of water; You prepare their grain, for so You have prepared it.
You drench its furrows and level its ridges; You soften it with showers and bless its growth.
You crown the year with Your goodness, and Your paths overflow with abundance.
The pastures of the wilderness overflow, and the hills gird themselves with joy.
The meadows are clothed with flocks, and the valleys are decked with grain; they shout and even sing.
Shout for joy to God, all the earth!
Sing the glory of Your name; make Your praise glorious.
Say to God, “How awesome are Your deeds! So great is Your power that Your enemies cringe before You.”
All the earth bows down to You and sings praise to You; they sing praise to Your name. Selah.
Come and see what God has done; He is awesome in His deeds toward mankind.
He turned the sea into dry land; they crossed the river on foot. There we rejoiced in Him.
He rules forever by His might; His eyes keep watch on the nations; let not the rebellious exalt themselves. Selah.
Bless our God, O peoples; let the sound of His praise be heard,
the One who has preserved our lives and has not let us stumble.
For You, O God, have tested us; You have refined us as silver is refined.
You brought us into the net; You laid a crushing burden on our backs.
You allowed people to trample us; we went through fire and water, yet You brought us out into abundance.
I will come into Your house with burnt offerings; I will fulfill my vows to You,
the vows my lips promised and my mouth spoke when I was in distress.
I will offer You burnt offerings of fattened animals, with the incense of rams; I will sacrifice bulls and goats. Selah.
Come and hear, all you who fear God, and I will tell what He has done for my soul.
I cried to Him with my mouth, and His praise was on my tongue.
If I had harbored iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.
But God has truly listened; He has attended to the voice of my prayer.
Blessed be God, because He has not rejected my prayer or withdrawn His steadfast love from me!
For the choirmaster, with stringed instruments—a psalm, a song. May God deal graciously with us and bless us; may He look upon us with favor—Selah.
so that Your way may be known throughout the earth, Your salvation among all nations.
Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You.
Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for You judge the peoples with equity and guide the nations of the earth. Selah.
Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You.
The earth has yielded its harvest; God, our God, blesses us.
God blesses us, that all the ends of the earth may fear Him.
May God arise; let His enemies be scattered; let those who hate Him flee before Him.
As smoke is driven away, so You drive them away; as wax melts before fire, so the wicked perish before God.
But the righteous rejoice and exult before God; they celebrate with joy.
Sing to God, sing praises to His name; extol Him who rides upon the clouds—His name is the LORD—and rejoice before Him.
Father of orphans and defender of widows is God in His holy dwelling.
God settles the lonely in homes; He leads prisoners out into prosperity; but the rebellious dwell in a parched land.
O God, when You went out before Your people, when You marched through the wilderness—Selah.
The earth quaked; the heavens poured down rain before God; even Sinai trembled before God, the God of Israel.
You poured out abundant rain, O God; You restored Your inheritance when it languished.
Your flock settled in it; in Your goodness, O God, You provided for the needy.
The Lord gives the command; the women who proclaim the good news are a mighty host:
“The kings of the armies flee, they flee!” and the women at home divide the spoil—
though you lie among the sheepfolds, the wings of a dove are covered with silver, its pinions with shimmering gold.
When the Almighty scattered kings there, snow fell on Zalmon.
The mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan; the many-peaked mountain is the mountain of Bashan.
Why do you look with envy, O many-peaked mountains, at the mountain God chose for His dwelling? Yes, the LORD will dwell there forever.
The chariots of God are tens of thousands—thousands upon thousands; the Lord is among them; Sinai is now in the sanctuary.
You ascended on high, leading captives in Your train; You received gifts from among men, even from the rebellious, that the LORD God might dwell there.
Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears our burdens; God is our salvation. Selah.
Our God is a God of salvation, and to the LORD, the Lord, belong deliverances from death.
But God will crush the heads of His enemies, the hairy scalp of the one who walks in his guilt.
The Lord said, “I will bring them back from Bashan; I will bring them back from the depths of the sea.”
that Your foot may be dipped in the blood of Your enemies, and the tongues of Your dogs may have their portion from the foe.
Your procession is seen, O God—the procession of my God, my King—into the sanctuary.
The singers go before, the musicians follow after, and among them are maidens playing tambourines:
Bless God in the great congregation; bless the LORD from the fountain of Israel.
There is Benjamin, the youngest, leading them; the princes of Judah in their throng; the princes of Zebulun; the princes of Naphtali.
Summon Your power, O God; the power, O God, by which You have worked for us.
Because of Your temple at Jerusalem, kings will bring gifts to You.
Rebuke the beast of the reeds, the herd of bulls among the calves of the peoples, trampling those who lust after tribute; scatter the peoples who delight in war.
Nobles will come from Egypt; Cush will hasten to stretch out her hands to God.
Sing to God, O kingdoms of the earth; sing praises to the Lord—Selah.
to Him who rides upon the highest heavens, the ancient heavens; behold, He sends out His voice, a mighty voice.
Ascribe power to God, whose majesty is over Israel, whose power is in the skies.
Awesome is God from His sanctuary; the God of Israel—He gives power and strength to His people. Blessed be God!
Save me, O God, for the waters have risen to my very soul.
I have sunk in the mire of the deep, where there is no foothold; I have entered the depths of the waters, and the flood has swept me away.
I am weary with my crying; my throat is parched. My eyes fail while I wait for my God.
Those who hate me without cause are more than the hairs of my head; mighty are my destroyers, my enemies who attack me with lies. What I did not steal, I am forced to restore.
O God, You know my folly, and my guilt is not hidden from You.
Let not those who hope in You be put to shame through me, O Lord, the LORD of Hosts; let not those who seek You be dishonored through me, O God of Israel.
For Your sake I have borne reproach; shame has covered my face.
I have become a stranger to my brothers, an alien to my mother’s sons.
For zeal for Your house has consumed me, and the reproaches of those who reproach You have fallen on me.
I wept and humbled my soul with fasting, but it became a reproach to me.
I made sackcloth my clothing, and I became a byword to them.
Those who sit at the gate gossip about me, and drunkards make songs about me.
But as for me, my prayer is to You, O the LORD, at an acceptable time. O God, in the abundance of Your mercy, answer me in the truth of Your salvation.
Deliver me from the mire, and let me not sink; let me be rescued from those who hate me and from the depths of the waters.
Let not the flood of waters sweep over me, nor the deep swallow me up, nor the pit close its mouth over me.
Answer me, O the LORD, for Your lovingkindness is good; according to the greatness of Your mercies, turn to me.
Hide not Your face from Your servant, for I am in distress; answer me quickly.
Draw near to my soul and redeem it; ransom me because of my enemies.
You know my reproach, my shame, and my dishonor; all my adversaries are before You.
Reproach has broken my heart, and I am sick; I looked for pity, but there was none, and for comforters, but I found none.
They gave me gall for my food, and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
Let their table become a snare before them, and let their well-being become a trap.
Let their eyes be darkened so that they cannot see, and let their loins tremble continually.
Pour out Your indignation upon them, and let Your burning anger overtake them.
Let their camp be desolate; let no one dwell in their tents.
For they persecute him whom You have struck, and they recount the pain of those You have wounded.
Add iniquity to their iniquity, and let them not come into Your righteousness.
Let them be blotted out of the book of life; let them not be recorded among the righteous.
But I am poor and in pain; let Your salvation lift me up.
I will praise the Name of God with a song, and I will magnify Him with thanksgiving.
This will please the LORD more than an ox or a bull with horns and hooves.
The humble will see it and be glad; you who seek God, let your heart live.
For the LORD hears the needy and does not despise His prisoners.
Let heaven and earth praise Him, the seas and everything that moves in them.
For God will save Zion and build the cities of Judah, that they may dwell there and possess it.
The descendants of His servants will inherit it, and those who love His Name will dwell in it.
Make haste, O God, to deliver me; make haste to help me, the LORD.
Let those who seek my life be ashamed and confounded; let those who delight in my calamity be turned back and disgraced.
Let those who cry, "Aha! Aha!" recoil in disgrace.
Let all who seek You rejoice and be glad in You; let those who love Your salvation say continually, "May God be exalted!"
Yet I am poor and needy; hasten to me, O God. You are my help and my deliverer; the LORD, do not delay.
In You, the LORD, I have taken refuge; let me never be put to shame.
In Your righteousness rescue me and deliver me; incline Your ear to me and save me.
Be my rock of refuge, to which I may continually come; You have given command to save me, for You are my rock and my fortress.
Deliver me, my God, from the hand of the wicked, from the grasp of the unjust and cruel.
For You are my hope, O Lord, the LORD, my confidence from my youth.
Upon You I have leaned from birth; You took me from my mother's womb. My praise is continually of You.
I have become a wonder to many, but You are my strong refuge.
My mouth is filled with Your praise and with Your splendor all day long.
Do not cast me off in the time of old age; do not forsake me when my strength fails.
For my enemies speak against me, and those who watch for my life consult together,
saying, “God has forsaken him; pursue and seize him, for there is no one to deliver.”
O God, do not be far from me; my God, hasten to help me.
Let those who accuse my soul be put to shame and consumed; let those who seek my harm be covered with scorn and disgrace.
But as for me, I will hope continually and will praise You more and more.
My mouth will tell of Your righteousness and of Your salvation all day long, for I do not know their full number.
I will come in the strength of the Lord the LORD; I will make mention of Your righteousness, Yours alone.
O God, You have taught me from my youth, and until now I declare Your wondrous works.
And even to old age and gray hair, O God, do not forsake me, until I declare Your strength to this generation, Your power to everyone who is to come.
Your righteousness, O God, reaches to the heavens; You who have done great things, O God, who is like You?
You who have shown me many and grievous troubles will revive me again; from the depths of the earth You will bring me up again.
You will increase my greatness and comfort me on every side.
I will also praise You with the harp, my God; I will sing praises to You with the lyre, O Holy One of Israel.
My lips will shout for joy when I sing praises to You, and my soul, which You have redeemed.
My tongue also will tell of Your righteousness all day long, for those who seek my harm are put to shame and disgraced.
Give the king your judgments, O God, and your righteousness to the king's son.
He will judge your people in righteousness and your afflicted with justice.
The mountains will bring peace to the people, and the hills will bring righteousness.
He will vindicate the afflicted among the people; He will save the children of the needy and crush the oppressor.
They will fear you while the sun endures, and as long as the moon shines, throughout all generations.
He will come down like rain upon freshly mown grass, like showers that water the earth.
In His days the righteous will flourish, and peace will abound until the moon is no more.
He will rule from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth.
Desert nomads will bow before Him, and His enemies will be humbled to the dust.
The kings of Tarshish and of the coastlands will bring tribute; the kings of Sheba and Seba will present gifts.
All kings will bow down to Him, and all nations will serve Him.
For He will deliver the needy who cry out, and the afflicted who have no helper.
He will have compassion on the poor and needy and preserve the lives of the needy.
He will redeem their lives from oppression and violence, and their blood will be precious in His sight.
Long may He live! May gold from Sheba be given to Him. May people pray for Him continually, and may they bless Him all day long.
May there be an abundance of grain in the land; may it wave upon the mountaintops. May its fruit be like the abundance of Lebanon, and may people flourish in the cities like grass upon the earth.
May His name endure forever; may it increase as long as the sun shines. May all nations be blessed in Him, and may they call Him blessed.
Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does wonders.
And blessed be His glorious name forever; may the whole earth be filled with His glory. Amen and Amen.
The prayers of David son of Jesse are ended.
Surely God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart.
But as for me, my feet had nearly slipped; my steps had almost given way.
For I envied the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
They have no struggles in their death; their bodies are well nourished.
They are free from common human burdens; they are not plagued as others.
Therefore pride is their necklace; they clothe themselves with violence.
Their eyes bulge with abundance, and their hearts overflow with schemes.
They scoff and speak wickedly; in their arrogance they threaten oppression.
Their mouths lay claim to heaven, and their tongues take possession of the earth.
Therefore their people turn to them and drink up waters in abundance.
They say, "How would God know? Does the Most High know anything?"
Behold, these are the wicked—always at ease, they amass wealth.
Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure and washed my hands in innocence.
I have been afflicted all day long, and every morning brings new chastening.
If I had spoken thus, I would have betrayed Your children.
When I tried to understand this, it troubled me deeply,
until I entered the sanctuary of God; then I understood their final destiny.
Surely You place them on slippery ground; You cast them down to ruin.
How suddenly are they destroyed, completely swept away by terrors!
They are like a dream when one awakes; when You arise, the Lord, You will despise their image.
When my heart was grieved and my spirit embittered,
I was senseless and ignorant; I was a brute beast before You.
Yet I am always with You; You hold me by my right hand.
You guide me with Your counsel, and afterward You will take me into glory.
Whom have I in heaven but You? And earth has nothing I desire besides You.
My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
Those who are far from You will perish; You destroy all who are unfaithful to You.
But as for me, it is good to be near God. I have made the Lord the LORD my refuge, that I may tell of all Your works.
O God, why have You rejected us forever? Why does Your anger smolder against the sheep of Your pasture?
Remember Your congregation, which You purchased long ago and redeemed as the tribe of Your inheritance—Mount Zion, where You dwell.
Turn Your steps to the everlasting ruins, to all that the enemy has destroyed in the sanctuary.
Your foes have roared within Your meeting place; they have set up their standards as signs.
They behaved like men wielding axes to cut through a thicket of trees.
With axes and hammers they smashed all the carved paneling.
They set Your sanctuary on fire; they profaned the dwelling place of Your Name.
They said in their hearts, “Let us subdue them completely.” They burned down every place where God met us in the land.
There are no signs for us to see; there is no longer any prophet, and none of us knows how long this will last.
How long, O God, will the adversary taunt? Will the enemy revile Your name forever?
Why do You withdraw Your hand? Why do You hold Your right hand behind Your back?
Yet God is my King from ancient times, working salvation on the earth.
You divided the sea by Your strength; You smashed the heads of the dragons of the sea;
You crushed the heads of Leviathan; You fed him to the creatures of the desert.
You split open the springs and torrents; You dried up the ever-flowing rivers.
The day is Yours, and also the night; You established the sun and moon.
You set all the boundaries of the earth; You made the summer and winter.
Remember how the enemy has mocked You, O the LORD, how a foolish people has blasphemed Your name.
Do not deliver the soul of Your dove to wild beasts; do not forget the lives of Your afflicted forever.
Consider Your covenant, for haunts of violence fill the dark places of the land.
Do not let the oppressed retreat in shame; may the poor and needy praise Your name.
Rise up, O God, and defend Your cause; remember how the foolish man mocks You all day long.
Do not ignore the clamor of Your adversaries, the uproar of Your enemies that ascends continually.
We give thanks to You, O God; we give thanks, for Your name is near. People declare Your wonders.
“When I choose an appointed time, I will judge with equity.
When the earth and all its inhabitants tremble, I am the One who holds up its pillars. Selah.
I say to the proud, ‘Do not boast,’ and to the wicked, ‘Do not exalt yourselves.
Do not exalt yourselves on high, nor speak arrogantly.’”
For exaltation comes not from the east or the west, nor from the wilderness,
but from God, who judges; He lowers one and exalts another.
For a cup is in the hand of the LORD, full of foaming wine mixed with spices. He pours it out, and all the wicked of the earth will drink it down to the dregs.
But I will proclaim forever; I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.
“I will cut off all the power of the wicked, but the righteous will be exalted.”
God is known in Judah; His name is great in Israel.
His tabernacle stood in Salem, and His dwelling place in Zion.
There He shattered the flashing arrows—the shield, the sword, and the instruments of war. Selah
You are radiant and majestic, surpassing the mountains where beasts of prey seize their quarry.
The stout-hearted were despoiled; they sank into their final slumber, and no warrior could even raise his hands.
At Your rebuke, O God of Jacob, horse and chariot alike sank into stupor.
You are fearsome indeed; who can stand before You once Your wrath is kindled?
From heaven You proclaimed judgment, and the earth feared and fell silent
when God arose to render judgment and to rescue all the oppressed of the earth. Selah
Surely human wrath will redound to Your praise; You will gird Yourself with the remnant of that fury.
Vow and pay to the the LORD your God; let all who surround Him bring tribute to the One who is to be feared.
He will cut off the spirit of princes; He is to be feared by the kings of the earth.
I cried aloud to God; I cried aloud to God, and He heard me.
In the day of my trouble I sought the the LORD; through the night my hand was stretched out and did not grow weary, yet my soul refused to be comforted.
I remember God, and I groan; I muse, and my spirit grows faint. Selah.
You hold my eyes open; I am so troubled that I cannot speak.
I have considered the days of old, the years of long ago.
At night I remember my song; I meditate in my heart, and my spirit searches deeply.
Will the the LORD reject forever? Will He never show favor again?
Has His steadfast love ceased forever? Has His promise failed for every generation?
Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has He in anger withheld His compassion? Selah.
So I said, "This is my grief: the right hand of the Most High has changed."
I will remember the deeds of the the LORD; yes, I will remember Your wonders of old.
I will meditate on all Your work and ponder Your mighty deeds.
Your way, O God, is holy. What god is great like our God?
You are the God who works wonders; You have made known Your strength among the peoples.
You have redeemed Your people with Your arm, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
The waters saw You, O God; the waters saw You and writhed; the depths also trembled.
The clouds poured out water; the skies resounded with thunder; Your arrows flashed back and forth.
The sound of Your thunder was in the whirlwind; Your lightning lit up the world; the earth trembled and shook.
Your way was in the sea, and Your path through the mighty waters, yet Your footprints were not known.
You led Your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
Listen attentively, my people, to my instruction; turn your ears toward the words of my mouth.
I will open my mouth in a parable; I will utter enigmatic sayings handed down from antiquity,
things that we have heard and known, that our fathers have told us.
We will not hide them from their children, but we will recount to the succeeding generations the renowned acts of the LORD, His power, and the wonders that He has done.
He established a testimony in Jacob and appointed instruction in Israel, which He commanded our fathers to teach to their children,
so that the generation to come might know them, even children yet unborn, and that they might arise and declare them to their children,
so that they might place their confidence in God and not forget God's deeds, but observe His commandments.
They were not to be like their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation, a generation whose heart was not resolute and whose spirit was not faithful toward God.
The Ephraimites, though equipped with bows, retreated on the day of battle.
They did not keep God's covenant, but refused to walk in accordance with His law.
They forgot His works and the wonders that He had shown them.
In the sight of their fathers He performed wonders in the land of Egypt, in the fields of Zoan.
He divided the sea and enabled them to pass through it, causing the waters to stand like a wall.
By day He led them with a cloud, and throughout the night with a blazing fire.
He split rocks in the wilderness and gave them water to drink in abundance, as from the ocean depths.
He brought forth streams from the rock and made waters flow down like rivers.
Yet they continued to sin against Him, rebelling against the Most High in the wilderness.
They tested God in their hearts by demanding the food they craved.
They spoke against God, saying, "Can God set a table in the wilderness?
He struck the rock so that water gushed out and streams overflowed. Can He also give bread, or provide meat for His people?"
Therefore, when the LORD heard, He was filled with wrath; a fire was kindled against Jacob, and His anger rose against Israel,
because they did not believe in God and did not trust in His saving power.
Yet He commanded the skies above and opened the doors of heaven,
and He rained down manna upon them to eat and gave them the grain of heaven.
Mortals ate the bread of the mighty; He sent them provisions in abundance.
He caused the east wind to blow through the heavens, and by His power He led forth the south wind.
He rained meat upon them like dust, winged birds like the sand of the seas.
He let them fall in the midst of their camp, all around their dwellings.
And they ate and were well filled, for He gave them what they craved.
But before they had satisfied their craving, while the food was still in their mouths,
the anger of God rose against them, and He struck down the strongest among them and laid low the young men of Israel.
In spite of all this, they still sinned; despite His wonders, they did not believe.
So He caused their days to vanish like a breath, and their years to end in terror.
When He struck them down, they sought Him; they repented and sought God earnestly.
They remembered that God was their rock, and that the Most High God was their Redeemer.
But they flattered Him with their mouths and lied to Him with their tongues.
Their hearts were not steadfast toward Him, and they were not faithful to His covenant.
Yet He, being compassionate, atoned for their iniquity and did not destroy them; He restrained His anger often and did not stir up all His wrath.
He remembered that they were but flesh, a wind that passes and does not return.
How often they rebelled against Him in the wilderness and grieved Him in the desert!
They tested God again and again and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
They did not remember His power or the day when He redeemed them from the foe.
He performed His signs in Egypt and His marvels in the fields of Zoan.
He turned their rivers to blood, so that they could not drink from their streams.
He sent among them swarms of flies that devoured them, and frogs that destroyed them.
He gave their crops to the destroying locust and the fruit of their labor to the locust.
He destroyed their vines with hail and their sycamore figs with frost.
He gave their cattle over to the hail and their flocks to thunderbolts.
He let loose upon them His burning anger, wrath, indignation, and distress—a company of destroying angels.
He made a path for His anger; He did not spare them from death, but gave their lives over to the plague.
He struck down every firstborn in Egypt, the firstfruits of their strength in the tents of Ham.
Then He led out His people like sheep and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.
He led them in safety, so that they were not afraid, but the sea overwhelmed their enemies.
And He brought them to His holy land, to the mountain that His right hand had won.
He drove out nations before them; He apportioned them a possession and settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.
Yet they tested and rebelled against the Most High God and did not keep His testimonies,
but turned back and acted treacherously like their fathers; they proved as treacherous as a warped bow.
For they provoked Him to anger with their high places and moved Him to jealousy with their idols.
When God heard, He was filled with wrath, and He utterly rejected Israel.
He forsook His dwelling at Shiloh, the tent where He dwelt among mankind,
and delivered His power to captivity and His glory into the hand of the foe.
He gave His people over to the sword and showed wrath against His heritage.
Fire devoured their young men, and their maidens had no nuptial song.
Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows made no lamentation.
Then the Lord awoke as from sleep, like a warrior roused by wine.
And He put His adversaries to rout; He consigned them to everlasting shame.
He rejected the tent of Joseph; He did not choose the tribe of Ephraim,
but He chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which He loves.
He built His sanctuary like the high heavens, like the earth, which He has founded forever.
He chose David His servant and took him from the sheepfolds;
from following the nursing ewes He brought him to shepherd Jacob His people, Israel His inheritance.
With an upright heart he shepherded them and guided them with skillful hand.
O God, the nations have invaded your inheritance; they have defiled your sanctuary and reduced Jerusalem to rubble.
They have given the corpses of your servants to the birds of the sky for food, and the flesh of your faithful to the beasts of the earth.
They have poured out their blood like water all around Jerusalem, and no one remains to bury them.
We have become an object of scorn to our neighbors, a laughingstock and derision to those around us.
How long, O the LORD, will you remain angry forever? Will your jealousy burn like fire?
Pour out your wrath on the nations that do not know you, on the kingdoms that do not call upon your name.
For they have ravaged Jacob and devastated his homeland.
Do not hold against us the sins of past generations; may your compassion come quickly to meet us, for we are brought very low.
Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of your name; deliver us and atone for our sins for the sake of your name.
Why should the nations say, “Where is their God?” Before our eyes, let the nations know that you avenge the blood of your servants that has been poured out.
Let the groaning of the prisoner come before you; by the greatness of your arm, preserve those condemned to die.
Repay our neighbors sevenfold for the insults they have hurled at you, O Lord.
But we, your people and the sheep of your pasture, will give thanks to you forever; from generation to generation we will proclaim your praise.
Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, You who guide Joseph like a flock; You who are enthroned between the cherubim, reveal Your glory.
Before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, awaken Your might and come to our salvation.
Restore us, O God; look upon us with favor, and we shall be saved.
O the LORD God of Hosts, how long will Your wrath burn against the prayers of Your people?
You have given them tears instead of bread and compelled them to drink tears in abundance.
You have made us an object of contention to our neighbors, and our enemies deride us.
Restore us, O God of Hosts; look upon us with favor, and we shall be saved.
You uprooted a vine from Egypt; You expelled the nations and planted it.
You cleared the ground before it, and it took root and filled the land.
The mountains were covered by its shade, and the mighty cedars were overshadowed by its branches.
Its branches reached the Sea, and its shoots stretched to the River.
Why have You torn down its walls, so that every passerby plucks its grapes?
The wild boar from the forest ravages it, and the creatures of the field feed upon it.
Return, O God of Hosts! Look down from heaven and behold; attend to this vine,
the root Your right hand planted, the son You strengthened for Yourself.
It is burned with fire and cut down; they perish at Your fierce rebuke.
Let Your hand rest upon the man at Your right hand, upon the son of man You have strengthened for Yourself.
Then we shall not turn back from You; revive us, and we will call upon Your name.
Restore us, O the LORD God of Hosts; look upon us with favor, and we shall be saved.
Sing aloud to God, our strength; shout for joy to the God of Jacob!
Raise a song; sound the tambourine; play the sweet-sounding lyre together with the harp.
Blow the ram’s horn at the new moon, at the full moon, on the day of our feast.
For it is a statute for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob.
He established it as a testimony for Joseph when He went out over the land of Egypt, where I heard a tongue I had not known:
“I relieved his shoulder of the burden; his hands were freed from the basket.
In your distress you called, and I rescued you; I answered you from the thundercloud; I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah
“Hear, O My people, and I will testify against you—Israel, if only you would listen to Me!
There shall be no foreign god among you; you shall not bow down to a foreign god.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.
“But My people would not listen to My voice; Israel refused to submit to Me.
So I gave them over to their stubborn hearts, to walk in their own counsels.
“If only My people would listen to Me, if Israel would walk in My ways,
how swiftly I would subdue their enemies and turn My hand against their foes!
Those who hate the LORD would feign obedience to Him, and their doom would last forever.
But I would feed you with the finest wheat and satisfy you with honey from the rock.”
God presides in the divine assembly; He judges among the gods.
“How long will you judge unjustly and show partiality to the wicked? Selah.
Defend the weak and the fatherless; vindicate the afflicted and the needy.
Rescue the weak and needy; deliver them from the hand of the wicked.
They know nothing; they understand nothing. They walk in darkness, and all the foundations of the earth are shaken.
I said, “You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High.
Yet you will die like mortals; you will fall like any prince.”
Arise, O God, and judge the earth, for You will inherit all the nations.
O God, do not keep silent; do not be quiet, O God, and do not be still.
See how Your enemies are in an uproar, and those who hate You have exalted themselves.
They devise crafty schemes against Your people and conspire against Your treasured ones.
They say, “Come, let us wipe them out as a nation, so that the name of Israel will be remembered no more.”
For with one mind they plot together; they form an alliance against You—
the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,
Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek, Philistia with the inhabitants of Tyre.
Even Assyria has joined them; they lend their strength to the descendants of Lot. Selah
Do to them as You did to Midian, as to Sisera and Jabin at the torrent of Kishon,
who perished at Endor and became like dung for the ground.
Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, and all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,
who said, “Let us take possession of God’s pastures for ourselves.”
Make them like whirling dust, O my God, like chaff before the wind.
As fire consumes a forest, as a flame sets the mountains ablaze,
so pursue them with Your tempest and terrify them with Your storm.
Fill their faces with shame, that they may seek Your name, the LORD.
Let them be ashamed and dismayed forever; let them be humiliated and perish.
Let them know that You alone—whose name is the LORD—are the Most High over all the earth.
How delightful are Your dwellings, O the LORD of Hosts!
My soul yearns—indeed, it faints—for the courts of the the LORD; my heart and my flesh cry out for the living God.
Even the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young—beside Your altars, O the LORD of Hosts, my King and my God.
Blessed are those who dwell in Your house; they are ever praising You. Selah.
Blessed are those whose strength is in You, whose hearts are set on pilgrimage.
As they pass through the Valley of Baca, they make it a place of springs; indeed, the autumn rains cover it with blessings.
They go from strength to strength, until each appears before God in Zion.
O the LORD God of Hosts, hear my prayer; give ear, O God of Jacob. Selah.
Behold our shield, O God, and look with favor upon the face of Your anointed.
For a day in Your courts is better than a thousand elsewhere; I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God than dwell in the tents of the wicked.
