The LORD protects the sojourner. He sustains the fatherless and the widow, but He thwarts the way of the wicked.
The LORD reigns forever—your God, O Zion, for all generations. Hallelujah!
Praise the LORD! It is good to sing praises to our God; how pleasant and fitting it is to praise Him!
The LORD builds up Jerusalem; He gathers the exiles of Israel.
He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
He counts the number of the stars and calls them all by name.
Great is our Lord and mighty in power; His understanding is beyond measure.
The LORD sustains the humble and casts the wicked down to the ground.
Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving; make music to our God on the harp.
He covers the sky with clouds, prepares rain for the earth, and makes grass grow on the mountains.
He provides food for the beasts and for the young ravens when they call.
He takes no pleasure in the strength of a horse, nor does He delight in a man's physical strength.
The LORD delights in those who fear Him, in those who hope in His unfailing love.
Praise the LORD, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion.
He strengthens the bars of your gates and blesses your people within you.
He grants peace within your borders and satisfies you with the finest wheat.
He sends His command to the earth; His word runs swiftly.
He gives snow like wool and scatters frost like ashes.
He hurls down His hail like pebbles. Who can withstand His icy blast?
He sends His word and melts them; He stirs up His wind, and the waters flow.
He declares His word to Jacob, His statutes and judgments to Israel.
He has not done this for any other nation; they do not know His laws. Praise the LORD!
Hallelujah! Praise the the LORD from the heavens; praise Him in the loftiest realms.
Praise Him, all His angels; praise Him, all His celestial hosts.
Praise Him, sun and moon; praise Him, all you radiant stars.
Praise Him, you highest heavens, and waters beyond the skies.
Let them praise the name of the the LORD, for at His command they were created.
He established them for all eternity; He decreed a law that shall never be revoked.
Praise the the LORD from the earth, you great sea creatures and all ocean depths,
fire and hail, snow and mist, stormy winds executing His word;
you mountains and all hills, fruit-bearing trees and all cedars;
wild beasts and all livestock, creeping things and winged birds.
Kings of the earth and all nations, you princes and all judges of the earth,
young men and maidens, elders and children.
Let them praise the name of the the LORD, for His name alone is exalted; His majesty surpasses earth and heaven.
He has raised up a horn for His people, the praise of all His saints, of Israel, a people near to Him. Hallelujah!
Hallelujah! Sing to the LORD a new song, His praise in the assembly of the faithful.
Let Israel rejoice in its Maker; let the children of Zion be joyful in their King.
Let them praise His name with dancing; let them sing praises to Him with tambourine and harp.
For the LORD takes pleasure in His people; He adorns the humble with salvation.
Let the faithful exult in glory; let them sing for joy on their beds.
Let the high praises of God be in their throats, and a double-edged sword in their hands,
to execute vengeance on the nations and punishment on the peoples,
to bind their kings with shackles and their nobles with fetters of iron,
to carry out the judgment written against them. This is an honor for all His faithful. Hallelujah!
Praise the LORD! Praise God in His sanctuary; praise Him in His mighty heavens.
Praise Him for His mighty acts; praise Him for His excellent greatness.
Praise Him with the sound of the trumpet; praise Him with harp and lyre.
Praise Him with tambourine and dancing; praise Him with strings and flute.
Praise Him with clashing cymbals; praise Him with resounding cymbals.
Let everything that has breath praise the LORD. Praise the LORD!
These are the proverbs of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel:
to know wisdom and discipline, to discern the words of understanding;
to receive instruction in prudent conduct, in righteousness, justice, and equity;
to impart shrewdness to the naive, and knowledge and discretion to the young.
Let the wise listen and gain further learning, and let the discerning acquire skillful guidance.
They will understand a proverb and a parable, the words of the wise and their riddles.
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and discipline.
Listen, my son, to your father's instruction, and do not forsake your mother's teaching,
for they will be a garland of grace upon your head and pendants around your neck.
My son, if sinners entice you, do not consent.
If they say, "Come with us; let us lie in wait for blood, let us ambush the innocent without cause.
Let us swallow them alive, as Sheol does, and whole, like those descending into the pit.
We shall find all kinds of precious wealth; we shall fill our houses with plunder.
Join us in this venture; we will all share one purse."
My son, do not walk in the way with them; restrain your foot from their path,
for their feet run to evil and they hurry to shed blood.
Indeed, it is futile to spread a net in full view of any bird,
yet these men lie in wait for their own blood; they ambush their own lives.
Such are the ways of all who are greedy for unjust gain; it costs its owners their lives.
Wisdom cries aloud in the street; she raises her voice in the squares.
At the head of the noisy streets she cries out; at the entrances of the city gates she speaks:
"How long, O naive ones, will you love naivety? How long will scoffers delight in their scoffing, and fools hate knowledge?
Heed my reproof; I will pour out my spirit to you; I will make my words known to you.
Because I called and you refused, I stretched out my hand and no one heeded;
because you ignored all my counsel and would have none of my reproof,
I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when terror strikes you,
when terror strikes you like a storm and your calamity comes like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish come upon you.
"Then they will call upon me, but I will not answer; they will seek me diligently, but they will not find me.
Because they hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the LORD,
because they would have none of my counsel and despised all my reproof,
therefore they shall eat the fruit of their way and be filled with their own devices.
For the turning away of the naive will kill them, and the complacency of fools will destroy them.
But whoever listens to me will dwell secure and will be at ease, without dread of disaster."
My son, if you receive my words and treasure my commandments within you,
inclining your ear to wisdom and directing your heart toward understanding;
indeed, if you call out for discernment and lift your voice in search of understanding;
if you seek it as silver and search for it as for concealed treasures—
then you will comprehend the fear of the LORD and discover the knowledge of God.
For the LORD bestows wisdom; from His mouth proceed knowledge and understanding.
He reserves sound wisdom for the upright and serves as a shield to those who walk in integrity,
guarding the paths of justice and preserving the way of His saints.
Then you will discern righteousness, justice, and equity—every virtuous path.
For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will delight your soul;
discretion will watch over you, and understanding will guard you,
delivering you from the way of evil and from those who speak perversely,
who abandon the paths of uprightness to walk in the ways of darkness,
who rejoice in doing evil and exult in perverse wickedness,
whose paths are crooked and whose ways are devious.
So you will be delivered from the forbidden woman, from the adulteress whose words are seductive,
who forsakes the companion of her youth and forgets the covenant of her God;
for her house sinks down to death, and her paths lead to the departed;
none who go to her return, nor do they regain the paths of life.
So you will walk in the way of the good and keep to the paths of the righteous.
For the upright will dwell in the land, and the blameless will remain in it;
but the wicked will be cut off from the land, and the treacherous will be uprooted from it.
My son, do not forget my teaching, but let your heart keep my commands.
For they will add long life and years of peace to you.
Do not let loving devotion and faithfulness forsake you; bind them around your neck; write them on the tablet of your heart.
Then you will find favor and good understanding in the sight of God and man.
Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding.
In all your ways acknowledge Him, and He will make your paths straight.
Do not be wise in your own eyes; fear the LORD and turn away from evil.
This will bring health to your body and refreshment to your bones.
Honor the LORD with your wealth and with the firstfruits of all your produce.
Then your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new wine.
My son, do not despise the discipline of the LORD, and do not resent His correction.
For the LORD corrects those He loves, as a father disciplines the son in whom he delights.
Blessed is the man who finds wisdom, and the man who gains understanding,
for her profit is better than the profit of silver, and her yield than fine gold.
She is more precious than rubies, and nothing you desire can compare with her.
Long life is in her right hand; in her left are riches and honor.
Her ways are pleasant, and all her paths are peace.
She is a tree of life to those who take hold of her, and those who hold her fast are blessed.
The LORD founded the earth by wisdom; He established the heavens by understanding.
By His knowledge the depths were broken open, and the clouds drip down dew.
My son, do not let them slip from your sight; keep sound wisdom and discretion.
They will be life to your soul and grace to your neck.
Then you will walk securely on your way, and your foot will not stumble.
When you lie down, you will not be afraid; your sleep will be sweet.
Do not be afraid of sudden terror or of the ruin that strikes the wicked when it comes.
For the LORD will be your confidence, and He will keep your foot from the snare.
Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in your power to act.
Do not say to your neighbor, “Go, and come back, and tomorrow I will give it,” when you have it with you.
Do not devise evil against your neighbor, who dwells securely beside you.
Do not contend with a man without cause, if he has done you no harm.
Do not envy a man of violence, and do not choose any of his ways.
For the perverse are an abomination to the LORD, but His secret counsel is with the upright.
The curse of the LORD is on the house of the wicked, but He blesses the dwelling of the righteous.
He mocks the mockers, but gives grace to the humble.
The wise will inherit honor, but fools are held up to shame.
Hear, sons, a father's instruction, and pay attention so that you may gain understanding.
For I give you good instruction; do not forsake my teaching.
For I was a son to my father, tender and the only child in my mother's sight.
He taught me and said to me, "Let your heart hold fast to my words; keep my commandments and live."
Acquire wisdom, acquire understanding; do not forget them, nor turn aside from the words of my mouth.
Do not forsake her, and she will guard you; love her, and she will keep you.
Wisdom is the principal thing; get wisdom, and in all your pursuits acquire understanding.
Exalt her, and she will promote you; she will bring you honor when you embrace her.
She will set on your head a garland of grace; a crown of glory she will bestow upon you.
Hear, my son, and receive my sayings, and the years of your life will be many.
I have taught you in the way of wisdom; I have led you in right paths.
When you walk, your steps will not be hindered; and if you run, you will not stumble.
Hold fast to instruction; do not let her go; guard her, for she is your life.
Do not enter the path of the wicked, and do not walk in the way of evil men.
Avoid it; do not pass through it; turn away from it and go on.
For they cannot sleep unless they have done wrong; their sleep is stolen from them unless they cause someone to fall.
For they eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.
But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, shining brighter and brighter until the full light of day.
The way of the wicked is like deep darkness; they do not know what makes them stumble.
My son, pay attention to my words; incline your ear to my sayings.
Let them not depart from your eyes; keep them in the midst of your heart.
For they are life to those who find them, and healing to all their flesh.
Keep your heart with all diligence, for from it flow the springs of life.
Put away from you a perverse mouth, and keep devious lips far from you.
Let your eyes look straight ahead, and let your eyelids look directly before you.
Ponder the path of your feet, and all your ways will be established.
Do not turn to the right or to the left; remove your foot from evil.
My son, heed my wisdom, and listen attentively to my understanding, so that you may preserve discretion, and your lips may safeguard knowledge.
For an adulteress speaks with seductive charm, and her flattery is smoother than oil;
yet her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a double-edged sword.
Her path descends to death, and her steps take hold of the grave.
She gives no thought to the path of life; her ways are restless, and she remains unaware.
Now, my sons, listen to me, and do not stray from the words of my mouth.
Keep your path far from her, and do not approach the door of her house,
lest you surrender your vigor to others and your years to a cruel man;
lest strangers grow strong on your wealth, and your toil enrich a foreigner’s house.
At the end of your life you will groan, when your flesh and body are spent,
and you will say, “How I hated discipline, and my heart despised correction!
I did not listen to my teachers, nor heed my instructors.
I was on the verge of utter ruin among the congregation and assembly.”
Drink from your own well, and keep your intimate life within your marriage;
should you pour your passion into the streets, or your desire into the public squares?
Let them belong to you alone, and never share them with strangers.
May your fountain be blessed, and may you rejoice in the wife of your youth—
a loving doe, a graceful deer. May her breasts satisfy you always; may you be continually captivated by her love.
Why, my son, should you be captivated by an adulteress, or embrace the bosom of a stranger?
For a man’s ways lie open before the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD weighs all his paths.
The wicked are snared by their own iniquity; the cords of their sin entangle them.
He dies for lack of discipline, led astray by his own abundant folly.
My son, if you have pledged surety for your neighbor, if you have sealed a pledge with a handshake for a stranger,
you are snared by the words of your mouth; you are trapped by your own utterances.
Then do this, my son, and deliver yourself, for you have come into your neighbor's power: go, humble yourself, and importune your neighbor.
Give no sleep to your eyes, nor slumber to your eyelids.
Deliver yourself like a gazelle from the hunter's hand, and like a bird from the hand of the fowler.
Go to the ant, you sluggard; observe her ways and grow wise.
Though she has no commander, overseer, or ruler,
she prepares her bread in summer and gathers her provender in harvest.
How long will you recline, O sluggard? When will you rise from your slumber?
A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,
and your poverty will come like a robber, and your want like an armed man.
A worthless man, a scoundrel, conducts himself with perverse speech,
winking with his eyes, signaling with his feet, gesturing with his fingers;
deceit is in his heart, he plots evil continually, and he sows discord.
Therefore his ruin will arrive suddenly; in an instant he will be shattered beyond remedy.
There are six things that the the LORD hates, indeed seven that are detestable to Him:
haughty eyes, a deceitful tongue, hands that shed innocent blood,
a heart that contrives wicked schemes, feet that hasten to do evil,
a false witness who utters lies, and one who sows discord among brothers.
My son, keep your father's commandment, and do not abandon the instruction of your mother.
Bind them upon your heart continually; fasten them around your neck.
When you walk, they will guide you; when you sleep, they will guard you; and when you awake, they will converse with you.
For the commandment is a lamp, the teaching is a light, and the reproofs of discipline are the way of life,
to preserve you from the adulterous woman, from the smooth tongue of a stranger.
Do not covet her beauty in your heart, nor let her captivate you with her glances.
For a harlot reduces a man to a crust of bread, but an adulteress hunts for the precious life.
Can a man carry fire in his bosom without burning his garments?
Or can one walk upon hot coals without scorching his feet?
So is the man who goes in to his neighbor's wife; no one who touches her will go unpunished.
People do not despise a thief if he steals to satisfy his hunger;
yet if he is caught, he must repay sevenfold; he must surrender all the wealth of his house.
He who commits adultery with a woman is devoid of understanding; he who does so destroys his own soul.
He will incur wounds and disgrace, and his reproach will never be erased.
For jealousy provokes a husband's fury, and he will show no mercy in the day of vengeance.
He will accept no ransom, nor will he be appeased even if you heap up bribes.
My son, keep my words and treasure my commandments within you;
keep my commandments and live, and guard my teaching as the most precious thing you protect.
Bind them on your fingers; write them on the tablet of your heart.
Say to wisdom, “You are my sister,” and call understanding your close companion,
so that they may keep you from the adulteress, from the seductress with her flattering words.
For at the window of my house I looked out through my lattice.
I saw among the naive, I noticed among the youths, a young man without understanding,
crossing the street near her corner and taking the road to her house,
in the twilight, at evening, in the blackest night and darkness.
And behold, a woman meets him, dressed as a prostitute, with a cunning heart.
She is loud and rebellious; her feet never remain at home.
Now in the street, now in the squares, she lurks at every corner.
She seizes him and kisses him, and with a brazen face she says: “
I have made my peace offerings; today I have paid my vows.
So I came out to meet you, to seek you eagerly, and I have found you.
I have spread my bed with coverings, with colored linens from Egypt.
I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
Come, let us satisfy ourselves with love until morning; let us delight in love.
For my husband is not at home; he has gone on a long journey.
He took a purse of silver with him; he will not return until the full moon.”
With her persuasive words she entices him; with her flattering speech she seduces him.
Suddenly he follows her, like an ox going to the slaughter, and like a fool led to the stocks,
until an arrow pierces his liver, like a bird darting into a snare; he does not know that it will cost him his life.
And now, my sons, listen to me, and be attentive to the words of my mouth.
Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways; do not stray into her paths.
For she has brought down many victims, and all her slain are mighty.
Her house is the way to Sheol, descending to the chambers of death.
Does not wisdom call out? Does not understanding raise her voice?
At the summit of the heights beside the road, at the crossroads she takes her stand.
Beside the gates, at the entrance to the city, at the doorways she cries aloud.
“To you, O men, I call out, and my voice is to the sons of men.
You simple ones, gain prudence; you fools, gain understanding.
Listen, for I will speak noble things, and the opening of my lips will be upright.
For my mouth utters truth, and wickedness is an abomination to my lips.
All the words of my mouth are righteous; nothing in them is crooked or perverse.
They are all plain to the discerning, and upright to those who find knowledge.
“Take my instruction rather than silver, and knowledge rather than choice gold.
For wisdom is better than rubies, and nothing desirable can compare with her.
I, Wisdom, dwell with prudence, and I find knowledge and discretion.
The fear of the LORD is hatred of evil; pride, arrogance, the evil way, and the perverse mouth I hate.
Counsel and sound judgment are mine; I am understanding; strength is mine.
By me kings reign, and rulers decree what is just.
By me princes rule, and nobles—all who judge with justice.
I love those who love me, and those who seek me diligently will find me.
With me are riches and honor, enduring wealth and righteousness.
My fruit is better than gold, even fine gold, and my produce than choice silver.
I walk in the way of righteousness, in the midst of the paths of justice.
That I may cause those who love me to inherit wealth, and fill their treasuries.
“The LORD possessed me at the beginning of His way, before His works of old.
I was established from eternity, from the beginning, before the earth.
When there were no depths, I was brought forth; when there were no springs abounding with water.
Before the mountains were settled, before the hills I was brought forth.
While He had not yet made the earth or the fields, or the first dust of the world.
I was there when He established the heavens, when He drew a circle on the face of the deep.
When He made firm the skies above, when He strengthened the fountains of the deep.
When He set a decree for the sea, that the waters should not transgress His command; when He laid the foundations of the earth.
Then I was beside Him as a master craftsman, and I was His delight day by day, rejoicing always before Him.
Rejoicing in His inhabited world, and my delight was with the sons of men.
“Now therefore, sons, listen to me, for blessed are those who keep my ways.
Hear instruction and be wise, and do not disregard it.
Blessed is the man who listens to me, waiting daily at my gates, keeping watch at the posts of my doors.
For whoever finds me finds life, and obtains favor from the LORD.
But whoever fails to find me injures himself; all who hate me love death.”
Wisdom has built her house; she has hewn out its seven pillars.
She has prepared her meat, mixed her wine, and set her table.
She has sent out her maidservants; she calls from the highest points of the city.
“Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” she says to anyone lacking judgment.
“Come, eat my bread and drink the wine I have mixed.
Leave your simple ways and live; walk in the way of understanding.”
Whoever corrects a scoffer invites insult; whoever rebukes the wicked incurs abuse.
Do not rebuke a scoffer, or he will hate you; rebuke a wise man, and he will love you.
Instruct a wise man, and he will be wiser still; teach a righteous man, and he will add to his learning.
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
For through me your days will be multiplied, and years will be added to your life.
If you are wise, your wisdom is for yourself; if you mock, you alone will bear it.
The woman Folly is clamorous; she is naive and knows nothing.
She sits at the door of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city,
to call to passersby who go straight on their way.
“Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” And to the one lacking judgment she says,
“Stolen water is sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant.”
But he does not know that the dead are there, that her guests are in the depths of Sheol.
A wise son gladdens his father, whereas a foolish son brings grief to his mother.
Treasures gained through wrongdoing profit nothing, but righteousness delivers from death.
The LORD will not allow the righteous to hunger; instead, He frustrates the craving of the wicked.
Indolence impoverishes a person, while diligent labor brings wealth.
A son who gathers during summer demonstrates prudence, but a son who sleeps through harvest brings disgrace.
Blessings crown the head of the righteous, whereas the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot.
Those wise in heart receive instruction, whereas a garrulous fool hastens toward ruin.
One who walks in integrity walks securely, but one who distorts his ways will be exposed.
One who signals deceit with a wink causes grief, and a garrulous fool comes to ruin.
The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, while the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all transgressions.
Wisdom is found on the lips of the discerning, but the undiscerning invite chastisement.
The wise store up knowledge, but the mouth of the fool invites destruction.
The rich man's wealth is his fortified city, whereas poverty ruins the poor.
The labor of the righteous leads to life, but the gain of the wicked leads to sin.
Whoever heeds instruction walks the path of life, but whoever rejects reproof goes astray.
One who conceals hatred has lying lips, and one who spreads slander is a fool.
Where words abound, transgression is never absent, but one who restrains his lips acts wisely.
The tongue of the righteous is choice silver, but the heart of the wicked is of little value.
The lips of the righteous nourish many, but fools perish for want of discernment.
The blessing of the LORD enriches, and He adds no sorrow to it.
A fool finds pleasure in wicked schemes, but a person of understanding delights in wisdom.
What the wicked dreads will overtake him, but the desire of the righteous will be granted.
When the whirlwind passes, the wicked are no more, but the righteous stand as an everlasting foundation.
Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to those who send him.
The fear of the LORD prolongs life, but the years of the wicked are cut short.
The hope of the righteous is joy, but the expectation of the wicked perishes.
The way of the LORD is a stronghold to the upright, but destruction to the workers of iniquity.
The righteous will never be shaken, but the wicked will not dwell in the land.
The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom, but a perverse tongue will be silenced.
The lips of the righteous know what is fitting, but the mouth of the wicked is perverse.
Dishonest scales are an abomination to the the LORD, whereas an accurate weight is His delight.
Pride brings disgrace, but wisdom dwells with the humble.
The integrity of the upright guides them, whereas the perversity of the treacherous destroys them.
Wealth is useless in the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from death.
The righteousness of the blameless makes his path straight, but the wicked falls through his own wickedness.
The righteousness of the upright delivers them, but the treacherous are ensnared by their own desires.
When a wicked person dies, his hope perishes, and all he expected from his power comes to nothing.
The righteous is rescued from trouble, and the wicked takes his place.
With his mouth the godless destroys his neighbor, but through knowledge the righteous are delivered.
When the righteous prosper, the city rejoices; when the wicked perish, there are shouts of joy.
By the blessing of the upright a city is exalted, but by the mouth of the wicked it is overthrown.
Whoever belittles his neighbor lacks sense, but a person of understanding remains silent.
A gossip reveals secrets, but one who is faithful in spirit conceals a matter.
Where there is no guidance, a people falls, but victory comes through many counselors.
He who guarantees a stranger's debt will surely suffer, but whoever refuses to pledge security is safe.
A gracious woman gains honor, but ruthless men gain only wealth.
A kind person benefits himself, but a cruel person harms his own body.
The wicked earns deceptive wages, but one who sows righteousness receives a true reward.
Righteousness leads to life, but pursuing evil leads to death.
Those with crooked hearts are an abomination to the the LORD, but those whose ways are blameless are His delight.
Be assured that an evil person will not go unpunished, but the offspring of the righteous will be delivered.
Like a gold ring in a pig's snout is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion.
The desire of the righteous leads only to good, but the hope of the wicked brings wrath.
One person gives freely, yet gains even more; another withholds unduly, but comes to poverty.
A generous person will prosper, and whoever refreshes others will himself be refreshed.
People curse the one who hoards grain, but blessing crowns the one who sells it.
Whoever seeks good finds favor, but evil comes to the one who searches for it.
Those who trust in their riches will fall, but the righteous will flourish like a green leaf.
Whoever troubles his own household will inherit nothing but emptiness, and the fool will serve the wise of heart.
The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and whoever wins souls is wise.
If the righteous are repaid on earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner!
Whoever cherishes discipline cherishes knowledge, but whoever despises correction reveals himself as senseless.
A virtuous man obtains favor from the LORD, but the LORD condemns the schemer.
Wickedness establishes no one, whereas the righteous remain unshakable.
A capable wife is her husband’s crown, but a shameful one corrodes his very bones.
The thoughts of the righteous are just, while the counsel of the wicked is treacherous.
The words of the wicked lie in ambush for bloodshed, but the speech of the upright delivers.
The wicked are overturned and vanish, but the household of the righteous endures.
A person is commended for sound judgment, while a perverse heart is held in contempt.
It is better to be lightly regarded yet possess a servant than to be self-important and go hungry.
The righteous attend to the lives of their animals, but even the compassion of the wicked is cruel.
Whoever tills his land will have abundant food, but whoever pursues empty schemes lacks sense.
The wicked covet the gains of evildoers, but the righteous flourish.
An evil person is snared by his transgressive speech, but the righteous escape trouble.
A person is satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth, and the work of his hands returns to him.
The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but a wise man listens to counsel.
A fool’s vexation is immediately evident, but a prudent person overlooks an insult.
Whoever speaks truthfully proclaims what is right, but a false witness spreads deceit.
Reckless words pierce like a sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.
Truthful lips are established forever, but a lying tongue endures only a moment.
Deceit fills the hearts of those who plot evil, but counselors of peace have joy.
No evil shall befall the righteous, but the wicked are filled with calamity.
Lying lips are an abomination to the LORD, but those who deal faithfully are His delight.
A prudent person conceals knowledge, but the heart of fools broadcasts folly.
The diligent hand will rule, but slackness leads to forced labor.
Anxiety depresses the heart, but a good word gladdens it.
The righteous guide their neighbors, but the way of the wicked leads them astray.
A lazy man does not roast his catch, but a diligent man values his possessions.
In the way of righteousness is life, and in its path there is no death.
A wise son heeds his father's correction, but a scoffer ignores rebuke.
From his words a man enjoys good things, but the appetite of the treacherous craves violence.
He who guards his mouth preserves his life, but one who speaks rashly brings ruin upon himself.
The indolent crave yet receive nothing, but the diligent are richly satisfied.
The righteous hate falsehood, but the wicked bring shame and disgrace.
Righteousness guards the blameless along their path, but wickedness overthrows the sinner.
Some feign wealth yet possess nothing; others feign poverty yet hold great riches.
A man's wealth may ransom his life, but a poor man hears no rebuke.
The light of the righteous brings joy, but the lamp of the wicked is extinguished.
Arrogance breeds only contention, but wisdom belongs to those who accept counsel.
Wealth gained hastily dwindles, but whoever gathers steadily multiplies it.
A deferred hope sickens the heart, but a longing fulfilled is a tree of life.
Whoever despises the word brings destruction upon himself, but whoever fears the commandment is rewarded.
The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, turning one away from the snares of death.
Sound judgment wins favor, but the way of the treacherous is harsh.
Every prudent person acts with knowledge, but a fool parades folly.
A wicked messenger falls into adversity, but a faithful envoy brings healing.
Poverty and shame befall those who spurn discipline, but whoever heeds correction is honored.
A longing fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but fools abhor turning from evil.
Whoever walks with the wise becomes wise, but the companion of fools suffers harm.
Calamity pursues sinners, but prosperity rewards the righteous.
A good person leaves an inheritance to grandchildren, but the sinner's wealth is stored up for the righteous.
The fallow ground of the poor yields abundant food, yet injustice sweeps it away.
Whoever spares the rod hates his son, but whoever loves him disciplines him diligently.
The righteous eat to their hearts' content, but the stomach of the wicked goes hungry.
Every wise woman builds her house, but a foolish one tears it down with her own hands.
He who walks in uprightness fears the LORD, but he who is crooked in his ways despises Him.
In a fool’s mouth is a rod of pride, but wise lips preserve them.
Where no oxen are, the manger is clean, but an abundant harvest comes by the strength of the ox.
A faithful witness does not lie, but a false witness breathes out lies.
A mocker seeks wisdom and finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.
Leave the presence of a fool, for you will gain no knowledge from his lips.
The wisdom of the prudent is to discern his way, but the folly of fools is deceit.
Fools mock at guilt, but goodwill is found among the upright.
The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares its joy.
The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death.
Even in laughter the heart may ache, and joy may end in grief.
The backslider in heart will be filled with his own ways, but a good man will be satisfied from above.
The simple believes every word, but the prudent gives thought to his steps.
A wise man fears and turns from evil, but a fool is reckless and overconfident.
A quick-tempered man acts foolishly, and a man of wicked schemes is hated.
The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
Evil men bow down before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
A poor man is hated even by his neighbor, but the rich have many friends.
He who despises his neighbor sins, but blessed is he who is kind to the poor.
Do not those who plan evil go astray? But lovingkindness and truth belong to those who plan good.
In all toil there is profit, but mere talk leads only to poverty.
The crown of the wise is their wealth, but the folly of fools is only folly.
A truthful witness saves lives, but a false witness breathes deceit.
In the fear of the LORD there is strong confidence, and His children will have a place of refuge.
The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning one away from the snares of death.
In a multitude of people is a king’s glory, but without people a prince is ruined.
He who is slow to anger has great understanding, but he who is quick-tempered exalts folly.
A tranquil heart gives life to the flesh, but envy makes the bones rot.
He who oppresses the poor taunts his Maker, but he who is kind to the needy honors Him.
The wicked are brought down by their own calamity, but the righteous have a refuge when they die.
Wisdom rests in the heart of the discerning, but among fools it is made known.
Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.
The king’s favor rests on a wise servant, but his wrath falls on one who brings shame.
A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
The tongue of the wise commends knowledge, whereas the mouth of fools spews nonsense.
The eyes of the LORD are in every place, observing both the wicked and the good.
A healing tongue is a tree of life, yet perversity in it crushes the spirit.
A fool despises his father's discipline, but one who heeds reproof acts prudently.
The house of the righteous holds great treasure, while the income of the wicked brings trouble.
Wise lips disseminate knowledge, but foolish hearts do not.
The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright is His delight.
The LORD detests the way of the wicked, yet He loves the one who pursues righteousness.
Harsh discipline awaits anyone who forsakes the path, and whoever hates reproof will die.
Even Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD; how much more, then, the hearts of human beings.
A mocker resents correction and will not consult the wise.
A joyful heart brightens the countenance, but sorrow of heart crushes the spirit.
The discerning heart seeks knowledge, whereas the mouth of fools feeds on folly.
All the days of the oppressed are wretched, but a cheerful heart enjoys a continual feast.
Better a little with reverence for the LORD than great wealth accompanied by turmoil.
Better a simple meal of vegetables where love dwells than a fattened ox served with hatred.
A hot-tempered person stirs up strife, but patience quiets contention.
The way of the lazy person is blocked with thorns, whereas the path of the upright is a highway.
A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish man treats his mother with contempt.
Folly delights those who lack sense, yet a person of understanding walks uprightly.
Plans fail without counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.
A person finds joy in a fitting reply; how good is a timely word.
The path of life leads upward for the discerning, so that he may avoid the grave below.
The LORD demolishes the house of the proud, but He sets the widow's boundary firm.
The LORD detests the thoughts of the wicked, but pure words are pleasing to Him.
Whoever is greedy for gain troubles his own household, but one who hates bribes will live.
The heart of the righteous weighs how to answer, while the mouth of the wicked gushes evil.
The LORD is far from the wicked, yet He hears the prayer of the righteous.
The light of the eyes rejoices the heart, and good news nourishes the bones.
The ear that heeds life-giving reproof will dwell among the wise.
Whoever disregards discipline despises himself, but one who heeds correction gains understanding.
The fear of the LORD is the instruction of wisdom, and humility comes before honor.
The plans of the heart belong to man, but the answer of the tongue comes from the LORD.
All a man's ways seem pure in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs the motives.
Entrust your works to the LORD, and your thoughts will be established.
The LORD has made everything for His own purpose—even the wicked for a day of disaster.
The LORD detests all who are proud of heart. Be assured that they will not go unpunished.
Through love and faithfulness sin is atoned for, and through the fear of the LORD a man avoids evil.
When a man's ways please the LORD, He makes even his enemies to be at peace with him.
Better is a little with righteousness than great revenues with injustice.
The heart of man plans his way, but the LORD establishes his steps.
An oracle is on the lips of a king; his mouth does not betray justice.
Honest scales and balances are the LORD's; all the weights in the bag are His concern.
It is an abomination to kings to do evil, for the throne is established by righteousness.
Righteous lips are the delight of kings, and he who speaks honestly is loved.
A king's wrath is a messenger of death, but a wise man will appease it.
In the light of a king's face there is life, and his favor is like a cloud bringing the spring rain.
How much better to get wisdom than gold, and to get understanding is to be chosen above silver!
The highway of the upright turns away from evil; he who guards his way preserves his life.
Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
It is better to be of a lowly spirit with the poor than to divide the spoil with the proud.
Whoever heeds instruction finds good, and blessed is he who trusts in the LORD.
The wise in heart are called discerning, and sweetness of the lips increases learning.
Understanding is a fountain of life to its possessor, but the instruction of fools is folly.
The heart of the wise instructs his mouth and adds learning to his lips.
Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.
There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death.
A worker's appetite works for him; his hunger drives him on.
A worthless man digs up evil, and on his lips there is a scorching fire.
A perverse man spreads strife, and a whisperer separates close friends.
A man of violence entices his neighbor and leads him in a way that is not good.
He who winks his eyes plans perverse things; he who purses his lips brings evil to pass.
Gray hair is a crown of glory; it is found in the way of righteousness.
He who is slow to anger is better than the mighty, and he who rules his spirit than he who takes a city.
The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD.
Better a dry morsel eaten in tranquility than a house filled with sacrificial feasts and strife.
A prudent servant will rule over a disgraceful son and share the inheritance among the brothers.
A crucible refines silver, and a furnace gold, but the LORD examines hearts.
An evildoer heeds deceitful lips, and a liar lends his ear to a ruinous tongue.
Whoever mocks the poor reproaches their Maker; whoever rejoices in calamity will not go unpunished.
Grandchildren are the crown of the aged, and the glory of children is their fathers.
Eloquent words ill suit a fool; how much more do lying lips misbecome a ruler.
A bribe works like a charm in its giver's hand; wherever he turns, he prospers.
He who covers an offense seeks love, but he who repeats a matter separates close friends.
A rebuke penetrates deeper into a discerning man than a hundred blows into a fool.
An evil man seeks only rebellion, so a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
Better to encounter a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool in his folly.
Whoever repays evil for good will never have evil depart from his house.
The onset of strife resembles released water; therefore abandon contention before it erupts.
Acquitting the guilty and condemning the innocent are alike an abomination to the LORD.
Why should a fool have money in his hand when he has no intention of acquiring wisdom?
A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
A man lacking judgment pledges his hand and becomes surety for his neighbor.
Whoever loves transgression loves strife; whoever builds a high gate invites destruction.
A man of crooked heart will not prosper, and one with a perverse tongue will fall into calamity.
He who begets a fool begets grief for himself; the father of a fool has no joy.
A joyful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
A wicked man accepts a bribe in secret to pervert the course of justice.
Wisdom is the focus of the discerning, but the eyes of a fool wander to the ends of the earth.
A foolish son is a grief to his father and bitterness to his mother.
It is not good to punish the innocent, nor to flog officials for their integrity.
A man of knowledge restrains his words, and a man of understanding maintains composure.
Even a fool is thought wise if he keeps silent, and discerning if he restrains his lips.
Whoever isolates himself pursues his own desire and rebels against all sound wisdom.
A fool takes no delight in understanding; he cares only to disclose what is in his heart.
The arrival of wickedness brings contempt in its wake, and disgrace follows hard upon shame.
The words of a man's mouth are deep waters, but the fountain of wisdom is a bubbling brook.
It is not good to show partiality to the wicked or to deny justice to the righteous.
A fool's lips stir up contention, and his mouth invites blows.
A fool's mouth is his ruin, and his lips are a snare to his soul.
A gossip's words are like tasty morsels; they sink deep into one's innermost being.
Whoever is slack in his work is a brother to the one who destroys.
The name of The LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run into it and are safe.
A rich man's wealth is his fortified city, and it is like a high wall in his imagination.
Before ruin, a man's heart is haughty, but humility precedes honor.
He who answers before he listens—this is his folly and his shame.
A man's spirit can sustain him in sickness, but who can bear a broken spirit?
The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks it out.
A man's gift makes room for him and leads him before great men.
The first to state his case seems right, until another comes and cross-examines him.
Casting the lot settles disputes and separates powerful opponents.
An offended brother is harder to win than a fortified city, and disputes are like the bars of a castle.
From the fruit of his mouth a man's stomach is filled; with the harvest of his lips he is satisfied.
Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
He who finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from the LORD.
The poor man pleads for mercy, but the rich man answers harshly.
A man of many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who stays closer than a brother.
Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a fool whose lips are perverse.
Even zeal is no good without knowledge, and he who hurries his footsteps misses the mark.
A man’s own folly subverts his way, yet his heart rages against the LORD.
Wealth attracts many friends, but a poor man is deserted by his friend.
A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who utters lies will not escape.
Many seek the favor of a prince, and everyone is a friend of one who gives gifts.
All the brothers of a poor man hate him—how much more do his friends avoid him! He may pursue them with pleading, but they are nowhere to be found.
He who acquires wisdom loves himself; one who safeguards understanding will find good.
A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who pours out lies will perish.
Luxury is unseemly for a fool—how much worse for a slave to rule over princes!
A man’s insight gives him patience, and his glory is to overlook an offense.
A king’s rage is like the roar of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.
A foolish son is his father’s ruin, and a quarrelsome wife is like a constant dripping.
Houses and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a prudent wife is from the LORD.
Laziness brings on deep sleep, and an idle soul will suffer hunger.
He who keeps a commandment preserves his soul, but he who is careless in his ways will die.
Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender.
Discipline your son, for in that there is hope; do not be a willing party to his death.
A man of great wrath will pay the penalty; if you rescue him, you will have to do it again.
Listen to counsel and accept discipline, that you may be wise in your latter days.
Many plans are in a man’s heart, but the purpose of the LORD will prevail.
The desire of a man is loving devotion, but a poor man is better than a liar.
The fear of the LORD leads to life, that one may rest content, untouched by trouble.
The slacker buries his hand in the dish; he will not even bring it to his mouth.
Strike a mocker, and the simple will learn prudence; rebuke a discerning man, and he will gain knowledge.
He who assaults his father or drives away his mother is a son who brings shame and disgrace.
Cease listening to instruction, my son, and you will stray from the words of knowledge.
A worthless witness mocks at justice, and the mouth of the wicked devours iniquity.
Judgments are prepared for mockers, and beatings for the backs of fools.
Wine is a mocker, strong drink a brawler, and whoever is led astray by them is not wise.
A king's terror is like a lion's roar; whoever provokes his anger forfeits his life.
It is honorable for a man to refrain from strife, but every fool quarrels.
The lazy man will not plow in winter; at harvest he seeks a crop and finds none.
A plan in a man's heart is deep water, but a man of understanding draws it out.
Many proclaim their own loyalty, but who can find a faithful man?
The righteous man walks in his integrity; blessed are his children after him.
A king seated on the throne of judgment winnows all evil with his eyes.
Who can say, "I have purified my heart; I am cleansed from my sin"?
Differing weights and differing measures are both an abomination to the LORD.
Even a child is known by his deeds, whether his conduct is pure and upright.
The hearing ear and the seeing eye—the LORD has made them both.
Do not love sleep, lest you come to poverty; open your eyes, and you will have plenty of bread.
"Bad, bad!" says the buyer, but when he has gone away, he boasts.
There is gold and an abundance of costly stones, but lips of knowledge are a precious jewel.
Take the garment of one who has become security for a stranger, and hold it in pledge when he becomes security for foreigners.
Bread gained by deceit is sweet to a man, but afterward his mouth will be full of gravel.
Plans are established by counsel, and war is waged by wise guidance.
Whoever gossips reveals secrets, so do not associate with a babbler.
Whoever curses his father or his mother—his lamp will be put out in utter darkness.
An inheritance gained hastily at first will not be blessed in the end.
Do not say, "I will repay evil"; wait for the LORD, and He will save you.
Differing weights are an abomination to the LORD, and dishonest scales are not good.
A man's steps are from the LORD; how then can man understand his way?
It is a snare to say rashly, "It is holy," and only afterward to consider one's vows.
A wise king winnows the wicked and drives the threshing wheel over them.
The spirit of man is the lamp of the LORD, searching all his innermost parts.
Steadfast love and faithfulness preserve the king, and by steadfast love his throne is upheld.
The glory of young men is their strength, but the splendor of old men is their gray hair.
Blows that wound cleanse away evil, and strokes make clean the innermost parts.
A king’s heart is like a watercourse in the LORD’s hand; He turns it wherever He wills.
Every person’s way seems right in his own eyes, yet the LORD weighs the heart.
Doing what is right and just is more acceptable to the LORD than offering sacrifices.
Haughty eyes and a proud heart—the very lamp of the wicked—constitute sin.
The plans of the diligent surely bring abundance, whereas every hasty scheme surely leads to poverty.
Wealth amassed by a deceitful tongue is a vanishing vapor, a pursuit that courts death.
The violence of the wicked will drag them away, because they refuse to act justly.
A guilty person’s path is devious and strange, but the pure person’s conduct is upright.
It is better to live in a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
The wicked person’s soul craves evil, and his neighbor finds no favor in his sight.
When a scoffer is punished, the simple gain wisdom; when a wise person is instructed, he gains knowledge.
The righteous person wisely considers the house of the wicked and brings them to ruin.
Whoever closes his ears to the cry of the poor will himself cry out and receive no answer.
A gift given secretly soothes anger, and a bribe concealed in the cloak pacifies great wrath.
Carrying out justice brings joy to the righteous but terror to evildoers.
A person who strays from the path of understanding will take his place among the dead.
Whoever loves pleasure will become poor; whoever loves wine and oil will never grow rich.
The wicked become a ransom for the righteous, and the treacherous for the upright.
It is better to live in a desert than with a quarrelsome and hot-tempered wife.
Precious treasure and oil are found in the wise person’s home, but a fool squanders them.
Whoever pursues righteousness and faithful love finds life, righteousness, and honor.
A wise person scales the city of the mighty and tears down the stronghold in which they trust.
Whoever guards his mouth and tongue keeps himself from trouble.
A proud, haughty scoffer is called “Mocker,” and he acts in arrogant fury.
The sluggard’s craving kills him, because his hands refuse to labor.
All day long he covets, while the righteous gives without holding back.
The wicked person’s sacrifice is detestable—especially when offered with evil intent.
A false witness will perish, but the person who listens will be heard forever.
A wicked person hardens his face, but the upright person makes his way secure.
No wisdom, understanding, or counsel can stand against the LORD.
The horse may be prepared for battle, but victory belongs to the LORD.
A good name is preferable to great riches, and favor is better than silver or gold.
The rich and the poor meet together; the LORD is the Maker of them all.
The prudent see danger and take cover, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
The reward of humility and the fear of the LORD is wealth, honor, and life.
Thorns and snares lie in the path of the perverse; whoever guards his life stays far from them.
Train a child in the way he should go, and even when he is old he will not turn from it.
The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.
Whoever sows injustice reaps trouble, and the rod of his fury will be destroyed.
A generous person will be blessed, for he gives some of his food to the poor.
Drive out a mocker, and conflict will depart; quarreling and disgrace will cease.
He who loves a pure heart and whose speech is gracious will have the king as his friend.
The eyes of the LORD guard knowledge, but He overturns the words of the treacherous.
The lazy person says, “There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the streets!”
The mouth of an adulterous woman is a deep pit; a man with whom the LORD is angry falls into it.
Folly is bound up in a child’s heart, but the rod of discipline will drive it far from him.
Whoever oppresses the poor to enrich himself, or gives to the rich, will surely come to poverty.
Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise, and apply your heart to my knowledge;
for it is pleasant when you keep them within you, when all of them are ready on your lips.
So that your trust may be in the LORD, I have made them known to you today—yes, to you.
Have I not written for you thirty sayings of counsel and knowledge,
to make you know what is right and true, that you may give a true answer to those who sent you?
Do not rob the poor, because he is poor, or crush the afflicted at the gate,
for the LORD will plead their cause and plunder those who rob them.
Do not make friends with a hot-tempered man, and do not associate with a man given to anger,
lest you learn his ways and entangle yourself in a snare.
Do not be among those who give pledges, among those who guarantee debts.
If you have nothing with which to pay, why should your bed be taken from under you?
Do not move the ancient landmark that your fathers have set.
Do you see a man skillful in his work? He will stand before kings; he will not stand before obscure men.
When you sit down to dine with a ruler, scrutinize with meticulous care whatever is set before you,
and place a knife to your throat if you are a man of voracious appetite.
Do not crave his delicacies, for such food is deceptive.
Do not exhaust yourself in the pursuit of riches; have the discernment to desist.
When your eyes light upon wealth, it vanishes, for it sprouts wings like an eagle and flies away to heaven.
Do not partake of the bread of a man with an evil eye, nor crave his delicacies;
for as he reckons within himself, so he truly is. “Eat and drink,” he says to you, yet his heart is not with you.
You will vomit up the morsel you have eaten and squander your gracious words.
Do not speak into a fool’s ears, for he will despise the wisdom of your words.
Do not remove an ancient boundary stone, and do not encroach upon the fields of the fatherless,
for their Redeemer is mighty; He will plead their cause against you.
Apply your heart to instruction and your ears to words of knowledge.
Do not withhold discipline from a child; if you strike him with the rod, he will not die.
You shall strike him with the rod and deliver his soul from Sheol.
My son, if your heart is wise, my heart too will rejoice.
My inmost being will rejoice when your lips speak what is upright.
Do not let your heart envy sinners, but remain in the fear of the LORD all the day.
Surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
Listen, my son, and be wise, and direct your heart in the way.
Do not join those who drink too much wine or gorge themselves on meat,
for the drunkard and the glutton will come to poverty, and drowsiness will clothe them in rags.
Listen to your father who gave you life, and do not despise your mother when she is old.
Buy the truth and do not sell it—wisdom, instruction, and understanding as well.
The father of a righteous man will greatly rejoice, and he who begets a wise son will delight in him.
Let your father and your mother be glad, and let her who bore you rejoice!
My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes delight in my ways.
For a prostitute is a deep pit, and an adulteress is a narrow well.
She lies in wait like a robber and multiplies the faithless among men.
Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has strife? Who has complaints? Who has wounds without cause? Who has bloodshot eyes?
Those who linger over wine, those who go to sample mixed drinks.
Do not gaze at wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup, when it goes down smoothly.
In the end it bites like a serpent and stings like an adder.
Your eyes will see strange things, and your heart will utter perversities.
You will be like one sleeping in the heart of the sea, or like one at the helm of a ship.
“They struck me, but I did not feel it! They beat me, but I did not know it! When will I wake up so I can find another drink?”
Do not be envious of evildoers, nor desire to consort with them.
For their hearts devise violence, and their lips give voice to trouble.
By wisdom a house is built, and by understanding it is established;
by knowledge its chambers are filled with every precious and pleasant treasure.
A wise man is strong, and a man of knowledge fortifies his power,
for by wise counsel you shall wage war, and in an abundance of counselors there is victory.
Wisdom is too lofty for a fool, so he does not open his mouth in the gate.
He who plots to do evil will be called a schemer,
and the scheme of folly is sin, while the scoffer is an abomination to mankind.
If you falter in the day of distress, your strength is small.
Rescue those being led away to death, and hold back those staggering toward slaughter.
If you say, "See, we did not know this," does not He who weighs the hearts perceive it? He who keeps your soul—does He not know? And will He not repay each person according to his deeds?
My son, eat honey, for it is good; yes, the honeycomb is sweet upon your tongue.
Know that wisdom is like this for your soul: if you find it, there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
Do not lie in wait, O wicked man, against the dwelling of the righteous, and do not ravage his resting place,
for a righteous man falls seven times and rises again, whereas the wicked are brought down by calamity.
Do not rejoice when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart be glad when he stumbles,
lest the LORD see it and be displeased, and turn away His wrath from him.
Do not fret because of evildoers, nor be envious of the wicked,
for the evil man has no future, and the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
My son, fear the LORD and the king, and do not associate with those given to change,
for their calamity will arise suddenly, and who knows the ruin that both will bring?
These also are sayings of the wise: to show partiality in judgment is not good.
He who says to the wicked, "You are righteous," peoples will curse him, and nations will abhor him;
but to those who rebuke the wicked will be delight, and a good blessing will come upon them.
He who gives a right answer kisses the lips.
Prepare your work outside and make it ready for yourself in the field; afterward, then build your house.
Do not be a witness against your neighbor without cause, and do not deceive with your lips.
Do not say, "I will do to him as he has done to me; I will repay the man according to his deeds."
I passed by the field of the sluggard and by the vineyard of the man lacking sense,
and behold, it was all overgrown with thorns; nettles had covered its surface, and its stone wall was broken down.
When I saw it, I reflected upon it; I looked, and received instruction:
A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,
and your poverty will come like a robber, and your want like an armed man.
These too are proverbs of Solomon, transcribed by the men of Hezekiah, king of Judah.
It is the glory of God to conceal a matter, but the glory of kings to search it out.
As the heavens are high and the earth is deep, so the hearts of kings are unsearchable.
Remove the dross from silver, and a vessel emerges for the refiner.
Remove the wicked from the king's presence, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
Do not exalt yourself in the king's presence, nor stand in the place of great men;
for it is better that someone say to you, “Come up here,” than that you be humbled before a noble whom your own eyes have seen.
Do not rush into litigation, lest you be left not knowing what to do in the end, when your neighbor puts you to shame.
Argue your case with your neighbor, but do not reveal another's secret.
Lest the one who hears it put you to shame, and your infamy never depart.
A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
Like a gold ring or an ornament of fine gold is a wise rebuke to a listening ear.
Like the cold of snow in the time of harvest is a faithful messenger to those who send him, for he refreshes the soul of his masters.
Like clouds and wind without rain is a man who boasts of a gift he does not give.
Through patience a ruler is persuaded, and a soft tongue breaks the bone.
If you find honey, eat only enough, lest you be filled with it and vomit.
Visit your neighbor's house sparingly, lest he grow weary of you and hate you.
A man who bears false witness against his neighbor is like a club, a sword, and a sharp arrow.
Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble is like a loose tooth and a slipping foot.
Whoever sings songs to a heavy heart is like one who takes off a garment on a cold day, or like vinegar poured on soda.
If your enemy is hungry, give him bread to eat, and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
For you will heap burning coals on his head, and the LORD will reward you.
The north wind brings forth rain, and a backbiting tongue brings angry looks.
It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop than in a house shared with a quarrelsome woman.
Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a distant land.
Like a muddied spring and a polluted well is a righteous man who gives way before the wicked.
It is not good to eat much honey, nor is it glorious to seek one's own glory.
Like a city broken down and without walls is a man who cannot control his spirit.
Like snow in summer and rain in harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool.
Like a fluttering sparrow or a darting swallow, an undeserved curse never settles.
A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the back of fools.
Do not answer a fool according to his folly, lest you also be like him.
Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own eyes.
Whoever entrusts a message to a fool cripples himself and brings violence upon himself.
Like the legs of a lame man that hang useless, so is a proverb in the mouth of fools.
Like one who binds a stone into a sling, so is one who gives honor to a fool.
Like a thorn that goes up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a proverb in the mouth of fools.
Like an archer who wounds everyone is one who hires a fool or hires passersby.
As a dog returns to its vomit, so a fool repeats his folly.
Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
The sluggard says, "There is a lion in the road! A lion in the streets!"
As a door turns on its hinges, so does a sluggard on his bed.
The sluggard buries his hand in the dish; it wearies him to bring it back to his mouth.
The sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer sensibly.
Like one who grabs a dog by the ears is a passerby who meddles in a quarrel not his own.
Like a madman hurling firebrands, arrows, and death,
so is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, "I was only joking!"
For lack of wood the fire goes out, and where there is no whisperer, quarreling ceases.
As charcoal to hot coals and wood to fire, so is a quarrelsome man for kindling strife.
The words of a whisperer are like delicious morsels; they go down into the innermost parts.
Like glaze covering an earthen vessel are fervent lips with an evil heart.
He who hates disguises himself with his lips, but he stores up deceit within him.
When he speaks graciously, do not believe him, for there are seven abominations in his heart.
Though his hatred is concealed by deception, his wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.
Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, and he who rolls a stone, it will come back on him.
A lying tongue hates those it crushes, and a flattering mouth works ruin.
Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring forth.
Let another praise you, not your own mouth; a stranger, not your own lips.
A stone is heavy, and sand is weighty, but a fool's provocation outweighs them both.
Wrath is cruel, and anger is a torrent, but who can stand before jealousy?
Open rebuke is better than love concealed.
Faithful are the wounds of a friend, but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.
A satisfied appetite loathes honey, yet to a hungry soul every bitter thing tastes sweet.
Like a bird straying from its nest, so is a man who strays from his home.
Oil and incense gladden the heart, and the sweetness of a friend's counsel refreshes the soul.
Do not abandon your friend or your father's friend, and do not enter your brother's house on the day of your disaster; a neighbor nearby is better than a brother far away.
Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, so that I may answer the one who taunts me.
The prudent foresee danger and take cover, but the naive proceed and suffer the penalty.
Take the garment of one who guarantees a stranger's debt, and hold it in pledge for a foreign woman.
Whoever loudly blesses his neighbor at dawn will have it reckoned to him as a curse.
A continual dripping on a rainy day and a contentious wife are alike.
To restrain her is like restraining the wind or grasping oil in one's right hand.
As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another.
He who tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and he who watches over his master will be honored.
As water reflects the face, so a man's heart reflects the man.
Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied, nor are human eyes ever satisfied.
The crucible is for silver and the furnace for gold, and a man is tested by the praise he receives.
Though you grind a fool in a mortar amid grain with a pestle, his folly will not depart from him.
Be sure to know the condition of your flocks, and give careful attention to your herds,
for wealth is not forever, nor does a crown endure to all generations.
When the grass disappears and new growth appears and the herbs of the mountains are gathered,
the lambs will provide your clothing, and the goats will be the price of a field.
And there will be enough goats' milk for your food, for the food of your household, and for the sustenance of your maidservants.
The wicked flee though no one pursues, but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
When a land rebels, it has many rulers, yet a man of understanding and knowledge maintains order.
A poor man who oppresses the poor is like a sweeping rain that leaves no food.
Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, but those who keep the law resist them.
Evil people do not understand justice, but those who seek the LORD understand it fully.
Better is a poor man who walks in integrity than a rich man whose ways are perverse.
A discerning son heeds instruction, but a companion of gluttons disgraces his father.
He who increases his wealth by interest and usury gathers it for one who is gracious to the poor.
If anyone refuses to listen to the law, even his prayers are detestable.
Whoever leads the upright into an evil way will fall into his own trap, but the blameless will inherit good.
A rich man is wise in his own eyes, but a poor man with discernment sees through him.
When the righteous triumph, there is great glory; when the wicked rise, people hide themselves.
He who conceals his sins will not prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them will find mercy.
Blessed is the man who always fears the LORD, but he who becomes obstinate falls into trouble.
Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a poor people.
A leader lacking judgment is a great oppressor, but he who hates dishonest gain will prolong his days.
A man burdened with bloodguilt will flee until death; let no one support him.
He who walks in integrity will be saved, but he who is perverse in his ways will suddenly fall.
He who works his land will have plenty of food, but he who pursues empty schemes will have his fill of poverty.
A faithful man will be richly blessed, but one eager to get rich will not go unpunished.
To show partiality is not good, yet a man will do wrong for a piece of bread.
A stingy man is eager to get rich and does not know that poverty is coming upon him.
He who rebukes a man will in the end gain more favor than he who flatters with his tongue.
He who robs his father or mother and says, "It is not wrong," is a partner to one who destroys.
A greedy man stirs up strife, but he who trusts in the LORD will prosper.
He who trusts in his own heart is a fool, but he who walks in wisdom will be delivered.
He who gives to the poor will lack nothing, but he who looks away will receive many curses.
When the wicked rise to power, people hide themselves; but when they perish, the righteous thrive.
A person who remains obstinately defiant after repeated rebukes will be shattered suddenly, beyond remedy.
When the righteous flourish, the people rejoice, but when the wicked rule, the people groan.
Whoever loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but one who consorts with prostitutes squanders his wealth.
By justice a king gives stability to the land, but one who exacts tribute tears it down.
A person who flatters his neighbor sets a trap for his feet.
An evil person is caught in his own sin, while the righteous sing and rejoice.
The righteous concern themselves with justice for the poor, but the wicked have no regard for such matters.
Mockers inflame a city, but the wise turn away anger.
When a wise person contends with a fool, the fool rages and mocks, and there is no peace.
Bloodthirsty men hate a person of integrity and seek to kill the upright.
A fool gives free rein to his temper, but a wise person restrains it.
If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials become wicked.
The poor and the oppressor have this in common: the LORD gives light to the eyes of both.
If a king judges the poor with truth, his throne will be established forever.
A rod of correction and reproof imparts wisdom, but a child left to himself disgraces his mother.
When the wicked are in authority, transgression increases, but the righteous will see their downfall.
Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; he will bring delight to your soul.
Where there is no prophetic vision, the people cast off restraint, but blessed is the one who keeps the law.
A servant is not corrected by words alone; though he understands, he will not respond.
Do you see a person hasty in his words? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
A servant pampered from youth will turn out to be insolent.
An angry person stirs up strife, and a hot-tempered person abounds in transgression.
A person’s pride will bring him low, but a humble spirit will obtain honor.
Whoever partners with a thief hates his own life; though he hears the curse, he will not testify.
The fear of man lays a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is safe.
Many seek a ruler’s favor, but justice for a person comes from the LORD.
An unjust person is an abomination to the righteous, and one who is upright in the way is an abomination to the wicked.
The words of Agur son of Jakeh—an oracle. The man declares, "I am weary, O God; I am weary, O God, and faint."
Surely I am more brutish than any man, and human understanding eludes me.
I have not learned wisdom, nor do I possess knowledge of the Holy One.

Who has ascended to heaven and descended? Who has gathered the wind into His hands? Who has bound the waters in His cloak? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is His name, and what is the name of His Son? Surely you know!
Every utterance of God is flawless; He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.
Do not add to His words, lest He rebuke you and demonstrate that you are a liar.
Two things I ask of You; do not withhold them from me before I die:
Keep falsehood and deceit far from me. Grant me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the bread allotted to me.
Otherwise, I might have too much and deny You, saying, "Who is the LORD?" Or I might become poor and steal, thereby profaning the name of my God.
Do not slander a servant to his master, lest he curse you and you be held guilty.
There is a generation that curses its father and does not bless its mother.
There is a generation that is pure in its own eyes yet is not cleansed of its filth.
There is a generation whose eyes are so haughty, whose eyelids are raised high.
There is a generation whose teeth are swords and whose jaws are knives, devouring the poor from the earth and the needy from among men.
The leech has two daughters who cry, "Give! Give!" There are three things that are never satisfied—four that never say, "Enough!"
Sheol, the barren womb, land that is never satisfied with water, and fire that never says, "Enough!"
An eye that mocks a father and scorns a mother's discipline will be pecked out by the ravens of the valley and devoured by vultures.
There are three things too wonderful for me, four that I cannot comprehend:
the path of an eagle through the sky, the path of a serpent upon a rock, the course of a ship through the sea, and the way of a man with a maiden.
This is the way of an adulterous woman: she eats, wipes her mouth, and says, "I have done nothing wrong."
Under three things the earth trembles; under four it cannot bear up:
a servant who becomes king, a fool who is filled with food,
an unloved woman who marries, and a maidservant who supplants her mistress.
Four things on earth are small, yet they are exceedingly wise:
the ants are not a powerful people, yet they store up their food in summer;
the rock badgers are not a mighty people, yet they make their dwellings in the cliffs;
the locusts have no king, yet they all march out in formation;
the lizard can be seized with the hands, yet it is found in the palaces of kings.
There are three things that are stately in their stride, four that are impressive in their gait:
a lion, mightiest among beasts, who does not retreat before anyone;
a strutting rooster, a goat, and a king with his army around him.
If you have acted foolishly by exalting yourself, or if you have devised evil, put your hand over your mouth.
For as churning milk produces butter, and wringing a nose produces blood, so stirring up anger produces strife.
The words of King Lemuel—an oracle that his mother imparted to him:
“What is it, my son? What is it, son of my womb? What is it, son of my vows?
Do not lavish your strength upon women, nor surrender your ways to those who destroy kings.
It is unbecoming for kings, Lemuel—it is unbecoming for kings to drink wine, nor for rulers to crave strong drink,
lest they drink and forget what has been decreed, thereby perverting justice for all the afflicted.
Give strong drink to the perishing, and wine to those whose souls are bitter.
Let them drink and forget their poverty, and remember their misery no more.
Open your mouth for those who have no voice, and plead the cause of all the dispossessed.
Open your mouth, judge with righteousness, and defend the poor and the needy.”
Who can discover a wife of noble character? She is far more precious than rubies.
The heart of her husband safely trusts in her, and he will suffer no lack of gain.
She brings him good, and not harm, throughout all the days of her life.
She procures wool and flax, and labors with willing hands.
She is comparable to the merchant ships, bringing her provision from afar.
She rises while it is still night to furnish food for her household and portions for her maidservants.
She contemplates a field and acquires it; from her earnings she plants a vineyard.
She equips herself with strength and fortifies her arms.
She perceives that her merchandise is good, and her lamp is not extinguished at night.
She stretches out her hands to the distaff, and her fingers grasp the spindle.
She extends her hands to the indigent and reaches out to the needy.
She is not afraid of snow for her household, for all her household are clothed in scarlet.
She fashions coverings for her bed; her raiment is fine linen and purple.
Her husband is renowned at the city gate, where he sits among the elders of the land.
She fashions linen garments and markets them; she delivers sashes to the merchant.
Strength and dignity constitute her attire, and she faces the days to come without dread.
She opens her mouth with wisdom, and faithful instruction is on her tongue.
She watches over the conduct of her household and does not live in idleness.
Her children rise up and call her blessed; her husband also praises her:
“Many daughters have done valiantly, but you surpass them all.”
Charm is deceitful and beauty is fleeting, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
Give her the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her publicly.
These are the words of the Teacher, the son of David, who reigned as king in Jerusalem.
“Utter futility,” says the Teacher, “utter futility; everything is futile.”
What profit does a person derive from all the toil he expends on earth?
One generation passes away and another arises, yet the earth abides in perpetuity.
