The sun rises and the sun sets, hastening to the place from which it rises again.
The wind proceeds southward and veers northward; circling, ever circling, it returns upon its circuits.
All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is never filled; to the place from which the rivers flow, they return to flow again.
All things are wearisome beyond utterance: the eye is never satiated with seeing, nor the ear contented with hearing.
What has been is what will be, and what has been accomplished is what will be accomplished; there is nothing new on earth.
Is there anything of which one may say, “Behold, this is new”? It has already existed in the ages that preceded us.
There is no remembrance of former things, and even those yet to come will leave no remembrance among those who succeed them.
I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
I devoted my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom all that is done in the world. What a burdensome occupation God has assigned to humanity, to be exercised therein!
I have observed all the works that are done on earth, and indeed all is futile, an empty pursuit.
What is crooked cannot be made straight, and what is deficient cannot be reckoned.
I said in my heart, “Look, I have magnified and increased wisdom beyond all who preceded me in Jerusalem, and my heart has perceived much wisdom and knowledge.”
Then I set my heart to know wisdom, and likewise to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also is an empty pursuit.
For in abundant wisdom is abundant vexation, and he who augments knowledge augments sorrow.
I said in my heart, “Come now, I will test you with pleasure; enjoy what is good.” Yet, as I discovered, this too was futility.
I said of laughter, “It is madness,” and of pleasure, “What does it accomplish?”

I searched my heart to cheer my flesh with wine—my heart still guiding me with wisdom—and to embrace folly, until I could see what is good for people to do under heaven during the few days of their lives.
I undertook great projects. I built houses for myself and planted vineyards for myself.
I made gardens and parks for myself, and I planted in them every kind of fruit tree.
I made reservoirs of water to irrigate a forest of growing trees.
I acquired male and female servants, and slaves were born in my household. I also owned more herds and flocks than anyone who had lived before me in Jerusalem.
I amassed silver and gold for myself, along with the treasure of kings and provinces. I acquired male and female singers, and a harem—the delights of mankind.
So I became greater and surpassed all who had been before me in Jerusalem, and my wisdom remained with me.
I did not deny my eyes anything they desired; I withheld no pleasure from my heart, for my heart took delight in all my labor, and this was my portion from all my labor.
Then I considered all that my hands had accomplished and all the toil I had expended, and I saw that all was futility—a fruitless pursuit; there was no profit under the sun.
Then I turned to consider wisdom, madness, and folly, for what can the person who comes after the king do except what has already been done?
I saw that wisdom has an advantage over folly, just as light has an advantage over darkness.
The wise person sees ahead, while the fool gropes in darkness; yet I perceived that the same fate overtakes them all.
Then I said to myself, “The fate of the fool will befall me as well. Why, then, have I been so exceedingly wise?” And I said to myself that this too is futility.
For there is no lasting memory of the wise, just as there is for the fool, since in the days to come all will have been forgotten. How tragic that the wise die just like the fool!
So I hated life, because the work done under the sun was grievous to me; for all is futility and a waste of effort.
I hated all my toil in which I had toiled under the sun, because I must leave it to the person who comes after me.
And who knows whether he will be wise or a fool? Yet he will take possession of all my labor and skill with which I toiled under the sun. This too is futility.
So I turned and gave my heart over to despair concerning all the toil of my labor under the sun.
For there is one whose labor is with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, yet he must leave his estate to one who has not worked for it. This too is futility and a great evil.
For what does a person gain from all his toil and from the anxious striving with which he labors under the sun?
Indeed, all his days are sorrowful, and his work is a vexation; even at night his heart does not rest. This too is futility.
There is nothing better for a person than to eat and drink and find enjoyment in his toil. I have also seen that this is from the hand of God.
For apart from Him, who can eat or find enjoyment?

For to the one who pleases Him, God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy; but to the sinner He gives the task of gathering and accumulating, only to hand it over to one who pleases God. This too is futility and a pointless pursuit.
There is a season for everything, and a time for every purpose on earth:
a time to be born and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot what is planted;
a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to tear down and a time to build;
a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance;
a time to scatter stones and a time to gather them, a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing;
a time to seek and a time to relinquish, a time to keep and a time to cast away;
a time to tear and a time to mend, a time to be silent and a time to speak;
a time to love and a time to hate, a time for war and a time for peace.
What gain does the worker derive from his toil?
I have seen the burden God has laid upon the human race to keep them occupied.
He has made everything beautiful in its time; He has also set eternity in the human heart, yet no one can fathom what God has done from beginning to end.
I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and to do good while they live,
and that every person should eat and drink and find satisfaction in all his labor—this is the gift of God.
I know that whatever God does endures forever; nothing can be added to it, and nothing can be taken from it. God has done this so that people will fear Him.
Whatever is has already been, and what is to come has already occurred; and God calls to account what has been driven away.
Moreover, I saw in this world that in the place of judgment there is wickedness, and in the place of righteousness there is wickedness.
I said in my heart that God will judge both the righteous and the wicked, for there is a time for every purpose and for every work there.
I said in my heart concerning the sons of men that God tests them, so that they may see that they themselves are like beasts.
For the fate of human beings and the fate of beasts is the same: as one dies, so dies the other. They all have the same breath, and man has no advantage over the beasts, for all is meaningless.
All go to one place: all are from the dust, and all return to dust.
Who knows whether the spirit of man ascends upward and the spirit of the beast descends into the earth?
So I saw that there is nothing better than that a man should rejoice in his works, for that is his portion. For who can bring him to see what will be after him?

I turned again and surveyed all the oppression inflicted beneath the sun. I saw the tears of the oppressed, with no one to comfort them; power belonged to their oppressors, and still no one comforted them.
So I declared the dead, who have already died, more fortunate than the living, who are still alive.
Yet better than both is the one who has never been born, who has not seen the evil deeds done beneath the sun.
Then I observed all toil and every skillful work, and I recognized that it arises from one person's envy of another. This too is vanity and a chasing after wind.
The fool folds his hands and destroys himself.
Better is a handful of quietness than two handfuls of toil and a chasing after wind.
I turned again and saw vanity beneath the sun.

There is someone alone, without companion, child, or brother, yet no end to his toil; his eyes are never satisfied with wealth. He asks, "For whom am I toiling and depriving myself of good?" This too is vanity and a grievous task.
Two are better than one, because they receive a good reward for their labor.
If one falls, the other can lift up his companion; but woe to the one who falls alone and has no second to raise him.
If two lie together, they keep warm, but how can one keep warm alone?
And if someone overpowers one, two can withstand him; a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Better is a poor but wise youth than an old and foolish king who no longer knows how to take warning.
For he came out of prison to reign, though he was born poor in his kingdom.
I saw all the living who walk beneath the sun, along with the successor, the child who will take his place.
There is no end to all the people who came before them, yet those who come after will not rejoice in him. This too is vanity and a chasing after wind.
Guard your steps when you enter the house of God. Draw near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools, for they do not realize that they are doing wrong.
Do not be hasty with your mouth, and do not let your heart rush to utter a word before God, for God is in heaven and you are on earth; therefore let your words be few.
For a dream comes with many cares, and a fool's voice with many words.
When you make a vow to God, do not delay to fulfill it, for He has no pleasure in fools. Fulfill what you have vowed.
It is better not to vow than to make a vow and not fulfill it.
Do not let your mouth cause you to sin, and do not tell the messenger that your vow was a mistake. Why should God be angry with your words and destroy the work of your hands?
For in a multitude of dreams and words there is emptiness; therefore fear God.
If you see the poor oppressed in a district and justice and righteousness denied, do not be astonished at the matter, for one official is watched by a higher one, and higher ones still are over them.
The profit of the land is for all; the king himself is served by the field.
Whoever loves money is never satisfied with money, and whoever loves wealth never has enough income. This too is meaningless.
When possessions increase, those who consume them increase as well; and what benefit is there to the owner except to see them with his own eyes?
The sleep of a laborer is sweet, whether he eats little or much, but the abundance of a rich person permits no sleep.
I have seen a grievous evil under the sun: wealth stored up to the harm of its owner,
or wealth lost through misfortune, so that when its owner has a son, nothing remains in his hand.
As a person comes from his mother's womb, so he returns naked; he takes nothing from his toil that he can carry away in his hand.
This too is a grievous evil: exactly as he came, so he goes, and what profit does he have from toiling for the wind?
All his days he eats in darkness, with much sorrow, sickness, and anger.
This is what I have observed to be good and fitting: to eat and drink and to enjoy the good from all one's labor under the sun during the few days of life God has given, for this is one's portion.
Furthermore, when God gives a person wealth and possessions and enables him to enjoy them, to accept his lot, and to rejoice in his labor, this is a gift from God.
For he will not dwell much on the days of his life, because God keeps him occupied with joy in his heart.
There is an evil I have seen in this world, and it weighs heavily upon humanity:

God gives a man riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing his heart desires, yet God does not grant him the power to enjoy it; instead a stranger consumes it. This is futility and a grievous affliction.

If a man begets a hundred children and lives many years—yes, many are the days of his years—but his soul is never satisfied with good, and moreover he has no burial, I say that the stillborn is better than he.
For it comes in futility and goes in darkness, and in darkness its name is covered.
Moreover, it has never seen the sun nor known anything, yet it has more rest than he.
Even if he lived two thousand years and never enjoyed what is good—do not all meet the same end?
All human toil is for the mouth, yet the appetite is never satisfied.
What advantage has the wise over the fool? What does the poor man gain by knowing how to conduct himself among the living?
Better is what the eyes see than the wandering of desire. This too is futility and an empty pursuit.
Whatever exists has already been named, and it is known what man is; he cannot contend with the One stronger than he.
Indeed, the more words, the more futility; and what advantage is there for man?
For who knows what is good for a man in life, during the few days of his fleeting existence, which pass like a shadow? Who can tell a man what will come after him in this world?
A good name is more valuable than costly perfume, and the day of one's death surpasses the day of one's birth.
It is better to enter a house of mourning than a house of feasting, because death is the common destiny of all humanity, and the living should take this truth to heart.
Grief surpasses laughter, for a sorrowful countenance can refine the heart.
The wise heart gravitates toward the house of mourning, whereas the foolish heart gravitates toward the house of pleasure.
It is better to heed a wise person's reproof than to listen to the songs of fools.
For as thorns crackle beneath a pot, so is the laughter of fools—and that too is futility.
Surely oppression can drive a wise person to madness, and a bribe corrupts the heart.
The conclusion of a matter is better than its commencement, and patience is superior to pride.
Do not be quick to anger in your spirit, for anger settles in the lap of fools.
Do not ask, "Why were former days better than these?" for such a question does not spring from wisdom.
Wisdom, like an inheritance, is good and advantageous to those who see the sun.
For wisdom is a shelter, as money is a shelter, but the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its possessor.
Consider the work of God: who can straighten what He has bent?
In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity reflect on this: God has made one alongside the other, so that a person cannot discover what will come after him.
In my futile life I have seen everything: a righteous person perishing in his righteousness, and a wicked person prolonging his life in his wickedness.
Do not be excessively righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why should you bring ruin upon yourself?
Do not be excessively wicked, and do not be a fool. Why should you die before your time?
It is good to grasp the one and not let the other slip from your hand, for the one who fears God will heed both warnings.
Wisdom empowers the wise person more than ten rulers in a city.
Surely there is no righteous person on earth who does good and never sins.
Do not give heed to every word people say, lest you hear your servant cursing you.
For you know in your heart that you yourself have cursed others many times.
All this I tested by wisdom, saying, "I will be wise," but it remained beyond me.
What exists is far off and profoundly deep. Who can discover it?
I set my mind to know, to investigate, and to seek out wisdom and the scheme of things, and to understand the folly of wickedness and the madness of folly.
I found something more bitter than death: the woman whose heart is snares and nets, whose hands are chains. The man who pleases God will escape her, but the sinner will be ensnared by her.
"Behold, this is what I have found," says the Teacher, "adding one thing to another to find the sum."
While my soul was still searching but not finding, I found one upright man among a thousand, but not one upright woman among them all.
Behold, I have found only this: God made mankind upright, but they have sought out many schemes.
Who is like the wise man, and who understands the interpretation of a matter? A man’s wisdom makes his face shine, and the sternness of his face is changed.
Keep the king’s command, I say, because of your oath before God.
Do not be hasty to leave his presence, and do not persist in an evil matter, for he does whatever he pleases.
Since a king’s word is supreme, who can say to him, “What are you doing?”
Whoever keeps a command will experience no harm, and a wise heart will know the proper time and procedure.
For there is a proper time and procedure for every matter, though a man’s misery weighs heavily upon him.
Since no one knows what will happen, who can tell him what is to come?
As no one has power over the wind to contain it, so no one has power over the day of death. There is no discharge from that war, nor will wickedness deliver those who practice it.
All this I have seen, and I applied my heart to every deed that is done under the sun, at a time when one man has power over another to his harm.
Then I saw the wicked buried—those who used to come and go from the holy place and received praise in the city where they did this. This too is futility.
When the sentence for a crime is not speedily executed, the hearts of men become fully set on doing evil.
Although a sinner does evil a hundred times and still lives long, yet I know that it will be well with those who fear God, who stand in awe before Him.
Yet it will not be well with the wicked, nor will he prolong his days like a shadow, because he does not fear God.
There is a futility that is done on the earth: there are righteous men who get what the wicked deserve, and there are wicked men who get what the righteous deserve. I say that this too is futility.

So I commended joy, for there is nothing better for a man under the sun than to eat and drink and be merry. For this will accompany him in his labor during the days of his life that God has given him under the sun.
When I applied my heart to know wisdom and to observe the activity that is done on the earth—even though one’s eyes do not see sleep day or night—

I saw every work of God, and that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun. For though a man labors to seek it out, yet he will not find it; indeed, even if a wise man claims to know it, he cannot find it.
For I set all this before my heart and sought to examine it thoroughly: the righteous, the wise, and their deeds are in God's hand, yet no one can know whether love or hatred lies ahead for them.

Everything befalls all alike: one fate overtakes the righteous and the wicked, the good and the evil, the clean and the unclean, the one who sacrifices and the one who refrains. As with the good, so with the sinner; as with the one who swears an oath, so with the one who dreads swearing.

This is the calamity in everything done on earth: one fate befalls everyone. Furthermore, the hearts of human beings are full of evil and madness throughout their lives, and afterward they join the dead.
Yet hope remains for anyone still among the living, for even the lowliest living person fares better than the greatest who has died.
The living know that they must die, but the dead know nothing; they receive no further reward, and even their memory is forgotten.
Their love, hatred, and jealousy have already vanished, and they will never again have any share in anything done on earth.
Go, then, eat your bread with joy and drink your wine with a glad heart, for God has already approved your works.
Let your garments be white at all times, and do not allow oil to be lacking on your head.
Enjoy life with the wife you love through all the days of your fleeting life that He has given you on earth—all your fleeting days—for this is your portion in life and in your toil on earth.
Whatever your hand finds to do, accomplish it with all your might, for in Sheol, where you are going, there is no work, planning, knowledge, or wisdom.

I have also seen on earth that the race is not won by the swift, nor the battle by the strong, nor bread by the wise, nor riches by the discerning, nor favor by the knowledgeable, for time and chance overtake them all.
Moreover, no one knows his appointed time. Like fish caught in a cruel net and birds caught in a snare, so human beings are trapped by disaster when it suddenly descends upon them.
I have also seen this wisdom on earth, and it seemed great to me:
there was a small city with few inhabitants, and a great king came against it, besieged it, and erected massive siege works against it.
Yet a poor wise man was found in it, and he delivered the city by his wisdom; nevertheless, no one remembered that poor man.
So I said, "Wisdom is better than strength," but the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words go unheeded.
The quiet words of the wise are heard more readily than the shouting of a ruler among fools.
Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.
Dead flies make the perfumer’s ointment give off a stench; so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.
A wise person’s heart inclines to the right, but a fool’s heart inclines to the left.
Even when a fool walks along the road, his sense is lacking, and he shows everyone that he is a fool.
If the ruler’s temper flares against you, do not abandon your post, for calmness lays great offenses to rest.
There is an evil I have seen under the sun—an error that proceeds from the ruler:
folly is set in many high places, while the rich sit in lowly positions.
I have seen slaves on horseback, while princes walk on foot like slaves.
Whoever digs a pit falls into it, and a serpent bites whoever breaks through a wall.
Whoever quarries stones may be injured by them, and whoever splits logs may be endangered by them.
If an axe is dull and its edge remains unsharpened, one must exert more strength, but wisdom makes the work succeed.
If a snake bites before it is charmed, the charmer gains no advantage.
The words of a wise person’s mouth are gracious, but a fool’s lips consume him.
The beginning of his talk is folly, and the end of his speech is evil madness.
A fool multiplies words, though no one knows what is to come, and who can tell him what will be after him?
A fool’s labor exhausts him, because he does not know the way to the city.
Woe to you, O land, when your king is a youth, and your princes feast in the morning.
Blessed are you, O land, when your king is the son of nobles, and your princes feast at the proper time—for strength and not for drunkenness.
Through sloth the roof sinks in, and through idle hands the house leaks.
Bread is made for laughter, wine gladdens life, and money answers everything.
Do not curse the king even in your thoughts, nor in your bedroom curse the rich, for a bird in flight may carry your words, or some winged creature may report the matter.
Be generous with your resources, for after many days you will recover them.
Distribute a portion among seven recipients, or even eight, because you cannot foresee what calamity may strike the land.
If the clouds grow full, they pour rain upon the earth; and if a tree falls to the south or to the north, it remains wherever it falls.
Whoever obsesses over the wind will not sow, and whoever stares at the clouds will not reap.
As you do not know the path of the wind, nor how bones are formed in the womb of a pregnant woman, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.
Sow your seed in the morning, and do not let your hand grow slack in the evening, for you do not know which will prosper—whether this or that—or whether both alike will be good.
Light is sweet, and it is pleasant for the eyes to behold the sun.
If a man lives many years, let him rejoice in all of them, but let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many; everything that is to come is futility.

Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth; walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes, but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
Remove vexation from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh, for youth and the dawn of life are futility.
Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of trouble come and the years approach when you will say, "I have no pleasure in them."
Before the sun and the light and the moon and the stars are darkened, and the clouds return after the rain;
when the keepers of the house tremble, and the mighty men stoop, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those who look through the windows grow dim;
when the doors to the street are closed, and the sound of grinding fades; when one rises at the sound of a bird, and all the daughters of song grow faint;

when men are afraid of heights and dangers on the road; when the almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper drags himself along, and the caper berry bursts; when man goes to his eternal home and mourners walk the streets.
Before the silver cord is severed and the golden bowl is crushed, the pitcher is shattered at the spring, and the wheel is broken at the well.
Then the dust returns to the ground it came from, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
"Meaningless! Meaningless!" says the Teacher. "Everything is meaningless!"
Not only was the Teacher wise, but he also taught the people knowledge; he pondered and searched out and set in order many proverbs.
The Teacher searched to find delightful words and to write words of truth correctly.
The words of the wise are like goads, and like firmly embedded nails driven by a single Shepherd.
Be warned, my son, of anything in addition to them: Of making many books there is no end, and much study wearies the body.
Now all has been heard; here is the conclusion of the matter: Fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the duty of all mankind.
For God will bring every deed into judgment, along with every hidden thing, whether good or evil.
The Song of Songs, which is Solomon's.
“Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth, for your love is sweeter than wine.
Your ointments give off a pleasing fragrance; your name is like perfume poured out, and so the young women love you.
Draw me after you, and let us run! The king has brought me into his chambers. We will rejoice and be glad in you; we will celebrate your love more than wine. Rightly do they love you.”
“I am dark, yet lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem—like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.
Do not stare at me because I am darkened, because the sun has scorched me. My mother's sons were angry with me and made me keeper of the vineyards, but I have not tended my own beauty.
Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you pasture your flock and where you rest it at noon, lest I become like a veiled woman wandering among the flocks of your companions.”
“If you do not know, O most beautiful among women, follow the tracks of the flock and pasture your young goats beside the shepherds' tents.
I compare you, my darling, to a mare among Pharaoh's chariots.
Your cheeks are lovely with ornaments, your neck with strings of jewels.
We will make you ornaments of gold studded with silver.”
“While the king is at his table, my nard releases its fragrance.
My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh resting between my breasts.
My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms in the vineyards of En Gedi.”
“Behold, you are beautiful, my darling; behold, you are beautiful; your eyes are doves.”
“Behold, you are handsome, my beloved, truly delightful; our couch is verdant.
The beams of our house are cedars, and our rafters are cypresses.”
I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.
Like a lily among thorns, so is my darling among the daughters.
Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, so is my beloved among the young men. I delight to sit in his shade, and his fruit is sweet to my taste.
He has brought me to the banquet hall, and his banner over me is love.
Sustain me with raisin cakes; refresh me with apples, for I am faint with love.
His left arm is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.
O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: do not arouse or awaken love until it so desires.
Listen! My beloved! Look! Here he comes, leaping across the mountains, bounding over the hills.
My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Look! There he stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattice.
My beloved spoke and said to me, “Arise, my darling, my beautiful one, and come away.
For now the winter is past; the rain is over and gone.
The flowers have appeared in the countryside; the season of singing has come, and the cooing of turtledoves is heard in our land.
The fig tree is ripening its early fruit; the blossoming vines spread their fragrance. Arise, my darling, my beautiful one, and come away.” “
O my dove, in the clefts of the rock, in the covert of the cliff, let me see your face, let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your countenance is lovely.”
Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that ruin the vineyards while our vineyards are in bloom.
My beloved is mine and I am his; he shepherds his flock among the lilies.
Until the day breaks and the shadows flee, turn, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of Bether.
Upon my bed in the night watches, I sought the one I love; I sought him, but he was not to be found.
I will arise now and go about the city, through its streets and squares, and seek the one I love. I sought him, but he was not to be found.
The sentinels patrolling the city found me, and I asked them, "Have you seen the one I love?"
Scarcely had I passed them before I found the one I love; I seized him and would not release him until I had brought him to my mother's house, to the chamber of her who bore me.
Daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and the does of the field: do not stir up or awaken love until it is ready.
Who is this coming up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with every fragrant powder of the merchant?
Behold, Solomon's palanquin, escorted by sixty warriors, the mightiest of Israel.
Each is skilled with the sword and trained for war; each man wears his sword upon his thigh because of the terrors of night.
King Solomon made for himself a palanquin of Lebanese cedar.
He made its posts of silver, its base of gold, its seat of purple; its interior is inlaid with love by the daughters of Jerusalem.
"Go out, daughters of Zion, and behold King Solomon, wearing the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding, the day his heart rejoiced."
“How exquisite you are, my darling—how exquisite indeed! Your eyes are like doves behind your veil; your hair descends like a flock of goats streaming down from Mount Gilead.
Your teeth resemble a flock of shorn ewes ascending from the washing, each bearing twins, with none left barren.
Your lips are like a scarlet thread, and your speech is altogether lovely; your cheeks glow like a slice of pomegranate behind your veil.”
“Your neck is like the tower of David, fashioned in courses of stone; upon it hang a thousand shields, every one the shield of a mighty warrior.
Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, grazing among the lilies.”
“Until the day breathes and the shadows flee, I will betake myself to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.
You are wholly beautiful, my darling; no blemish is found in you.”
“Come with me from Lebanon, my bride; come with me from Lebanon. Gaze down from the summit of Amana, from the summit of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of lions and the mountains of leopards.
You have captivated my heart, my sister, my bride; you have captivated my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your necklace.
How delightful is your love, my sister, my bride! Your love surpasses wine in delight, and the fragrance of your perfume exceeds every spice.
Your lips, my bride, drip with honey; honey and milk are beneath your tongue; and the fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of Lebanon.”
“You are a garden enclosed, my sister, my bride, a spring enclosed, a fountain sealed.
Your shoots form an orchard of pomegranates with precious fruits, henna with nard,
nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of frankincense, myrrh and aloes, with all the choicest spices.
You are a garden spring, a well of living water streaming down from Lebanon.”
“Awake, north wind, and come, south wind! Breathe upon my garden, that its fragrance may be diffused. Let my beloved enter his garden and partake of its choicest fruit.”

"I have entered my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh amid my spices; I have eaten my honeycomb with its honey; I have drunk my wine with its milk. Eat, O friends; drink, and be drunk with love, O beloved ones."

I was slumbering, yet my heart kept watch. Listen! My beloved knocks, saying, "Open to me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my flawless one, for my head is drenched with dew, my locks with the dampness of night."
I have taken off my robe; how could I put it on again? I have washed my feet; how could I soil them?
My beloved thrust his hand through the opening, and my heart was stirred for him.
I arose to open to my beloved, and my hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh, upon the handles of the bolt.
I opened to my beloved, but my beloved had turned and gone. My soul failed me when he spoke. I sought him, but I did not find him; I called him, but he did not answer.
The watchmen who patrol the city found me; they struck me and wounded me; the keepers of the walls took my veil from me.
"I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved, tell him that I am sick with love."
"What makes your beloved better than another beloved, O most beautiful among women? What makes your beloved better than another beloved, that you so charge us?"
"My beloved is radiant and ruddy, distinguished among ten thousand.
His head is like pure gold; his locks are wavy, black as a raven.
His eyes are like doves beside the watercourses, washed in milk, and set like jewels.
His cheeks are like beds of spices, towers of perfumes; his lips are lilies, dripping liquid myrrh.
His hands are rods of gold set with topaz; his body is ivory work adorned with sapphires.
His legs are pillars of marble set on bases of fine gold; his stature is like Lebanon, choice as the cedars.
His mouth is sweetness itself, and he is altogether desirable. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem."
“Where has your beloved gone, O most beautiful among women? Where has your beloved turned, that we may seek him with you?”
“My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to graze among the gardens and gather lilies.”
“I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine; he grazes among the lilies.”
“You are beautiful, my darling, as Tirzah, lovely as Jerusalem, awesome as an army with banners.
Turn your eyes away from me, for they have overcome me. Your hair is like a flock of goats descending from Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin, and not one is missing.
Your temples are like a slice of pomegranate behind your veil.
There are sixty queens and eighty concubines, and virgins beyond number.
My dove, my perfect one, is unique, the only daughter of her mother, the favorite of the one who bore her. The maidens see her and call her blessed; the queens and concubines praise her.”
“Who is this who looks down like the dawn, beautiful as the moon, bright as the sun, awesome as an army with banners?”
“I went down to the walnut grove to see the blossoms of the valley, to see whether the vines were in bloom or the pomegranates were budding.
Before I realized it, my desire had set me among the chariots of my noble people.”
“Return, return, O Shulammite! Return, return, that we may look upon you. Why would you gaze at the Shulammite as on the dance of Mahanaim?”
"How beautiful your feet are in sandals, daughter of a noble! The curves of your hips are like jewels, fashioned by a master craftsman.
Your navel is a rounded goblet that never lacks mixed wine; your belly is a heap of wheat encircled by lilies.
Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
Your neck is like an ivory tower; your eyes are the pools of Heshbon beside the gate of Bath-rabbim; your nose is like the tower of Lebanon that looks toward Damascus.
Your head crowns you like Mount Carmel, and the tresses of your head are like purple; a king is held captive in its tresses.
How beautiful and pleasant you are, my love, with your delights!
Your stature resembles a palm tree, and your breasts are like its clusters.
I said, 'I will climb the palm tree and take hold of its fruit.' May your breasts be like clusters of the vine, and the fragrance of your breath be like apples;
and may your mouth be like the finest wine, flowing smoothly for my beloved and gliding over the lips of those who sleep."
"I am my beloved's, and his desire is for me.
Come, my beloved, let us go out into the fields and lodge in the villages.
Let us rise early and go to the vineyards; let us see whether the vine has budded, whether the blossom has opened, and whether the pomegranates are in bloom—there I will give you my love.
The mandrakes give forth their fragrance, and at our doors are all choice fruits, new and old, which I have treasured up for you, my beloved."
“If only you were my brother, nursed at my mother’s breast, I could kiss you before the world, and none would despise me.
I would lead you and bring you to my mother’s house, where you would teach me; I would make you drink spiced wine, the rich juice pressed from my pomegranate.
His left hand would support my head, while his right arm embraced me.
I charge you, daughters of Jerusalem: do not rouse or awaken love until it is ready.”
“Who is this ascending from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved?” “Beneath the apple tree I awakened you; there your mother labored with you, and there the woman who bore you was in travail.
Place me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm; for love is as strong as death, and jealousy is as unyielding as the grave. Its flashes are flashes of fire—the very flame of the LORD.
Many waters cannot quench love, nor can rivers sweep it away. If a man offered all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly despised.”
“We have a little sister, and she has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister on the day she is spoken for?
If she proves a wall, we will build upon her a silver parapet; if she proves a door, we will enclose her with cedar boards.”
“I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers. Then I became in his eyes as one who finds peace.”
“Solomon possessed a vineyard at Baal-hamon; he entrusted it to keepers, each of whom was to bring a thousand pieces of silver for its fruit.
My vineyard, my own, is before me. You, Solomon, may have the thousand, and the keepers two hundred.”
“O you who dwell in the gardens, while companions listen for your voice—let me hear it.”
“Hasten, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag upon the mountains of spices.”
The vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem that Isaiah son of Amoz saw during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Hear, O heavens, and listen, O earth, for the LORD has spoken: “I reared children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against Me.
The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master’s feeding trough, but Israel does not know; My people do not understand.”

Alas, sinful nation, a people weighed down with iniquity, offspring of evildoers, children who deal corruptly! They have forsaken the LORD; they have despised the Holy One of Israel; they have turned away from Him.
Why should you be struck down again? You will only add rebellion. The whole head is sick, and the whole heart is faint.
From the sole of the foot to the head there is no soundness—only wounds, bruises, and open sores, neither cleansed nor bandaged nor soothed with oil.
Your land is desolate; your cities are burned with fire. Foreigners devour your fields before your eyes; it is desolate, as if ravaged by foreigners.
And the Daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a melon patch, like a city under siege.
If the LORD of Hosts had not left us a small remnant, we would have been like Sodom; we would have resembled Gomorrah.
Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom; listen to the instruction of our God, you people of Gomorrah!
“What are your many sacrifices to Me?” says the LORD. “I have had enough of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fattened cattle. I have no delight in the blood of bulls, lambs, or goats.
When you come to appear before Me, who has required this of you—this trampling of My courts?
Bring no more vain offerings; incense is an abomination to Me. New moons, Sabbaths, and convocations—I cannot endure iniquity along with solemn assembly.
My soul hates your New Moons and your appointed feasts; they have become a burden to Me; I am weary of bearing them.
When you spread out your hands, I will hide My eyes from you; even though you multiply prayers, I will not listen. Your hands are stained with blood.
Wash and make yourselves clean; remove the evil of your deeds from before My eyes; stop doing evil.
Learn to do good; seek justice; correct the oppressor; defend the fatherless; plead for the widow.”
“Come now, let us reason together,” says the LORD. “Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow; though they are red like crimson, they will become like wool.
If you are willing and obedient, you will eat the good of the land.
But if you refuse and rebel, you will be devoured by the sword.” For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
How the faithful city has become a prostitute! She who was full of justice—righteousness lodged in her—but now murderers.
Your silver has become dross; your wine is diluted with water.
Your rulers are rebels and companions of thieves. Everyone loves a bribe and chases gifts. They do not defend the fatherless, and the widow’s case does not come before them.
Therefore the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, declares: “Ah, I will be relieved of My adversaries and avenge Myself on My enemies.
I will turn My hand against you; I will purge your dross as with lye, and remove all your alloy.
I will restore your judges as at the first, and your counselors as at the beginning. Afterward you will be called the City of Righteousness, the Faithful City.
Zion will be redeemed with justice, and her repentant ones with righteousness.
But rebels and sinners will be crushed together, and those who forsake the LORD will perish.
For you will be ashamed of the oaks you desired, and you will blush for the gardens you chose.
For you will be like an oak whose leaves wither, and like a garden without water.
The strong man will become tinder, and his work a spark; both will burn together, and no one will quench them.”
The message that Isaiah son of Amoz beheld concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
In the last days the mountain of the house of the LORD will be established as the chief of the mountains; it will be raised above the hills, and all the nations will stream to it.

Many peoples will come and say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob. He will teach us His ways, so that we may walk in His paths." For out of Zion will go forth the law, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

He will arbitrate among the nations and render decisions for many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not take up sword against nation, nor will they train for war anymore.
Come, O house of Jacob, let us walk in the light of the LORD.
For You have abandoned Your people, the house of Jacob, because they are filled with influences from the east and with soothsayers like the Philistines, and they make alliances with foreigners.
Their land is full of silver and gold, and there is no end to their treasures. Their land is full of horses, and there is no end to their chariots.
Their land is full of idols; they bow down to the work of their hands, to what their fingers have made.
So mankind is humbled and brought low; do not forgive them.
Go into the rocks and hide in the dust from the terror of the LORD and the splendor of His majesty.
The proud look of man will be humbled, and the loftiness of men will be brought low; the LORD alone will be exalted in that day.
For the Day of the LORD of Hosts will come against all that is proud and lofty, against all that is lifted up, and it will be brought low—
against all the cedars of Lebanon, lofty and lifted up, and against all the oaks of Bashan;
against all the high mountains and all the lofty hills;
against every high tower and every fortified wall;
against all the ships of Tarshish and every stately vessel.
So the pride of man will be brought low, and the loftiness of men will be humbled; the LORD alone will be exalted in that day.
And the idols will vanish completely.
People will flee to caves in the rocks and holes in the ground, away from the terror of the LORD and the splendor of His majesty, when He rises to shake the earth.
In that day people will throw their silver and gold idols to the moles and bats—idols they made to worship.
They will enter the crevices of the rocks and the clefts of the cliffs, away from the terror of the LORD and the splendor of His majesty, when He rises to shake the earth.
Stop trusting in man, whose life is but a breath in his nostrils. What is he worth?
For behold, the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, is removing from Jerusalem and from Judah every support and stay—both the whole supply of bread and the whole supply of water—
the mighty man and the warrior, the judge and the prophet, the diviner and the elder,
the captain of fifty and the man of rank, the counselor, the skilled artisan, and the expert in incantations.
I will appoint mere youths as their princes, and children will rule over them.
The people will oppress one another—man against man, neighbor against neighbor; the young will be insolent toward the elderly, and the contemptible toward the honorable.
A man will seize his brother in his father's house and say, "You have a cloak; you be our leader, and take charge of this heap of ruins."
On that day he will cry out, "I am no healer. I have neither bread nor clothing in my house. Do not make me leader of the people."
For Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen, because their tongues and their deeds are against the LORD, defying His glorious presence.
The expression of their faces witnesses against them; they parade their sin like Sodom and do not conceal it. Woe to their souls, for they have brought disaster upon themselves.
Tell the righteous that it will be well with them, for they will eat the fruit of their deeds.
Woe to the wicked—it will go ill with them, for what their hands have wrought will be done to them.
My people are oppressed by children, and women rule over them. O My people, your guides mislead you, and they have swallowed up the course of your paths.
The LORD stands to contend; He stands to judge the peoples.
The LORD will enter into judgment with the elders and princes of His people: "It is you who have devoured the vineyard; the plunder of the poor is in your houses.
What do you mean by crushing My people and grinding the faces of the poor?" declares the Lord, the LORD of Hosts.
Moreover, the LORD says: "Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, walking with outstretched necks, flirting with their eyes, tripping along with mincing steps, with ankle chains jingling—
the Lord will bring sores on the heads of the daughters of Zion, and the LORD will make their foreheads bare."
In that day the Lord will take away their finery: the ankle chains, headbands, and crescents;
the headdresses, ankle chains, and sashes; the perfume boxes and amulets;
the signet rings and nose rings;
the festive robes, capes, cloaks, and purses;
the mirrors, linen garments, turbans, and shawls.
Instead of fragrance there will be stench; instead of a belt, a rope; instead of well-set hair, baldness; instead of fine clothing, sackcloth; and instead of beauty, a brand.
Your men will fall by the sword, and your warriors in battle.
Her gates will lament and mourn; stripped of all, she will sit on the ground.
In that day seven women will cling to one man and say, “We will provide our own bread and clothing; only let your name be called upon us. Take away our disgrace.”
In that day the Branch of the LORD will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the pride and glory of the remnant of Israel.
And it will come to pass that whoever remains in Zion and survives in Jerusalem will be called holy—everyone who is recorded among the living in Jerusalem.
When the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and cleansed the bloodstains from the midst of Jerusalem by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.
Then the LORD will create over all of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud and smoke by day, and the brightness of a flaming fire by night; for over all the glory there will be a canopy.
It will be a shelter for shade from the heat by day, and a refuge and hiding place from the storm and rain.
Let me sing for my beloved a song of my beloved concerning His vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a very fertile hill.

He dug it and cleared it of stones, and planted it with choice vines; He built a watchtower in its midst, and hewed out a wine vat in it. He expected it to yield grapes, but it yielded only worthless, sour fruit.
And now, O inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah, judge between Me and My vineyard.
What more could have been done for My vineyard that I did not do in it? When I expected grapes, why did it yield worthless fruit?
Now I will tell you what I am going to do to My vineyard: I will remove its hedge, and it shall be devoured; I will break down its wall, and it shall be trampled.
I will make it a wasteland; it shall not be pruned or hoed, and briers and thorns shall grow up. I will also command the clouds to withhold rain from it.
For the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are His pleasant planting. He expected justice, but found bloodshed; righteousness, but found an outcry!
Woe to those who accumulate house after house and field after field, until no space remains, so that you are left to dwell alone in the land!
The LORD of hosts has sworn in my hearing: "Surely many houses shall become desolate, great and beautiful houses, without inhabitant.
For ten acres of vineyard will yield only a bath of wine, and a homer of seed will yield only an ephah of grain."
Woe to those who rise early in the morning to pursue strong drink, who linger late into the evening until wine inflames them!
They have lyre and harp, tambourine and flute and wine at their feasts, but they do not regard the work of the LORD, nor do they see the deeds of His hands.
Therefore My people go into exile for lack of knowledge; their honored men go hungry, and their multitude is parched with thirst.
Therefore Sheol has enlarged its appetite and opened its mouth without limit; down go her splendor, her masses, her revelry, and those who rejoice in her.
So man is humbled, and each one is brought low, and the eyes of the haughty are brought low.
But the LORD of hosts is exalted in justice, and the Holy God shows Himself holy in righteousness.
Then lambs shall graze as in their pasture, and nomads shall eat among the ruins of the rich.
Woe to those who drag iniquity along with ropes of deceit and haul sin as with cart ropes,
who say, "Let Him act quickly, let Him hasten His work, that we may see it; let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, that we may know it!"
Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who put darkness for light and light for darkness, who put bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter!
Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and shrewd in their own sight!
Woe to those who are champions at drinking wine and valiant men at mixing strong drink,
who acquit the guilty for a bribe and deprive the innocent of their right!

Therefore, as the tongue of fire devours stubble and as dry grass is consumed by the flame, so their root shall be as rottenness and their blossom shall go up like dust; for they have rejected the law of the LORD of hosts and have despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

Therefore the anger of the LORD was kindled against His people, and He stretched out His hand against them and struck them; the mountains quaked, and their corpses were as refuse in the midst of the streets. For all this His anger has not turned away, and His hand is still stretched out.
He will raise a signal for nations far away and whistle to summon them from the ends of the earth; and suddenly they come, swift and speedy!
None among them is weary, none stumbles; no one slumbers or sleeps; no waistband is loose, nor is a sandal strap broken.
Their arrows are sharp, all their bows are bent; their horses' hoofs are reckoned like flint, and their wheels like the whirlwind.
Their roaring is like a lion's; like young lions they roar; they growl and seize prey; they carry it off, and there is none to deliver.
In that day they will roar over it like the roaring of the sea. If one looks to the land, there is darkness and distress; and the light is darkened by its clouds.
In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted, and the train of His robe filled the temple.
Above Him stood seraphim, each with six wings: with two they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew.
And one called to another, saying, "Holy, holy, holy is the the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory."
The foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of him who called, and the house was filled with smoke.
Then I said, "Woe to me, for I am ruined! For I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell among a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the the LORD of hosts."
Then one of the seraphim flew to me, having in his hand a burning coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.
He touched it to my mouth and said, "Look, this has touched your lips; your iniquity is taken away, and your sin is atoned for."
I heard the voice of the Lord saying, "Whom shall I send, and who will go for Us?" And I said, "Here am I. Send me."
He said, "Go and say to this people: 'Keep on hearing, but do not understand; keep on seeing, but do not perceive.
Make the heart of this people calloused, make their ears dull, and close their eyes, lest they see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn and be healed.'"
Then I said, "How long, O Lord?" He said, "Until cities lie waste without inhabitant, houses without people, and the land is utterly desolate;
until the the LORD removes people far away, and forsaken places are many in the midst of the land.
And though a tenth remain in it, it will be burned again, like a terebinth or an oak whose stump remains when it is felled. The holy seed is its stump."

In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to wage war against it, but they could not overpower it.
When the house of David was told, "Aram has allied itself with Ephraim," the hearts of Ahaz and his people trembled as the trees of the forest shake before the wind.
Then the LORD said to Isaiah, "Go out, you and your son Shear-jashub, to meet Ahaz at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway to the Fuller's Field,

and say to him, 'Be careful, keep calm, and do not be afraid. Do not let your heart grow faint because of these two smoldering firebrands, because of the fierce anger of Rezin and Aram and the son of Remaliah.'"
"Because Aram, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah have plotted evil against you,
they say, 'Let us invade Judah and terrify it, and let us break it open and install the son of Tabeel as king in its midst.'"
"But the Lord the LORD says, 'It will not stand, and it will not come to pass.
For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered so that it is no longer a people.
The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not stand firm in faith, you will not stand at all.'"
Then the LORD spoke again to Ahaz:
"Ask a sign for yourself from the LORD your God; ask it either in the depths below or in the heights above."
But Ahaz said, "I will not ask; I will not put the LORD to the test."
Then Isaiah said, "Hear then, O house of David! Is it too small a thing for you to weary people, that you should also weary my God?
Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign: Behold, the virgin will conceive and bear a son, and she will call His name Immanuel.
He will eat curds and honey when He knows to refuse the evil and choose the good.
For before the boy knows to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land of the two kings you dread will be laid waste.
The LORD will bring upon you and your people and your father's house days such as have not come since the day Ephraim turned away from Judah—the king of Assyria."
In that day the LORD will whistle for the fly that is at the far reaches of the rivers of Egypt and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.
They will all come and settle in the steep ravines and in the clefts of the rocks, in all the thornbushes and in all the pastures.
In that day the Lord will use a razor hired from beyond the Euphrates—the king of Assyria—to shave the head and the hair of the legs and to remove the beard.
In that day a man will raise a young cow and two sheep.
And because of the abundance of milk they give, he will eat curds; for everyone left in the land will eat curds and honey.
In that day every place where there were a thousand vines worth a thousand shekels of silver will become briers and thorns.
Men will go there with bows and arrows, because the whole land will be briers and thorns.
As for all the hills that were hoed with a hoe, you will not go there for fear of briers and thorns; they will become places where oxen graze and sheep trample.
Then the the LORD said to me, "Take a large tablet and write on it with an ordinary stylus: 'Maher-shalal-hash-baz.'"
I will take faithful witnesses to record it—Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah.
I approached the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. Then the the LORD said to me, "Name him Maher-shalal-hash-baz."
Before the boy knows how to say "My father" or "My mother," the wealth of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria will be carried off by the king of Assyria.
The the LORD spoke to me again:
"Because this people has rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah and puts its confidence in Rezin and the son of Remaliah,
therefore, behold, the Lord is bringing against them the floodwaters of the River—mighty and many—the king of Assyria and all his glory. It will overflow all its channels and run over all its banks.
It will sweep through Judah, overflow, and pass through; it will reach up to the neck. The spreading of his wings will fill the breadth of your land, O Immanuel."
Band together, you peoples, and be shattered; listen, all you distant lands; arm yourselves, and be shattered; arm yourselves, and be shattered.
Devise a plan, but it will be thwarted; speak a word, but it will not stand, for God is with us.
For this is what the the LORD said to me with His strong hand upon me, warning me not to follow the way of this people:
"Do not call conspiracy everything this people calls conspiracy. Do not fear what they fear, and do not dread what they dread.
The the LORD of Hosts is the One you are to regard as holy; He is the One you are to fear; He is the One you are to dread."
He will be a sanctuary, but a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense to both houses of Israel, a trap and a snare to the people of Jerusalem.
Many will stumble over them; they will fall and be broken; they will be snared and captured.
Preserve the testimony and seal the instruction among my disciples.
I will wait for the the LORD, who is hiding His face from the house of Jacob, and I will put my hope in Him.
Here I am, with the children the the LORD has given me. We are signs and wonders in Israel from the the LORD of Hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.
When people tell you to consult the spirits of the dead and the spiritists who whisper and mutter, shouldn't a people consult their God? Why consult the dead on behalf of the living?
Turn to the instruction and the testimony! If they do not speak according to this word, they have no light of dawn.
They will roam through the land, dejected and hungry. When they are famished, they will become enraged; and looking upward, they will curse their king and their God.
Then they will look to the earth and see only distress and darkness and fearful gloom, and they will be driven into utter darkness.

Nevertheless, those who were in anguish will no longer know gloom: in former times He humbled the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but in the latter time He will bring honor to the road by the sea, beyond the Jordan, to Galilee of the nations.
The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; upon those dwelling in the land overshadowed by death, a light has dawned.
You have expanded the nation and heightened its joy; they rejoice before You as people rejoice at the harvest, and as men exult when dividing the plunder.
For as in the day of Midian’s defeat, You have shattered the yoke that burdened them, the bar laid across their shoulders, and the rod of their oppressor.
Every trampling boot of battle and every garment stained with blood will be fuel for the flames.
For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given, and the government will rest upon His shoulders; and His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

Of the increase of His government and of peace there will be no end. He will reign upon David’s throne and over His kingdom, to establish it and to uphold it with justice and righteousness from that time forth and forevermore. The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this.
The Lord has sent a message against Jacob, and it has fallen upon Israel.
All the people will know it—Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria—who speak with pride and arrogance of heart, saying:
“The bricks have fallen, but we will rebuild with dressed stones; the sycamores have been cut down, but we will replace them with cedars.”
Therefore the LORD has raised up Rezin’s foes against him and stirred up his enemies.
Arameans from the east and Philistines from the west have devoured Israel ravenously. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away, and His hand is still upraised.
Yet the people have not returned to Him who struck them, nor have they sought the LORD of Hosts.
So the LORD will cut off from Israel both head and tail, palm branch and reed, in a single day.
The elder and honorable man is the head, and the prophet who teaches lies is the tail.
For those who guide this people mislead them, and those who are guided are swallowed up.

Therefore the Lord does not rejoice in their young men, and He shows no compassion to their fatherless and widows; for every one of them is godless and wicked, and every mouth speaks folly. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away, and His hand is still upraised.
For wickedness burns like a fire that consumes thorns and briers; it sets the thickets of the forest ablaze, so that it rolls upward in a column of smoke.
By the wrath of the LORD of Hosts the land is scorched, and the people become fuel for the fire; no one spares his brother.
They carve meat on the right but remain hungry; they eat on the left but are not satisfied. Each preys upon his own kin.
Manasseh devours Ephraim, and Ephraim devours Manasseh; together they turn against Judah. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away, and His hand is still upraised.
Woe to those who decree injustice, who draft oppressive statutes and commit them to writing.
They turn aside the needy from justice and rob the poor of My people of their rights, so that widows become their spoil and they plunder the fatherless.
What will you do on the day of reckoning, when destruction comes from afar? To whom will you flee for help, and where will you leave your glory?
Nothing will remain but to crouch among the captives or fall among the slain. In all this, His anger is not turned away, and His hand is still stretched out.
Woe to Assyria, the rod of My anger; the staff in their hands is My wrath.
I will send him against a godless nation and dispatch him against a people under My wrath, to seize the spoil, to plunder the plunder, and to trample them down like mud in the streets.
Yet he does not intend this, and his heart does not think so; rather, it is in his heart to destroy and to cut off not a few nations.
For he says, "Are not my princes all kings?
Is not Calno like Carchemish? Is not Hamath like Arpad? Is not Samaria like Damascus?
As my hand has reached the kingdoms of the idols, whose carved images exceeded those of Jerusalem and Samaria,
shall I not do to Jerusalem and her idols as I have done to Samaria and her idols?"
When the Lord has finished all His work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, He will punish the king of Assyria for the arrogant pride of his heart and the haughty look in his eyes.

For he says, "By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom, for I am prudent. I have removed the boundaries of nations and plundered their treasures; like a mighty man I have brought down their inhabitants.
My hand has found, as a nest, the wealth of the peoples; and as one gathers forsaken eggs, I have gathered all the earth; and there was none that moved a wing, or opened the mouth, or chirped."

Shall the axe boast over him who hews with it, or shall the saw magnify itself against him who wields it? As if a rod should wield him who lifts it, or as if a staff should lift up him who is not wood!
Therefore the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, will send leanness among his stout ones, and beneath his glory a fire will be kindled like a blazing flame.
The Light of Israel will become a fire, and His Holy One a flame; it will burn and devour his thorns and his briers in one day.
The glory of his forest and his fruitful field He will consume, both soul and body; and it will be as when a sick man wastes away.
The remnant of the trees of his forest will be so few that a child could write them down.
In that day the remnant of Israel and the survivors of the house of Jacob will no longer rely on him who struck them, but will truly rely on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
A remnant will return, the remnant of Jacob, to the Mighty God.
Though your people, O Israel, be as the sand of the sea, a remnant of them will return. Destruction is decreed, overflowing with righteousness.
For the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, will carry out the destruction decreed upon the whole earth.

Therefore thus says the Lord, the LORD of Hosts: "O My people, who dwell in Zion, do not be afraid of the Assyrian. He will strike you with a rod and lift up his staff against you, as in the way of Egypt.
For in a very little while My fury will be spent, and My anger will be directed to their destruction.
The LORD of Hosts will stir up a scourge against him, as in the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb; and He will raise His staff over the sea, and lift it as in Egypt.
In that day his burden will depart from your shoulder, and his yoke from your neck; and the yoke will be broken because the neck has grown too fat for it."
He has come to Aiath; he has passed through Migron; at Michmash he stores his supplies.
They have gone over the pass; they have taken up their lodging at Geba. Ramah trembles; Gibeah of Saul has fled.
Lift up your voice, O daughter of Gallim! Give ear, O Laishah! O poor Anathoth!
Madmenah is in flight; the inhabitants of Gebim take to flight.
This very day he will halt at Nob; he will shake his fist at the mountain of the house of Zion, at the hill of Jerusalem.
Behold, the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, will lop off the boughs with terror; and the tall ones will be hewn down, and the lofty will be brought low.
He will cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon will fall by the Mighty One.
A shoot shall spring from the stump of Jesse, and a Branch from his roots shall bear fruit.
The Spirit of the LORD shall rest upon Him—a Spirit of wisdom and understanding, a Spirit of counsel and might, a Spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.
His delight shall be in the fear of the LORD; He shall not judge by the sight of His eyes, nor decide by the hearing of His ears.

Rather, with righteousness He shall judge the poor, and with equity He shall decide for the meek of the earth. He shall strike the earth with the rod of His mouth, and with the breath of His lips He shall slay the wicked.
Righteousness shall be the belt about His waist, and faithfulness the sash about His hips.
The wolf shall dwell with the lamb, the leopard shall lie down with the goat, the calf and the young lion and the fattened calf together, and a little child shall lead them.
The cow and the bear shall graze; their young shall lie down together; and the lion shall eat straw like the ox.
The nursing child shall play over the hole of the cobra, and the weaned child shall put his hand into the viper's den.
They shall not hurt nor destroy in all My holy mountain, for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the waters cover the sea.
In that day the Root of Jesse shall stand as a banner for the peoples; the nations shall seek Him, and His resting place shall be glorious.
On that day the Lord shall extend His hand a second time to recover the remnant of His people from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the coastlands of the sea.
He shall raise a banner for the nations and gather the outcasts of Israel; He shall assemble the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
The jealousy of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off. Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not harass Ephraim.
They shall swoop down upon the Philistines in the west; together they shall plunder the people of the east. They shall lay their hands on Edom and Moab, and the Ammonites shall obey them.
The LORD shall dry up the gulf of the Sea of Egypt; with a scorching wind He shall wave His hand over the Euphrates and strike it into seven streams, so that people may cross in sandals.
There shall be a highway for the remnant of His people who remain from Assyria, as there was for Israel when they came up from the land of Egypt.
In that day you will say, ‘The LORD, I will praise You, for though You were angry with me, Your anger has turned away, and You comfort me.’
Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust and not be afraid. For Yah, the LORD, is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation.
With joy you will draw water from the springs of salvation.
And in that day you will say, ‘Give thanks to the LORD; call on His name; make known His deeds among the peoples; proclaim that His name is exalted.’
Sing to the LORD, for He has done glorious things; let this be known throughout the earth.
Shout aloud and sing for joy, O inhabitant of Zion, for great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel.
This is the oracle concerning Babylon that Isaiah son of Amoz saw.
Raise a banner on a bare hilltop; call out to them. Wave a hand, that they may enter the gates of the nobles.
I have commanded My consecrated ones; I have also summoned My mighty men to execute My wrath—those who exult in My majesty.
A sound of uproar on the mountains, like a great multitude; a sound of tumult among kingdoms, of nations gathered together. The LORD of Hosts is mustering the army for battle.
They come from a distant land, from the ends of the heavens—the LORD and the weapons of His wrath—to destroy the whole earth.
Wail, for the day of the LORD is near; it will come as ruin sent by the Almighty.
Therefore all hands will grow feeble, and every human heart will melt.
They will be seized with terror; pangs and sorrows will grip them. They will writhe like a woman in labor. They will stare at one another in astonishment, and their faces will burn like flames.
Behold, the day of the LORD is coming—cruel, with fury and fierce anger—to make the earth a desolation and to destroy its sinners from it.
For the stars of heaven and their constellations will not give their light; the sun will be darkened at its rising, and the moon will not shed its light.
I will punish the world for its evil and the wicked for their iniquity. I will put an end to the arrogance of the proud and humble the haughtiness of tyrants.
I will make mortal man scarcer than pure gold and mankind rarer than the gold of Ophir.
Therefore I will shake the heavens, and the earth will be shaken from its place, at the wrath of the LORD of Hosts and in the day of His fierce anger.
Like a hunted gazelle, or like sheep with no one to gather them, each will turn to his own people, and each will flee to his own land.
Whoever is found will be pierced through, and whoever is captured will fall by the sword.
Their infants will be dashed to pieces before their eyes; their houses will be plundered, and their wives will be violated.
Behold, I am stirring up the Medes against them, who have no regard for silver and no delight in gold.
Their bows will dash the young men to pieces; they will have no mercy on the fruit of the womb, and their eyes will not pity children.
And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty and pride of the Chaldeans, will be like Sodom and Gomorrah when God overthrew them.
It will never be inhabited or lived in from generation to generation; no Arab will pitch his tent there, and no shepherds will make their flocks lie down there.
But desert creatures will lie there, and their houses will be full of howling creatures; ostriches will dwell there, and wild goats will leap there.
Hyenas will howl in their citadels, and jackals in their luxurious palaces. Her time is near, and her days will not be prolonged.
For The LORD will again have compassion on Jacob; He will once more choose Israel and settle them in their own land. Foreigners will join them and attach themselves to the house of Jacob.

Nations will escort them and bring them to their homeland, and the house of Israel will take possession of them in the LORD’s land as male and female servants. They will make captives of their captors and rule over their oppressors.
In that day the LORD will give you rest from your anguish and from your agitation, from the harsh labor in which you were enslaved.
You will take up this taunt against the king of Babylon and say, “How the oppressor has ceased! How his fury has ended!
The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of rulers,
who struck the peoples in wrath with blows that never ceased, who subdued the nations in anger with persecution that knew no restraint.
The whole earth is at rest and quiet; it breaks forth into song. “
Even the cypresses and the cedars of Lebanon rejoice over you: ‘Since you have been laid low, no woodcutter comes up against us.’ “
Sheol beneath is stirred up to meet you when you come; it rouses the shades for you, all the leaders of the earth; it raises the kings of the nations from their thrones. “
All of them will answer and say to you: ‘You too have become as weak as we are; you have become like us.’ “
Your pomp is brought down to Sheol, the sound of your harps; maggots are spread beneath you, and worms are your covering. “
How you have fallen from heaven, O Day Star, son of the dawn! How you have been cut down to the earth, you who laid low the nations!
You said in your heart, ‘I will ascend to heaven; above the stars of God I will raise my throne; I will sit on the mount of assembly in the far reaches of the north.
I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will make myself like the Most High.’
But you are brought down to Sheol, to the depths of the pit. “
Those who see you will stare at you and ponder over you: ‘Is this the man who made the earth tremble, who shook kingdoms,
who made the world like a wilderness and destroyed its cities, who did not release his prisoners to their homes?’ “
All the kings of the nations lie in honor, each in his own tomb,
but you are cast out, away from your grave, like a despised branch, clothed with the slain, those pierced by the sword, who go down to the stones of the pit, like a corpse trampled underfoot.
You will not be joined with them in burial, because you have destroyed your land and slain your people. May the offspring of evildoers never be named!
Prepare a slaughter for his sons for the guilt of their fathers, lest they rise and possess the earth and fill the face of the world with cities.”
“I will rise up against them,” declares the LORD of Hosts, “and I will cut off from Babylon name and remnant, offspring and posterity,” declares the LORD.
“And I will make it a possession of hedgehogs and marshes, and I will sweep it with the broom of destruction,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
The LORD of Hosts has sworn: ‘Surely, as I have planned, so it shall be, and as I have purposed, so it shall stand,’
to break the Assyrian in My land, and on My mountains to trample him underfoot. Then his yoke will depart from them, and his burden will be lifted from their shoulders.
This is the purpose that has been purposed concerning the whole earth, and this is the hand that is stretched out over all the nations.
For the LORD of Hosts has purposed, and who will annul it? His hand is stretched out, and who will turn it back?
In the year that King Ahaz died came this oracle:
Do not rejoice, all you Philistines, that the rod that struck you is broken; for from the serpent’s root will come forth a viper, and its fruit will be a flying, fiery serpent.
The firstborn of the poor will graze, and the needy will lie down in safety; but I will kill your root with famine, and it will slay your remnant.
Wail, O gate! Cry out, O city! Melt away, all you Philistines! For smoke comes out of the north, and there is no straggler in its ranks.
What will one answer the messengers of the nation? ‘The LORD has founded Zion, and in her the afflicted of His people will find refuge.’
An oracle concerning Moab: Ar is laid waste and silenced in a single night; Kir is laid waste and silenced in a single night.
Dibon ascends to its high places to weep; over Nebo and Medeba Moab wails. Every head is shaved, and every beard is cut off.
In its streets they wear sackcloth; on its rooftops and in its squares everyone wails, collapsing in tears.
Heshbon and Elealeh cry out; their voices are heard as far as Jahaz. Therefore Moab's warriors cry aloud, and their souls tremble within them.
My heart cries out for Moab; her fugitives flee to Zoar, to Eglath-shelishiyah. They ascend the slope of Luhith weeping, and on the road to Horonaim they raise a cry of destruction.
The waters of Nimrim run dry; the grass withers, the tender growth dies, and no greenery remains.
Therefore they carry away the abundance they have gained and their stored-up treasures across the Brook of the Willows.
