For the cry has encircled the borders of Moab; her wailing reaches Eglaim, and her wailing reaches Beer-elim.
The waters of Dimon are full of blood; yet I will bring still more upon Dimon—a lion against the fugitives of Moab and against the remnant of the land.
Send the lamb to the ruler of the land, from Sela, by way of the desert, to the mount of Daughter Zion.
Like fluttering birds driven from the nest, so the daughters of Moab are at the fords of the Arnon.
Give counsel, render justice; make your shadow like night at noonday; hide the outcasts; do not betray the wanderer.
Let My outcasts dwell with you; be a refuge for Moab from the destroyer. For the oppressor is at an end, destruction has ceased, and the oppressors have vanished from the land.
A throne will be established in steadfast love, and in the tent of David one will sit on it in faithfulness—a judge who seeks justice and is swift to do righteousness.
We have heard of the pride of Moab—how proud he is!—of his arrogance, his pride, and his wrath; but his boasting is false.
Therefore Moab will wail for Moab; all of Moab will moan. You will mourn for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, utterly stricken.

For the fields of Heshbon languish, and the vine of Sibmah; the rulers of the nations have trampled its choicest vines, which reached as far as Jazer and strayed toward the desert. Its shoots spread abroad and passed over the sea.
Therefore I weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah; I drench you with my tears, O Heshbon and Elealeh, for the shouts of joy have fallen silent over your summer fruit and your harvest.
Joy and gladness are removed from the fruitful field; in the vineyards no one sings or shouts; no treader treads out wine in the presses; I have put an end to the shouting.
Therefore my heart laments for Moab like a harp, my inmost being for Kir-hareseth.
And when Moab presents himself, when he wearies himself on the high place, and when he comes to his sanctuary to pray, he will not prevail.
This is the word that the LORD has spoken concerning Moab in the past.

But now the LORD has spoken, saying, “Within three years, as a hired worker counts the years, Moab’s splendor and all her great multitude will be despised, and her remnant will be very small and feeble.”
An oracle concerning Damascus: Behold, Damascus will cease to be a city and will become a heap of ruins.
The cities of Aroer will be deserted; they will become pastures for flocks, which will lie down without anyone to frighten them.
The fortress will disappear from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus; the remnant of Aram will be like the glory of the Israelites, declares the LORD of Hosts.
In that day the glory of Jacob will fade, and the fat of his body will waste away.
It will be as when a reaper gathers standing grain and harvests the heads of grain with his arm; it will be like one gleaning heads of grain in the Valley of Rephaim.
Yet gleanings will remain, like an olive tree that has been beaten—two or three berries on the topmost branches, four or five on the fruitful boughs, declares the LORD, the God of Israel.
In that day men will look to their Maker and turn their eyes to the Holy One of Israel.
They will not look to the altars their hands made, nor regard the Asherah poles and incense altars their fingers fashioned.
In that day their fortified cities will be like abandoned thickets and high places forsaken because of the Israelites, and there will be desolation.
For you have forgotten the God of your salvation and failed to remember the Rock of your strength. Therefore you plant your pleasant vineyards and set out imported vines.
Though on the day you plant them, you make them grow, and in the morning you sow them, your seeds sprout, yet the harvest will be a heap of rubble in the day of disease and incurable pain.
Oh, the raging of many nations—they rage like the raging of the sea! Oh, the uproar of the peoples—they roar like the roar of mighty waters!
The nations roar like the roar of great waters, but He will rebuke them, and they will flee far away, chased like chaff on the hills before the wind, like tumbleweed before a gale.
In the evening, sudden terror! Before morning, they are gone! This is the portion of those who loot us, and the lot of those who plunder us.
Woe to the land of whirring wings, beyond the rivers of Cush!

It sends envoys by sea in papyrus boats across the waters. “Go, swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth, to a people feared near and far, a nation mighty and conquering, whose land the rivers divide.”
All you inhabitants of the world and dwellers on earth, when a standard is raised on the mountains, you see it; when a trumpet sounds, you hear it.
For thus says the the LORD to me: “I will be quiet and watch from My dwelling place, like shimmering heat in the sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.”
For before the harvest, when the blossom fades and the flower becomes a ripening grape, He will cut off the shoots with pruning knives and remove the spreading branches.

They will be left together for the mountain birds of prey and the beasts of the earth; the birds of prey will feed on them through the summer, and all the beasts of the earth will feed on them through the winter.

At that time a gift will be brought to the the LORD of Hosts from a people tall and smooth, from a people feared near and far, a nation mighty and conquering, whose land the rivers divide—to the place of the name of the the LORD of Hosts, Mount Zion.
An oracle concerning Egypt: Behold, the LORD rides upon a swift cloud and comes to Egypt; the idols of Egypt tremble before Him, and the heart of Egypt melts within it.
I will stir up Egypt against Egypt, and they will fight—each against his brother, each against his neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
The spirit of Egypt will be emptied within it, and I will confound its counsel; then they will inquire of the idols, the sorcerers, the mediums, and the necromancers.
I will deliver Egypt into the hand of a harsh master, and a fierce king will rule over them,” declares the Lord GOD of Hosts.
The waters of the sea will dry up, and the river will be drained and parched.
Its canals will become foul, and the streams of Egypt will diminish and dry up; reeds and rushes will wither.
The meadows by the Nile, on the bank of the river, and all that is sown along the Nile will dry up, be driven away, and be no more.
The fishermen will mourn, and all who cast hooks into the Nile will lament; those who spread nets upon the water will pine away.
The workers in flax will be ashamed, and the weavers of fine linen will be dismayed.
Her foundations will be crushed, and all who earn wages will be sick at heart.
The princes of Zoan are utterly foolish; Pharaoh’s wisest counselors give senseless advice. How can you say to Pharaoh, “I am a son of the wise, a son of ancient kings”?
Where, then, are your wise men? Let them tell you, and let them make known what the LORD of Hosts has purposed against Egypt.
The princes of Zoan have become fools, and the princes of Memphis are deluded; the cornerstones of her tribes have led Egypt astray.
The LORD has poured into her a spirit of confusion, so that they make Egypt stagger in everything it does, as a drunkard staggers in his vomit.
Egypt will be left with no one capable of acting—neither leader nor follower, neither the mighty nor the lowly.
In that day the Egyptians will be like women, trembling and terrified before the uplifted hand of the LORD of Hosts, which He shakes over them.
The land of Judah will become a source of dread to Egypt; whenever it is mentioned, they will fear because of the purpose that the LORD of Hosts has purposed against them.
In that day five cities in the land of Egypt will speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to the LORD of Hosts; one of them will be called the City of Destruction.
In that day there will be an altar to the LORD in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar to the LORD at its border.
It will be a sign and a witness to the LORD of Hosts in the land of Egypt. When they cry to the LORD because of oppressors, He will send them a Savior and Champion, and He will deliver them.

The LORD will make Himself known to the Egyptians, and the Egyptians will know the LORD in that day. They will worship with sacrifices and offerings, and they will make vows to the LORD and fulfill them.
The LORD will strike Egypt, striking and healing, and they will return to the LORD. He will listen to their pleas and heal them.
In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria, and Assyria will come into Egypt, and Egypt into Assyria, and the Egyptians will worship together with the Assyrians.
In that day Israel will be the third partner with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the earth,
whom the LORD of Hosts has blessed, saying, “Blessed be Egypt My people, and Assyria the work of My hands, and Israel My inheritance.”
In the year that Tartan came to Ashdod—when Sargon, king of Assyria, had sent him, and he waged war against Ashdod and captured it—
at that time the LORD spoke through Isaiah son of Amoz, saying, “Go, remove the sackcloth from your waist and take the sandals off your feet.” He did so, and he walked naked and barefoot.
Then the LORD said, “Just as My servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and portent against Egypt and Cush,
so the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Cush—young and old alike—naked and barefoot, with their buttocks bared, to Egypt’s shame.”
Then those who put their hope in Cush and boasted in Egypt will be dismayed and ashamed.
In that day the inhabitants of this coastland will say, “See what has become of our hope, to whom we fled for help, that we might be delivered from the king of Assyria! How then can we escape?”
An oracle concerning the wilderness of the sea: As whirlwinds sweep through the Negev, so it advances from the wilderness, from a land of terror.
A harsh vision has been declared to me: the traitor betrays, and the ravager ravages. Go up, Elam; besiege, Media; I have brought all her sighing to an end.
Therefore my loins are filled with anguish; pangs seize me like the pangs of a woman in labor. I am so bewildered that I cannot hear; I am so dismayed that I cannot see.
My heart reels; dread terrifies me. The twilight I longed for has been turned into trembling for me.
They prepare the banquet, they post the watch, they eat, they drink. Arise, princes; anoint the shield!
For thus the Lord said to me: "Go, set a watchman; let him report what he sees."
He sees chariots, pairs of horsemen, chariots of donkeys, and chariots of camels; and he listens with meticulous attention.
Then he cried like a lion: "O Lord, I stand on my watchtower continually by day, and at my post I am stationed every night."
And behold, here comes a chariot of men, with a pair of horsemen. And he answered and said, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon, and all the carved images of her gods he has shattered to the ground."
O my people, crushed on the threshing floor, I declare to you what I have heard from the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel.
An oracle concerning Dumah. A voice calls to me from Seir: "Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?"
The watchman says, "Morning comes, and also the night. If you will inquire, inquire; return again."
An oracle concerning Arabia. In the thickets of Arabia you will lodge, O caravans of Dedanites.
Bring water to the thirsty; meet the fugitive with bread, O inhabitants of the land of Tema.
For they have fled from the swords, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, and from the weight of battle.
For thus the Lord said to me: "Within a year, according to the years of a hired worker, all the glory of Kedar will come to an end."
And the remainder of the number of archers, the mighty men of the sons of Kedar, will be few; for the LORD God of Israel has spoken.
An oracle concerning the Valley of Vision: What ails you now, that you have all gone up to the rooftops?
O city of commotion, O town of revelry! Your slain are not slain by the sword, nor killed in battle.
All your leaders have fled together, captured without a bow; all your fugitives were captured together, having fled far away.
Therefore I said, "Turn away from me; let me weep bitterly. Do not try to console me over the destruction of the daughter of my people."
For the Lord the LORD of Hosts has a day of tumult, trampling, and confusion in the Valley of Vision—tearing down walls and crying out to the mountain.
Elam takes up the quiver, with chariots and horsemen, and Kir uncovers the shield.
Your choicest valleys are full of chariots, and horsemen are posted at the gates.
He has uncovered the defense of Judah. In that day you looked to the weapons in the House of the Forest.
You saw that the breaches in the City of David were many, and you collected the water of the lower pool.
You counted the houses of Jerusalem and tore down houses to fortify the wall.
You made a reservoir between the walls for the water of the old pool, but you did not look to Him who made it, nor did you consider Him who planned it long ago.
On that day the Lord the LORD of Hosts called for weeping and wailing, for shaving the head and wearing sackcloth.
But look, there is joy and gladness, slaughtering cattle and killing sheep, eating meat and drinking wine: "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!"
The LORD of Hosts has revealed in my ears: "Surely this iniquity will not be forgiven you until you die," says the Lord the LORD of Hosts.

This is what the Lord the LORD of Hosts says: "Go, say to this steward, to Shebna, who is in charge of the palace: 'What are you doing here, and who gave you permission to cut out a tomb for yourself here—cutting your tomb on the height and chiseling a resting place for yourself in the rock? Look, the the LORD is about to hurl you away, O man. He will seize you firmly and roll you up tightly like a ball and throw you into a large country. There you will die, and there your glorious chariots will be—the shame of your master's house. I will depose you from your office, and you will be ousted from your position.'"
"In that day I will summon My servant, Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
I will clothe him with your robe and fasten your sash around him. I will hand your authority over to him, and he will be a father to the residents of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.
I will place on his shoulder the key to the house of David. What he opens no one will shut, and what he shuts no one will open.
I will drive him like a peg into a firm place, and he will become a throne of honor for his father's house.
All the glory of his father's house will hang on him: the offspring and the offshoots—all the small vessels, from bowls to every kind of jar."
"In that day," declares the the LORD of Hosts, "the peg driven into a firm place will give way; it will be cut down and fall, and the load hanging on it will be cut off." For the the LORD has spoken.
An oracle concerning Tyre: Wail, you ships of Tarshish, for Tyre has been destroyed; there is no house left and no harbor, and from the land of Cyprus the news has been revealed to them.
Be still, you inhabitants of the coastland, you merchants of Sidon, whose traders have crossed the sea.
On the great waters came the grain of Shihor; the harvest of the Nile was her revenue, and she became the marketplace of the nations.
Be ashamed, Sidon, fortress of the sea, for the sea has declared, “I have not labored, nor given birth; I have not raised young men, nor brought up virgins.”
When the report reaches Egypt, they will writhe in anguish at the report of Tyre.
Cross over to Tarshish; wail, you inhabitants of the coastland.
Is this your jubilant city, whose origin reaches back to ancient days, whose feet carried it to settle in a distant land?
Who has planned this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, whose merchants are princes and whose traders are the renowned of the earth?
The LORD of Hosts has planned it, to profane all pride of beauty and to humble all the honored of the earth.
Cross your land like the Nile, daughter of Tarshish, for there is no harbor left.
He stretched out His hand over the sea and shook the kingdoms; the the LORD has commanded concerning Canaan to destroy its strongholds.
And He said, “You shall exult no more, O oppressed virgin daughter of Sidon. Arise, cross over to Cyprus; even there you will find no rest.”

Behold, the land of the Chaldeans—this is the people that was not; Assyria appointed it for the beasts of the desert. They raised up its siege towers, they overthrew its palaces, and they made it a ruin.
Wail, ships of Tarshish, for your stronghold is destroyed.
In that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, like the days of one king. At the end of seventy years it will be with Tyre as in the song of the prostitute:
“Take a harp, go about the city, O forgotten prostitute; make sweet melody, sing many songs, that you may be remembered.”
At the end of seventy years the the LORD will visit Tyre, and she will return to her hire, and she will prostitute herself with all the kingdoms of the world on the face of the earth.

Her merchandise and her hire will be holy to the the LORD. It will not be stored or hoarded, but her merchandise will be for those who dwell before the the LORD, for sufficient food and for durable clothing.
Behold, the LORD is about to lay waste the earth and devastate it; He will distort its surface and scatter its inhabitants.

It will be as with the people, so with the priest; as with the slave, so with his master; as with the maidservant, so with her mistress; as with the buyer, so with the seller; as with the lender, so with the borrower; as with the creditor, so with the debtor.
The earth will be utterly emptied and utterly plundered, for the LORD has spoken this word.
The earth mourns and withers; the world languishes and fades; the exalted of the earth languish.
The earth is defiled under its inhabitants, for they have transgressed the laws, violated the statutes, and broken the everlasting covenant.
Therefore a curse devours the earth, and its inhabitants bear their guilt; therefore the inhabitants of the earth are scorched, and few people are left.
The new wine mourns, the vine languishes, and all the merry-hearted sigh.
The mirth of the tambourines ceases, the uproar of the revelers ends, and the mirth of the lyre is stilled.
They no longer drink wine with singing; strong drink is bitter to those who drink it.
The ruined city is broken down; every house is shut up so that no one may enter.
There is an outcry in the streets over the wine; all joy grows dark; the gladness of the earth is banished.
Desolation remains in the city, and the gate is struck down in ruin.
For thus it will be in the midst of the earth among the peoples, as at the gleaning of an olive tree, as at the gleanings when the grape harvest is done.
They lift up their voices and sing for joy; over the majesty of the LORD they shout from the west.
Therefore in the east give glory to the LORD; in the coastlands of the sea, give glory to the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
From the ends of the earth we hear songs of praise to the Righteous One. But I said, "I am wasting away! I am wasting away! Woe is me! The treacherous betray; the treacherous betray utterly."
Terror and the pit and the snare are upon you, O inhabitant of the earth!

He who flees at the sound of terror will fall into the pit, and he who climbs out of the pit will be caught in the snare. For the windows of heaven are opened, and the foundations of the earth tremble.
The earth is utterly broken, the earth is split apart, and the earth is violently shaken.
The earth reels like a drunkard and sways like a hut; its transgression lies heavy upon it, and it falls, never to rise again.
On that day the LORD will punish the host of heaven in heaven, and the kings of the earth on the earth.
They will be gathered together as prisoners in a pit; they will be shut up in a prison, and after many days they will be punished.
Then the moon will be confounded, and the sun ashamed, for the LORD of hosts reigns on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and His glory is before His elders.
You, the LORD, are my God. I will exalt You; I will praise Your name, for You have done wonders—plans formed long ago in perfect faithfulness.
For You have made the city a heap, the fortified city a ruin; the palace of foreigners is a city no more, and it will never be rebuilt.
Therefore a strong people glorify You, and cities of ruthless nations fear You.
For You have been a refuge to the poor, a refuge to the needy in his distress, a shelter from the storm and a shade from the heat; for the breath of the ruthless is like a storm against a wall.
Like heat in a parched land, You subdue the uproar of foreigners; like heat in the shade of a cloud, the song of the ruthless is silenced.
On this mountain the LORD of Hosts will prepare a feast of rich food for all peoples, a banquet of aged wine—rich food full of marrow, aged wine well refined.
On this mountain He will swallow up the shroud that enfolds all peoples, the veil that is spread over all nations.
He will swallow up death forever. The Lord GOD will wipe away tears from all faces, and the reproach of His people He will remove from all the earth, for the LORD has spoken.
In that day they will say, “Surely this is our God; we trusted in Him, and He saved us. This is the LORD; we trusted in Him. Let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation.”
For the hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain, but Moab will be trampled in his place as straw is trampled in the dung pile.
He will spread out his hands within it, as a swimmer spreads out his hands to swim; his pride will be brought low, along with the skill of his hands.
He has brought down your high walls and fortresses; He has brought them down to the ground, to the dust.
In that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: “We have a strong city; He establishes salvation as walls and ramparts.”
Open the gates, that the righteous nation may enter—the one that keeps faith.
You will keep in perfect peace the one whose mind is stayed on You, because he trusts in You.
Trust in the LORD forever, for in GOD the LORD is the Rock of Ages.
For He has brought down those who dwell on high; He lays the lofty city low. He brings it down to the ground; He casts it to the dust.
Feet will trample it—the feet of the oppressed, the steps of the poor.
The path of the righteous is level; O Upright One, You make smooth the way of the righteous.
Yes, in the way of Your judgments, O the LORD, we wait for You. Your name and renown are the desire of our souls.
My soul yearns for You in the night; indeed, my spirit within me seeks You early. For when Your judgments come upon the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
Though grace is shown to the wicked, he does not learn righteousness. In the land of uprightness he acts unjustly and does not see the majesty of the LORD.
O the LORD, Your hand is lifted high, but they do not see it. Let them see Your zeal for Your people and be put to shame. Let the fire reserved for Your enemies consume them.
O the LORD, You will ordain peace for us, for indeed, You have done all our works for us.
O the LORD our God, other lords besides You have ruled over us, but Your name alone do we honor.
The dead will not live; the departed spirits will not rise. Therefore You have punished and destroyed them; You have wiped out all memory of them.
You have enlarged the nation, O the LORD; You have enlarged the nation. You have gained glory for Yourself; You have extended all the borders of the land.
O the LORD, they sought You in their distress; when You disciplined them, they poured out a quiet prayer.
As a pregnant woman about to give birth writhes and cries out in her pain, so were we in Your presence, O the LORD.
We were with child; we writhed in pain; but we gave birth to wind. We have not brought salvation to the earth, nor have the inhabitants of the world been born.
Your dead will live; their bodies will rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust! For Your dew is like the dew of the morning, and the earth will bring forth her dead.
Go, my people, enter your rooms and shut your doors behind you. Hide yourselves a little while until the wrath has passed.
For behold, the LORD is coming out of His place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity. The earth will reveal her bloodshed and will no longer conceal her slain.
In that day the LORD will punish Leviathan the fleeing serpent with His hard, great, and strong sword; He will punish Leviathan the twisting serpent and slay the dragon that is in the sea.
In that day, “Sing of a delightful vineyard:
I, the LORD, am its keeper; I water it continually. I guard it night and day, lest anyone harm it.
I have no wrath. If only thorns and briers confronted Me, I would march against them in battle and burn them all together.
Or let him take hold of My stronghold and make peace with Me—yes, let him make peace with Me.”
In days to come Jacob will take root; Israel will blossom and put forth shoots, and the face of the world will be filled with fruit.
Has He struck them as He struck their attackers? Or have they been slain as their slayers were slain?
In exact measure, when you sent her away, you contended with her. He removed her with His fierce blast in the day of the east wind.

Therefore by this the guilt of Jacob will be atoned for, and this will be the full fruit of removing his sin: when he makes all the stones of the altar like crushed chalkstones, so that no Asherah poles or incense altars remain standing.
The fortified city stands desolate, an abandoned settlement forsaken like the wilderness; there the calf grazes, there it lies down and strips its branches bare.

When its boughs are dry, they are broken; women come and set them ablaze. For this is a people without understanding; therefore their Maker will not have compassion on them, and their Creator will not be gracious to them.
In that day the LORD will thresh from the Euphrates River to the Brook of Egypt, and you will be gathered one by one, O people of Israel.

In that day a great trumpet will be blown, and those who were lost in the land of Assyria and those who were driven out to the land of Egypt will come and worship the LORD on the holy mountain at Jerusalem.
Woe to the majestic crown of Ephraim’s drunkards, to the fading flower of his glorious splendor, to the city on the summit of the fertile valley, to those overcome by wine!
Behold, the Lord has a strong and mighty one. Like a hailstorm, like a destructive tempest, like a flooding downpour, He will hurl it to the ground with His hand.
The majestic crown of Ephraim’s drunkards will be trampled underfoot.

The fading flower of his glorious splendor, on the summit of the fertile valley, will be like a ripe fig before the harvest: the moment someone sees it, he devours it while it still rests in his hand.
On that day the LORD of Hosts will be a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty to the remnant of His people,
a spirit of justice to him who sits in judgment, a strength to those who turn back the battle at the gate.

These also stagger from wine and reel from strong drink: priest and prophet stagger from strong drink and are befuddled by wine. They reel from strong drink; they err in vision, they stumble in judgment.
For all their tables are covered with vomit; there is not a spot without filth.
Whom will He teach knowledge, and whom will He instruct in the message? Those just weaned from milk, those newly removed from the breast?
For they say, “Order on order, order on order, line on line, line on line, a little here, a little there.”
Indeed, with mocking lips and foreign tongue He will speak to this people,
to whom He has said, “This is the place of rest, let the weary rest; this is the place of repose.” But they would not listen.

So the word of the the LORD will come to them: “Order on order, order on order, line on line, line on line, a little here, a little there,” so that they may go and stumble backward, be broken, snared, and captured.
Therefore hear the word of the the LORD, you scoffers who rule this people in Jerusalem.

For you have said, “We have made a covenant with death, and an agreement with Sheol. When the overwhelming scourge passes through, it will not touch us, because we have made lies our refuge and falsehood our hiding place.”
Therefore this is what the Lord the the LORD says: “See, I lay a stone in Zion, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation. The one who believes will never be shaken.
I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the plumb line. Hail will sweep away the refuge of lies, and water will flood the hiding place.
Your covenant with death will be dissolved, and your agreement with Sheol will not stand. When the overwhelming scourge passes through, you will be trampled.
As often as it passes through, it will carry you away. Morning by morning it will pass through, by day and by night. Sheer terror will come from understanding the message.
Indeed, the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket too small to wrap around you.”
For the the LORD will rise up as He did at Mount Perazim; He will rouse Himself as in the Valley of Gibeon, to do His work, His strange work, and to perform His task, His unusual task.
So now, do not mock, or your bonds will become stronger. Indeed, I have heard from the Lord the the LORD of Hosts a decree of destruction against the whole land.
Listen and hear my voice; pay attention and hear my words.
Does the plowman plow all day to sow? Does he continually loosen and break up the soil?
When he has leveled its surface, does he not sow caraway and scatter cumin? Does he not plant wheat in rows and barley in plots, and rye along the border?
For his God instructs him and teaches him properly.
For caraway is not threshed with a sledge, nor is a cart wheel rolled over cumin. But caraway is beaten out with a stick, and cumin with a rod.
Grain is crushed, but not without limit; though he drives the wheels of his cart over it, his horses do not crush it.
This also comes from the the LORD of Hosts; He is wonderful in counsel and great in wisdom.
Woe to Ariel, Ariel, the city where David camped! Year after year, let the festivals run their course.
I will besiege Ariel, and she will mourn and lament; she will be to Me like an altar hearth.
I will encamp all around you, and besiege you with towers; I will raise siegeworks against you.
You will be brought low, and you will speak from the earth; your words will be muffled in the dust. Your voice will be like a ghost rising from the ground, and your speech will whisper from the dust.
But the multitude of your enemies will be like fine dust, and the horde of the ruthless like blowing chaff. Then suddenly, in an instant,
you will be judged by the LORD of Hosts with thunder and earthquake and a great roar, with whirlwind and storm and a consuming fire.
The multitude of all the nations that fight against Ariel—all who war against her and her stronghold and distress her—will be like a dream, a vision in the night.

It will be as when a hungry man dreams he is eating, but awakens to find his soul empty; or as when a thirsty man dreams he is drinking, but awakens faint, with his thirst unquenched. So will it be with all the nations that wage war against Mount Zion.
Be stunned and amazed; blind yourselves and remain sightless! They are drunk, but not on wine; they stagger, but not from strong drink.
For the LORD has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep; He has shut your eyes—the prophets—and veiled your heads—the seers.
So the entire vision is to you like the words of a sealed scroll. If it is handed to someone who can read, and he is asked to read it, he will say, "I cannot, because it is sealed."
Or if the scroll is handed to one who cannot read, and he is asked to read it, he will say, "I cannot read."

Therefore the Lord said: "Because this people draw near to Me with their mouths and honor Me with their lips, while their hearts are far from Me, and their reverence for Me is merely a commandment taught by men,
I will again confound this people with wonder upon wonder. The wisdom of the wise will vanish, and the discernment of the discerning will be hidden."
Woe to those who dig deep to hide their plans from the LORD! In darkness they do their work and say, "Who sees us? Who knows us?"

You have turned everything upside down. Shall the potter be regarded as clay? Shall what is made say of its maker, "He did not make me"? Or shall what is formed say of Him who formed it, "He has no understanding"?
In just a little while, will not Lebanon be turned into a fertile field, and the fertile field seem like a forest?
In that day the deaf will hear the words of the scroll, and out of darkness and gloom the eyes of the blind will see.
The humble will increase their joy in the LORD, and the poor among men will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
For the ruthless will vanish, the mockers will disappear, and all who look for evil will be cut down:
those who with a word make a person out to be a sinner, who ensnare the mediator at the gate, and who with false charges deprive the innocent of justice.
Therefore this is what the LORD, who redeemed Abraham, says to the house of Jacob: "No longer will Jacob be ashamed; no longer will his face grow pale.
For when he sees his children, the work of My hands, among him, they will honor My name; they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob and stand in awe of the God of Israel.
Those who stray in spirit will come to understanding, and those who complain will accept instruction."
Woe to the rebellious children, declares the the LORD, who take counsel, but not from Me, and who devise plans, but not by My Spirit, adding sin to sin.
They go down to Egypt without asking My counsel, to take refuge in Pharaoh’s strength and to trust in Egypt’s shadow.
Therefore Pharaoh’s strength will be your shame, and trust in Egypt’s shadow will be your humiliation.
For his princes are at Zoan, and his envoys reach Hanes;
yet they will all be put to shame by a people who cannot help them, who bring neither aid nor profit, but only shame and reproach.

An oracle concerning the beasts of the South: through a land of hardship and distress, of lioness and lion, of viper and flying serpent, they carry their riches on donkeys’ backs and their treasures on camels’ humps, to a people who cannot help.
Egypt’s help is futile and empty; therefore I have called her “Rahab the Do-Nothing.”
Now go, write it on a tablet before them, and inscribe it in a book, that it may stand for the time to come, forever and ever.
For this is a rebellious people, deceitful children, children who refuse to hear the instruction of the the LORD.
They say to the seers, “Do not see,” and to the prophets, “Do not prophesy to us what is right; speak to us pleasant things, prophesy illusions.
Turn aside from the path, get out of the way, and let us hear no more about the Holy One of Israel.”
Therefore thus says the Holy One of Israel: “Because you reject this word and trust in oppression and deceit, and rely on them,
this iniquity will be to you like a breach ready to fall, a bulge in a high wall, whose collapse comes suddenly, in an instant.
He will smash it like a potter’s jar, crushed so thoroughly that no fragment will be found among its pieces large enough to take fire from the hearth or draw water from the cistern.”
For thus says the Lord, the the LORD, the Holy One of Israel: “In returning and rest you will be saved; in quietness and trust will be your strength. But you were unwilling.”
Instead, you said, “No, we will flee on horses”—so you will flee—and, “We will ride on swift horses”—so swift will be those who pursue you.
A thousand will flee at the threat of one; at the threat of five you will flee, until you are left like a flagstaff on a mountaintop and like a banner on a hill.
Therefore the the LORD waits to be gracious to you; therefore He will rise up to show you mercy. For the the LORD is a God of justice; blessed are all who wait for Him.
O people of Zion, who dwell in Jerusalem, you will weep no more. He will be gracious to you at the sound of your cry; when He hears it, He will answer you.
Although the Lord gives you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, your Teacher will no longer hide Himself, but your eyes will see your Teacher.
Your ears will hear a word behind you, saying, “This is the way; walk in it,” whenever you turn to the right or to the left.
You will defile your silver-plated idols and your gold-plated images. You will throw them away like menstrual cloths and say, “Be gone!”
Then He will give rain for the seed you sow in the ground, and the bread that the ground yields will be rich and plentiful. In that day your livestock will graze in broad pastures.
The oxen and donkeys that work the soil will eat salted fodder winnowed with shovel and pitchfork.
On every high mountain and every lofty hill there will be streams and watercourses in the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall.

The light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times brighter, like the light of seven days, in the day the the LORD binds up the brokenness of His people and heals the wound He inflicted.
Behold, the name of the the LORD comes from afar, burning with His anger and heavy with smoke. His lips are full of fury, and His tongue is like a devouring fire.
His breath is like an overflowing stream that reaches to the neck, to sift the nations in a sieve of destruction and to put a misleading bridle in the jaws of the peoples.
You will have a song as in the night of a consecrated feast, and gladness of heart as when one goes with a flute to the mountain of the the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
The LORD will make the splendor of His voice heard and show the descent of His arm, with the indignation of His anger and the flame of a devouring fire, with a cloudburst, a tempest, and hailstones.
For at the voice of the the LORD Assyria will be shattered, as He strikes with the rod.
Every stroke of the appointed rod that the the LORD brings down on him will be to the sound of tambourines and harps, as He fights with His uplifted arm.
For Topheth has long been prepared; it is made ready for the king. Its pyre is deep and wide, with plenty of fire and wood. The breath of the the LORD, like a stream of brimstone, sets it ablaze.

Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, relying on horses, trusting in chariots because they are many, and in horsemen because they are very strong, yet who have not looked to the Holy One of Israel and have not sought the LORD.
Yet He too is wise and will bring disaster; He will not retract His words. He will rise against the house of evildoers and against the helpers of those who work iniquity.
Now the Egyptians are men, not God, and their horses are flesh, not spirit. When the LORD stretches out His hand, the helper will stumble, the helped will fall, and all will perish together.

For thus says the LORD to me: "As a lion growls, and a young lion over its prey—though a band of shepherds is called out against it, it is not terrified by their shouting, nor cowed by their clamor—so the LORD of Hosts will come down to fight on Mount Zion and on its hill."
Like birds hovering, so the LORD of Hosts will protect Jerusalem; He will protect and deliver it, pass over and rescue it.
Return to Him from whom they have deeply revolted, O children of Israel.
For on that day each man will reject his silver idols and his gold idols—things your hands have made for you to sin.
Assyria will fall by a sword not wielded by man; a sword not of human making will consume him. He will flee from the sword, and his young men will be pressed into forced labor.
"His rock will pass away in terror, and his princes will be dismayed at the battle standard," declares the LORD, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
Behold, a king will reign in righteousness, and princes will rule with justice.
Each will be like a shelter from the wind and a refuge from the storm, like streams of water in a dry land, and like the shade of a massive rock in a weary land.
Then the eyes of those who see will no longer be closed, and the ears of those who hear will listen attentively.
The mind of the rash will understand and know, and the stammering tongue will speak clearly and fluently.
No longer will the fool be called noble, nor the scoundrel be said to be honorable.
For the fool speaks folly, and his heart is devoted to iniquity—to practice ungodliness, to utter error concerning the LORD, to leave the hungry soul empty, and to deprive the thirsty of drink.
The scoundrel's devices are evil; he plans wicked schemes to ruin the poor with lying words, even when the needy's plea is just.
But the noble plans noble things, and by noble things he stands firm.
Rise up, you women who are at ease; hear my voice. You complacent daughters, give ear to my speech.
In little more than a year you will shudder, you complacent women, for the grape harvest will fail and the fruit harvest will not come.
Tremble, you women who are at ease; shudder, you complacent ones. Strip yourselves bare and tie sackcloth around your waists.
Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine,
for the soil of My people overgrown with thorns and briers—for every joyful house and the exultant city.
For the palace is forsaken, the populous city deserted; the hill and the watchtower have become caves forever, a delight for wild donkeys, a pasture for flocks;
until the Spirit is poured out on us from on high, and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field, and the fruitful field is counted as forest.
Then justice will dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness will abide in the fruitful field.
And the work of righteousness will be peace, and the service of righteousness will be quietness and confidence forever.
My people will dwell in a peaceful habitation, in secure dwellings, and in quiet resting places.
And it will hail when the forest falls, and the city will be utterly brought low.
Blessed are you who sow beside all waters, who let the feet of the ox and the donkey roam free.

Woe to you, destroyer, though you have not been destroyed; and woe to you, traitor, though no one has betrayed you! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed; when you cease betraying, they will betray you.
O the LORD, be gracious to us; we have waited for You. Be our strength each morning, and our salvation in the hour of distress.
At the roar of the nations, peoples fled; at your exaltation, they were scattered.
Your spoil will be gathered as the caterpillar gathers; like swarming locusts, they will swarm over it.
The LORD is exalted, for He dwells on high; He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
Steadfastness will mark your times, a wealth of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge; the fear of the the LORD is your treasure.
Behold, their warriors cry out in the streets; the messengers of peace weep bitterly.
The highways are deserted; wayfarers have ceased. The covenant is broken; cities are despised; humanity is no longer regarded.
The land mourns and languishes; Lebanon is ashamed and withers; Sharon is like a desert; Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.
“Now I will arise,” says the the LORD. “Now I will be exalted; now I will be lifted up.”
You conceive chaff, and you give birth to stubble; your breath is a fire that consumes you.
The peoples will be burned to lime; like thorns cut down, they will be set ablaze.
You who are far off, hear what I have done; you who are near, acknowledge My power.
The sinners in Zion are terrified; trembling grips the godless: “Who among us can dwell with consuming fire? Who among us can dwell with everlasting burning?”

He who walks in righteousness and speaks what is right, who despises gain from oppression, who shakes his hands free of bribes, who stops his ears from hearing of bloodshed and shuts his eyes against seeing evil—
he will dwell on the heights; his refuge will be the mountain fortress; his food will be provided, and his water assured.
Your eyes will see the King in His beauty; they will behold a land stretching afar.
Your heart will ponder the terror: “Where is the scribe? Where is the weigher? Where is the counter of towers?”
You will no longer see the insolent people, a people whose speech is too obscure to comprehend, whose stammering tongue cannot be understood.

Look upon Zion, the city of our appointed feasts! Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a tranquil habitation, a tent that will not be moved; its stakes will never be pulled up, nor will any of its cords be broken.
But there the Majestic One, the the LORD, will be for us a place of rivers and wide canals, where no galley with oars will go, and no majestic vessel will pass.
For the the LORD is our Judge, the the LORD is our Lawgiver, the the LORD is our King; He will save us.
Your rigging is slack; it cannot hold the mast firmly, nor can it spread the sail. Then an abundance of spoil will be divided; even the lame will carry off plunder.
And no resident will say, “I am sick.” The people who dwell there will be forgiven their iniquity.
Come near, you nations, to listen; pay attention, you peoples! Let the earth hear, along with all that fills it—the world and everything that springs from it.
The LORD is angry with all the nations and furious with all their armies. He will devote them to destruction; He will give them over to slaughter.
Their slain will be left unburied, and the stench of their corpses will rise; the mountains will be drenched with their blood.
All the host of heaven will rot away, and the skies will be rolled up like a scroll. All their stars will wither, like a leaf withering on the vine, like foliage on a fig tree.
When My sword has drunk its fill in the heavens, then it will come down on Edom, on the people I have devoted to destruction, for judgment.

The LORD’s sword is bathed in blood; it is covered with fat—the blood of lambs and goats, the fat of the kidneys of rams. For the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah, a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
And the wild oxen will fall with them, the young bulls with the mighty bulls. Their land will be drenched with blood, and their dust will be fattened with fat.
For the LORD has a day of vengeance, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.
Her streams will be turned to pitch, and her dust to sulfur; her land will become burning pitch.
It will not be quenched night or day; its smoke will rise forever. From generation to generation it will lie desolate; no one will pass through it forever and ever.
The pelican and the porcupine will possess it, and the owl and the raven will dwell in it. He will stretch over it the measuring line of chaos and the plumb line of destruction.
No nobles will be left to proclaim a kingdom, and all her princes will come to nothing.
Thorns will overrun her palaces, nettles and thistles her fortresses. She will become a haunt of jackals, an abode for ostriches.
The desert creatures will meet with the hyenas, and one wild goat will cry to another; there too the night creature will settle and find a resting place.
There the owl will make her nest, lay eggs, hatch them, and gather her young under her shadow. Yes, the kites will be gathered there, each with its mate.
Search the book of the LORD and read: not one of these will be missing; none will lack her mate. For His mouth has commanded, and His Spirit has gathered them.
He has allotted their portions, and His hand has divided it among them. They will possess it forever; from generation to generation they will dwell there.
The wilderness and the arid land will rejoice; the desert will exult and blossom like a crocus.
It will bloom profusely and rejoice with joyful song. The glory of Lebanon will be given to it, the splendor of Carmel and Sharon. They will see the glory of the LORD, the splendor of our God.
Strengthen the weak hands and steady the faltering knees.
Say to those whose hearts are anxious, “Be strong; do not fear! Look, your God will come with vengeance, with divine retribution; He will come and save you.”
Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped.
Then the lame will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will shout for joy. For waters will gush forth in the wilderness, and streams in the desert.
The burning sand will become a pool, and the parched ground, springs of water. In the haunt of jackals, where they rest, grass will become reeds and papyrus.
And a highway will be there; it will be called the Way of Holiness. The unclean will not travel on it, but it will be for those who walk that road—even fools will not go astray.
No lion will be there, nor will any ferocious beast come upon it; they will not be found there. But the redeemed will walk there.
And the ransomed of the LORD will return and enter Zion with singing, everlasting joy crowning their heads. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.
In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
Then the king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, with a heavy force. He stood by the conduit of the upper pool, on the road to the Fuller's Field.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came out to him.
Rabshakeh said to them, "Say now to Hezekiah, 'Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria: What is this confidence in which you trust?
You say you have counsel and strength for war, but those are empty words. On whom do you now trust, that you have rebelled against me?
Look, you are trusting in Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff, which pierces the hand of anyone who leans on it. That is what Pharaoh king of Egypt is to all who trust in him.
But if you say to me, "We trust in the LORD our God," is it not He whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, "You shall worship before this altar"?
Now make a wager with my master the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses if you can put riders on them.
How then could you turn back even the least of my master's officers, when you are relying on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
Have I come up against this land to destroy it apart from the LORD? The LORD said to me, "Go up against this land and destroy it."'"
Then Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. Do not speak to us in Hebrew within earshot of the people on the wall."

Rabshakeh replied, "Has my master sent me to speak these words to your master and to you, and not to the men sitting on the wall? They are doomed, along with you, to eat their own dung and drink their own urine."
Then Rabshakeh stood and called out in a loud voice in Hebrew, "Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
Thus says the king: 'Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he cannot deliver you.
Do not let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD by saying, "The LORD will surely deliver us; this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria."

Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of Assyria: "Make peace with me and come out to me. Then each of you will eat from his own vine and from his own fig tree, and each of you will drink the water of his own cistern,
until I come and take you to a land like your own—a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards."
Beware lest Hezekiah mislead you by saying, "The LORD will deliver us." Has any of the gods of the nations delivered his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Did they deliver Samaria from my hand?
Who among all the gods of these lands has delivered his land from my hand, that the LORD should deliver Jerusalem from my hand?'"
But they were silent and did not answer him a word, for the king's command was, "Do not answer him."
Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and told him the words of Rabshakeh.
When King Hezekiah heard the report, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and entered the house of the LORD.
He sent Eliakim, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the scribe, and the senior priests, all clothed in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
They told him, "This is what Hezekiah says: 'Today is a day of distress, rebuke, and disgrace. Children have come to the point of birth, but there is no strength to deliver them.'

Perhaps the the LORD your God has heard the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master, the king of Assyria, sent to defy the living God, and He will rebuke the words that the the LORD your God has heard. Therefore pray for the remnant that still survives."
So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
Isaiah said to them, "Tell your master: This is what the the LORD says: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed Me.
I am going to put a spirit in him so that he hears a rumor and returns to his own land; there I will make him fall by the sword."
When the Rabshakeh heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish, he returned and found him fighting against Libnah.

Now Sennacherib heard that Tirhakah, king of Cush, had marched out to fight against him, so he sent messengers to Hezekiah with this message: "Say to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying, 'Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.'
Surely you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands—how they devoted them to destruction. And will you be rescued?
Did the gods of the nations my fathers destroyed rescue them—Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena, or Ivvah?"
Hezekiah took the letter from the messengers' hands, read it, and went up to the house of the LORD. There he spread it out before the LORD.
And Hezekiah prayed to the LORD: "O the LORD of Hosts, God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made heaven and earth.
Incline Your ear, O the LORD, and hear; open Your eyes, O the LORD, and see. Hear all the words Sennacherib has sent to defy the living God.
It is true, O the LORD, that the kings of Assyria have laid waste all the lands and their territories.
They have thrown their gods into the fire, for they were not gods at all, but the work of human hands—wood and stone—so they destroyed them.
Now, O the LORD our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone are the LORD."
Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent word to Hezekiah: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Because you have prayed to Me about Sennacherib king of Assyria,
this is the word the LORD has spoken concerning him: The virgin daughter of Zion despises you and mocks you; the daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head behind you.
Whom have you reproached and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes to the heights? Against the Holy One of Israel.

By your servants you have reproached the Lord and said, 'With my many chariots I have ascended the heights of the mountains, the farthest reaches of Lebanon; I will cut down its tallest cedars and its finest cypresses; I will reach its farthest height, the forest of Carmel.
I have dug wells and drunk foreign water; with the soles of my feet I have dried up all the streams of Egypt.' "
Have you not heard? Long ago I ordained it; in ancient days I planned it. Now I have brought it to pass, that you should turn fortified cities into heaps of rubble.
Their inhabitants are weak; they are dismayed and put to shame. They are like grass in the field, like tender green shoots, like grass on the rooftops—blighted before it can grow.
But I know your sitting down, your going out and your coming in, and your raging against Me.
Because you rage against Me and your complacency has reached My ears, I will put My hook in your nose and My bit in your mouth, and I will turn you back by the way you came. "
This will be a sign for you: This year you will eat what grows by itself; in the second year, what springs from that; but in the third year you will sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
The surviving remnant of the house of Judah will take root below and bear fruit above.
For out of Jerusalem will come a remnant, and survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this. "
Therefore this is what the LORD says concerning the king of Assyria: He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow here; he will not advance against it with a shield or build a siege ramp against it.
He will return by the way he came; he will not enter this city, declares the LORD.
I will defend this city and save it for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David."
Then the angel of the LORD went out and struck down 185,000 men in the Assyrian camp. When the people arose early in the morning, there lay all the dead bodies.
So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and withdrew; he returned and stayed in Nineveh.

One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. His son Esarhaddon reigned in his place.

In those days Hezekiah fell gravely ill and stood at the brink of death. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, "This is what the LORD says: 'Set your affairs in order, for you are going to die; you will not recover.'"
Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall and prayed to the LORD.
He said, "Please, the LORD, remember how I have walked before You in truth and with a whole heart, and how I have done what is good in Your sight." Then Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah:
"Go and tell Hezekiah that this is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: 'I have heard your prayer and seen your tears; I will add fifteen years to your life.
I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city.
This will be the sign to you from the LORD that the LORD will do what He has promised:
I will make the shadow cast by the sun retreat ten steps on the stairway of Ahaz.'" So the shadow moved back ten steps.
This is the poem Hezekiah king of Judah wrote after his illness and recovery: "
I said, 'In the prime of my life I must go through the gates of Sheol; I am deprived of the rest of my years.'
I said, 'I will never again see the LORD—the LORD in the land of the living; I will no longer look upon humanity among the inhabitants of the world.'
Like a shepherd's tent, my dwelling is pulled up and carried away; like a weaver, I have rolled up my life. He cuts me off from the loom; from day to night You bring me to an end. "
I waited quietly until morning, but like a lion He breaks all my bones; from day to night You bring me to an end.
Like a crane or swallow I chirp; I moan like a dove. My eyes grow weak as I look to the heavens. O Lord, I am oppressed; be my security.
What can I say? He has spoken to me, and He Himself has done it. I will walk slowly all my years because of the anguish of my soul. "
O Lord, by such things men live, and in all of them my spirit finds life. You have restored me to health and let me live.
Surely it was for my own good that I had such anguish. In Your love You have delivered my soul from the pit of oblivion, for You have cast all my sins behind Your back.
For Sheol cannot praise You; Death cannot sing Your praise. Those who go down to the Pit cannot hope for Your faithfulness. "
The living, only the living, can praise You, as I do today; fathers will tell their children about Your faithfulness.
The LORD is willing to save me, so we will sing my songs with stringed instruments all the days of our lives in the house of the LORD."
Then Isaiah said, "Prepare a poultice of figs and apply it to the boil, and he will recover."
And Hezekiah had asked, "What will be the sign that I will go up to the house of the LORD?"
At that time Merodach-baladan, son of Baladan and king of Babylon, dispatched letters and a gift to Hezekiah, having heard that Hezekiah had been ill and had recovered.

Hezekiah welcomed the envoys with gladness and showed them everything in his treasure house—the silver, the gold, the spices, the precious oil, his entire armory, and all that was found in his storehouses. Nothing in his palace or throughout his dominion was withheld from them.
Then Isaiah the prophet went to King Hezekiah and asked, “Where did these men come from, and what did they say to you?” “They came to me from a distant land,” Hezekiah replied, “from Babylon.”
“What have they seen in your palace?” Isaiah asked. “They have seen everything in my palace,” Hezekiah answered. “There is nothing in my storehouses that I did not show them.”
Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the the LORD of Hosts:”

“Behold, the days are coming when all that is in your palace, together with everything your fathers have stored up to this day, will be carried away to Babylon. Nothing will remain,” says the the LORD.
“And some of your descendants—your own flesh and blood—will be taken away and made eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.”
Then Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The word of the the LORD that you have spoken is good.” For he thought, “There will be peace and security throughout my lifetime.”
“Comfort, comfort My people,” says your God.

Speak to the heart of Jerusalem and proclaim to her that her servitude is fulfilled, that her iniquity has been pardoned; for she has received from the LORD’s hand a double recompense for all her sins.
A voice cries out: “Prepare the way of the LORD in the wilderness; make straight in the desert a highway for our God.”
Every valley shall be raised, and every mountain and hill made low; the crooked ground shall become level, and the rugged places a plain.
And the glory of the LORD will be revealed, and all flesh together will behold it, for the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
A voice says, “Cry out!” And I asked, “What shall I cry?” “All flesh is grass, and all its splendor is like the flower of the field.
The grass withers and the flower fades when the breath of the LORD blows upon it; surely the people are grass.
The grass withers and the flower fades, but the word of our God endures forever.”

Go up on a high mountain, O Zion, herald of good tidings; lift up your voice with strength, O Jerusalem, herald of good tidings. Lift it up; do not be afraid. Say to the cities of Judah, “Here is your God!”
Behold, the Lord the LORD comes with might, and His arm rules for Him. Behold, His reward is with Him, and His recompense before Him.
Like a shepherd He will tend His flock; in His arm He will gather the lambs and carry them in His bosom; He will gently lead the nursing ewes.

Who has measured the waters in the hollow of His hand, or marked off the heavens with a span? Who has contained the dust of the earth in a third of a measure, or weighed the mountains on scales and the hills on a balance?
Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD, or informed Him as His counselor?
Whom did He consult to enlighten Him, and who taught Him the path of justice? Who taught Him knowledge, and showed Him the way of understanding?
Behold, the nations are like a drop in a bucket; they are regarded as dust on the scales. Behold, He lifts up the islands like fine dust.
Lebanon is not sufficient for fuel, nor its animals enough for a burnt offering.
All the nations are as nothing before Him; they are regarded by Him as nothingness and emptiness.
To whom, then, will you compare God? What likeness will you set up for Him?
An idol is cast by a craftsman and overlaid with gold by a goldsmith, while silver chains are forged for it.
One who is impoverished chooses wood that will not rot; he seeks out a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not topple.
Do you not know? Have you not heard? Has it not been declared to you from the beginning? Have you not understood from the foundations of the earth?
He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the heavens like a canopy and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in.
He brings princes to nothing and makes the rulers of the earth as emptiness.
Scarcely are they planted, scarcely are they sown, scarcely has their stem taken root in the earth, when He blows on them and they wither, and a whirlwind sweeps them away like chaff.
“To whom will you compare Me, that I should be His equal?” says the Holy One.
Lift up your eyes on high and see: Who created these? He who brings out their host by number, calling them all by name. Because of His great might and strong power, not one of them is missing.
Why do you say, O Jacob, and speak, O Israel, “My way is hidden from the LORD, and my claim is passed over by my God”?
Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He will not grow tired or weary; His understanding is unsearchable.
He gives power to the faint and increases the strength of the weak.
Even youths grow tired and weary, and young men stumble and fall.
But those who wait upon the LORD will renew their strength; they will soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not faint.
“Maintain your silence before Me, O coastlands, and let the peoples renew their strength; let them draw near and then speak, and let us draw near together for judgment.

Who has stirred up one from the east, calling him in righteousness to His service? He delivers nations into his hand and subjugates kings before him, reducing them to dust beneath his sword and to wind-driven chaff before his bow.
He pursues them and advances unscathed along a path his feet have never before trodden.
Who has accomplished this and brought it to pass, summoning the generations from the beginning? I, the LORD—the First and the Last—I am He.”
The coastlands behold and tremble, and the ends of the earth are seized with dread as they draw near and assemble.
Each one strengthens his neighbor and says to his brother, “Be strong!”

The craftsman encourages the goldsmith, and the one who smooths the metal with a hammer spurs on the striker of the anvil; he declares the soldering good and fastens it with nails so that it will not topple.
“But you, O Israel, My servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, descendant of Abraham My friend—
I brought you from the ends of the earth and summoned you from its remotest corners. I said, ‘You are My servant.’ I have chosen you and have not rejected you.
Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you; I will indeed help you; I will uphold you with My righteous right hand.
Behold, all who rage against you will be put to shame and disgraced. Those who contend with you will be brought to nothing and will perish.
You will seek them, yet you will not find them; those who war against you will be reduced to nothing.
For I am the LORD your God, who grasps your right hand and says to you, ‘Do not fear; I will help you.’”
“Do not fear, O worm Jacob, O few men of Israel. I will help you,” declares the LORD. “Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.”
“Behold, I will make you a new, sharp threshing sledge with many teeth. You will thresh the mountains and crush them, and you will reduce the hills to chaff.
You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away; the gale will scatter them. But you will rejoice in the LORD; you will glory in the Holy One of Israel.”
The poor and needy seek water, yet there is none; their tongues are parched with thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them; I, the God of Israel, will not abandon them.
I will open rivers on the barren heights and springs in the midst of the valleys. I will transform the desert into a pool of water and the dry land into flowing springs.
I will plant cedars in the wilderness, along with acacias, myrtles, and olive trees; I will set pines in the desert, together with fir and cypress,
so that all may see and know, may consider and understand, that the hand of the LORD has accomplished this and that the Holy One of Israel has created it.
“Present your case,” says the LORD. “Bring forth your strong arguments,” says the King of Jacob.
“Let them come and declare to us what will happen. Tell us what the former things were, so that we may reflect upon them and know their outcome. Or announce to us the things that are to come.
Tell us what is to come hereafter, that we may know that you are gods. Yes, do good or do evil, that we may be dismayed and filled with terror.
Behold, you are nothing, and your work amounts to nothing. He who chooses you is detestable.”
I have raised up one from the north, and he has come—from the east he calls upon My name. He treads upon rulers as upon mortar, as a potter tramples clay.
Who has declared this from the beginning, that we may know, and from times past, that we may say, ‘He is righteous’? No one proclaimed it, no one foretold it, no one heard your words.
I was the first to say to Zion, ‘Behold, here they are!’ and I gave to Jerusalem a herald of good news.
But when I look, there is no one; there is no counselor among them who, when I ask, can return an answer.
Behold, they are all a delusion; their works are nothing; their images are but wind and confusion.
Behold My Servant, whom I uphold, My chosen one, in whom My soul delights; I have put My Spirit upon Him; He will bring forth justice to the nations.
He will not cry out or raise His voice, nor make His voice heard in the street.
A bruised reed He will not break, and a smoldering wick He will not snuff out; He will faithfully bring forth justice.
He will not grow faint or be discouraged until He has established justice on the earth, and the coastlands will wait for His law.
Thus says the the LORD God, who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and its offspring, who gives breath to the people on it and spirit to those who walk in it: “
I, the the LORD, have called You in righteousness; I will take hold of Your hand. I will keep You and appoint You as a covenant for the people, a light for the nations,
to open the eyes of the blind, to bring prisoners out of the dungeon, and those who sit in darkness out of the prison.
I am the the LORD; that is My name. I will not give My glory to another, nor My praise to idols.
See, the former things have come to pass, and now I declare new things; before they spring forth I announce them to you.”
Sing to the the LORD a new song, His praise from the ends of the earth, you who go down to the sea and all that fills it, the coastlands and their inhabitants.
Let the wilderness and its cities lift up their voices, the villages where Kedar dwells; let the inhabitants of Sela sing for joy; let them shout from the tops of the mountains.
Let them give glory to the the LORD and declare His praise in the coastlands.
The The LORD will go forth like a warrior; He will stir up His zeal like a man of war. He will shout; yes, He will roar. He will prevail against His enemies.
“I have been silent for a long time; I have been still and restrained Myself. Now I will cry out like a woman in labor; I will gasp and pant together.
I will lay waste the mountains and hills and dry up all their vegetation; I will turn the rivers into islands and dry up the pools.

I will lead the blind by a way they do not know; I will guide them in paths they have not known. I will turn darkness into light before them and make the crooked places straight. These things I will do, and I will not forsake them.”
They will be turned back and utterly put to shame—those who trust in carved images, who say to molten images, ‘You are our gods.’
Hear, you deaf, and look, you blind, that you may see.
Who is blind but My servant, or deaf like My messenger whom I send? Who is blind like the one devoted to Me, or blind like the servant of the the LORD?
You have seen many things, but you do not observe them; your ears are open, but you do not hear.
The the LORD was pleased, for His righteousness' sake, to magnify the law and make it glorious.
But this is a people plundered and looted, all of them trapped in holes or hidden in prisons. They have become plunder with no one to rescue them, spoil with no one to say, ‘Bring them back!’
Who among you will pay attention to this, who will listen and hear hereafter?
Who gave Jacob to the plunderer, and Israel to the looters? Was it not the the LORD, against whom we have sinned? They were unwilling to walk in His ways, and they did not obey His law.
So He poured out on him the heat of His anger and the violence of war. It enveloped him in flames, yet he did not understand; it burned him, but he did not take it to heart.
But now this is what the LORD says—He who created you, Jacob, He who formed you, Israel: “Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name; you are Mine.
When you pass through the waters, I will be with you, and the rivers will not sweep over you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned, and the flames will not consume you.
“For I am the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior. I have given Egypt as your ransom, Cush and Seba in your place.
Because you are precious and honored in My sight, and because I love you, I will give people in your place and nations in exchange for your life.
“Do not fear, for I am with you. I will bring your offspring from the east and gather you from the west.
I will say to the north, ‘Give them up,’ and to the south, ‘Do not hold them back.’ Bring My sons from afar and My daughters from the ends of the earth—
everyone who is called by My name, whom I created for My glory, whom I formed and made.
“Bring out the people who are blind, though they have eyes, and the deaf, though they have ears.

Let all the nations be gathered together and the peoples assembled. Who among them can declare this and show us former things? Let them bring their witnesses to prove themselves right, and let them hear and say, ‘It is true.’

“You are My witnesses,” declares the LORD, “and My servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe Me and understand that I am He. Before Me no god was formed, nor will there be one after Me.
I, even I, am the LORD, and apart from Me there is no savior.
I have revealed, saved, and proclaimed—I, not a foreign god among you. You are My witnesses,” declares the LORD, “that I am God.
Even from eternity I am He, and no one can deliver out of My hand. When I act, who can reverse it?”
This is what the LORD says—your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: “For your sake I will send to Babylon and bring them all down as fugitives, even the Chaldeans, in the ships in which they rejoice.
I am the LORD, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, your King.”
This is what the LORD says—He who made a way through the sea, a path through the mighty waters,
who brings out the chariot and horse, the army and reinforcements together, and they lie down, never to rise again; they are extinguished, quenched like a wick:
“Do not remember the former things; do not consider the things of old.
See, I am doing a new thing; now it springs forth. Do you not perceive it? I will make a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert.
The beasts of the field will honor Me—the jackals and the ostriches—because I provide water in the wilderness and rivers in the desert, to give drink to My people, My chosen.
The people I formed for Myself will declare My praise.
“Yet you have not called upon Me, Jacob; you have grown weary of Me, Israel.
You have not brought Me sheep for your burnt offerings, nor honored Me with your sacrifices. I have not burdened you with grain offerings, nor wearied you with frankincense.
You have not bought Me sweet cane with money, nor satisfied Me with the fat of your sacrifices. But you have burdened Me with your sins; you have wearied Me with your iniquities.
I, even I, am He who blots out your transgressions for My own sake, and I will not remember your sins.
Remind Me; let us argue the case together. State your case, so that you may be proved right.
Your first father sinned, and your spokesmen have rebelled against Me.
So I will profane the princes of the sanctuary, and I will consign Jacob to destruction and Israel to reproach.”
But now listen, O Jacob, My servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.
Thus says the the LORD, your Maker and Former, who formed you in the womb and will help you: "Do not fear, O Jacob, My servant, and Jeshurun, whom I have chosen."
For I will pour water upon the thirsty land and streams upon the dry ground; I will pour My Spirit upon your offspring and My blessing upon your descendants.
They will spring up among the grass like willows beside flowing streams.
One will say, "I belong to the LORD," another will call himself by the name of Jacob, and another will write on his hand, "The LORD's," and will surname himself by the name of Israel.
Thus says the the LORD, Israel's King and Redeemer, the the LORD of Hosts: "I am the First and I am the Last, and there is no God but Me.
Who then is like Me? Let him call out and declare it; let him set it in order before Me, since I established the ancient people. Let them declare the things to come and what will happen.
Do not fear or be dismayed. Have I not announced it to you long ago and declared it? You are My witnesses. Is there any God but Me? There is no Rock; I know not one."
All who fashion idols are nothing, and their precious things are worthless. Their witnesses see nothing and know nothing, so they will be put to shame.
Who fashions a god or casts an idol to no profit?
Behold, all his companions will be put to shame, and the craftsmen are but men. Let them all gather and stand up; they will tremble and be put to shame.
The blacksmith takes a tool, works in the coals, and fashions it with hammers; he works with his strong arm. Even he grows hungry and loses strength; he drinks no water and becomes faint.
The woodworker extends a measuring line, outlines it with chalk, shapes it with planes, and marks it with a compass. He makes it like the form of a man, like the beauty of man, to dwell in a house.
He cuts down cedars, or he takes a cypress or an oak and makes it strong for himself among the trees of the forest. He plants a pine, and the rain makes it grow.
It becomes fuel for man. He takes some and warms himself; he kindles a fire and bakes bread. He also makes a god and worships it; he makes an idol and bows down to it.
Half of it he burns in the fire; on that half he eats meat; he roasts meat and is satisfied. He warms himself and says, "Ah, I am warm; I have seen the fire."
The rest of it he makes into a god, into his idol; he bows to it, worships it, prays to it, and says, "Deliver me, for you are my god."
They know nothing and understand nothing, for their eyes are plastered shut so they cannot see, and their hearts cannot understand.
