They have grown fat and sleek; they have excelled in evil deeds. They do not plead the cause of the orphan, nor do they defend the rights of the needy.
Shall I not punish them for these things? declares the LORD. Shall I not avenge Myself on a nation such as this?
An appalling and horrible thing has happened in the land.
The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests rule by their own authority; My people love it so. But what will you do when the end comes?”
Flee for safety, O sons of Benjamin, from the midst of Jerusalem! Blow the trumpet in Tekoa, and raise a signal over Beth-haccerem, for a great calamity is seen coming from the north.
I will destroy the beautiful and delicate Daughter of Zion.
Shepherds and their flocks will come against her; they will pitch tents all around her and graze, each in his own portion.
Prepare for war against her! Arise, and let us attack at noon! Woe to us, for the day wanes and the evening shadows lengthen.
Arise, and let us attack by night and destroy her palaces!
For thus says the LORD of Hosts: "Cut down her trees and cast up a siege ramp against Jerusalem. This is the city to be punished; oppression fills her midst.
As a well keeps its water fresh, so she keeps her wickedness fresh. Violence and destruction are heard in her; sickness and wounds are continually before Me.
Be corrected, O Jerusalem, or My soul will be torn from you; I will make you a desolation, a land without inhabitants."
Thus says the LORD of Hosts: "The remnant of Israel will be gleaned as thoroughly as a vine; pass your hand again over the branches, like a grape gatherer."

To whom shall I speak and give warning, that they may hear? Behold, their ear is uncircumcised, and they cannot listen. Behold, the word of the LORD has become a reproach to them; they take no delight in it.

But I am full of the wrath of the LORD; I am weary of holding it in. Pour it out upon the children in the street and upon the company of young men together, for husband and wife alike will be captured, and the aged along with those full of years.
Their houses shall pass to others, their fields and wives together, for I will stretch out My hand against the inhabitants of the land, declares the LORD.
For from the least of them to the greatest, everyone is greedy for unjust gain; and from prophet to priest, everyone deals falsely.
They have healed the wound of My people lightly, saying, 'Peace, peace,' when there is no peace.

Were they ashamed when they committed abomination? No, they were not at all ashamed; they did not know how to blush. Therefore they shall fall among those who fall; at the time that I punish them, they shall stumble, says the LORD.
Thus says the LORD: "Stand by the roads, and look, and ask for the ancient paths, where the good way is; and walk in it, and find rest for your souls." But they said, "We will not walk in it."
I set watchmen over you, saying, "Pay attention to the sound of the trumpet!" But they said, "We will not pay attention."
Therefore hear, O nations, and know, O assembly, what will befall them.
Hear, O earth: behold, I am bringing disaster upon this people, the fruit of their schemes, because they have not paid attention to My words; and as for My law, they have rejected it.
What use to Me is frankincense from Sheba, or sweet cane from a distant land? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable, nor your sacrifices pleasing to Me.
Therefore thus says the LORD: "Behold, I will lay stumbling blocks before this people; fathers and sons together shall stumble over them; neighbor and friend shall perish."
Thus says the LORD: "Behold, a people is coming from the north country, a great nation is stirring from the farthest parts of the earth.
They lay hold on bow and javelin; they are cruel and have no mercy; their voice roars like the sea; they ride on horses, set in array as a man for war, against you, O Daughter of Zion!"
We have heard the report of it; our hands fall limp; anguish has taken hold of us, pain as of a woman in labor.
Do not go out into the field, nor walk on the road, for the enemy has a sword; terror is on every side.
O Daughter of My people, put on sackcloth, and roll in ashes; make mourning as for an only son, most bitter lamentation, for suddenly the destroyer will come upon us.
I have made you an assayer among My people, a fortified tower, that you may know and test their ways.
They are all stubborn rebels, slanderers; they are bronze and iron, all of them corrupt.
The bellows blow fiercely; the lead is consumed by the fire; in vain the refiner refines, for the wicked are not separated.
They are called rejected silver, for the LORD has rejected them.
This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
“Stand in the gate of the LORD’s house and proclaim this word there: ‘Hear the word of the LORD, all you people of Judah who enter these gates to worship the LORD.’”
“Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: ‘Amend your ways and your deeds, and I will let you dwell in this place.
Do not trust in deceptive words that say, “This is the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD.”
For if you truly amend your ways and your deeds, if you truly execute justice between one person and another,
if you do not oppress the foreigner, the fatherless, or the widow, or shed innocent blood in this place, and do not follow other gods to your own harm,
then I will let you dwell in this place, in the land I gave to your fathers from ancient times and forever.’”
“Behold, you are trusting in deceptive words that cannot profit.
Will you steal and murder, commit adultery and swear falsely, burn incense to Baal, and follow other gods you have not known,
and then you come and stand before Me in this house, which bears My Name, and say, ‘We are delivered!’—only to go on doing all these abominations?
Has this house, which bears My Name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? Behold, I Myself have seen it,” declares the LORD.
“But go now to My place in Shiloh, where I first made a dwelling for My Name, and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of My people Israel.
And now, because you have done all these things, declares the LORD, and because I spoke to you again and again but you would not listen, and I called you but you would not answer,
I will do to the house called by My Name, in which you trust, and to the place I gave to you and your fathers, what I did to Shiloh.
I will cast you out of My presence, just as I cast out all your brothers, all the descendants of Ephraim.”
“As for you, do not pray for this people, nor lift up a cry or prayer for them, and do not intercede with Me, for I will not hear you.
Do you not see what they are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
The children gather wood, the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead dough to make cakes for the Queen of Heaven; and they pour out drink offerings to other gods, to provoke Me to anger.
Is it Me they are provoking?” declares the LORD. “Is it not themselves, to their own shame?”

“Therefore thus says the Lord the LORD: Behold, My anger and My wrath will be poured out on this place, on man and beast, on the trees of the field and on the fruit of the ground; it will burn and will not be quenched.”
“Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: ‘Add your burnt offerings to your sacrifices and eat the flesh yourselves!
For when I brought your fathers out of the land of Egypt, I did not speak to them or command them concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices.
But this is what I commanded them: ‘Obey My voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be My people; and walk in all the way that I command you, that it may be well with you.’
But they did not listen or pay attention; instead, they followed the stubbornness of their evil hearts and turned away rather than moving forward.
From the day your fathers came out of the land of Egypt to this day, I have persistently sent to you all My servants the prophets,
yet they did not listen to Me or pay attention; instead, they hardened themselves in defiance. They acted more wickedly than their fathers.
So you shall speak all these words to them, but they will not listen to you. You shall call to them, but they will not answer you.
And you shall say to them, ‘This is the nation that did not obey the voice of the LORD their God, and did not accept discipline; truth has perished and is cut off from their mouth.’”
“Cut off your hair and cast it away; raise a lamentation on the bare heights, for the LORD has rejected and forsaken the generation of His wrath.
For the people of Judah have done evil in My sight,” declares the LORD. “They have set their abominations in the house that is called by My Name, to defile it.
And they have built the high places of Topheth, which is in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire, something I did not command, nor did it enter My mind.

Therefore, behold, the days are coming,” declares the LORD, “when it will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter; for they will bury in Topheth until there is no room.
And the corpses of this people will be food for the birds of the air and for the beasts of the earth, and none will frighten them away.

And I will put an end to the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of the bridegroom and the bride, in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, for the land will become a desolate waste.”

At that time, declares the LORD, the bones of the kings of Judah, the bones of its officials, the bones of the priests, the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem will be brought out of their tombs.

They will be spread out before the sun, the moon, and all the host of heaven, which they loved and served, after which they walked, which they sought, and to which they bowed down. They will not be gathered or interred; they will be like dung on the surface of the ground.
Death will be chosen rather than life by all the remnant that remains of this evil family in all the places where I have driven them, declares the LORD of hosts.
You shall say to them, “Thus says the LORD: Do men fall and not rise again? If one turns away, does he not return?”
Why then has this people turned away in perpetual backsliding? They hold fast to deceit; they refuse to return.

I have listened and heard, but they do not speak what is right. No one repents of his wickedness, saying, “What have I done?” Everyone rushes headlong into his own course, like a horse charging into battle.
Even the stork in the heavens knows her appointed times, and the turtledove, swallow, and crane observe the time of their coming; but My people do not know the ordinance of the LORD.
How can you say, “We are wise, and the law of the LORD is with us”? Surely the lying pen of the scribes has made it a lie.
The wise men will be put to shame; they will be dismayed and taken. Behold, they have rejected the word of the LORD, so what wisdom is in them?
Therefore I will give their wives to others and their fields to new owners, because from the least to the greatest everyone is greedy for gain; from prophet to priest, everyone practices deceit.
They have healed the wound of My people lightly, saying, “Peace, peace,” when there is no peace.

Were they ashamed when they committed abomination? No, they were not at all ashamed; they did not know how to blush. Therefore they will fall among the fallen; at the time of their punishment they will stumble, says the LORD.
When I would gather them, declares the LORD, there are no grapes on the vine, nor figs on the fig tree; even the leaf has withered, and what I gave them has passed away from them.

“Why do we sit still? Gather together; let us enter the fortified cities and perish there, for the LORD our God has condemned us to perish and has given us poisoned water to drink, because we have sinned against the LORD.”
“We looked for peace, but no good came; for a time of healing, but behold, terror.”

The snorting of their horses is heard from Dan; at the sound of the neighing of their stallions the whole land quakes. They come and devour the land and its fullness, the city and those who dwell in it.
“For behold, I am sending among you serpents, adders that cannot be charmed, and they will bite you,” declares the LORD.
My joy is gone; grief is upon me; my heart is sick.

Behold, the cry of my people from far and wide in the land: “Is the LORD not in Zion? Is her King not in her?” “Why have they provoked Me to anger with their carved images and with their foreign idols?”
“The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved.”
For the wound of the daughter of my people I am crushed; I mourn, and dismay has taken hold of me.
Is there no balm in Gilead? Is there no physician there? Why then has the health of the daughter of my people not been restored?
If only my head were a spring of water and my eyes a fountain of tears, I would weep day and night for the slain among my people.
If only I had a traveler's shelter in the wilderness, I would leave my people and go far from them, for they are all adulterers, a crowd of treacherous men.
"They bend their tongues like bows to shoot lies; they grow strong in the land, but not for faithfulness. They advance from one evil to the next, and they do not acknowledge Me," declares the LORD.
"Let every man guard yourselves, and trust no neighbor, for every brother is a schemer and every neighbor goes about slandering.
Each man deceives his neighbor and refuses to speak the truth; they have trained their tongues to lie and wear themselves out doing wrong.
Your dwelling is amid deceit; in deceit they refuse to know Me," declares the LORD.
Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts says: "See, I will refine and test them, for what else can I do because of My people?
Their tongues are drawn bows that shoot lies; deceit fills their mouths. They speak peace to their neighbors while setting ambushes in their hearts.
Should I not punish them for these things? Should I not take vengeance on a nation like this?" declares the LORD.

I will take up weeping and wailing for the mountains and a lament for the wilderness pastures, because they are burned over so that no one passes through, and the lowing of cattle is not heard. From the birds of the sky to the beasts, all have fled and gone.
I will make Jerusalem a heap of ruins, a haunt of jackals, and the cities of Judah a desolation without inhabitant.

Who is the wise man who understands this? To whom has the mouth of the LORD spoken, that he might declare it? Why has the land perished and been scorched like a wilderness, with no one passing through?
The LORD said, "Because they have forsaken My law, which I set before them, and have not obeyed My voice or walked in it.
Instead, they have followed the stubbornness of their hearts and the Baals, as their fathers taught them."
Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: "See, I will feed this people wormwood and give them bitter water to drink.
I will scatter them among nations that neither they nor their fathers have known, and I will send the sword after them until I have finished them off."
This is what the LORD of Hosts says: "Consider, and call for the mourning women, that they may come; send for the skilled women, that they may come.
Let them hurry and raise a wailing over us, so that our eyes may overflow with tears and our eyelids gush water.
For a voice of wailing is heard from Zion: 'How ruined we are! We are deeply ashamed, because we have left the land, because our dwellings have been thrown down.'"
"Hear, women, the word of the LORD, and let your ear receive the word of His mouth. Teach your daughters to wail, and each woman her neighbor to lament.
For death has climbed through our windows and entered our palaces, cutting off children from the streets and young men from the squares."
Speak: "This is what the LORD says: 'The corpses of men will fall like dung on the open field, like sheaves behind the reaper, with no one to gather them.'"
"This is what the LORD says: 'Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom, nor the mighty man boast in his might, nor the rich man boast in his riches.

But let the one who boasts boast in this: that he understands and knows Me, that I am the LORD, who practices steadfast love, justice, and righteousness on the earth, for in these things I delight,' declares the LORD."
"See, days are coming," declares the LORD, "when I will punish all who are circumcised yet uncircumcised:

Egypt, Judah, Edom, the Ammonites, Moab, and all who live in the wilderness and clip the hair at their temples. For all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart."
Hear the word that the LORD has spoken against you, O house of Israel.
Thus says the LORD: Do not learn the way of the nations, and do not be dismayed by the signs of the heavens, for the nations are dismayed by them.
For the customs of the peoples are utterly futile: a man cuts a tree from the forest, and a craftsman shapes it with an axe.
He overlays it with silver and gold, and they fasten it with nails and hammers so that it will not topple.
They are like scarecrows in a cucumber patch; they cannot speak, and they must be carried because they cannot walk. Do not fear them, for they can do no evil, nor can they do any good.
There is none like You, the LORD; You are great, and Your name is great in might.
Who would not fear You, King of the nations? For it is Your due; for among all the wise men of the nations and in all their kingdoms, there is none like You.
Yet they are altogether brutish and foolish; the teaching of idols is nothing but wood.

Silver is beaten into plates and brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz—the work of a craftsman and of a goldsmith's hands. Their garments are blue and purple; all of them are the work of skilled men.
But the LORD is the true God; He is the living God and an everlasting King. At His wrath the earth quakes, and the nations cannot endure His indignation.
Thus you shall say to them: "The gods that did not make the heavens and the earth shall perish from the earth and from beneath these heavens."
He made the earth by His power; He established the world by His wisdom, and by His understanding He stretched out the heavens.

When He utters His voice, there is a tumult of waters in the heavens, and He makes the vapors ascend from the ends of the earth. He makes lightning for the rain and brings forth the wind from His storehouses.
Every person is brutish, devoid of knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his carved image, for his molten idol is a lie, and there is no breath in them.
They are futile, a work of delusions; in the time of their visitation they shall perish.
The Portion of Jacob is not like these; for He is the Maker of all things, and Israel is the tribe of His inheritance. The LORD of hosts is His name.
Gather your belongings from the ground, O inhabitant of the besieged city.
For thus says the LORD: "Behold, I will sling out the inhabitants of the land at this time, and I will bring distress upon them, so that they may be captured."
Woe is me because of my brokenness! My wound is severe; yet I said, "Truly, this is my grief, and I must bear it."
My tent is plundered, and all my cords are broken. My children have gone from me and are no more; there is no one to pitch my tent again or to set up my curtains.
For the shepherds have become brutish and have not sought the LORD; therefore they have not prospered, and all their flock is scattered.
Behold, the sound of a report is coming—a great commotion from the north country—to make the cities of Judah a desolation, a haunt of jackals.
The LORD, I know that the way of man is not in himself; it is not in man who walks to direct his steps.
Correct me, the LORD, but with justice; not in Your anger, lest You reduce me to nothing.

Pour out Your wrath upon the nations that do not know You, and upon the families that do not call on Your name; for they have devoured Jacob, they have devoured him and consumed him, and they have laid waste his homeland.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the the LORD, saying:
“Hear the words of this covenant and speak them to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
Tell them that this is what the the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this covenant

that I commanded your fathers when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron furnace, saying, “Obey Me, and do everything I command you, and you will be My people, and I will be your God,”
in order to fulfill the oath I swore to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is this day.’” Then I answered, “Amen, O the LORD.”
Then the the LORD said to me, “Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem: ‘Hear the words of this covenant and carry them out.’
For from the time I brought your fathers out of the land of Egypt until this day, I have warned them earnestly and without ceasing, saying, ‘Obey My voice.’

Yet they refused to listen or give heed, but each walked in the stubbornness of his evil heart. So I brought upon them all the curses of this covenant, which I had commanded them to obey, but they did not keep them.”
Then the the LORD said to me, “A conspiracy has been found among the men of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem.

They have returned to the iniquities of their fathers who refused to heed My words. They have pursued other gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have violated the covenant I made with their fathers.
Therefore this is what the the LORD says: ‘I am about to bring upon them a calamity from which they cannot escape. They will cry out to Me, but I will not listen to them.
Then the cities of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods to whom they have been burning incense, but these gods cannot save them in their time of disaster.
Your gods are as numerous as your cities, O Judah, and the altars you have set up to shame—altars to burn incense to Baal—are as numerous as the streets of Jerusalem.’”
“As for you, do not pray for these people. Do not raise a cry or a prayer on their behalf, for I will not listen when they call to Me in their time of disaster.
What right does My beloved have to be in My house, when she has done so many evil things? Can consecrated meat avert your punishment when you rejoice in your evil?
The the LORD formerly called you a flourishing olive tree, beautiful with good fruit. But with the roar of a mighty storm He will set fire to it, and its branches will be consumed.

The the LORD of Hosts, who planted you, has decreed disaster upon you, because of the evil that the house of Israel and the house of Judah have done, provoking Me to anger by burning incense to Baal.”
And the the LORD informed me, so I knew. Then He showed me their deeds.

I was like a gentle lamb led to slaughter; I did not know that they had devised plans against me: “Let us destroy the tree with its fruit; let us cut him off from the land of the living, that his name may be remembered no more.”
O the LORD of Hosts, who judges righteously, who tests the heart and mind, let me see Your vengeance upon them, for to You I have committed my cause.
Therefore this is what the the LORD says concerning the men of Anathoth who are seeking your life, saying: “You must not prophesy in the name of the the LORD, or you will die by our hand.”
Therefore this is what the the LORD of Hosts says: “I will punish them. The young men will die by the sword; their sons and daughters will die by famine.
Not even a remnant will be left, for I will bring disaster on the men of Anathoth in the year of their punishment.”
You are righteous, the LORD, when I plead with You. Yet I wish to contend with You: Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why are all who deal treacherously at ease?
You planted them, and they have taken root; they grow and bear fruit. You are always on their lips, but You are far from their hearts.
But You know me, the LORD; You see me and test my heart toward You. Drag them away like sheep to be slaughtered, and set them apart for the day of carnage.

How long will the land mourn and the grass of every field wither? Because of the wickedness of those who dwell in it, the beasts and the birds are swept away, for the people have said, "He will not see what happens to us." "
If you have raced with foot soldiers and they have exhausted you, how can you compete with horses? If you stumble in a land of peace, how will you do in the thickets of the Jordan?
For even your brothers and your father's house have betrayed you; even they have cried aloud after you. Do not trust them, though they speak well of you." "
I have forsaken My house; I have abandoned My inheritance. I have given the beloved of My soul into the hands of her enemies.
My inheritance has become to Me like a lion in the forest. She has roared against Me; therefore I hate her.
Is not My inheritance to Me like a speckled bird of prey, with birds of prey all around her? Go, gather all the beasts of the field; bring them to devour her." "
Many shepherds have destroyed My vineyard; they have trampled My plot of ground. They have turned My pleasant field into a desolate wasteland.
They have made it a desolation; desolate, it mourns before Me. The whole land is laid waste, but no one takes it to heart.
Over all the barren heights in the wilderness destroyers have come, for the sword of the LORD devours from one end of the earth to the other. No flesh has peace." "
They have sown wheat but harvested thorns. They have worn themselves out to no avail. Be ashamed of your harvests because of the fierce anger of the LORD." "

This is what the LORD says: 'As for all My evil neighbors who touch the inheritance that I bequeathed to My people Israel, I am about to uproot them from their land, and I will uproot the house of Judah from among them.
But after I have uprooted them, I will return and have compassion on them and bring them back, each to his own inheritance and each to his own land.
And if they will diligently learn the ways of My people—to swear by My name, "As surely as the LORD lives"—just as they taught My people to swear by Baal, then they will be built up among My people.
But if they will not obey, then I will uproot that nation and destroy it, declares the LORD.'"
Thus says the LORD to me, "Go and purchase a linen belt for yourself, fasten it around your waist, and do not wash it in water."
So I bought the belt according to the word of the LORD and fastened it around my waist.
Then the word of the LORD came to me a second time, saying,
"Take the belt that you bought, which is on your waist, and arise, go to the Euphrates, and hide it there in a cleft of the rock."
So I went and hid it by the Euphrates, as the LORD had commanded me.
After many days the LORD said to me, "Arise, go to the Euphrates, and take from there the belt that I commanded you to hide there."
So I went to the Euphrates, dug, and took the belt from the place where I had hidden it; and there it was, the belt ruined and utterly useless.
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
"Thus says the LORD: 'In this way I will destroy the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.

This evil people, who refuse to hear My words, who walk in the stubbornness of their heart and have gone after other gods to serve them and bow down to them, will be like this belt, which is good for nothing.

For as the belt clings to the waist of a man, so I have made the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah cling to Me, declares the LORD, that they might be for Me a people, and a name, and a praise, and a glory; but they would not hear.'"

And you shall say to them this word: "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'Every jar will be filled with wine.'" And they will say to you, "Do we not indeed know that every jar will be filled with wine?"

And you shall say to them, "Thus says the LORD: 'Behold, I will fill all the inhabitants of this land—the kings who sit on David's throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem—with drunkenness.
And I will dash them one against another, fathers and sons together, declares the LORD. I will not pity, nor spare, nor have compassion, but will destroy them.'"
"Hear and give ear; do not be proud, for the LORD has spoken."

"Give glory to the LORD your God before He brings darkness, and before your feet stumble on the dark mountains, and while you hope for light, He turns it into deathly gloom and makes it deep darkness."
But if you will not hear it, my soul will weep in secret because of your pride; my eye will weep bitterly and run down with tears, because the LORD's flock has been taken captive.
"Say to the king and to the queen mother, 'Humble yourselves and sit down, for your glorious crown has fallen from your heads.
The cities of the Negev will be shut up, with no one to open them; all Judah will be carried into exile, carried completely away.'"
"Lift up your eyes and see those who come from the north. Where is the flock that was given to you, your beautiful flock?
What will you say when He appoints over you those whom you have taught to be your allies at your head? Will not pangs seize you like a woman in labor?
And if you say in your heart, 'Why have these things come upon me?' it is because of the greatness of your iniquity. Your skirts are uncovered, your heels are made bare."
"Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard its spots? Then neither can you do good—you who are accustomed to doing evil.
Therefore I will scatter them like chaff driven by the desert wind.
This is your lot, the portion measured out to you from Me, declares the LORD, because you have forgotten Me and trusted in falsehood.
I will also uncover your skirts over your face, and your shame will be seen.

I have seen your adulteries and your lustful neighings, the shameless lewdness of your prostitution; on the hills and in the fields I have seen your detestable acts. Woe to you, O Jerusalem! How long will you remain unclean?"
The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah concerning the droughts.
Judah mourns, and her gates languish; they bow to the ground in blackness, and the cry of Jerusalem rises.
Her nobles send their servants for water; they come to the cisterns and find none; they return with empty vessels, ashamed and confounded, and they cover their heads.
Because the ground is dismayed—there has been no rain in the land—the plowmen are ashamed and cover their heads.
Even the doe in the field gives birth and abandons her young, because there is no grass.
The wild donkeys stand on the bare heights, panting like jackals; their eyes fail because there is no vegetation.
Though our iniquities testify against us, do, O the LORD, for Your name's sake; for our backslidings are many, and we have sinned against You.
O Hope of Israel, her Savior in time of distress, why should You be like a stranger in the land, like a traveler who turns aside to spend the night?
Why should You be like a man stunned, like a mighty one who cannot save? Yet You are in our midst, O the LORD, and we are called by Your name; do not forsake us.
Thus says the LORD to this people: “They love to wander; they have not restrained their feet. Therefore the LORD does not accept them; now He will remember their iniquity and punish their sins.”
The LORD said to me, “Do not pray for the welfare of this people.
When they fast, I will not hear their cry; when they offer burnt offering and grain offering, I will not accept them; rather, I will consume them by sword, famine, and pestilence.”
Then I said, “Ah, Lord, the LORD! Behold, the prophets say to them, ‘You will not see the sword, nor will there be famine in this place; but I will give you true peace in this place.’”

“The prophets prophesy lies in My name,” the LORD said to me. “I have not sent them, nor commanded them, nor spoken to them. They prophesy to you a lying vision, worthless divination, and the deceit of their own minds.

Therefore thus says the LORD concerning the prophets who prophesy in My name, though I did not send them, and who say, ‘No sword or famine shall come upon this land’: By sword and famine those prophets shall be consumed.

And the people to whom they prophesy shall be cast out in the streets of Jerusalem because of famine and sword, with no one to bury them—their wives, their sons, and their daughters. I will pour out their evil upon them.”

The LORD told Jeremiah to declare to them, “My eyes overflow with tears night and day, and let them not cease, for the virgin daughter of my people has been shattered by a great breach, a very grievous wound.”

If I go out into the field, behold, those slain by the sword; if I enter the city, behold, diseases from famine. For both prophet and priest ply their trade throughout the land, but they have no knowledge.
Have You utterly rejected Judah? Has Your soul loathed Zion? Why have You struck us so that there is no healing? We looked for peace, but no good came; for a time of healing, but behold, terror.
We acknowledge our wickedness, O the LORD, the iniquity of our fathers; for we have sinned against You.
For Your name's sake, do not spurn us; do not dishonor the throne of Your glory. Remember; do not break Your covenant with us.
Are there any among the idols of the nations that can bring rain? Or can the heavens give showers? Is it not You, O the LORD our God? Therefore we hope in You, for You have made all these things.
Then the LORD said to me, “Even if Moses and Samuel should stand before Me, My heart would not turn toward this people. Send them away from My presence, and let them go.

If they ask you, ‘Where shall we go?’ you must tell them that this is what the LORD says: ‘Those destined for death, to death; those for the sword, to the sword; those for famine, to famine; and those for captivity, to captivity.’
I will appoint over them four kinds of destroyers, declares the LORD: the sword to kill, the dogs to drag away, and the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth to devour and destroy.
I will make them an object of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, because of what Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, did in Jerusalem. “
Who will have pity on you, O Jerusalem? Who will mourn for you? Who will turn aside to inquire after your welfare?
You have rejected Me, declares the LORD. You have turned away from Me. So I have stretched out My hand against you and destroyed you; I am weary of showing compassion.
I will winnow them with a winnowing fork at the gates of the land. I will bereave and destroy My people, for they did not turn from their ways.
Their widows will be more numerous than the sand of the sea. I will bring a destroyer at noon against the mothers of young men. I will suddenly bring upon them anguish and terror.

The mother of seven will grow faint and breathe her last; her sun will set while it is still day; she will be disgraced and humiliated. And the rest of them I will put to the sword in the presence of their enemies, declares the LORD.” “
Ah, woe to me, my mother, that you bore me, a man of strife and contention to all the land! I have neither lent nor borrowed, yet everyone curses me.”
The LORD said, “Surely I will deliver you for a good purpose; surely I will make your enemies plead with you in time of disaster and in time of distress.
Can anyone smash iron—iron from the north—or bronze?
Your wealth and your treasures I will give as plunder, without cost, for all your sins, throughout your territory.
I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know, for My anger has blazed like fire; it will burn against you.” “
O the LORD, You know; remember me and take vengeance for me on my persecutors. In Your patience, do not take me away. Know that I bear reproach for Your sake.
Your words were found, and I ate them; Your words became to me a joy and the delight of my heart, because I am called by Your name, O the LORD God of Hosts.
I never sat with the merrymakers, nor did I celebrate. Because of Your hand, I sat alone, for You had filled me with indignation.
Why is my pain perpetual and my wound incurable, refusing to be healed? You have indeed become to me a deceitful brook—water that is not reliable.”

Therefore this is what the LORD says: “If you return, I will restore you; you will stand before Me. And if you extract the precious from the worthless, you will be as My mouth. They will turn to you, but you must not turn to them.
I will make you a fortified wall of bronze to this people; they will fight against you but will not overcome you, for I am with you to save you and deliver you, declares the LORD.
I will deliver you from the hand of the wicked and redeem you from the grasp of the ruthless.”
The word of the the LORD came to me, saying,
“You shall not take a wife for yourself, nor shall you have sons and daughters in this place.”
For this is what the the LORD says concerning the sons and daughters born in this place, and concerning their mothers who bore them and their fathers who begot them in this land:

“They shall die of deadly diseases. They shall not be lamented or buried; they shall be as dung on the surface of the ground. They shall fall by sword and famine, and their corpses shall be food for the birds of the sky and for the beasts of the earth.”

For this is what the the LORD says: “Do not enter a house where there is a funeral meal. Do not go to lament, nor show sympathy, because I have withdrawn My peace from this people,” declares the the LORD, “along with My loving devotion and compassion.”
“Great and small shall die in this land. They shall not be buried, and no one shall mourn for them, nor shall anyone cut himself or shave his head for them.
No food will be offered to comfort those who mourn the dead; not even a cup of consolation will be given for the loss of a father or mother.
You shall not enter a house of feasting to sit with them, to eat and drink.”

For this is what the the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “I will put an end in this place, before your eyes and in your days, to the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride.”

And when you tell this people all these words, and they say to you, “Why has the the LORD pronounced all this great evil against us? What is our iniquity? What is our sin that we have committed against the the LORD our God?”

Then you shall say to them, “Because your fathers have forsaken Me, declares the the LORD, and have walked after other gods and served them and worshiped them, and have forsaken Me and have not kept My law.
And you have done worse than your fathers, for behold, every one of you walks after the stubbornness of his evil heart, so as not to listen to Me.”
“Therefore I will cast you out of this land into a land that neither you nor your fathers have known, and there you shall serve other gods day and night, because I will show you no favor.”
“Therefore, behold, days are coming,” declares the the LORD, “when it shall no longer be said, ‘As the the LORD lives who brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt,’

but, ‘As the the LORD lives who brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north and from all the lands where He had driven them.’ And I will bring them back to their land that I gave to their fathers.”

“Behold, I am sending for many fishermen,” declares the the LORD, “and they shall fish for them; and afterward I will send for many hunters, and they shall hunt them from every mountain and from every hill and out of the clefts of the rocks.”
“For My eyes are on all their ways; they are not hidden from Me, and their iniquity is not concealed from My eyes.

And I will first repay double for their iniquity and their sin, because they have profaned My land; they have filled My inheritance with the carcasses of their detestable things and their abominations.”

O the LORD, my strength and my stronghold, my refuge in the day of trouble! To You the nations shall come from the ends of the earth and say, “Our fathers have inherited nothing but lies, futility, and things in which there is no profit.”
“Can a man make gods for himself? Yet they are not gods!
Therefore, behold, I will make them know—this time I will make them know My hand and My might, and they shall know that My name is the the LORD.”
Judah’s sin is inscribed with an iron stylus, engraved with a diamond point upon the tablet of their heart and upon the horns of your altars.
Even their children remember their altars and their Asherah poles beside verdant trees on the high hills.
O My mountain in the open country, I will surrender your wealth and all your treasures as plunder, and your high places, because of sin throughout your territory.
You yourself will relinquish the inheritance I gave you, and I will enslave you to your enemies in a land you do not know; for you have kindled a fire in My anger that will burn forever.
Thus says the LORD: “Cursed is the man who trusts in mankind, who makes flesh his strength and turns his heart away from the LORD.
He will be like a stunted shrub in the wasteland; he will not perceive prosperity when it comes. He will dwell in the parched places of the desert, in a salt land where no one lives.
Blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD, whose hope is the LORD.

He is like a tree planted by the waters, sending out its roots toward the stream. It does not fear when heat comes; its leaves remain green. It has no anxiety in a year of drought and never fails to bear fruit.
The heart is deceitful above all things and incurably sick. Who can fathom it?
I, the LORD, search the heart and test the mind, to repay each person according to his conduct, according to the fruit of his deeds.”
Like a partridge that broods over eggs it did not lay is the one who amasses wealth unjustly. In the middle of his days his riches will desert him, and in the end he will prove a fool.
From the beginning, a glorious throne, exalted on high, has been the place of our sanctuary.
O the LORD, the Hope of Israel, all who forsake You will be put to shame; those who turn away from me will be written in the dust, for they have forsaken the LORD, the fountain of living waters.
Heal me, O the LORD, and I will be healed; save me, and I will be saved, for You are my praise.
Behold, they keep saying to me, ‘Where is the word of the LORD? Let it come now!’
As for me, I have not shrunk from shepherding in Your service, nor have I longed for the day of calamity; You know that what passed my lips was spoken before You.
Do not be a terror to me; You are my refuge in the day of disaster.
Let my persecutors be put to shame, but do not let me be put to shame; let them be dismayed, but do not let me be dismayed. Bring upon them the day of evil; crush them with double ruin.
Thus says the LORD to me: “Go and stand at the gate of the sons of the people, through which the kings of Judah enter and leave, and at all the gates of Jerusalem,
and say to them, ‘Hear the word of the LORD, you kings of Judah and all Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem who enter through these gates.
Thus says the LORD: Guard yourselves, and do not carry a burden or bring it through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day.
Do not carry a burden out of your houses on the Sabbath day, and do no work, but consecrate the Sabbath day, as I commanded your fathers.’
“But they did not listen or incline their ear; they stiffened their necks and refused to hear or receive instruction.
But if you diligently listen to Me—declares the LORD—and bring no burden through the gates of this city on the Sabbath, and consecrate the Sabbath day by doing no work on it,

then kings and princes who sit on David’s throne will enter through the gates of this city, riding in chariots and on horses—they and their officials, the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem—and this city will endure forever.

People will come from the cities of Judah, from the region around Jerusalem, from Benjamin, from the Shephelah, from the hill country, and from the Negev, bringing burnt offerings, sacrifices, grain offerings, incense, and thank offerings to the house of the LORD.

But if you do not listen to Me to consecrate the Sabbath day and to refrain from carrying a burden as you enter the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath, then I will kindle a fire in its gates, and it will consume the palaces of Jerusalem and will not be quenched.”
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD said,
"Arise and go down to the potter's house, and there I will let you hear My words."
So I went down to the potter's house, and there he was working at the wheels.
The vessel he was fashioning from clay was spoiled in the potter's hand, so he reworked it into another vessel, as it seemed good to the potter to make.
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
"O house of Israel, can I not do with you as this potter does?" declares the LORD. "Look, as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are you in My hand, O house of Israel!
"The instant I speak concerning a nation and concerning a kingdom, to uproot and to tear down and to destroy it,
if that nation against which I have spoken turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster that I intended to bring upon it.
"And the instant I speak concerning a nation and concerning a kingdom, to build and to plant it,
if it does evil in My sight, so that it does not obey My voice, then I will relent concerning the good with which I said I would benefit it.

"Now therefore speak to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying, 'Thus says the LORD: Behold, I am fashioning disaster against you and devising a plan against you. Return now, every man, from his evil way, and make your ways and your deeds good.'"
But they said, "It is utterly futile! For we will walk according to our own plans, and each of us will follow the stubborn dictates of his evil heart."
Therefore thus says the LORD: "Ask now among the nations, 'Who has heard such things?' The virgin of Israel has committed an appalling atrocity.
"Would anyone abandon the snow of Lebanon that descends from the rocky slopes? Or would the cold waters flowing from a distant source be forsaken?
Yet My people have forgotten Me; they burn incense to worthless idols, and they have caused themselves to stumble from the ancient paths and to walk in bypaths rather than on the main road.
"They have made their land a desolation and a lasting object of scorn; everyone who passes by it is appalled and shakes his head.
I will scatter them before the enemy like an east wind; in the day of their calamity I will turn My back on them and not My face."

Then they said, "Come, let us devise plans against Jeremiah, for instruction will not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet. Come, let us destroy him with slander, and let us not heed any of his words."
Attend to me, O the LORD. Listen to what my accusers are saying!
Should evil be repaid with good? For they have laid a trap for my life. Remember how I stood before You to speak good on their behalf, to turn away Your wrath from them.
Therefore hand their children over to famine and deliver them to the sword. Let their wives be bereaved and widowed; let their men be put to death, their young men struck down by the sword in battle.
Let a cry be heard from their houses when You suddenly bring raiders against them, for they have laid a trap to capture me and have hidden traps for my feet.

But You, O the LORD, know all their counsel against me to slay me. Do not pardon their iniquity, nor blot out their sin from Your sight. Let them stumble before You; deal with them in the time of Your anger.
Thus said the the LORD: “Go and purchase an earthen flask from a potter, taking with you some of the elders of the people and some of the elders of the priests.
Go out to the Valley of Ben Hinnom, at the entrance to the Potsherd Gate, and proclaim there the words that I will speak to you.”

Say: “Hear the word of the the LORD, O kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem. Thus says the the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: ‘Behold, I am about to bring disaster upon this place, so that everyone who hears of it will be stunned.

Because they have forsaken Me and have alienated this place, and have burned incense in it to other gods whom neither they nor their fathers nor the kings of Judah have known, and have filled this place with the blood of the innocent.
They have built the high places of Baal, to burn their sons in the fire as burnt offerings to Baal—something I did not command, nor did I speak it, nor did it so much as enter My mind.
Therefore, behold, days are coming, declares the the LORD, when this place will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter.

In this place I will thwart the counsel of Judah and Jerusalem; I will make them fall by the sword before their enemies and by the hand of those who seek to take their lives; and I will give their corpses as food to the birds of heaven and to the beasts of the earth.
I will make this city a desolation and a hissing; everyone who passes by it will be astonished and hiss at all her wounds.

I will make them eat the flesh of their sons and daughters; each will devour the flesh of his neighbor in the siege and distress with which their enemies and those seeking to take their lives will distress them.’”
“Then break the flask before the eyes of the men who go with you.

And say to them, ‘Thus says the the LORD of Hosts: “Just as this flask is broken, so I will break this people and this city, so that it cannot be repaired again. They will bury the dead in Topheth, for there will be no place left to bury them.
Thus I will do to this place and to its inhabitants, declares the the LORD, and I will make this city like Topheth.

The houses of Jerusalem and the houses of the kings of Judah will be unclean, like the place Topheth—all the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to all the host of heaven and poured out drink offerings to other gods.”’”
Then Jeremiah came from Topheth, where the the LORD had sent him to prophesy, and he stood in the court of the house of the the LORD and said to all the people,

“Thus says the the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: ‘Behold, I am bringing upon this city and upon all its towns all the disaster that I have spoken against it, because they have been obstinate and would not listen to My words.’”
When Pashhur the priest, the son of Immer and chief officer in the house of the LORD, heard Jeremiah prophesying all these things,
he had Jeremiah the prophet beaten and put in the stocks at the Upper Gate of Benjamin in the house of the LORD.
The next day Pashhur released Jeremiah from the stocks, and Jeremiah said to him, “The LORD has not called your name Pashhur, but Terror on Every Side.”

For thus says the LORD: “Behold, I am making you a terror to yourself and to all your friends; they will fall by the sword of their enemies while your eyes see it. I will give all Judah into the hand of the king of Babylon; he will carry them captive to Babylon and strike them down with the sword.

I will hand over to their enemies all the wealth of this city—all its products, all its valuables, and all the treasures of the kings of Judah. They will plunder them, seize them, and carry them off to Babylon.
And you, Pashhur, and all who dwell in your house, will go into captivity. You will go to Babylon, and there you will die and be buried—you and all your friends to whom you have prophesied falsely.”
“You deceived me, O the LORD, and I was deceived; You overpowered me and prevailed. I am a laughingstock all day long; everyone mocks me.
For whenever I speak, I cry out and proclaim, ‘Violence and destruction!’ So the word of the LORD has become to me a reproach and derision all day long.
If I say, ‘I will not mention Him or speak any more in His name,’ His word is in my heart like a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I am weary of holding it in, and I cannot.”

“For I have heard the whispering of many: ‘Terror on every side! Denounce him; let us denounce him!’ All my trusted friends watch for my stumbling, saying, ‘Perhaps he will be deceived, so that we may prevail against him and take our revenge on him.’”

“But the LORD is with me like a mighty warrior; therefore my persecutors will stumble and not prevail. They will be utterly put to shame, because they have failed, with an everlasting disgrace that will never be forgotten.
O the LORD of Hosts, who tests the righteous and sees the heart and mind, let me see Your vengeance upon them, for to You I have committed my cause.
Sing to the LORD! Praise the LORD! For He has rescued the life of the needy from the hand of evildoers.”
“Cursed be the day I was born! May the day my mother bore me never be blessed!
Cursed be the man who brought my father the news, saying, ‘A son is born to you!’ and filled him with joy.
May that man be like the cities the LORD overthrew without relenting; may he hear a cry in the morning and an alarm at noon.
For he did not kill me in the womb, so that my mother would have been my grave and her womb pregnant forever.
Why did I come out of the womb to see trouble and sorrow, and to end my days in shame?”
This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD when King Zedekiah sent to him Pashhur son of Malchijah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah. They said,

“Please inquire of the LORD on our behalf, for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon is waging war against us. Perhaps the LORD will perform for us all His wonders, so that Nebuchadnezzar will withdraw from us.”
But Jeremiah answered them, “Tell Zedekiah that

this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I am about to turn against you the weapons of war in your hands, with which you are fighting the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans who besiege you outside the wall. And I will gather them into the center of this city.
And I Myself will fight against you with an outstretched hand and a mighty arm, with anger, wrath, and great fury.
I will strike down the inhabitants of this city, both man and beast; they will die by a severe plague.

After that, declares the LORD, I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, and the people in this city who survive the plague, sword, and famine, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, to their enemies, and to those seeking their lives. He will put them to the sword; he will not spare them, nor have pity, nor have compassion.’”
“And to this people you shall say, ‘This is what the LORD says: See, I set before you the way of life and the way of death.
Whoever stays in this city will die by sword and famine and plague, but whoever goes out and surrenders to the Chaldeans who besiege you will live; he will escape with his life.
For I have set My face against this city for harm and not for good, declares the LORD. It will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.’”
“Moreover, say to the house of the king of Judah, ‘Hear the word of the LORD!

O house of David, this is what the LORD says: Administer justice every morning, and rescue the victim of robbery from the hand of his oppressor, lest My wrath go forth like fire and burn with none to quench it, because of your evil deeds.
Behold, I am against you, O inhabitant of the valley, O rock of the plain, declares the LORD—you who say, “Who can come down against us? Who can enter our dwellings?”
I will punish you as your deeds deserve, declares the LORD. I will kindle a fire in your forest that will consume all around you.’”
Thus says the the LORD: “Go down to the house of the king of Judah and speak this word there:
‘Hear the word of the the LORD, O king of Judah, who sits on the throne of David—you, your servants, and your people who enter these gates.

Thus says the the LORD: Do justice and righteousness, and rescue the robbed from the hand of the oppressor. Do not mistreat or violently oppress the resident alien, the fatherless, or the widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place.
For if you truly do this, then kings who sit on David’s throne will enter the gates of this house, riding in chariots and on horses—they, their servants, and their people.
But if you will not obey these words, I swear by Myself, declares the the LORD, that this house will become a desolation.’”

For thus says the the LORD concerning the house of the king of Judah: “You are like Gilead to Me, like the summit of Lebanon; yet I will surely make you a wilderness, like cities that are not inhabited.
I will appoint destroyers against you, each with his weapons; they will cut down your choicest cedars and cast them into the fire.”
Many nations will pass by this city, and every man will say to his neighbor, “Why has the the LORD done such a thing to this great city?”
And they will answer, “Because they have forsaken the covenant of the the LORD their God and have worshiped and served other gods.”
Do not weep for the dead, nor grieve for him; weep bitterly for the one who goes away, for he will never return or see his native land again.
For thus says the the LORD concerning Shallum son of Josiah, king of Judah, who reigned in place of his father Josiah and who went away from this place: He shall not return here,
but he will die in the place to which they have carried him captive, and he will never see this land again.
Woe to the one who builds his house by unrighteousness and his upper rooms by injustice, who makes his neighbor serve him for nothing and does not give him his wages,
who says, “I will build myself a spacious house with large upper rooms,” and cuts out windows for it, paneling it with cedar and painting it with vermilion.
Do you think you reign because you excel in cedar? Did not your father eat and drink and do justice and righteousness? Then it was well with him.
He judged the cause of the poor and needy; then it was well. Is not this to know Me? declares the the LORD.
But your eyes and heart are set only on your dishonest gain, on shedding innocent blood, and on practicing oppression and violence.

Therefore thus says the the LORD concerning Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: They shall not lament for him, saying, “Alas, my brother!” or “Alas, my sister!” They shall not lament for him, saying, “Alas, lord!” or “Alas, his majesty!”
He will be buried like a donkey—dragged out and thrown beyond the gates of Jerusalem.
Go up to Lebanon and cry out, and lift up your voice in Bashan; cry out from Abarim, for all your lovers have been destroyed.
I spoke to you in your prosperity, but you said, “I will not listen.” This has been your way from your youth, for you have not obeyed My voice.
The wind will sweep away all your shepherds, and your lovers will go into captivity; then you will be ashamed and confounded because of all your evil.
O inhabitant of Lebanon, nested among the cedars, how you will groan when pangs come upon you, pain like that of a woman in labor!
As I live, declares the the LORD, though Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were the signet ring on My right hand, yet I would tear you from there.
I will give you into the hand of those who seek your life, and into the hand of those of whom you are afraid, and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of the Chaldeans.
I will hurl you and the mother who bore you into another country, where you were not born, and there you will die.
They will never return to the land for which they long.
Is this man Coniah a despised, broken pot, a vessel no one wants? Why are he and his children hurled and cast into a land they do not know?
O land, land, land, hear the word of the the LORD!
Thus says the the LORD: Write this man down as childless, a man who will not prosper in his days, for none of his offspring will prosper, sitting on the throne of David or ruling again in Judah.
Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of My pasture! declares the the LORD.

Therefore this is what the the LORD, the God of Israel, says about the shepherds who tend My people: “You have scattered My flock and driven them away, and you have not attended to them. Behold, I will attend to you for the evil of your deeds,” declares the the LORD.
“Then I Myself will gather the remnant of My flock from all the lands to which I have driven them, and I will bring them back to their pasture, where they will be fruitful and multiply.
I will raise up shepherds over them who will tend them, and they will no longer be afraid or dismayed, nor will any go missing,” declares the the LORD.
“Behold, the days are coming,” declares the the LORD, “when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, and He will reign wisely and do justice and righteousness in the land.
In His days Judah will be saved, and Israel will dwell securely. And this is His name by which He will be called: The LORD Our Righteousness.”
“So then, the days are coming,” declares the the LORD, “when they will no longer say, ‘As surely as the the LORD lives, who brought the Israelites up out of the land of Egypt,’

but, ‘As surely as the the LORD lives, who brought and led the descendants of the house of Israel up out of the land of the north and from all the other lands to which I had banished them.’ Then they will dwell in their own land.”
As for the prophets: My heart is broken within me; all my bones tremble. I am like a drunken man, like a man overcome by wine, because of the the LORD and because of His holy words.
For the land is full of adulterers; because of the curse the land mourns; the pastures of the wilderness are withered. Their course is evil, and their might is not right.
“For both prophet and priest are ungodly; even in My house I have found their wickedness,” declares the the LORD.

“Therefore their path will be like slippery paths in the darkness; they will be driven away and fall in it. For I will bring disaster upon them in the year of their punishment,” declares the the LORD.
“I have seen a horrible thing in the prophets of Samaria: They prophesied by Baal and led My people Israel astray.

And among the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen a horrible thing: They commit adultery and walk in falsehood; they strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one turns from his wickedness. They are all like Sodom to Me, and their inhabitants like Gomorrah.”

Therefore this is what the the LORD of Hosts says about the prophets: “I will feed them wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink, because from the prophets of Jerusalem ungodliness has spread throughout the land.”

This is what the the LORD of Hosts says: “Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you. They are filling you with false hopes; they speak visions from their own minds, not from the mouth of the the LORD.”
“They keep saying to those who despise Me, ‘The the LORD says you will have peace,’ and to everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his own heart, ‘No disaster will befall you.’”
“But who has stood in the council of the the LORD to see and hear His word? Who has given heed to His word and obeyed?”
“Behold, the storm of the the LORD has gone forth in wrath, even a whirling tempest; it will swirl about the head of the wicked.
The anger of the the LORD will not turn back until He has fully accomplished the purposes of His heart. In the latter days you will understand it clearly.”
“I did not send these prophets, yet they have run with their message; I did not speak to them, yet they have prophesied.
But if they had stood in My council, they would have proclaimed My words to My people and turned them back from their evil ways and their evil deeds.”
“Am I a God who is only near,” declares the the LORD, “and not a God far away?
Can a man hide in secret places where I cannot see him?” declares the the LORD. “Do I not fill the heavens and the earth?” declares the the LORD.
“I have heard what the prophets are saying who prophesy lies in My name, saying, ‘I had a dream! I had a dream!’
How long will this continue in the hearts of these prophets who prophesy lies, these prophets of deceitful dreams?
They suppose they can make My people forget My name by their dreams, which they recount to one another, just as their fathers forgot My name for Baal.”
“Let the prophet who has a dream retell his dream, but let the one who has My word speak My word truthfully. What does straw have in common with grain?” declares the the LORD.
“Is not My word like fire,” declares the the LORD, “and like a hammer that smashes a rock?”
“Therefore behold, I am against the prophets,” declares the the LORD, “who steal My words from one another.
I am against the prophets,” declares the the LORD, “who wag their own tongues and declare, ‘The the LORD declares.’

I am against the prophets who prophesy false dreams,” declares the the LORD. “They tell them and lead My people astray with their reckless lies, yet I did not send them or command them, and they do not profit these people at all,” declares the the LORD.
“Now when these people or a prophet or priest asks you, ‘What is the oracle of the the LORD?’ you are to tell them, ‘You are the oracle—I will forsake you,’” declares the the LORD.
“As for the prophet or priest or anyone who says, ‘This is the oracle of the the LORD,’ I will punish that man and his household.”
“This is what you are to say to one another and to your brothers: ‘What has the the LORD answered? What has the the LORD spoken?’
But never again use the phrase, ‘The oracle of the the LORD,’ for every man’s own word becomes his oracle, and you have perverted the words of the living God, the the LORD of Hosts, our God.”
“This is what you should ask the prophet: ‘What has the the LORD answered you? What has the the LORD spoken?’

But if you say, ‘The oracle of the the LORD,’ then this is what the the LORD says: ‘Because you have used this phrase, “The oracle of the the LORD,” when I specifically told you not to, I will surely forget you.’
I will surely forget you and cast you out of My presence, both you and the city I gave to you and your fathers.
I will bring upon you everlasting shame and perpetual disgrace that will not be forgotten.”

After Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, into exile—along with the officials of Judah, the craftsmen, and the metalworkers from Jerusalem—and had brought them to Babylon, the LORD showed me two baskets of figs placed before the temple of the LORD.
One basket contained very good figs, like first-ripe figs, but the other contained very bad figs, so spoiled they could not be eaten.
Then the LORD asked me, “What do you see, Jeremiah?” I answered, “Figs—the good ones very good, and the bad ones very bad, so spoiled they cannot be eaten.”
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
“Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Like these good figs, so I will regard with favor the exiles of Judah, whom I have sent away from this place to the land of the Chaldeans.
I will set My eyes on them for good, and I will bring them back to this land. I will build them up and not tear them down; I will plant them and not uproot them.
I will give them a heart to know Me, for I am the LORD. They will be My people, and I will be their God, for they will return to Me with all their heart.”

“But like the bad figs, so spoiled they cannot be eaten,” says the LORD, “so I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, and the remnant of Jerusalem—those remaining in this land and those living in Egypt.
I will make them a horror and an offense to all the kingdoms of the earth, a reproach and a byword, a taunt and a curse in all the places to which I banish them.
I will send against them sword, famine, and plague until they have perished from the land I gave to them and their fathers.”
The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah—the first year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
This is what Jeremiah the prophet said to all the people of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem:

"From the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, until this very day—twenty-three years—the word of the the LORD has come to me, and I have spoken to you again and again, but you have not listened.
And the the LORD has sent to you all His servants the prophets again and again, but you have not listened or inclined your ears to hear."
They said, "Turn now, each of you, from your evil way and deeds, and you can dwell in the land that the the LORD has given to you and your fathers forever and ever.
Do not follow other gods to serve and worship them, and do not provoke Me to anger with the works of your hands. Then I will not harm you."
"But you did not listen to Me," declares the the LORD, "so as to provoke Me to anger with the works of your hands to your own harm."
Therefore this is what the the LORD of Hosts says: "Because you have not obeyed My words,

behold, I will summon all the families of the north," declares the the LORD, "and I will send for My servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and I will bring them against this land and its inhabitants and against all the surrounding nations. I will devote them to destruction and make them an object of horror and scorn, an everlasting desolation.
Moreover, I will banish from them the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of the bride and bridegroom, the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp.
And this whole land will become a desolate wasteland, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon seventy years.

But when seventy years are complete, I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation, the land of the Chaldeans, for their guilt," declares the the LORD, "and I will make it an everlasting desolation.
I will bring upon that land all the words I have pronounced against it, everything written in this book that Jeremiah has prophesied against all the nations.
For many nations and great kings will enslave them, and I will repay them according to their deeds and the work of their hands."
For this is what the the LORD, the God of Israel, said to me: "Take from My hand this cup of the wine of wrath, and make all the nations to whom I send you drink it.
And they will drink and stagger and go mad because of the sword that I will send among them."
So I took the cup from the the LORD's hand and made all the nations drink it, to whom the the LORD had sent me:
Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, its kings and officials, to make them a desolation, an object of horror and scorn, and a curse, as they are this day;
Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his officials, his people,
and all the mixed tribes; all the kings of the land of Uz; all the kings of the land of the Philistines—Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and the remnant of Ashdod;
all the kings of Tyre and Sidon; the kings of the coastlands across the sea;
Dedan, Tema, Buz, and all who cut the corners of their hair;
all the kings of Arabia and all the kings of the mixed tribes who dwell in the desert;
all the kings of Zimri, Elam, and Media;
all the kings of the north, near and far, one after another, and all the other kingdoms of the earth. And after all of them, the king of Sheshach will drink it too.
Then you are to tell them that this is what the the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: "Drink, get drunk, and vomit; fall and rise no more, because of the sword I will send among you."
If they refuse to take the cup from your hand to drink, then you are to tell them that this is what the the LORD of Hosts says: "You must drink it!

For behold, I am beginning to bring disaster on the city that bears My name, and do you think you will go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, for I am summoning a sword against all the inhabitants of the earth," declares the the LORD of Hosts.

"Now as for you, prophesy all these words to them and say to them that the the LORD will roar from on high; He will raise His voice from His holy dwelling. He will roar loudly over His pasture; He will shout like those who tread the grapes against all the inhabitants of the earth.

The tumult will resound to the ends of the earth, because the the LORD has an indictment against the nations; He will execute judgment on all mankind; He will put the wicked to the sword," declares the the LORD.
This is what the the LORD of Hosts says: "Behold, disaster is going out from nation to nation; a great storm is being stirred up from the farthest ends of the earth."
Those slain by the the LORD on that day will be spread from one end of the earth to the other. They will not be mourned, gathered, or buried; they will be like dung on the face of the ground.
Wail, you shepherds, and cry out; roll in the dust, you leaders of the flock, for the days of your slaughter have come, and you will be shattered like a precious vessel.
Flight will elude the shepherds, and escape will elude the leaders of the flock.
Hear the sound of the shepherds' cries and the wails of the leaders of the flock, for the the LORD is destroying their pasture.
The peaceful pastures will become desolate because of the fierce anger of the the LORD.
Like a lion He has left His den, for their land has become a desolation because of the wrath of the oppressor and because of His fierce anger.
At the commencement of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this message came from the LORD:

“This is what the LORD says: Stand in the courtyard of the LORD’s house and speak to all the cities of Judah that come to worship in the LORD’s house; deliver every word that I command you to speak to them, and do not omit a single word.
Perhaps they will listen and turn back—each from his wicked way—so that I may relent concerning the disaster I am planning to bring upon them because of the wickedness of their deeds.
And you are to say to them, ‘This is what the LORD says: If you do not listen to Me and walk in My law, which I have set before you,
and if you do not heed the words of My servants the prophets, whom I have been sending to you again and again—though you have not listened—
then I will make this house like Shiloh, and I will make this city an object of cursing among all the nations of the earth.’”
Now the priests, the prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the house of the LORD.
And when Jeremiah had finished speaking all that the LORD had commanded him to say to all the people, the priests, the prophets, and all the people seized him, crying, “You must die!”

“Why have you prophesied in the name of the LORD, declaring that this house will be like Shiloh and this city will be laid waste and uninhabited?” And all the people gathered around Jeremiah in the house of the LORD.
When the officials of Judah heard of these things, they came up from the king’s palace to the house of the LORD and sat at the entrance of the New Gate of the LORD’s house.
Then the priests and prophets said to the officials and all the people, “This man deserves to die, for he has prophesied against this city, as you have heard with your own ears.”
Then Jeremiah said to all the officials and all the people, “The LORD sent me to prophesy against this house and against this city all the words that you have heard.
So now, amend your ways and your deeds, and obey the voice of the LORD your God, so that He may relent concerning the disaster He has pronounced against you.
As for me, I am in your hands; do with me whatever you think is good and right.

But know for certain that if you put me to death, you will bring innocent blood upon yourselves, upon this city, and upon its inhabitants; for in truth the LORD has sent me to speak all these words in your hearing.”
Then the officials and all the people said to the priests and prophets, “This man does not deserve to die, for he has spoken to us in the name of the LORD our God.”
Some of the elders of the land then rose and said to the whole assembly, “

Micah the Moreshite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, saying, ‘This is what the LORD of Hosts says: Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become a heap of ruins, and the temple mount will become a forested hill.’

Did Hezekiah king of Judah or anyone in Judah put him to death? Did they not fear the LORD and implore His favor, so that the LORD relented concerning the disaster He had pronounced against them? Yet we are bringing a great evil upon ourselves.”

Moreover, there was a man named Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim who prophesied in the name of the LORD; he prophesied against this city and against this land in accordance with all the words of Jeremiah.
When King Jehoiakim and all his mighty men and officials heard his words, the king sought to put him to death; but when Uriah heard of it, he was afraid and fled to Egypt.
Then King Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt—Elnathan son of Achbor, along with some other men.
They brought Uriah out of Egypt and delivered him to King Jehoiakim, who struck him down with the sword and cast his corpse into the burial place of the common people.
Nevertheless, Ahikam son of Shaphan supported Jeremiah, so that he was not handed over to the people to be put to death.
In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
“Thus says the LORD to me: ‘Make for yourself bonds and yokes and put them on your neck,

and send them to the king of Edom, to the king of Moab, to the king of the Ammonites, to the king of Tyre, and to the king of Sidon by the hand of the messengers who come to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah.
Command them to go to their masters, saying, “Thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: ‘Thus you shall say to your masters,
“I have made the earth, the people, and the beasts that are on the face of the earth by My great power and by My outstretched arm, and I will give it to the one who is pleasing in My sight.
Now I have given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, My servant, and I have given him also the beasts of the field to serve him.
All the nations shall serve him, his son, and his grandson, until the time for his own land comes; then many nations and great kings will make him their servant.

It shall be that the nation or kingdom that will not serve him—Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon—and that will not put its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, I will punish that nation with the sword, with famine, and with pestilence,” declares the LORD, “until I have destroyed it by his hand.”’”’”
“But as for you, do not listen to your prophets, your diviners, your dreamers, your soothsayers, or your sorcerers who speak to you, saying, ‘You will not serve the king of Babylon.’
For they prophesy a lie to you in order to remove you far from your land; and I will drive you out and you will perish.
But the nation that will bring its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serve him, I will let remain on its land,” declares the LORD, “and they will till it and dwell in it.”
I spoke words like these to Zedekiah king of Judah, saying, “Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serve him and his people, and live!
Why will you die, you and your people, by the sword, famine, and pestilence, as the LORD has spoken concerning the nation that will not serve the king of Babylon?
So do not listen to the words of the prophets who speak to you, saying, ‘You will not serve the king of Babylon,’ for they prophesy a lie to you.
