For I have not sent them,” declares the LORD, “but they prophesy falsely in My name, in order that I may drive you out and that you may perish, you and the prophets who prophesy to you.”

Then I spoke to the priests and to all this people, saying, “Thus says the LORD: ‘Do not listen to the words of your prophets who prophesy to you, saying, “Behold, the vessels of the LORD’s house will now shortly be brought again from Babylon,” for they prophesy a lie to you.
Do not listen to them; serve the king of Babylon, and live! Why should this city become a ruin?

But if they are prophets, and if the word of the LORD is with them, let them now entreat the LORD of hosts that the vessels which are left in the house of the LORD, in the house of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem, may not go to Babylon.’”
For thus says the LORD of hosts concerning the pillars, concerning the sea, concerning the stands, and concerning the rest of the vessels that are left in this city,
which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon did not take when he carried into exile Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, from Jerusalem to Babylon, along with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem.
Yes, thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, concerning the vessels that are left in the house of the LORD and in the house of the king of Judah and in Jerusalem:
“They will be carried to Babylon and will be there until the day I visit them,” declares the LORD. “Then I will bring them up and restore them to this place.”

In the fifth month of that year—the fourth year, early in the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah—the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur, from Gibeon, said to me in the house of the LORD before the priests and all the people:
"Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: 'I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Within two years I will bring back to this place all the vessels of the house of the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took from here and carried to Babylon.
I will also bring back to this place Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah and all the exiles of Judah who went to Babylon, declares the LORD, for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.'"
Then the prophet Jeremiah replied to the prophet Hananiah in the presence of the priests and all the people standing in the house of the LORD:
"Amen! May the LORD do so. May the LORD fulfill your words, which you have prophesied, and bring back the vessels of the house of the LORD and all the exiles from Babylon to this place.
But listen now to this word that I am speaking in your hearing and in the hearing of all the people.
The prophets who preceded us from ancient times prophesied against many lands and great kingdoms, foretelling war, disaster, and plague.
As for the prophet who prophesies peace, his words will prove true only when they come to pass; then it will be known that the LORD has truly sent him."
Then the prophet Hananiah took the yoke from Jeremiah's neck and broke it.

In the presence of all the people, Hananiah declared, "Thus says the LORD: 'In this same way, within two years, I will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the neck of all the nations.'" Then Jeremiah the prophet went on his way.
After the prophet Hananiah had broken the yoke from Jeremiah's neck, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
"Go and tell Hananiah, 'Thus says the LORD: You have broken the wooden yokes, but you have made iron yokes in their place.'

For thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: 'I have put an iron yoke on the neck of all these nations, that they may serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and they will serve him; I have even given him the beasts of the field.'"
Then the prophet Jeremiah said to the prophet Hananiah, "Listen, Hananiah! The LORD has not sent you, and you have made this people trust in a lie.
Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am about to remove you from the face of the earth. This very year you will die, because you have spoken rebellion against the LORD."
And in the seventh month of that year, the prophet Hananiah died.

These are the words of the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the rest of the elders of the exile, to the priests, to the prophets, and to all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from Jerusalem to Babylon—
after King Jeconiah, the queen mother, the eunuchs, the officials of Judah and Jerusalem, the craftsmen, and the metalworkers had departed from Jerusalem.
He sent it by the hand of Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Babylon, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, with this message:
Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, to all the exiles whom I have carried away from Jerusalem to Babylon:
Build houses and live in them; plant gardens and eat their fruit.
Take wives and have sons and daughters; take wives for your sons and give your daughters to men, that they may bear sons and daughters. Multiply there, and do not decrease.
Seek the peace of the city to which I have carried you away, and pray to the LORD for it, for in its peace you will have peace.
For thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Do not let your prophets and your diviners who are among you deceive you, and do not listen to the dreams that you dream.
For they prophesy falsely to you in My name; I have not sent them, declares the LORD.
For thus says the LORD: When seventy years have been completed for Babylon, I will attend to you and fulfill My good word to you, to bring you back to this place.
For I know the plans that I have for you, declares the LORD, plans for welfare and not for harm, to give you a future and a hope.
Then you will call upon Me and come and pray to Me, and I will hear you.
You will seek Me and find Me when you seek Me with all your heart.

I will be found by you, declares the LORD, and I will restore your fortunes and gather you from all the nations and all the places where I have driven you, declares the LORD, and I will bring you back to the place from which I exiled you.
Because you have said, "The LORD has raised up prophets for us in Babylon,"
for thus says the LORD concerning the king who sits on David's throne and concerning all the people who dwell in this city—your brothers who did not go out with you into exile:
Behold, I am sending against them sword, famine, and pestilence, and I will make them like rotten figs, too bad to be eaten.

I will pursue them with sword, famine, and pestilence, and I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, a curse, a desolation, a hissing, and a reproach among all the nations where I have driven them,
because they did not listen to My words, declares the LORD, which I sent to them persistently by My servants the prophets, but you did not listen, declares the LORD.
Hear the word of the LORD, all you exiles whom I sent from Jerusalem to Babylon.

Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, concerning Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who prophesy falsely to you in My name: Behold, I will deliver them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will strike them down before your eyes.
Because of them, all the exiles of Judah who are in Babylon will take up a curse, saying, "May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon burned in the fire."

Because they have done a disgraceful thing in Israel, have committed adultery with their neighbors' wives, and have spoken a false word in My name that I did not command them; and I am the One who knows and bears witness, declares the LORD.
And you shall say to Shemaiah the Nehelamite:
"Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Because you sent letters in your name to all the people who are in Jerusalem, to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests, saying,

'The LORD has appointed you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to be an officer in the house of the LORD over every man who is mad and prophesies, that you may put him in the stocks and in neck irons.
Now why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who prophesies to you?
For he has sent to us in Babylon, saying, "The exile will be long; build houses and live in them, and plant gardens and eat their fruit." ' "
Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the hearing of Jeremiah the prophet.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,
"Send to all the exiles, saying, 'Thus says the LORD concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Because Shemaiah has prophesied to you, though I did not send him, and has made you trust in a lie,

therefore thus says the LORD: Behold, I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants. He shall not have a man dwelling among this people, and he shall not see the good that I will do for My people, declares the LORD, because he has spoken rebellion against the LORD.' "
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying:
This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: "Write in a book all the words I have spoken to you.

For behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will restore the prosperity of My people Israel and Judah," declares the LORD, "and I will bring them back to the land I gave their fathers, and they will possess it."
These are the words the LORD spoke concerning Israel and Judah.
For thus says the LORD: "We have heard a cry of terror, of fear, and of no peace.
Ask now, and see: Can a man give birth? Why then do I see every man with his hands on his loins like a woman in labor, and every face drained of color?
Alas, that day is so great that none is like it; it is a time of distress for Jacob, yet he will be saved out of it."
"And in that day," declares the LORD of Hosts, "I will break the yoke from your neck and snap your bonds, so that foreigners will no longer enslave him.
Instead, they will serve the LORD their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them."

"So do not fear, O Jacob My servant," declares the LORD, "and do not be dismayed, O Israel; for behold, I will save you from afar, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob shall return and be tranquil and secure, with no one to terrify him.

For I am with you to save you," declares the LORD, "For I will make a complete end of all the nations among whom I scattered you, but I will not make a complete end of you; yet I will discipline you justly, and I will by no means leave you unpunished."
For thus says the LORD: "Your injury is incurable; your wound is severe.
There is no one to plead your case, no remedy to heal your wound; there is no recovery for you.

All your allies have forgotten you; they do not seek you. For I have struck you with an enemy's blow, with the discipline of a cruel oppressor, because of the greatness of your iniquity; your sins have increased.
Why do you cry out over your injury? Your pain is incurable. Because of the greatness of your iniquity and your many sins, I have done these things to you.

Therefore all who devour you shall be devoured, and all your adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity; those who plunder you shall be plundered, and all who prey upon you I will give as plunder.
For I will restore health to you and heal you of your wounds, declares the LORD, because they have called you an outcast, saying, 'This is Zion, whom no one cares for.'"

Thus says the LORD: "Behold, I will restore the prosperity of Jacob's tents and have compassion on his dwellings; the city shall be rebuilt on its mound, and the palace shall remain on its proper site.
From them shall come thanksgiving and the sound of those who celebrate; I will multiply them, and they shall not be diminished; I will honor them, and they shall not be lightly esteemed.
Their children shall be as in former days, and their congregation shall be established before Me; and I will punish all their oppressors.

Their leader shall be one of their own, and their ruler shall come forth from their midst; I will bring him near, and he shall approach Me. For who is the one who would devote his heart to approach Me? declares the LORD.
And you shall be My people, and I will be your God."
Behold, the storm of the LORD has gone forth in fury, a sweeping whirlwind; it will burst upon the head of the wicked.
The fierce anger of the LORD will not turn back until He has accomplished and established the intentions of His heart. In the latter days you will understand this.
“At that time,” declares the LORD, “I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and they will be My people.”
This is what the LORD says: “The people who survived the sword found favor in the wilderness when Israel went to find rest.”
The LORD appeared to me from afar: “I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have drawn you with loving devotion.”
“I will build you up again, O Virgin Israel. You will again take up your tambourines and go out in joyful dancing.
Again you will plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria; the farmers will plant and enjoy the fruit.”
For there will be a day when watchmen will call out on the hills of Ephraim: “Arise, let us go up to Zion, to the LORD our God.”
For this is what the LORD says: “Sing with joy for Jacob; shout among the chief of the nations. Make your praises heard and say, ‘O LORD, save Your people, the remnant of Israel.’”

“Behold, I will bring them from the land of the north and gather them from the ends of the earth. Among them will be the blind and the lame, the pregnant woman and the woman in labor; together they will return here.

They will come with weeping, and with consolations I will lead them; I will make them walk beside streams of water, on a level path where they will not stumble. For I am Israel's Father, and Ephraim is My firstborn.”
Hear the word of the LORD, O nations, and proclaim it to the distant coastlands: “The One who scattered Israel will gather them and keep them as a shepherd keeps his flock.”
For the LORD has ransomed Jacob and redeemed him from the hand that was stronger than he.

They will come and shout for joy on the heights of Zion; they will be radiant over the bounty of the LORD— the grain, the new wine, the oil, and the young of the flocks and herds. Their soul will be like a well-watered garden, and they will not languish anymore.
“Then the virgin will rejoice in the dance, young men and old as well. I will turn their mourning into joy and give them comfort and joy for their sorrow.
I will fill the priests with abundance, and My people will be satisfied with My goodness,” declares the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: “A voice is heard in Ramah, mourning and great weeping, Rachel weeping for her children, refusing to be comforted, because they are no more.”
This is what the LORD says: “Restrain your voice from weeping and your eyes from tears, for your labor will be rewarded,” declares the LORD. “They will return from the land of the enemy.”
“There is hope for your future,” declares the LORD. “Your children will return to their own territory.”
“I have surely heard Ephraim's moaning: ‘You disciplined me, and I was disciplined like an untrained calf. Restore me, and I will return, for You are the LORD my God.
After I turned away, I repented; and after I was instructed, I struck my thigh in grief. I was ashamed and humiliated because I bore the disgrace of my youth.’”

“Is not Ephraim a precious son to Me, a delightful child? Though I often speak against him, I still remember him. Therefore My heart yearns for him; I have great compassion for him,” declares the LORD.
“Set up road markers for yourself; make signposts. Consider well the path you have traveled. Return, O Virgin Israel, return to these cities of yours.”
“How long will you wander, O faithless daughter? For the LORD has created a new thing on the earth: a woman will embrace a man.”

This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “When I restore their fortunes, they will once again speak this word in the land of Judah and in its cities: ‘The LORD bless you, O righteous dwelling, O holy mountain!’
And Judah and all its cities will dwell together there, the farmers and those who move with the flocks.”
“For I will refresh the weary soul, and replenish every languishing soul.”
At this I awoke and looked around. My sleep had been pleasant to me.
“Behold, the days are coming,” declares the LORD, “when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man and the seed of beast.
Just as I watched over them to uproot and tear down, to destroy and demolish, and to bring disaster, so will I watch over them to build and to plant,” declares the LORD.
“In those days, it will no longer be said: ‘The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.’
Instead, everyone will die for his own iniquity; whoever eats the sour grapes will bear the consequences himself.”
“Behold, the days are coming,” declares the LORD, “when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah—
“not like the covenant I made with their fathers when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, a covenant which they broke, though I was a husband to them,” declares the LORD.

“But this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days,” declares the LORD: “I will put My law within them and write it on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they will be My people.

“No longer will a man teach his neighbor or a man his brother, saying, ‘Know the LORD,’ for they will all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest,” declares the LORD. “For I will forgive their iniquity and remember their sins no more.”

This is what the LORD says: “He who gives the sun for light by day, who sets in order the moon and stars for light by night, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar— the LORD of Hosts is His name—”
“If these fixed laws were to cease from My presence,” declares the LORD, “then the descendants of Israel would also cease to be a nation before Me for all time.”

This is what the LORD says: “If the heavens above could be measured and the foundations of the earth below could be searched out, then I would also reject all the descendants of Israel because of all they have done,” declares the LORD.
“Behold, the days are coming,” declares the LORD, “when the city will be rebuilt for the LORD from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
“The measuring line will go out straight to the hill of Gareb and then turn toward Goah.

“And the whole valley of the dead bodies and ashes, and all the fields as far as the Kidron Valley, to the corner of the Horse Gate toward the east, will be holy to the LORD. It will never again be uprooted or demolished.”
This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
At that time the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was confined in the courtyard of the guard in the palace of the king of Judah.
Zedekiah king of Judah had imprisoned him, saying, "Why do you prophesy as you do, saying, 'The LORD says: I am about to give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.
Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape the hand of the Chaldeans, but he will surely be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will speak with him face to face and see him eye to eye.
He will take Zedekiah to Babylon, where he will remain until I attend to him, declares the LORD. If you fight against the Chaldeans, you will not succeed.'"
Jeremiah said, "The word of the LORD came to me, saying:
'Behold, Hanamel, son of your uncle Shallum, is coming to you to say, "Buy for yourself my field in Anathoth, for the right of redemption is yours to buy it."'

Then, in accordance with the word of the LORD, my cousin Hanamel came to me in the courtyard of the guard and said to me, 'Please buy my field in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin, for the right of inheritance and redemption is yours. Buy it for yourself.' Then I knew that this was the word of the LORD."
So I bought the field in Anathoth from my cousin Hanamel and weighed out to him seventeen shekels of silver.
I signed and sealed the deed, called in witnesses, and weighed out the silver on the scales.
Then I took the deed of purchase—the sealed copy with its terms and conditions, as well as the unsealed copy—

and I gave the deed to Baruch son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, in the presence of my cousin Hanamel and of the witnesses who signed the deed, and in the presence of all the Jews sitting in the courtyard of the guard.
In their presence I charged Baruch, saying, "Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel:
'Take these deeds—both the sealed copy and the unsealed copy of the purchase deed—and put them in a clay jar, so they will last a long time.
For this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: Houses, fields, and vineyards will again be bought in this land.'"
After I had given the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to the LORD:
"Ah, Lord the LORD, You have made the heavens and the earth by Your great power and outstretched arm; nothing is too difficult for You.
You show loving devotion to thousands, but You repay the iniquity of the fathers into the lap of their children after them—O great and mighty God, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.
Great in counsel and mighty in deed, Your eyes are open to all the ways of the sons of men, to give to each man according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds.
You performed signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, and to this day, both in Israel and among mankind, You have made a name for Yourself, as it is this day.
You brought Your people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and with great terror.
You gave them this land, which You had sworn to give their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey." "
They came in and took possession of it, but they did not obey Your voice or walk in Your law. They did not do all that You commanded them to do, so You brought upon them all this disaster.

See, the siege ramps have reached the city to capture it, and the city has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans who fight against it, because of the sword, famine, and plague. What You have spoken has come to pass, and behold, You see it.
Yet You, Lord the LORD, have said to me, 'Buy the field for silver and call in witnesses,' even though the city has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans."
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying, "
Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh. Is anything too difficult for Me?
Therefore thus says the LORD: 'Behold, I am giving this city into the hand of the Chaldeans and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

The Chaldeans who fight against this city will come and set it on fire and burn it down, along with the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to Baal and poured out drink offerings to other gods, in order to provoke Me.

For the children of Israel and the children of Judah have done only evil in My sight from their youth; indeed, the children of Israel have done nothing but provoke Me by the work of their hands, declares the LORD.
This city has been a cause of My anger and wrath from the day they built it until this day, so I will remove it from My sight,

because of all the evil of the children of Israel and the children of Judah, which they have done to provoke Me—their kings, their officials, their priests, their prophets, and the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
They turned away from Me, not toward Me; though I taught them again and again, they would not listen or accept correction.
They set up their abominations in the house that is called by My name, to defile it.

They built the high places of Baal in the Valley of Ben Hinnom to make their sons and daughters pass through the fire to Molech—something I did not command them, nor did it enter My mind that they should do such an abomination, causing Judah to sin.'"
"Now therefore, thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, concerning this city, of which you say, 'It has been given into the hand of the king of Babylon by sword, famine, and plague':
'Behold, I will gather them from all the lands to which I have driven them in My anger and wrath and great indignation, and I will bring them back to this place and make them dwell in safety.
They will be My people, and I will be their God.
I will give them one heart and one way, that they may fear Me forever, for their good and for the good of their children after them.
I will make an everlasting covenant with them, that I will not turn away from doing good to them; and I will put My fear in their hearts, so that they will not depart from Me.'"
"I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land in truth, with all My heart and with all My soul.
For thus says the LORD: 'Just as I have brought all this great disaster upon this people, so I will bring upon them all the good that I have promised them.
Fields will be bought in this land of which you say, "It is desolate, without man or beast; it has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans."

Men will buy fields for silver, sign and seal the deeds, and call in witnesses in the land of Benjamin, in the places around Jerusalem, in the cities of Judah, in the cities of the hill country, in the cities of the lowland, and in the cities of the Negev; for I will restore their fortunes, declares the LORD.'"
While Jeremiah was still confined in the courtyard of the guard, the word of the LORD came to him a second time:
"Thus says the LORD, who made the earth, the LORD who formed it and established it—the LORD is His name—"
"Call to Me, and I will answer you, and I will tell you great and hidden things that you do not know."

"For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about the houses of this city and the palaces of the kings of Judah that have been torn down to make defenses against the siege ramps and the sword:

The Chaldeans are coming to fight and to fill those houses with the dead bodies of the people whom I will strike down in My anger and wrath, because I have hidden My face from this city on account of all its wickedness.
"Nevertheless, I will bring health and healing to it; I will heal them and reveal to them an abundance of peace and truth.
I will restore Judah and Israel from captivity and rebuild them as they were at first.
I will cleanse them from all the iniquity by which they have sinned against Me, and I will pardon all their iniquities by which they have sinned against Me and rebelled against Me.

Then this city will bring Me renown, joy, praise, and glory before all the nations of the earth who hear of all the good that I do for them; they will tremble and quake at all the good and all the prosperity that I provide for it."

"This is what the LORD says: In this place, which you say is a wasteland without man or beast—in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem that are desolate, without inhabitant, without man, and without beast—there will again be heard

the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, and the voices of those who bring thank offerings to the house of the LORD, saying, 'Give thanks to the LORD of Hosts, for the LORD is good; His steadfast love endures forever.' For I will restore the land from captivity as it was at first," says the LORD.
"This is what the LORD of Hosts says: In this desolate place, without man or beast, and in all its cities, there will again be pastures for shepherds resting their flocks.

In the cities of the hill country, the cities of the foothills, the cities of the Negev, the land of Benjamin, the outskirts of Jerusalem, and the cities of Judah, the flocks will again be counted," says the LORD.
"The days are coming," declares the LORD, "when I will fulfill the gracious promise I made concerning the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
In those days and at that time I will cause a righteous Branch to sprout for David, and He will execute justice and righteousness in the land.
In those days Judah will be saved, and Jerusalem will dwell in safety, and this is the name by which it will be called: The LORD Our Righteousness."
"For this is what the LORD says: David will never lack a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel,
and the Levitical priests will never lack a man before Me to offer burnt offerings, to burn grain offerings, and to make sacrifices."
And the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,
"This is what the LORD says: If you can break My covenant with the day and My covenant with the night, so that day and night no longer come at their appointed time,
then My covenant with David My servant may be broken, and with the Levitical priests My ministers, so that David will not have a descendant to reign on his throne.
As the host of heaven cannot be counted and the sand of the sea cannot be measured, so I will multiply the offspring of David My servant and the Levites who minister to Me."
And the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,
"Have you not noticed what these people are saying: 'The LORD has rejected the two families that He chose'? Thus they despise My people and no longer regard them as a nation.
This is what the LORD says: If I have not established My covenant with day and night and the fixed order of heaven and earth,

then I would reject the descendants of Jacob and of David My servant, and I would not choose a ruler from the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. For I will restore them from captivity and have compassion on them."

The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, together with all his army, all the kingdoms of the earth under his dominion, and all the peoples, were waging war against Jerusalem and all its cities:

The LORD, the God of Israel, said, "Go and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah and tell him, 'This is what the LORD says: Behold, I am about to hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.
And you will not escape from his hand but will surely be captured and handed over to him. You will see the king of Babylon eye to eye and speak with him face to face, and you will go to Babylon.
Yet hear the word of the LORD, O Zedekiah king of Judah. This is what the LORD says concerning you: You will not die by the sword;

you will die in peace. As spices were burned for your fathers, the former kings who preceded you, so a fire will be kindled for you, and they will lament, 'Alas, O master!' For I have spoken this word, declares the LORD.'"
Then Jeremiah the prophet proclaimed all these words to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem,
while the Babylonian army was besieging Jerusalem and every remaining city of Judah—Lachish and Azekah—because those were the only fortified cities still left in Judah.
After King Zedekiah had covenanted with all the people in Jerusalem to proclaim liberty,
so that each man would release his Hebrew slaves, both male and female, and no one would keep a fellow Hebrew in bondage,
all the officials and all the people who entered into the covenant consented to free their male and female slaves and to hold them in bondage no longer. They heeded the agreement and set them free.
But afterward they reversed course and re-enslaved the men and women they had released.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying,
"Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I established a covenant with your ancestors when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage, instructing them that

at the end of seven years each of you must release his fellow Hebrew who has sold himself to you. He may serve you six years, and then you must send him away free. But your ancestors neither listened nor inclined their ears.
Recently you repented and did what was right in My sight by proclaiming freedom to one another, and you ratified a covenant before Me in the house called by My name.
But then you turned back and desecrated My name. Each of you reclaimed the male and female slaves you had released to go wherever they pleased, and you subdued them into slavery again.

"Therefore this is what the LORD says: You have not obeyed Me; you have not proclaimed freedom to your brothers and neighbors. So now I proclaim freedom for you, declares the LORD—freedom to the sword, to pestilence, and to famine! I will make you a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
And those who violated My covenant and failed to uphold the terms of the covenant they made before Me, I will treat like the calf they cut in two, walking between its pieces.
The officials of Judah and Jerusalem, the court officials, the priests, and all the people of the land who passed between the pieces of the calf,
I will deliver into the hands of their enemies, into the hands of those who seek their lives. Their corpses will become food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.

And Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials I will deliver into the hands of their enemies, into the hands of those who seek their lives, and into the hand of the Babylonian army, which has withdrawn from you.

Behold, I will issue a command, declares the LORD, and I will bring them back to this city; they will fight against it, capture it, and burn it with fire. And I will devastate the cities of Judah so that no one can dwell there."
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying,
“Go to the house of the Rechabites and speak to them, and bring them to one of the chambers of the house of the LORD, and give them wine to drink.”
So I took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah, son of Habazziniah, and his brothers and all his sons and the whole house of the Rechabites,

and I brought them into the house of the LORD, to the chamber of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God, which was beside the chamber of the officials, above the chamber of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the keeper of the threshold.
Then I set before the sons of the house of the Rechabites pitchers full of wine and cups, and said to them, “Drink wine.”

But they said, “We will not drink wine, for our father Jonadab son of Rechab commanded us, saying, ‘You and your sons must never drink wine. Moreover, you shall not build a house, sow seed, or plant a vineyard, nor shall any of these belong to you; but you shall dwell in tents all your days, that you may live many days on the face of the earth where you sojourn.’
So we have obeyed the voice of our father Jonadab son of Rechab in all that he commanded us, not to drink wine all our days—we, our wives, our sons, and our daughters—
and not to build houses for us to dwell in, and we have no vineyard or field or seed.
But we have dwelt in tents and have obeyed and done according to all that our father Jonadab commanded us.

But when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against the land, we said, ‘Come, let us go to Jerusalem because of the army of the Chaldeans and the army of the Arameans.’ So we have been dwelling in Jerusalem.”
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,
“Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Go and say to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, ‘Will you not receive instruction to listen to My words?’ declares the LORD.”

“The words of Jonadab son of Rechab, which he commanded his sons not to drink wine, have been kept; they have not drunk to this day, because they obeyed their father’s command. But I have spoken to you again and again, and you have not listened to Me.

I have also sent to you all My servants the prophets, again and again, saying, ‘Turn now, every one of you, from his evil way, and amend your deeds, and do not go after other gods to serve them, and you shall dwell in the land that I gave to you and your fathers.’ But you have not inclined your ear or listened to Me.
Because the sons of Jonadab son of Rechab have kept the command of their father that he commanded them, but this people has not listened to Me.”

“Therefore thus says the LORD God of Hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I am bringing upon Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the disaster that I have spoken against them, because I spoke to them and they did not listen, and I called to them and they did not answer.”

And Jeremiah said to the house of the Rechabites, “Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Because you have obeyed the command of your father Jonadab and kept all his commands and done according to all that he commanded you,
therefore thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Jonadab son of Rechab will never fail to have a man to stand before Me.”
In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this proclamation came to Jeremiah from the the LORD:
"Take a scroll and inscribe upon it all the words I have spoken to you concerning Israel, Judah, and all the nations—from the day I first addressed you, in the days of Josiah, until this very day.
Perhaps the people of Judah will heed all the calamity I intend to inflict upon them, so that each may turn from his wicked course. Then I will forgive their iniquity and their sin."
Accordingly, Jeremiah summoned Baruch son of Neriah, and while Jeremiah dictated, Baruch inscribed upon a scroll all the words the the LORD had spoken to him.
"I am confined; I cannot enter the temple of the the LORD.

Therefore, you must go to the the LORD's house on a day of fasting and read aloud to the people at the temple the words of the the LORD from the scroll you wrote at my dictation. Read them also to all the people of Judah who come from their towns.
Perhaps their supplication will find favor before the the LORD, and each will turn from his wicked course; for great is the anger and wrath the the LORD has pronounced against these people."
Baruch son of Neriah carried out everything Jeremiah the prophet commanded; he read the words of the the LORD from the scroll in the the LORD's house.

In the ninth month of the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, a fast was proclaimed before the the LORD for all the people in Jerusalem and for all those arriving from the towns of Judah.

From the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court at the entrance of the New Gate of the the LORD's house, Baruch read from the scroll the words of Jeremiah in the hearing of all the people.
When Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan heard all the words of the the LORD from the scroll,

he descended to the scribe's chamber in the king's palace, where all the officials were seated: Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Akbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the other officials.
Micaiah reported to them everything he had heard Baruch read from the scroll to the people.

Then all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah son of Shelemiah son of Cushi to Baruch, saying, "Bring the scroll you have read to the people, and come." So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and went to them.
They said to him, "Sit down, please, and read it to us." So Baruch read it to them.
When they heard all the words, they looked at one another in alarm and said to Baruch, "We must surely report all these words to the king."
Then they asked Baruch, "Tell us, how did you write all these words? Did Jeremiah dictate them to you?"
Baruch answered them, "He dictated all these words to me, and I wrote them with ink on the scroll."
The officials said to Baruch, "You and Jeremiah, go and hide; do not let anyone know where you are."
After they had deposited the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, they went to the king in the courtyard and reported everything to him.
The king sent Jehudi to retrieve the scroll, and he brought it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe and read it to the king and to all the officials standing beside him.
It was the ninth month, and the king was sitting in the winter house, with a fire burning in the brazier before him.
Whenever Jehudi had read three or four columns, the king cut them off with a scribe's knife and cast them into the fire in the brazier, until the entire scroll was consumed by the flames.
The king and all his attendants who heard all these words were not afraid, nor did they tear their garments.
Even though Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll, he would not listen to them.
Instead, the king commanded Jerahmeel, a son of the king, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet; but the the LORD had hidden them.
After the king had burned the scroll containing the words Baruch had written at Jeremiah's dictation, the word of the the LORD came to Jeremiah:
"Take another scroll and inscribe upon it all the former words that were on the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.

Tell Jehoiakim king of Judah, 'This is what the the LORD says: You burned this scroll and said, "Why did you write on it that the king of Babylon will certainly come and destroy this land and remove from it both man and beast?"

Therefore this is what the the LORD says about Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no one to sit on the throne of David, and his dead body will be cast out to the heat by day and to the frost by night.

I will punish him, his offspring, and his attendants for their iniquity; I will bring on them and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem and the people of Judah every disaster I have pronounced against them, because they did not listen.'"

Then Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to the scribe Baruch son of Neriah, and as Jeremiah dictated, Baruch wrote on it all the words of the scroll that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire. And many similar words were added to them.
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, appointed Zedekiah son of Josiah to reign over Judah in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim.
Yet neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land obeyed the words of the LORD, which He had spoken through Jeremiah the prophet.
Nevertheless, King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah the prophet, saying, “Please pray to the LORD our God on our behalf.”
At that time Jeremiah was free to come and go among the people, for they had not yet imprisoned him.
Meanwhile, Pharaoh's army had marched out of Egypt, and when the Chaldeans besieging Jerusalem heard the report, they withdrew from the city.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet:
“This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Tell the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of Me, that Pharaoh's army, which has set out to help you, will withdraw to its own land in Egypt.
Then the Chaldeans will return and fight against this city; they will capture it and burn it with fire.’”
This is what the LORD says: “Do not deceive yourselves by saying, ‘The Chaldeans will surely withdraw from us,’ for they will not withdraw.
Even if you were to defeat the entire Chaldean army fighting against you, and only wounded men remained in their tents, they would still rise up, each from his tent, and burn this city with fire.”
When the Chaldean army withdrew from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh's army,
Jeremiah set out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin to claim his portion there among the people.
But when he reached the Gate of Benjamin, a captain of the guard named Irijah son of Shelemiah, son of Hananiah, arrested Jeremiah the prophet, saying, “You are deserting to the Chaldeans!”
“That is a lie,” Jeremiah replied. “I am not deserting to the Chaldeans!” But Irijah would not listen to him; instead, he arrested Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.
The officials were angry with Jeremiah, and they beat him and imprisoned him in the house of Jonathan the scribe, which they had converted into a prison.
So Jeremiah was put into a cell in the dungeon, where he remained many days.

Then King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah and received him in his palace, where he questioned him privately, “Is there a word from the LORD?” Jeremiah answered, “There is,” and added, “You will be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon.”
Jeremiah then said to King Zedekiah, “What offense have I committed against you or your servants or these people, that you have put me in prison?
Where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, ‘The king of Babylon will not come against you or this land’?
But now, please listen, my lord the king: may my petition come before you, and do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the scribe, lest I die there.”

So King Zedekiah gave orders, and Jeremiah was placed in the courtyard of the guard; he was given a loaf of bread each day from the bakers' street until all the bread in the city was gone. Thus Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.
Now Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchijah heard the words Jeremiah was speaking to all the people:

“This is what the LORD says: ‘Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword, famine, and plague, but whoever surrenders to the Chaldeans will live; he will preserve his life as plunder and survive.’
This is what the LORD says: ‘This city will surely be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.’”

Then the officials said to the king, “This man must be put to death, for he is discouraging the warriors who remain in this city, as well as all the people, by speaking such words to them; for this man seeks not the welfare of this people, but their ruin.”
“He is in your hands,” King Zedekiah replied. “For the king can do nothing to stop you.”

So they took Jeremiah and dropped him into the cistern of Malchiah, the king’s son, which was in the courtyard of the guard. They lowered Jeremiah with ropes. Now there was no water in the cistern, but only mud, and Jeremiah sank into the mud.
Now Ebed-melech the Cushite, a eunuch in the king’s palace, heard that they had put Jeremiah in the cistern. While the king was sitting at the Gate of Benjamin,
Ebed-melech went out from the king’s palace and said to the king,

“My lord the king, these men have acted wickedly in all they have done to Jeremiah the prophet. They have thrown him into the cistern, where he will die of hunger, for there is no more bread in the city.”
So the king commanded Ebed-melech the Cushite, “Take thirty men from here with you and lift Jeremiah the prophet out of the cistern before he dies.”

So Ebed-melech took the men with him and went to the king’s palace, to a place beneath the treasury, and took from there rags and worn-out clothes. He lowered these to Jeremiah in the cistern using ropes.
Then Ebed-melech the Cushite said to Jeremiah, “Put these rags and worn-out clothes under your arms to cushion the ropes.” Jeremiah did so,
and they pulled Jeremiah up with the ropes and lifted him out of the cistern. And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.

Then King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah the prophet and received him at the third entrance of the house of the LORD. “I am going to ask you something,” said the king to Jeremiah. “Do not hide anything from me.”
“If I tell you,” Jeremiah replied, “you will surely put me to death. And if I give you advice, you will not listen to me.”

But King Zedekiah swore secretly to Jeremiah, “As surely as the LORD lives, who gave us our very lives, I will not put you to death, and I will not hand you over to the men who are seeking your life.”

Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, “This is what the LORD God of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: ‘If you surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, your life will be spared, and this city will not be burned down; you and your household will live.
But if you do not surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, this city will be delivered into the hands of the Chaldeans, who will burn it down, and you yourself will not escape their grasp.’”
But King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, “I am afraid of the Jews who have deserted to the Chaldeans, for the Chaldeans may hand me over to them, and they may abuse me.”
“They will not hand you over,” Jeremiah replied. “Obey the voice of the LORD in what I am telling you, that it may go well with you and your soul may live.
But if you refuse to surrender, this is the word that the LORD has shown me: “

All the women who are left in the house of the king of Judah will be led out to the officials of the king of Babylon, and those women will say: ‘They misled you and overcame you— your trusted friends. Your feet sank in the mud; they turned away from you.’
All your wives and children will be led out to the Chaldeans, and you yourself will not escape their grasp, for you will be seized by the king of Babylon, and this city will be burned down.”
Then Zedekiah warned Jeremiah, “Do not let anyone know about this conversation, or you will die.
If the officials hear that I have spoken with you, and they come and ask you, ‘What did you say to the king? Do not hide it from us, or we will put you to death,’
then tell them, ‘I was presenting my petition to the king not to send me back to the house of Jonathan to die there.’”
Then all the officials came to Jeremiah and questioned him, and he told them exactly what the king had instructed. So they left him alone, for the conversation had not been overheard.
And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard until the day Jerusalem was captured.
In the ninth year of Zedekiah, king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came against Jerusalem with his entire army and besieged it.
In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the city was breached.

Then all the officials of the king of Babylon entered and sat in the Middle Gate: Nergal-sharezer of Samgar, Nebo-sarsekim the Rabsaris, Nergal-sharezer the Rabmag, and all the remaining officials of the king of Babylon.

When Zedekiah, king of Judah, and all the soldiers saw them, they fled and left the city by night, taking the way of the king’s garden through the gate between the two walls, and they went out toward the Arabah.

But the Chaldean army pursued them and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho; they seized him and brought him to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he pronounced judgment on him.
At Riblah the king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes, and he also killed all the nobles of Judah.
Then he put out Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him with bronze fetters, and took him to Babylon.
The Chaldeans burned the king’s house and the houses of the people, and they broke down the walls of Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, carried into exile to Babylon the remnant of the people who remained in the city, along with those who had deserted to him and the rest of the people.
But Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, left in the land of Judah some of the poor people who had nothing, and at that time he gave them vineyards and fields.
Now Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had given orders concerning Jeremiah through Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, saying,
“Take him and look after him; do him no harm, but do for him whatever he requests of you.”

So Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, Nebushazban the Rabsaris, Nergal-sharezer the Rabmag, and all the chief officers of the king of Babylon sent and took Jeremiah out of the courtyard of the guard.
They entrusted him to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, to take him home, and so Jeremiah remained among the people.
While Jeremiah had been confined to the courtyard of the guard, the word of the LORD came to him:

“Go and tell Ebed-melech the Cushite that this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: ‘I am about to fulfill My words against this city for disaster and not for prosperity, and all of them will be fulfilled before your eyes on that day.
But I will rescue you on that day, declares the LORD, and you will not be delivered into the hands of the men you fear.
For I will surely save you, and you will not fall by the sword; because you have trusted in Me, you will escape with your life, declares the LORD.’”

This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, had released him at Ramah, when he had found him bound in chains among all the captives of Jerusalem and Judah who were being exiled to Babylon.
The captain of the guard found Jeremiah and said to him, “The LORD your God decreed this disaster for this place,
and now the LORD has brought it about and has done just as He warned. Because you people sinned against the LORD and did not obey His voice, this has happened to you.

But now, behold, I am freeing you today from the chains on your wrists. If it seems good to you to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will take care of you. But if it seems wrong to you to come with me to Babylon, stay here. Look, the whole land is before you; wherever it seems good and right to you, go there.

But before Jeremiah could turn back, the captain of the guard added, ‘Return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah, and stay with him among the people; or go wherever else seems right to you.’ Then the captain of the guard gave him a ration of food and a gift, and let him go.
So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and stayed with him among the people who were left in the land.

When all the commanders of the armies in the field and their men heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land and had put under his charge the men, women, children, and the poorest of the land who had not been exiled to Babylon,

they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah—Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite, along with their men.

And Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, swore an oath to them and their men, saying, “Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you.

As for me, I will stay in Mizpah to represent you before the Chaldeans who come to us. As for you, gather in wine, summer fruit, and oil, put them in your vessels, and live in your cities that you have taken.”
When all the Jews in Moab, Ammon, Edom, and all the other lands heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Judah and had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, over them,
they all returned out of all the places to which they had been banished. They came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and gathered an abundant harvest of wine and summer fruit.
Then Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies in the field came to Gedaliah at Mizpah
and said to him, “Are you aware that Baalis king of the Ammonites has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to take your life?” But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

Then Johanan son of Kareah spoke privately to Gedaliah at Mizpah: “Let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah. No one will know. Why should he take your life and scatter all the Jews who have gathered to you, so that the remnant of Judah would perish?”
But Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, “Do not do this thing, for you are speaking falsely about Ishmael.”

In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah—descended from the royal line and formerly one of the king’s principal officers—arrived at Mizpah with ten companions to visit Gedaliah son of Ahikam. There they shared a meal, and while Gedaliah governed the land under Babylonian appointment, Ishmael turned hospitality into treachery.
He and his ten men rose, struck Gedaliah down with the sword, and murdered the very official whom the king of Babylon had entrusted with authority over the land.
Ishmael also slaughtered every Jew who had gathered with Gedaliah at Mizpah, together with the Chaldean soldiers stationed there.
The crime remained concealed for two days, so that no one yet knew what had happened.

Eighty men from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria—men whose beards had been shaved, whose garments were torn, and whose bodies bore the marks of mourning—came bearing grain offerings and frankincense to the house of the LORD.
Ishmael son of Nethaniah emerged from Mizpah to intercept them, weeping as he advanced, and when he reached them he urged, “Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam.”
Once they had entered the city, Ishmael and his accomplices slaughtered the pilgrims and cast their bodies into a cistern.
Ten of the men, however, pleaded, “Do not kill us; we have concealed stores of wheat, barley, oil, and honey in the fields.” Ishmael spared them and did not execute them with their kinsmen.

The cistern into which he had hurled all the corpses of those he killed alongside Gedaliah was the large reservoir that King Asa had constructed as a defense against Baasha king of Israel; Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with the slain.

Ishmael then seized the entire remnant of Mizpah’s population—the king’s daughters and everyone else left there, whom Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, had placed under Gedaliah’s supervision—and led them away as captives toward the Ammonites.
When Johanan son of Kareah and all the military commanders with him heard of every atrocity Ishmael son of Nethaniah had committed,
they mobilized their men and marched to confront him. They overtook him beside the great pool at Gibeon.
At the sight of Johanan and his commanders, the people who had been with Ishmael rejoiced.
The captives Ishmael had seized from Mizpah broke away and rallied to Johanan son of Kareah.
Ishmael himself escaped with eight men and fled to the Ammonites.

Johanan son of Kareah and his commanders then gathered the whole remnant they had recovered from Ishmael after the murder of Gedaliah son of Ahikam—soldiers, women, children, and eunuchs—and brought them back from Gibeon.
They traveled onward and settled at Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem, intending to continue into Egypt,
because they feared the Chaldeans. Ishmael son of Nethaniah had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land, and they dreaded retaliation from Babylon.
Then all the commanders of the forces, along with Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least to the greatest, drew near
and said to Jeremiah the prophet, "Let our plea for mercy come before you, and pray to the LORD your God for us—for all this remnant, since we are left but a few, as your eyes can see.
May the LORD your God show us the way we should go and the thing we should do."

Jeremiah the prophet said to them, "I have heard you. Behold, I will pray to the LORD your God according to your words, and whatever the LORD answers you I will tell you; I will withhold nothing from you."
Then they said to Jeremiah, "May the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not act according to all the word that the LORD your God sends you to us.
Whether it is good or bad, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we are sending you, so that it may go well with us when we obey the voice of the LORD our God."
At the end of ten days, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah.
Then he summoned Johanan son of Kareah, all the commanders of the forces who were with him, and all the people from the least to the greatest,
and said to them, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, to whom you sent me to present your plea before Him:
If you will remain in this land, then I will build you up and not tear you down; I will plant you, and not uproot you, for I have relented concerning the disaster I brought on you.
Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, whom you fear. Do not be afraid of him, declares the LORD, for I am with you to save you and to deliver you from his hand.
I will show you compassion, so that he will have compassion on you and restore you to your land. "
But if you say, 'We will not remain in this land,' disobeying the voice of the LORD your God,
and saying, 'No, we will go to the land of Egypt, where we will not see war or hear the sound of the trumpet or be hungry for bread, and we will dwell there,'
then hear the word of the LORD, O remnant of Judah. Thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: If you set your faces to enter Egypt and go to live there,
then the sword you fear will overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine you dread will follow close after you to Egypt, and there you will die.
All the men who set their faces to go to Egypt to live there will die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence. They will have no remnant or survivor from the disaster I will bring on them.

For thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: As My anger and My wrath were poured out on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so My wrath will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt. You will become an execration, a horror, a curse, and a taunt. You will see this place no more. "
The LORD has said to you, O remnant of Judah, 'Do not go to Egypt.' Know for certain that I have warned you this day

that you have gone astray at the cost of your lives. For you sent me to the LORD your God, saying, 'Pray for us to the LORD our God, and whatever the LORD our God says, declare to us and we will do it.'
And I have told you today, but you have not obeyed the voice of the LORD your God in anything that He sent me to tell you.
Now therefore know for certain that you will die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence in the place where you desire to go to live."
When Jeremiah had finished telling all the people every word of the LORD their God—everything the LORD their God had sent him to tell them—
Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah, “You are speaking falsely. The LORD our God has not sent you to say, ‘Do not go to Egypt to reside there.’
Rather, Baruch son of Neriah is inciting you against us, so that we may be handed over to the Chaldeans to be killed or exiled to Babylon.”
So Johanan son of Kareah, all the commanders of the forces, and all the people disobeyed the voice of the LORD and did not remain in the land of Judah.

Instead, Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces took all the remnant of Judah who had returned from all the nations where they had been scattered, in order to dwell in the land of Judah—

the men, the women, the children, the king's daughters, and every person whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, as well as Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
They entered the land of Egypt because they did not obey the voice of the LORD, and they went as far as Tahpanhes.
The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes:
“Take some large stones in your hand and hide them in mortar in the brickwork at the entrance of Pharaoh's house in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah.

Then say to them, ‘Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will send for and take Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, My servant, and I will set his throne above these stones that I have hidden, and he will spread his royal canopy over them.
He will come and strike the land of Egypt—those destined for death to death, those for captivity to captivity, and those for the sword to the sword.

I will kindle a fire in the temples of the gods of Egypt, and he will burn them and carry them off. He will wrap himself in the land of Egypt as a shepherd wraps himself in his garment, and he will depart from there in peace.
He will shatter the sacred pillars of Beth-shemesh in the land of Egypt and burn down the temples of the gods of Egypt with fire.’”
The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews living in the land of Egypt—at Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, and in the land of Pathros—saying:
“This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: You have seen all the disaster I brought on Jerusalem and on all the cities of Judah. They lie in ruins today, without inhabitant,
because of the wickedness they committed, provoking Me to anger by burning incense and serving other gods that neither they nor you nor your fathers ever knew.
Yet I sent you all My servants the prophets again and again, saying, ‘Do not do this detestable thing that I hate.’
But they did not listen or incline their ear; they did not turn from their wickedness or stop burning incense to other gods.
Therefore My wrath and anger poured out and burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, so that they became the desolate ruin they are today.”

“Now this is what the LORD, the God of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: Why are you bringing such great disaster on yourselves by cutting off from Judah man and woman, child and infant, leaving yourselves without a remnant?

Why are you provoking Me to anger with the works of your hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt where you have gone to reside? You will be cut off and become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth.

Have you forgotten the wickedness of your fathers, the wickedness of the kings of Judah, the wickedness of their wives, your own wickedness, and the wickedness of your wives, which they committed in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
To this day they have not humbled themselves or shown reverence, nor have they followed My law or My statutes that I set before you and your fathers.”
“Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am determined to bring disaster on you and to cut off all Judah.

I will take away the remnant of Judah who have set their faces to go to Egypt to reside there; they will all perish in Egypt. They will fall by the sword and die by famine. From the least to the greatest, they will die by sword and famine. They will become an object of cursing and horror, of condemnation and reproach.
I will punish those who live in Egypt, just as I punished Jerusalem, by sword, famine, and plague,
so that none of the remnant of Judah who have gone to reside in Egypt will escape or survive to return to the land of Judah, except a few fugitives.”

Then all the men who knew that their wives were burning incense to other gods, and all the women standing by—a great assembly—and all the people living in Pathros in the land of Egypt, answered Jeremiah:
“As for the word you have spoken to us in the name of the LORD, we will not listen to you!

Instead, we will surely do whatever we have promised: We will burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, just as we, our fathers, our kings, and our officials did in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. Then we had plenty of food, were well off, and saw no disaster.
But from the time we stopped burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything and have been consumed by sword and famine.”

And the women added, “When we burned incense to the Queen of Heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, did we make her cakes in her image and pour out drink offerings to her without our husbands’ knowledge?”
Then Jeremiah said to all the people, both men and women, who were answering him:

“As for the incense you burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem—you, your fathers, your kings, your officials, and the people of the land—did not the LORD remember and bring it to mind?

So the LORD could no longer endure it, because of your evil deeds and the abominations you committed. Therefore your land has become a desolation, a horror, and a curse, without inhabitant, as it is this day.

Because you burned incense and sinned against the LORD, and did not obey the voice of the LORD or walk in His law, His statutes, and His testimonies, this disaster has befallen you, as it is this day.”
Then Jeremiah said to all the people and all the women, “Hear the word of the LORD, all you people of Judah who are in the land of Egypt.

This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: You and your wives have spoken with your mouths and fulfilled with your hands your promise, ‘We will surely fulfill our vows that we have made to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and to pour out drink offerings to her.’ So go ahead, then! Keep your vows and carry them out!”

“But hear this word of the LORD, all you people of Judah who live in the land of Egypt: I have sworn by My great name, says the LORD, that My name will never again be invoked by anyone of Judah in all the land of Egypt, saying, ‘As surely as the Lord the LORD lives.’
I am watching over them for harm and not for good, and every man of Judah who is in the land of Egypt will meet his end by sword or famine until they are finished.
Yet a small number who escape the sword will return from Egypt to the land of Judah, and all the remnant of Judah who went to dwell in Egypt will know whose word will stand, Mine or theirs.”
“This will be a sign to you, declares the LORD, that I will punish you in this place, so that you will know that My words of doom will surely come to pass against you.

This is what the LORD says: I am going to hand Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt over to his enemies, to those who seek his life, just as I handed Zedekiah king of Judah over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy who was seeking his life.”
The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah, when he wrote these words in a book at Jeremiah's dictation, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying:
"This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning you, Baruch:
'You said, "Woe to me, for the LORD has added sorrow to my pain! I am exhausted with groaning and have found no rest."'
"Thus you shall say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Behold, what I have built I am breaking down, and what I have planted I am uprooting—that is, the whole land.
And are you seeking great things for yourself? Do not seek them, for I am bringing disaster on all flesh, declares the LORD. But I will give you your life as plunder wherever you go.'"
The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.

Concerning Egypt: the army of Pharaoh Neco, king of Egypt, which was defeated at Carchemish on the Euphrates by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
Prepare shield and buckler, and advance to battle.
Harness the horses and mount, O horsemen; take your stand with helmets; polish the spears and put on the coats of mail.
Why have I seen it? They are dismayed and turn backward; their warriors are beaten down and flee headlong; they do not look back; terror is on every side, declares the LORD.
Let not the swift escape, nor the mighty man get away; northward by the river Euphrates they stumble and fall.
Who is this rising like the Nile, like rivers whose waters surge?
Egypt rises like the Nile, and its waters surge like rivers; it says, "I will rise, I will cover the earth, I will destroy the city and its inhabitants."
Advance, O horses; rage, O chariots; let the warriors go out—Cush and Put, who handle the shield, and the Ludim, who draw the bow.

That day is to the Lord the LORD of Hosts a day of vengeance, to avenge Himself on His foes; the sword shall devour and be satisfied, and drink its fill of their blood; for the Lord the LORD of Hosts has a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates.
Go up to Gilead and take balm, O virgin daughter of Egypt! In vain you have multiplied remedies; there is no healing for you.
The nations have heard of your shame, and your cry has filled the land; for warrior has stumbled against warrior, and both have fallen together.
The word that the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to strike the land of Egypt:
"Declare in Egypt and proclaim in Migdol; proclaim also in Memphis and in Tahpanhes; say, 'Take your stand and prepare yourself, for the sword devours around you.'"
Why are your mighty ones swept away? They did not stand, because the LORD drove them.
He multiplied the stumbling; indeed, one fell upon another, and they said, "Arise, let us return to our people and to the land of our birth, away from the sword of the oppressor."
There they cried out, "Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise; he has let the appointed moment pass by."
As I live, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts, surely, as Tabor among the mountains and as Carmel by the sea, so shall he come.
Prepare your baggage for exile, O daughter who dwells in Egypt, for Memphis shall become a desolation and be burned, without inhabitant.
Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but a gadfly from the north has come upon her.

Even her hired soldiers in her midst are like fattened calves; they too have turned and fled together; they did not stand, for the day of their calamity has come upon them, the time of their punishment.
Her sound is like a serpent's hiss, for they march in force and come against her with axes, like woodcutters.
They shall cut down her forest, declares the LORD, though it is impenetrable, because they are more numerous than locusts and without number.
The daughter of Egypt shall be put to shame; she shall be delivered into the hand of a people from the north.
The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says, "Behold, I will punish Amon of Thebes, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, and her gods, and her kings—Pharaoh and those who trust in him.

I will deliver them into the hand of those who seek their lives, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and into the hand of his servants. Afterward Egypt shall be inhabited as in the days of old," declares the LORD.

But as for you, Jacob My servant, do not be afraid, and do not be dismayed, O Israel, for I will save you from afar and your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and be at rest and secure, and no one will make him afraid.

You, Jacob My servant, do not be afraid, declares the LORD, for I am with you; I will make a full end of all the nations among whom I have driven you, but I will not make a full end of you. I will discipline you justly, and I will by no means leave you unpunished.
The word of the the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh attacked Gaza.

“Thus says the the LORD: Behold, waters are rising from the north and will become an overflowing torrent. They will flood the land and everything in it—the city and its inhabitants. People will cry out, and every inhabitant of the land will wail
at the thunder of galloping hooves, the rumble of chariots, and the clatter of wheels. Fathers will not even turn to their children, because their hands are too weak.
For the day has come to destroy all the Philistines and to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every surviving ally. For the the LORD is destroying the Philistines, the remnant from the coasts of Caphtor.”
“Gaza shaves its head in mourning; Ashkelon falls silent. O remnant of their valley, how long will you keep cutting yourselves in grief?
Alas, sword of the the LORD! How long before you are quiet? Return to your sheath; rest and be still.
How can it be quiet when the the LORD has given it a command? Against Ashkelon and the seacoast He has appointed it.”
Concerning Moab, this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: "Woe to Nebo, for it has been devastated! Kiriathaim has been captured; the stronghold is disgraced and dismayed.
No longer will Moab be praised. In Heshbon they plotted evil against her, saying, 'Come, let us cut her off from being a nation.' You too, Madmen, will be silenced; the sword will pursue you."
A cry of anguish rises from Horonaim: 'Plunder and great destruction!'
Moab is shattered; even her little ones raise a cry.
On the ascent to Luhith they climb weeping, and on the descent to Horonaim they hear cries of distress.
"Flee and save your lives; make yourselves like a shrub in the desert.
Because you have trusted in your works and treasures, you too will be captured; Chemosh will go into exile together with his priests and officials."
The destroyer will come against every city, and no city will escape. The valley will be ruined and the plateau destroyed, because the LORD has spoken.
"Give Moab wings, for she will take flight; her towns will become a wasteland, without a single inhabitant.
Cursed is he who does the work of the LORD deceitfully, and cursed is he who withholds his sword from blood."

Moab has been at ease from his youth; he has settled on his dregs and has not been poured from vessel to vessel, nor has he gone into exile. Therefore his flavor remains, and his aroma has not changed.
"Therefore, behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will send to him those who pour, and they will pour him out; they will empty his vessels and shatter his wine jars."
Then Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, their confidence.
"How can you say, 'We are mighty men, warriors valiant in battle'?"
Moab has been destroyed, and her cities have gone up in smoke; her best young men have gone down to the slaughter, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.
The disaster of Moab is near at hand; his calamity has come quickly.
Mourn for him, all you who surround him, all you who know his name. Say, "How the mighty staff is broken, the glorious scepter!"
"Come down from your glory and sit in thirst, O daughter dwelling in Dibon, for the destroyer of Moab has come up against you; he has destroyed your fortresses.
Stand by the road and watch, O inhabitant of Aroer; ask him who flees and her who escapes; say, 'What has happened?'"
Moab is put to shame, for it is broken down; wail and cry out! Declare by the Arnon that Moab is destroyed.
Judgment has come upon the plateau: upon Holon, Jahzah, and Mephaath,
upon Kerioth, Bozrah, and all the cities of the land of Moab, far and near.
The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken, declares the LORD.
"Make him drunk, for he has exalted himself against the LORD; Moab will wallow in his vomit and become a laughingstock."
"Was not Israel a laughingstock to you? Whenever you spoke of him, you shook your head.
Leave the cities and dwell among the rocks, O inhabitants of Moab; be like a dove that nests in the clefts of a gorge."
We have heard of the pride of Moab—his exceeding pride—his arrogance, pride, and haughtiness, and the loftiness of his heart.
"I know his insolence, declares the LORD, but it is futile; his boastings have accomplished nothing."
"Therefore I wail for Moab; I cry out for all Moab; I mourn for the men of Kir-heres.
O vine of Sibmah, I weep for you more than for Jazer. Your branches have spread to the sea and reached the Sea of Jazer. The destroyer has fallen upon your summer fruit and your grape harvest.
Joy and gladness are removed from the fruitful field and from the land of Moab. I have made the wine to cease from the winepresses; no one treads them with shouting; their shouting is not shouting.
From the cry of Heshbon to Elealeh, they raise their voices to Jahaz; from Zoar to Horonaim and Eglath-shelishiyah; for even the waters of Nimrim will become desolate."
"And I will bring an end to Moab, declares the LORD, to the one who offers sacrifice on the high place and burns incense to his god.
