Therefore My heart laments for Moab like flutes; My heart laments for the men of Kir-heres like flutes, because the wealth he acquired has perished."
For every head is shaved and every beard clipped; on every hand are gashes, and on every waist is sackcloth.
On all the rooftops of Moab and in its streets there is mourning, for "I have broken Moab like a vessel no one wants," declares the LORD.
How shattered it is! How they wail! How Moab has turned his back in shame! So Moab will become a laughingstock and a terror to all around him.
For thus says the LORD: "Behold, one will fly like an eagle and spread his wings over Moab.
Kerioth will be captured and the strongholds taken. The heart of Moab's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
Moab will be destroyed as a people, because he magnified himself against the LORD.
Terror, pit, and snare await you, O inhabitant of Moab, declares the LORD.

He who flees from the terror will fall into the pit, and he who climbs out of the pit will be caught in the snare; for I will bring upon them, upon Moab, the year of their punishment, declares the LORD."
In the shadow of Heshbon the refugees stand exhausted, for a fire has gone out from Heshbon, a flame from the midst of Sihon; it has consumed the forehead of Moab and the crown of the sons of tumult.
"Woe to you, Moab! The people of Chemosh have perished, for your sons have been taken captive and your daughters into captivity."
"Yet I will restore the fortunes of Moab in the latter days, declares the LORD." Thus far is the judgment on Moab.
Concerning the Ammonites, this is what the LORD says: “Does Israel have no sons? Is there no heir? Why then has their king inherited Gad, and his people settled in its cities?”

“Therefore, behold, days are coming,” declares the LORD, “when I will cause the battle cry to be heard against Rabbah of the Ammonites; she will become a heap of ruins, and her daughters will be burned with fire. Then Israel will dispossess those who dispossessed him,” says the LORD.

“Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is ruined! Cry out, daughters of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth, lament, and run back and forth among the walls, for their king will go into exile, together with his priests and officials.”
“Why do you boast in the valleys, your valley flowing away, O faithless daughter, who trusts in her treasures, saying, ‘Who will come against me?’”
“Behold, I am bringing terror upon you from all around you,” declares the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, “and you will be driven out, each man straight ahead, and no one will gather the fugitives.”
“But afterward I will restore the fortunes of the Ammonites,” declares the LORD.
Concerning Edom, this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Is wisdom no more in Teman? Has counsel perished from the prudent? Has their wisdom decayed?”
“Flee, turn back, and hide deep, O inhabitants of Dedan! For I will bring the calamity of Esau upon him, the time when I punish him.”
“If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave gleanings? If thieves came by night, would they not steal only enough for themselves?”
“But I have stripped Esau bare; I have uncovered his hiding places, and he cannot conceal himself. His offspring are devastated, along with his brothers and neighbors, and he is no more.”
“Leave your orphans; I will preserve them alive, and let your widows trust in Me.”
“For this is what the the LORD says: ‘If those who do not deserve to drink the cup must drink it, will you go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, but you will surely drink it.’”
“For I have sworn by Myself,” declares the LORD, “that Bozrah will become a desolation, a reproach, a waste, and a curse, and all its cities will be perpetual ruins.”
“I have heard a message from the the LORD, and a messenger is sent among the nations: ‘Gather yourselves together and come against her; rise up for battle!’”
“Behold, I will make you small among the nations, despised among men.”

“The terror you inspire has deceived you, and the pride of your heart, O you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, who hold the height of the hill. Though you make your nest as high as the eagle's, from there I will bring you down,” declares the LORD.
“Edom will become an object of horror; everyone who passes by her will be appalled and will hiss at all her wounds.”
“As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors,” says the the LORD, “no man will dwell there, nor will any son of man reside in it.”

“Behold, he will come up like a lion from the thickets of the Jordan against the enduring pasture; for I will suddenly make him run away from her, and I will appoint over her whomever I choose. For who is like Me? Who will summon Me? And who is the shepherd who can stand before Me?”

“Therefore hear the plan that the the LORD has devised against Edom and the strategies He has plotted against the inhabitants of Teman: Surely the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; surely their pasture will be appalled at them.”
“At the sound of their fall the earth will tremble; the sound of their cry will be heard at the Red Sea.”
“Behold, he will come up and fly like an eagle and spread his wings over Bozrah; and the heart of the warriors of Edom will be in that day like the heart of a woman in labor.”
“Concerning Damascus: Hamath and Arpad are put to shame, for they have heard a bad report; they are dismayed. There is anxiety by the sea; it cannot be calmed.”
“Damascus has become feeble; she has turned to flee, and panic has seized her; anguish and pain have taken hold of her, like a woman in labor.”
“How is the city of praise not forsaken, the city of My joy?”
“Therefore her young men will fall in her streets, and all the men of war will be silenced in that day,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
“I will set fire to the wall of Damascus, and it will consume the palaces of Ben-hadad.”
“Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon defeated, this is what the the LORD says: ‘Arise, go up against Kedar, and destroy the people of the East.’”
“They will take their tents and their flocks, their tent curtains and all their goods; they will carry off their camels for themselves, and will shout to them, ‘Terror on every side!’”
“Flee, wander far away, hide in the depths, O inhabitants of Hazor,” declares the LORD, “for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has taken counsel against you and devised a plan against you.”
“Arise, go up against a nation at ease, that dwells securely,” declares the LORD, “that has no gates or bars, that dwells alone.”

“Their camels will become plunder, and their multitude of livestock a spoil, and I will scatter to every wind those who have shaved temples, and I will bring their disaster from every side,” declares the LORD.
“Hazor will become a haunt of jackals, a desolation forever; no one will dwell there, nor will any son of man reside in it.”
The word of the the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah:
“This is what the the LORD of Hosts says: ‘Behold, I will break the bow of Elam, the chief of their might.’”
“I will bring the four winds from the four quarters of heaven against Elam, and I will scatter them to all these winds, and there will be no nation to which the outcasts of Elam will not go.”

“I will shatter Elam before their enemies and before those who seek their life; I will bring disaster upon them, My fierce anger,” declares the LORD, “and I will send the sword after them until I have consumed them.”
“I will set My throne in Elam and destroy from there king and officials,” declares the LORD.
“But in the latter days I will restore the fortunes of Elam,” declares the LORD.
This is the word that the LORD spoke concerning Babylon and the land of the Chaldeans through Jeremiah the prophet:

“Announce and declare among the nations; raise a banner and proclaim it; do not conceal it. Say, ‘Babylon has been captured; Bel is put to shame; Marduk is shattered; her idols are put to shame; her images are shattered.’
For a nation from the north has come against her; it will make her land a desolation. No one will live in it; both man and beast will flee.
“In those days and at that time,” declares the LORD, “the children of Israel and the children of Judah will come together, weeping as they go, and they will seek the LORD their God.
They will ask the way to Zion, turning their faces toward it, as they come to join themselves to the LORD in an everlasting covenant that will never be forgotten.
My people are lost sheep; their shepherds have led them astray, turning them away on the mountains. They have wandered from mountain to hill; they have forgotten their resting place.
All who found them devoured them, and their enemies said, ‘We are not guilty, for they have sinned against the LORD, their true pasture, the LORD, the hope of their fathers.’
“Flee from the midst of Babylon; leave the land of the Chaldeans; be like the he-goats that lead the flock.

For behold, I am raising up against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the land of the north. They will array themselves against her; from there she will be captured. Their arrows will be like a skilled warrior who does not return empty-handed.
Chaldea will be plundered; all who plunder her will be satisfied,” declares the LORD.
“Because you rejoice, because you exult—you who plunder My inheritance—because you frolic like a heifer threshing grain and neigh like stallions,
your mother will be greatly shamed; she who bore you will be disgraced. Behold, she will be the least of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land, and a desert.
Because of the wrath of the LORD, she will not be inhabited; she will be completely desolate. Everyone who passes through Babylon will be horrified and hiss at all her wounds.
“Set yourselves in array against Babylon on every side, all you who bend the bow; shoot at her, spare no arrows, for she has sinned against the LORD.

Raise a shout against her on every side! She has surrendered; her fortifications have fallen; her walls are torn down. For it is the vengeance of the LORD; take vengeance on her; as she has done, do to her.
Cut off the sower from Babylon, and the one who wields the sickle at harvest time. In the face of the oppressor's sword, each will turn to his own people, each will flee to his own land.
Israel is a scattered flock, chased away by lions. First the king of Assyria devoured him; now Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has gnawed his bones.
Therefore thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: “I will punish the king of Babylon and his land as I punished the king of Assyria.
I will bring Israel back to his pasture, and he will graze on Carmel and Bashan; his soul will be satisfied on the hills of Ephraim and Gilead.

“In those days and at that time,” declares the LORD, “a search will be made for Israel's guilt, but there will be none, and for Judah's sins, but they will not be found; for I will forgive those I leave as a remnant.
“Go up against the land of Merathaim, and against the residents of Pekod. Put them to the sword and devote them to destruction,” declares the LORD. “Do all that I have commanded you.
“The sound of battle is in the land—the sound of great destruction.
How the hammer of the whole earth is cut down and broken! How Babylon has become a desolation among the nations!
I have set a snare for you, O Babylon, and you have been caught. You did not know it; you were found and seized because you contended with the LORD.
“The LORD has opened His armory and brought out His weapons of wrath, because this is the work of the Lord the LORD of Hosts in the land of the Chaldeans.
Come against her from the farthest border. Open her granaries; pile her up like heaps of grain and devote her to destruction; leave her no survivors.
Put all her young bulls to the sword; let them go down to the slaughter. Woe to them, for their day has come—the time of their punishment.
Listen to the voice of those fleeing and escaping from Babylon, proclaiming in Zion the vengeance of the LORD our God, the vengeance for His temple.

Summon the archers against Babylon—all who bend the bow. Encamp all around her; let no one escape. Repay her according to her deeds; do to her as she has done. For she has defied the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
“Therefore her young men will fall in her streets, and all her warriors will be silenced in that day,” declares the LORD.
“Behold, I am against you, O arrogance,” declares the Lord the LORD of Hosts. “Your day has come, the time when I will punish you.
Arrogance will stumble and fall, with no one to pick her up. I will set fire to her cities, and it will consume everything around her.
Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “The people of Israel are oppressed, and the people of Judah as well. All their captors hold them fast; they refuse to release them.
Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of Hosts is His name. He will fervently plead their case, so that He may bring rest to the earth, but turmoil to the inhabitants of Babylon.
“A sword is against the Chaldeans,” declares the LORD, “and against the inhabitants of Babylon, and against her officials and wise men.
A sword is against her diviners, and they will become fools. A sword is against her warriors, and they will be dismayed.
A sword is against her horses and chariots, and against all the foreigners in her midst, and they will become women. A sword is against her treasuries, and they will be plundered.
A drought is upon her waters, and they will be dried up. For it is a land of idols, and they go mad over idols.
Therefore the desert creatures and hyenas will live there, and ostriches will dwell in her. She will never again be inhabited or lived in from generation to generation.
As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighboring towns,” declares the LORD, “no man will dwell there; no one will live there.
“Behold, a people is coming from the north; a great nation and many kings are stirred up from the ends of the earth.
They grasp bow and spear; they are cruel and without mercy. Their voice roars like the sea, and they ride on horses, arrayed like men for war against you, O daughter of Babylon.
The king of Babylon has heard the report about them, and his hands grow feeble. Anguish grips him, pain like that of a woman in labor.

Like a lion coming up from the thickets of the Jordan to a perennial pasture, I will suddenly chase them from her. Who is the chosen one I will appoint over her? For who is like Me? Who will summon Me? And who is the shepherd who can stand against Me?

Therefore hear the plan that the LORD has made against Babylon, and the strategy He has devised against the land of the Chaldeans: The little ones of the flock will be dragged away; their pasture will be made desolate because of them.
At the sound of Babylon's capture the earth will tremble, and a cry will be heard among the nations.”
The LORD says: "Behold, I am stirring up against Babylon and against the inhabitants of Leb-kamai a destroying wind.
I will send foreigners to Babylon, and they will winnow her and empty her land, for they will be against her on every side in the day of trouble.
Let the archer not bend his bow, and let him not rise up in his armor. Do not spare her young men; devote all her army to destruction.
They will fall down slain in the land of the Chaldeans and pierced through in her streets.
For Israel and Judah have not been forsaken by their God, the LORD of Hosts, though their land is full of guilt before the Holy One of Israel."
Flee from the midst of Babylon, and save each his life! Do not perish in her guilt, for it is the time of the LORD's vengeance; He is repaying her what she deserves.
Babylon was a golden cup in the LORD's hand, intoxicating all the earth. The nations drank her wine; therefore the nations went mad.
Suddenly Babylon has fallen and been shattered. Wail for her; take balm for her pain—perhaps she may be healed.
We tried to heal Babylon, but she was not healed. Forsake her, and let each of us go to his own country, for her judgment has reached to heaven and has been lifted up to the clouds.
The LORD has brought forth our vindication. Come, let us declare in Zion the work of the LORD our God.

Sharpen the arrows! Fill the quivers! The LORD has stirred up the spirit of the kings of Media, because His plan against Babylon is to destroy it, for it is the vengeance of the LORD, the vengeance for His temple.

Raise a banner against the walls of Babylon! Strengthen the guard, station the watchmen, prepare the ambushes, for the LORD has both planned and accomplished what He spoke against the inhabitants of Babylon.
O you who dwell by many waters, rich in treasures, your end has come, the thread of your life is cut.
The LORD of Hosts has sworn by Himself: "Surely I will fill you with men as with locusts, and they will raise a shout against you."
He who made the earth by His power, who established the world by His wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by His understanding—

when He utters His voice, there is a tumult of waters in the heavens, and He makes the clouds rise from the ends of the earth. He makes lightning for the rain and brings forth the wind from His storehouses.
Every man is senseless and devoid of knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his idol, for his molten image is a lie, and there is no breath in them.
They are worthless, a work of delusion; at the time of their punishment they will perish.
The Portion of Jacob is not like these, for He is the Maker of all things, and Israel is the tribe of His inheritance. The LORD of Hosts is His name.
You are My war club, My weapon of war. With you I shatter nations and destroy kingdoms.
With you I shatter horse and rider; with you I shatter chariot and driver.
With you I shatter man and woman; with you I shatter old and young; with you I shatter young man and virgin.
With you I shatter shepherd and flock; with you I shatter farmer and team; with you I shatter governors and officials.
Before your eyes I will repay Babylon and all the inhabitants of Chaldea for all the evil they have done in Zion, declares the LORD.
"Behold, I am against you, O destroying mountain, you who destroy the whole earth. I will stretch out My hand against you and roll you down from the crags and make you a burned-out mountain.
They will not take from you a stone for a corner nor a stone for a foundation, but you will be desolate forever," declares the LORD.

Raise a banner in the land! Blow the trumpet among the nations! Consecrate the nations against her; summon against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Appoint a marshal against her; bring up horses like a swarm of locusts.
Consecrate the nations against her—the kings of Media, her governors and all her officials, and all the land of their dominion.
The land trembles and writhes, for the LORD's plans against Babylon stand: to make the land of Babylon a desolation without inhabitant.
The mighty men of Babylon have stopped fighting; they sit in their strongholds. Their strength has failed; they have become like women. Her dwellings are set on fire; her bars are broken.
One runner runs to meet another, and one messenger to meet another, to tell the king of Babylon that his city has been captured from end to end.
The fords have been seized, and the marshes are burned with fire, and the soldiers are terrified.
For thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: "The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trodden; yet a little while, and the time of her harvest will come."

Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured us, he has crushed us, he has made us an empty vessel. He has swallowed us like a monster; he has filled his belly with our delicacies; he has driven us out.
"May the violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon," says the inhabitant of Zion. "And may my blood be upon the inhabitants of Chaldea," says Jerusalem.
Therefore thus says the LORD: "Behold, I will plead your cause and take vengeance for you. I will dry up her sea and make her fountain dry.
Babylon will become a heap of ruins, a haunt of jackals, a horror and a hissing, without inhabitant.
They will roar together like young lions; they will growl like lion cubs.
While they are heated, I will prepare their feast and make them drunk, that they may exult and sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake.
I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with male goats," declares the LORD.
How Sheshach has been captured, the praise of the whole earth seized! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
The sea has come up over Babylon; she is covered with the multitude of its waves.
Her cities have become a desolation, a dry land and a desert, a land in which no one dwells and through which no son of man passes.
I will punish Bel in Babylon, and I will bring out of his mouth what he has swallowed. The nations will no longer stream to him; yes, the wall of Babylon has fallen.
Come out of her midst, My people, and save each his life from the fierce anger of the LORD.

Let not your heart grow faint, nor be afraid at the report that is heard in the land. For a report will come in one year, and after that in another year a report, and violence in the land, and ruler against ruler.
Therefore behold, days are coming when I will punish the idols of Babylon, and her whole land will be put to shame, and all her slain will fall in her midst.
Then heaven and earth and all that is in them will shout for joy over Babylon, for the destroyers will come against her from the north, declares the LORD.
As Babylon caused the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon the slain of all the earth have fallen.
You who have escaped the sword, go, do not stand still! Remember the LORD from afar, and let Jerusalem come up in your heart.
We are ashamed, for we have heard reproach; dishonor has covered our faces, for foreigners have come into the holy places of the LORD's house.
Therefore behold, days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will punish her idols, and throughout her land the wounded will groan.
Even if Babylon were to mount up to heaven, and even if she were to fortify the height of her strength, yet destroyers from Me would come to her, declares the LORD.
A sound of a cry from Babylon, and great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans!
For the LORD is laying Babylon waste and has caused her great voice to perish. Her waves roar like many waters; the noise of their voice resounds.
For the destroyer has come upon her, upon Babylon, and her mighty men are captured; their bows are broken, for the LORD is a God of recompense; He will surely repay.

I will make drunk her princes and her wise men, her governors, her officials, and her mighty men, and they will sleep an everlasting sleep and not wake, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.

Thus says the LORD of Hosts: "The broad walls of Babylon will be completely razed, and her high gates will be burned with fire. The peoples will toil for nothing, and the nations will weary themselves for fire."

The word that Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, when he went with Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Now Seraiah was chief quartermaster.
Jeremiah wrote in a single scroll all the disaster that was to come upon Babylon—all these words that are written concerning Babylon.
And Jeremiah said to Seraiah, "When you come to Babylon, see that you read all these words aloud,
and say, 'O LORD, You have spoken concerning this place to cut it off, so that no one shall dwell in it, neither man nor beast, but it shall be desolate forever.'
And when you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the Euphrates,
and say, 'Thus Babylon shall sink and shall not rise from the disaster that I am bringing upon her, and they shall be exhausted.' Thus far are the words of Jeremiah."
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eleven years. His mother’s name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
He did evil in the sight of the the LORD, just as Jehoiakim had done.
Because of the anger of the the LORD against Jerusalem and Judah, He finally banished them from His presence; and Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

In the ninth year of Zedekiah’s reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came with his entire army against Jerusalem. They encamped around it and built siege works against it.
The city remained under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
By the fourth month, on the ninth day, the famine in the city had grown severe, and there was no bread for the people.
Then the city wall was breached. While the Chaldeans surrounded the city, all the men of war fled by night through the gate between the two walls near the king’s garden and made for the Arabah.
But the Chaldean army pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah on the plains of Jericho, and his whole army scattered from him.
They captured the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he pronounced judgment on him.
There at Riblah the king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes, and he also slaughtered all the princes of Judah.
Then he put out Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him with bronze shackles, took him to Babylon, and imprisoned him until the day of his death.
On the tenth day of the fifth month—in the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon—Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, who served in the presence of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
He burned the house of the the LORD, the king’s palace, and all the houses of Jerusalem; every important building he burned with fire.
The whole Chaldean army, together with the captain of the guard, tore down all the walls around Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, carried into exile the rest of the people who remained in the city, those who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude.
But he left some of the poorest of the land to tend the vineyards and fields.
The Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars, the stands, and the bronze Sea in the house of the the LORD, and they carried all the bronze to Babylon.
They also took the pots, shovels, snuffers, basins, pans, and all the bronze utensils used in the temple service.
The captain of the guard took the basins, censers, sprinkling bowls, pots, lampstands, dishes, and bowls—everything made of gold or silver.
The two pillars, the Sea, and the twelve bronze bulls beneath the stands, which King Solomon had made for the house of the the LORD, were beyond weighing; their bronze could not be measured.
Each pillar stood eighteen cubits high; its circumference was twelve cubits, and its wall was four fingers thick and hollow.
The bronze capital on top was five cubits high, and around it were a latticework and pomegranates, all of bronze. The second pillar was the same.
There were ninety-six pomegranates on the outside, and one hundred pomegranates in all around the latticework.
The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three doorkeepers.

From the city he also took the eunuch who oversaw the men of war, seven of the king’s close advisors who were found in the city, the scribe of the commander of the army who conscripted the people of the land, and sixty of the common people who were found in the city.
Nebuzaradan took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
There in the land of Hamath the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death. Thus Judah was carried away captive from its land.
This is the number of people Nebuchadnezzar carried into exile: in the seventh year, 3,023 Jews.
In the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, 832 people from Jerusalem.
In the twenty-third year, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away 745 Jews. In all, 4,600 people were taken captive.

On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, pardoned Jehoiachin king of Judah and released him from prison.
He spoke kindly to him and set his throne above the thrones of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
Jehoiachin changed out of his prison clothes and ate regularly at the king’s table for the rest of his life.
For the rest of his life, the king of Babylon gave him a daily allowance, a portion each day, until the day of his death.
How desolate sits the city once thronged with people! How like a widow she has become, she who was mighty among the nations and a princess among provinces, now reduced to vassalage.
Bitterly she weeps through the night, tears staining her cheeks; among all her former allies, none remains to console her, for every friend has betrayed her and become an enemy.
Judah has been carried into exile, crushed by affliction and grinding toil; dwelling among foreign peoples, she finds no rest, and her persecutors overtake her amid her anguish.
Zion's roads mourn because no pilgrims attend the festivals; her gates stand empty; her priests sigh; her young women grieve; and the city itself is steeped in bitterness.
Her adversaries now dominate her; her enemies thrive, for the LORD has afflicted her because of her many transgressions; her children have been led away captive before the oppressor.
All the splendor has departed from Daughter Zion. Her princes resemble deer searching in vain for pasture; robbed of strength, they flee before the hunter.

In the days of her affliction and homelessness, Jerusalem remembers all the treasures she once possessed; when her people fell into enemy hands and no one came to rescue them, her foes gloated and mocked her ruin.
Jerusalem sinned grievously, and so she became an object of scorn; all who once honored her now despise her, having seen her shame exposed; she groans and turns away in humiliation.
Her defilement clung to her garments; she never considered her end, so her collapse astonished everyone; no one comforted her. "Look, the LORD, upon my affliction, for the enemy has triumphed!"
The enemy stretched out his hand over all her treasures, for she watched the nations invade her sanctuary—people You had forbidden to enter Your assembly.
All her people groan, searching for bread; they barter their treasures for food to sustain their lives. "Look, the LORD, and take notice, for I have become contemptible."
Does this mean nothing to all you who pass by? Look and see whether any sorrow equals mine, the sorrow the LORD brought upon me in the day of His fierce anger.
From above He sent fire into my bones, and it overpowered them; He spread a net for my feet and turned me back; He has made me desolate and faint all day long.
My transgressions are bound into a yoke; by His hand they are fastened together and placed upon my neck; He has sapped my strength; the Lord has delivered me into the hands of those I cannot resist.
The Lord has rejected all my warriors within me; He has summoned a time of judgment against me to crush my young men; the Lord has trampled the virgin Daughter of Judah like grapes in a winepress.
Because of these things I weep; my eyes overflow with tears, because a comforter is far from me, and no one restores my spirit; my children are desolate because the enemy has prevailed.
Zion stretches out her hands, yet no one comforts her; the LORD has commanded concerning Jacob that his enemies surround him; Jerusalem has become an unclean thing among them.
The LORD is righteous, for I rebelled against His command; hear, all you peoples, and behold my suffering; my young men and young women have gone into exile.
I called to my allies, but they betrayed me; my priests and elders perished in the city as they searched for food to sustain themselves.
"Look, the LORD, for I am in distress; my innermost being churns; my heart is overturned within me, because I have been utterly rebellious. Outside, the sword bereaves; inside, there is only death."
They heard my groaning, yet no one comforted me; all my enemies heard of my calamity and rejoiced that You have done it. You have brought the day You proclaimed; now let them become like me.
Let all their wickedness come before You, and do to them as You have done to me because of all my transgressions; for my groans are many and my heart is sick.
How the Lord has covered Daughter Zion with cloud in His anger! He has cast down from heaven to earth the splendor of Israel. He has not remembered His footstool in the day of His wrath.

The Lord has swallowed up without mercy all the dwellings of Jacob; in His wrath He has torn down the strongholds of Daughter Judah. He has brought her down to the ground and profaned the kingdom and its princes.
In fierce anger He has cut off every horn of Israel; He has withdrawn His right hand at the approach of the enemy. He has burned against Jacob like a blazing fire that consumes everything around it.
He has bent His bow like an enemy; His right hand stood ready like a foe. He has slain all who were pleasing to the eye; in the tent of Daughter Zion He has poured out His wrath like fire.
The Lord has become like an enemy; He has swallowed up Israel. He has swallowed up all her palaces; He has destroyed her strongholds. He has multiplied mourning and lamentation in Daughter Judah.
He has laid waste His tabernacle like a garden; He has destroyed His appointed meeting place. The LORD has made Zion forget festival and Sabbath; in His fierce anger He has despised king and priest.
The Lord has rejected His altar; He has abandoned His sanctuary. He has delivered the walls of her palaces into the enemy’s hand; they have raised a shout in the house of the LORD as on a feast day.
The LORD determined to destroy the wall of Daughter Zion. He stretched out a measuring line and did not withhold His hand from destroying. He made rampart and wall lament; together they wasted away.
Her gates have sunk into the ground; He has destroyed and broken her bars. Her king and princes are among the nations; the law is no more, and her prophets find no vision from the LORD.
The elders of Daughter Zion sit on the ground in silence; they have thrown dust on their heads and put on sackcloth. The virgins of Jerusalem have bowed their heads to the ground.
My eyes are spent with tears; my soul is in anguish; my heart is poured out on the ground because of the ruin of my people, because children and nursing infants faint in the streets of the city.
They cry out to their mothers, “Where is grain and wine?” as they faint like the wounded in the streets of the city, as their lives are poured out in their mothers’ arms.
What can I say for you? To what can I compare you, Daughter Jerusalem? To what can I liken you, that I may comfort you, Virgin Daughter Zion? For your wound is as deep as the sea. Who can heal you?
Your prophets have seen for you false and foolish visions; they have not exposed your iniquity to restore your fortunes, but have seen for you false oracles and misleading delusions.
All who pass by clap their hands at you; they hiss and shake their heads at Daughter Jerusalem: “Is this the city that was called the perfection of beauty, the joy of all the earth?”
All your enemies open their mouths against you; they hiss and gnash their teeth. They say, “We have swallowed her up. This is the day we have waited for; we have lived to see it.”

The LORD has done what He planned; He has fulfilled His word, which He commanded long ago. He has overthrown you without pity; He has let the enemy gloat over you; He has exalted the horn of your foes.
Their hearts cried out to the Lord. O wall of Daughter Zion, let your tears flow like a river day and night. Give yourself no rest; let your eyes find no rest.

Arise, cry out in the night at the beginning of the watches; pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord. Lift up your hands to Him for the lives of your children, who faint from hunger at the head of every street.

Look, O the LORD, and consider: Whom have You ever treated like this? Should women eat their offspring, the children they have nurtured? Should priest and prophet be slain in the sanctuary of the Lord?
Young and old lie together in the streets; my young men and maidens have fallen by the sword. You have slain them in the day of Your anger; You have slaughtered them without mercy.
You summoned my terrors on every side, as on a feast day. In the day of the LORD’s anger no one escaped or survived; those I nurtured and reared, my enemy has destroyed.
I am the man who has seen affliction under the rod of His wrath.
He has driven me and brought me into darkness, with no light.
Surely against me He turns His hand again and again, all day long.
He has worn out my flesh and skin; He has broken my bones.
He has besieged me and surrounded me with bitterness and hardship.
He has made me dwell in darkness like those long dead.
He has walled me in so that I cannot escape; He has weighed me down with heavy chains.
Even when I cry out and plead for help, He shuts out my prayer.
He has blocked my paths with hewn stone and made my ways crooked.
He is to me like a bear lying in wait, a lion in hiding.
He has turned aside my paths and torn me to pieces; He has made me desolate.
He has bent His bow and set me as a target for the arrow.
He has pierced my kidneys with the arrows of His quiver.
I have become a laughingstock to all my people; they mock me in song all day long.
He has filled me with bitterness and given me gall to drink.
He has broken my teeth with gravel and covered me with ashes.
My soul has been deprived of peace; I have forgotten prosperity.
I said, "My endurance is gone, and my hope in the LORD has perished."
Remember my affliction and my wandering, the bitterness and the poison.
My soul remembers them and is bowed down within me.
Yet this I call to mind, and therefore I have hope:
Because of the LORD's steadfast love we are not consumed, for His mercies never fail.
They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness.
"The LORD is my portion," says my soul, "therefore I will hope in Him."
The LORD is good to those who wait for Him, to the soul who seeks Him.
It is good to wait quietly for the salvation of the LORD.
It is good for a man to bear the yoke in his youth.
He sits alone and keeps silent, for the LORD has laid it upon him.
Let him put his mouth in the dust—there may yet be hope.
Let him offer his cheek to the one who strikes him; let him be filled with disgrace.
For the Lord will not cast off forever.
Though He brings grief, He will show compassion according to His abundant steadfast love.
For He does not afflict from His heart or grieve the children of men.
To crush underfoot all the prisoners of the earth,
to deny a man justice before the Most High,
to subvert a person in his lawsuit—the Lord does not approve.
Who has spoken and it came to pass, unless the Lord has commanded it?
Is it not from the mouth of the Most High that both calamity and good proceed?
Why should a living man complain, a man, concerning the punishment for his sins?
Let us examine and probe our ways, and let us return to the LORD.
Let us lift up our hearts and hands to God in heaven.
We have sinned and rebelled; You have not forgiven.
You have covered Yourself with anger and pursued us; You have slain without pity.
You have wrapped Yourself in a cloud so that no prayer can pass through.
You have made us scum and refuse among the nations.
All our enemies open their mouths against us.
Terror and the pit have come upon us, devastation and destruction.
Streams of tears flow from my eyes because of the destruction of the daughter of my people.
My eyes will flow without ceasing, without relief,
until the LORD looks down and sees from heaven.
My eyes bring grief to my soul because of all the daughters of my city.
My enemies hunted me like a bird without cause.
They flung me alive into a pit and cast stones at me.
Waters closed over my head; I said, "I am cut off."
I called on Your name, the LORD, from the depths of the pit.
You heard my voice; do not hide Your ear from my cry for relief.
You drew near on the day I called on You; You said, "Do not fear."
You have pleaded my cause, O Lord; You have redeemed my life.
You, the LORD, have seen the wrong done to me; judge my case.
You have seen all their vengeance, all their schemes against me.
You, the LORD, have heard their taunts, all their schemes against me,
the whispers and murmurs of my adversaries against me all day long.
Look at their sitting down and their rising up; I am their mocking song.
Repay them, the LORD, according to the work of their hands.
Give them anguish of heart; Your curse be upon them.
Pursue them in anger and destroy them from under the heavens of the LORD.
Alas, how the gold has dimmed, the finest gold altered; the sacred stones lie scattered at every street corner.
Zion's precious sons, once valued like pure gold, are now reckoned as earthen vessels, the work of a potter's hands.
Even jackals offer the breast to nurse their young, but the daughter of my people has become cruel, like ostriches in the wilderness.
The nursing child's tongue clings to the roof of its mouth for thirst; little children beg for bread, yet no one gives them any.
Those who once feasted on delicacies perish in the streets; those reared in scarlet embrace ash heaps.
The punishment of the daughter of my people exceeds the sin of Sodom, which was overthrown in an instant without human hands.
Her nobles were purer than snow, whiter than milk; their bodies were ruddier than coral, their forms like sapphire.
Now their faces are darker than soot; they are not recognized in the streets; their skin has shriveled upon their bones and become as dry as wood.
Those slain by the sword are better off than those slain by famine, who waste away, pierced through, for lack of the field's produce.
The hands of compassionate women have boiled their own children; they became food for them in the destruction of the daughter of my people.
The LORD has vented His wrath; He has poured out His fierce anger. He set fire to Zion, and it consumed her foundations.
The kings of the earth and all the inhabitants of the world did not believe that foe or enemy could enter the gates of Jerusalem.
It was because of the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests, who shed the blood of the righteous in her midst.
They wandered blind through the streets, defiled with blood, so that no one could touch their garments.
"Depart! Unclean!" people cried to them. "Depart, depart, do not touch!" So they fled and wandered; among the nations it was said, "They shall dwell here no longer."
The LORD Himself scattered them; He will no longer regard them. They did not honor the priests, nor show favor to the elders.
Our eyes still fail, watching in vain for help; from our watchtowers we watched for a nation that could not save.
They stalked our steps so that we could not walk in our streets; our end drew near, our days were finished, for our end had come.
Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles of heaven; they chased us over the mountains and ambushed us in the wilderness.
The LORD's Anointed, the breath of our life, was caught in their pits. We had said, "Under his shadow we shall live among the nations."
Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom, you who dwell in the land of Uz; yet the cup will pass to you; you will be drunk and exposed.
O daughter of Zion, your iniquity is accomplished; He will not exile you again. He will punish your iniquity, O daughter of Edom; He will expose your sins.
Remember, the LORD, what has befallen us; look upon our disgrace and see it.
Our inheritance has been transferred to strangers, and our dwellings to foreigners.
We have become orphans, fatherless; our mothers are like widows.
We must purchase the water we drink, and our wood comes only at a price.
Our pursuers press upon our necks; we are exhausted, and no rest is granted to us.
We have submitted to Egypt and to Assyria merely to obtain sufficient bread.
Our fathers sinned and are gone, yet we bear their iniquities.
Slaves dominate us, and there is no deliverer from their hand.
We obtain our bread at the risk of our lives, because of the sword in the wilderness.
Our skin is scorched like an oven by the fierce heat of famine.
Women are violated in Zion, and virgins in the cities of Judah.
Princes are suspended by their hands, and the elders receive no honor.
Young men are compelled to grind at the mill, and boys stagger under burdens of wood.
The elders have abandoned the city gate, and the young men their songs.
The joy of our hearts has ceased; our dancing has been turned into mourning.
The crown has fallen from our head; woe to us, for we have sinned!
For this our hearts are faint; for these things our eyes grow dim—for Mount Zion, which lies desolate, where jackals roam.
But You, the LORD, reign forever; Your throne endures from generation to generation.
Why do You forget us forever? Why do You forsake us for so many days?
Restore us to Yourself, the LORD, that we may be restored; renew our days as of old—
unless You have utterly rejected us and remain exceedingly angry with us.
In the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, while I was among the exiles by the river Chebar, the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.
On the fifth day of the month—it was the fifth year of the exile of King Jehoiachin—
the word of the the LORD came to Ezekiel the priest, son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar; and the hand of the the LORD was upon him there.

As I looked, a storm wind came from the north—a great cloud with fire flashing forth continually, and brightness all around it; and from its midst came something like gleaming metal, from the midst of the fire.
From its midst also came the likeness of four living creatures, and this was their appearance: they had the likeness of a man.
Each had four faces and four wings.
Their legs were straight, and the soles of their feet were like the hooves of a calf; they gleamed like burnished bronze.
Human hands were beneath their wings on their four sides; and the four of them had faces and wings.
Their wings touched one another; they did not turn when they went, but each went straight ahead.
As for the likeness of their faces, each had a human face; on the right, a lion's face; on the left, an ox's face; and all four had an eagle's face.
Their faces and wings were separated above; two wings of each touched one another, and two covered their bodies.
Each went straight ahead; wherever the spirit was about to go, they went, without turning as they went.

As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, like torches moving back and forth among the living creatures; the fire was radiant, and lightning flashed out of it.
The living creatures darted to and fro like flashes of lightning.
Now as I looked at the living creatures, a wheel was on the ground beside each living creature, corresponding to its four faces.
The appearance of the wheels and their construction was like the gleam of beryl, and all four had the same likeness; their appearance and construction were as though a wheel were within a wheel.
When they went, they went in any of their four directions without turning as they went.
As for their rims, they were high and awe-inspiring, and their rims were full of eyes all around the four of them.
When the living creatures went, the wheels went beside them; and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up.
Wherever the spirit was about to go, they went in that direction, and the wheels rose close beside them; for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.

When those went, these went; and when those stood still, these stood still; and when those were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up close beside them; for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
Over the heads of the living creatures there was the likeness of an expanse, shining like crystal, spread out above their heads.
Under the expanse their wings were straight, one toward the other; each had two which covered their bodies on this side and two which covered on that side.

When they moved, I heard the sound of their wings like the sound of many waters, like the voice of the Almighty—a sound of turmoil like the sound of an army. When they stood still, they lowered their wings.
A voice came from above the expanse that was over their heads; when they stood still, they lowered their wings.
Above the expanse over their heads was the likeness of a throne, in appearance like a sapphire stone; and on the throne, high up, was a figure with the appearance of a man.

From what appeared to be His waist upward, I saw something like gleaming metal, like fire enclosed all around; and from His waist downward, I saw what looked like fire, with brightness surrounding it.

Like the appearance of the rainbow in the clouds on a rainy day, so was the appearance of the surrounding radiance. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the the LORD. And when I saw it, I fell on my face and heard a voice speaking.
He said to me, “Mortal man, rise to your feet, and I will speak with you.”
As He spoke to me, the Spirit entered me and raised me to my feet, and I heard Him speaking.
He said to me, “Mortal man, I am sending you to the Israelites, to a rebellious nation that has rebelled against Me. They and their ancestors have transgressed against Me to this very day.
They are brazen and hard-hearted descendants; to them I am sending you, and you must tell them, ‘This is what the Lord, the LORD, says.’
Whether they listen or refuse—for they are a rebellious people—they will know that a prophet has been among them.”

“And you, mortal man, do not fear them or their words, though you are surrounded by people as hostile as thorns and as dangerous as scorpions. Do not fear their words, and do not be dismayed by their looks, for they are a rebellious people.
You must speak My words to them, whether they listen or refuse, for they are a rebellious people.
But you, mortal man, hear what I am saying to you. Do not be rebellious like that rebellious people; open your mouth and eat what I give you.”
Then I looked, and, to my astonishment, a hand was extended toward me, holding a scroll.
He spread it before me; it was written on both sides, and inscribed upon it were lamentations, mourning, and woe.
And He said to me, “Son of man, eat what you find; eat this scroll, and go, speak to the house of Israel.”
So I opened my mouth, and He fed me the scroll.
Then He said to me, “Son of man, eat this scroll that I am giving you, and fill your stomach with it.” So I ate it, and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth.
Then He said to me, “Son of man, go to the house of Israel and speak My words to them.
For you are not being sent to a people of unfamiliar speech and difficult language, but to the house of Israel—
not to many peoples of unfamiliar speech and difficult language whose words you cannot understand. Surely, if I had sent you to them, they would have listened to you.
But the house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you, because they are not willing to listen to Me. For the whole house of Israel is stubborn and obstinate.
Behold, I have made your face as hard as their faces, and your forehead as hard as their foreheads.
I have made your forehead like diamond, harder than flint. Do not fear them or be dismayed by their presence, though they are a rebellious house.”
Moreover, He said to me, “Son of man, take all My words that I speak to you to heart, and listen with your ears.
Go now to your people in exile and speak to them. Tell them, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says,’ whether they listen or refuse.”
Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me a great rumbling: “Blessed be the glory of the the LORD from His place!”
It was the sound of the wings of the living creatures brushing against one another and the sound of the wheels beside them—a great rumbling.
So the Spirit lifted me up and carried me away, and I went in bitterness and in the anger of my spirit, while the hand of the the LORD was strong upon me.
I came to the exiles at Tel Abib, who were living by the Kebar River, and I sat among them, overwhelmed, for seven days.
At the end of seven days the word of the the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from My mouth, warn them for Me.

When I say to a wicked person, ‘You will surely die,’ and you do not warn him or speak to turn him from his wicked way so that he may live, that wicked person will die in his iniquity, and I will hold you accountable for his blood.
But if you warn a wicked person and he does not turn from his wickedness and his wicked way, he will die in his iniquity, but you will have saved yourself.

Again, if a righteous person turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, and I place a stumbling block before him, he will die. Since you did not warn him, he will die in his sin, and his righteous deeds will not be remembered; but I will hold you accountable for his blood.
But if you warn a righteous person not to sin, and he does not sin, he will live because he heeded the warning, and you will have saved yourself.”
Then the hand of the the LORD was upon me, and He said, “Get up and go out to the plain, and there I will speak with you.”
So I got up and went out to the plain, and there stood the glory of the the LORD, like the glory I had seen by the Kebar River, and I fell on my face.
Then the Spirit entered me and set me on my feet. He spoke to me and said, “Go, shut yourself inside your house.
And you, Son of man, they will put ropes on you and bind you with them, so that you cannot go out among them.
I will make your tongue cling to the roof of your mouth, so that you will be mute and unable to rebuke them, for they are a rebellious house.

But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you will say to them, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says.’ Whoever listens, let him listen; and whoever refuses, let him refuse, for they are a rebellious house.”
And you, son of man, take a brick for yourself, set it before you, and inscribe on it a city—Jerusalem.
Lay siege to it: build a siege wall against it, raise a siege ramp against it, pitch camps against it, and station battering rams around it on every side.
Then take an iron plate and set it as an iron wall between you and the city; fix your face against it, and let it be besieged while you besiege it. This shall be a sign to the house of Israel.
Lie on your left side and place the iniquity of the house of Israel upon it; you shall bear their iniquity for the number of days you lie on it.
For I have assigned you three hundred and ninety days, corresponding to the years of their iniquity, and you shall bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.
When you have completed these, lie again on your right side and bear the iniquity of the house of Judah. I have assigned it to you for forty days, a day for each year.
Set your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, with your arm bared, and prophesy against it.
Behold, I will bind you with cords, so that you cannot turn from one side to the other until you have completed the days of your siege.

And you, take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt, and put them into one vessel, and make bread from them; you shall eat it for the three hundred and ninety days that you lie on your side.
The food you eat shall be by weight—twenty shekels a day—and you shall eat it at fixed times.
You shall drink water by measure, a sixth of a hin, and you shall drink it at fixed times.
You shall eat it as a barley cake baked publicly over human dung.
The LORD said, "Thus shall the sons of Israel eat their defiled bread among the nations, where I will drive them."

Then I said, "Ah, Lord the LORD! Behold, I have never defiled myself; from my youth until now I have not eaten what died of itself or was torn by beasts, nor has any abominable flesh entered my mouth."
He said to me, "See, I give you cow dung instead of human dung, and you shall prepare your bread over it."
And He said to me, "Son of man, behold, I am breaking the supply of bread in Jerusalem. They shall eat bread by weight and in anxiety, and drink water by measure and in dismay,
so that they may lack bread and water, be appalled at one another, and waste away because of their iniquity."
"And you, son of man, take for yourself a sharp sword; take it as a barber's razor and pass it over your head and over your beard; then take scales for weighing and divide them.

During the days of the siege, when they are completed, burn a third in the fire in the midst of the city; take a third and strike around it with the sword; scatter a third to the wind, and I will draw the sword after them.
Take from there a few in number and bind them in your skirts.
Take some of them again and throw them into the midst of the fire and burn them in the fire; from it a fire will go out to all the house of Israel.
"Thus says the Lord the LORD: This is Jerusalem; I have set her in the midst of the nations, with countries all around her.

She has rebelled against My ordinances by doing wickedness more than the nations, and against My statutes more than the countries around her, for they have rejected My ordinances and have not walked in them.

Therefore thus says the Lord the LORD: Because you were more turbulent than the nations around you, and you have not walked in My statutes, nor have you done My ordinances, but you have done according to the ordinances of the nations around you.
Therefore thus says the Lord the LORD: Behold, I, even I, am against you, and I will execute judgments in your midst in the sight of the nations.
Because of all your abominations, I will do to you what I have not done, and the like of which I will not do again.
"Therefore fathers will eat their sons in your midst, and sons will eat their fathers; and I will execute judgments on you, and I will scatter all your remnant to every wind.

Therefore, as I live, says the Lord the LORD, surely because you have defiled My sanctuary with all your detestable things and with all your abominations, I will also withdraw My gaze; My eye will not spare, and I will have no pity.

A third of you will die by pestilence and be consumed by famine in your midst; a third will fall by the sword around you; and a third I will scatter to every wind, and I will draw the sword after them.

Thus My anger will be spent, and I will cause My wrath to rest on them, and I will be appeased; and they will know that I am the LORD, that I have spoken in My zeal when I have spent My wrath on them.
I will make you a desolation and a reproach among the nations that are around you, in the sight of all who pass by.

It will be a reproach and a taunt, an instruction and an astonishment to the nations that are around you, when I execute judgments on you in anger and in wrath and in furious rebukes. I, the LORD, have spoken.
When I send against them the deadly arrows of famine, which are for destruction, which I will send to destroy you, I will increase the famine upon you and break your staff of bread.
I will send upon you famine and evil beasts, and they will bereave you; pestilence and blood will pass through you, and I will bring the sword upon you. I, the LORD, have spoken."
The word of the LORD came to me, saying:
“Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them.”

“Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord the LORD! Thus says the Lord the LORD to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys: I am about to bring a sword against you, and I will destroy your high places.
Your altars will be desolate, your incense altars will be smashed, and I will cast down your slain before your idols.
I will lay the corpses of the Israelites before their idols, and I will scatter your bones around your altars.

In all your dwellings the cities will be laid waste, and the high places will be desolate, so that your altars may be ruined and desolate, your idols broken and brought to nothing, your incense altars cut down, and your works blotted out.
The slain will fall in your midst, and you will know that I am the LORD.”
“Yet I will leave a remnant, so that you will have some who escape the sword among the nations when you are scattered among the countries.

Then those of you who escape will remember Me among the nations where they are carried captive, because I was crushed by their adulterous heart that turned away from Me, and by their eyes that lusted after their idols; and they will loathe themselves for the evils they have committed, for all their abominations.
They will know that I am the LORD; I have not spoken in vain when I said I would bring this evil upon them.”

Thus says the Lord the LORD: “Clap your hand and stamp your foot, and say, ‘Alas!’ because of all the evil abominations of the house of Israel, for they will fall by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence.
He who is far away will die by pestilence, he who is near will fall by the sword, and he who remains and is besieged will die by famine; and I will spend My fury upon them.

Then you will know that I am the LORD, when their slain lie among their idols around their altars, on every high hill and on all the mountaintops, under every green tree and under every leafy oak—wherever they offered a pleasing aroma to all their idols.
I will stretch out My hand against them and make the land a desolation and a waste, from the wilderness to Diblah; and they will know that I am the LORD.”
The word of the the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, this is what the Lord the LORD says to the land of Israel: The end! The end has come upon the four corners of the land.
The end is now upon you, and I will send My anger against you; I will judge you according to your ways and repay you for all your abominations.
My eye will not spare you, nor will I have pity; I will bring your ways upon you, and your abominations will be in your midst. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
“Thus says the Lord the LORD: Disaster! An unprecedented disaster! Behold, it is coming.
The end has come; the end has come; it has roused itself against you. Behold, it is coming.
Doom has come upon you, O inhabitant of the land. The time has come; the day is near—tumult rather than joyful shouting on the mountains.
“Now I will soon pour out My wrath upon you and spend My anger against you; I will judge you according to your ways and repay you for all your abominations.
My eye will not spare you, nor will I have pity; I will repay you according to your ways, while your abominations are in your midst. Then you will know that I, the LORD, am the One who strikes.
“Behold, the day! Behold, it comes! Doom has gone forth; the rod has blossomed; arrogance has sprouted.
Violence has risen into a rod of wickedness; none of them shall remain—neither their multitude nor their wealth—and there will be no lamentation among them.
“The time has come; the day has arrived. Let not the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn, for wrath is upon all their multitude.

For the seller shall not return to what he has sold, as long as they live; for the vision concerning all their multitude will not be revoked, and because of their iniquity no one among them will preserve his life.
They have blown the trumpet and prepared everything, but no one goes to battle, for My wrath is upon all their multitude.
“The sword is outside, and pestilence and famine are within; he who is in the field will die by the sword, and he who is in the city will be consumed by famine and pestilence.
But those who escape will flee to the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them moaning, each one for his own iniquity.
“All hands will falter, and every knee will buckle.
They will gird themselves with sackcloth, and shuddering will cover them; shame will be on every face, and baldness on all their heads.

“They will cast their silver into the streets, and their gold will become an unclean thing; their silver and gold will not be able to deliver them in the day of the the LORD's wrath. They will not satisfy their appetites or fill their stomachs, for their wealth has become the stumbling block of their iniquity.
They took pride in their beautiful jewelry and made from it their detestable images and abominations; therefore I have made it an unclean thing to them.
“I will hand it over to foreigners as plunder, and to the wicked of the earth as spoil, and they will profane it.
I will turn My face away from them, and they will profane My treasured place; robbers will enter it and profane it.
“Forge the chain, for the land is full of bloodshed and the city is full of violence.
I will bring the most ruthless of the nations, and they will take possession of their houses; I will put an end to the pride of the mighty, and their holy places will be profaned.
“Anguish is coming; they will seek peace, but there will be none.
Disaster upon disaster will come, and rumor upon rumor; they will seek a vision from a prophet, but the law will vanish from the priest and counsel from the elders.

The king will mourn, the prince will be clothed in despair, and the hands of the people of the land will tremble. I will deal with them according to their conduct, and I will judge them by their own standards. Then they will know that I am the LORD.”
In the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth day of the month, I was sitting in my house, and the elders of Judah were sitting before me, when the hand of the Lord the LORD fell upon me there.
I looked, and I saw a figure. From what appeared to be His waist down, it was like fire, and from His waist up, His appearance was as bright as gleaming metal.

He stretched out the form of a hand and took me by a lock of my head. The Spirit lifted me up between earth and heaven and brought me in visions of God to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the inner gate that faces north, where the seat of the image of jealousy, which provokes jealousy, was located.
And there I saw the glory of the God of Israel, just as I had seen in the plain.
He said to me, “Son of man, lift your eyes toward the north.” So I lifted my eyes toward the north, and there, north of the altar gate, was this image of jealousy at the entrance.

He said to me, “Son of man, do you see what they are doing? They are committing great abominations here, by which the house of Israel is driving Me far from My sanctuary. But you will see still greater abominations.”
Then He brought me to the entrance of the court, and I looked and saw a hole in the wall.
He said to me, “Son of man, dig through the wall.” So I dug through the wall and saw a doorway.
He said to me, “Go in and see the wicked abominations they are committing here.”
So I went in and looked, and I saw carved all around the walls every kind of creeping thing, detestable animal, and all the idols of the house of Israel.
Standing before them were seventy men of the elders of Israel, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan among them. Each had a censer in his hand, and a thick cloud of incense was rising.

He said to me, “Son of man, have you seen what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in the dark, each in his own hidden chamber of idols? For they are saying, ‘The LORD does not see us; the LORD has abandoned the land.’”
He said to me, “You will see them committing still greater abominations.”
Then He brought me to the entrance of the north gate of the house of the LORD, and there I saw women sitting and weeping for Tammuz.
He said to me, “Son of man, have you seen this? You will see still greater abominations than these.”

He brought me into the inner court of the house of the LORD, and there at the entrance to the temple of the LORD, between the portico and the altar, were about twenty-five men. They had turned their backs to the temple of the LORD and their faces toward the east, and they were bowing down to the sun in the east.

He said to me, “Son of man, have you seen this? Is it a trivial thing for the house of Judah to commit the abominations they are practicing here? For they have filled the land with violence and have returned to provoke Me to anger, and behold, they are treating Me with open contempt.”
Therefore I will act in wrath. My eye will not spare them, nor will I have pity. Though they cry out to Me with a loud voice, I will not listen to them.
Then I heard Him call out in a loud voice, “Draw near, O executioners of the city, each with his weapon of destruction in his hand.”

Suddenly six men came from the direction of the upper gate, which faces north, each carrying his weapon of slaughter. Among them was a man clothed in linen with a writing kit at his waist. They came in and stood beside the bronze altar.
Now the glory of the God of Israel had gone up from the cherub, where it had been, to the threshold of the temple. And the LORD called to the man clothed in linen who had the writing kit at his waist
and said to him, “Go throughout the city of Jerusalem and put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and groan over all the abominations committed in it.”
And to the others He said in my hearing, “Follow him through the city and strike. Do not let your eyes pity or spare anyone.

“Slaughter the old men, the young men and maidens, the women and children; but do not touch anyone who has the mark. And begin at My sanctuary.” So they began with the elders who were before the temple.
Then He said to them, “Defile the temple and fill the courts with the slain. Go out!” So they went out and began killing throughout the city.
While they were killing, I was left alone. I fell facedown and cried out, “Alas, O Lord the LORD! Will You destroy the entire remnant of Israel by pouring out Your wrath on Jerusalem?”

He replied, “The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great. The land is full of bloodshed, and the city is full of perversity. For they say, ‘The LORD has forsaken the land, and the LORD does not see.’
But as for Me, I will not look with pity, nor will I spare them. I will bring their deeds upon their own heads.”
Then the man clothed in linen with the writing kit at his waist reported back, “I have done as You commanded.”
Then I looked, and behold, above the expanse that was over the heads of the cherubim there appeared something like a sapphire stone, in appearance like a throne.

And He spoke to the man clothed in linen, saying, "Go in among the wheels beneath the cherub, and fill your hands with burning coals from between the cherubim, and scatter them over the city." And he went in as I watched.
Now the cherubim were standing on the south side of the temple when the man went in, and the cloud filled the inner court.
Then the glory of the LORD rose from above the cherub to the threshold of the temple; the temple was filled with the cloud, and the court was filled with the brightness of the glory of the LORD.
And the sound of the wings of the cherubim was heard as far as the outer court, like the voice of God Almighty when He speaks.
When He commanded the man clothed in linen, saying, "Take fire from between the wheels, from between the cherubim," he went in and stood beside a wheel.
Then the cherub stretched out his hand from between the cherubim to the fire that was between the cherubim, took some, and put it into the hands of the man clothed in linen, who took it and went out.
The cherubim appeared to have the form of a man's hand under their wings.
Then I looked, and behold, four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel beside each cherub; and the appearance of the wheels was like the gleaming of a beryl stone.
As for their appearance, all four had the same likeness, as if a wheel were within a wheel.
When they moved, they went in any of their four directions without turning as they went; but they followed in the direction the head faced without turning as they went.
Their entire bodies, their backs, their hands, and their wings were full of eyes all around, as were their four wheels.
In my hearing, the wheels were called "the whirling wheels."
Each one had four faces: the first face was that of a cherub, the second the face of a man, the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle.
Then the cherubim rose upward. These were the living creatures I had seen by the Kebar River.
When the cherubim moved, the wheels moved beside them; and when the cherubim lifted their wings to rise from the ground, the wheels did not turn from beside them.
When the cherubim stood still, the wheels stood still; and when they rose, the wheels rose with them, because the spirit of the living creatures was in them.
Then the glory of the LORD moved from the threshold of the temple and stood above the cherubim.

As I watched, the cherubim lifted their wings and rose up from the ground, with the wheels beside them. They stopped at the entrance of the east gate of the LORD's house, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
These were the living creatures I had seen beneath the God of Israel by the Kebar River, and I knew that they were cherubim.
Each had four faces and four wings, and under their wings was something like human hands.
Their faces were the same as those I had seen by the Kebar River. Each one moved straight ahead.

The Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the east gate of the house of the the LORD, which faces east. And behold, at the entrance of the gateway there were twenty-five men. Among them I saw Jaazaniah son of Azur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, leaders of the people.
And He said to me, "Son of man, these are the men who devise iniquity and give wicked counsel in this city."
They say, "We need not build houses yet; this city is like a secure pot, and we are safe within it."
Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, son of man.
Then the Spirit of the the LORD fell upon me, and He said to me, "Say: Thus says the the LORD: That is exactly what you are thinking, O house of Israel, for I know what comes into your mind.
You have multiplied your slain in this city and filled its streets with the slain.
"Therefore thus says the Lord the LORD: Your slain whom you have laid in its midst, they are the meat, and this city is the pot; but I will bring you out of its midst.
You fear the sword, and I will bring the sword upon you, declares the Lord the LORD.
"I will bring you out of its midst and give you into the hand of foreigners, and execute judgments among you.
You shall fall by the sword; I will judge you at the border of Israel, and you shall know that I am the the LORD.
"This city shall not be your pot, nor shall you be the meat in its midst. I will judge you at the border of Israel.
And you shall know that I am the the LORD, for you have not walked in My statutes, nor executed My judgments, but have done according to the judgments of the nations that are around you."
When I prophesied, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. Then I fell on my face and cried out with a loud voice and said, "Ah, Lord the LORD! Will You make a full end of the remnant of Israel?"
Again the word of the the LORD came to me, saying,

"Son of man, your brothers—your brothers, the men of your kindred and all the house of Israel, all of them—are those of whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said, 'Go far away from the the LORD; this land has been given to us for a possession.'

"Therefore say: Thus says the Lord the LORD: Although I have removed them far off among the nations and scattered them among the countries, yet I have been a sanctuary to them for a little while in the countries where they have gone.
"Therefore say: Thus says the Lord the LORD: I will gather you from the peoples and assemble you out of the countries where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.
And when they come there, they will remove from it all its detestable things and all its abominations.
"And I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within them. I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,
that they may walk in My statutes and keep My rules and obey them. And they shall be My people, and I will be their God.
"But as for those whose heart goes after their detestable things and their abominations, I will bring their conduct down upon their own heads, declares the Lord the LORD."
Then the cherubim lifted up their wings, with the wheels beside them, and the glory of the God of Israel was over them above.
And the glory of the the LORD went up from the midst of the city and stood on the mountain that is on the east side of the city.
Then the Spirit lifted me up and brought me in a vision by the Spirit of God into Chaldea, to the exiles. Then the vision that I had seen went up from me.
And I spoke to the exiles all the things that the the LORD had shown me.
The word of the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, you dwell among a rebellious house—people who have eyes to see but do not see, and ears to hear but do not hear—because they are a rebellious house.

As for you, Son of man, prepare an exile’s baggage for yourself, and go into exile by day in their sight. You shall go from your place to another place in their sight; perhaps they will understand, though they are a rebellious house.
You shall bring out your baggage by day in their sight, as baggage for exile, and you shall go out at evening in their sight, as those who must go into exile.
In their sight dig through the wall for yourself, and bring your baggage out through it.
In their sight you shall lift the baggage upon your shoulder and carry it out at dusk. You shall cover your face so that you may not see the land, for I have made you a sign for the house of Israel.”

I did as I was commanded. I brought out my baggage by day, as baggage for exile, and in the evening I dug through the wall with my own hands. I brought out my baggage at dusk, carrying it on my shoulder in their sight.
In the morning the word of the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, has not the house of Israel, the rebellious house, said to you, ‘What are you doing?’
Say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: This oracle concerns the prince in Jerusalem and all the house of Israel who are in it.’
Say, ‘I am a sign for you: as I have done, so shall it be done to them. They shall go into exile, into captivity.’

And the prince who is among them shall lift his baggage upon his shoulder at dusk, and shall go out. They shall dig through the wall to bring him out through it. He shall cover his face, so that he may not see the land with his eyes.
I will spread My net over him, and he shall be taken in My snare. I will bring him to Babylon, to the land of the Chaldeans, yet he shall not see it, and he shall die there.
I will scatter to every wind all who are around him, his helpers and all his troops, and I will draw the sword after them.
And they shall know that I am the LORD, when I disperse them among the nations and scatter them among the countries.
But I will let a few of them escape from the sword, from famine and pestilence, that they may declare all their abominations among the nations where they go, and may know that I am the LORD.”
The word of the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, eat your bread with quaking, and drink your water with trembling and with anxiety.
