And say to the people of the land, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: Concerning the inhabitants of Jerusalem in the land of Israel, they shall eat their bread with anxiety and drink their water in dismay, because their land will be stripped of its fullness, on account of the violence of all those who dwell in it.’
And the inhabited cities shall be laid waste, and the land shall become a desolation; and you shall know that I am the LORD.”
The word of the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, what is this proverb that you have in the land of Israel, saying, ‘The days grow long, and every vision comes to nothing’?

Therefore say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: I will put an end to this proverb, and they shall no more use it as a proverb in Israel.’ But say, ‘The days are near, and the fulfillment of every vision.’
For there shall be no more any false vision or flattering divination within the house of Israel.

For I am the LORD; I will speak the word that I will speak, and it will be performed. It will no longer be delayed, but in your days, O rebellious house, I will speak the word and perform it, declares the Lord GOD.”
The word of the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, behold, the house of Israel say, ‘The vision that he sees is for many days from now, and he prophesies of times far off.’
Therefore say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: None of My words will be delayed any longer, but the word that I speak will be performed, declares the Lord GOD.’”
The word of the LORD came to me:
“Son of Man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who are prophesying, and say to those who prophesy from their own hearts, ‘Hear the word of the LORD!’
Thus says the Lord GOD: Woe to the foolish prophets who follow their own spirit and have seen nothing!
Your prophets, O Israel, have been like foxes among ruins.
You have not gone up into the breaches, nor built up a wall for the house of Israel, that it might stand in battle in the day of the LORD. “
They have seen false visions and lying divinations. They say, ‘Declares the the LORD!’ when the the LORD has not sent them, yet they expect Him to fulfill their word.
Have you not seen a false vision and uttered a lying divination whenever you have said, ‘Declares the the LORD!’ although I have not spoken? “
Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Because you have uttered falsehood and seen lying visions, therefore behold, I am against you, declares the Lord GOD.

My hand will be against the prophets who see false visions and who give lying divinations. They shall not be in the council of My people, nor be enrolled in the register of the house of Israel, nor shall they enter the land of Israel. And you shall know that I am the Lord GOD. “
Precisely because they have misled My people, saying, ‘Peace,’ when there is no peace, and because, when the people build a wall, these prophets smear it with whitewash,
say to those who smear it with whitewash that it shall fall! There shall be a deluge of rain, and you, O great hailstones, shall fall, and a stormy wind shall break out.
And when the wall falls, will it not be said to you, ‘Where is the coating with which you smeared it?’ “
Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: I will make a stormy wind break out in My wrath, and there shall be a deluge of rain in My anger, and great hailstones in wrath to make a full end.

And I will break down the wall that you have smeared with whitewash, and bring it down to the ground, so that its foundation will be laid bare. And it will fall, and you shall perish in the midst of it. And you shall know that I am the the LORD. “
Thus I will spend My wrath upon the wall and upon those who smeared it with whitewash, and I will say to you, ‘The wall is no more, and those who smeared it are no more—
the prophets of Israel who prophesied concerning Jerusalem and saw visions of peace for her, when there was no peace,’ declares the Lord GOD.” “
And you, Son of Man, turn against the daughters of your people who prophesy out of their own hearts; prophesy against them

and say, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: Woe to the women who sew magic bands upon all wrists and make veils over the heads of persons of every stature, to hunt souls! Will you hunt down the souls of My people and keep your own souls alive?

You have profaned Me among My people for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread, putting to death souls who should not die and keeping alive souls who should not live, by your lying to My people, who listen to lies.’ “

Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am against your magic bands with which you hunt the souls like birds, and I will tear them from your arms, and I will let the souls go, the souls that you hunt like birds.
I will also tear off your veils and deliver My people out of your hand, and they shall be no more in your hand as prey, and you shall know that I am the the LORD. “
Because you have disheartened the righteous with falsehood, although I did not grieve them, and have strengthened the hands of the wicked, so that he does not turn from his evil way and live,
therefore you shall no more see false visions nor practice divination. I will deliver My people from your hand. And you shall know that I am the the LORD.”
Some of the elders of Israel came to me and sat before me.
Then the word of the the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, these men have brought their idols into their hearts and have set the stumbling block of their iniquity before their faces. Should I allow Myself to be consulted by them at all?

“Therefore speak to them and say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord the the LORD: Every man of the house of Israel who sets up his idols in his heart and puts the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face, and then comes to the prophet, I the the LORD will answer him according to the multitude of his idols,
so that I may lay hold of the hearts of the house of Israel, because they have all turned away from Me through their idols.’
“Therefore say to the house of Israel, ‘Thus says the Lord the the LORD: Repent and turn away from your idols, and turn your faces away from all your abominations.’

For every man of the house of Israel, or of the strangers who sojourn in Israel, who separates himself from Me and sets up his idols in his heart and puts the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face, and comes to the prophet to inquire of Me concerning himself, I the the LORD will answer him Myself.
I will set My face against that man and make him a sign and a byword, and I will cut him off from the midst of My people, and you shall know that I am the the LORD.
“And if a prophet is deceived and speaks a word, I the the LORD have deceived that prophet, and I will stretch out My hand against him and destroy him from the midst of My people Israel.
They shall bear their iniquity; the iniquity of the one who inquires will be the same as the iniquity of the prophet.
so that the house of Israel may no longer stray from Me, nor defile themselves with all their transgressions, but that they may be My people and I may be their God, declares the Lord the the LORD.”
The word of the the LORD came to me, saying,

“Son of man, when a land sins against Me by trespassing grievously, and I stretch out My hand against it and break its supply of bread and send famine into it and cut off from it both people and animals,
even if these three men—Noah, Daniel, and Job—were in it, they could deliver only their own lives by their righteousness, declares the Lord the the LORD.
“If I cause wild beasts to pass through the land and they rob it of its children, so that it becomes desolate and no one passes through because of the beasts,
as I live, declares the Lord the the LORD, these three men in its midst would not deliver sons or daughters; they alone would be delivered, while the land would become desolate.
“Or if I bring a sword upon that land and say, ‘Let a sword pass through the land,’ and I cut off from it both people and animals,
as I live, declares the Lord the the LORD, these three men in its midst would not deliver sons or daughters; they alone would be delivered.
“Or if I send a pestilence into that land and pour out My wrath upon it in blood, to cut off from it both people and animals,
as I live, declares the Lord the the LORD, Noah, Daniel, and Job in its midst would not deliver son or daughter; they, by their righteousness, would deliver only their own lives.
“For thus says the Lord the the LORD: ‘How much more when I send upon Jerusalem My four dreadful judgments—sword, famine, wild beasts, and pestilence—to cut off from it both people and animals.’

Yet behold, survivors will be left in it, sons and daughters who will be brought out; behold, they will come out to you, and you will see their ways and their deeds, and you will be comforted concerning the disaster that I have brought upon Jerusalem, all that I have brought upon it.
They will comfort you when you see their ways and their deeds, and you will know that I have not done without cause all that I have done in it, declares the Lord the the LORD.”
The word of the the LORD came to me with this message:
“Son of man, in what respect does the wood of the vine surpass every other wood—the vine branch found among the trees of the forest?
Can wood be taken from it to fashion anything useful? Would anyone carve from it a peg on which to hang a vessel?
Behold, it is consigned to the fire for fuel; the fire has consumed both extremities, and its core is charred. Is it now fit for any work?
Behold, even when it was intact, it was not fashioned for work; how much less, after fire has consumed and charred it, can it be fashioned for work?”
“Therefore, this is what the Lord the the LORD declares: Just as the vine tree among the forest’s trees, which I consigned to the fire for fuel, so I have consigned the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
I will set My face against them; although they emerge from the fire, the fire will consume them. Then you shall know that I am the the LORD, when I set My face against them.
I will render the land desolate, because they have acted with treachery,” declares the Lord the the LORD.
The word of the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, confront Jerusalem with her abominations.”
Say, “Thus says the Lord GOD to Jerusalem: Your lineage and your nativity are rooted in the land of the Canaanites; your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite.
On the day of your birth, your umbilical cord remained uncut, nor were you cleansed with water. You were neither salted nor swaddled.
No eye pitied you enough to perform even one of these offices for you out of compassion. Rather, you were abandoned in the open field, held in contempt on the very day of your birth.
Then I passed by and beheld you weltering in your blood, and as you lay in your blood I declared to you, ‘Live!’
I caused you to thrive like a field plant. You grew, matured, and became surpassingly beautiful; your breasts were formed and your hair grew, though you were still naked and bare.

Then I passed by and saw you, and behold, your time had come, the time for love. So I spread My cloak over you and covered your nakedness. I swore to you and entered into a covenant with you, and you became Mine, declares the Lord GOD.
Then I bathed you with water, washed your blood from you, and anointed you with oil.
I clothed you in embroidered cloth and shod you with sandals of fine leather. I wrapped you in fine linen and covered you with silk.
I bedecked you with jewelry and put bracelets on your wrists and a chain around your neck.
I put a ring on your nose, earrings on your ears, and a splendid crown on your head.
So you were decked with gold and silver, and your clothing was fine linen, silk, and embroidered cloth. You ate fine flour, honey, and oil. You grew surpassingly beautiful and rose to queenship.
Your renown spread among the nations on account of your beauty, for it was flawless in the splendor I had conferred upon you, declares the Lord GOD.
But you reposed confidence in your beauty and played the harlot, and you squandered your charms upon every passerby, so that your beauty became theirs.
You took some of your garments and fashioned them into garish shrines, and on them you prostituted yourself. Such things ought never to have transpired; indeed, they should not have occurred at all.
You also took the fine jewelry of gold and silver that I had given you, and you fashioned male idols from them, prostituting yourself with them.
You took your embroidered garments to cover them, and you set My oil and My incense before them.
You also placed before them the food I had given you—the fine flour, oil, and honey with which I nourished you—and presented it to them as a fragrant offering, declares the Lord GOD.
You even took the sons and daughters you bore to Me and sacrificed them as sustenance to idols. Was your harlotry not sufficient?
You slaughtered My children and passed them through the fire to idols.
And amid all your abominations and harlotries, you did not recall the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, weltering in your blood.
‘Alas, alas for you!’ declares the Lord GOD. And after all your wickedness—
you erected a mound for yourself and established a high place in every square.
At the head of every street you built your high places and prostituted your beauty, offering yourself to every passerby and multiplying your harlotries.
You prostituted yourself with your libidinous neighbors, the Egyptians, and escalated your promiscuity to provoke Me to anger.
Therefore I stretched out My hand against you and reduced your portion. I gave you over to the desire of those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who were ashamed of your lewd conduct.
You also prostituted yourself with the Assyrians, because you remained unsatisfied; even then you were not satiated.
You multiplied your promiscuity with the land of the Chaldeans, yet even then you were not satiated.
How frail your heart is, declares the Lord GOD, when you do all these things, the doings of an impudent harlot!
When you erected your mounds at the head of every street and made your high places in every square, you were not even comparable
The word of the LORD came to me:
"Son of man, set forth a riddle and tell a parable to the house of Israel.
"Say: 'Thus says the Lord, the LORD: A great eagle with great wings and long pinions, full of plumage of many colors, came to Lebanon and took the top of the cedar.
He broke off its topmost shoot and carried it to a land of merchants, and he set it in a city of traders.
He took some of the seed of the land and planted it in fertile soil; he placed it beside abundant waters and set it out like a willow.
It sprouted and became a low, spreading vine, its branches turning toward him, while its roots remained beneath it. So it became a vine and sent out branches and put forth shoots.

But there was another great eagle with great wings and abundant plumage. Behold, this vine bent its roots toward him and sent out its branches toward him, away from the bed where it had been planted, that he might water it.
It had been planted in good soil beside abundant waters, so that it might bear branches and produce fruit and become a splendid vine.'

"Say: 'Thus says the Lord, the LORD: Will it prosper? Will he not pull up its roots and strip off its fruit, so that it withers—so that all its new growth withers? It will not take a strong arm or many people to pull it from its roots.
Behold, it is planted; will it prosper? When the east wind strikes it, will it not utterly wither? It will wither on the beds where it grew.'"
Then the word of the LORD came to me:

"Say now to the rebellious house, 'Do you not know what these things mean? Say: Behold, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and took its king and its princes and brought them to himself in Babylon.'
"He took one of the royal offspring and made a covenant with him, putting him under oath. He also took away the leading men of the land,
so that the kingdom might be brought low and not raise itself up, but keep his covenant in order to stand.
"But he rebelled against him by sending envoys to Egypt to obtain horses and a large army. Will he succeed? Will he escape who does such things? Can he break the covenant and yet escape?
As I live, declares the Lord, the LORD, surely in the place of the king who made him king—whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke—in Babylon he shall die.
Pharaoh with his mighty army and great company will not help him in war, when siege mounds are raised and siege walls built to cut off many lives.
He despised the oath by breaking the covenant, and behold, he gave his hand in pledge and did all these things; he shall not escape.
"Therefore thus says the Lord, the LORD: As I live, surely My oath that he despised and My covenant that he broke I will bring upon his head.
I will spread My net over him, and he shall be caught in My snare. I will bring him to Babylon and judge him there for the treachery he committed against Me.
All his fugitives in all his ranks shall fall by the sword, and those who remain shall be scattered to every wind. Then you shall know that I am the LORD; I have spoken."

"Thus says the Lord, the LORD: I Myself will take a sprig from the lofty top of the cedar and set it out. I will break off a tender shoot from the topmost of its young twigs and plant it on a high and lofty mountain.

On the mountain height of Israel I will plant it, that it may bear branches and produce fruit and become a noble cedar. Under it every kind of bird will dwell; in the shade of its branches birds of every sort will nest.

Then all the trees of the field shall know that I am the LORD. I bring down the high tree and exalt the low tree; I dry up the green tree and make the dry tree flourish. I am the LORD; I have spoken, and I will do it."
The word of the LORD came to me:
“What do you mean by repeating this proverb in the land of Israel: ‘The parents have sinned, and the children suffer the consequences’?
“As surely as I live, declares the Lord, the LORD, you will no longer repeat this proverb in Israel.
Indeed, every life belongs to Me; the life of the father and the life of the son alike are Mine. The person who sins is the one who will die.
“Suppose a man is righteous, practicing justice and righteousness—

if he does not join in sacrificial meals on the high places or worship the idols of the house of Israel, does not commit adultery with his neighbor’s wife or have sexual relations with a woman during her menstrual period,
does not oppress anyone, but returns a debtor’s collateral, commits no robbery, gives bread to the hungry, and clothes the naked,
does not lend at interest or take profit, refrains from injustice, and administers true justice between one person and another,
and lives by My statutes and faithfully keeps My ordinances—he is righteous; he will certainly live, declares the Lord, the LORD.
“Now suppose he fathers a son who is violent and sheds blood, committing any of these acts, although the father himself did none of them.
This son eats at the high places, commits adultery with his neighbor’s wife,
oppresses the poor and needy, commits robbery, refuses to return collateral, worships idols, and commits abominations,
lends at interest and takes profit. Shall such a man live? He will not live. Because he has committed all these abominations, he will certainly die, and his blood will be on his own head.
“Now suppose that wicked man has a son who sees all the sins his father committed; he observes them, yet refuses to imitate them.
He does not join in sacrificial meals on the high places or worship the idols of Israel, and does not commit adultery with his neighbor’s wife.
He does not oppress anyone, demands no collateral, commits no robbery, but gives bread to the hungry and clothes the naked.
He refrains from wrongdoing, takes no interest or profit, obeys My ordinances, and lives by My statutes. He will not die for his father’s guilt; he will certainly live.
As for his father, because he extorted, robbed his fellow citizen, and did what was evil among his people, he will die for his own iniquity.
“Yet you ask, ‘Why should the son not bear the father’s guilt?’ When the son has acted justly and rightly and has carefully observed all My statutes, he will certainly live.

The one who sins is the one who dies. A son will not bear his father’s guilt, and a father will not bear his son’s guilt. The righteousness of a righteous person will rest on him, and the wickedness of a wicked person will rest on him.
“But if a wicked person turns away from all the sins he has committed and keeps all My statutes, practicing justice and righteousness, he will certainly live; he will not die.
None of the transgressions he committed will be remembered against him; because of the righteousness he has practiced, he will live.
Do I take pleasure in the death of the wicked? declares the Lord, the LORD. Is it not rather My desire that he turn from his ways and live?

But if a righteous person turns away from his righteousness and commits injustice, doing the same abominations as the wicked, will he live? None of the righteous deeds he has done will be remembered; because of the treachery he has committed and the sin he has sinned, he will die.
“Yet you say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ Listen, house of Israel: Is My way not just? Are not your ways the ones that are unjust?
When a righteous person turns away from his righteousness and dies, he dies because of the iniquity he has committed.
And when a wicked person turns away from the wickedness he has committed and practices justice and righteousness, he will preserve his life.
Because he considered and turned away from all the transgressions he committed, he will certainly live; he will not die.
Yet the house of Israel says, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ House of Israel, are My ways not just? Are not your ways the ones that are unjust?

“Therefore I will judge you, house of Israel—each person according to his ways, declares the Lord, the LORD. Repent and turn away from all your transgressions, so that iniquity will not be your downfall.
Throw off from yourselves all the transgressions you have committed, and make for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why should you die, house of Israel?
For I take no pleasure in the death of anyone, declares the Lord, the LORD; therefore turn and live.”
And you, take up a lamentation for the princes of Israel.
And say, “What was your mother? A lioness among lions she crouched; among young lions she reared her cubs.
She brought up one of her cubs, and he became a young lion; he learned to tear his prey and devoured men.
The nations heard of him, so they caught him in their pit and brought him with hooks to the land of Egypt.
“When she saw that her hope was lost, she took another of her cubs and made him a young lion.
He prowled among the lions; he became a young lion, learned to tear his prey, and devoured men.
He violated their widows, laid waste their cities, and the land with all that filled it was appalled at the sound of his roaring.
Then nations from the surrounding provinces set themselves against him; they spread their net over him, and he was caught in their pit.
They put him in a cage with hooks and brought him to the king of Babylon; they brought him into fortresses, so that his voice would no longer be heard on the mountains of Israel.
“Your mother was like a vine in your lineage, planted by the waters; she was fruitful and full of branches because of abundant waters.
She had strong branches, fit for the scepters of rulers; her height was exalted among the clouds, and she was conspicuous in her height and in the multitude of her branches.
But she was uprooted in fury and thrown to the ground; the east wind dried up her fruit; her strong branches were broken and withered; fire consumed them.
Now she is planted in the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty land.
Fire has gone out from a rod of her branches and consumed her fruit, so that she has no strong branch—a scepter to rule. This is a lamentation, and it has become a lamentation.”
In the seventh year, on the tenth day of the fifth month, some of the elders of Israel came to inquire of the LORD, and they sat down before me.
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

“Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Have you come to inquire of Me? As surely as I live, I will not be consulted by you, declares the Lord GOD.’
Will you judge them, will you judge them, son of man? Confront them with the abominations of their fathers.

“And tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘On the day I chose Israel, I swore an oath to the descendants of the house of Jacob and made Myself known to them in the land of Egypt. I swore to them, saying, “I am the LORD your God.”’
On that day I swore to them that I would bring them out of the land of Egypt into a land I had searched out for them, a land flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all lands.
I said to them, ‘Each of you must throw away the abominations before his eyes, and you must not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.’

But they rebelled against Me and refused to listen. None of them cast away the detestable idols before their eyes, and they did not forsake the idols of Egypt. So I resolved to pour out My wrath on them and vent My anger against them in the land of Egypt.

But I acted for the sake of My name, so that it would not be profaned in the eyes of the nations among whom they lived, in whose sight I had revealed Myself to them by bringing them out of the land of Egypt.
“So I brought them out of the land of Egypt and led them into the wilderness.
And I gave them My statutes and made known to them My ordinances, by which a man will live if he practices them.
I also gave them My Sabbaths as a sign between us, so that they would know that I am the LORD who sanctifies them.

Yet the house of Israel rebelled against Me in the wilderness. They did not follow My statutes, and they rejected My ordinances, by which a man will live if he practices them. They greatly profaned My Sabbaths. So I resolved to pour out My wrath on them in the wilderness to consume them.
But I acted for the sake of My name, lest it be profaned in the eyes of the nations in whose sight I had brought them out.
“Moreover, I swore to them in the wilderness that I would not bring them into the land I had given them—a land flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all lands—
because they rejected My ordinances and failed to walk in My statutes; they profaned My Sabbaths, for their hearts went after their idols.
Yet I looked on them with pity and did not destroy them or make an end of them in the wilderness.
“Then I said to their children in the wilderness: ‘Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers or keep their ordinances or defile yourselves with their idols.
I am the LORD your God. Walk in My statutes, keep My ordinances, and practice them.
Keep My Sabbaths holy, that they may be a sign between us, so that you will know that I am the LORD your God.’

But the children rebelled against Me. They did not walk in My statutes or keep My ordinances, although the man who practices them will live by them. They profaned My Sabbaths. So I resolved to pour out My wrath on them and vent My anger against them in the wilderness.
But I withheld My hand and acted for the sake of My name, lest it be profaned in the eyes of the nations in whose sight I had brought them out.
However, I swore to them in the wilderness that I would scatter them among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands,
because they had not observed My ordinances but had rejected My statutes and profaned My Sabbaths, and their eyes were fixed on the idols of their fathers.
So I gave them over to statutes that were not good and ordinances by which they could not live.
And I let them become defiled through their gifts—the sacrifice of every firstborn—that I might devastate them, so that they would know that I am the LORD.
“Therefore, son of man, speak to the house of Israel and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Your fathers blasphemed Me by their unfaithfulness against Me.

When I brought them into the land I had sworn to give them, they saw every high hill and every leafy tree, and there they offered their sacrifices, presented their offerings, made their soothing aromas, and poured out their drink offerings.
So I asked them, “What is this high place to which you go?” And to this day it is called Bamah.’
Therefore tell the house of Israel that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Will you defile yourselves the way your fathers did, and prostitute yourselves after their detestable idols?

When you offer your gifts and pass your sons through the fire, you defile yourselves with all your idols to this day. Should I let you inquire of Me, house of Israel? As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will not be consulted by you.’
“The plan you have in mind will never come to pass when you say, ‘Let us be like the nations, like the peoples of other lands, serving wood and stone.’
As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, with a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and outpoured wrath I will rule over you.
With a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and outpoured wrath I will bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the lands to which you have been scattered.
“I will bring you into the wilderness of the nations, and there I will enter into judgment with you face to face.
Just as I entered into judgment with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so I will enter into judgment with you, declares the Lord GOD.
I will make you pass under the rod and bring you into the bond of the covenant.
And I will purge from among you the rebels and transgressors. I will bring them out of the land where they live, but they will not enter the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

“As for you, O house of Israel, this is what the Lord GOD says: Go and serve, every one of you, his idols—but later you will surely listen to Me, and you will no longer profane My holy name with your gifts and idols.

For on My holy mountain, on the high mountain of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, there the whole house of Israel, all of them, will serve Me in the land. There I will accept them and there I will require your contributions and the choicest of your offerings, with all your holy things.

When I bring you from the peoples and gather you from the lands to which you have been scattered, I will accept you as a pleasing aroma. And I will show My holiness through you in the sight of the nations.
“Then you will know that I am the LORD, when I bring you into the land of Israel, the land I swore to give your fathers.
There you will remember your ways and all the acts by which you defiled yourselves, and you will loathe yourselves for all the evils you have done.
Then you will know that I am the LORD, when I have dealt with you for the sake of My name and not according to your wicked ways and corrupt acts, O house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.”
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, set your face toward the south, preach against the south, and prophesy against the forest of the Negev.

Say to the forest of the Negev: Hear the word of the LORD! This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I am about to ignite a fire in you, and it will devour all your trees, both green and dry. The blazing flame will not be extinguished, and every face from south to north will be scorched by it.
Then all flesh will see that I, the LORD, have kindled it; it will not be quenched.’”
Then I said, “Ah, Lord GOD, they are saying of me, ‘Isn’t he just telling parables?’”
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, turn your attention toward Jerusalem and preach against the sanctuaries; prophesy against the land of Israel.
Say to the land of Israel: Thus says the LORD: Behold, I am against you, and I will draw My sword from its sheath and cut off from you the righteous and the wicked.
Because I will cut off from you the righteous and the wicked, My sword will go out from its sheath against all flesh from south to north.
Then all flesh will know that I, the LORD, have drawn My sword from its sheath; it will not be sheathed again.
“As for you, son of man, groan; with a broken spirit and bitter grief, groan before their eyes.

And when they ask you, ‘Why are you groaning?’ you are to say, ‘Because of the news that is coming. Every heart will fail, every hand will hang limp, every spirit will faint, and every knee will buckle. Behold, it is coming, and it will happen,’ declares the Lord the LORD.”
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord: A sword, a sword, sharpened and polished,
sharpened for the slaughter, polished to flash like lightning—should we then rejoice in the scepter of My son? The sword despises every tree.
It has been given to be polished, to be grasped in the hand. It is sharpened and polished, to be placed in the hand of the slayer.
Cry out and wail, son of man, for it is against My people; it is against all the princes of Israel. They are delivered to the sword with My people. Therefore strike your thigh.
Surely the sword has been tested, and what if the scepter, which the sword despises, does not endure?” declares the Lord the LORD.
“So prophesy, son of man, and strike your hands together. Let the sword strike twice, even three times. It is a sword for the slain, a sword for the great slaughter, piercing them on every side.
So that hearts may melt and many may stumble, I have set the sword at all their gates. Ah, it flashes like lightning; it is drawn for slaughter.
Unite yourself, turn to the right; set yourself, turn to the left, wherever your face is directed.
I will also strike My hands together, and I will satisfy My wrath. I, the LORD, have spoken.”
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, mark out two roads for the sword of the king of Babylon to take; both will come from the same land. Make a signpost at the head of the road to each city.
Mark out a road for the sword to come against Rabbah of the Ammonites, and another against Judah into fortified Jerusalem.
For the king of Babylon stands at the fork in the road, at the head of the two roads, to use divination: He shakes the arrows, consults the idols, and examines the liver.

In his right hand is the divination for Jerusalem: to set up battering rams, to give the command to slaughter, to lift up a battle cry, to set up battering rams against the gates, to build a siege ramp, and to erect a siege wall.
It will seem like a false divination to those who have sworn an oath to him, but it will remind them of their guilt, so that they will be captured.

Therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: Because you have brought your guilt to mind by exposing your transgressions, so that your sins are visible in all your deeds—because you have drawn attention to them, you will be taken captive.
“And you, O profane and wicked prince of Israel, whose day has come, whose time of punishment has arrived,
this is what the Lord the LORD says: Remove the turban, and take off the crown. The present order will not stand; exalt the lowly and bring down the exalted.
A ruin, a ruin, a ruin I will make it. It will not be restored until the arrival of Him to whom it belongs; to Him I will give it.”
“Now prophesy, son of man, and say: Thus says the Lord the LORD to the Ammonites and their contempt: A sword, a sword is drawn for slaughter, polished to devour, to flash like lightning,
while they offer you false visions and lying divinations, prophesying that you will be laid on the necks of the slain wicked, whose day has come, whose time of punishment has arrived.
Return it to its sheath. In the place where you were created, in the land of your origin, I will judge you.
I will pour out My wrath upon you; I will blow the fire of My fury against you. I will hand you over to brutal men, skilled in destruction.
You will be fuel for the fire; your blood will be in the midst of the land. You will be no more remembered, because I, the LORD, have spoken.”
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, will you judge, will you judge the city of blood? Then make known to her all her abominations.”
Say, “Thus says the Lord GOD: A city that sheds blood within herself and makes idols to defile herself has drawn near her time.

You are guilty because of the blood you have shed, and you are defiled by the idols you have made; you have brought your days near and reached your years. Therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations and a mockery to all the lands.
Those near and far will mock you, you whose name is defiled and who are great in turmoil.”
Behold, the princes of Israel in you—each one according to his power—have been there to shed blood.
In you they have dishonored father and mother; in your midst they have oppressed the sojourner; in you they have wronged the orphan and the widow.
You have despised My holy things and profaned My Sabbaths.
Slanderers are in you to shed blood, and they eat on the mountains; they commit lewdness in your midst.
In you they have uncovered their father's nakedness; in you they have humiliated the woman during her menstrual uncleanness.
One man has committed an abomination with his neighbor's wife; another has lewdly defiled his daughter-in-law; another has violated his sister, his father's daughter, in you.
In you they have taken bribes to shed blood; you have taken interest and usury; you have extorted your neighbors by violence; and you have forgotten Me, declares the Lord GOD.
And behold, I have clapped My hands at your dishonest gain and at the blood that is in your midst.
Can your heart endure, or can your hands be strong, in the days when I deal with you? I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it.
I will scatter you among the nations and disperse you through the lands, and I will remove your uncleanness from you.
You will be profaned in the sight of the nations, and you will know that I am the LORD.
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, the house of Israel has become dross to Me; all of them—bronze, tin, iron, and lead—are in the furnace; they are the dross of silver.”
Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Because all of you have become dross, behold, I am gathering you into Jerusalem.
As one gathers silver, bronze, iron, lead, and tin into a furnace to blow fire upon it and melt it, so I will gather you in My anger and wrath, and I will put you in and melt you.
I will gather you and blow on you with the fire of My wrath, and you will be melted in it.
As silver is melted in a furnace, so you will be melted in it; and you will know that I, the LORD, have poured out My wrath upon you.
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, say to her, ‘You are a land that has not been cleansed and has not been rained upon in the day of wrath.’”
A conspiracy of her prophets is in her midst, like a roaring lion tearing its prey; they devour lives, seize treasure and valuables, and make many widows in her midst.

Her priests have done violence to My law and have profaned My holy things; they have made no distinction between the holy and the common, and they have not taught the difference between the unclean and the clean; they have hidden their eyes from My Sabbaths, so that I am profaned among them.
Her princes in her midst are like wolves tearing prey, shedding blood and destroying lives to make dishonest gain.
Her prophets plaster them with whitewash, seeing false visions and divining lies for them, saying, “Thus says the Lord GOD,” when the LORD has not spoken.
The people of the land practice extortion and commit robbery; they oppress the poor and needy and mistreat the foreigner without justice.
I sought for a man among them who would build up the wall and intercede before Me for the land, that I might not destroy it, but I found none.
So I poured out My indignation upon them; I consumed them with the fire of My wrath; I brought their ways upon their own heads, declares the Lord GOD.
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
"Son of man, two women were born to the same mother.
"They prostituted themselves in Egypt and gave themselves to promiscuity in their youth; there their breasts were caressed, and there their virginity was violated.
The elder was named Oholah, and her sister Oholibah. They became Mine, and they bore sons and daughters. As for their names, Oholah is Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem.
"Oholah prostituted herself while she was still Mine. She lusted after her lovers, the Assyrians, her neighbors—
warriors clothed in blue, governors and commanders, all desirable young men, horsemen riding horses.
She lavished her prostitution upon all of them, the choicest men of Assyria, and defiled herself with every idol of everyone she coveted.
She did not abandon the prostitution she had begun in Egypt, when men lay with her in her youth, caressed her virgin breasts, and poured out their desire upon her.
"Therefore I delivered her into the hands of her lovers, the Assyrians she had coveted.
They exposed her shame, seized her sons and daughters, and killed her with the sword. She became a byword among women, and they executed judgment upon her.
"Her sister Oholibah saw this, yet she was even more depraved in her lust than her sister, and her prostitution exceeded her sister's.
She lusted after the Assyrians—governors and commanders, warriors arrayed in splendor, horsemen riding horses, all desirable young men.
I saw that both were defiled and had followed the same path.
"Yet she increased her prostitution. She saw men carved upon a wall, images of Chaldeans drawn in vermilion,
girded with belts around their waists and flowing turbans upon their heads, all resembling officers—the likeness of Babylonians, Chaldeans from their native land.
As soon as she saw them, she lusted after them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.
"Then the Babylonians came to her bed of love and defiled her with their lust. After she had been defiled by them, she turned away from them in disgust.
When she flaunted her prostitution and exposed her shame, I turned away from her in disgust, just as I had turned away from her sister.
Yet she increased her prostitution, recalling the days of her youth when she prostituted herself in Egypt.
She lusted after lovers there whose flesh is like the flesh of donkeys and whose emission is like the emission of horses.
So you revisited the lewdness of your youth, when the Egyptians handled your breasts and caressed your youthful bosom.
"Therefore, Oholibah, this is what the Lord GOD says: I am about to rouse your lovers against you—those from whom you turned away in disgust—and I will bring them against you from every side:
the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans—Pekod, Shoa, and Koa—and all the Assyrians with them, desirable young men, governors and commanders, officers and men of renown, all riding horses.

"They will come against you with an assembly of peoples, with weapons, chariots, and wagons. They will surround you on every side with buckler, shield, and helmet. I will place judgment before them, and they will judge you according to their own standards.

I will pour out My jealousy upon you, and they will deal with you in wrath. They will cut off your nose and your ears, and your survivors will fall by the sword. They will seize your sons and daughters, and your survivors will be consumed by fire.
They will strip off your clothes and take away your fine ornaments.
So I will put an end to your lewdness and your prostitution, which began in Egypt. You will no longer lift your eyes to them, nor will you remember Egypt again.
"For this is what the Lord GOD says: I am going to deliver you into the hands of those you hate, into the hands of those from whom you turned away in disgust.
They will treat you with hatred and take all your wealth. They will leave you naked and bare, and the shame of your prostitution will be exposed. Your lewdness and prostitution will be uncovered.
I will do these things to you because you prostituted yourself with the nations and defiled yourself with their idols.
You have walked in the way of your sister; therefore I will put her cup into your hand.
"This is what the Lord GOD says: You will drink your sister's cup, a cup deep and wide; it will bring you scorn and derision, for it holds much.
You will be filled with drunkenness and grief—a cup of horror and desolation, the cup of your sister Samaria.
You will drink it and drain it; you will scrape its shards with your teeth and tear your breasts. For I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.
"Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you have forgotten Me and cast Me behind your back, you must bear the consequences of your lewdness and prostitution."
The LORD said to me, "Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah? Then declare to them their abominations.
"For they have committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. They committed adultery with their idols, and they even sacrificed to them the children they bore to Me.
They have also done this to Me: they defiled My sanctuary on that day and profaned My Sabbaths.
On the very day they sacrificed their children to their idols, they entered My sanctuary to profane it. Yes, this is what they did inside My house.
"Furthermore, they sent for men who came from afar. When they arrived, you bathed yourself for them, painted your eyes, and adorned yourself with jewelry.
You sat on a stately couch with a table spread before it, on which you had placed My incense and My oil.
The sound of a carefree crowd was there; and with ordinary men, drunkards were brought in from the desert. They put bracelets on the women's wrists and beautiful crowns upon their heads.
"Then I said of her who was worn out by adulteries, 'Will they now commit adultery with her, and she with them?'
Men went in to her as to a prostitute. So they went in to Oholah and Oholibah, those lewd women.
"But righteous men will judge them with the judgment of adulteresses and murderers, because they are adulteresses and blood is on their hands.
For this is what the Lord GOD says: I will bring a mob against them and consign them to terror and plunder.
The mob will stone them and cut them down with their swords. They will kill their sons and daughters and burn their houses.
"So I will put an end to lewdness in the land, and all the women will be warned not to imitate your lewdness.
They will repay you for your lewdness, and you will bear the penalty of your idolatry. Then you will know that I am the Lord GOD."
In the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, write down the name of this day, this very day. The king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem this very day.
And utter a parable to the rebellious house and say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: “Put on the pot, put it on, and also pour water into it;
gather its pieces into it, all the good pieces—thigh and shoulder—fill it with the choice bones.
Take the choicest of the flock, and also pile the bones under it; boil its pieces and cook the bones in it.”’

“Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: ‘Woe to the bloody city, to the pot whose rust is in it, and whose rust has not gone out of it! Take out its pieces one by one; none of them has been allotted by lot.
For her blood was in her midst; she put it on the bare rock; she did not pour it out on the ground, to cover it with dust.
To rouse My wrath, to take vengeance, I have set her blood on the bare rock, that it may not be covered.’
“Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: ‘I also will make the pile great.
Heap on the wood, kindle the fire; boil the meat well, mix in the spices, and let the bones be burned.
Then set it empty on the coals, that it may heat and its bronze may glow, that its filth may be melted in it, its rust consumed.
She has wearied herself with toil, yet her great rust does not go out of her; her rust does not go out by fire.
In your lewdness is uncleanness; because I cleansed you, but you were not cleansed from your uncleanness, you shall not be cleansed anymore until I have satisfied My wrath upon you.

I, the LORD, have spoken; it shall come to pass, and I will do it. I will not refrain, nor will I spare, nor will I relent. According to your ways and according to your deeds they will judge you,’ declares the Lord GOD.”
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, behold, I am about to take the delight of your eyes away from you at a stroke; but do not mourn or weep, nor let your tears fall.
Groan quietly; make no mourning for the dead. Bind on your turban, and put your sandals on your feet, and do not cover your upper lip, and do not eat the food brought by mourners.”
So I spoke to the people in the morning, and in the evening my wife died; and the next morning I did as I was commanded.
And the people said to me, “Will you not tell us what these things mean to us, that you are acting like this?”
Then I said to them, “The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

‘Speak to the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I will profane My sanctuary, the pride of your power, the delight of your eyes, and the yearning of your soul, and your sons and your daughters whom you left behind shall fall by the sword.
And you shall do as I have done; you shall not cover your upper lip, nor eat the food brought by mourners.
Your turbans shall be on your heads and your sandals on your feet; you shall not mourn or weep, but you shall rot away in your iniquities and groan to one another.
Thus Ezekiel is a sign to you; according to all that he has done you shall do. When this comes, then you will know that I am the Lord GOD.’”
“As for you, son of man, on the day when I take from them their stronghold, their joy and glory, the delight of their eyes and their heart's desire, and also their sons and daughters,
on that day a fugitive will come to you to bring you news.
On that day your mouth will be opened to the fugitive, and you shall speak and be mute no longer. So you shall be a sign to them, and they shall know that I am the LORD.”
The word of the LORD came to me, declaring:
“Son of man, confront the Ammonites and prophesy against them.

Say to the Ammonites: ‘Hear the word of the Lord GOD: Thus says the Lord GOD: Because you said, “Aha!” over My sanctuary when it was profaned, and over the land of Israel when it was desolate, and over the house of Judah when they went into exile,

therefore, behold, I am delivering you into the possession of the eastern peoples, and they shall pitch their encampments among you and establish their dwellings within you. They shall eat your fruit, and they shall drink your milk.
I will transform Rabbah into a pasture for camels and the Ammonites into a fold for flocks. Then you shall know that I am the LORD.’
“For thus says the Lord GOD: Because you clapped your hands, stamped your feet, and rejoiced with all the scorn in your soul against the land of Israel,

therefore, behold, I have stretched out My hand against you, and I will deliver you as plunder to the nations; I will excise you from the peoples and annihilate you among the countries. I will destroy you. Then you shall know that I am the LORD.”
“Thus says the Lord GOD: Because Moab and Seir said, ‘Look, the house of Judah is like all the nations,’
therefore, behold, I will lay open Moab’s flank from its cities to its frontier—the splendor of the land—Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim.
I will consign it, together with the Ammonites, to the eastern peoples as a possession, so that the Ammonites will no longer be remembered among the nations.
I will execute judgments against Moab. Then they shall know that I am the LORD.”
“Thus says the Lord GOD: Because Edom acted vindictively toward the house of Judah and incurred grievous guilt by exacting vengeance upon them,

therefore thus says the Lord GOD: I will stretch out My hand against Edom, and I will cut off from it both human and beast, and I will render it desolate from Teman; moreover, Dedan shall fall by the sword.

I will execute My vengeance upon Edom through My people Israel, and they shall deal with Edom according to My anger and according to My wrath; thus they shall know My vengeance, declares the Lord GOD.”
“Thus says the Lord GOD: Because the Philistines acted vengefully and took vengeance with spiteful malice, seeking to destroy with perpetual enmity,
therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am stretching out My hand against the Philistines, and I will cut off the Cherethites and annihilate the remnant of the coast.
I will execute great vengeance upon them with furious rebukes. Then they shall know that I am the LORD when I lay My vengeance upon them.”
In the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, the word of the the LORD came to me:

“Son of man, because Tyre has exulted over Jerusalem, saying that the gateway of the nations has been shattered, that its commerce has turned to Tyre, and that Tyre will prosper now that Jerusalem is ruined,
“therefore this is what the Lord the the LORD says: Behold, I am against you, O Tyre, and I will bring up many nations against you, as the sea brings up its waves.
“They will destroy your walls and tear down your towers; I will scrape away your rubble and make you a bare rock.
“You will become a place in the sea where nets are spread, for I have spoken, declares the Lord the the LORD.
Your daughters in the open country will be killed by the sword, and they will know that I am the the LORD.”

“For this is what the Lord the the LORD says: Behold, I will bring against Tyre Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of kings, from the north, with horses, chariots, and horsemen, a great company, and many people.
“He will kill your daughters in the open country with the sword. He will set up a siege wall against you, pour out a siege ramp against you, and raise shields against you.
He will direct the blow of his battering rams against your walls and break down your towers with his swords.
“The dust of his horses will cover you. When he enters your gates as through a breached city, your walls will tremble at the sound of horsemen, wagons, and chariots.
With the hooves of his horses he will trample all your streets. He will kill your people with the sword, and your mighty pillars will fall to the ground.
“They will plunder your wealth and loot your merchandise. They will break down your walls and demolish your fine houses, and they will throw your stones, timber, and rubble into the sea.
I will put an end to the sound of your songs, and the music of your harps will be heard no more.
I will make you a bare rock; you will become a place where nets are spread; you will never be rebuilt, for I, the the LORD, have spoken, declares the Lord the the LORD.”
“This is what the Lord the the LORD says to Tyre: Will not the coastlands shake at the sound of your fall, when the wounded groan and slaughter takes place in your midst?

“Then all the princes of the sea will step down from their thrones, remove their robes, and strip off their embroidered garments. They will clothe themselves with trembling, sit on the ground, tremble continually, and be appalled at you.

“They will take up a lament for you, asking how you have perished, O renowned city, inhabited by seafaring men—you who were mighty on the sea, you and your inhabitants, who imposed your terror on all who dwell there.
“Now the coastlands tremble on the day of your fall; the coastlands by the sea are dismayed at your passing.”
“For this is what the Lord the the LORD says: When I make you a desolate city, like cities that are not inhabited, when I bring the deep over you and the great waters cover you,

“then I will bring you down with those who go down to the pit, to the people of old, and I will make you dwell in the lowest parts of the earth, among the ancient ruins, with those who go down to the pit, so that you will not be inhabited. Yet I will bestow beauty in the land of the living.
“I will make you a horror, and you will be no more. Though you are sought, you will never be found again, declares the Lord the the LORD.”
"And you, son of man, raise a lamentation over Tyre.
Say to Tyre, you who dwell at the entrances of the sea, merchant of the peoples to many coastlands, 'Thus says the Lord, the LORD: You, Tyre, have said, "I am perfect in beauty."'"
Your borders are in the heart of the seas; your builders have perfected your beauty.
They built all your planks of cypress from Senir; they took cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you.
Of oaks from Bashan they made your oars; of ivory inlaid with boxwood from the coasts of Kittim they made your deck.
Fine embroidered linen from Egypt was your sail, to serve as your banner; blue and purple from the coastlands of Elishah were your awning.
The inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were your rowers; your skilled men, Tyre, were your pilots.
The elders of Gebal and its skilled men were within you, repairing your seams; all the ships of the sea and their sailors were in you to barter for your merchandise.
Men of Persia, Lud, and Put were in your army, your men of war; they hung shield and helmet in you; they gave you splendor.
Men of Arvad and your army were on your walls all around, and the Gammadim were in your towers; they hung their shields on your walls all around; they perfected your beauty.
Tarshish traded with you because of your great wealth; for your wares they exchanged silver, iron, tin, and lead.
Javan, Tubal, and Meshech traded with you; they exchanged human beings and bronze vessels for your merchandise.
From Beth-togarmah they exchanged horses, war horses, and mules for your wares.
The Dedanites traded with you; many coastlands were your market; they brought you ivory tusks and ebony in payment.
Aram traded with you because of your many products; they exchanged turquoise, purple, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and agate for your wares.
Judah and the land of Israel traded with you; they exchanged wheat of Minnith, meal, honey, oil, and balm for your merchandise.
Damascus traded with you because of your many products and your great wealth: wine of Helbon and wool of Zahar.
Dan and Javan from Uzal traded wrought iron, cassia, and cane in your market; these were among your merchandise.
Dedan traded with you in saddlecloths for riding.
Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were your customers; they traded with you in lambs, rams, and goats.
The merchants of Sheba and Raamah traded with you; for your wares they exchanged the finest spices, all kinds of precious stones, and gold.
Haran, Canneh, and Eden, and the merchants of Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad traded with you.
They traded with you in fine garments of blue, embroidered work, and multicolored rugs with cords tightly twisted and knotted.
The ships of Tarshish were the carriers for your merchandise. So you were filled and heavily laden in the heart of the seas.
Your rowers have brought you into great waters; the east wind has broken you in the heart of the seas.

Your wealth, your wares, your merchandise, your mariners, your pilots, your caulkers, your traders, all your men of war who are in you, and your whole assembly within you will fall into the heart of the seas on the day of your ruin.
The countryside will quake at the sound of your pilots' cry.
All who handle the oar will abandon their ships; the mariners and all the pilots of the sea will stand on the shore.
They will raise their voices over you and cry out bitterly; they will throw dust on their heads and roll in ashes.
They will shave their heads for you and put on sackcloth; they will weep for you with anguish of soul and bitter mourning.
In their wailing they will take up a lamentation for you and lament over you: "Who is like Tyre, silenced in the midst of the sea?"
When your wares went out from the seas, you satisfied many peoples; with your abundant wealth and merchandise you enriched the kings of the earth.
Now you are broken by the seas in the depths of the waters; your merchandise and all your company have fallen within you.
All the inhabitants of the coastlands are appalled at you; their kings shudder with horror; their faces are contorted.
The merchants among the peoples hiss at you; you have become a horror and will be no more forever.
The word of the the LORD came to me, saying,

“Son of man, say to the prince of Tyre, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says: Because your heart has been lifted up, and you have said, “I am a god; I sit in the seat of the gods, in the heart of the seas,” yet you are a man and not a god, and you have set your heart as the heart of a god. “‘
Behold, you are wiser than Daniel; no secret is hidden from you.
By your wisdom and understanding you have gained wealth for yourself, and you have gathered gold and silver into your treasuries.
By your great wisdom in trade you have increased your wealth, and your heart has been lifted up because of your wealth. “‘
Therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: Because you have set your heart as the heart of a god,
therefore, behold, I will bring strangers against you, the most ruthless of the nations; they will draw their swords against the beauty of your wisdom and profane your splendor.
They will bring you down to the pit, and you will die the death of the slain in the heart of the seas. “‘
Will you still say, “I am a god,” before your killer, when you are only a man and not a god, in the hands of those who slay you?
You will die the death of the uncircumcised at the hands of foreigners, for I have spoken, declares the Lord the LORD.’”
The word of the the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, raise a lamentation over the king of Tyre, and say to him, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says: You were the seal of perfection, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty. “‘

You were in Eden, the garden of God; every precious stone was your covering: sardius, topaz, diamond, beryl, onyx, jasper, sapphire, emerald, and carbuncle. Your settings and mountings were made of gold; they were prepared on the day you were created.
You were an anointed guardian cherub; I placed you on the holy mountain of God, and you walked among the fiery stones. “‘
You were blameless in your ways from the day you were created, until unrighteousness was found in you.

In the abundance of your trade you were filled with violence, and you sinned; so I cast you out in disgrace from the mountain of God, and I destroyed you, O covering cherub, from among the fiery stones.
Your heart was proud because of your beauty; you corrupted your wisdom for the sake of your splendor. I cast you to the ground; I made you a spectacle before kings. “‘

By the multitude of your iniquities and the dishonesty of your trade, you profaned your sanctuaries; so I brought fire from within you, and it consumed you. I reduced you to ashes on the earth in the sight of all who looked at you.
All who knew you among the peoples are appalled at you; you have come to a horrible end and will be no more.’”
The word of the the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, set your face against Sidon, and prophesy against her.

Say, ‘This is what the Lord the LORD says: Behold, I am against you, O Sidon, and I will be glorified in your midst. They will know that I am the the LORD when I execute judgments in her and show My holiness in her. “‘
For I will send pestilence into her, and blood into her streets; the slain will fall in her midst, by the sword against her on every side. Then they will know that I am the the LORD.
For the house of Israel there will no longer be a pricking brier or a painful thorn among all their neighbors who scorn them, and they will know that I am the Lord the LORD. “‘

This is what the Lord the LORD says: When I gather the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they have been scattered, I will show My holiness among them in the sight of the nations. Then they will dwell in their own land, which I gave to My servant Jacob.

They will dwell securely in it, build houses, and plant vineyards. They will dwell securely when I execute judgments on all their neighbors who have scorned them. Then they will know that I am the the LORD, their God.’”
In the tenth year, on the twelfth day of the tenth month, the word of the the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, oppose Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and prophesy against him and against all Egypt.”
Speak and say, “This is what the Lord the LORD says: Behold, I am against you, Pharaoh, king of Egypt, the great beast that lies among his rivers, who says, ‘The Nile is mine; I made it.’
I will put hooks in your jaws and make the fish of your rivers cling to your scales. I will pull you out of your rivers, and all the fish of your rivers will cling to your scales.

I will cast you into the wilderness, you and all the fish of your rivers. You will fall on the open field; you will not be gathered or buried. I have given you as food to the beasts of the earth and to the birds of the heavens.
Then all the inhabitants of Egypt will know that I am the the LORD, because they have been an unreliable support for the house of Israel.
When they took hold of you by the hand, you splintered and tore their shoulders; when they leaned on you, you broke and made their hips give way.”
Therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: “Behold, I will bring the sword against you and cut off from you both people and animals.
The land of Egypt will become a desolation and a waste, and they will know that I am the the LORD, because he said, ‘The Nile is mine; I made it.’
Therefore I am against you and against your rivers, and I will make the land of Egypt an utter waste and desolation, from Migdol to Syene, as far as the border of Cush.
No human foot or animal hoof will pass through it, and it will remain uninhabited for forty years.

I will make the land of Egypt a desolation among desolate lands, and its cities a desolation among ruined cities for forty years. I will scatter Egypt among the nations and disperse them among the countries.”
For this is what the Lord the LORD says: “At the end of forty years I will gather Egypt from the peoples among whom they were scattered.
I will restore Egypt's fortunes and bring them back to the land of Pathros, their homeland, and there they will be a lowly kingdom.
It will be the lowliest of the kingdoms and will never again exalt itself above the nations; I will make them so small that they will not rule over the nations.
Egypt will no longer be a source of confidence for the house of Israel, a reminder of their guilt when they turn to it for help; then they will know that I am the Lord the LORD.”
In the twenty-seventh year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the word of the the LORD came to me:

“Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, made his army labor hard against Tyre; every head was worn bald and every shoulder rubbed bare; yet neither he nor his army received wages from Tyre for the labor they performed against it.”

Therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: “Behold, I will give the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. He will carry off its wealth, plunder its stores, and seize its goods; it will be wages for his army.
I have given him the land of Egypt as payment for his labor, because they served Me, declares the Lord the LORD.
On that day I will give new strength to the house of Israel, and I will give you a voice among them; then they will know that I am the the LORD.”
The word of the LORD came to me:
"Son of man, prophesy and say, 'Thus says the Lord GOD: "Wail, 'Alas for the day!'
For the day is near, the day of the LORD is near—a day of clouds, a time of doom for the nations.
A sword will come against Egypt, and anguish will be in Cush when the slain fall in Egypt. Her wealth will be carried off, and her foundations will be torn down.
Cush, Put, Lud, all Arabia, Kub, and the people of the land of the covenant will fall by the sword along with them."'"
Thus says the LORD: "Those who support Egypt will fall, and the pride of her strength will collapse. From Migdol to Syene they will fall by the sword within her," declares the Lord GOD.
"They will be desolate among desolate lands, and their cities will lie among ruined cities.
Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I set fire to Egypt and all her allies are shattered.
On that day messengers will go out from Me in ships to terrify Cush, which is at ease. Anguish will come upon them on the day of Egypt's doom. Yes, it is coming!"
Thus says the Lord GOD: "I will put an end to the hordes of Egypt by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
He and his army—the most ruthless of nations—will be brought in to destroy the land. They will draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain.
I will dry up the streams of the Nile and sell the land to evil men. I will lay waste the land and everything in it by the hands of foreigners. I, the LORD, have spoken."
Thus says the Lord GOD: "I will destroy the idols and put an end to the images in Memphis. There will no longer be a prince in Egypt, and I will instill fear in that land.
I will desolate Pathros, set fire to Zoan, and execute judgment on Thebes.
I will pour out My wrath on Pelusium, the stronghold of Egypt, and cut off the multitude of Thebes.
I will set fire to Egypt; Pelusium will writhe in anguish, Thebes will be breached, and Memphis will face trouble every day.
The young men of On and Pi-beseth will fall by the sword, and those cities will go into captivity.
The day will be darkened in Tehaphnehes when I break there the yoke of Egypt. Her proud strength will cease to be in her; a cloud will cover her, and her daughters will go into captivity.
So I will execute judgments on Egypt, and they will know that I am the LORD."
In the eleventh year, in the seventh month, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
"Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt. It has not been bound up for healing, nor has it been wrapped in a bandage to make it strong enough to hold a sword.
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: 'Behold, I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and I will break his arms, both the strong and the broken. I will make the sword fall from his hand.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands.
I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put My sword in his hand, but I will break the arms of Pharaoh, and he will groan before him like a mortally wounded man.

I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, but the arms of Pharaoh will fall. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I put My sword into the hand of the king of Babylon and he wields it against the land of Egypt.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands. Then they will know that I am the LORD.'"
In the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first day, the word of the LORD came to me, saying:
“Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his hordes: “‘Whom are you like in your greatness?
“‘Consider Assyria, once a cedar in Lebanon, with beautiful branches and forest shade, towering to a great height, its crown among the clouds.
The waters nourished it; the deep made it grow tall, its rivers flowing around its base and its channels reaching all the trees of the field.
Therefore it towered higher than all the trees of the field; its boughs multiplied, and its branches grew long as they spread because of abundant waters.
“‘All the birds of the air nested in its boughs, and all the beasts of the field gave birth under its branches; all the great nations lived in its shade.
It was beautiful in its greatness, in the length of its limbs, for its roots spread to abundant waters.

“‘The cedars in the garden of God could not rival it, nor could the cypresses match its boughs. The plane trees were as nothing compared with its branches. No tree in the garden of God could compare with it in beauty.
“‘I made it beautiful with its many branches, the envy of all the trees of Eden in the garden of God.
“‘Therefore this is what the Lord the LORD says: “‘‘Because it towered high and set its crown among the clouds, and because its heart was proud of its height,
I delivered it into the hand of the ruler of the nations, for him to deal with it according to its wickedness. I have driven it out.

Foreigners, the most ruthless of nations, have cut it down and left it. Its branches have fallen on the mountains and in every valley; its boughs lie broken in all the ravines of the earth. All the peoples of the earth have departed from its shade and abandoned it.
All the birds of the air nested on its fallen trunk, and all the beasts of the field lived among its branches.

This happened so that no other tree by the waters would exalt itself in its height, nor set its crown among the clouds; no other well-watered tree would reach up in its height. For they all have been consigned to death, to the depths of the earth, among the sons of men, with those who descend to the Pit.’

“‘This is what the Lord the LORD says: “‘‘On the day it was brought down to Sheol, I caused mourning; I covered the deep over it; I held back its rivers, and its abundant waters were restrained. I made Lebanon mourn for it, and all the trees of the field wilted on its account.

I made the nations quake at the sound of its fall, when I cast it down to Sheol with those who descend to the Pit. Then all the trees of Eden, the choicest and best of Lebanon, all the well-watered trees, were comforted in the earth below.
They too descended with it to Sheol, to those slain by the sword. Its allies, those who lived in its shade among the nations, also descended into the earth below.’

“‘Which of the trees of Eden can be compared with you in glory and greatness? Yet you will be brought down with the trees of Eden to the earth below. You will lie among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his hordes, declares the Lord the LORD.’”
In the twelfth year, on the first day of the twelfth month, the word of the the LORD came to me:

“Son of man, take up a lamentation for Pharaoh king of Egypt, and say to him: ‘You are like a young lion among the nations, yet you are like a monster in the seas; you thrash about in your rivers, churn the water with your feet, and muddy their rivers.’
“This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will spread My net over you with a great assembly of peoples, and they will haul you up in My dragnet.
“‘I will leave you on the land and cast you upon the open field. I will settle all the birds of heaven on you, and I will sate every beast of the earth with you.
“‘I will lay your flesh upon the mountains and fill the valleys with your remains.
I will drench the land with the outflow of your blood, even to the mountains, and the ravines will be filled with you.
“‘When I extinguish you, I will cover the heavens and darken their stars; I will veil the sun with a cloud, and the moon will withhold its light.
All the luminaries of heaven I will darken over you, and I will bring darkness upon your land,’ declares the Lord GOD.
“‘I will also trouble the hearts of many peoples when I bring your ruin among the nations, in lands you have not known.

“‘I will make many peoples aghast at you, and their kings will shudder with horror because of you when I brandish My sword before them. On the day of your downfall each will tremble unceasingly for his life.’
“For this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘The sword of the king of Babylon will come against you.
“‘By the swords of the mighty I will bring down your hordes; the most ruthless of nations, all of them, will pillage the pride of Egypt, and all her hordes will be annihilated.
“‘I will destroy all her livestock beside abundant waters, so that no human foot or beast's hoof will ever muddy them again.
Then I will make their waters settle and cause their rivers to flow like oil,’ declares the Lord GOD.
“‘When I make the land of Egypt a desolation, emptied of all that fills it, and when I strike down all who dwell in it, then they will know that I am the the LORD.’
“‘This is the lamentation that will be chanted; the daughters of the nations will chant it. Over Egypt and all her hordes they will chant it,’ declares the Lord GOD.”
In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, the word of the the LORD came to me, saying:
“Son of man, wail over the hordes of Egypt and consign her, with the daughters of mighty nations, to the lowest parts of the earth, to those who descend into the Pit.
‘Whom do you surpass in beauty? Go down and be laid among the uncircumcised.’
They will fall among those slain by the sword. The sword is given; drag her away with all her hordes.
“Mighty chiefs will speak to him from the midst of Sheol concerning his allies: ‘They have come down; they lie with the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword.’
“Assyria is there with her whole company; her graves surround her. All of them are slain, fallen by the sword.
“Her graves are set in the depths of the Pit, and her company surrounds her grave. All of them are slain, fallen by the sword—those who once spread terror in the land of the living.

“Elam is there with all her hordes around her grave. All of them are slain, fallen by the sword—those who went down uncircumcised to the depths of the earth, who once spread terror in the land of the living. They bear their disgrace with those who descend into the Pit.

“They have made a bed for her among the slain, with all her hordes. Her graves surround her. All of them are uncircumcised, slain by the sword, because their terror was spread in the land of the living. They bear their disgrace with those who descend into the Pit; she has been placed among the slain.
“Meshech and Tubal are there with all their hordes. Their graves surround them. All of them are uncircumcised, slain by the sword, because they spread their terror in the land of the living.

“They do not lie with the fallen warriors of old, who went down to Sheol with their weapons of war, whose swords were placed beneath their heads, and whose shields rested on their bones, though the terror of the mighty was in the land of the living.
“But you too will be broken and lie among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword.
“Edom is there, her kings and all her princes, who despite their might are laid among those slain by the sword. They lie with the uncircumcised and with those who descend into the Pit.

“All the chiefs of the north and all the Sidonians are there, who went down in shame with the slain, despite the terror of their might. They lie uncircumcised with those slain by the sword, and bear their disgrace with those who descend into the Pit.
“Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over all his hordes—Pharaoh and all his army, slain by the sword, declares the Lord GOD.
“For I have put his terror in the land of the living, yet he will be laid among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword—Pharaoh and all his hordes, declares the Lord GOD.”
The word of the the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, speak to your people and say to them: When I bring the sword against a land, and its people appoint one of their own as watchman,
and he sees the sword coming against the land and blows the trumpet to warn the people—
“if anyone hears the trumpet yet disregards the warning, and the sword comes and carries him off, his blood is on his own head.
He heard the trumpet but failed to heed the warning; his blood is upon him. Had he heeded the warning, he would have preserved his life.
