But if the watchman sees the sword approaching and does not sound the trumpet, so that the people remain unwarned, and the sword comes and claims one of them, that individual is taken away in his guilt, yet I will hold the watchman accountable for his blood.
“So you, son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from My mouth, you shall give them warning from Me.
If I say to the wicked, ‘You will surely die,’ and you do not speak to warn the wicked to turn from his way, that wicked person will die in his iniquity, but I will require his blood at your hand.
But if you warn the wicked to turn from his way, and he does not turn, he will die in his iniquity; yet you will have delivered your soul.”
“And you, son of man, say to the house of Israel, ‘This is what you have said: “Our transgressions and our sins weigh upon us, and we are wasting away because of them. How, then, can we live?”’

Say to them, ‘As I live, declares the Lord the LORD, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked; rather, I desire that the wicked turn from their ways and live. Turn back, turn back from your evil ways! Why will you die, O house of Israel?’”

“And you, son of man, say to the sons of your people, ‘The righteousness of the righteous will not deliver him when he sins, nor will the wickedness of the wicked cause him to stumble when he turns from it; moreover, the righteous will not be able to live by his righteousness when he sins.

Though I promise the righteous that he will surely live, yet if he relies upon his righteousness and commits injustice, none of his righteous deeds will be remembered; he will die because of the injustice he has committed.’”
“Again, though I declare to the wicked, ‘You will surely die,’ yet if he turns from his sin and does what is just and right—
if the wicked restores the pledge, returns what he has stolen, and walks in the statutes of life without committing injustice, he will surely live; he will not die.
None of the sins he has committed will be remembered against him. Because he has done what is just and right, he will surely live.’”
“Yet the sons of your people say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just,’ when in fact it is their own way that is not just.
When the righteous turns from his righteousness and commits injustice, he will die for it.
And when the wicked turns from his wickedness and does what is just and right, he will live by doing so.
Yet you say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ O house of Israel, I will judge each of you according to your ways.”
In the twelfth year of our exile, on the fifth day of the tenth month, a fugitive from Jerusalem came to me and reported, “The city has been struck down.”

Now the hand of the the LORD had been upon me the evening before the fugitive arrived, and He had opened my mouth by the time the man reached me in the morning; thus my mouth was opened, and I was no longer mute.
The word of the the LORD came to me:

“Son of man, the inhabitants of these ruins in the land of Israel are saying, ‘Abraham was only one man, yet he took possession of the land; but we are many, and the land has been given to us as a possession.’
Therefore say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord the LORD: You consume meat with its blood still in it, lift up your eyes to your idols, and shed blood; shall you then possess the land?
You rely upon your sword, you commit abominations, and each of you defiles his neighbor’s wife; shall you then possess the land?’

“Say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord the LORD: As I live, surely those who are in the ruins will fall by the sword; those in the open field I will give to the beasts to be devoured; and those in strongholds and caves will die of plague.
I will make the land a desolation and a waste, and its proud strength will come to an end; the mountains of Israel will be desolate, so that no one passes through.
Then they will know that I am the the LORD, when I make the land a desolation and a waste because of all the abominations they have committed.’”
“As for you, son of man, your people are talking about you beside the walls and at the doors of their houses, saying to one another, ‘Come and hear the word that comes from the the LORD.’
They come to you as people come, and they sit before you and hear your words, but they will not act upon them; for with their mouths they express devotion, yet their hearts pursue dishonest gain.
“Indeed, to them you are like one who sings love songs with a beautiful voice and plays an instrument skillfully, for they hear your words, but they will not act upon them.
When this comes to pass—and it will come to pass—then they will know that a prophet has been among them.”
The word of the LORD came to me.

"Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel; prophesy and say to them: Thus says the Lord the LORD: Woe to the shepherds of Israel who feed themselves! Should not the shepherds feed the flock?
You eat the fat, you clothe yourselves with the wool, you slaughter the fatlings, but you do not feed the flock.
You have not strengthened the weak, healed the sick, bound up the injured, brought back the strayed, or sought the lost; instead, you have ruled them with force and harshness.
"So they were scattered because there was no shepherd, and they became food for every beast of the field; they were scattered.
My flock wandered over all the mountains and on every high hill; My flock was scattered over all the face of the earth, and no one searched or sought for them.
"Therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the LORD:

As I live, declares the Lord the LORD, because My flock became prey and food for every beast of the field for lack of a shepherd, and because My shepherds did not search for My flock, but fed themselves and did not feed My flock,
therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the LORD:

Thus says the Lord the LORD: Behold, I am against the shepherds, and I will require My flock at their hand and remove them from feeding the flock; the shepherds will no longer feed themselves. I will deliver My flock from their mouth, so that they will no longer be food for them.
"For thus says the Lord the LORD: Behold, I Myself will search for My flock and seek them out.

As a shepherd seeks out his flock when he is among his sheep that have been scattered, so will I seek out My flock, and I will rescue them from all the places where they have been scattered on a day of clouds and thick darkness.

I will bring them out from the peoples and gather them from the countries, and bring them into their own land. I will feed them on the mountains of Israel, by the ravines, and in all the inhabited places of the country.

I will feed them in a good pasture, and on the mountain heights of Israel shall be their fold. There they shall lie down in a good fold, and on rich pasture they shall feed, on the mountains of Israel.
I Myself will be the shepherd of My flock, and I will make them lie down, declares the Lord the LORD.
I will seek the lost, bring back the strayed, bind up the injured, and strengthen the weak, but the fat and the strong I will destroy; I will feed them with justice.
"As for you, My flock, thus says the Lord the LORD: Behold, I judge between sheep and sheep, between rams and goats.
Is it not enough for you to feed on the good pasture, that you must trample the rest of your pasture with your feet? And to drink of clear water, that you must foul the rest with your feet?
And My flock must eat what you have trampled with your feet, and drink what you have fouled with your feet.
Therefore thus says the Lord the LORD to them: Behold, I Myself will judge between the fat sheep and the lean sheep.
Because you push with side and shoulder, and thrust at all the weak with your horns, till you have scattered them abroad,
I will rescue My flock, and they shall no longer be a prey; and I will judge between sheep and sheep.
"And I will set up over them one shepherd, My servant David, and he shall feed them; he shall feed them and be their shepherd.
And I, the LORD, will be their God, and My servant David shall be prince among them. I, the LORD, have spoken.
I will make with them a covenant of peace and banish wild beasts from the land, so that they may dwell securely in the wilderness and sleep in the woods.
And I will make them and the places round about My hill a blessing, and I will send down the rain in its season; they shall be showers of blessing.

And the trees of the field shall yield their fruit, and the earth shall yield its increase, and they shall be secure in their land. And they shall know that I am the LORD, when I have broken the bars of their yoke and delivered them from the hand of those who enslaved them.
They shall no more be a prey to the nations, nor shall the beasts of the earth devour them. They shall dwell securely, and none shall make them afraid.
And I will raise up for them a planting of renown, and they shall no more be consumed with hunger in the land, nor bear the reproach of the nations any more.
And they shall know that I am the LORD their God with them, and that they are My people, the house of Israel, declares the Lord the LORD.
And you, My flock, the flock of My pasture, are human beings, and I am your God, declares the Lord the LORD."
The word of the the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, direct your attention to Mount Seir and prophesy against it.”
“Thus says the Lord the LORD: I am against you, Mount Seir; I will take decisive action against you and make you a wasteland, utterly desolate.
I will reduce your cities to ruins, and you will become a desolation. Then you will know that I am the the LORD.
“Because you have harbored a perpetual enmity and delivered the Israelites to the sword in their time of calamity, at the time of their final punishment,
therefore, as surely as I live, declares the Lord the LORD, I will destine you for bloodshed, and bloodshed will pursue you. Since you did not despise bloodshed, bloodshed will pursue you.
I will make Mount Seir a desolation and a waste, and I will remove from it every traveler and resident.
I will fill its mountains with its slain; those struck down by the sword will fall across your hills, valleys, and ravines.
I will make you an everlasting desolation, and your cities will never be inhabited. Then you will know that I am the the LORD.
“Because you said, ‘These two nations and these two lands will be mine, and we will possess them,’ although the the LORD was there,

therefore, as surely as I live, declares the Lord the LORD, I will deal with you according to the anger and jealousy you displayed in your hatred toward them, and I will make Myself known among them when I judge you.
Then you will know that I, the the LORD, have heard all the contemptuous words you spoke against the mountains of Israel when you said, ‘They are desolate; they have been given to us to devour.’
You vaunted yourselves against Me with your mouths and multiplied your words against Me; I have heard them.
“Thus says the Lord the LORD: When the whole earth rejoices, I will make you a desolation.

As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel because it was desolate, so I will do to you. You will be a desolation, Mount Seir, and all Edom, all of it. Then they will know that I am the the LORD.”
And you, Son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel and say: Hear the word of the LORD, O mountains of Israel.
Thus says the Lord GOD: Because the enemy has said concerning you, ‘Aha! The ancient heights have become our possession,’

therefore prophesy and declare that this is what the Lord GOD says: Because they have made you desolate and have trampled you on every side, so that you became a possession of the rest of the nations and the subject of gossip and slander among the people,

Therefore, O mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD. This is what the Lord GOD says to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys, to the desolate ruins and abandoned cities, which have become plunder and a mockery to the rest of the nations around them:

Thus says the Lord GOD: Surely in My burning zeal I have spoken against the rest of the nations and against all Edom, who with wholehearted joy and utter contempt claimed My land as their own possession, to plunder its pastureland.

Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel and say to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys: This is what the Lord GOD says: Behold, I have spoken in My burning anger and jealousy, because you have borne the reproach of the nations.
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I have sworn with an uplifted hand that the nations around you will themselves bear their own shame.
But you, O mountains of Israel, will put forth your branches and bear your fruit for My people Israel, for their coming is near.
For behold, I am for you, and I will turn to you, and you will be tilled and sown.
I will multiply people upon you, all the house of Israel in its entirety. The cities will be inhabited and the ruins rebuilt.

I will multiply upon you man and beast, and they will increase and be fruitful. I will make you inhabited as in former times and will make you prosper more than before. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
I will cause My people Israel to walk upon you; they will possess you, and you will be their inheritance and will no longer deprive them of children.
Thus says the Lord GOD: Because they say to you, ‘You are a devourer of men and have deprived your nation of children,’
therefore you will no longer devour men, nor deprive your nation of children anymore, declares the Lord GOD.
I will no longer allow the taunts of the nations to be heard against you, nor will you bear the reproach of the peoples any longer or cause your nation to stumble anymore, declares the Lord GOD.
Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, when the house of Israel lived in their own land, they defiled it with their ways and their deeds. Their conduct before Me was like the uncleanness of a woman in her menstrual impurity.
So I poured out My wrath upon them for the blood they had shed on the land, and for their idols with which they had defiled it.
I scattered them among the nations, and they were dispersed throughout the lands. I judged them according to their ways and their deeds.
And wherever they went among the nations, they profaned My holy name, because it was said of them, ‘These are the people of the LORD, yet they had to leave His land.’
But I had concern for My holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the nations to which they had gone.”

Therefore say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord GOD: It is not for your sake, O house of Israel, that I am about to act, but for the sake of My holy name, which you have profaned among the nations to which you have gone.

I will sanctify My great name, which has been profaned among the nations—the name you have profaned among them. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, declares the Lord GOD, when I am sanctified in you before their eyes.
For I will take you from the nations and gather you from all the countries, and I will bring you into your own land.
I will also sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean. I will cleanse you from all your filthiness and from all your idols.
I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.
I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes and to carefully observe My ordinances.
Then you will live in the land that I gave to your fathers; you will be My people, and I will be your God.
I will save you from all your uncleanness. I will summon the grain and make it abundant, and I will not bring famine upon you.
I will multiply the fruit of the trees and the produce of the fields, so that you will no longer suffer the reproach of famine among the nations.
Then you will remember your evil ways and your deeds that were not good, and you will loathe yourselves for your iniquities and your abominations.
It is not for your sake that I am about to act, declares the Lord GOD. Let this be known to you. Be ashamed and disgraced for your ways, O house of Israel!
Thus says the Lord GOD: On the day I cleanse you from all your iniquities, I will resettle the cities, and the ruins will be rebuilt.
The desolate land will be cultivated instead of lying desolate in the sight of all who pass by.
Then they will say, ‘This land that was desolate has become like the garden of Eden, and the cities that were ruined, desolate, and destroyed are now fortified and inhabited.’
Then the nations around you that remain will know that I, the LORD, have rebuilt what was destroyed and have replanted what was desolate. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it.
Thus says the Lord GOD: Once again I will allow the house of Israel to ask Me for this: I will multiply their people like a flock.
Like the flock of holy things, like the flock of Jerusalem during her appointed feasts, so will the ruined cities be filled with flocks of people. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
The hand of the the LORD came upon me, and the the LORD carried me out by the Spirit and set me down in the middle of a valley full of bones.
He led me back and forth among them, and I saw that they were very numerous across the valley floor, and they were exceedingly dry.
He said to me, "Son of man, can these bones live?" I answered, "O Lord the the LORD, You alone know."
Then He said to me, "Prophesy to these bones and say to them, 'Dry bones, hear the word of the the LORD.'"
"This is what the Lord the the LORD says: I am about to bring breath into you, and you will live.
I will attach tendons to you, put flesh upon you, cover you with skin, and put breath in you; then you will live, and you will know that I am the the LORD."
So I prophesied as I was commanded. As I prophesied, there was a noise, a rattling sound, and the bones came together, bone to bone.
I looked, and I saw tendons and flesh appear on them, and skin cover them, but there was no breath in them.

Then He said to me, "Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, Son of man, and say to the breath, 'This is what the Lord the the LORD says: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe into these slain, that they may live.'"
So I prophesied as He commanded me, and breath entered them; they came to life and stood on their feet—an exceedingly great army.
Then He said to me, "Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel. "They are saying that their bones are dried up, that their hope is lost, and that they are cut off."
"Therefore prophesy and say to them, 'This is what the Lord the the LORD says: My people, I am going to open your graves and bring you up from them; I will bring you into the land of Israel.
Then you will know that I am the the LORD, when I open your graves and bring you up from them.
I will put My Spirit in you, and you will live, and I will settle you in your own land. Then you will know that I, the the LORD, have spoken and have done it, declares the the LORD.'"
The word of the the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, take a single stick and write on it, 'For Judah and for the Israelites associated with him.' Then take another stick and write on it, 'For Joseph—the stick of Ephraim—and for all the house of Israel associated with him.'
Join them together into one stick, so that they become one in your hand."
He said to me, "When your people ask you, 'Won't you tell us what these things mean?'"

"Say to them, 'This is what the Lord the the LORD says: I am going to take the stick of Joseph, which is in Ephraim's hand along with the tribes of Israel associated with him, and join it to the stick of Judah. I will make them into a single stick, and they will become one in My hand.'
The sticks on which you write will be in your hand before their eyes."
"Then say to them, 'This is what the Lord the the LORD says: I will take the Israelites out of the nations where they have gone. I will gather them from all around and bring them into their own land.
I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, and one king will rule over them all. They will no longer be two nations and will never again be divided into two kingdoms.

They will no longer defile themselves with their idols, their detestable practices, or any of their transgressions. I will save them from all their backsliding in which they sinned, and I will cleanse them. They will be My people, and I will be their God.'"
"My servant David will be king over them, and there will be one shepherd for all of them. They will walk in My judgments, keep My statutes, and observe them.

They will live in the land I gave to My servant Jacob, the land where your fathers lived. They and their children and their grandchildren will live there forever, and My servant David will be their prince forever."
"I will make a covenant of peace with them; it will be an everlasting covenant. I will establish them and multiply them, and I will set My sanctuary among them forever.
My tabernacle will be with them; I will be their God, and they will be My people.
Then the nations will know that I, the the LORD, sanctify Israel, when My sanctuary is among them forever."
The word of the the LORD came to me, saying,
"Son of man, set your face against Gog, of the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him.
And say, ‘Thus says the Lord the the LORD: Behold, I am against you, O Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
I will turn you around, put hooks in your jaws, and bring you out with your whole army—horses and horsemen, all fully armed, a vast company with bucklers and shields, every one brandishing a sword.
Persia, Cush, and Put will march with them, all with shields and helmets;
Gomer and all its troops, Beth-togarmah from the far north and all its troops—many peoples are with you. "‘
Be prepared and make yourself ready, you and all your hordes assembled around you, and assume command over them.

After many days you will be mustered; in the latter years you will come into the land restored from war, whose people have been gathered from many nations to the mountains of Israel, which had long been desolate. They were brought out from the nations, and now they dwell securely.
You and all your troops, along with many peoples, will advance like a storm; you will be like a cloud covering the land.’ "
‘Thus says the Lord the the LORD: On that day, thoughts will arise in your mind, and you will devise an evil plan.
You will say, “I will go up against a land of unwalled villages; I will come against a tranquil people living securely, all of them dwelling without walls, bars, or gates—
to seize spoil and plunder, to turn your hand against the resettled ruins and against a people gathered from the nations, who have acquired livestock and goods and dwell at the center of the earth.”

Sheba, Dedan, and the merchants of Tarshish, with all its villages, will say to you, “Have you come to seize spoil? Have you assembled your hordes to carry off plunder—to take silver and gold, to take livestock and goods, to seize a vast spoil?”’ "
Therefore, son of man, prophesy and say to Gog, ‘Thus says the Lord the the LORD: On that day, when My people Israel are dwelling securely, will you not take notice?
You will come from your place in the far north—you and many peoples with you—all riding horses, a great company and a mighty army.

You will advance against My people Israel like a cloud covering the land. In the latter days, O Gog, I will bring you against My land, so that the nations may know Me when I am sanctified in you before their eyes.
Thus says the Lord the the LORD: Are you the one I spoke of long ago through My servants the prophets of Israel, who prophesied in those days for years that I would bring you against them?’ "‘
On that day, when Gog comes against the land of Israel, declares the Lord the the LORD, My wrath will flare up.
In My zeal and in My blazing wrath I have spoken: Surely on that day there will be a great earthquake in the land of Israel.

The fish of the sea, the birds of the air, the beasts of the field, every creeping thing on the ground, and every person on the face of the earth will tremble at My presence. The mountains will be thrown down, the cliffs will collapse, and every wall will fall to the ground.
I will summon a sword against Gog on all My mountains, declares the Lord the the LORD; every man's sword will be against his brother.
I will execute judgment on him with plague and bloodshed; I will pour down on him, on his troops, and on the many peoples with him a torrential rain, hailstones, fire, and brimstone.
I will magnify and sanctify Myself, and I will make Myself known in the sight of many nations. Then they will know that I am the the LORD.’"
And you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say, "Thus says the Lord, the LORD: Behold, I am against you, O Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
I will turn you around, urge you onward, bring you up from the far north, and lead you against the mountains of Israel.
I will strike your bow from your left hand and knock your arrows from your right hand.
On the mountains of Israel you will fall—you and all your troops and the nations with you. I will give you as food to every bird of prey and wild animal.
You will fall in the open field, for I have spoken, declares the Lord, the LORD.
I will send fire on Magog and on those who dwell securely in the coastlands, and they will know that I am the LORD.
I will make My holy name known among My people Israel, and I will no longer allow My holy name to be profaned. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, the Holy One in Israel.
Behold, it is coming, and it will surely happen, declares the Lord, the LORD. This is the day of which I have spoken."

Then the inhabitants of the cities of Israel will go out and use the weapons for fuel and burn them—the shields, small and large, the bows and arrows, the clubs and spears. For seven years they will use them for fuel.

They will not need to gather wood from the fields or cut it from the forests, because they will use the weapons for fuel. They will loot those who looted them and plunder those who plundered them, declares the Lord, the LORD.

On that day I will give Gog a burial place in Israel—the Valley of the Travelers east of the sea. It will obstruct the travelers, because Gog and all his multitude will be buried there. So it will be called the Valley of Hamon-gog.
For seven months the house of Israel will be burying them in order to cleanse the land.
All the people of the land will bury them, and it will be a day of renown for Me when I am glorified, declares the Lord, the LORD.
Men will be continually appointed to travel through the land and bury the invaders left on its surface; after the seven months, they will conduct a further search.
As they pass through the land, anyone who sees a human bone will set up a marker beside it, until those assigned to bury have buried it in the Valley of Hamon-gog.
A city there will also be called Hamonah. Thus they will cleanse the land.

Now as for you, son of man, this is what the Lord, the LORD says: Tell every kind of bird and every wild animal: "Assemble and come, gather together from all around to My sacrifice that I am preparing for you—a great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel—and you will eat flesh and drink blood.
You will eat the flesh of warriors and drink the blood of the princes of the earth, as though they were rams, lambs, goats, and bulls—all of them fattened animals of Bashan.
At the sacrifice I am preparing, you will eat fat until you are satiated and drink blood until you are drunk.
At My table you will gorge yourselves on horses and charioteers, on mighty warriors and all the men of war, declares the Lord, the LORD."
I will display My glory among the nations, and all the nations will see My judgment that I have executed and My hand that I have laid upon them.
From that day forward the house of Israel will know that I am the LORD their God.

And the nations will know that the house of Israel went into exile for their iniquity, because they were treacherous toward Me. So I turned away from them and delivered them into the hands of their enemies, and they all fell by the sword.
I dealt with them according to their impurity and transgressions, and I turned away from them.
Therefore this is what the Lord, the LORD says: Now I will bring back the exiles of Jacob and have compassion on the whole house of Israel, and I will be zealous for My holy name.
They will forget their shame and all the treachery they committed against Me, when they dwell securely in their land, with no one to make them afraid.
When I bring them back from the nations and gather them out of their enemies' lands, I will reveal My holiness through them in the sight of many nations.
Then they will know that I am the LORD their God, for though I sent them into exile among the nations, I will gather them back to their own land, not leaving any of them behind.
And I will no longer turn away from them, for I will pour out My Spirit on the house of Israel, declares the Lord, the LORD.

In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month—in the fourteenth year after the city was struck down—on that very day the hand of the LORD was upon me, and He brought me there.
In visions of God He brought me to the land of Israel and set me down on a very high mountain, on whose southern slope stood a structure resembling a city.
When He brought me there, I saw a man whose appearance was like bronze; he was standing in the gateway with a linen cord and a measuring reed in his hand.

The man said to me, "Son of man, look with your eyes, hear with your ears, and set your heart on all that I show you, for you have been brought here so that I may show it to you. Declare to the house of Israel all that you see."

I saw a wall surrounding the outside of the temple area. The measuring reed in the man's hand was six cubits long—each cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth—and he measured the wall's thickness as one reed and its height as one reed.
He then entered the gateway facing east, ascended its steps, and measured the threshold of the gate as one reed wide.
Each gate chamber measured one reed in length and one reed in width, with five cubits between adjacent chambers; the inner threshold of the gate beside the portico facing inward measured one reed.
He measured the portico of the gateway toward the temple at one reed.
The portico of the gateway measured eight cubits, and its jambs two cubits; the portico of the gateway faced the temple.
The east gate had three gate chambers on each side, all with identical measurements, and the gateposts on either side shared those same measurements.
He measured the gateway's entrance at ten cubits wide and the gateway itself at thirteen cubits long.
A barrier one cubit wide stood in front of the gate chambers on each side, and each gate chamber was six cubits square.
He measured the gateway from the roof of one gate chamber to the roof of the opposite chamber: its width was twenty-five cubits, from doorway to doorway.
He measured the gateposts at sixty cubits, and the gateway extended around to the gatepost of the courtyard.
From the front of the gate at the entrance to the front of the inner portico of the gate was fifty cubits.
The gate chambers and their posts had beveled windows all around within the gateway, and windows encircled the inner portico; palm trees were carved on each side.
He then brought me into the outer court, where chambers and a paved surface extended all around the court; thirty chambers faced the pavement.
The pavement lay beside the gates, corresponding in length to the gates; this was the lower pavement.
He measured the width from the front of the lower gate to the front of the inner court: one hundred cubits on the east and one hundred cubits on the north.
He also measured the length and width of the outer court's gate that faced north.
Its three gate chambers on each side, its posts, and its portico had the same measurements as the first gate: the gate was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its windows, portico, and palm trees had the same measurements as those of the gate facing east; seven steps led up to it, with its portico opposite them.
The inner court also had a gate facing the north gate, just as there was toward the east, and he measured the distance from gate to gate at one hundred cubits.
He led me to the south side, where a gate faced south, and he measured its posts and portico; they had the same measurements as the others.
Both the gate and its portico had windows all around, like the other windows; the gate was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Seven steps led up to it, with its portico opposite them, and palm trees were carved on its posts, one on each side.
The inner court also had a gate facing south, and he measured the distance from gate to gate toward the south at one hundred cubits.
He brought me to the inner court through the south gate and measured the south gate; it had the same measurements as the others.
Its chambers, posts, and portico had the same measurements as the others, and both it and its portico had windows all around; the gate was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Porticoes extended all around, twenty-five cubits long and five cubits wide.
Its portico faced the outer court, palm trees were carved on its posts, and eight steps led up to it.
He brought me to the east side of the inner court and measured the gate; it had the same measurements as the others.
Its chambers, posts, and portico had the same measurements as the others, and both it and its portico had windows all around; the gate was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its portico faced the outer court, palm trees were carved on its posts, one on each side, and eight steps led up to it.
He brought me to the north gate and measured it; it had the same measurements as the others.
Its chambers, posts, and portico had the same measurements as the others, and it had windows all around; the gate was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its portico faced the outer court, palm trees were carved on its posts, one on each side, and eight steps led up to it.
A chamber with a doorway stood by the gateposts of the gates; there they wash the burnt offering.
In the portico of the gate were two tables on each side, on which to slaughter the burnt offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering.
Outside, beside the portico at the entrance of the north gate, were two tables on one side and two on the other, on which to slaughter the burnt offering.
At the side of the portico were four tables on each side—eight tables in all—on which to slaughter the sacrifices.

Four tables of cut stone served for the burnt offering, each one cubit and a half long, one cubit and a half wide, and one cubit high; on them they placed the utensils used to slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice.
Hooks, each a handbreadth long, were fastened all around the inside, and the flesh of the offerings was to be placed on the tables.
Outside the inner gate were chambers for the singers in the inner court—one beside the north gate facing south, and one beside the south gate facing north.
The man said to me, "This chamber facing south is for the priests who keep charge of the temple,
and the chamber facing north is for the priests who keep charge of the altar. These are the sons of Zadok, who alone among the Levites may approach the LORD to minister to Him."
He measured the court: a perfect square, one hundred cubits long and one hundred cubits wide. The altar stood in front of the temple.
He brought me to the portico of the temple and measured the jambs of the portico: five cubits on each side. The width of the gateway was three cubits on each side.
The portico was twenty cubits long and eleven cubits wide, with steps by which they ascended it. Pillars stood by the jambs, one on each side.
Then he brought me to the outer sanctuary and measured the jambs: six cubits wide on one side and six cubits wide on the other.
The entrance itself was ten cubits wide, with sidewalls five cubits thick on either side. He measured the sanctuary and found it forty cubits long and twenty cubits wide.
He then entered the inner room and measured the jambs of its entrance at two cubits; the entrance was six cubits wide, and its sidewalls were seven cubits thick.
He measured the room at twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide, corresponding to the outer sanctuary, and he said to me, "This is the Most Holy Place."
He measured the wall of the temple at six cubits thick, and the side chambers at four cubits wide, all around the temple.

The side chambers rose in three stories, thirty chambers on each level. Ledges encircled the temple wall to support the side chambers, so that they did not rest their weight on the temple wall itself.
The chambers grew wider with each ascending story, because the wall stepped back as it rose; consequently, the building broadened from the lowest story to the highest through the middle.
I observed that the temple stood on a raised platform all around, which formed the foundation for the side chambers; it measured a full six cubits.
The outer wall of the side chambers was five cubits thick.
Between these chambers and the temple lay an open space twenty cubits wide on every side.
The side chambers opened onto this open area through one doorway, with one doorway facing north and another facing south; the open area itself was five cubits wide all around.
The building facing the separate courtyard on the west was seventy cubits wide; its wall was five cubits thick all around, and its length was ninety cubits.
He measured the temple at one hundred cubits long; the separate courtyard, the building, and their walls were also one hundred cubits long.
The width of the east front of the temple and of the separate courtyard was one hundred cubits.

He also measured the building that faced the rear of the separate courtyard, together with its galleries on either side, at one hundred cubits. The inner sanctuary and the porticoes of the court were included in these measurements.

The thresholds, the beveled windows, and the galleries around all three sections faced the threshold; each was paneled with wood all around, from the floor up to the windows, and the windows were covered.
From above the doorway to the inner house and to the outside, and on every wall all around, inside and outside, the work was executed according to measure.
Cherubim and palm trees were carved, with a palm tree between each cherub; each cherub had two faces.

One face was human, turned toward the palm tree on one side, and the other was that of a young lion, turned toward the palm tree on the opposite side; this pattern extended around the entire building.
From the floor to above the doorway, cherubim and palm trees were carved on the wall of the sanctuary.
The sanctuary had a square doorframe, and the front of the Holy Place had a corresponding appearance.
The altar was made of wood—three cubits high and two cubits long—with its corners, base, and sides of wood. He said to me, "This is the table that stands before the LORD."
The outer sanctuary and the Holy Place each had two doors.
Each door had two folding leaves—two leaves for one door and two for the other.
Cherubim and palm trees were carved on the doors of the sanctuary, just as they were carved on the walls. A wooden canopy extended over the outside of the doorway, facing the portico.
Beveled windows and palm trees appeared on both sides of the portico's jambs, as well as on the side chambers of the temple and on the canopies.
He led me out by the way to the north, to the outer court, and brought me to the chamber that faced the separate place and faced the building toward the north.
Its entrance faced north; it was one hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide.
The galleries were set back in three tiers, corresponding to the twenty cubits of the inner court and to the pavement of the outer court.
Before the chambers ran an inner walkway ten cubits wide, with a passage one cubit wide, and their doors opened to the north.
The upper rooms were narrower, because the terraces occupied more of their space than those below and in the middle of the building.
Because the chambers rose in three stories like the pillars of the courts yet lacked actual pillars, their upper stories were set back from the lower and middle ones at ground level.
Outside them, a wall fifty cubits long ran opposite the chambers along the outer court.
The chambers facing the outer court were fifty cubits long, while the full length facing the temple was one hundred cubits.
Below these chambers was an entrance from the east, by which one entered them from the outer court.
Along the eastern wall of the court, opposite the separate place and the building, were chambers.
A walkway lay before them, resembling the chambers facing north: as long as they were, so wide, with all their exits, regulations, and doors.
Their doors matched those of the south-facing chambers: a door stood at the head of the walkway, the walkway before the garden hedge, as one entered from the east.

He said to me, "The chambers on the north and on the south, facing the separate place, are holy chambers. There the priests who are nearest to the LORD shall eat the most holy offerings; there they shall place the most holy offerings, the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering, because the place is holy."

When the priests enter, they shall not go out from the holy place to the outer court; there, in the court, they shall lay aside the garments in which they minister, because they are holy, and put on other garments before they approach the people.
When he had finished measuring the inner house, he led me out by the gate facing east and measured the area all around.
He measured the east side with the measuring reed: five hundred reeds.
He measured the north side: five hundred reeds.
He measured the south side: five hundred reeds.
He turned to the west side and measured: five hundred reeds.
He measured it on all four sides. It had a wall all around, five hundred cubits long and five hundred cubits wide, to separate the holy from the common.
Then he brought me to the gate—the gate facing east.
And there was the glory of the God of Israel, coming from the east. His voice sounded like the roar of many waters, and the earth was radiant with His glory.
The vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when He came to destroy the city, and like the vision I had seen by the River Chebar; and I fell on my face.
The glory of the LORD entered the temple by the gate facing east.
Then the Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple.
While the man stood beside me, I heard someone speaking to me from the temple.

“Son of man, this is the place of My throne and the place for the soles of My feet, where I will dwell among the Israelites forever. The house of Israel and their kings must no longer defile My holy name by their prostitution or by the carcasses of their kings at their high places.

When they set their threshold beside My threshold and their doorposts beside My doorposts, with only a wall between Me and them, they defiled My holy name by the abominations they committed; so I consumed them in My anger.
Now let them put their prostitution and the carcasses of their kings far from Me, and I will dwell among them forever.
“As for you, Son of man, describe the temple to the house of Israel, so that they may be ashamed of their iniquities. Let them measure the plan.

And if they are ashamed of all they have done, make known to them the design of the temple—its arrangement, its exits and entrances, its entire design, and all its statutes, forms, and laws. Write it down before their eyes, so that they may keep its entire design and all its statutes and carry them out.”
This is the law of the temple: The whole area all around the top of the mountain shall be most holy. Behold, this is the law of the temple.

And these are the measurements of the altar in cubits (the cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth): The gutter shall be a cubit deep and a cubit wide, with a rim of one span around its edge. And this is the height of the altar.
From the base on the ground to the lower ledge shall be two cubits, and the width one cubit; and from the smaller ledge to the larger ledge shall be four cubits, and the width one cubit.
The altar hearth shall be four cubits high, and four horns shall project upward from the hearth.
The altar hearth shall be square, twelve cubits long and twelve cubits wide.
The ledge shall be square, fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits wide on all four sides, with a rim of half a cubit around it and a gutter of one cubit around it. Its steps shall face east.
Then He said to me, “Son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says: These are the statutes of the altar on the day it is built, for offering burnt offerings on it and for sprinkling blood on it.
You shall give a young bull as a sin offering to the Levitical priests of the descendants of Zadok, who approach Me to minister to Me—declares the Lord GOD.
You shall take some of its blood and put it on the four horns of the altar, on the four corners of the ledge, and all around the rim. Thus you shall purify it and make atonement for it.
You shall take the bull of the sin offering and burn it in the appointed place of the temple, outside the sanctuary.
“On the second day you shall offer a male goat without blemish for a sin offering, and they shall purify the altar as they purified it with the bull.
When you have finished purifying it, you shall offer a young bull without blemish and a ram without blemish from the flock.
You shall present them before the LORD, and the priests shall throw salt on them and offer them up as a burnt offering to the LORD.
For seven days you shall prepare a goat for a sin offering each day, along with a young bull and a ram from the flock, both without blemish.
For seven days they shall make atonement for the altar and cleanse it and consecrate it.
And when these days are completed, from the eighth day onward the priests shall offer your burnt offerings and your peace offerings on the altar, and I will accept you, declares the Lord GOD.”
He brought me back by way of the outer gate of the sanctuary facing east, and it was shut.
The LORD said to me, "This gate will remain shut; it will not be opened, and no one will enter through it, because the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered through it. Therefore it will remain shut."
Only the prince may sit in it to eat bread before the LORD; he will enter by way of the porch of the gate and go out by the same way.
He brought me to the front of the temple by way of the north gate, and I saw the glory of the LORD filling the house of the LORD; I fell on my face.

The LORD said to me, "Son of man, pay close attention and look with your eyes and listen with your ears to everything I tell you concerning all the statutes and laws of the house of the LORD. Pay close attention to the entrance of the house and to all its exits."
Say to the rebellious house of Israel, "Thus says the Lord the LORD: House of Israel, you have had enough of all your abominations.

When you brought foreigners—uncircumcised in heart and flesh—into My sanctuary, profaning My house, while you offered My food, the fat and the blood, they broke My covenant in addition to all your abominations.
You have not kept charge of My holy things; instead, you have appointed others to keep My charge in My sanctuary for yourselves.
Thus says the Lord the LORD: No foreigner uncircumcised in heart or flesh will enter My sanctuary—not any foreigner among the Israelites."
But the Levites who went far from Me when Israel strayed from Me after their idols will bear their guilt.

They will serve in My sanctuary, keeping charge at the gates of the house and ministering to the house. They will slaughter burnt offerings and sacrifices for the people and stand before them to serve them.

Because they served the people in the presence of their idols and caused the house of Israel to stumble into iniquity, I have sworn against them, declares the Lord the LORD, and they will bear their iniquity.
They must not come near Me to serve as priests or approach any of My holy things, especially the most holy things; they will bear their shame and the abominations they committed.
I will appoint them to keep charge of the temple, for all its service and all that is done in it.

But the Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept charge of My sanctuary when the Israelites went astray from Me, will come near to Me to serve Me. They will stand before Me to offer Me fat and blood, declares the Lord the LORD.
They will enter My sanctuary and come near My table to serve Me, and they will keep My charge.
When they enter the gates of the inner court, they must wear linen garments; no wool may be on them while they serve at the gates of the inner court or inside.
They must wear linen turbans on their heads and linen undergarments on their waists, and they must not wear anything that makes them sweat.

When they go out to the outer court to the people, they must remove the garments in which they served, leave them in the holy rooms, and put on other garments, so that they do not consecrate the people with their garments.
They must not shave their heads or let their hair grow long; they must trim their hair.
No priest may drink wine when he enters the inner court.
They must not marry widows or divorced women, but only virgins from Israel's descendants, or a widow of a priest.
They will teach My people the difference between holy and profane and help them distinguish unclean from clean.
In disputes they will stand to judge according to My ordinances; they will keep My laws and statutes at all My appointed feasts and sanctify My Sabbaths.
They must not defile themselves by approaching a dead person, except for father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or an unmarried sister.
Afterward he must count seven days for his purification.
On the day he enters the sanctuary, into the inner court, to serve in the sanctuary, he must offer his sin offering, declares the Lord the LORD.
It will be their inheritance: I am their inheritance. You must give them no possession in Israel; I am their possession.
They will eat the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering, and every devoted thing in Israel will belong to them.

The first of all firstfruits and every contribution from all your contributions will belong to the priests; you must also give the priest the first of your dough, so that a blessing may rest on your house.
The priests must not eat anything found dead or torn by beasts, whether bird or animal.

When you allot the land as an inheritance, you shall set apart a portion for the LORD, a holy portion of the land: twenty-five thousand cubits long and ten thousand cubits wide. It shall be holy throughout its entire border.
Within this area there shall be a square for the sanctuary, five hundred cubits by five hundred cubits, with fifty cubits of open land around it.
From this measured area you shall measure a length of twenty-five thousand cubits and a width of ten thousand cubits, and in it shall be the sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.
It shall be a holy portion of the land for the priests, the ministers of the sanctuary who approach to minister to the LORD; it shall be a place for their houses and a holy place for the sanctuary.
An area twenty-five thousand cubits long and ten thousand cubits wide shall belong to the Levites, the ministers of the temple, as their possession, with twenty rooms.
You shall give the city an allotment five thousand cubits wide and twenty-five thousand cubits long, alongside the holy portion; it shall belong to the whole house of Israel.

The prince shall have land on both sides of the holy district and the city property—bordering the holy district on one side and the city property on the other—extending westward and eastward, with a length equal to one of the tribal portions, from the western border to the eastern border.
This land shall be his property in Israel; and My princes shall no longer oppress My people, but they shall give the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes.

This is what the Lord the LORD says: "Enough for you, princes of Israel! Put away violence and plundering, practice justice and righteousness, and stop your dispossessions of My people," declares the Lord the LORD.
You shall have honest balances, an honest ephah, and an honest bath.
The ephah and the bath shall be the same measure, so that the bath contains one-tenth of a homer and the ephah one-tenth of a homer; their measure shall be according to the homer.
The shekel shall be twenty gerahs; twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels, and fifteen shekels shall make a mina for you.
This is the contribution you shall offer: one-sixth of an ephah from a homer of wheat, and one-sixth of an ephah from a homer of barley.
The prescribed portion of oil shall be one-tenth of a bath from each cor—a cor being ten baths, or one homer, since ten baths make a homer.

From the flock, one sheep out of every two hundred from the well-watered pastures of Israel shall be given for grain offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings, to make atonement for them, declares the Lord the LORD.
All the people of the land shall contribute to this offering for the prince in Israel.

It shall be the prince’s duty to provide the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings for the festivals, new moons, Sabbaths, and all the appointed feasts of the house of Israel. He shall provide the sin offering, grain offering, burnt offering, and peace offerings to make atonement for the house of Israel.
This is what the Lord the LORD says: "In the first month, on the first day of the month, you are to take a young bull without blemish and purify the sanctuary."

The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering and put it on the doorposts of the temple, on the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner court.
You are to do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who sins unintentionally or through ignorance; and you are to make atonement for the temple.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you shall have the Passover, a feast of seven days; unleavened bread shall be eaten.
On that day the prince shall provide for himself and for all the people of the land a bull for a sin offering.
During the seven days of the feast he shall provide seven bulls and seven rams without blemish as a burnt offering to the LORD each day, and a male goat for a sin offering each day.
He shall provide a grain offering of an ephah for each bull and an ephah for each ram, and a hin of oil for each ephah.
In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, during the feast, he shall make the same provision for seven days—as a sin offering, burnt offering, grain offering, and oil.
Thus says the Lord the LORD: “The inner gate of the courtyard facing east shall be shut during the six working days, but it shall be opened on the Sabbath and on the day of the New Moon.

The prince shall enter from outside by way of the vestibule of the gate and stand at the gatepost; the priests shall prepare his burnt offering and his peace offerings, and he shall worship at the threshold of the gate. Then he shall go out, but the gate shall not be closed until evening.
On the Sabbaths and on the New Moons, the people of the land shall worship at the entrance of that gate before the the LORD.”
The burnt offering that the prince presents to the the LORD on the Sabbath day shall be six lambs without blemish and a ram without blemish.
The grain offering for the ram shall be an ephah, and the grain offering for the lambs shall be as much as he can afford, together with a hin of oil per ephah.
On the day of the New Moon he shall offer a young bull without blemish, six lambs, and a ram; they shall be without blemish.
He shall provide a grain offering of an ephah for the bull, an ephah for the ram, and as much as he can afford for the lambs, together with a hin of oil per ephah.
When the prince enters, he shall enter by way of the vestibule of the gate and go out by the same way.

But when the people of the land come before the the LORD at the appointed feasts, whoever enters by the north gate to worship shall go out by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate shall go out by the north gate. No one shall return by the gate through which he came, but each shall go out straight ahead.
The prince shall be among them; when they enter, he shall enter, and when they go out, he shall go out.
At the festivals and the appointed feasts, the grain offering shall be an ephah with a bull, an ephah with a ram, and as much as he can afford with the lambs, together with a hin of oil per ephah.

When the prince provides a freewill offering, either a burnt offering or peace offerings, as a freewill offering to the the LORD, the gate facing east shall be opened for him. He shall offer his burnt offering and his peace offerings as he does on the Sabbath, and then he shall go out; after he has gone out, the gate shall be shut.
You shall present a lamb a year old without blemish as a burnt offering to the the LORD each day; morning by morning you shall present it.

You shall also provide with it a grain offering each morning: one-sixth of an ephah, and one-third of a hin of oil to moisten the fine flour, as a grain offering to the the LORD. This is a perpetual statute.
So the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil shall be prepared every morning as a continual burnt offering.
Thus says the Lord the LORD: “If the prince gives a gift to any of his sons, it is his inheritance and shall belong to his sons; it is their possession by inheritance.
But if he gives a gift of his inheritance to one of his servants, it shall be his until the Year of Liberty; then it shall return to the prince. His inheritance, however, shall belong to his sons.

The prince shall not take any of the people’s inheritance or evict them from their property. He shall give an inheritance to his sons from his own property, so that none of My people shall be scattered from his property.”
Then he brought me through the entrance beside the gate into the holy chambers for the priests, which faced north; and behold, there was a place at the western extremity.

He said to me, “This is the place where the priests shall boil the guilt offering and the sin offering and bake the grain offering, so that they do not bring them out into the outer court and sanctify the people.”
Then he brought me out into the outer court and led me around to the four corners of the court; and behold, in every corner of the court there was an inner court.
In the four corners of the court were enclosed courts, forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide; the four of them in the corners had the same dimensions.
A row of masonry ran all around them—around the four of them—and boiling places had been made beneath the rows all around.
Then he said to me, “These are the boiling houses where the ministers of the temple shall boil the sacrifices of the people.”

He brought me back to the entrance of the temple, and, behold, water was flowing out from under the threshold of the temple toward the east—for the temple faced east—and the water was flowing down from under the south side of the temple, south of the altar.
Then he brought me out by way of the north gate and led me around the outside to the outer gate facing east; and, behold, water was trickling from the south side.
When the man went out toward the east with a measuring line in his hand, he measured a thousand cubits and led me through the water, and it was ankle-deep.
He measured another thousand cubits and led me through the water, and it was knee-deep; then he measured another thousand and led me through the water, and it was waist-deep.
He measured another thousand, and it was a river that I could not cross, for the water had risen and was deep enough to swim in—a river that could not be crossed.
He said to me, “Son of man, have you seen this?” Then he led me and brought me back to the bank of the river.
When I returned, I saw that on the bank of the river there were very many trees on both sides.
He said to me, “These waters go out to the eastern region and flow down into the Arabah. When they enter the sea—the sea of stagnant waters—the water will become fresh.

Wherever the river goes, every living creature that swarms will live, and there will be very many fish, because these waters go there and become fresh; so everything will live wherever the river reaches.”
Fishermen will stand along its banks; from En-gedi to En-eglaim it will be a place for spreading nets. Its fish will be of many kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea, exceedingly abundant.
But its swamps and marshes will not become fresh; they will be left for salt.

Along both banks of the river, every tree for food will grow; its leaf will not wither, nor will its fruit fail. It will bear fresh fruit every month, because its water flows from the sanctuary. Its fruit will be for food, and its leaves for healing.
Thus says the Lord, the LORD: “This is the boundary by which you shall inherit the land according to the twelve tribes of Israel; Joseph shall have two portions.
And you shall inherit it, each as his brother, because I swore to give it to your fathers; this land shall fall to you as an inheritance. “
This is the boundary of the land: on the north side, from the Great Sea by way of Hethlon toward Zedad.
Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim, which is between the border of Damascus and the border of Hamath; and Hazar-hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.
The boundary shall be from the sea to Hazar-enan, along the border of Damascus and the border of Hamath to the north; this is the north side.
On the east side, from between Hauran and Damascus, along the Jordan, between Gilead and the land of Israel, to the eastern sea, as far as Tamar; this is the east side.
On the south side, from Tamar to the waters of Meribah-kadesh, along the Brook of Egypt to the Great Sea; this is the south side.
On the west side, the Great Sea shall be the boundary, up to a point opposite Lebo-hamath; this is the west side. “
You shall divide this land among you according to the tribes of Israel.

You shall allot it as an inheritance for yourselves and for the strangers who sojourn among you, who bear children among you; and they shall be to you as native-born among the children of Israel. With you they shall be allotted an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
In whatever tribe the stranger sojourns, there you shall give him his inheritance, declares the Lord, the LORD.”

These are the names of the tribes: at the northern frontier, Dan shall receive one portion, bordering the road of Hethlon to the entrance of Hamath and reaching Hazar-enan on the border of Damascus, with Hamath to the north; and Dan’s territory shall extend from the east side to the west side.
Asher shall receive one portion along the border of Dan, from the east side to the west side.
Naphtali shall receive one portion along the border of Asher, from the east side to the west side.
Manasseh shall receive one portion along the border of Naphtali, from the east side to the west side.
Ephraim shall receive one portion along the border of Manasseh, from the east side to the west side.
Reuben shall receive one portion along the border of Ephraim, from the east side to the west side.
Judah shall receive one portion along the border of Reuben, from the east side to the west side.
Along the border of Judah, from the east side to the west side, shall be the offering you set apart: 25,000 cubits in width and as long as one of the portions; the sanctuary shall be in its midst.
The offering you set apart to the the LORD shall be 25,000 cubits in length and 10,000 cubits in width.

This holy offering shall belong to the priests: 25,000 cubits on the north, 10,000 cubits on the west in width, 10,000 cubits on the east in width, and 25,000 cubits on the south in length; and the sanctuary of the the LORD shall be in its center.
It shall be for the consecrated priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept My charge and did not go astray when the Israelites went astray, as the Levites did.
It shall be for them an offering from the offering of the land, a most holy portion, bordering the territory of the Levites.
Alongside the border of the priests, the Levites shall have 25,000 cubits in length and 10,000 cubits in width; the entire area shall be 25,000 by 10,000 cubits.
They shall not sell any of it, nor exchange it, nor transfer this choice portion of the land, because it is holy to the the LORD.
The remaining land, 5,000 cubits in width alongside the 25,000, shall be common land for the city—for dwelling and for pasture—and the city shall be in its midst.
These shall be its measurements: 4,500 cubits on the north side, 4,500 cubits on the south side, 4,500 cubits on the east side, and 4,500 cubits on the west side.
The pastureland around the city shall be 250 cubits on the north, 250 cubits on the south, 250 cubits on the east, and 250 cubits on the west.
The remainder of the length bordering the holy offering—10,000 cubits eastward and 10,000 cubits westward—shall belong to the workers of the city, and its produce shall be food for them.
The workers of the city who cultivate it shall come from all the tribes of Israel.
The entire portion shall be a square—25,000 cubits by 25,000 cubits—and you shall set apart the holy offering together with the property of the city.

The remaining land on both sides of the holy offering and of the property of the city shall belong to the prince; it shall extend eastward from the 25,000 cubits of the holy offering to the eastern border, and westward from the 25,000 cubits to the western border, and the holy offering and the sanctuary of the temple shall be in the center.

Thus the property of the Levites and the property of the city shall lie in the center of the area belonging to the prince; the prince’s portion shall lie between the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin.
As for the rest of the tribes, Benjamin shall receive one portion from the east side to the west side.
Simeon shall receive one portion along the border of Benjamin, from the east side to the west side.
Issachar shall receive one portion along the border of Simeon, from the east side to the west side.
Zebulun shall receive one portion along the border of Issachar, from the east side to the west side.
Gad shall receive one portion along the border of Zebulun, from the east side to the west side.
The southern border of Gad shall run from Tamar to the waters of Meribah-kadesh, then along the Brook of Egypt to the Great Sea.
This is the land you shall allot as an inheritance to the tribes of Israel, and these are their portions, declares the Lord the LORD.
These shall be the exits of the city: on the north side, 4,500 cubits.
The gates of the city shall be named after the tribes of Israel: on the north, three gates—the gate of Reuben, the gate of Judah, and the gate of Levi.
On the east side, 4,500 cubits, three gates—the gate of Joseph, the gate of Benjamin, and the gate of Dan.
On the south side, 4,500 cubits, three gates—the gate of Simeon, the gate of Issachar, and the gate of Zebulun.
On the west side, 4,500 cubits, three gates—the gate of Gad, the gate of Asher, and the gate of Naphtali.
The circumference of the city shall be 18,000 cubits, and from that day on the name of the city shall be: the LORD Is There.
In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.

And the LORD delivered Jehoiakim king of Judah into his power, together with some of the vessels of the house of God; he carried them to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, and placed the vessels in the treasury of his god.
Then the king commanded Ashpenaz, his chief of the eunuchs, to bring in some of the Israelites from the royal family and from the nobility—

young men without physical defect, handsome, proficient in all wisdom, endowed with knowledge and insight, and able to serve in the king’s palace. He was to teach them the literature and language of the Chaldeans.

The king assigned them a daily portion of the royal delicacies and of the wine he drank, and he ordered that they be sustained and trained for three years, after which they were to enter the king’s service.
Among these were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah of the tribe of Judah.
The chief of the eunuchs gave them names: Daniel he called Belteshazzar; Hananiah, Shadrach; Mishael, Meshach; and Azariah, Abednego.

But Daniel resolved in his heart that he would not defile himself with the king’s delicacies or with the wine he drank. Therefore he asked the chief of the eunuchs for permission not to defile himself.
Now God had given Daniel favor and compassion in the sight of the chief of the eunuchs.

The chief of the eunuchs said to Daniel, “I fear my lord the king, who has assigned your food and your drink. Why should he see your faces looking worse than those of the other young men your age? You would endanger my head before the king.”
Daniel then said to the steward whom the chief of the eunuchs had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
“Please test your servants for ten days. Give us vegetables to eat and water to drink.
Then let our appearance be compared before you with that of the young men who eat the king’s delicacies, and deal with your servants according to what you see.”
He agreed to this proposal and tested them for ten days.
At the end of the ten days, their appearance was better and they were healthier than all the young men who ate the king’s delicacies.
So the steward took away their delicacies and the wine they were to drink, and gave them vegetables.
To these four young men God gave knowledge and skill in all literature and wisdom; and Daniel understood all visions and dreams.
At the end of the time the king had set for their training, the chief of the eunuchs brought them before Nebuchadnezzar.
The king spoke with them, and among all of them none was found like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah; so they entered the king’s service.
In every matter of wisdom and understanding about which the king questioned them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his entire kingdom.
Daniel remained there until the first year of King Cyrus.
In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams that left his spirit deeply agitated, and sleep abandoned him.
The king commanded that the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and Chaldeans be summoned to tell him what he had dreamed. When they arrived, they stood before the king.
The king said to them, “I have had a dream, and my spirit is troubled until I understand it.”
The Chaldeans answered the king in Aramaic: “Long live the king! Tell your servants the dream, and we will declare its interpretation.”

The king replied to the Chaldeans, “My decision is final: if you do not make the dream known to me, together with its interpretation, you will be torn to pieces and your houses will be reduced to rubble.
But if you declare the dream and its interpretation, you will receive from me gifts, rewards, and great honor. Therefore, tell me the dream and its interpretation.”
They answered a second time, “Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will declare its interpretation.”
The king answered, “I know with certainty that you are deliberately stalling, because you see that my decision is final.

If you do not make the dream known to me, one decree applies to all of you: you have colluded to speak deceitful and corrupt words before me until circumstances change. So tell me the dream, and then I will know that you can declare its interpretation.”
The Chaldeans answered the king, “No mortal on earth can do what the king demands, for no great and powerful king has ever asked such a thing of any magician, enchanter, or Chaldean.
What the king asks is too difficult; no one can reveal it to him except the gods, whose dwelling is not with mortals.”
At this the king became furious and enraged, and he commanded that all the wise men of Babylon be destroyed.
So the decree was issued, and the wise men were about to be killed; they sought out Daniel and his companions to execute them.
Then Daniel replied with prudence and discretion to Arioch, the captain of the king’s guard, who had gone out to execute the wise men of Babylon.
He asked Arioch, the king’s captain, “Why is the king’s decree so severe?” Then Arioch explained the matter to Daniel.
So Daniel went in and asked the king to grant him time, promising that he would declare the interpretation to the king.

Then Daniel went to his house and explained the matter to his companions—Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah—and urged them to seek mercy from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his companions would not be destroyed along with the rest of Babylon’s wise men.
Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a night vision, and Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
Daniel answered and said, “Blessed be the name of God from age to age, for wisdom and power belong to Him.
He changes the times and seasons; He removes kings and establishes kings. He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who have understanding.
He reveals what is deep and hidden; He knows what lies in darkness, and light dwells with Him.
To You, O God of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, because You have given me wisdom and power and have now revealed to me what we requested of You—You have made known to us the king’s matter.”

Therefore Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy Babylon’s wise men. He went and said to him, “Do not destroy Babylon’s wise men. Bring me before the king, and I will declare the interpretation to the king.”
Then Arioch hurriedly brought Daniel before the king and said to him, “I have found a man among the exiles from Judah who will declare the interpretation to the king.”
The king answered Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, “Are you able to make known to me the dream I saw and its interpretation?”
Daniel answered before the king, “No wise man, enchanter, magician, or astrologer can reveal to the king the mystery he has asked about.

But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, and He has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the latter days. Your dream and the visions of your head as you lay on your bed are these:
As for you, O king, while you lay on your bed, your thoughts turned to what would happen after this, and the revealer of mysteries has made known to you what is to be.

As for me, this mystery has been revealed to me, not because I possess greater wisdom than anyone alive, but so that the interpretation may be made known to the king, and that you may understand the thoughts of your mind.”
“You, O king, were watching, and behold, there was a great statue. This statue was enormous and dazzling, and it stood before you; its appearance was terrifying.
The head of the statue was of fine gold; its chest and arms were of silver; its belly and thighs were of bronze;
its legs were of iron; its feet were partly of iron and partly of clay.
As you watched, a stone was cut out, not by human hands, and it struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and crushed them.

Then the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold were crushed together and became like chaff from the summer threshing floors; the wind carried them away, and no trace of them could be found. But the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
“This is the dream. Now we will tell the king its interpretation.
You, O king, are king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given kingdom, power, strength, and glory.
Wherever people dwell, along with the beasts of the field and the birds of the heavens, He has placed them in your hand and has made you ruler over them all—you are the head of gold.
After you, another kingdom will arise, inferior to yours; then a third kingdom, of bronze, which will rule over all the earth.
Finally, a fourth kingdom will be strong as iron, because iron crushes and shatters everything; and like iron that pulverizes, it will crush and break all these.
“And as you saw the feet and toes—partly of potter’s clay and partly of iron—so the kingdom will be divided. Yet it will retain some of the firmness of iron, just as you saw iron mixed with clay.
As the toes were partly iron and partly clay, so the kingdom will be partly strong and partly brittle.
As you saw iron mixed with clay, so people will mingle with one another through marriage, but they will not hold together, just as iron does not mix with clay.

In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, and its sovereignty will not be transferred to another people. It will crush all those kingdoms and bring them to an end, and it will stand forever.

This is the meaning of the stone you saw cut from the mountain without human hands, which crushed the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold. The great God has made known to the king what will happen after this. The dream is certain, and its interpretation is trustworthy.”
Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and paid homage to Daniel, and he commanded that an offering and incense be presented to him.
The king answered Daniel, “Truly, your God is the God of gods and the Lord of kings and the revealer of mysteries, for you were able to reveal this mystery.”
Then the king gave Daniel great honors and many lavish gifts, and he appointed him ruler over the entire province of Babylon and chief prefect over all its wise men.
At Daniel’s request, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to administer the province of Babylon, while Daniel remained at the king’s court.
King Nebuchadnezzar made a golden image sixty cubits high and six cubits wide, and he set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.

Then King Nebuchadnezzar sent word to assemble the satraps, prefects, governors, advisers, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the other provincial officials, so that they might attend the dedication of the image he had set up.

So the satraps, prefects, governors, advisers, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the other provincial officials assembled for the dedication of the image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up, and they stood before it.
Then the herald proclaimed with a mighty voice, “Peoples, nations, and languages, this is what you are commanded:
As soon as you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes, and every kind of music, you are to fall down and worship the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
Whoever does not fall down and worship shall be thrown immediately into the midst of a blazing furnace.”

Therefore, when all the peoples heard the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, and every kind of music, all the peoples, nations, and languages fell down and worshiped the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
