I will sell your sons and daughters into the hands of the people of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans, to a distant nation, for the LORD has spoken.
Proclaim this among the nations: Prepare for war; rouse the mighty men; let all the warriors approach and advance.
Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning hooks into spears; let the weak say, "I am strong!"
Hurry and come, all you nations from every side, and assemble there. Bring down Your warriors, O the LORD!
Let the nations be roused and advance to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the nations on every side.
Swing the sickle, for the harvest is ripe; come and tread the grapes, for the winepress is full; the vats overflow, for their wickedness is great.
Multitudes, multitudes in the Valley of Decision! For the Day of the LORD is near in the Valley of Decision.
The sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will no longer shine.
The LORD will roar from Zion and raise His voice from Jerusalem; heaven and earth will tremble. But the LORD will be a refuge for His people, a stronghold for the people of Israel.
Then you will know that I am the LORD your God, who dwells in Zion, My holy mountain. Jerusalem will be holy, and foreigners will never again pass through it.

In that day the mountains will drip with new wine, and the hills will flow with milk; all the streams of Judah will run with water, and a spring will flow from the house of the LORD to water the Valley of Shittim.
Egypt will become a wasteland and Edom a desert wasteland, because of the violence done to the people of Judah, in whose land they shed innocent blood.
But Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
For I will avenge their blood, which I have not yet avenged, for the LORD dwells in Zion.

The words of Amos, who was among the shepherds of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel two years before the earthquake, in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel.
The LORD roars from Zion and utters His voice from Jerusalem; the pastures of the shepherds mourn, and the summit of Carmel withers.
Thus says the LORD: "For their many transgressions, I will not revoke the punishment, because they have brutally crushed Gilead.
I will send fire into the house of Hazael, and it will consume the palaces of Ben-hadad.

I will break the defenses of Damascus, cut off the inhabitants of the Valley of Aven, and remove the one who holds the scepter from Beth-eden; the people of Aram will go into exile to Kir," says the LORD.
Thus says the LORD: "For their many transgressions, I will not revoke the punishment, because they carried an entire population into exile to hand it over to Edom.
I will send fire upon the wall of Gaza, and it will consume its palaces.

I will cut off the inhabitants of Ashdod and the one who holds the scepter from Ashkelon; I will turn My hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines will perish," declares the Lord, the LORD.
Thus says the LORD: "For their many transgressions, I will not revoke the punishment, because they delivered up an entire captive population to Edom and did not remember the covenant of brotherhood.
I will send fire upon the wall of Tyre, and it will consume its palaces."

Thus says the LORD: "For their many transgressions, I will not revoke the punishment, because he pursued his brother with the sword and showed no mercy; his anger raged continually, and his wrath he kept forever.
I will send fire upon Teman, and it will consume the palaces of Bozrah."
Thus says the LORD: "For their many transgressions, I will not revoke the punishment, because they ripped open pregnant women in Gilead to enlarge their territory.
I will set fire to the wall of Rabbah, and it will consume its palaces, amid shouting on the day of battle and amid a tempest on the day of the whirlwind.
Their king will go into exile, he and his princes together," says the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not revoke its punishment, because he burned the bones of the king of Edom to lime.
So I will send fire against Moab, and it will consume the citadels of Kerioth. Moab will perish amid uproar, amid shouting, and amid the sound of the trumpet.
I will cut off the judge from its midst and slay all its princes along with him,” declares the LORD.

This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of Judah, and for four, I will not revoke its punishment, because they rejected the law of the LORD and have not kept His statutes, but their false gods led them astray—the false gods their fathers followed.
So I will send fire against Judah, and it will consume the palaces of Jerusalem,” declares the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not revoke its punishment, because they sell the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals.
They trample the heads of the poor into the dust of the earth and deny justice to the oppressed. A man and his father go in to the same young woman, thereby profaning My holy name.
They lie down beside every altar on garments taken in pledge, and in the house of their God they drink the wine of those who have been fined.
“Yet it was I who destroyed the Amorite before them, whose height was like that of cedars and who was as strong as oaks. I destroyed his fruit above and his roots below.
It was I who brought you up from the land of Egypt and led you forty years in the wilderness, so that you might possess the land of the Amorite.
I raised up prophets from among your sons and Nazirites from among your young men. Is this not so, O children of Israel?” declares the LORD.
“But you made the Nazirites drink wine and commanded the prophets, ‘You shall not prophesy.’”
“Behold, I will crush you in your place, as a cart is crushed when loaded with sheaves.
The swift will have no escape; the strong will not be able to use his strength, and the warrior will not save his life.
The archer will not hold his ground, the swift runner will not escape, and the horseman will not save his life.
Even the bravest among the mighty will flee naked on that day,” declares the LORD.
Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, children of Israel—against the whole family that I brought up out of the land of Egypt:
You alone have I known among all the families of the earth; therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities.
Do two walk together unless they have agreed to meet?
Does a lion roar in the forest when he has no prey? Does a young lion cry out from his den unless he has caught something?
Does a bird fall into a snare on the ground unless a trap has been set for it? Does a snare spring up from the earth unless it has caught something?
If a trumpet is blown in a city, do the people not tremble? If calamity comes upon a city, has not the LORD done it?
Surely the Lord, the LORD, does nothing without revealing His secret to His servants the prophets.
The lion has roared; who will not fear? The Lord, the LORD, has spoken; who will not prophesy?

Proclaim over the palaces of Ashdod and over the palaces in the land of Egypt, and say, “Assemble on the mountains of Samaria and observe the great tumult within her and the oppressions in her midst.”
“They do not know how to do what is right,” declares the LORD—“those who hoard violence and plunder in their palaces.”
Therefore thus says the Lord, the LORD: “An enemy will surround the land, strip you of your strength, and plunder your palaces.”

Thus says the LORD: “As a shepherd rescues from the mouth of a lion two legs or a piece of an ear, so the children of Israel who dwell in Samaria will be rescued—with only a corner of a bed and a piece of a Damascene couch.”
Hear and testify against the house of Jacob, declares the Lord, the LORD, the God of Hosts:
“For on the day when I punish Israel for its transgressions, I will punish the altars of Bethel as well; the horns of the altar will be cut off and fall to the ground.
I will strike the winter house along with the summer house; the houses of ivory will perish, and many houses will come to an end,” declares the LORD.
Hear this word, you pampered women of Bashan on Mount Samaria, who oppress the poor and crush the needy, who say to your masters, “Bring us something to drink.”
The Lord the LORD has sworn by His holiness: “Behold, days are coming upon you when they will take you away with hooks, and your descendants with fishhooks.
You will go out through the breaches, each woman straight ahead, and you will be cast out toward Harmon,” declares the LORD.
“Come to Bethel and transgress; at Gilgal multiply your transgression; bring your sacrifices in the morning, your tithes every three days.
Offer a thanksgiving sacrifice of leavened bread, and proclaim your freewill offerings and make them known; for this is what you love to do, O children of Israel,” declares the Lord the LORD.
“I gave you famine in all your cities and a shortage of bread in every place, yet you did not return to Me,” declares the LORD.

“I also withheld rain from you when the harvest was still three months away. I sent rain on one city but withheld it from another; one field received rain, while the field that did not receive rain withered.
Two or three cities wandered to another city for water but were not satisfied; yet you did not return to Me,” declares the LORD.
“I struck you with blight and mildew; the locust devoured your many gardens and vineyards, your fig trees and your olive trees; yet you did not return to Me,” declares the LORD.

“I sent a plague among you as I did to Egypt; I killed your young men with the sword, along with your captured horses; I filled your nostrils with the stench of your camps; yet you did not return to Me,” declares the LORD.
“I overthrew some of you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a burning stick snatched from the fire; yet you did not return to Me,” declares the LORD.
“Therefore, this is what I will do to you, O Israel; because I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, O Israel.”

For behold, He who forms the mountains and creates the wind, who reveals His thoughts to man, who turns the dawn into darkness and treads on the heights of the earth—the LORD, the God of Hosts, is His name.
Hear this word, O house of Israel—the lament I raise over you:
The virgin Israel has fallen; she will rise no more. She lies forsaken on her own soil, and no one lifts her up.
For thus says the Lord, the LORD: "The city that sends out a thousand men will have only a hundred remain, and the one that sends out a hundred will have only ten remain for the house of Israel."
For thus says the LORD to the house of Israel: "Seek Me and live.
Do not seek Bethel, do not enter Gilgal, and do not cross over to Beersheba; for Gilgal will surely go into exile, and Bethel will be reduced to nothingness."
Seek the LORD and live, lest He break out like fire in the house of Joseph and devour it, with no one to quench it in Bethel.
You who turn justice into wormwood and cast righteousness to the ground!

He who made the Pleiades and Orion, who turns deep darkness into morning and darkens day into night, who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out upon the face of the earth—the the LORD is His name.
He who makes devastation burst upon the strong, so that ruin overtakes the fortress.
They hate the one who reproves in the gate, and they abhor the one who speaks with integrity.

Therefore, because you trample the poor and exact from him a levy of wheat, you have built houses of hewn stone, but you will not dwell in them; you have planted pleasant vineyards, but you will not drink their wine.
For I know that your transgressions are many and your sins are mighty—you who oppress the righteous, accept bribes, and push aside the needy in the gate.
Therefore the prudent keep silent in such a time, for it is an evil time.
Seek good and not evil, that you may live, and so the the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be with you, as you have said.
Hate evil and love good, and establish justice in the gate; perhaps the the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.

Therefore thus says the the LORD, the God of Hosts, the Lord: "In all the squares there will be wailing, and in all the streets they will cry, 'Alas! Alas!' They will summon the farmer to mourning and those skilled in lamentation to wailing.
In all vineyards there will be wailing, for I will pass through your midst," says the the LORD.
Woe to you who desire the day of the the LORD! Why do you desire the day of the the LORD? It is darkness, and not light—
as when a man flees from a lion and a bear meets him, or he enters the house and leans his hand against the wall and a serpent bites him.
Is not the day of the the LORD darkness, and not light, and gloom with no brightness in it?
"I hate, I despise your feasts, and I take no delight in your solemn assemblies.
Even though you offer Me your burnt offerings and your grain offerings, I will not accept them; and the peace offerings of your fattened animals I will not regard.
Take away from Me the noise of your songs; I will not listen to the melody of your harps.
But let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream."
"Did you bring to Me sacrifices and offerings during the forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?
You will carry Sikkuth your king, and Kiyyun your star god—your images that you made for yourselves—
and I will send you into exile beyond Damascus," says the the LORD, whose name is the God of Hosts.
Woe to those who live in ease in Zion, and to those who feel secure on the mountain of Samaria—the distinguished men of the foremost nation, to whom the house of Israel comes.
Cross over to Calneh and observe; go from there to great Hamath; then descend to Gath of the Philistines. Are they superior to your kingdoms? Is their territory more extensive than yours?
You postpone the day of calamity and hasten the reign of violence.
You recline on beds of ivory and sprawl upon your couches. You feast on lambs from the flock and calves from the stall.
You improvise music on the harp as David did, and compose songs for yourselves.
You drink wine from bowls and anoint yourselves with the choicest oils, yet you do not grieve over the ruin of Joseph.
Therefore, you will now be led into exile at the head of the captives, and your feasting and lounging will cease.
The Lord the LORD has sworn by Himself—the LORD, the God of Hosts, declares: “I abhor the pride of Jacob and detest his citadels, so I will surrender the city and all that fills it.”
If ten men remain in one house, they will die.

And if a relative who is to burn the bodies lifts up the bones to carry them out of the house, he will say to the one in the innermost recesses of the house, “Are any still with you?” “None,” that person will reply. Then the relative will say, “Silence! We must not invoke the name of the LORD.”
For the LORD has issued a command; He will shatter the great house into fragments and the small house into rubble.
Do horses gallop on rocky crags? Does one plow there with oxen? Yet you have turned justice into poison and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood.
You who exult over nothing and say, “Have we not seized power for ourselves by our own strength?”
For behold, I am raising up a nation against you, O house of Israel, declares the LORD God of Hosts; and they will oppress you from the entrance of Hamath to the Brook of the Arabah.
This is what the Lord, the LORD, showed me: behold, He was forming locusts just as the latter growth was beginning, after the king's mowings.
When they had finished eating the grass of the land, I said, "O Lord, the LORD, please forgive! How can Jacob stand? He is so small."
The LORD relented concerning this. "It shall not be," said the Lord, the LORD.
This is what the Lord, the LORD, showed me: behold, the Lord, the LORD, was calling for judgment by fire, and it devoured the great deep and was consuming the land.
Then I said, "O Lord, the LORD, cease, please! How can Jacob stand? He is so small."
The LORD relented concerning this. "This also shall not be," said the Lord, the LORD.
This is what He showed me: behold, the Lord was standing beside a wall built with a plumb line, with a plumb line in His hand.
And the LORD said to me, "Amos, what do you see?" And I said, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "Behold, I am setting a plumb line in the midst of My people Israel; I will no longer spare them.
The high places of Isaac shall be made desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste, and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword."
Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, "Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel. The land is not able to bear all his words.
For thus Amos has said, 'Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel must surely go into exile away from his land.'"
And Amaziah said to Amos, "O seer, go, flee to the land of Judah, earn your living there, and prophesy there,
but never again prophesy at Bethel, for it is the king's sanctuary, and it is a royal temple."
Then Amos answered and said to Amaziah, "I was no prophet, nor a prophet's son, but I was a herdsman and a tender of sycamore figs.
But the LORD took me from following the flock, and the LORD said to me, 'Go, prophesy to My people Israel.'"
"You say, 'Do not prophesy against Israel, and do not preach against the house of Isaac.'"

"Your wife shall be a prostitute in the city, and your sons and your daughters shall fall by the sword, and your land shall be measured and divided, and you yourself shall die in an unclean land; and Israel shall surely go into exile away from its land."
Thus the Lord the LORD showed me, and behold, a basket of summer fruit.
And He said, “Amos, what do you see?” And I said, “A basket of summer fruit.” Then the the LORD said to me, “The end has come upon My people Israel; I will no longer spare them.”
“In that day,” declares the Lord the LORD, “the songs of the temple will become wailing. Many will be the corpses, strewn everywhere in silence.
Hear this, you who trample the needy and do away with the humble of the land,
saying, “‘When will the New Moon be over so we can sell grain, and the Sabbath so we can market wheat? We will reduce the ephah and increase the shekel; we will cheat with dishonest scales,
“‘buying the poor with silver and the needy for a pair of sandals, and selling the sweepings of the wheat.’”
The the LORD has sworn by the Pride of Jacob: “I will never forget any of their deeds.”
Will not the land tremble for this, and all who dwell in it mourn? All of it will rise like the Nile; it will surge and subside like the Nile of Egypt.
“And in that day,” declares the Lord the LORD, “I will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight.

I will turn your feasts into mourning and all your songs into lamentation; I will put sackcloth on every waist and baldness on every head. I will make it like the mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day.”
“Behold, the days are coming,” declares the Lord the LORD, “when I will send a famine on the land—not a famine of bread or a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the words of the the LORD.
People will stagger from sea to sea and wander from north to east, seeking the word of the the LORD, but they will not find it.
In that day the beautiful virgins and young men will faint from thirst.
Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria and say, “‘As surely as your god lives, O Dan,’ or, ‘As surely as the way of Beersheba lives’— “they will fall and never rise again.”

I saw the Lord standing by the altar, and He said, “Strike the capitals so that the thresholds quake; shatter them upon the heads of everyone, and I will put to death whoever survives with the sword. No one will escape; no one will be delivered.”
“Though they dig down to Sheol, from there My hand will seize them; though they ascend to heaven, from there I will bring them down.

“Though they hide on the summit of Carmel, there I will search them out and take them; though they conceal themselves from My sight at the bottom of the sea, there I will command the serpent to bite them.
“Though their enemies drive them into exile, there I will command the sword to slay them. I will set My eyes upon them for harm and not for good.”
The Lord, the LORD of Hosts, is He who touches the earth and it melts; all who dwell in it mourn. All of it rises like the Nile and sinks like the river of Egypt.
He builds His upper chambers in the heavens and founds His vault upon the earth. He calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out upon the face of the earth; the LORD is His name.
“Are you not like the Cushites to Me, O children of Israel?” declares the LORD. “Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Arameans from Kir?”
“Surely the eyes of the Lord, the LORD, are on the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from the face of the earth. Yet I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob,” declares the LORD.
“For behold, I will give the command, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations as grain is sifted in a sieve, yet not one pebble will fall to the ground.
“All the sinners among My people will die by the sword—all those who say, ‘Disaster will never overtake or confront us.’”
“In that day I will raise up the fallen tent of David; I will repair its gaps, rebuild its ruins, and restore it as in the days of old,
“so that they may take possession of the remnant of Edom and all the nations called by My name,” declares the LORD, who will do this.

“Behold, the days are coming,” declares the LORD, “when the plowman will overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes will overtake the sower of seed. The mountains will drip with sweet wine, and all the hills will flow with it.”
“I will restore My people Israel from captivity; they will rebuild and inhabit the ruined cities; they will plant vineyards and drink their wine; they will make gardens and eat their fruit.
“I will plant them on their own soil, and they will never again be uprooted from the land that I have given them,” says the LORD your God.

The vision of Obadiah: This is what the Lord, the LORD, says concerning Edom: We have heard a message from the LORD, and an envoy has been sent among the nations to say, 'Rise up, and let us go to war against her!'
"Look, I will make you small among the nations; you will be utterly despised.
The pride of your heart has deceived you, you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, whose home is on high, who say in your heart, 'Who can bring me down to the ground?'
Even if you soar as high as an eagle and set your nest among the stars, from there I will bring you down," declares the LORD.

If thieves had come to you, or robbers in the night—how devastated you would be!—would they not steal only as much as they needed? If grape pickers had come to you, would they not leave some gleanings?
How thoroughly Esau has been plundered; his hidden treasures have been uncovered!
All your allies have driven you to the border; your trusted friends have deceived and overpowered you; those who shared your bread have set a trap beneath you, and you have no discernment.
"On that day," declares the LORD, "will I not destroy the wise from Edom and understanding from Mount Esau?"
Your mighty men, O Teman, will be terrified, so that everyone on Mount Esau will be cut off in the slaughter.
Because of the violence you did to your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will be cut off forever.
On the day you stood by and did nothing, when strangers carried off his wealth and foreigners entered his gates and cast lots for Jerusalem, you were like one of them.
You should not have gloated over your brother in his day of calamity, nor rejoiced over the people of Judah in the day of their ruin, nor boasted on the day of their distress.

You should not have entered the gate of My people in the day of their disaster; you should not have gloated at their misfortune in the day of their disaster; and you should not have seized their wealth in the day of their disaster.
You should not have stood at the crossroads to cut down their fugitives, nor should you have handed over their survivors in the day of distress.
For the day of the LORD is near for all nations. As you have done, so it will be done to you; your recompense will return upon your own head.
For just as you drank on My holy mountain, so all the nations will drink continually; they will drink and swallow, and they will be as though they never existed.
But on Mount Zion there will be deliverance, and it will be holy, and the house of Jacob will possess its inheritance.

The house of Jacob will be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble; they will set them ablaze and devour them, and no survivor will remain from the house of Esau, for the LORD has spoken.

Those of the Negev will possess the mountain of Esau, and those of the lowlands the land of the Philistines; they will possess the fields of Ephraim and the fields of Samaria, and Benjamin will possess Gilead.
The exiles of this host of the children of Israel who are among the Canaanites as far as Zarephath, and the exiles of Jerusalem who are in Sepharad, will possess the cities of the Negev.
Deliverers will ascend Mount Zion to judge the mountain of Esau, and the kingdom will be the LORD's.
The word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai:
"Rise and go to Nineveh, that great city, and proclaim against it, for their wickedness has reached My presence."

But Jonah rose to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the LORD. He went down to Joppa, found a ship bound for Tarshish, paid its fare, and went down into it to sail with them to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD.
Then the LORD hurled a violent wind upon the sea, and a mighty tempest arose upon the waters, so that the ship threatened to break apart.

The sailors grew terrified, and each cried out to his own god. They hurled the ship's cargo into the sea to lighten the vessel. Meanwhile, Jonah had gone down into the innermost hold, lain down, and fallen into a deep sleep.
The captain approached him and said, "How can you sleep? Rise and call upon your god! Perhaps that god will be mindful of us, so that we may not perish."
Then they said to one another, "Come, let us cast lots, that we may discover on whose account this calamity has befallen us." So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.
Then they said to him, "Please tell us on whose account this calamity has befallen us. What is your occupation? Where have you come from? What is your country? And from what people are you?"
He said to them, "I am a Hebrew, and I revere the LORD, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land."
Then the men were seized with great fear and said to him, "What is this you have done?" For they knew that he was fleeing from the presence of the LORD, because he had told them.
Then they said to him, "What must we do to you, that the sea may become calm for us?" For the sea was growing ever more tempestuous.
He said to them, "Lift me up and throw me into the sea; then the sea will become calm for you, for I know that this great storm has come upon you because of me."
Nevertheless, the men rowed strenuously to return the ship to land, but they could not, for the sea grew increasingly tempestuous against them.

Therefore they cried out to the LORD and said, "Please, O the LORD, let us not perish on account of this man's life, and do not hold us guilty of innocent blood; for You, O the LORD, have done as You pleased."
So they lifted Jonah and cast him into the sea, and the sea ceased from its raging.
Then the men feared the LORD greatly, and they offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows.
And the LORD appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah remained in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
From the belly of the fish, Jonah prayed to the the LORD his God.
And he said, “In my distress I called to the the LORD, and He answered me. From the depths of the grave I cried for help, and You heard my voice.
You cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the current surrounded me; all Your breakers and Your waves passed over me.
And I said, ‘I have been driven away from before Your eyes; yet I will look again toward Your holy temple.’
The waters closed over me and threatened my life; the deep surrounded me, and seaweed was wrapped around my head.
I descended to the foundations of the mountains; the earth closed around me forever; yet You brought my life up from the pit, O the LORD my God.
When my soul fainted within me, I remembered the the LORD, and my prayer came to You, into Your holy temple.
Those who cling to worthless idols abandon the faithful love that could have been theirs.
But I, with a voice of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to You; what I have vowed I will pay. Salvation belongs to the the LORD.”
And the the LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto the dry land.
The word of the the LORD came to Jonah a second time, saying,
“Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and proclaim to it the message I am telling you.”
So Jonah arose and went to Nineveh according to the word of the the LORD. Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city—a journey of three days to cross.
Jonah began to enter the city, going a day’s journey, and he cried out, “Yet forty days, and Nineveh will be overthrown!”
The people of Nineveh believed God, and they proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from the greatest to the least.
When the word reached the king of Nineveh, he rose from his throne, removed his robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
Then he issued a proclamation in Nineveh: “By the decree of the king and his nobles, let no human being or animal—neither herd nor flock—taste anything at all. They must not eat or drink water.
Furthermore, let both people and animals be covered with sackcloth, and let them cry out earnestly to God. Let each one turn from his evil way and from the violence in his hands.
Who knows? God may turn and relent; He may turn from His fierce anger, so that we will not perish.”
When God saw their actions—that they had turned from their evil way—He relented from the calamity He had threatened to bring upon them, and He did not carry it out.
It displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was furious.

He prayed to the LORD and said, “Please, the LORD, was this not what I said while I was still in my own country? That is why I fled to Tarshish at the outset, for I knew that You are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, and that You relent from bringing disaster.
And now, the LORD, please take my life from me, for death is better to me than life.”
The LORD replied, “Do you have a good reason to be angry?”
Jonah left the city and sat down east of it. There he built a shelter and sat in its shade, waiting to see what would become of the city.
Then the LORD God appointed a plant, and it grew up over Jonah to provide shade for his head and to relieve him from his discomfort. Jonah rejoiced greatly over the plant.
But at dawn the next day, God appointed a worm, which attacked the plant so that it withered.
When the sun rose, God appointed a scorching east wind. The sun beat down on Jonah's head until he grew faint, and he asked to die, saying, “It is better for me to die than to live.”
The LORD said to Jonah, “Is it right for you to be angry about the plant?” Jonah replied, “I have a good reason to be angry, even to death.”
The LORD said, “You had compassion on the plant, which you did not labor over or cultivate. It sprang up in a night and perished in a night.
Should I not then have compassion on Nineveh, that great city, in which there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand people who cannot distinguish right from wrong, along with many animals?”
The word of the LORD that came to Micah of Moresheth in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
Hear, O peoples, all of you; listen, O earth, and everyone in it! Let the Lord, the LORD, be a witness against you, the Lord from His holy temple.
For behold, the LORD is coming out of His place; He will come down and tread on the high places of the earth.
The mountains will melt beneath Him, and the valleys will split apart, like wax before the fire, like water cascading down a slope.
All this is because of the transgression of Jacob and the sins of the house of Israel. What is the transgression of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what is the high place of Judah? Is it not Jerusalem?
Therefore I will make Samaria a heap of rubble in the open field, a planting place for vineyards. I will pour out her stones into the valley and lay bare her foundations.

All her carved images will be smashed, and all her wages will be burned in the fire; I will destroy all her idols. For she gathered them from a prostitute’s wages, and to a prostitute’s wages they will return.
Because of this I will lament and wail; I will go barefoot and naked. I will howl like jackals and mourn like ostriches.
For her wound is incurable; it has reached Judah; it has approached the gate of My people, as far as Jerusalem.
Do not tell it in Gath; do not weep at all. Roll in the dust in Beth Ophrah.
Pass on, O inhabitant of Shaphir, naked and ashamed. The inhabitant of Zaanan does not come out. The lamentation of Beth Ezel will take away its support from you.
For the inhabitant of Maroth pines for good, but disaster has come down from the LORD to the gate of Jerusalem.
Harness the chariot to the steeds, O inhabitant of Lachish. She was the beginning of sin to the Daughter of Zion, for the transgressions of Israel were found in you.
Therefore you will give parting gifts to Moresheth-gath. The houses of Achzib will be a deception to the kings of Israel.
I will yet bring a conqueror against you, O inhabitant of Mareshah. The glory of Israel will come to Adullam.
Shave your head and cut off your hair for the children of your delight; make yourself bald like the vulture, for they have gone from you into exile.
Woe to those who devise wickedness and plot evil on their beds; at daybreak they carry it out, because power lies in their hands.
They covet fields and seize them, and houses, and take them; they oppress a man and his household, a person and his inheritance.
Therefore thus says the LORD: "Behold, I am planning disaster against this family, from which you cannot escape; and you shall not walk haughtily, for it is an evil time.

In that day they will take up a taunt against you and chant a bitter lamentation: 'We are utterly ruined! He changes the portion of my people; how He takes it from me! To the faithless He apportions our fields.'
Therefore you will have no one in the assembly of the LORD to apportion land by lot."
"Do not prophesy," their prophets say. "Do not prophesy about these things; disgrace will not overtake us."
"Should it be said, O house of Jacob, 'Is the Spirit of the LORD impatient? Are these His doings?' Do not My words bring good to him who walks uprightly?
But lately My people have risen up as an enemy; you strip the robe from peaceful passersby, from those returning from war.
You drive the women of My people from their pleasant homes; you take My splendor from their children forever.
Arise and depart, for this is not your resting place, because it is defiled; it brings destruction, even a grievous destruction.
If a man, walking in falsehood and lies, says, 'I will prophesy to you of wine and strong drink,' he would be the prophet for this people."
"I will surely gather all of you, Jacob; I will surely gather the remnant of Israel. I will put them together like sheep in a fold, like a flock in its pasture; it will be noisy with people.
The Breaker goes up before them; they break through and pass the gate and go out by it. Their king passes on before them, with the LORD at their head."
I said, "Hear now, you leaders of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel: Is it not your obligation to know justice?
You hate what is good and love what is evil; you tear the skin from My people and the flesh from their bones.
You devour the flesh of My people, strip off their skin, break their bones, and spread them out like meat in a pot, like stew in a cauldron.
Then they will cry out to the LORD, but He will not answer them; at that time He will hide His face from them, because they have done evil deeds."
Thus says The LORD concerning the prophets who lead My people astray, who bite with their teeth and cry, "Peace!" but declare holy war against anyone who does not feed them.
Therefore night will come upon you without visions, and darkness without divination; the sun will set on the prophets, and the day will grow dark over them.
The seers will be ashamed, the diviners confounded, and all of them will cover their mouths, for there is no answer from God.
But I am full of power by the Spirit of the LORD, and of justice and might, to declare to Jacob his transgression and to Israel his sin.
Hear this, you leaders of the house of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel, you who abhor justice and pervert every right.
You build Zion with blood and Jerusalem with injustice.
Her leaders judge for a bribe, her priests teach for a price, and her prophets divine for money; yet they lean on the LORD and say, "Is not the LORD among us? No calamity will overtake us."
Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become a heap of ruins, and the temple mount will become a forested hill.
In the latter days, the mountain of the house of the the LORD will stand firm as the foremost of the mountains, raised high above the hills, and peoples will stream to it.

Many nations will go and say, “Come, let us ascend to the mountain of the the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob, that He may teach us His ways and that we may walk in His paths; for teaching will go forth from Zion, and the word of the the LORD from Jerusalem.”

He will judge between many peoples and settle disputes for mighty nations afar; they will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not raise sword against nation, nor will they train for war again.
Each man will sit beneath his vine and beneath his fig tree, and no one will make him afraid, for the mouth of the the LORD of Hosts has spoken.
For every people walks in the name of its god, but we will walk in the name of the the LORD our God forever and ever.
In that day, declares the the LORD, I will gather the lame and assemble the outcast—those whom I have afflicted.
I will make the lame into a remnant and the distant into a mighty nation, and the the LORD will reign over them on Mount Zion from now on and forever.
And you, tower of the flock, stronghold of the daughter of Zion, to you the former sovereignty will come; the kingdom will come to the daughter of Jerusalem.
Why do you cry aloud? Is there no king within you? Has your counselor perished, that pain has seized you like a woman in labor?

Writhe and groan, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in labor, for now you will leave the city and dwell in the open field; you will go as far as Babylon. There you will be rescued; there the the LORD will redeem you from the power of your enemies.
Now many nations are gathered against you, saying, “Let her be defiled, and let our eyes gloat over Zion.”
But they do not know the thoughts of the the LORD, nor do they understand His counsel, that He has gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor.

Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion, for I will make your horn iron and your hooves bronze; you will crush many peoples, and I will devote their gain to the the LORD and their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.
Now, city of soldiers, muster your forces, for a siege is laid against us; with a rod they strike the judge of Israel on the cheek.
And you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come for Me One to be ruler over Israel, whose origins are from of old, from ancient days.
Therefore He will hand them over until the woman in labor gives birth; then the rest of His brothers will return to the Israelites.
He will stand and shepherd His flock in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD His God. And they will live securely, for now He will be great to the ends of the earth.
He will be their peace. When Assyria invades our land and treads in our citadels, we will raise against him seven shepherds and eight leaders of men.
They will rule the land of Assyria with the sword and the land of Nimrod at its gates; He will deliver us when the Assyrian invades our land and marches within our borders.
The remnant of Jacob will be among many peoples like dew from the LORD, like showers on the grass, which do not wait for man or linger for mankind.

The remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like a lion among the beasts of the forest, like a young lion among flocks of sheep; if it passes through, it tramples and tears, and there is no one to rescue.
Your hand will be raised against your adversaries, and all your enemies will be cut off.
And on that day, declares the LORD, I will cut off your horses from among you and destroy your chariots.
I will cut off the cities of your land and tear down all your fortresses.
I will cut off sorcery from your hand, and you will have no soothsayers.
I will cut off your carved images and your sacred pillars from among you, and you will no longer bow down to the work of your hands.
I will uproot your Asherah poles from among you and destroy your cities.
I will execute vengeance in anger and wrath on the nations that have not obeyed.
Listen now to what the LORD declares: "Arise and present your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice."
Hear, O mountains, the LORD's indictment, and you enduring foundations of the earth, for the LORD has a case against His people, and He will contend with Israel.
"My people, what have I done to you? How have I wearied you? Bear witness against Me.
For I brought you up from the land of Egypt and ransomed you from the house of bondage; I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam before you.
My people, recall what Balak king of Moab devised, and what Balaam son of Beor answered him; remember the route from Shittim to Gilgal, that you may know the righteous deeds of the LORD."
"With what shall I come before the LORD and bow before the God of heaven? Shall I come before Him with burnt offerings, with calves a year old?
Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?"
He has shown you, O man, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
The voice of the LORD calls to the city—and it is sound wisdom to fear Your name: "Hear the rod and Him who appointed it!
Are there still ill-gotten treasures in the house of the wicked, and a deficient ephah under curse?
Can anyone be innocent with dishonest scales and a bag of deceitful weights?
For her rich men are full of violence, her inhabitants speak lies, and their tongues are steeped in deceit.
"Therefore I will strike you with a devastating blow and make you desolate because of your sins.
You will eat but not be satisfied, and emptiness will linger within your midst. You will hoard but not secure, and what you save I will give to the sword.
You will sow but not reap; you will tread olives but not anoint yourself with oil; and you will press new wine but not drink it.

For the statutes of Omri are kept, and all the works of the house of Ahab; and you have walked in their counsels, that I may make you a desolation, and your inhabitants a hissing; and you will bear the reproach of My people."
Woe to me! I have become like one who gathers summer fruit after the vintage has been gleaned: no cluster remains to eat, and no first-ripe fig that my soul craves.
The faithful have vanished from the land; not one upright person remains among humanity. They all lurk for blood, and each man hunts his brother as though casting a net.
Both hands are adept at evil; the ruler demands a bribe, the judge is open to a price, and the powerful man speaks whatever his soul craves, so they weave it all together.
The best of them is like a briar; the most upright is worse than a thorn hedge. The day of your watchmen has come; now your punishment will be their confusion.
Do not trust a neighbor; do not place confidence in a friend; guard the words of your mouth from the one who lies in your bosom.
For a son dishonors his father, a daughter rises against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man's enemies are those of his own household.
But I will look to the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation; my God will hear me.
Do not rejoice over me, my enemy: though I have fallen, I will rise again; though I dwell in darkness, the LORD will be light to me.

I will bear the indignation of the LORD, for I have sinned against Him, until He pleads my cause and executes judgment on my behalf; He will bring me out into the light, and I will see His righteousness.
Then my enemy will see it, and shame will cover the one who said to me, "Where is the LORD your God?" My eyes will gaze upon her; now she will be trampled like mud in the streets.
A day for building your walls! On that day the boundary will be extended far.
In that day they will come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, from Egypt to the Euphrates, from sea to sea and mountain to mountain.
Yet the earth will be desolate because of its inhabitants, as the fruit of their deeds.
Shepherd your people with your staff, the flock of your inheritance, who dwell alone in a forest in the midst of Carmel; let them graze in Bashan and Gilead as in the days of old.
As in the days when you came out of the land of Egypt, I will show them wonders.
The nations will see and be ashamed of all their might; they will put their hands over their mouths; their ears will be deaf.
They will lick the dust like a serpent, like the crawling things of the earth; they will come trembling from their strongholds; they will turn in dread to the LORD our God, and they will fear You.
Who is a God like You, who pardons iniquity and passes over the transgression of the remnant of His heritage? He does not hold His anger forever, for He delights in steadfast love.
He will again have compassion on us; He will subdue our iniquities; and You will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
You will give truth to Jacob and steadfast love to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from the days of old.
An oracle concerning Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
The LORD is jealous and avenging; the LORD is avenging and full of wrath. The LORD takes vengeance on His adversaries and reserves wrath for His enemies.
The LORD is slow to anger and great in power; the LORD will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. His path is in the whirlwind and storm, and clouds are the dust of His feet.
He rebukes the sea and dries it up; He makes all the rivers run dry. Bashan and Carmel wither, and the flower of Lebanon fades.
The mountains quake before Him, and the hills melt away. The earth trembles at His presence—the world and all its inhabitants.
Who can withstand His indignation? Who can endure His burning anger? His wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks are shattered before Him.
The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; He cares for those who trust in Him.
But with an overwhelming flood He will make an end of Nineveh; He will pursue His enemies into darkness.
Whatever you plot against the LORD, He will bring to an end; trouble will not rise up a second time.
For they will be entangled like thorns and consumed like the drink of drunkards; they will be burned up like dry stubble.
From you, O Nineveh, has come forth one who plots evil against the LORD and counsels wickedness.
This is what the LORD says: "Though they are strong and many, they will still be mowed down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, I will afflict you no more.
Now I will break their yoke from your neck and tear away your bonds."

The LORD has issued a decree concerning you, Nineveh: "Your name will no longer be perpetuated; I will cut off the carved image and cast idol from the house of your gods; I will prepare your grave, for you are contemptible."

Look to the mountains—the feet of one who brings good news, who proclaims peace! Celebrate your festivals, O Judah; fulfill your vows. For the wicked will never again march through you; they will be utterly cut off.
The scatterer has come up against you. Guard the fortress, watch the road, brace for action, and marshal all your strength.
For the LORD will restore the splendor of Jacob like the splendor of Israel, though destroyers have laid them waste and ruined their vines.
The shields of his mighty men are red; the warriors are clad in scarlet. The chariots flash with fire on the day they are made ready, and the spears of cypress are brandished.
The chariots dash through the streets; they race madly through the squares. Their appearance is like torches; they dart like lightning.
He summons his nobles; they stumble as they advance. They hasten to its wall; the siege shield is set up.
The river gates are thrown open, and the palace collapses.
It is decreed: she is exiled and led away; her maidservants moan like doves and beat upon their breasts.
Nineveh has been like a pool of water throughout her days, but now they are fleeing. "Stop! Stop!" they cry, but no one turns back.
Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold! There is no end to the treasure, an abundance of every precious thing.
She is emptied! Yes, she is desolate and laid waste! Hearts melt, knees knock, bodies tremble, and every face grows pale.
Where is the lions' den, the feeding ground of the young lions, where the lion and lioness prowled with their cubs, with nothing to make them afraid?
The lion tore enough for his cubs and strangled prey for his lionesses. He filled his lairs with prey and his dens with torn flesh.

"Behold, I am against you," declares the LORD of Hosts. "I will burn up your chariots in smoke, and the sword will devour your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers will no longer be heard."
Woe to the city of blood, full of lies, full of plunder, never without prey.
The crack of the whip, the rumble of wheels, galloping horses, and bounding chariots!
Charging horsemen; flashing sword and gleaming spear; countless slain, heaps of corpses, bodies without number—they stumble over the dead.
All because of the countless harlotries of the harlot, the charming one, mistress of sorceries, who sells nations through her harlotries and families through her sorceries.
Behold, I am against you, declares the LORD of Hosts, and I will lift your skirts over your face; I will show the nations your nakedness and the kingdoms your shame.
I will pelt you with filth, treat you with contempt, and make you a spectacle.
Then everyone who sees you will shrink back and say, "Nineveh is devastated; who will grieve for her?" Where can I find comforters for you?
Are you better than Thebes, situated on the Nile, with water all around her, whose defense was the sea and whose wall was the water?
Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength; Put and Libya were her helpers.
Yet she was carried away; she went into captivity. Her infants were dashed to pieces at the head of every street. They cast lots for her nobles, and all her great men were bound in chains.
You too will become drunk; you will go into hiding; you too will seek refuge from the enemy.
All your fortresses are like fig trees with first-ripe figs: if shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater.
Look, your troops are women in your midst; the gates of your land are wide open to your enemies; fire has consumed your gate bars.
Draw water for the siege, strengthen your fortresses, work the clay, tread the mortar, and repair the brick kiln.
There fire will consume you; the sword will cut you down and devour you like the locust. Multiply yourself like the locust; multiply yourself like the grasshopper.
You have increased your merchants more than the stars of heaven. The locust strips the land and flies away.
Your guards are like locusts, and your officials are like swarms of locusts that settle in the walls on a cold day; when the sun rises, they flee, and no one knows where they are.
Your shepherds slumber, O king of Assyria; your nobles sleep. Your people are scattered on the mountains, and no one gathers them.
There is no healing for your wound; your injury is fatal. Everyone who hears the report about you claps their hands over you, for who has not endured your relentless cruelty?
The oracle that Habakkuk the prophet received in a vision.
“How long, the LORD, must I cry for help, and You do not hear? I cry out to You, ‘Violence!’ and You do not save.
Why do You make me see iniquity, and why do You look at oppression? For devastation and violence are before me; strife arises, and contention is stirred up.
Therefore the law is paralyzed, and justice never goes forth. For the wicked hem in the righteous, so that justice is perverted.” “
Look among the nations and observe; be utterly astonished, for I am doing a work in your days that you would not believe even if it were told.
For behold, I am raising up the Chaldeans—that bitter and impetuous nation—who march through the breadth of the earth to seize dwellings not their own.
They are dreaded and feared; their justice and dignity proceed from themselves.” “
Their horses are swifter than leopards, fiercer than wolves at dusk. Their horsemen charge ahead; they come from afar, flying like an eagle swooping to devour.
They all come for violence; their hordes advance like the east wind; they gather captives like sand.” “
They mock kings, and rulers are a laughingstock to them; they laugh at every fortress, pile up earth, and capture it.
Then they sweep by like the wind and pass on—guilty men whose strength is their god.” “
Are You not from everlasting, the LORD my God, my Holy One? We will not die. the LORD, You have appointed them for judgment; and You, O Rock, have established them for correction.
Your eyes are too pure to look on evil; You cannot tolerate wrongdoing. Why do You look on the treacherous and keep silent when the wicked devours one more righteous than himself?
You have made mankind like the fish of the sea, like creeping things with no ruler.
He brings all of them up with a hook; he catches them in his net and gathers them in his dragnet. Therefore he rejoices and is glad.
Therefore he sacrifices to his net and burns incense to his dragnet, for by them his portion is rich and his food is plentiful.
Will he then empty his net and continue slaughtering the nations without mercy?”
I will stand at my watchpost and station myself on the rampart; I will keep watch to see what He will say to me, and what answer I am to give to my complaint.
Then the the LORD answered me: “Write down the vision and inscribe it plainly on tablets, so that a herald may run with it.
For the vision awaits an appointed time; it speaks of the end and will not prove false. Though it lingers, wait for it, since it will surely come and will not delay.
“Behold, his soul is puffed up within him and is not upright, but the righteous shall live by his faith.

Indeed, wine is treacherous; a proud man is never at rest. He enlarges his appetite like Sheol, and like Death he is never satisfied. He gathers all nations to himself and collects all peoples as his own.
“Will not all these take up a taunt against him, with mockery and riddles, saying, ‘Woe to him who amasses what is not his own—how long must this go on?—and burdens himself with pledges!’
Will not your creditors suddenly arise, and those who torment you awaken? Then you will become plunder for them.
Because you have plundered many nations, the remnant of the peoples will plunder you—because of human bloodshed and violence against lands, cities, and all their inhabitants.
“Woe to him who builds his house through unjust gain, setting his nest on high to escape calamity!
You have devised shame for your house by cutting off many peoples, and you have sinned against your own soul.
For the stone will cry out from the wall, and the beam will answer it from the woodwork.
“Woe to him who builds a city with bloodshed and establishes a town by iniquity!
Behold, is it not from the the LORD of Hosts that the peoples labor only to feed the fire, and the nations weary themselves in vain?
For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the the LORD, as the waters cover the sea.
“Woe to him who gives his neighbor drink, pouring out your wrath and making him drunk, so that you may gaze on their nakedness!
You are filled with shame instead of glory. You too—drink and be exposed! The cup in the the LORD’s right hand will come around to you, and disgrace will cover your glory.
For the violence against Lebanon will cover you, and the destruction of the beasts will terrify you, because of the blood of men and the violence done to the land, the city, and all who dwell in it.
“What use is an idol, that its maker should carve it—or a cast image, a teacher of lies? For its maker trusts in his own creation, making idols that cannot speak.
Woe to him who says to wood, ‘Awake!’ and to a silent stone, ‘Arise!’ Can it teach? Behold, it is overlaid with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all within it.
“But the the LORD is in His holy temple; let all the earth keep silence before Him.”
A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, set to Shigionoth:
The LORD, I have heard Your report; I stand in awe of Your deeds, the LORD. Revive Your work in the midst of the years; make it known in the midst of the years. In wrath, remember mercy.
God came from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. His glory covered the heavens, and His praise filled the earth.
His radiance was like the sunlight; rays flashed from His hand, where His power was hidden.
Pestilence went before Him, and scorching fever followed in His steps.
He stood and measured the earth; He looked and startled the nations; the ancient mountains crumbled; the perpetual hills collapsed. His ways are everlasting.
I saw the tents of Cushan in distress; the curtains of Midian trembled.
Were You angry at the rivers, the LORD? Was Your wrath against the streams? Did You rage against the sea when You rode on Your horses, on Your chariots of salvation?
You brandished Your bow; You called for many arrows. Selah. You split the earth with rivers.
The mountains saw You and quaked; torrents of water swept by. The deep roared and lifted its waves on high.
Sun and moon stood still in their places at the flash of Your flying arrows, at the gleam of Your glittering spear.
You marched across the earth in fury; You threshed the nations in wrath.
You went forth for the salvation of Your people, for the salvation of Your anointed. You crushed the head of the house of the wicked and stripped him from head to foot. Selah.
With his own spear You pierced the head of his warriors when they stormed out to scatter us, gloating as though ready to devour the poor in secret.
You trampled the sea with Your horses, churning the great waters.
I heard and my heart pounded; my lips quivered at the sound. Decay entered my bones; I trembled where I stood. Yet I will wait patiently for the day of calamity to come upon the people who invade us.
Though the fig tree does not bud and no fruit is on the vines, though the olive crop fails and the fields produce no food, though the sheep are cut off from the fold and no cattle are in the stalls,
yet I will exult in the LORD; I will rejoice in the God of my salvation!
The Lord the LORD is my strength; He makes my feet like those of a deer; He makes me walk on high places. For the director of music. On my stringed instruments.
The word of the LORD that came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.
"I will utterly sweep away everything from the face of the earth," declares the LORD.

"I will sweep away both man and beast; I will sweep away the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea, along with the stumbling blocks of the wicked. I will cut off mankind from the face of the earth," declares the LORD.
"I will stretch out My hand against Judah and against all the inhabitants of Jerusalem. I will cut off from this place every remnant of Baal, the names of the pagan priests along with the priests,
those who bow down on the rooftops to the host of heaven, those who bow down and swear to the LORD but also swear by Milcom,
and those who turn back from following the LORD, and those who neither seek the LORD nor inquire of Him," declares the LORD.
Be silent before the Lord, the LORD, for the Day of the LORD is near. Indeed, the LORD has prepared a sacrifice; He has consecrated His guests.
"On the Day of the LORD, I will punish the officials and the sons of the king and all who dress in foreign clothes.
On that day I will punish all who leap over the threshold, who fill the house of their master with violence and deceit," declares the LORD.
"On that day," declares the LORD, "a cry will go up from the Fish Gate, a wailing from the Second District, and a loud crash from the hills."
Wail, O inhabitants of the Hollow, for all the merchants are ruined; all who weigh out silver are cut off.
"At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps and punish the men who are complacent, who say in their hearts, 'The LORD will do nothing, either good or evil.'
Their wealth will be plundered and their houses laid waste. They will build houses but not inhabit them, and plant vineyards but not drink their wine," declares the LORD.
The great Day of the LORD is near—near and coming quickly. The sound of the Day of the LORD is bitter; there the mighty warrior cries out.
That day is a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress, a day of ruin and desolation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and blackness,
a day of trumpet blast and battle cry against the fortified cities and against the high corner towers.
"I will bring distress upon mankind, so that they walk like the blind, because they have sinned against the LORD. Their blood will be poured out like dust, and their flesh like dung."

Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to deliver them on the Day of the LORD's wrath. The whole earth will be consumed by the fire of His jealousy. For He will make a sudden end of all who dwell on the earth.
Gather yourselves, gather together, O nation without shame.
Before the decree is born, before the day passes like chaff, before the fierce anger of the LORD comes upon you, before the Day of the LORD comes upon you.
Seek the LORD, all you humble people of the land who have done what His justice requires. Seek righteousness; seek humility. Perhaps you will be sheltered on the day of the LORD's wrath.
For Gaza will be abandoned, and Ashkelon left a desolation; Ashdod will be emptied by midday, and Ekron will be uprooted.
Woe to the inhabitants of the seacoast, O nation of the Cherethites! The word of the LORD is against you, O Canaan, land of the Philistines; and I will destroy you, and no one will remain.
The seacoast will become pastureland, with shepherd encampments and sheepfolds.

It will belong to the remnant of the house of Judah; there they will pasture and lie down in the evening within the houses of Ashkelon, for the LORD their God will attend to them and restore their fortunes.
I have heard the taunting of Moab and the reviling of the Ammonites, who have taunted My people and threatened their borders.

Therefore, as I live, declares the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, Moab will become like Sodom and the Ammonites like Gomorrah—a land of weeds and salt pits, a desolation forever. The remnant of My people will plunder them, and the survivors of My nation will inherit them.
This is what they will receive in return for their pride, for taunting and exalting themselves against the people of the LORD of Hosts.
The LORD will be fearsome to them when He reduces to nothing all the gods of the earth; then every nation will bow down to Him, each in its own place, even all the coastlands of the nations.
You too, O Cushites, will be slain by My sword.
He will stretch out His hand against the north and destroy Assyria, and He will make Nineveh a desolation, dry as the wilderness.

Flocks will lie down in her midst, every beast of the nations; both the desert owl and the screech owl will lodge in her pillars. Their calls will echo through the windows; desolation will be on the threshold, for He has laid bare the cedar beams.

This is the exultant city that dwelt securely, that said in her heart, "I am, and there is no one besides me." How she has become a desolation, a lair for wild beasts! Everyone who passes by her hisses and shakes his fist.
Woe to the oppressing city—rebellious and defiled!
She has not obeyed the voice; she has not accepted correction; she has not trusted in the LORD; she has not drawn near to her God.
Her princes within her are roaring lions; her judges are evening wolves that leave nothing for the morning.
Her prophets are reckless and treacherous; her priests have profaned the sanctuary and done violence to the law.
The LORD within her is righteous; He does no wrong. Morning by morning He dispenses justice; He does not fail at dawn, yet the unjust knows no shame.
I have cut off nations; their corner towers lie desolate; I have made their streets waste, so that no one passes by; their cities are destroyed, so that no man remains and no one dwells there.
I said, “Surely you will fear Me and accept correction.” Then her dwelling would not be cut off for all that I have appointed against her. But they rose early and corrupted all their deeds.

“Therefore wait for Me,” declares the LORD, “until the day I rise to plunder. For My decision is to gather nations, to assemble kingdoms, to pour out upon them all My indignation—all My fierce anger. For in the fire of My jealousy all the earth will be consumed.”
For at that time I will restore pure lips to the peoples, so that all of them may call upon the name of the LORD and serve Him with one accord.
From beyond the rivers of Cush My worshipers, My dispersed ones, will bring Me an offering.

On that day you will not be put to shame for any of the deeds by which you have transgressed against Me. For then I will remove from your midst those who rejoice in their pride, and you will never again be haughty on My holy mountain.
But I will leave within your midst a meek and humble people, and they will trust in the name of the LORD.
The remnant of Israel will no longer do wrong or speak lies, nor will a deceitful tongue be found in their mouths. They will feed and lie down, with no one to make them afraid.
Sing, O Daughter of Zion; shout aloud, O Israel! Be glad and rejoice with all your heart, O Daughter of Jerusalem!
The LORD has taken away your punishment; He has turned back your enemy. The LORD, the King of Israel, is in your midst; never again will you fear any harm.
On that day it will be said to Jerusalem, “Do not fear, O Zion; do not let your hands hang limp.”
The LORD your God is among you; He is mighty to save. He will rejoice over you with gladness; He will quiet you with His love; He will rejoice over you with singing.
I will gather those among you who grieve over the appointed feasts, so that you will no longer suffer reproach.
Behold, at that time I will deal with all your oppressors. I will save the lame and gather the outcast, and I will give them praise and honor in every land where they were put to shame.

“At that time I will bring you in; at that time I will gather you. For I will give you fame and praise among all the peoples of the earth when I restore your fortunes before your very eyes,” says the LORD.

In the second year of King Darius, on the first day of the sixth month, the word of the the LORD came through Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest:
"This is what the the LORD of Hosts says: 'These people say, "The time has not yet come to rebuild the house of the the LORD."'
Then the word of the the LORD came through Haggai the prophet, saying:
"Is it time for you yourselves to dwell in your paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins?
"Now, therefore, this is what the the LORD of Hosts says: Consider your ways.

"You have sown much, but harvested little. You eat, but you never have enough; you drink, but you never have your fill. You clothe yourselves, but no one is warm. And he who earns wages earns them only to see them vanish.
"This is what the the LORD of Hosts says: Consider your ways.
"Go up to the mountain and bring wood and build the house, so that I may be pleased with it and be glorified, says the the LORD.

"You expected much, but it amounted to little. What you brought home, I blew away. Why? declares the the LORD of Hosts. Because of My house, which remains in ruins, while each of you is busy with his own house.
"Therefore, because of you, the heavens have withheld their dew and the earth has withheld its crops.
"I called for a drought on the land and the mountains, on the grain, the new wine, the olive oil, on what the ground produces, on people and livestock, and on all the labor of your hands."

Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Joshua son of Jehozadak the high priest, and all the remnant of the people obeyed the voice of the the LORD their God and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the the LORD their God had sent him. And the people feared the the LORD.
Then Haggai, the messenger of the the LORD, delivered the the LORD's message to the people: "I am with you, declares the the LORD."

So the The LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people. They came and worked on the house of the the LORD of Hosts, their God,
on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of King Darius.
On the twenty-first day of the seventh month, the word of the LORD came through the prophet Haggai, saying:
“Say now to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the remnant of the people:”

“Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? How do you see it now? Does it not seem to you like nothing in comparison? Yet now be strong, Zerubbabel,” declares the LORD. “Be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest,” declares the LORD. “Be strong, all you people of the land,” declares the LORD. “Work, for I am with you,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
“This is the covenant I made with you when you came out of Egypt, and My Spirit remains among you. Do not be afraid.”
For thus says the LORD of Hosts: “Once more, in a little while, I will shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.
I will shake all the nations, and the treasures of all the nations will be brought in, and I will fill this house with glory,” says the LORD of Hosts.
“The silver is Mine, and the gold is Mine,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
“The latter glory of this house will be greater than the former,” says the LORD of Hosts, “and in this place I will grant peace,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Haggai the prophet, saying:
“Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Ask now the priests concerning the law, saying:”
“If a man carries holy meat in the fold of his garment, and with that fold touches bread, or stew, or wine, or oil, or any food, does it become holy?” And the priests answered, “No.”
Then Haggai said, “If one defiled by contact with a corpse touches any of these, does it become unclean?” And the priests answered, “It becomes unclean.”
Then Haggai answered and said, “So it is with this people and this nation before Me,” declares the LORD, “and so it is with every work of their hands; whatever they offer there is unclean.”
“And now, consider carefully from this day forward, from before a stone was laid upon a stone in the temple of the LORD.
Since those days, when one came to a heap of twenty measures, there were but ten; when one came to the winepress to draw out fifty measures, there were but twenty.
I struck you with blight and mildew and hail in all the work of your hands, yet you did not return to Me,” declares the LORD.
“Consider carefully from this day forward, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the day the foundation of the temple of the LORD was laid—consider it carefully.
Is the seed still in the barn? Even the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, and the olive tree have not yet produced fruit. But from this day on I will bless you.”
And the word of the LORD came a second time to Haggai on the twenty-fourth day of the month, saying:
“Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, saying: I will shake the heavens and the earth.

I will overthrow the thrones of kingdoms and destroy the power of the kingdoms of the nations; I will overturn chariots and their riders, and horses and their riders will fall, each by the sword of his brother.”

“On that day,” declares the LORD of Hosts, “I will take you, My servant Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel,” declares the LORD, “and I will make you like My signet ring, for I have chosen you,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
In the eighth month of the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, saying:
The LORD was very angry with your fathers.
Therefore say to them, “Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Return to Me,” declares the LORD of Hosts, “and I will return to you,” says the LORD of Hosts.

“Do not be like your fathers, to whom the former prophets cried out, ‘Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Turn from your evil ways and your evil deeds.’ But they did not listen or pay attention to Me,” declares the LORD.
“Where are your fathers now? And the prophets, do they live forever?”

But did not My words and My statutes, which I commanded My servants the prophets, overtake your fathers? Then they repented and said, “As the LORD of Hosts purposed to do to us according to our ways and deeds, so He has done to us.”
On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, the month of Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, saying:
I saw by night, and behold, a man riding on a red horse, and he stood among the myrtle trees in the hollow; and behind him were red, sorrel, and white horses.
Then I said, “What are these, my lord?” And the angel who talked with me said to me, “I will show you what these are.”
And the man standing among the myrtle trees answered and said, “These are the ones whom the LORD has sent to walk to and fro throughout the earth.”
And they answered the angel of the LORD who stood among the myrtle trees and said, “We have walked to and fro throughout the earth, and behold, all the earth sits still and is at rest.”

Then the angel of the LORD answered and said, “O the LORD of Hosts, how long will You not have mercy on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, against which You have had indignation these seventy years?”
And the LORD answered the angel who talked with me with good and comforting words.
So the angel who talked with me said to me, “Cry out, saying,” “Thus says the LORD of Hosts: I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great jealousy.
And I am very angry with the nations that are at ease; for I was a little angry, and they made the disaster worse.”
Therefore thus says the LORD: “I have returned to Jerusalem with mercies; My house shall be built in it,” says the LORD of Hosts, “and a measuring line shall be stretched out over Jerusalem.”
Cry out again, saying, “Thus says the LORD of Hosts: My cities shall again overflow with prosperity, and the LORD will again comfort Zion and will again choose Jerusalem.”
Then I lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, four horns.
And I said to the angel who talked with me, “What are these?” And he answered me, “These are the horns that have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.”
Then the LORD showed me four craftsmen.

And I said, “What are these coming to do?” And he said, “These are the horns that have scattered Judah, so that no one could lift up his head; but these have come to terrify them, to cast down the horns of the nations that lifted up their horns against the land of Judah to scatter it.”
I lifted my eyes and looked, and behold, a man was standing there with a measuring line in his hand.
I asked, "Where are you going?" He said, "I am going to measure Jerusalem, to find out how wide and how long it is."
Then the angel who had been speaking with me went out, and another angel came out to meet him.
He said to him, "Run and tell that young man: 'Jerusalem will be inhabited without walls because of the multitude of people and livestock within it.'"
"And I will be a wall of fire around her," declares the LORD, "and I will be the glory within her."
"Up! Up! Flee from the land of the north," declares the LORD, "for I have scattered you like the four winds of heaven," declares the LORD.
"Up, Zion! Escape, you who dwell with the Daughter of Babylon."
For thus says the LORD of Hosts: "After His glory has sent Me against the nations that have plundered you—for whoever touches you touches the apple of His eye—
I will surely raise My hand against them, so that they will become plunder for their own servants. Then you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent Me."
"Shout for joy and be glad, O Daughter of Zion, for behold, I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst," declares the LORD.
"On that day many nations will join themselves to the LORD and become My people, and I will dwell in your midst. Then you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent Me to you."
The LORD will take possession of Judah as His portion in the holy land, and He will once again choose Jerusalem.
Be silent before the LORD, all people, for He has roused Himself from His holy dwelling.
Then he showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the Angel of the the LORD, with Satan standing at his right hand to accuse him.
And the LORD said to Satan, “The LORD rebuke you, Satan! Indeed, the the LORD, who has chosen Jerusalem, rebuke you! Is this not a man rescued from destruction?”
Now Joshua was clothed in filthy garments as he stood before the Angel.

So He answered and spoke to those standing before Him, saying, “Remove the filthy garments from him.” Then He said to Joshua, “See, I have removed your iniquity from you, and I will clothe you in rich robes.”
Then I said, “Let them put a clean turban on his head.” So they put a clean turban on his head and clothed him, while the Angel of the the LORD stood by.
And the Angel of the the LORD gave this charge to Joshua:
“This is what the the LORD of Hosts says: ‘If you walk in My ways and keep My charge, then you will govern My house and keep My courts, and I will give you a place among these who are standing here.
